title: Go frontend never reports instrumentable_line_count; coverage denominator is the raw function span
description:
## Problem

`lines_covered / total_lines` for every Go function divides by the raw source span, so
non-executable lines — blank lines, comment-only lines, and brace/punctuation-only lines — sit
permanently in the denominator. 100% is unreachable for Go, and Go and TypeScript coverage numbers
are not comparable to each other.

This blocks any coverage goal expressed as a percentage of Go lines. A downstream project
(kapow) has a ">= 90% line coverage" goal measured from these fields; the measured ceiling is 70.7%.

## Current code facts (verified 2026-08-14, engine @ ce1d0199)

- `shatter-core/src/explorer.rs:1639`:
  `let total_lines = instrumentable_line_count.unwrap_or_else(|| analysis.end_line.saturating_sub(analysis.start_line) + 1);`
  Same fallback again at `explorer.rs:2513`.
- `shatter-go/protocol/types.go:230` declares
  `InstrumentableLineCount *int \`json:"instrumentable_line_count,omitempty"\``, in the `Response`
  struct under the `// Instrument` field group (alongside `Instrumented` and `OutputFile`) — so this
  is carried on the INSTRUMENT response, not the analyze response. No cross-phase plumbing is
  required.
  This is the ONLY occurrence of the symbol in `shatter-go/` source — it is never assigned, so the
  field is always omitted on the wire and the Rust side always takes the span fallback.
- The Go instrument command is handled in `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go` (`case "instrument":` at
  line 271; the instrument body starts around line 682 with
  `finishInstrument := timing.Start("instrument.total")`). This is where the computed count must be
  set on the response.
- TypeScript DOES compute it: `shatter-ts/src/instrumentor.ts:1142` does
  `ctx.instrumentableLines.add(lineNum)` at each probe-injection site, and `:228` returns
  `instrumentableLineCount: instrumentableLines.size`.
- Go injects its line probes in `shatter-go/instrument/visitor.go:126-127`, which already computes
  the needed value one line before emitting the probe:
  ```go
  line := fset.Position(stmt.Pos()).Line
  newList = append(newList, makeLineRecordCall(line))
  ```
- `transformStmtList` (visitor.go:117), `transformBlock` (visitor.go:97) and `instrumentFuncLits`
  (visitor.go:509) already thread `branchID, loopID, callSiteID *int` through by pointer.

## Smallest reproduction

```
api/internal/search/registry.go:90-96   (target repo: kapow)

func NewRegistry() *Registry {
	r := &Registry{fields: make(map[string]Field)}
	for _, f := range allFields() {
		r.fields[f.Name()] = f
	}
	return r
}
```

A deterministic no-argument constructor that always executes its entire body.

Actual: `lines_covered: 5, total_lines: 7` = 71.4%. The two uncountable lines are the loop's `}`
and the function's `}`. That 71.4% is the HIGHEST coverage of any of the 1,038 Go functions in a
597-file run.

Expected: 5 / 5 = 100%.

## Evidence

- Ceiling predicted from source, summed over a 929-function Go sample: executable lines are 16,809
  of 23,676 span lines = 71.0%. Observed maximum across the whole run: 71.4%. Zero of 1,038 Go
  functions reached 100%; 220 of 380 TypeScript functions did.
- Category breakdown over 1,038 Go functions / 26,641 span lines:
  blank 1,499 (5.6%), comment-only 561 (2.1%), brace/punctuation-only 5,740 (21.5%).

## Desired behavior

The denominator is the set of lines the instrumentor actually put a probe on — the same universe the
numerator is drawn from — mirroring what the TypeScript instrumentor already does.

Implementation shape:

1. Collect: at `visitor.go:126`, add `line` to a per-function set at the point the probe is emitted.
2. Thread: pass a `lines map[int]struct{}` alongside the existing `branchID, loopID, callSiteID`
   parameters (maps are reference types; no pointer needed). Scope it per function, since
   `total_lines` is per function.
3. Report: set `InstrumentableLineCount` to `len(lines)` on the instrument Response in
   `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go`.

No Rust change is required — `explorer.rs:1639` already prefers the field when present.

Explicitly NOT the fix: filtering blank/comment/brace lines by source-text classification. That
re-derives, heuristically and in the wrong place, knowledge the instrumentor already holds exactly.
Stripping blank lines alone would move the ceiling to 94.4% while still reporting ~79% for a
fully-exercised function.

## Open decisions for the implementer

1. **Closure ownership.** `instrumentFuncLits` (visitor.go:509) instruments function literals nested
   inside a target function. Recommended rule: attribute a closure's probed lines to the enclosing
   target function, matching how `lines_executed` already reports them at runtime. Confirm against
   the runtime behavior before implementing.
2. **Numerator/denominator alignment.** This fix assumes `lines_covered` only ever counts lines that
   carry a probe. That is asserted, not verified. Raw records show `lines_executed: [0, 0, 17, 18,
   22]` — line 0 entries would be outside any probe set and, once the denominator shrinks, could
   produce >100%. Verify the relationship and clamp or drop out-of-set lines as part of this change.

## Size

Small — one Go collection+threading change plus tests, assuming decision 2 does not uncover a
numerator defect. If it does, split the numerator fix into a follow-up.

## Acceptance

- `shatter-go` populates `InstrumentableLineCount` on the analysis response.
- A Go unit test asserts the count excludes blank, comment-only, and brace-only lines for a fixture
  function.
- A new in-repo fixture under `examples/go/` (alongside the existing `configured-receiver`,
  `error-only-completion`, etc.) containing a function whose body always executes fully reports
  100% — verified by `cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go`.
- At least one Go E2E case asserts a fully-exercised function reports 100%.
- `task parity` and `task conformance` pass. `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` is updated only if this
  changes a declared capability status; a frontend filling in a field it already declares does not
  by itself require a matrix edit.
- Optional external confirmation (not a CI gate): re-measuring kapow's Go tier moves 14.5% ->
  ~23.0% with no change to `lines_covered` (3,863 covered; denominator 26,641 -> ~16,809). Recipe:
  `make shatter-clean && rm -rf ~/.config/shatter/go-workspace/analysis` then
  `bash scripts/shatter-source-set.sh explore --jobs 4` in the kapow repo, aggregating
  `lines_covered`/`total_lines` over `shatter-artifacts/files/*.json`.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Rust frontend emission of the same field — verify separately and file a sibling if it has the gap.
- Changing what counts as *covered* (the numerator).
- Regression-snapshot churn: this changes reported percentages, so checked-in snapshots will move.
  Updating them is in scope; re-baselining unrelated snapshots is not.

## Artifacts

`kapow/shatter-artifacts/files/api__internal__search__registry.go.json`
close_reason:
Landed on main at 651d7d369f66559dac1ceb7697a57349336e494e (merge commit; feature tip 66e217c3a8e6609dae5af26eacc4984ed4da6f84).

Gate evidence:
- go test -count=1 ./instrument/... -> ok
- go test -count=1 ./protocol/... -> ok (458.9s)
- task parity -> All golden checks passed; scripts/validate-parity.py --verbose -> Parity check passed
- task conformance -> 42/42 checks passed
- land-work-run-verifier.py on exact preview tree c371641b53b0e05f5beb1d803062b13e491862ee -> exit 0, 3 selected checks, all 8 changed paths covered
- land-work-verify-landing.py -> landed tree matches verified preview tree exactly

Independent code review confirmed the correctness of the line-dedup

shatter-go/CLAUDE.md were not updated for this protocol-visible change

before landing.

title: Async panic reported complete
description:
Observed while running `make shatter` in `/home/ketan/project/zolem` on 2026-05-12. During exploration of `internal/fixture/watcher.go::StartWatcher`, the target process printed a nil-pointer panic from a spawned goroutine:

`panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`
`zolem.dev/zolem/internal/fixture.watchLoop(... watcher.go:114 ...)`

Immediately afterward, Shatter wrote the `StartWatcher` artifact and emitted progress status `completed` for `StartWatcher`. The final report shows `StartWatcher` as completed with 92.86% coverage.

This is a correctness problem: asynchronous goroutine panics from explored executions should be captured as failures or at least surfaced as unsafe behavior, not classified as successful completion.
acceptance_criteria:
If an explored Go execution panics in any goroutine, the function result records a failure or explicit panic finding.
The progress stream and final report do not mark that function as completed/successful without surfacing the panic.
Add a Go frontend regression test where the function starts a goroutine that panics after return or shortly before return.

title: Rust 1.93 clippy breakage on shatter-core
description:
Rust 1.93.0 toolchain introduced new clippy lints that now error on shatter-core --all-targets:

- 17 errors: approximate_constants (f32/f64 PI literals in tests — should use std::f64::consts::PI)
- 1 error: overly_complex_bool_expr (test_runner.rs:699 — actual boolean logic simplification)
- 60 warnings (useless_vec, etc)

Files affected:
- shatter-core/src/export.rs (lines 968, 1085, 1179, 1188)
- shatter-core/src/float_probe.rs (line 329)
- shatter-core/src/mock_fixture.rs (lines 1002, 1008)
- shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs (line 2253)
- shatter-core/src/pipeline.rs (line 1493)
- shatter-core/src/protocol.rs (line 2364)
- shatter-core/src/shrink.rs (line 883)
- shatter-core/src/sym_expr.rs (line 197)
- shatter-core/src/test_arbitraries.rs (lines 60, 76)
- shatter-core/src/test_runner.rs (line 699, logic bug)
- shatter-core/src/triage.rs (lines 801, 805)

This is blocking merge-gate verification for multiple ready branches.

Acceptance:
- cargo clippy -p shatter-core --all-targets is clean
- All existing tests pass
- npx task test-standard is green on main

title: TS numeric schema accepts floats
description:
# Summary
TypeScript batch analysis fails before exploration when the frontend emits floating-point numeric literals such as `Number.MAX_VALUE` but the orchestrator schema expects `i64`.

## Protocol-Visible Behavior
- Does this change the wire format or semantics of any protocol message? yes
- If yes, which commands or fields are affected: TypeScript frontend numeric literal or value fields deserialized by the orchestrator
- Is this change backward-compatible? yes

## Parity Impact
- [ ] `buildSymExpr` (instrumentor.ts) — update `buildSymExprWithFlow` to handle the same node type
- [ ] `buildSymExprWithFlow` (instrumentor.ts) — update `buildSymExpr` to handle the same node type
- [x] Random explorer (`shatter-core/src/explorer.rs`) — verify concolic orchestrator (`orchestrator.rs`) gets the same change
- [x] Concolic orchestrator (`shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs`) — verify random explorer (`explorer.rs`) gets the same change
- [ ] CLI wiring in `main.rs` — verify both `--concolic` and default explorer paths receive the new config or flag

## Default Behavior
- Is new functionality enabled by default? yes
- If no, what flag or config option enables it:

## Required Test Updates
- [ ] Unit tests added or updated
- [ ] Property tests (proptest / fast-check / rapid) added for any new public function
- [ ] E2E concolic tests verified (`cargo test --test e2e_concolic`)
- [ ] Conformance tests verified (`npx task conformance`) — required if protocol-visible
- [ ] Walkthrough updated (`demo/walkthrough.sh`) if the compact demo narrative changes
- [ ] Gauntlet updated (`demo/gauntlet.sh`) or equivalent targeted coverage added for non-demo CLI changes

## Contract Updates
- Are runtime contracts (`#[requires]` / `#[ensures]`) needed? yes
- If yes, identify the trust boundary that justifies them (Z3 FFI / subprocess JSON / cross-collection index): subprocess JSON between TS frontend and Rust orchestrator
- Confirm all three qualifying criteria are met: trust boundary, type gap, silent corruption (see `shatter-core/CLAUDE.md`)

## Reproduction
- Scan a TS file that references `Number.MAX_VALUE`, such as lodash `src/toFinite.ts`.
- Observe: `invalid type: floating point ..., expected i64` during batch analysis.

## Acceptance
- The orchestrator accepts floating-point numeric values from the TS frontend.
- Previously failing files like `toFinite.ts` analyze successfully.
- Tests cover float-valued protocol payloads.

title: Build concolic orchestrator (single-function exploration loop)
description: Implement the core concolic loop in shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs: (1) generate initial inputs, (2) execute function via frontend, (3) collect branch decisions and symbolic constraints, (4) negate uncovered branch constraints, (5) solve for new inputs via Z3, (6) repeat until coverage plateau or budget exhausted. Uses a worklist of branch targets ordered by novelty. This is the heart of shatter's exploration engine.

title: Observe records path evidence
description:
# Observe records path evidence

**Type:** feature  **Priority:** 1  **Parent:** str-k2dny  **Depends on:** str-k2dny.3

## Problem and desired behavior

`str-k2dny.3` adds `path_evidence::collect_path_predicate_evidence(&PathPredicateBundle, &ObservationOutput, &PathPredicateTarget, &[ExecutionEvidenceMetadata]) -> Result<PathPredicateBundle, PathEvidenceCollectionError>`, but no production command calls it. Its metadata has `context_fingerprint: Option<String>` and `witness: Option<String>`. Add one opt-in path to the single-function `shatter observe` command: `--path-predicate-bundle BUNDLE.json --path-evidence-provenance PROVENANCE.json`. When both are supplied, read the existing bundle and a small provenance JSON file containing a `PathPredicateTarget` plus a nonempty `context_fingerprint`, run normal exploration, collect evidence from its actual `ObservationOutput`, and atomically write the updated bundle. Pass metadata with `context_fingerprint: Some(the supplied value)` and `witness: None` once per ordered raw result. Require both flags together through clap or an equivalent early validation. Without either flag, `observe` follows its existing path.

Example provenance file shape (the strings are user assertions, not generated values):

```json
{
  "target": {
    "qualified_function": "example.compare",
    "frontend": "typescript",
    "source_fingerprint": "source-v1"
  },
  "context_fingerprint": "context-v1"
}
```

The provenance file is an explicit operator assertion about the target source and execution context, not a fingerprint inferred by Shatter. Validate its shape and nonempty fields before spawning the frontend, then analyze the function. Require exact string equality between `target.qualified_function` and Analyze's `func.name` (no suffix normalization), plus exact selected frontend label; reject names whose Analyze form differs. Require at least one predicate in the bundle to have the exact supplied target. Read and validate the bundle before exploration; after successful exploration, collect into a new bundle, atomically write it, then emit the ordinary observation JSON. Any validation, exploration, collection, or write error returns nonzero; a collection or write error emits no success observation JSON and leaves the existing bundle unchanged. Do not claim that the CLI independently verifies `target.source_fingerprint` or the semantic correctness of the asserted context. Use the existing store's atomic write, but do not claim multi-process read-modify-write safety. Failure while emitting observation JSON after a successful bundle write is outside the bundle-unchanged guarantee.

## Current code facts

- `shatter-cli/src/commands/observe.rs::run_observe` analyzes exactly one `<file>:<function>`, runs either `orchestrator::explore` or `explorer::explore_function`, converts both paths to `ObservationOutput`, and then writes `ObserveStageOutput`. Both paths currently configure no mocks, execution profile, invocation plan, or setup file, which makes a single operator-supplied context assertion a narrow first integration.
- `shatter-cli/src/args.rs::CliCommand::Observe` holds the command options; `shatter-cli/src/main.rs` forwards them to `run_observe`. `run_observe` selects `func.name` from the Analyze response and `parsed.language.label()` supplies the frontend label (`typescript`, `go`, or `rust`). `Observe` already requires the normal `--allow-host-writes` gate for live execution. This is a three-file CLI wiring change plus focused tests.
- `shatter-core/src/explorer.rs::ObservationOutput.raw_results` is an ordered vector of `(inputs, mocks, ExecuteResult)`; it does not store a context fingerprint or stable witness identity. The concolic conversion preserves raw results. A path hash, tuple index, prepare ID, or artifact name is not a justified witness reference.
- `shatter-core/src/invariants.rs::PathPredicateTarget` comprises `qualified_function`, `frontend`, and `source_fingerprint`. `evaluate_path_predicate` requires exact context equality and exact full ordered branch-path equality, despite the `path_prefix` field name. No production code currently computes a path-predicate context fingerprint or source fingerprint.
- `shatter-core/src/path_predicate_store.rs::{read_path_predicate_bundle,write_path_predicate_bundle}` validate the bundle; writing replaces it atomically but the caller must serialize concurrent read-modify-write operations. `str-k2dny.3` supplies the collector and per-result metadata type.

## Scope and technical limits

Keep this to opt-in live `observe` collection for an already-authored bundle. The provenance JSON may use a small CLI-local deserializable struct with `target` and `context_fingerprint`; it is not a new protocol message or automatically generated identity. Do not infer predicates, create witness IDs, broaden to parallel multi-target `explore`/`scan`, change raw-result or wire schemas, or add replay/regression behavior. Since the assertion is caller supplied, document that the operator must use the same context/source identity as the predicate author and serialize updates to a shared bundle. A later child can establish verified per-execution provenance and automatic witness references.

## Acceptance checks

1. With a real TypeScript single-function `shatter observe` run in random and concolic modes (using the command's required `--allow-host-writes`), a matching preexisting bundle receives counts from its `raw_results`, remains readable after the atomic write, has no invented witness references, and the ordinary observe JSON emits. Run `task affected` and any selected E2E gate.
2. Paired-flag, malformed/empty provenance, exact Analyze-name/frontend mismatch, absent exact target, and collection/write failures return nonzero without changing the existing bundle; test a write failure with controlled I/O failure after a valid read. An opt-out run retains existing output. Unit checks cover frontend-label and Analyze-name comparisons beyond the TypeScript E2E fixture.
3. CLI help and a short usage example state that source/context are operator assertions, path matching uses the full ordered branch sequence, and callers must serialize shared-bundle writes. Run `/walkthrough-review` because this changes CLI help/output.
acceptance_criteria: Opt-in observe updates a matching existing bundle in both modes; invalid provenance and failed collection/write preserve the bundle; help explains operator assertions and serialized writes.

title: Path evidence from exploration
description:
# Path evidence from exploration

**Type:** feature  **Priority:** 1  **Parent:** str-k2dny

## Problem

`str-k2dny.1` defines path predicate evaluation and `.2` adds bounded evidence recording plus a standalone bundle, but a caller must manually construct every `PathObservation`. Exploration already retains ordered raw execution tuples, so a core-library collector should project them into evidence without claiming context or witness identity that the tuples do not contain.

## Desired behavior

Add `collect_path_predicate_evidence` in new `shatter-core/src/path_evidence.rs` (registered in `lib.rs`) with inputs `&PathPredicateBundle`, `&ObservationOutput`, `&PathPredicateTarget`, and `&[ExecutionEvidenceMetadata]`, returning `Result<PathPredicateBundle, PathEvidenceCollectionError>`. `ExecutionEvidenceMetadata` has `context_fingerprint: Option<String>` and `witness: Option<String>`, aligned by index to `raw_results`. The typed target is caller supplied; the collector never infers target or context from the output. `PathEvidenceCollectionError` distinguishes `InvalidBundle(PathPredicateStoreError)`, metadata length mismatch, empty witness, and recorder error (including counter overflow). Widen `path_predicate_store::validate_bundle` from private to `pub(crate)` for reuse. The supplied target is a filter, not separately validated: an empty target matches no valid predicate and is a no-op.

For each raw result, construct `PathObservation.inputs` from tuple element 0, project every `ExecuteResult.branch_path` in order to `(branch_id, taken)` without deduplication, and set the observation point to `Entry`. The existing evaluator requires exact equality against the full ordered path, even though the scope field is named `path_prefix`. Map `thrown_error: Some(_)` to `Thrown` even if a return value is also present; otherwise map `return_value: Some(value)` to `Return { value }` and `None` to `Unavailable`. Other execution fields, including truncation and connection failures, do not affect this mapping. `Some(Value::Null)` is an explicit typed return; ordinary serde may deserialize JSON null to `None`, which this collector treats as `Unavailable` and the evaluator counts as `MissingValue`. This issue makes no wire-level null distinction. Pass metadata context directly to the existing evaluator, which decides whether it matches the predicate scope. Call `.2`'s recorder once per raw result for every predicate whose target equals the supplied target. The recorder attaches witnesses only to holding or violating results. Zero matching predicates is a validated no-op; other targets remain unchanged. Prevalidate the bundle, metadata length, and all witness strings, then update a clone so any recorder error leaves the input bundle unchanged.

## Current code facts

- `shatter-core/src/explorer.rs` defines `ObservationOutput.raw_results` as ordered `(Vec<Value>, Vec<MockConfig>, ExecuteResult)` tuples. Those tuples do not retain setup context, execution profile, invocation plan, context fingerprint, or stable witness identity.
- `shatter-core/src/execution_record.rs` defines `BranchDecision` with `branch_id` and `taken`; the vector order retains repeated loop decisions.
- `shatter-core/src/protocol.rs` defines `ExecuteResult.return_value: Option<Value>` and `thrown_error: Option<ErrorInfo>`.
- `shatter-core/src/invariants.rs` defines `PathObservation`, `PathOutcome`, `PathPredicateTarget`, and `record_path_predicate_observation`, which validates and atomically updates one record.
- `shatter-core/src/path_predicate_store.rs` defines `PathPredicateBundle`, its version check/validation, and standalone read/write. The collector may reuse its validation but does not perform file I/O.
- `str-k2dny.1` and `str-k2dny.2` are closed and merged on `main`. This API consumes `explorer::ObservationOutput`; other raw-result holders are unchanged.

## Scope

Core-library collection API and focused tests only. Do not derive context from mocks or a path hash, change `ObservationOutput` or the protocol schema, wire the CLI, infer new predicates, alter lifecycle, or add replay/regression behavior. A later epic child must wire this API into a production entrypoint; this issue's result is a core-library capability.

## Acceptance checks

1. Given realistic raw tuples, matching target records count holds, violations, and inapplicable observations correctly; unrelated targets stay unchanged, repeated branch decisions preserve their order, and witness references route through the `.2` recorder.
2. Missing or mismatched context and ambiguous missing returns stay inapplicable via the existing evaluator; thrown errors take precedence over return values. Invalid bundle, metadata length, empty witness, and a failed recorder update report the specified error and leave the input bundle unchanged. Exercise overflow with a valid predicate whose eligible/holds counters are at `u32::MAX` (evidence is excluded from its ID).
3. The updated bundle passes the `.2` write/read round trip. A bounded proptest checks that each matching record's eligible plus not-applicable delta equals the raw result count, unrelated records remain identical, and a failed update preserves the input. Focused Rust tests and `task affected` pass; no protocol parity or E2E update is expected for a core-only API.
acceptance_criteria: Matching target evidence updates from ordered raw executions; caller metadata controls context and witnesses; errors preserve input bundle; round trip and Rust gates pass.
notes: Code review boundary: this child ships a core-library collector only; no production caller or E2E claim. Follow-up str-k2dny.4 (blocked by .3) wires shatter observe, validates Analyze name/frontend against operator-supplied target, supplies asserted context, and tests the real command. The collector intentionally trusts its caller to bind the qualified target to ObservationOutput (function_name may be unqualified), includes every raw result, ignores mocks/other ExecuteResult fields, and preserves lifecycle while updating evidence.

title: Path predicate evidence store
description:
# Path predicate evidence store

**Type:** feature  **Priority:** 1  **Parent:** str-k2dny

## Problem

`str-k2dny.1` landed a validated `PathPredicateRecord` and `evaluate_path_predicate`, but evaluation leaves evidence untouched and no file can preserve the record across runs. The epic's later measurement, replay, and regression work needs a durable record of eligible, holding, violating, and inapplicable observations without treating inapplicable results as proof.

## Desired behavior

A core-library caller can submit a validated v1 predicate, an already-formed `PathObservation`, and an optional opaque witness reference, then obtain an updated record and save/reload it in a separate versioned JSON bundle. The caller supplies context and witness references; this issue does not derive them from mocks, setup, profile, or execute plans.

## Current code facts

- `shatter-core/src/invariants.rs` defines `PathPredicateRecord`, `PredicateEvidence`, `evaluate_path_predicate`, `validate_path_predicate`, and `canonical_path_predicate_id`. Identity excludes `evidence` and `lifecycle`; evidence has `eligible`, `holds`, `violated`, `not_applicable`, and two witness string arrays. Validation requires `eligible == holds + violated`.
- `shatter-core/src/observation_aggregator.rs` preserves raw `(inputs, mocks, ExecuteResult)` tuples but does not retain a predicate context fingerprint or witness reference. Automatic aggregation belongs to a later child.
- `shatter-core/src/spec.rs` owns the existing `FileSpecBundle` wire format and uses a sibling temp file plus rename for writes. This issue uses a separate artifact to avoid changing the spec schema or CLI output.
- `shatter-core/Cargo.toml` already includes `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tempfile`, and `proptest`.

## Contract

- Expose `record_path_predicate_observation(record: &mut PathPredicateRecord, observation: &PathObservation, witness: Option<&str>) -> Result<PredicateEvaluation, PredicateEvidenceError>` in `invariants.rs`. Validate the starting record, evaluate exactly once, and increment exactly one result bucket. `holds` or `violated` also increments `eligible`; `not_applicable` increments only its own counter. Use checked arithmetic and return typed invalid-record, empty-witness, or overflow errors without mutation. Preserve `predicate_id` and `lifecycle`; all lifecycle states continue to accumulate evidence.
- Witness references are opaque strings, not raw inputs, mocks, outcomes, or secrets. Reject an empty supplied reference even for an inapplicable observation. A holding result routes its reference to `supporting_witnesses`; a violating result routes to `refuting_witnesses`; an inapplicable result ignores a nonempty reference. Deduplicate each list in insertion order. At the cap of 16, discard a new distinct reference while still counting the observation; keep the first 16.
- Add a public `PathPredicateBundle { schema_version: u32, predicates: Vec<PathPredicateRecord> }` in a new `shatter-core/src/path_predicate_store.rs`, exported from `lib.rs`, with wire shape `{ "schema_version": 1, "predicates": [...] }`. An empty array is valid. Read accepts unsorted records; write sorts by `predicate_id`. Both directions reject duplicate IDs, unknown bundle versions, bad IDs, inconsistent evidence, and witness lists with empties, duplicates, more than 16 entries, or more references than matching observations. Deserialization rejects malformed records and unknown envelope or nested fields; typed writes revalidate all records. Do not silently repair corrupt data.
- Expose `read_path_predicate_bundle(path: &Path) -> Result<PathPredicateBundle, PathPredicateStoreError>` and `write_path_predicate_bundle(path: &Path, bundle: &PathPredicateBundle) -> Result<(), PathPredicateStoreError>`. A missing file returns an I/O NotFound error; callers create an empty bundle explicitly. Write with a unique temporary sibling in the same directory and rename only after complete serialization and write. Create parent directories. A failed serialization, validation, or write leaves any existing destination unchanged; temp files are cleaned on failure. Atomicity means replacement visibility, not crash durability (`fsync` is out of scope). Use a private pre-persist failure seam for a deterministic test with an existing destination. Document that callers coordinate concurrent read-modify-write operations externally; no multi-writer merge is claimed by this issue. This intentionally uses a unique temp name unlike `spec.rs`'s fixed `.json.tmp` sibling.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit tests cover all three result buckets, exact counters, witness routing/dedup/cap, repeated observations, all lifecycle states, invalid starting records, and overflow without partial mutation (a valid record can set both `eligible` and `holds` to `u32::MAX`). A semantic property test checks the evidence arithmetic and `eligible == holds + violated` over bounded result sequences; add a focused generator because `test_arbitraries.rs` has no path predicate generator.
2. A bundle round-trip preserves records, evidence, lifecycle and canonical IDs in stable order. Reader and writer reject duplicate IDs, corrupt/unknown-version records, invalid witness lists, and unknown bundle versions; malformed input fails closed. Missing-file error, valid empty bundle, and unsorted-input normalization are covered.
3. An injected failure immediately before rename leaves the old artifact readable and unchanged and removes the temp file. A caller can load a bundle, apply another observation to its record, write it, and reload the accumulated evidence.

## In scope

Pure evidence accumulation and a standalone validated core-library artifact for path predicates.

## Out of scope

Inferring predicates, computing context or witness fingerprints, automatically collecting observations, changing `FunctionSpec`/CLI/protocol output, exploration feedback, shrinking, replay, regression artifacts, confidence or proof claims. The existing invariant-support issue `str-49drv.96` concerns the older function/class invariant format, not this predicate store.

## Verification

Run `cargo test -p shatter-core path_predicate`, `task affected` (record its selected gates), and the `check-rust` skill's Rust test/clippy quality gate. No protocol or frontend parity changes are expected.

title: Beads: find what the post-checkout hook waits on, list every JSONL-import entry point, and record one reproducible latency baseline
description:
## Problem

Maintainer decision D4 (2026-09-23) retires the beads JSONL import in shatter,
because the beads `post-checkout` hook stalls landings and new worktrees for
minutes. The decision is taken; this issue does not reopen it. But the
implementation issue (beads-retire-jsonl-import-dolt-remote) needs three facts
that the audit did not establish:

1. **What the hook is waiting on.** The measured runs use about 10 s of CPU
   over minutes of wall time, so the time is spent waiting. Low CPU does not
   say *what* is waited on: the JSONL import itself, a Dolt server start, a
   lock held by a sibling worktree's bd process, or the network (for example
   a Dolt remote fetch). Turning the import off only fixes the stall if the
   wait is inside the import path.
2. **Every place the import can run.** shatter has beads-managed
   `post-checkout` **and** `post-merge` hooks, and bd may also auto-import on
   ordinary commands when `import.auto` is true. A fix verified only on
   checkout could leave the other paths importing.
3. **One baseline.** The audit's numbers come from different runs and are not
   comparable (see Evidence). The implementation's latency targets need a
   baseline taken with a recorded command, binary and directory.

## Evidence (re-verified 2026-09-23)

The existing measurements, with their sources. They are separate runs, not
one contradictory run:

| Number | Command | Where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| about 6 min, about 10 s CPU | `bd -v hooks run post-checkout` (direct, no `timeout` wrapper) | not recorded | D4 text in `audits/2026-09-22.md` ("Maintainer decisions") |
| 2m59.7s | `time bd hooks run post-checkout` (direct) | a linked worktree | finding agent-repo-07 |
| 234.9-301.2 s | land.py `create_preview` (runs `git worktree add`, so the hook runs under `timeout 300`) | `/tmp/land-work-preview-*` | 11 landings 09-19..09-22, `drafts/shatter-agent/08-beads-hook-timeout-decision.md` |
| "timed out after 300s", 32 times | hook-wrapped runs | various | session transcripts (sessions-05) |

The hook-wrapped runs cannot exceed 300 s because of
`timeout "${BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT:-300}"`; the 6-minute figure is from a direct,
unwrapped run.

- Hooks present in `/home/ketan/project/shatter/.git/hooks/` (shared by all
  worktrees): `post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `pre-commit`,
  `prepare-commit-msg`, `pre-push`. `post-checkout` and `post-merge` both
  carry the `BEADS INTEGRATION v0.63.3` block that runs
  `timeout "$_bd_timeout" bd hooks run <hook> "$@"`.
- `bd version` → `1.1.0 (8e4e59d39)`; two binaries on PATH
  (`/usr/local/bin/bd`, `~/.local/bin/bd`).
- `bd config show`: `import.auto = true (default)`,
  `import.path = issues.jsonl (default)`, `export.auto = false`,
  `backup.git-push = true`, `no-hooks = false`.
- Preview and linked worktrees logged "post-checkout JSONL import warning: no
  Dolt remote configured" (sessions-05, transcript 19cbf3b5) even though the
  primary checkout lists a Dolt remote `origin`.
- Findings: sessions-05, agent-repo-07, prior-03.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Baseline table.** For each of (a) `bd hooks run post-checkout` direct,
      (b) `bd hooks run post-merge` direct, (c) `git worktree add <scratch>
      -b <scratch-branch> origin/main` (hook-wrapped), run in both the primary
      checkout and a linked worktree: the exact command, `command -v bd` and
      `bd version`, the working directory, the wall and CPU time (`/usr/bin/time
      -v` or `time`), and the JSONL record count. Attached to the close reason.
- [ ] **Wait attributed.** One traced run (for example `strace -f -tt -e
      trace=network,file,process,futex` or bd's debug logging) identifies where
      the wall time goes, as a breakdown that accounts for at least 80% of it
      (for example: "import loop N s, Dolt server start M s, lock wait K s").
      The trace excerpt is attached.
- [ ] **Import entry points listed.** From bd 1.1.0 source (file:line cited),
      every code path that reads `issues.jsonl` into the DB: which hooks, and
      whether ordinary `bd` commands auto-import when `import.auto` is true.
      For each, the setting that turns it off, and whether that setting is
      stored in a tracked file (`.beads/config.yaml`) or only in the local DB
      (so it would not reach a fresh clone).
- [ ] **Remote visibility explained.** Why linked and preview worktrees report
      "no Dolt remote configured" while the primary lists `origin` (for
      example: remote config stored per database directory), with the command
      output that shows it.
- [ ] **Conclusion stated.** One paragraph: does disabling the import remove
      the wait? If part of the wait is outside the import (for example Dolt
      server start), name it and its measured share, so the implementation
      issue can set its targets from data.
- [ ] No hook file is edited, no `BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT` is set, and no hook
      bypass is used for this work (D4).

## Suggested approach

Run in a scratch linked worktree so the primary checkout is not disturbed.
Take the trace on the direct `bd hooks run` form, which has no 300 s cap.

## Out of scope

- Changing any configuration or hook (beads-retire-jsonl-import-dolt-remote).
- The clobber scan (beads-jsonl-import-clobber-check).
- Any hook-timeout env var or hook-bypass guidance (D4).

title: Recover the deleted 2026-09-04 audit report (unreachable commit e067979d) and land it so the 50 open str-qwua7 children can read their evidence
description:
## Problem

The 2026-09-04 audit report and its evidence lived only on the local branch
`audit-2026-09-04`. That branch has since been deleted, and its commits are
unreachable. The str-qwua7 epic (62 children, 50 open) and other open issues
cite `audits/2026-09-04...` paths that do not exist on main. A fresh agent
cannot read the evidence for the audit's own follow-up work, and the commits
will be lost at the next `git gc` prune unless a ref holds them.

## Evidence (re-verified 2026-09-23 in /home/ketan/project/shatter)

- `git for-each-ref | grep -i audit` lists only `refs/heads/audit-2026-09-22`
  and `refs/remotes/origin/audit-kapow-2026-05-24`. `audit-2026-09-04` is gone
  (the 2026-09-22 audit findings still saw it: "102 behind / 7 ahead").
- `git cat-file -t e067979d` → `commit`, and no reflog entry holds it. The
  chain: `e067979d` (tip, 2026-09-07 "audit: 2026-09-04 record ids of decided
  issues"), `032c1319`, `a21108b2`, `ce8c1f04`, `e577d697`, `6eb87f9d`,
  `42c112cd` (2026-09-04 "audit: 2026-09-04"); parent 84941b37.
- `git ls-tree -r --name-only e067979d -- audits/2026-09-04 | wc -l` → **97**
  files (gates, triage-drafts, ui), plus `audits/2026-09-04.md`.
- Unreachable 2026-06-09 audit commits: `f9dad247` (latest, 2026-06-12),
  `a7a27ea3`, `f307ac3a`, `8b8bcc14`.
- str-qwua7.44 (open) says root `audits/` moves to `docs/audits/` only after
  the 09-04 branch lands at `audits/`.

## Acceptance criteria

## Out of scope

title: Beads: remove every `bd sync` instruction from docs and skills, and stop CI drift-patrol and branch cleanup from trusting the stale issues.jsonl
description:
## Problem

AGENTS.md and the repo skills require `bd sync`, but that command does not
exist in the installed bd 1.1.0. Two automated consumers still treat the
committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` as the truth, although it is a stale export
frozen at 2026-09-07:

- CI drift-patrol tracker-hygiene;
- `scripts/cleanup-merged-remote-branches.sh`, which reads its "in-progress,
  do not delete" set from it.

Maintainer decision D4 (2026-09-23) retires the JSONL import and makes a Dolt
remote the sync channel (beads-retire-jsonl-import-dolt-remote). This issue
brings the docs, skills and scripts in line with that decision.

**Ownership.** This issue owns the removal of **every** line-level `bd sync`
instruction, including the ones inside the AGENTS.md landing prose (`:125`)
and the "Beads Sync Cadence" section (`:345-369`). The broader rewrite of the
landing sections into a pointer to `bento:land-work` stays with str-qwua7.23
(see the qwua7-23-agents-md-rtk-and-landing note, which already assigns the
line-level removal here). No ordering between the two is needed: whichever
lands second rebases over the other.

## Evidence (re-verified 2026-09-23 in the audit-2026-09-22 worktree)

- `bd version` reports 1.1.0. `bd sync --help` fails with
  `Error: unknown command "sync" for "bd"`. bd warns that two binaries are on
  PATH (`/usr/local/bin/bd`, `~/.local/bin/bd`).
- `bd sync` instructions:
  - AGENTS.md:125 (landing step 5: "`bd sync` once here")
  - AGENTS.md:293 ("`bd sync` intentionally commits `.beads/*.jsonl`")
  - AGENTS.md:340 (commit-message convention `bd sync: close ...`)
  - AGENTS.md:345-369 (the whole "Beads Sync Cadence" section)
  - `.claude/skills/audit/SKILL.md:385` ("handled by `bd sync`")
- AGENTS.md:7 and :19 deliberately name nonexistent commands (`bd claim`,
  `bd assign --self`, `bd start`) to forbid them. Any command check must not
  flag these negative examples.
- `.beads/PRIME.md:8` gives a different procedure ("`bd dolt pull` →
  `git commit` → `git push`").
- `scripts/drift-patrol.py:188-221` falls back to the committed
  `.beads/issues.jsonl` when bd is not on PATH, which is the case in CI.
  `docs/DRIFT-PATROL.md:53-55` documents this.
- `scripts/cleanup-merged-remote-branches.sh`:
  - `:105-133` reads the in-progress set from the tracked JSONL, then
    (`:135-150`) optionally supplements it with a bulk
    `bd list --status in_progress`;
  - `:157-183` and `:244-273`: before each delete under `--execute`, a fresh
    per-branch `bd show <id>` re-check protects a branch whose issue is
    in_progress or assigned (fail closed); if bd is not on PATH this layer is
    skipped with a WARNING (`:249`);
  - `--skip-bd` (`:13-17`, `:52`) skips both the in-progress set and the
    per-branch re-check.
  - Tests: `scripts/test_cleanup_merged_remote_branches.sh`.
  AGENTS.md:274-277 documents the JSONL source. Concrete effect today: the
  JSONL lists str-rmcrl, str-vr7vq, str-0z1im, str-6vl7p and str-8q1b4 as
  `in_progress`, but all are closed in the live DB, so their merged remote
  branches (`origin/str-rmcrl-clippy-const-assert`,
  `origin/str-vr7vq-shatter-init-gitignore`,
  `origin/str-0z1im-negzero-roundtrip`,
  `origin/str-6vl7p-redundant-canonicalize`,
  `origin/str-8q1b4-resume-report-parity`) are still protected.
- JSONL vs live DB: 1,733 vs 1,778 issues and 20 status mismatches (details
  in beads-jsonl-import-clobber-check).
- `.beads/issues.recovered.jsonl` is tracked (1,201 lines) with no
  explanation; last touched by 29295bf7 (2026-05-24, "bd sync: hide jsonl
  export from auto import").
- Findings: prior-03 (P1), agent-repo-06 (the verifier set P2; D4 folds it
  into the P1 retirement), docs-16. Source draft:
  `drafts/shatter-agent/05-bd-sync-removed-jsonl-stale.md`; its "keep or
  untrack" decision is replaced by D4.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn "bd sync" AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md .beads/PRIME.md .claude/ docs/ scripts/`
      returns only (a) historical audit reports under `audits/` or
      `docs/audits/`, (b) changelog entries, and (c) mentions that explicitly
      say `bd sync` does not exist. The command and its output are in the
      close reason. Every former instruction links to the one sync procedure
      that beads-retire-jsonl-import-dolt-remote wrote into AGENTS.md;
      PRIME.md's session-close line matches it.
- [ ] The `bd sync: close <id>` commit convention and the "one `bd sync`
      commit per landing" cadence text are removed or replaced by the
      Dolt-remote equivalent.
- [ ] **Cleanup script** (`scripts/cleanup-merged-remote-branches.sh`):
      - The in-progress set comes from live bd after `bd dolt pull`; the
        tracked-JSONL read is removed.
      - `bd dolt pull` fails but local bd answers: dry-run lists candidates
        marked "unverified (pull failed)"; `--execute` deletes nothing and
        exits non-zero with the reason.
      - bd not on PATH or not answering: dry-run lists candidates as
        unverified; `--execute` deletes nothing and exits non-zero. It never
        falls back to the JSONL.
      - `--skip-bd` is kept only for dry-run; `--skip-bd --execute` is
        rejected with a usage error (maintainer may override this in the
        issue before work starts; record the choice).
      - The per-branch live `bd show` re-check before each delete is kept.
      - `scripts/test_cleanup_merged_remote_branches.sh` gains cases with a
        stubbed `bd` for: pull fails; bd missing; `--skip-bd --execute`
        rejected; and **a branch whose issue is claimed after the bulk list
        but before its delete is not deleted**. Each new case is shown
        failing on the pre-change script (paste the red run) and passing
        after.
- [ ] **Drift-patrol** (`scripts/drift-patrol.py`): tracker checks read live
      bd (after `bd dolt pull`) where bd is available. Where bd is absent (CI)
      they return the existing `SKIP` status with a reason, never a PASS/FAIL
      computed from the JSONL. `docs/DRIFT-PATROL.md:53-55` is updated.
      `scripts/test_drift_patrol.py` has a case with bd absent asserting SKIP.
      `python3 scripts/drift-patrol.py --only tracker-hygiene` output from a
      bd-less environment (for example `PATH` without bd) is in the close
      reason.
- [ ] **Recorded maintainer decision:** `.beads/issues.jsonl` stays tracked as
      a plain export (who refreshes it; documented as "not read by anything"),
      or it is untracked. The chosen state is applied.
- [ ] `.beads/issues.recovered.jsonl` is deleted, or AGENTS.md explains why it
      is kept.
- [ ] **bd command lint.** A check in `docs-smoke` (or a meta test) extracts
      `bd <subcommand>` invocations **only from fenced `bash`/`sh` code blocks
      and inline code spans that begin a command line** in AGENTS.md,
      PRIME.md and `.claude/skills/**`, and compares the subcommand against a
      checked-in list generated from `bd help` at bd 1.1.x (so CI needs no bd
      binary). Lines that name a command to forbid it are exempt via an
      explicit marker (for example `<!-- bd-lint: forbidden-example -->`) or
      because they are prose, not code. Tests: a fixture with `bd sync` in a
      code block fails; the AGENTS.md:7/:19 negative examples pass; a
      fixture using a real subcommand passes.
- [ ] AGENTS.md "bd Quick Reference" states the expected bd version (1.1.x)
      and which binary on PATH is canonical.
- [ ] `task affected` is green, with the `Gates selected` line in the close
      reason.

## Suggested approach

Doc rewrite in one commit; the cleanup script, drift-patrol change and bd
lint, each with its tests, in separate commits. Coordinate with
drift-patrol-workflow-go-mod (bucket shatter-ci-workflows), which fixes the
drift-patrol workflow that is the CI consumer.

## Out of scope

- Disabling the import and configuring the remote
  (beads-retire-jsonl-import-dolt-remote).
- bento's generic `beads-issue-flow` guidance (bento beads-dolt-remote-guidance).
- Replacing the AGENTS.md landing sections with a land-work pointer
  (str-qwua7.23). This issue removes only the `bd sync` lines in them.
- The audit skill's landing-order rewrite (str-qwua7.22; see
  qwua7-22-audit-land-before-file-note). This issue only removes the
  `bd sync` sentence at SKILL.md:385.
- Any hook-timeout env var or hook-bypass guidance (D4).

P1, task. Labels: agents, beads, docs, drift, audit-2026-09-22.

- Blocked by: beads-retire-jsonl-import-dolt-remote.
- Related: drift-patrol-workflow-go-mod, qwua7-23-agents-md-rtk-and-landing,
  qwua7-22-audit-land-before-file-note. Supersedes str-ly5bz (see
