title: Path predicate contract
description:
# Path predicate contract and fixture

**Type:** feature  **Priority:** 1

## Problem

Shatter currently detects a small set of invariants from execution records, but candidate checks are private closures and are not durable, path-scoped or context-aware. A later exploration or coding agent cannot reliably tell which behavior a relationship describes, and missing output can be mistaken for null.

## Desired behavior

Add a versioned, serializable path-level predicate contract and evaluator for one bounded family: scalar input equality and ordering at function entry. The evaluator returns `holds`, `violated`, or `not_applicable(reason)` and is usable by later persistence, exploration, shrinking and replay work.

## Current code facts

- `shatter-core/src/invariants.rs` defines `InvariantKind` and currently stores executable candidate checks as private closures; it has no general input/input comparison template.
- `shatter-core/src/observation_aggregator.rs` retains raw input, mock and `ExecuteResult` observations.
- `shatter-core/src/protocol.rs` defines `ExecuteResult`; its `branch_path` contains `BranchDecision` values from `shatter-core/src/execution_record.rs` with `(branch_id: u32, taken: bool)`.
- `shatter-core/src/spec.rs` is the existing specification serialization surface; this issue does not change it.

## Normative schema (version 1)

Define these Rust types in `shatter-core/src/invariants.rs`:

```text
PathPredicateRecord {
  schema_version: 1,
  predicate_id: String,
  target: { qualified_function, frontend, source_fingerprint },
  scope: { path_prefix: Vec<(u32,bool)>, observation_point: Entry,
           context_fingerprint: String },
  expression: Compare { op, left: InputPath, right: InputPath },
  semantics_version: "json-scalars-v1",
  lifecycle: Candidate | Frozen | Refuted | Stale,
  evidence: { eligible: u32, holds: u32, violated: u32,
              not_applicable: u32, supporting_witnesses: Vec<String>,
              refuting_witnesses: Vec<String> }
}
```

Concrete serde shapes are: `target` has three required strings; `scope.path_prefix` is an array of two-element `[u32,bool]` arrays; `scope.observation_point` is the string `"entry"`; `scope.context_fingerprint` is a required non-empty string. `expression` is `{ "kind":"compare", "op":"eq|ne|lt|le|gt|ge", "left":InputPath, "right":InputPath }`; `InputPath` is `{ "kind":"input_path", "parameter":u32, "path":[PathSegment] }`; `PathSegment` is `{ "kind":"field", "value":string }` or `{ "kind":"index", "value":u64 }`. `lifecycle` is a string enum and is read-only in this issue. `evidence` is optional read-only metadata with four nonnegative `u32` counts and two string arrays; it is excluded from identity.

`InputPath` contains a parameter index and tagged path segments: `{kind: Field, value: String}` or `{kind: Index, value: u64}`. Operators are `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge`. Version 1 accepts only finite numeric operands and performs no implicit string/number/null coercion. Integer values use exact integer comparison; finite floats use parsed IEEE-754 comparison. NaN, infinity, overflow and unsupported shapes fail closed.

`ObservationPoint` is a serde-tagged enum with the single wire value `"entry"`. `path_prefix` is the projection of `ExecuteResult.branch_path` to ordered `(branch_id: u32, taken: bool)` pairs; source line and symbolic constraint are deliberately excluded, and repeated loop decisions are retained in order. Applicability requires exact sequence equality, including length and order. `context_fingerprint` is an opaque, precomputed string supplied by the caller; this issue compares it but does not compute it. A later context-capture issue owns hashing mocks/setup/profile/execute-plan data. Secrets are never serialized.

`predicate_id` is lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of UTF-8 bytes of compact JSON produced by an explicit recursive object-key sort (using `BTreeMap` or equivalent), after removing `predicate_id`, `evidence` and `lifecycle`; `schema_version`, `semantics_version`, target and context remain in the hash. Tagged enum forms are serialized exactly as `{"kind":"compare","op":...,"left":...,"right":...}` and path segments as `{ "kind":"field"|"index", "value":... }`; the ordered path-prefix array is never sorted. Version-1 expressions contain no numeric constants, so canonical numeric edge cases are confined to observation values. Add a golden canonical input and expected digest. This issue does not mutate evidence counters or witness lists; evidence accumulation belongs to the persistence issue.

Applicability reasons are: `missing_value`, `explicit_null`, `wrong_type`, `thrown_outcome`, `scope_mismatch`, `unsupported_operation`, `unsupported_schema`, and `context_unavailable`. The exact result JSON is `{ "status":"holds" }`, `{ "status":"violated" }`, or `{ "status":"not_applicable", "reason":"..." }`. `eligible == holds + violated`; `not_applicable` is a separate non-eligible count and does not satisfy or refute a predicate.

Use serde tagged enums for `PathExpression`, `PathSegment`, `PredicateEvaluation` and `NotApplicableReason`; use snake_case wire names. `PathObservation` is `{inputs:[Value],branch_path:[[u32,bool]],observation_point:"entry",context_fingerprint:string|null,outcome:{kind:"return",value:Value}|{kind:"thrown"}|{kind:"unavailable"}}`. The return value is ignored by this input-only evaluator but retained for round-trip compatibility. Version 1 accepts only already-parsed JSON numbers represented as `i64` or finite `f64`; lexical `1` is integer, lexical `1.0` is float, and integer values above `i64::MAX` or non-finite/overflowing values are rejected as `unsupported_schema` during parsing. Both operands must have the same numeric category; mixed integer/float comparison is `not_applicable(unsupported_operation)`. Bools, strings, arrays and objects are `wrong_type`; explicit null is `explicit_null`. `thrown_outcome` is returned for `outcome=Thrown` after schema/context/path checks.

Evaluation precedence is strict: (1) schema/record validation; (2) observation-point validation; (3) if either predicate or observation context fingerprint is absent, return `context_unavailable`; (4) if fingerprints differ, return `context_unavailable`; (5) exact branch-path comparison, returning `scope_mismatch` on difference; (6) `Thrown` returns `thrown_outcome`, and `Unavailable` returns `missing_value`; (7) path resolution; (8) operand type/range validation; (9) comparison. Thus malformed schema wins over all other reasons, context wins over path, path wins over outcome, and outcome wins over operand resolution.

Expose `parse_path_predicate(raw: &str) -> Result<PathPredicateRecord, PredicateParseError>` and `validate_path_predicate(&PathPredicateRecord) -> Result<(), PredicateValidationError>`; unknown tags, malformed JSON, unsupported schema versions and structural violations are parse/validation errors classified as `unsupported_schema` before evaluation. Validation rejects empty target/context strings, parameter indexes outside an observation's inputs, invalid tagged segments, empty/unknown operators, invalid lifecycle strings, negative counts, and `eligible != holds + violated`. `evidence` may be omitted and defaults to zero counts/empty lists; null evidence is invalid. A predicate context is required in a validated record; only an observation context may be absent, which produces `context_unavailable`.

Expose:

```rust
evaluate_path_predicate(
    predicate: &PathPredicateRecord,
    observation: &PathObservation,
) -> PredicateEvaluation
```

Unknown schema versions and malformed records return `not_applicable(unsupported_schema)` rather than panic or silently pass.

## Fixture

Add frontend-independent JSON fixtures at `shatter-core/tests/fixtures/path_invariant/manifest.json` and synthetic `PathObservation` records. The manifest uses `{schema_version:1,cases:[{name,predicate,observation,expected}]}`. Branch paths encode as `[[0,true],[1,false]]`; a returned observation encodes `"outcome":{"kind":"return","value":null}` and a thrown observation encodes `"outcome":{"kind":"thrown"}`. Include exact observations for equality, inequality, ordering, matching context, absent context, mismatched context, missing, explicit null, wrong type, mixed numeric categories, out-of-range numeric value, thrown outcome, unavailable outcome, unsupported schema, and scope mismatch. Do not include replay-only return-change variants in this issue; later replay tests own them. No CLI, protocol, or TypeScript build is required here.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit tests construct records and assert the exact status/reason for every named reason, including precedence combinations and missing versus explicit null.
2. Canonical serialization is byte-stable; changing target, scope, expression, context or semantics changes `predicate_id`, while changing evidence/lifecycle does not. JSON round-trip preserves the record; unknown schema is unsupported.
3. A property-based test runs 1,000 deterministic cases comparing the evaluator with a simple reference evaluator over bounded scalar paths; malformed expressions fail closed. The fixture manifest covers every named observation and expected status/reason.

## In scope

Predicate types, evaluator, canonical IDs, applicability semantics, bounded evidence references, synthetic JSON fixtures and focused tests.

## Out of scope

CLI/report changes, protocol/frontend mirrors, collection or affine inference, solver translation, confidence/proof claims, mutation scheduling, shrinking integration, replay and regression artifact generation. Those consume this contract in later issues.

## Verification

Run `cargo test -p shatter-core invariants` and `cargo test -p shatter-core --test path_predicate_fixture` for focused tests, `task affected` for the changed core files, and the repository’s normal Rust quality gate before landing. New public functions require the semantic property tests described above under Shatter’s formal-methods policy. `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` remains unchanged because this issue has no protocol-visible type.
acceptance_criteria: Implement v1 typed scalar path predicates and exact applicability semantics; add canonical SHA-256 ID golden tests and JSON round-trip/unknown-schema tests; add the 1,000-case bounded property test and path_invariant manifest, then pass focused tests, task affected, and Rust quality gates.
notes: Post-creation cross-check correction: clarified evidence identity, parse/validate boundary, exact result shapes, numeric lexical semantics, ExecuteResult source, and canonical hash fields.
close_reason: df05fe3d9e319e90c8565ef45db1ed8793bd2199 landed and pushed to main; task affected exit 0 (smoke, core:clippy, core:test); cargo test -p shatter-core invariants exit 0; cargo test -p shatter-core --test path_predicate_fixture exit 0; exact merge-preview task check exit 0 via land-work verifier

title: Path-level invariant lifecycle
description: Make path-level inferred invariants useful across discovery, exploration, user/agent output, replay, and regression checks. The first child owns a bounded scalar predicate contract; later children add persistence, measurement, exploration feedback, replay, and durable regression artifacts. Inferred properties remain scoped evidence, not formal proof or automatic intent.

title: discover_configs walks up past shared system dirs (/tmp) with no boundary
description:
## Problem
shatter-core/src/config.rs::discover_configs_with_paths walks upward from start_dir toward filesystem root with no stopping boundary (no git-root detection, no home-dir/device boundary, nothing). On a shared multi-tenant machine, any process that runs `shatter init` (or triggers implicit init) with a relative or shared CWD like /tmp leaves a `.shatter/config.yaml` directly under /tmp. Every subsequent shatter invocation anywhere under /tmp -- including every unit test that uses tempfile::TempDir (which creates dirs directly under /tmp) -- silently picks up that stray global config as an extra, unwanted discovered config.

## Evidence
Hit directly while landing str-qwua7.9: `task test-standard` failed on main itself (pre-existing, unrelated to the branch being landed) with:
- config::tests::discover_configs_empty_when_no_shatter_dirs: assertion failed: configs.is_empty()
- config::tests::discover_configs_finds_nearest_first: left: 3, right: 2
- config::tests::hierarchical_merge_integration: left: 3, right: 2

Root cause: a stray `/tmp/.shatter/config.yaml` (freshly created that day, boilerplate `shatter init` output, uid=ketan) leaked by some other concurrent session's shatter invocation with CWD=/tmp or similar. Removed it to unblock landing; it will recur under concurrent multi-agent use of this machine until the walk-up has a real boundary.

## Fix
Bound discover_configs's upward walk so it cannot escape into shared system directories. Candidate boundaries (pick one, document the choice): stop at the nearest .git repository root; stop at $HOME; stop at a filesystem device/mount boundary (st_dev changes); or some combination. Whatever is chosen, add a regression test that plants a `.shatter/config.yaml` above the boundary and confirms discovery does not cross it.

## Acceptance
- discover_configs has a documented, tested upper boundary that does not depend on the absence of stray global state.
- A new test proves a `.shatter/config.yaml` placed above the chosen boundary (e.g. directly under a tempdir standing in for /tmp) is NOT picked up.
- Existing discover_configs tests remain green regardless of what happens to exist above the test's own TempDir on the host machine.
acceptance_criteria: discover_configs's upward walk has a documented, tested boundary; a new regression test proves a config above that boundary is not picked up; existing tests are immune to stray global .shatter state on the host.

title: HTML scan reports omit attempted failures
description:
## Problem
A scan that attempts one function and fails its harness renders HTML as Functions 0 / Paths Found 0 / Coverage 0% / Skipped 0, with no failed-function identity or diagnostic. The same report's JSON and Markdown retain the failure. Mixed scans silently omit failures too.

## Current code facts
- shatter-core/src/report.rs: CodebaseReport contains attempted_functions, completed_functions, failed_functions and failed: Vec<FailedFunctionReport>. FailedFunctionReport already carries function_name, display_name, qualified_id, file_path, reason and optional language/status/error_type/error_message/failed_at.
- shatter-core/src/html_templates.rs: ScanReportTemplate/render_scan_report has completed results and skipped rows but never projects codebase.failed. The skipped field's comment incorrectly claims attempted failures are included.
- shatter-core/templates/scan_report.html shows only completed count under "Functions", paths, coverage and skips.
- The existing Skipped card equals skipped_functions.len(): expected + unsupported + interrupted. The per-row skipped list excludes category "interrupted"; those entries instead produce the existing Not Attempted note. Preserve this contract, including the inclusive card count.

## Smallest regression fixture
Construct ScanReport { functions: [], codebase: CodebaseReport { attempted_functions: 1, completed_functions: 0, failed_functions: 1, total_discovered_functions: 1, failed: [failure], ..Default::default() }, ... }. Use FailedFunctionReport for checkout in src/checkout.ts, qualified_id src/checkout.ts::checkout, reason "build error: AUDIT_FIXTURE_BUILD_FAILURE <missing & module>", error_type build_error, failed_at frontend. Render using report::generate_html_scan_report(&report, None) and report::format_markdown_report(&report).

At reviewed HEAD e50fc399f328711cbbe237c1e3918e96c1080656, a rebuilt core-library probe (Cargo fresh=false) printed HTML marker present: false; Markdown marker present: true; HTML failed-function identity present: false. This is synthetic renderer evidence, not a new downstream scan failure. Supplementary source/JSON/HTML/Markdown/raw log and screenshots: /tmp/shatter-followup-ui-RBR75s/; the fixture above is sufficient without those files.

## Requested outcome
Expose existing attempted/completed/failed counts; label the current Functions count unambiguously as Completed. Add a distinct failed-functions section with display name (existing function_name fallback), source path when available, diagnostic, and optional stage/category. Fall back to reason when structured metadata is absent. Escape source/error text. Preserve completed details and the current skipped/interrupted distinction and inclusive Skipped card.

## Scope and related work
HTML view model, scan template and focused renderer tests; about two production files plus tests. No JSON schema, frontend protocol, execution, coverage denominator, CLI-exit, source-highlight or VS Code changes. HTML/Markdown/JSON must agree on existing failure facts; no TS/Go/Rust handler changes or conformance expansion.

Live tracker checked 2026-09-13: closed str-jeen.46 introduced counts with JSON/Markdown acceptance; closed str-4mmd populated metadata; closed str-jjt2h addressed never-attempted budgeting. None implements this HTML projection. Preserve their semantics.

Evidence-location note: /tmp paths above are ephemeral, session-local breadcrumbs and may no longer exist. They are not prerequisites; use the inline reproduction and repository entrypoints.

## Acceptance checks

1. Failed-only fixture visibly shows attempted 1, completed 0, failed 1, function identity and diagnostic; it is not presented as an empty or merely skipped run.
2. Mixed fixture with two completed, one failed, one expected skip and one interrupted entry preserves both completed results; shows failure separately; shows Skipped 2, one benign skipped row, and Not Attempted 1. Missing optional failure fields fall back correctly; unsafe text is escaped; no-failure input has no phantom rows.
3. Focused tests compare the existing failure counts/identities/diagnostics with the same report's JSON/Markdown; visually inspect generated failed-only and mixed pages. Run the repo's selected Rust gates.

Audit reference: shatter-review-2026-09-13/UI-1

Mixed fixture with two completed, one failed, one expected skip and one interrupted entry preserves both completed results; shows failure separately; shows Skipped 2, one benign skipped row, and Not Attempted 1. Missing optional failure fields fall back correctly; unsafe text is escaped; no-failure input has no phantom rows.
Focused tests compare the existing failure counts/identities/diagnostics with the same report's JSON/Markdown; visually inspect generated failed-only and mixed pages. Run the repo's selected Rust gates.

title: Staged private keys lack a commit guard
description:
Problem: five distinct complete unencrypted Ed25519 keys entered reachable history in b64f40a2a62404886f5af580b3cd7dd7e0356d7c and were deleted in be2d935d8802cc2c38c62e687f6d93924caacf89 on 2026-03-13. Deletion did not remove Git objects. This is prevention, not a claim of active compromise.

Current code: .gitignore already excludes .agentsea/ and .codex/. scripts/setup-hooks.sh's managed precommit section calls scripts/precommit-rust.sh but no staged private-key detector. Taskfile.yml meta has optional Semgrep/repository checks, no private-key check. Ignore rules alone cannot reject git add -f or key files at ordinary paths.

Requested change: add a small redacting, dependency-light staged-blob guard to the existing precommit installation. Reject complete line-delimited OpenSSH/PEM private-key blocks (RSA, EC, generic/encrypted PRIVATE KEY variants), regardless of extension. Inspect index blobs, not only working-tree contents. Emit path/type only, never matching lines or key bytes. Git/blob read errors fail closed. Preserve existing Beads/quality sections and existing ignores. Wire synthetic test execution into task meta.

Smallest regression: temporary Git repo; stage synthetic noncredential BEGIN/body/END private-key text, force-stage it under .agentsea/ssh/deploy_key, then stage another at an ordinary path. Stub the Rust checker to succeed and run the installed hook. The current template lacks key-specific rejection. Also replace a staged-key working file with clean content; the staged key must still be rejected. Public ssh-ed25519 lines, unstaged-only blocks and a documentation sentence mentioning key types are controls.

Scope: one staged-content prevention behavior (checker, hook wiring, synthetic tests, existing meta registration). No general credential platform, operator credential-store access, real-key fixtures/authentication, key rotation, history rewrite or deletion. No matching issue found in checked export. Public identification is preserved in /tmp/shatter-key-identification-2026-09-10.md, but no private material is needed here.

Tracker dedup refreshed against the 1736-issue live bd snapshot captured 2026-09-13 (/tmp/shatter-backlog-str-live-20260913.json), reading relevant descriptions and statuses including the str-qwua7 audit children. Source checked in the working checkout; prior synthetic-renderer evidence is explicitly dated 2026-09-10/11 and does not assert a new full test run.
Resolved hook/test entrypoints: scripts/setup-hooks.sh defines PRE_COMMIT_BODY and preserves Beads hook text using BEGIN/END SHATTER QUALITY markers plus a template version. scripts/test_setup_hooks.sh already creates a mktemp Git repo, copies the installer, checks idempotent installation, and stubs commands for invocation tests; task meta runs that script. Extend those fixtures for the index guard. scripts/precommit-rust.sh currently enumerates names with newline-delimited git diff --cached and suppresses Git errors; do not copy that behavior into the security guard. Use NUL-delimited index/name records and blob object IDs so newline/space/leading-dash filenames are handled without shell interpolation, and test at least a newline-containing synthetic path. Detection is format-based prevention, not proof of key validity or exhaustive secret detection.

Evidence-location note: /tmp paths above are ephemeral, session-local breadcrumbs and may no longer exist. They are not prerequisites; use the inline reproduction and repository entrypoints.

## Acceptance checks

1. Installed precommit rejects synthetic staged full private-key blocks, force-added ignored paths and staged-key/clean-working-file mismatch; diagnostics never include the synthetic body.
2. Public-key-only and unstaged-only controls pass; Git/blob read failure returns nonzero; tests never read real credentials.
3. setup-hooks stays idempotent and preserves existing Beads/quality behavior; synthetic guard tests run through task meta.

Audit reference: shatter-review-2026-09-13/staged_private_key_guard
acceptance_criteria:
Installed precommit rejects synthetic staged full private-key blocks, force-added ignored paths and staged-key/clean-working-file mismatch; diagnostics never include the synthetic body.
Public-key-only and unstaged-only controls pass; Git/blob read failure returns nonzero; tests never read real credentials.
setup-hooks stays idempotent and preserves existing Beads/quality behavior; synthetic guard tests run through task meta.

title: Unicode return values panic in spec builder
description:
A valid Unicode return value can panic during specification construction, before a caller chooses a final output format.

Current code facts: shatter-core/src/spec.rs format_value_short (1018-1024) serializes JSON and slices &s[..37] whenever s.len()>40. build_spec_class calls format_class_label, which calls this helper for returns. The helper also formats precondition values, examples and global-state displays within spec.rs.

Self-contained reproduction: let value = serde_json::json!(format!("{}é{}", "a".repeat(35), "b".repeat(10))); let s=value.to_string(); assert_eq!(s.len(),49); assert!(!s.is_char_boundary(37)); format_value_short(&value) panics. For the user-facing path, place value in an ExecuteResult.return_value with one input and branch decision; pass group_into_classes(raw_results) plus ObservationOutput {raw_results,..Default::default()} and TypeInfo::Str to build_spec. The recorded backtrace is format_value_short -> format_class_label -> build_spec_class -> build_spec. A fresh core build reproduced it on 2026-09-11; source reread unchanged on 2026-09-12. Optional raw source/log: /tmp/shatter-followup-numeric-f2LZz8/probe.rs and probe.stderr.log.

Requested change: truncate the serialized preview only on a valid UTF-8 boundary. Preserve the existing 40-byte display budget including the three-byte ASCII ellipsis by selecting the greatest character boundary at or before byte 37. This explicit byte-budget choice avoids requiring grapheme/display-width redesign in this bug. Never alter the underlying JSON return value or stored input/output example.

Scope/size: spec.rs helper plus direct/full-builder tests. Other modules with similar slicing are follow-up leads, not hidden scope here. title: Spec diff drops noncanonical observed outcomes
description:
Spec-diff misses an output change that both runs already observed because spec construction preserves only one representative outcome per path. This is loss of collected evidence, not a demand for exhaustive sampling or all possible return values.

Current code facts: equivalence.rs ClassMember contains input/return/error but build_class (154-174) emits all_inputs plus only canonical_return_value/canonical_thrown_error. spec.rs build_spec_class emits one ConcreteExample. build_spec receives ObservationOutput.raw_results tuples of inputs, Vec<MockConfig>, and ExecuteResult. spec_diff.rs:98-114 compares representative postconditions only.

Self-contained library reproduction: construct ExecuteResult records with branch_path=[BranchDecision { branch_id:1,line:1,taken:true,constraint:Default::default(),conditions:None }], lines_executed=[1], tuple mocks=[], inputs=[n], and return_value as follows. Baseline records: (1 -> 1), (2 -> 2). Candidate records: (1 -> 1), (2 -> 4). Call group_into_classes(records), make ObservationOutput { function_name:"f",iterations:2,unique_paths:1,lines_covered:1,total_lines:1,raw_results:records,..Default::default() }, then build_spec(...,&TypeInfo::Int {int_width:None,int_signed:None}). Both choose 1 -> 1; diff_specs().is_empty()==true and has_regressions()==false despite both observing input 2.

Requested artifact change: add defaulted comparison_witnesses: Vec<SpecComparisonWitness> to FunctionSpec. Each witness preserves inputs, supplied mocks, branch_path, return_value, thrown_error and the recorded context needed to reject known-incomparable observations: ExecuteResult.side_effects, calls_to_external, and capture_truncation. Keep every observation (including repeated/conflicting outcomes); this field is evidence, not a set of all possible returns. Do not copy unrelated performance counters or overwrite the human-facing canonical example. Existing JSON artifact readers must accept the missing field as legacy evidence.

Resolved state/context facts: ExecuteResult (protocol.rs:1130) has no complete initial-state snapshot. Its side_effects can contain GlobalStateChange { variable,before,after } and EnvironmentRead { variable,value } (execution_record.rs:117-138); calls_to_external records observed dependency calls. Scope/loop-body events are execution traces, not an initial global-state snapshot. MockConfig includes cycling return_values and default_behavior (ReturnGenerated, RepeatLast, ThrowError, Passthrough), but not a general persisted mock cursor. Therefore equal inputs/mocks cannot prove equal ambient state or determinism.

Bounded comparison policy (decision made for this ticket):
- First select a key of matching branch path + structurally equal input vector + supplied mock vector. JSON object key order is irrelevant; array and mock-vector order remains meaningful. For each record, its recorded-context signature is the first GlobalStateChange.before per variable (ordered by variable name), plus the ordered EnvironmentRead observations and ordered calls_to_external (symbol/args/return_value). Require exactly one distinct context signature on each side and equality of those two signatures; differing/multiple contexts produce recorded_context_differs, not a target-code regression. A missing side of recorded state, opaque GlobalMutation without before values, or was_truncated capture produces incomplete_recorded_context. Preserve recorded context in the artifact even where this first comparison version cannot use it. Both sides having empty captured context is allowed only under the explicit unrecorded-state limitation below, not called proof of a stateless target.
- For a matching recorded context, partition all observations on EACH side into distinct outcomes after the existing nondeterminism-aware return comparison. A key can yield a changed-witness regression only when each side has exactly one distinct observed outcome and the two outcomes differ. If either side has multiple distinct outcomes, emit ambiguous_observed_outcomes as inconclusive, regardless of set overlap. Do not choose first/last, compare the Cartesian product, or discard conflicting evidence. Duplicates and record reordering cannot change the comparison classification.
- Make evidence limits explicit: comparisons are conditional on recorded context; no complete initial-state snapshot, unknown environment, unrecorded mock cursor, live services or nondeterminism are proven equal. A singleton observed outcome is not proof of determinism. Unsupported/unrecorded state remains a stated evidence limit, not an inferred universal behavioral contract.

Nondeterminism lookup resolved: spec_diff.rs::postconditions_equal_ignoring_nondeterminism unions both specs' masks, ignores whole return or selected return.<path> fields for Returns, and ordinarily compares Throws/ReturnsVoid. Reuse that outcome semantics; whole-return-masked witnesses carry no evidence of a return-value change. Retained error comparison follows the existing Postcondition::Throws representation rather than introducing a new stack-normalization contract.

Additive reporting contract: retain existing SpecDiff fields, and add defaulted changed_witnesses (input/context plus old/new outcome) and inconclusive_witnesses (input/context plus a closed reason such as missing_comparable_witness, recorded_context_differs, incomplete_recorded_context, ambiguous_observed_outcomes). has_regressions includes definite changed_witnesses, not inconclusive entries; JSON and text expose the same distinction. A diff containing only inconclusive entries must not say the specs are behaviorally equivalent or report a confirmed regression. Coordinate reuse of the canonical insufficient-evidence note with CORE-4 instead of creating divergent statuses. No mandated CLI exit-code redesign.

Repeated-outcome acceptance control (a proposed new regression, not a previously run failure): baseline same input [2], mocks=[], path=[(1,true)] has returns [2,4]; candidate has the same records reversed [4,2]. Both retain both observations; result is ambiguous_observed_outcomes, no changed-witness regression, and order-independent. Also cover one side conflicting versus a singleton side. The original singleton-per-key input-2 mismatch still reports a changed witness.

Scope/size: one end-to-end observed-witness comparison behavior, primarily spec.rs/spec_diff.rs plus tests and mechanical artifact fixtures. No replay subsystem, new target scans, exhaustive-output inference, branch-renumbering algorithm, or full ambient-state model. Keep canonical display concise. Old specs with no comparison_witnesses use only their available canonical evidence and report limited evidence, without manufacturing missing outcomes.

Protocol-visible behavior: frontend message shapes unchanged; FunctionSpec/SpecDiff artifacts gain defaulted evidence/status fields. Default: retain collected comparison evidence. Parity: text/JSON identify the same changed input and inconclusive reason. Tests: group->build->serialize/deserialize->diff; record-order/duplicate/conflict controls; mismatched/incomplete context controls and nondeterminism masks. Contracts: none required.

Open str-qwua7.38 addresses unmatched classes after path renumbering, not noncanonical outcome retention on an identical path. Closed str-wfqh fixes bundle parsing, str-nq20 adds a separate comparison/replay surface, and str-su5o.6 supplies masks to preserve. Open str-0m0vn seeding cannot recover discarded outcomes. No direct duplicate; file new and coordinate overlapping comparison files.

Land its canonical comparability guard and explicit insufficient-evidence reporting first, then reuse that result vocabulary for retained witnesses and legacy fallback. The tracker dependency will name the filed issue ID; do not independently invent a second canonical comparison status.

Conflicting outcomes, mismatched/incomplete recorded context, and missing comparable evidence are explicitly inconclusive; duplicate/reordered records do not change classification.

notes:
Follow-on refinement ideas (2026-09-21, from str-nfg4y landing analysis) -- additive to the bounded comparison policy above, not a change to it:

1. Residual gap: this issue's matching only helps when both sides' retained observation sets actually overlap on a comparable key. If two independently-explored runs never sample the same (branch_path, inputs, mocks) key at all (small budget, narrow domain, unlucky RNG on both sides), the result is still inconclusive -- there is nothing to match. Real closure of this gap requires not relying on two independently-sampled specs: consider a spec-diff mode that, when a class has no comparable witness, falls back to re-executing the OLD spec's recorded canonical input against the NEW source (the same mechanism `shatter revalidate` already uses to detect drift from cached behaviors), producing a directly comparable result instead of an inconclusive note. This changes spec-diff's input contract from "two spec JSON files" to "one spec JSON plus access to the new code/frontend" for this fallback path only -- a real scope question, not a drop-in change, and likely its own follow-up issue rather than folded into this one's already-decided bounded comparison policy.

2. Retention-bound mitigation: whatever cap is chosen for comparison_witnesses' size per class, prefer retaining the deterministic Z3-solved witness (see str-cl330, once available) as the FIRST retained witness rather than an arbitrary/random one. Two runs of unchanged code would then retain the identical witness deterministically, raising cross-run match rate even under a tight retention bound, without needing to retain every observation. Depends on str-cl330 landing first (or independently reimplementing just the deterministic-witness selection for retention purposes).

3. str-mfmmr's lost_properties fix should consume whatever matched-witness data this issue produces, rather than re-deriving its own separate canonical-input matching -- avoids the two aggregate/pairwise mechanisms drifting out of sync on what counts as "comparable."

title: Float constants lose precision before solving
description:
Finite floating-point constants are rounded to millionths before Z3 sees them, changing predicates and emitting incorrect witnesses.

Current code facts: shatter-core/src/solver.rs:514-516 computes (*v * 1_000_000.0).round() as i64 and constructs Real::from_rational(scaled,1_000_000). extract_concrete_values converts model rationals back to f64. This is solver encoding, not display formatting.

Reproduction (a unit test in shatter-core/src/solver.rs; notation expands directly to existing public types): x = SymExpr::Param { name: "x", path: [] }; I(n) = SymExpr::Const(ConstValue::Int(n)); F(n) = SymExpr::Const(ConstValue::Float(n)); B(op,a,b) = SymExpr::BinOp { op, left: Box::new(a), right: Box::new(b) }. Call solve_constraints(&constraints, Some(5000), &[ParamInfo { name: "x".into(), typ, type_name: None }]). This is a direct library reproduction, not a new frontend execution. On 2026-09-11 a fresh rebuild of current core at audited HEAD e50fc399f328711cbbe237c1e3918e96c1080656 produced the actual results below. Source was reread on 2026-09-12 and still contains the encoding. Optional original evidence: /tmp/shatter-followup-numeric-f2LZz8/probe.rs and probe.stdout.log; all necessary assertions are inline here.

typ=TypeInfo::Float; constraints=[B(Eq,x,F(0.0000001))]. Expected SAT with x equal to the supplied f64 constant. Actual SAT x=0.0; native assertion model["x"] == ConcreteValue::Float(0.0000001) is false.

Requested change: encode each supported finite f64 constant without fixed decimal quantization or saturating i64 scale casts. The bounded numeric contract for this fix is to preserve the supplied finite f64 value in the real-valued encoding (e.g. its exact binary rational), and round a returned model only when producing the required f64 witness. If a value cannot be represented/extracted faithfully by the supported path, return an explicit unsupported/error result instead of a silently changed equality witness. Do not claim that real arithmetic thereby implements IEEE-754 operations, infinities, NaNs, or overflow; those are out of scope.

Scope/size: constant conversion/extraction and solver semantic tests. System prevention: include small nonzero magnitudes and sign symmetry in the constant/model equality corpus, not only whole-number literals.

Protocol-visible behavior: no frontend JSON shape change; corrected core semantics affect solver consumers using the existing SymExpr/ParamInfo contract. Parity: shared core conversion must apply to direct solve_constraints, solve_for_new_path, and solve_for_mcdc_independence; do not repair only one caller. Default: corrected existing behavior, no opt-in flag. Required tests: The tiny-value reproduction; positive/negative finite constants around and below 1e-6; a bounded finite-f64 identity-equality property that checks the returned candidate or explicit unsupported outcome. Use existing shared semantic generators where suitable; run repository-selected Rust gates and the applicable concolic integration task through its normal wrapper. Contracts: no new contract required for this fix; existing Z3-boundary/type checks must remain valid. 

Resolved implementation lookups: SolverError::Unsupported(String) is the existing explicit unsupported mechanism (solver.rs:19); Real::from_rational is used at constant construction, and extract_concrete_values first uses as_rational then attempts f64 string parsing. No new result enum is needed for an explicit error. The tiny 1e-7 identity case must succeed with that value; blanket unsupported for it is not an acceptable fix.

Live duplicate check: searched the 1,736-issue Shatter snapshot obtained with bd on 2026-09-12 (/tmp/shatter-backlog-str-live-20260912.json); searched titles/descriptions and read relevant matching issue bodies. No direct open duplicate. Closed str-weo completed expression translation and str-r6fr added type/shape tests; neither specifies finite-constant quantization correctness.

Evidence-location note: /tmp paths above are ephemeral, session-local breadcrumbs and may no longer exist. They are not prerequisites; use the inline reproduction and repository entrypoints.

## Acceptance checks

1. x == 1e-7 no longer emits zero; supported identity equalities yield a witness equal to the supplied finite constant.
2. Tests cover signs and sub-micro magnitudes, prevent fixed-scale overflow/quantization, and require explicit unsupported/error for values the encoder/extractor cannot faithfully handle.
3. The documented real-constant contract explicitly distinguishes literal fidelity from full IEEE-754 operation semantics, with no frontend wire change.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
**Audit 2026-09-22 (finding core-19, corrected by cross-check): the affected range is much larger than "precision beyond six decimals".**

**1. Constants with magnitude above 2147.483647 are corrupted, not only rounded.** The pinned `z3` crate is 0.19.10 (`Cargo.lock`). Its `Real::from_rational(num: i64, den: i64)` passes `num as c_int` and `den as c_int` to `Z3_mk_real` (`z3-0.19.10/src/ast/real.rs:63-75`). The caller scales by 1e6 first, so the numerator overflows a 32-bit int once `|v| > 2147.483647`, and the `as` cast wraps silently. Example: `3000.0` becomes `3_000_000_000 as i32 = -1_294_967_296`, which Z3 reads as **-1294.967296**. A branch `if x > 3000.0` is therefore solved as `x > -1294.97`. Above about 9.2e12 the earlier `f64 as i64` cast also saturates, and `i64::MAX as i32` is `-1`, so every such constant becomes -0.000001. This was verified from source; the runtime was not re-run for this note.

Thresholds such as 5000.0, 86400.0 or 1e6 are common in real code, so this is a wrong-answer bug in the core solver on ordinary inputs, of the same class as str-t854z (P1). **Proposed priority: P1.**

**2. Test for exact rational equality, not f64 round-trip.** A shortest-round-trip decimal string does not meet this issue's contract. Binary f64 `0.1` is exactly `3602879701896397 / 36028797018963968`, while the decimal `"0.1"` is `1/10`. Both round-trip to the same f64, so a round-trip assertion would pass an inexact encoding. Required tests:
- A unit test on the constant translation: for each value in a fixed corpus (`0.1`, `2147.483648`, `3000.0`, `-3000.0`, `1e13`, `1e-7`, `5e-324`, `f64::MAX`), the Z3 numeral equals the exact binary rational from `f64::integer_decode`, compared as big integers (numerator and denominator strings from Z3 against the expected ones). Build the numeral with `Real::from_rational_str` (present in z3 0.19.10, `real.rs:25`) or `Real::from_big_rational`, not `from_rational`.
- A bounded proptest over finite f64 values with the same exact-equality assertion.
- A regression test on current `main`: `x: Float`, constraint `x > 3000.0` (and `x < -3000.0`) must produce a model that satisfies the original f64 comparison. It must fail before the fix and pass after it, with both outputs quoted in the close note.

**3. Model extraction must be fixed with the translation, or the new tests cannot pass.** Exact rationals for tiny or very large values have numerators and denominators beyond `i64`. `extract_concrete_values` (`solver.rs:1036-1045`) first calls `as_rational()`, which uses `Z3_get_numeral_small` and returns `None` outside `i64`. It then tries `val.to_string().parse::<f64>()`. Z3 prints such a numeral as an s-expression like `(/ 1.0 10000000.0)`, so the parse fails and the variable is left out of the model without any error. The fix must convert big rationals to the nearest f64 (for example through the numeral's decimal or rational string), or return `SolverError::Unsupported`. It must never drop the assignment. str-aureo already puts extraction in scope; this adds the concrete failure mode. Separate the tests: translation tests (point 2) check the Z3 numeral, and model round-trip tests check the extracted `ConcreteValue`.

**4. NaN and infinities** go to `SolverError::Unsupported` explicitly, as the issue already requires. Add a test for each.

Verify with `task affected` (record `Gates selected`) and `task e2e` (this is a solver change, and `task e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d subprocess suites).

Related: str-t854z (same function `to_z3_expr`; coordinate if both are in flight).

title: Numeric variables split across solver sorts
description:
A declared numeric parameter can become independent Int and Real variables when its surrounding literals differ. This causes both false UNSAT (reachable fractional inputs disappear) and false SAT (the emitted single value violates a constraint).

Current code facts: shatter-core/src/solver.rs VarTable (lines 73-114) keeps independent integer and real maps; to_z3_expr (493-509) lets a comparison hint override a compatible declared numeric sort; extract_concrete_values (1023-1049) merges both maps by name, real overwriting integer. to_z3_real already supports Int-to-Real coercion. shatter-ts/src/analyzer.ts:1102 maps TypeScript number to Float while instrumentor.ts:890 emits integer-valued literals as Int, so the mixed representation is an ordinary supported input, not a malformed protocol message.

Reproduction (a unit test in shatter-core/src/solver.rs; notation expands directly to existing public types): x = SymExpr::Param { name: "x", path: [] }; I(n) = SymExpr::Const(ConstValue::Int(n)); F(n) = SymExpr::Const(ConstValue::Float(n)); B(op,a,b) = SymExpr::BinOp { op, left: Box::new(a), right: Box::new(b) }. Call solve_constraints(&constraints, Some(5000), &[ParamInfo { name: "x".into(), typ, type_name: None }]). This is a direct library reproduction, not a new frontend execution. On 2026-09-11 a fresh rebuild of current core at audited HEAD e50fc399f328711cbbe237c1e3918e96c1080656 produced the actual results below. Source was reread on 2026-09-12 and still contains the encoding. Optional original evidence: /tmp/shatter-followup-numeric-f2LZz8/probe.rs and probe.stdout.log; all necessary assertions are inline here.

Case A: typ=TypeInfo::Float; constraints=[B(Gt,x,I(0)), B(Lt,x,I(1))]. Expected SAT with 0 < x < 1, e.g. 0.5; actual UNSAT. Replacing I(0)/I(1) with F(0.0)/F(1.0) yields SAT x=0.5.

Use existing shared semantic generators where suitable; run repository-selected Rust gates and the applicable concolic integration task through its normal wrapper. Contracts: no new contract required for this fix; existing Z3-boundary/type checks must remain valid. 

Resolved implementation lookups: shared generators are shatter-core/src/test_arbitraries.rs::arb_sym_expr(depth) and arb_param_info; use typed/bounded subsets rather than arbitrary ill-typed expressions. title: Meta-gate git test scripts leak GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, corrupting the invoking worktree
description:
While landing str-mpgg1 (a beads-hook policy revert), `task check`'s pre-push gate corrupted the worktree it ran in — twice, reproducibly:

Run 1: a stray `init` commit appeared and HEAD was reset from the merge commit back to the pre-merge base commit, silently discarding the merge commit from the branch tip (recovered via `git reflog` + `git reset --hard`).

Run 2 (same worktree, retried after recovery): same pattern plus `README` was deleted, and the push failed with `fatal: a branch named 'str-abc1.2' already exists` / `error: remote origin already exists`.

`str-abc1.2` is not a real branch anywhere in this repo — it is the literal throwaway branch name `scripts/test_target_dir_report_json.sh` creates inside its own `mktemp -d` scratch repo (`git -C "$BASE_REPO" worktree add -q -b str-abc1.2 "$WT_MATCH"`). The fact that this exact name collided against the REAL worktree, and that HEAD/README in the real worktree ended up matching throwaway-repo operations, points to `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` (or a similar git env var) leaking out of one of the meta-gate's throwaway-repo test scripts and being inherited by a later command in the same `task check` process tree — so a later, unrelated git command (possibly the pre-push hook's own git invocation, or a sibling test script) silently operates against whatever repo those leaked vars point at instead of its intended target.

Candidate scripts to audit: scripts/test_target_dir_report_json.sh and scripts/test_cleanup_merged_remote_branches.sh (both build mktemp-scoped throwaway repos/worktrees using git -C / cd), and the scripts under test themselves — scripts/target-dir-report.sh and scripts/cleanup-merged-remote-branches.sh — in case one of them exports GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE rather than using git -C/--git-dir per invocation.

Fix approach:
1. `unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` at the top of every throwaway-repo test script, before any git command runs — cheap insurance regardless of leak source.
2. Audit target-dir-report.sh and cleanup-merged-remote-branches.sh for any export of these vars instead of git -C/--git-dir scoping.
3. Consider running these specific test scripts under a scrubbed environment (env -i PATH=... HOME=... bash script.sh) from the Taskfile as belt-and-suspenders.

Acceptance: `task check` run twice in a row from a scratch worktree produces a no-op diff on the real repo (git log --oneline -5 before/after identical, no stray commits, no deleted/modified tracked files). The two suspect test scripts still pass. No regression in their actual coverage (target-dir-report / cleanup-merged-remote-branches behavior).
notes: Overlapping Git fixture corruption fix is now landed and pushed under str-jttrf: main merge 483f1a4e08ec5a4be59a613723c917ebc45f7252. It sanitizes all existing shell/Python Git fixture entrypoints, removes numbered config injection, fixes test bootstrap and receipt commit-tree handling, and adds a caller-state sentinel regression across 7 entrypoints and 2 contamination profiles. Final preview task check, verifier test-standard/parity/conformance, and real main pre-push task check all passed (exit 0). Review remaining scope against this landed fix before continuing; your existing branch/worktree has been preserved.

Verified: main's scm.rs already scrubs GIT_DIR/GIT_COMMON_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY/GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES identically to str-y0rcz-fix-git-env-leak's one commit, which was a superseded early snapshot carrying no unique content beyond this. Branch deleted, no landing needed.

title: GIT_DIR env leak lets git-sandbox test scripts corrupt the real repo when run from hooks
description:
## Problem

Several test scripts under `task check` build isolated throwaway git repos
using `git -C <tempdir> ...` (or `cd <tempdir> && git ...`) to test git-sandbox
behavior in isolation. When these scripts run inside a git hook (pre-commit,
pre-push), git has already set `GIT_DIR` (and typically `GIT_WORK_TREE`) in
the environment to point at the real invoking repository. `-C <tempdir>` only
changes the working directory used for relative-path resolution — it does NOT
override an explicit `GIT_DIR` env var, which takes precedence for repository
discovery. Result: these scripts' git operations silently target the real
repository instead of their intended temp fixture.

## Evidence (found 2026-09-07 during a swarm landing of str-wyde8)

- `scripts/test_target_dir_report_json.sh` does
  `git -C "$BASE_REPO" worktree add -q -b str-abc1.2 "$WT_MATCH"`. Found a
  real local branch `str-abc1.2` in the actual repo (not on `origin` — verified
  via `git ls-remote`), matching this script's fixture branch name exactly.
  Deleted it after confirming.
- `scripts/test_cleanup_merged_remote_branches.sh` does `git remote add origin
  "$BARE"` inside its own temp clone. Under a leaked `GIT_DIR`, this fails
  with `error: remote origin already exists` — it's colliding with the real
  repo's actual `origin`, not a fixture.
- Live-fire: while investigating the first finding, a SECOND, unrelated
  worktree (a `land-work` preview I had just created and verified, containing
  a clean 2-parent merge commit) was corrupted mid-investigation — its HEAD
  was moved onto branch `main` and given fresh `git init`-style "init"
  commits, apparently by a concurrent teammate's `task check` run hitting the
  same leak against a different target worktree. `git reflog` on that worktree
  showed a repeated commit→reset→commit→reset cycle, meaning other concurrent
  agents on the same machine had already been hitting and manually
  resetting this exact corruption before this session even started.
- A separate stale `/tmp/land-work-preview-*` worktree (unrelated to this
  session, left over from a past landing) was found holding local branch
  `main` checked out with ~80 staged file changes reintroducing directories
  already deleted by `str-qwua7.41` (`shatter-vs/`, `cross/`, `Cross.toml`) —
  consistent with this same bug corrupting a past land-work preview.

## Impact

- Pre-push/pre-commit hooks that run `task check`/`task affected` can
  spuriously fail (or, worse, silently succeed after corrupting real repo
  state) whenever the check suite includes one of these scripts.
- Under concurrent multi-agent use (swarms, parallel worktrees on one
  machine), any worktree can be corrupted by ANY other worktree's hook run,
  not just its own — because GIT_DIR is an absolute path into whichever repo
  the hook-invoking process happened to inherit, and once a script mis-targets
  it, the blast radius is "the repo," not "the script's caller."
- Real risk of accidentally pushing corrupted/reintroduced content to `main`
  if an agent trusts a dirty "main" worktree as legitimate work rather than
  recognizing it as this bug's residue.

## Fix

Each git-sandbox test script that builds a temp repo must explicitly isolate
itself from the environment before its first `git init`/`git clone`/`git -C`
call, e.g.:
```sh
unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES
```
at the top of the script (or wrap every git invocation with `env -u GIT_DIR
-u GIT_WORK_TREE ...`). Consider adding this as a shared helper/lint rule
(e.g. `scripts/git-sandbox-test-lib.sh`) sourced by every script under
`scripts/test_*.sh` that calls `git init`, so future scripts of this shape
don't reintroduce the same bug. Grep for other `git init`/`git clone` sites
under `scripts/` to find the full affected set — `test_target_dir_report_json.sh`
and `test_cleanup_merged_remote_branches.sh` are confirmed; there may be more.

## Immediate cleanup done this session

- Deleted stray local branch `str-abc1.2` (never reached origin).
- Removed a stale, corrupted `/tmp/land-work-preview-hia0yzke` worktree
  (holding `main` with ~80 reintroduced-file staged changes from a past
  landing session).
- Removed this session's own corrupted `/tmp/land-work-preview-5wca0my7`
  preview worktree after recovering the verified merge commit by SHA.

## Acceptance criteria

- All `scripts/test_*.sh` (and any Python equivalents) that build an isolated
  git fixture explicitly unset GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE (or
  equivalent isolation) before their first git operation.
- A regression test (or a shared sourced helper with its own test) proves a
  script under test cannot see/mutate the real repo's branches/remotes even
  when GIT_DIR is pre-set in the environment to the real repo.
- `task check` passes when invoked via the pre-push hook from a real worktree
  (not just when invoked directly from a shell without inherited GIT_DIR).
notes:
Operator requested Codex to finish this repair after primary checkout recovery. Continuing the existing dedicated branch, preserving c2ac82fa before rebasing only its issue changes onto recovered origin/main. Review found regression setup itself inherits Git variables; correcting that and proving actual fixture entrypoints preserve caller state before landing. str-y0rcz covers the same corruption and will be cross-referenced after verified completion.
Safe outer regression reproduced 7 failures on the initial patch, including mutations to disposable caller config/index/refs and a missed receipt commit-tree environment. Fixed bootstrap, local Git config isolation, and that subprocess; Python fixtures reuse the existing examples sanitizer. Focused suite passes (67 tests); meta and real pre-push affected gates pass. Independent Claude reviews approved original change and follow-up; remaining comments describe documented manual registration/alias conventions, not correctness defects. Final merge-candidate verifier is running.

Safe outer regression reproduced 7 failures before repair and now protects 7 fixture entrypoints under pointer/config contamination. Validation: focused Python suite 67 tests exit 0; final affected subset 38 tests exit 0; task meta cache-helper-tests exit 0; task affected selected smoke/check exit 0 from real feature pre-push; final preview task check exit 0; project verifier task test-standard, task parity, task conformance each passed exit 0; main pre-push task check exit 0. Two independent Claude reviews approved. Unchanged Task stages used valid caches; optional unavailable lint tools skipped by configured tasks. Evidence: /home/ketan/.local/state/shatter/str-jttrf-landing-20260912. Overlap: str-y0rcz.

title: Exclude setup/teardown lifecycle exports from target discovery
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
Discovery name rule. Skip exported functions named setup/teardown/beforeAll/afterAll/beforeEach/afterEach when the file also exports a setup-shaped API; unit test in discovery.rs; documented in SPEC/README. No rename of the external example required.

## Problem
Scans treat exported `setup`/`teardown` lifecycle helpers as ordinary targets and fuzz them; `teardown` throws on mismatched scope, producing 390 `Teardown scope mismatch` clusters across three gauntlet steps (87+ garbage clusters per run) and burying real results. Either discovery must exclude lifecycle exports, or the `*.shatter.setup.ts` convention must be enforced/documented so example files like `setup-file-level.ts` are never discovered as targets.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-core/src/discovery.rs:490-532` — `SESSION_SETUP_ROOT_PREFIX`, `FILE_SETUP_INFIX`, `SetupConfigOverride`, `discover_setup_files()` (str-0s76.3): recognised setup files are `shatter.setup.{ext}`, `.shatter/setup.{ext}`, `<stem>.shatter.setup.{ext}`. A plain `setup-file-level.ts` does not match, so its exports are targets.
- Gauntlet: `audits/2026-09-04/gates/gauntlet-excerpt.txt` — clusters under `### teardown` from `setup-file-level.ts` in Step 6 (133), Step 23 (132), Step 55 (125); `teardown` reports 75–100% coverage so no threshold fires.
- Walkthrough shows the same clusters (`gates/walkthrough-excerpt.txt:956-957, 2049-2059`).
- `demo/gauntlet-scan-allowlist.yaml` — no entry for this class.
- The example file lives in the external examples repo (matched by `demo/gauntlet-scan-allowlist.yaml:111-112` for other files), so the fix may need a discovery rule rather than a rename.

## Acceptance checks
- Discovery skips functions named `setup`/`teardown`/`beforeAll`/`afterAll`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach` (exact list decided and documented) when exported from a file that also exports a recognised setup-shaped API, OR the example is renamed to the `*.shatter.setup.ts` convention and `discover_setup_files()` gains a warning when a file exports lifecycle names without matching the convention. State which in the fix.
- Unit test in `discovery.rs` for the chosen rule; gauntlet Steps 6/23/55 show zero `Teardown scope mismatch` clusters.
- SPEC/README setup-file section documents the rule.

## Scope
In: discovery rule or convention enforcement + warning, tests, docs sentence, gauntlet re-run.
Out: the gate checker changes (item 8).

## Size
Small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 13; evidence audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md (§"Demo gates" Teardown, rec. 7), gates/gauntlet-excerpt.txt, gates/walkthrough-excerpt.txt.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- Discovery skips functions named `setup`/`teardown`/`beforeAll`/`afterAll`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach` (exact list decided and documented) when exported from a file that also exports a recognised setup-shaped API, OR the example is renamed to the `*.shatter.setup.ts` convention and `discover_setup_files()` gains a warning when a file exports lifecycle names without matching the convention. State which in the fix.
- Unit test in `discovery.rs` for the chosen rule; gauntlet Steps 6/23/55 show zero `Teardown scope mismatch` clusters.
- SPEC/README setup-file section documents the rule.
notes: Landed on main (49b89203), merge from str-qwua7.56-lifecycle-discovery (73e385fa). Independent code review before merge found a real gap: shatter run's layer-iteration loop never applied the lifecycle-export exclusion, so it would still explore setup/teardown and reproduce the bug this issue exists to fix (CLAUDE.md parallel-path rule). Fixed inline (shatter-cli/src/commands/run.rs) with a new integration test (run_lifecycle_export_exclusion.rs) that was verified to fail without the fix. A second, non-blocking review finding (dry-run JSON summary counters undercount lifecycle-excluded exports) was filed separately as str-qwua7.56.1. title: explore implicit init: print "Created …" lines to stderr and detect language from the target, not the directory
description:
## Problem
When `explore` auto-initializes a project, it prints "Created .shatter/config.yaml (detected language: unknown)" on **stdout** ahead of the markdown report — contaminating `--format`/`--spec` consumers — and reports `unknown` for a single `.ts` target because detection looks only at directory marker files. Both are fixable regardless of whether implicit init stays (p2-27b).

## Current code facts
- `shatter-cli/src/main.rs:43-52` calls `run_implicit_init` before command dispatch; `shatter-cli/src/commands/init.rs:42 pub(crate) fn run_implicit_init(...)`.
- `init.rs:91` `println!("  Created  .shatter/config.yaml  (detected language: {language})")` — stdout.
- `init.rs:132 fn detect_language(dir: &Path) -> String` returns `"unknown"` (:140) when no `package.json`/`go.mod`/`Cargo.toml` is present; tests `:199-226` cover directory markers only; the explore target's extension is never consulted.
- Captured `ui/live-firstrun.*`: "Created …" lines precede `# Shatter Explore`. Pairs with p1-09 (`--spec-json` stdout exclusivity): both must hold for stdout to be clean.

## Acceptance checks
- All init/implicit-init status lines go to stderr at `info` level (explicit `shatter init` may keep stdout — decide and document in SPEC §2.8).
- `detect_language` takes the target file list: extension majority first (`.ts/.tsx` → typescript, `.go` → go, `.rs` → rust), directory markers as tiebreak; a single-`.ts`-target run never prints "unknown"; unit tests for both orders.
- Regression test in `shatter-cli/tests/`: `explore --spec-json <t>` and `--format text` in a fresh dir produce stdout that starts with the report/JSON.

## Scope
In: output stream and detection order. Out: whether implicit init runs at all (p2-27b), gitignore semantics (str-vr7vq branch).

## Size
small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 27; evidence audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md §2; audit §9.

comments.text:
Audit 2026-09-22 (findings cli-ux-04, verified P1; frontend-go-12, init-path part; docs-15) adds evidence and widens scope. Raising to P1.

**1. This breaks JSON contracts, not only the look of explore.** In a fresh directory, `shatter scan . --format json` writes the following to **stdout** before the `{`:

```
  Created  .shatter/
  Created  .shatter/config.yaml  (detected language: unknown)
  Created  .gitignore …
Initialized Shatter project at …
```

`json.load` then fails with `Expecting value: line 1 column 3` (`audits/2026-09-22/cli-ux-transcripts/scan-json.out`, on branch `audit-2026-09-22`). `shatter explore c.ts:classifyNumber > report.md` has the same problem: the report file starts with the init lines (docs-15).

**2. Code facts (re-checked on `56c86168`).** `shatter-cli/src/commands/init.rs:82`, `:91` and `:143` use `println!`. Implicit init goes through `maybe_implicit_init` (`shatter-cli/src/main.rs:53`, which itself prints `No .shatter/ found — initializing project` to stderr) into `run_implicit_init` (`init.rs:42`). Today it is called only from explore (`main.rs:318`) and scan (`main.rs:648`), so fixing `run_init_impl` covers both. An earlier audit draft said list-targets and spec-diff also trigger it. That is not true at this commit. They still need fresh-directory JSON contract tests (below) so that a future implicit-init call site cannot regress them.

**3. Language detection says `unknown`** for pure-Go and pure-Rust directories as well as bare TS files (`cli-ux-transcripts/go-explore.out`, `rust-explore.out`). `detect_language` (`init.rs:150`) looks only for `package.json`/`go.mod`/`Cargo.toml` in the resolved directory. Detect from the target file extension(s) first.

**4. The printed path can be empty.** `init.rs:143` prints `resolved_dir.display()` from the directory passed in, unchanged. For a bare filename target the parent is `Some("")`, so implicit init has printed `Initialized Shatter project at ` with nothing after it (frontend-go-12). Print the canonicalized absolute path.

**Extra acceptance criteria for this issue:**

- [ ] Implicit-init status lines go to stderr at info level. (Explicit `shatter init` may keep stdout. Decide and document in SPEC §2.8, as the issue already says.)
- [ ] The language is detected from the target files, with directory markers as the tiebreak. A pure-Go or pure-Rust target never prints `unknown`.
- [ ] The printed project path is absolute and never empty.
- [ ] `shatter-cli/tests/json_stdout_contract.rs` gains fresh-directory (not yet initialized) cases, each asserting that the whole of stdout parses as JSON: `scan --format json` (the implicit-init case), and as guards for the other JSON-on-stdout commands, `list-targets --format json`, `spec-diff --json`, `compare --json` and `revalidate --output-format json`. `specify --json` (needs an observation file from `shatter observe`, a pipeline-stage command) and `discover-deps --json` (Linux-only strace diagnostic) are intentionally not covered here; say so in the test file. At close, show the `scan --format json` case failing on current `main` and passing after the fix. The guard cases already pass.
- [ ] A fresh-directory `explore <file>:<fn>` (markdown on stdout) case asserts that stdout contains none of the init status lines (`Created`, `Initialized Shatter project`). This covers docs-15 and does not depend on str-qwua7.11.
- [ ] Not in this issue: a whole-stdout-is-JSON case for explore `--spec-json`. That belongs to str-qwua7.11 (open, P1), which makes `--spec-json` stdout-exclusive; its own acceptance should add the fresh-directory case. Snapshot `shatter diff --json` is being removed (retire-snapshot-diff, D2), so there is no case for it.
- [ ] `task affected` passes, and its `Gates selected` output is recorded.

Related: str-qwua7.58 (keep implicit init; document it; `--no-init`), str-qwua7.11 (`--spec-json` stdout exclusivity; both must hold for stdout to be clean).

title: Rust frontend: walkthrough examples 0% covered — analyzer/harness param-type disagreement (hypothesis)
description:
## Problem
The walkthrough's own Rust examples are 0% covered: `classify_number(0)` and `safe_divide(0.0, 0.0)` throw `runtime_error: input 0 deserialization failed: invalid type: integer 0, expected a string` on every call. **Hypothesis:** the analyzer reports numeric parameter types (so the explorer generates ints/floats) while the generated execute harness deserializes those parameters as `String`. This is a product bug in the Rust frontend, not an explorer limit, and it is masked by the demo gate (p1-08). The first step is diagnosis: confirm which harness mode the walkthrough examples take and reproduce with the walkthrough example itself before touching codegen.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs:2471, 2484, 2498` — candidate harness codegen sites where the parameter deserialization type appears to be chosen as `String` for these params (unconfirmed which mode emitted the walkthrough harness).
- Walkthrough Step 7 (`walkthrough.log:2570-2620`, excerpt in `audits/2026-09-04/gates/walkthrough-excerpt.txt`): `classify_number`, `safe_divide` → 0% coverage, all calls error. `negotiate_language` 0/102 lines, 2/13 branches with **no** deserialization error — possibly a separate defect; verify whether it shares the cause, otherwise file it separately.
- Analyzer side: `shatter-rust/src/analyzer.rs` (`convert_type_path` at `:1263` handles type resolution) reports the param types the planner uses.
- Three harness modes exist (bin-only, crate-backed dispatch `generate_dispatch_harness` ~`executor.rs:2596-3010`, crate_bridge) — str-bh9wu (open) already documents mode-specific type-handling inconsistencies; check which mode the walkthrough examples hit.
- Regression guard precedent: `shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic_rust.rs`.

## Acceptance checks
- Step 1 (diagnosis): a note on the issue stating the harness mode used for the walkthrough Rust examples and a reproduction command on the walkthrough example (`demo/walkthrough.yaml` Rust step) — before any code change.
- A unit test in `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs` tests (or a fixture under `examples/rust/`) with `fn classify_number(n: i64)` and `fn safe_divide(a: f64, b: f64)` executes with numeric inputs and reports non-zero `lines_executed`.
- The walkthrough Rust step shows >0% coverage for `classify_number` and `safe_divide` with no `deserialization failed` errors; `negotiate_language` either also >0% or a separate issue is filed and linked.
- Analyzer-reported param type and harness deserialization type come from one source of truth (a shared mapping function) across all three harness modes, with a test asserting agreement for all primitive kinds.
- `task rust-fe:test` and `task e2e-rust` (or equivalent) green.

## Scope
In: the type-mapping bug across harness modes for primitive params; regression test; walkthrough re-run.
Out: struct/enum synthesis gaps (str-1fik/str-wfd2, str-bh9wu, str-emmrq).

## Size
Small–medium (depends on whether all three harness modes share the defect).

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 12; evidence audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md (§"Demo gates" Rust deserialization, rec. 6), gates/walkthrough-excerpt.txt.

title: Hide execution-only global flags on non-executing commands
description:
## Problem
Every leaf subcommand shows 13+ flags because the six global timing flags plus `--allow-host-writes`, `--set`, `--color`, `--render`, `--project-dir` are `global = true` and so repeat on `init`, `cache`, `telemetry`, `spec-diff`, `doctor` — commands that execute nothing. `spec-diff --help` is 60 lines for two flags of its own, and carries a five-line sandboxing paragraph that cannot apply. This is independent of str-9ee5 (flag vocabulary unification and `help_heading` grouping for explore/scan), which stays the owner of grouping; cross-reference, do not merge.

## Current code facts
- `shatter spec-diff --help` — 60 lines, 13 flags, 2 of its own; `--allow-host-writes` (a 5-line paragraph about sandboxing) shown on a command that executes nothing (`audits/2026-09-04/ui/help-spec-diff.txt`).
- `explore` 79 flags, `scan` 69; explore `--help` is 15 KB; globals are interleaved with command flags by declaration order (`--log-level`, `--max-iterations`, `--per-function-timeout`, `-v`, `-q`, `--timeout-explore`, `--time-limit`, `--timing` …); no `help_heading` anywhere in `shatter-cli/src/args.rs` (4.1k lines, variants already boxed for clap's stack budget).
- Global flags are defined on the top-level `Cli` struct in `args.rs`; clap `global = true` propagates them; `hide = true` per subcommand or moving execution-only globals (`--allow-host-writes`, timing) onto an `ExecutionOptions` flattened only into executing commands is the mechanism.

## Acceptance checks
- `shatter spec-diff --help`, `init --help`, `doctor --help`, `cache --help`, `telemetry --help` no longer show `--allow-host-writes`, `--set`, or the six timing flags; display/global flags (`--color`, `--render`, `--log-level`, `-v/-q`, `--project-dir`) may stay. Target ≤ 7 flags on `spec-diff`.
- Snapshot tests of `--help` output for `spec-diff` and `doctor` under `shatter-cli/tests/`; `task docs-smoke` green (flag names unchanged).

## Scope
In: moving execution-only globals (`--allow-host-writes`, timing flags, `--set`) off non-executing commands via an `ExecutionOptions` struct flattened only into executing commands (or per-command `hide`); snapshot tests.
Out: `help_heading` grouping and flag renames (str-9ee5), `ExploreOptions` flatten consolidation (audit item 20), tracker-ID removal from help text (audit P2).

## Size

title: Restore bd (orphan dolt server) and add a patrol check for dolt-running-but-port-file-missing
description:
## Problem
During the audit every `bd` invocation failed for the whole session: an orphaned `dolt sql-server` held the database's exclusive lock while `.beads/dolt-server.{pid,port}` did not exist, so `bd` could not discover it, tried to auto-start a second server, and timed out after 10 s with "Dolt server unreachable … locked by another dolt process". The state has since cleared (bd works as of 2026-09-05), but nothing detects or explains it, and it will recur whenever a session dies mid-`bd`.

## Current code facts
- Observed: `/usr/local/bin/dolt sql-server -H 127.0.0.1 -P 43105` PID 28938, uptime ≈49 h; `.beads/dolt-server.port` and `.beads/dolt-server.pid` absent; `.beads/dolt-server.log` tail `database "dolt" is locked by another dolt process`; error text `Dolt server unreachable at 127.0.0.1:0 and auto-start failed: server started (PID …) but not accepting connections on port NNNNN: timeout after 10s`.
- `.beads/config.yaml:14` — `auto-start: true` (so each call spawns a doomed second server; `.beads/dolt-server.log` is 6.1 MB of these).
- `.beads/export-state.json` dated 2026-07-05 / 1524 issues vs `issues.jsonl` 1653 rows; `.beads/last-touched` named an issue absent from the export — export bookkeeping lags when the DB is unreachable.
- `scripts/drift-patrol.py` `tracker-hygiene` already falls back to `issues.jsonl` and names its source; it has no server-state check. `agent-env-doctor` (bento) checks plugins/hooks only (bento item 44 is the cross-repo side).
- AGENTS.md "bd Quick Reference" documents no recovery command.

## Acceptance checks
- The recovery recipe lives in the check's remediation text in `scripts/drift-patrol.py` (printed on FAIL, like every other check): detect (`pgrep -af 'dolt sql-server'` vs `.beads/dolt-server.port`), stop (`bd dolt stop` / `kill <pid>`), `bd dolt start`, verify `bd stats`. AGENTS.md's bd Quick Reference gets a one-line pointer to `python3 scripts/drift-patrol.py --only tracker-server`.
- `scripts/drift-patrol.py` gains a `tracker-server` check that FAILs when a `dolt sql-server` process whose args reference this repo's `.beads/dolt` exists and `.beads/dolt-server.port` is missing or names a port nobody listens on; SKIP when no dolt process at all. The process list and port-file contents are passed in as data (function parameters with `pgrep`/file readers as defaults) so `scripts/test_drift_patrol.py` covers FAIL/PASS/SKIP with injected values and needs no live orphan.

## Scope
In: patrol check + remediation text + test, one-line AGENTS.md pointer. Decision for maintainer: proposed to also set `auto-start: false` in `.beads/config.yaml`? Default **no** — keep auto-start; the check makes the failure diagnosable.
Out: fixing bd/dolt upstream (upstream-beads), bento doctor (bento item 44), a SessionStart hook (touches the shared hook set; not wanted unless asked).

## Size
Small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 16; evidence audits/2026-09-04/issues-hygiene.md (§0, finding 1, R1).

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (audits/2026-09-04.md, branch audit-2026-09-04)
acceptance_criteria:
- The recovery recipe lives in the check's remediation text in `scripts/drift-patrol.py` (printed on FAIL, like every other check): detect (`pgrep -af 'dolt sql-server'` vs `.beads/dolt-server.port`), stop (`bd dolt stop` / `kill <pid>`), `bd dolt start`, verify `bd stats`. AGENTS.md's bd Quick Reference gets a one-line pointer to `python3 scripts/drift-patrol.py --only tracker-server`.
- `scripts/drift-patrol.py` gains a `tracker-server` check that FAILs when a `dolt sql-server` process whose args reference this repo's `.beads/dolt` exists and `.beads/dolt-server.port` is missing or names a port nobody listens on; SKIP when no dolt process at all. The process list and port-file contents are passed in as data (function parameters with `pgrep`/file readers as defaults) so `scripts/test_drift_patrol.py` covers FAIL/PASS/SKIP with injected values and needs no live orphan.

New scripts/drift-patrol.py tracker-server check detects an orphaned dolt sql-server process (missing/unreachable .beads/dolt-server.port) by resolving .beads/dolt via 'git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir' and matching /proc/<pid>/cwd, since bd sets cwd rather than a --data-dir flag; FAILs on orphan, SKIPs when no dolt process exists, PASSes when reachable. Remediation text + one-line AGENTS.md pointer added; auto-start left true per scope. Gate evidence: python3 scripts/test_drift_patrol.py -> 43/43 pass; python3 scripts/drift-patrol.py --only tracker-server run live against the actual running dolt server on this machine -> correctly PASSes; land-work-run-verifier.py against the exact merge preview -> passed (3 selected checks); land-work-verify-landing.py against origin/main -> tree+sha match confirmed.
