title: Demo gates must fail on 0% coverage, all-throwing functions and lifecycle-helper clusters
description:
## Problem
Both demo gates say "All steps passed" while the demo output is broken. The walkthrough's Rust step reports `classify_number` and `safe_divide` at 0% coverage with every call throwing `input 0 deserialization failed` (marked `(ok)`); the gauntlet emits 390 `Teardown scope mismatch` error clusters from fuzzing exported `setup`/`teardown` helpers. The checkers test "exit 0 and no panic", not "sane result", and the walkthrough's error regex does not even match the deserialization message.

## Current code facts
- `demo/walkthrough.sh:261` — `error_pattern='\[error\]|failed to deserialize|panic|SIGSEGV|error: exploration error'`; the live message is `runtime_error: input 0 deserialization failed: invalid type: integer 0, expected a string` (`walkthrough.log:2570-2620`), which does not match `failed to deserialize`. Coverage is never checked; `negotiate_language` 0/102 lines also `(ok)`.
- Root cause of the Rust 0%: analyzer types the params numerically but the generated harness deserializes into `String` — `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs:2471/2484/2498` (tracked as item 12; this issue must not be closed by that fix alone).
- `demo/gauntlet_check_output.py` — `PROCESS_ERROR_RE = \[error\]|failed to deserialize|panic|SIGSEGV|error: exploration error`; the `| FAIL |` row check fires only on coverage-threshold failures; `teardown` reaches 75–100% coverage so nothing fires.
- `audits/2026-09-04/gates/gauntlet-excerpt.txt` — 390 `throws Error: Teardown scope mismatch` clusters in Step 6 "Scan Standalone TypeScript" (133), Step 23 "Scan Total Timeout" (132), Step 55 "HTML Scan Report" (125), all under `### teardown` from `setup-file-level.ts`.
- `demo/gauntlet-scan-allowlist.yaml` — does not list this class (and currently would not need to, because nothing flags it); allowlist entries have no expiry field.
- Discovery root cause (setup/teardown exports treated as targets) is item 13.

## Acceptance checks
- Explicit step: `demo/walkthrough.sh` stops using its own `error_pattern` at `:261` and calls `demo/gauntlet_check_output.py` on its captured output, so both gates share one checker.
- `gauntlet_check_output.py` FAILs a step when: any function reports 0% coverage with ≥1 iteration; every call of a function ends in an input-deserialization error (`deserialization failed` added to `PROCESS_ERROR_RE`); a thrown-error cluster matches a lifecycle/scope class (`Teardown scope mismatch`) that is not allowlisted.
- Allowlist entries gain a required `expires:` date; the checker fails when an entry is past expiry. Two entries are added so the gates stay green in CI until the product fixes land: (1) the Rust walkthrough cases `classify_number`, `safe_divide`, `negotiate_language` (0% coverage / deserialization failed) with an expiry of 30 days, to be removed when p1-12 lands; (2) the `Teardown scope mismatch` lifecycle class with the same expiry, pending the p1-13 decision. Both entries cite their issue id.
- Running the gates on the audit's captured logs (`gates/walkthrough-excerpt.txt`, `gates/gauntlet-excerpt.txt`) reproduces FAIL; after items 12 and 13 land, both gates are green for the right reason.
- With the two allowlist entries in place, `task walkthrough` and `task gauntlet` are green on the current tree; removing either entry makes the corresponding gate red (verified once and noted). `task check` (`Taskfile.yml:475`) does not include the demo gates, so CI is unaffected either way.

## Scope
In: checker logic, walkthrough wiring to the shared checker, allowlist expiry schema plus the two expiring entries, tests for the checker on captured logs. Functions legitimately at 0% (unsupported fixtures) use ordinary allowlist entries with an expiry, same mechanism.
Out: the Rust type bug (item 12) and the discovery policy (item 13) — this issue makes the gates able to see them.

Small–medium.

Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 8; evidence audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md (§"Demo gates", rec. 5), gates/walkthrough-excerpt.txt, gates/gauntlet-excerpt.txt.

title: explore --spec-json on stdout must emit only JSON
description:
## Problem
`shatter explore --spec-json <target>` writes the markdown explore report and then the JSON spec to the same stdout, so `json.load` fails at line 1. Only `--spec-out FILE` or `-o` produce clean JSON. QUICKSTART recommends the `--spec-json` pair without warning, and any agent or CI job piping the command gets unparseable output.

## Current code facts
- `audits/2026-09-04/ui/live-specjson.out` — begins `# Shatter Explore … | 1 | classifyNumber(0) | …` followed by `{ "function_name": …`.
- `shatter-cli/src/args.rs` — explore has `--spec-json`, `--spec` (markdown), `--spec-out` ("implies --spec-json"), `-o/--output`; `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs` `run_explore` (`:4116`) writes the report and then the spec (finalization section; see also `finalize_explore`).
- `--format json` on `scan` writes clean stdout (usability-ui.md §"agent affordances") — the precedent to match.
- `QUICKSTART.md` recommends `explore --spec-json` (see §4/§5 around `:115-125`).

## Acceptance checks
- When `--spec-json` (or `--spec`) targets stdout, the explore report goes to **stderr** (chosen over suppression: keeps it visible to humans and matches the `scan --format json` precedent); stdout is exactly one JSON document (or one markdown spec). Decision for maintainer: `--spec` (markdown) follows the same rule by default; if a combined human view is wanted, add it as `--spec --with-report` later.
- CLI integration test in `shatter-cli/tests/`: run `explore --spec-json` on a fixture and `serde_json::from_slice(stdout)` succeeds; a second test asserts `-o`/`--spec-out` behaviour is unchanged.
- SPEC §2.1 (explore) states the stdout contract for `--spec-json`; QUICKSTART example unchanged or adjusted to match.

## Scope
In: explore output routing, tests, SPEC/QUICKSTART sentence.
Out: unifying the five machine-readable-output spellings (audit P2 item 20).

## Size
Small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 9; evidence audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md (§2 P1, §"agent affordances", rec. 1), ui/live-specjson.out.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (audits/2026-09-04.md, branch audit-2026-09-04)
acceptance_criteria:
- When `--spec-json` (or `--spec`) targets stdout, the explore report goes to **stderr** (chosen over suppression: keeps it visible to humans and matches the `scan --format json` precedent); stdout is exactly one JSON document (or one markdown spec). Decision for maintainer: `--spec` (markdown) follows the same rule by default; if a combined human view is wanted, add it as `--spec --with-report` later.
- CLI integration test in `shatter-cli/tests/`: run `explore --spec-json` on a fixture and `serde_json::from_slice(stdout)` succeeds; a second test asserts `-o`/`--spec-out` behaviour is unchanged.
- SPEC §2.1 (explore) states the stdout contract for `--spec-json`; QUICKSTART example unchanged or adjusted to match.
close_reason: Landed to main at 2e7d61b3. Fix: explore --spec-json/--spec now routes the header/per-function report/footer to stderr when the spec targets stdout (no --spec-out), so stdout carries exactly one parseable document. Applied uniformly across finalize_explore and run_explore via a shared spec_targets_stdout() helper (post-review; was hand-duplicated at first). SPEC.md §2.1 documents the contract. Gates: task affected (docs,smoke,cli:clippy,cli:test,e2e-ts/go/rust,gauntlet) exit 0, both locally and via pre-push hook, twice (once pre-review-fix, once post-review-fix). 3 integration tests in shatter-cli/tests/explore_spec_json_stdout_purity.rs, TDD-verified. Rebased once (str-qwua7.1 landed first). Code review: 3 Important/Minor findings across 2 passes, all fixed -- (1) print_stderr exited the whole process on stderr BrokenPipe, which could truncate an in-progress stdout JSON stream on a stderr-side failure unrelated to stdout health -- now drops the write and continues; (2) spec_to_stdout's duplicated formula (this project's flagged 'parallel parity' drift risk) extracted to shared spec_targets_stdout(); (3) run_explore's footer eprintln!/println! branches duplicated 5 conditional lines verbatim -- now built as one string with a single print call; (4) leftover doc-comment contradiction on print_stderr fixed in a follow-up commit. Also flagged by swarm-qwua7-10 in parallel: str-qwua7.14's 2026-09-08 'not reproducible' closure looks stale (reproduces live against a fresh examples checkout) -- not touched here, out of scope for this issue.

title: Implement SPEC §2.11 exit codes: 2 for tool/usage errors, 1 only for fired gates
description:
## Problem
SPEC §2.11 reserves exit 2 for usage and tool errors and 1 for fired gates, and gives "malformed spec file" as its example of 2. Observed: file not found, unsupported extension, unknown function, malformed spec file and the sandbox refusal all exit 1; only clap usage errors exit 2. A CI job cannot distinguish "regression found" from "spec file corrupt" or "sandbox not configured".

## Current code facts
- Live runs (`audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md` §2): `explore nope.ts:foo` → `Error: file not found: 'nope.ts'` exit 1; `explore foo.txt:bar` (unsupported extension) exit 1; `explore arithmetic-v1.ts:doesNotExist` → `[error] Analyze error (FunctionNotFound)… Error: explore: all 1 attempted target(s) failed` exit 1; `spec-diff bad.json v1.spec.json` → `Error: failed to parse spec 'bad.json': EOF while parsing…` exit 1; host-write refusal exit 1.
- `SPEC.md` §2.11 (around `:589`) — exit-code table; also cites nonexistent `--failure-threshold` (should be `--fail-on-failures=PERCENT`, `help-scan.txt:272`).
- `shatter-cli/src/main.rs:1381` `categorize_error` — classifies exit codes by substring-matching `Display` output; shatter-cli has zero `anyhow` and 56 `Result<_, String>` signatures (rust-quality.md), which is why classes cannot be matched structurally.
- `shatter-cli/src/host_writes.rs:98-124` — refusal returns `Err(refusal_message())` (a `String`).
- str-9fn2 (closed, 2026-08-26) introduced the "three-way exit code convention" in SPEC; implementation did not follow for these classes.

## Acceptance checks
- A `CliError` (or `anyhow` + typed error kinds) carries an exit class; `categorize_error` maps by kind, not substring.
- Exit 2 for: file not found, unsupported extension, function not found, malformed spec/config file, sandbox refusal. Exit 1 only for fired gates (`--fail-on-failures`, spec-diff differences, coverage budgets). Exit 0 otherwise.
- Multi-target semantics (`scan`, `run`, multi-target `explore`): exit **2 if no target could start** (all failed before execution — missing file, unsupported extension, unknown function, refusal); exit **1 if at least one target succeeded and at least one failed** (partial failure is a fired-gate class, with a summary line naming the failed targets); exit 0 when all succeed and no gate fires.
- Origin sites to tag with an error kind: `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs` target resolution (file/extension/function lookups), `shatter-cli/src/host_writes.rs:98-124` (refusal), `shatter-cli/src/commands/spec_diff.rs` spec parsing, config loading in `shatter-core/src/config.rs` callers.
- One CLI integration test per class plus the two multi-target cases in `shatter-cli/tests/` asserting the code; SPEC §2.11 updated (including the `--failure-threshold` → `--fail-on-failures` fix) and `docs-smoke` passes.

## Scope
In: error type, classifier, the listed classes, tests, SPEC table.
Out: full `anyhow` migration of all 56 signatures (audit item 22) — do only what the classifier needs, but shape it so item 22 can extend it.

## Size
Medium.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 10; evidence audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md (§2 exit codes, rec. 2), docs-accuracy.md (P2-2), rust-quality.md (`categorize_error`).

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (audits/2026-09-04.md, branch audit-2026-09-04)
acceptance_criteria:
- A `CliError` (or `anyhow` + typed error kinds) carries an exit class; `categorize_error` maps by kind, not substring.
- Exit 2 for: file not found, unsupported extension, function not found, malformed spec/config file, sandbox refusal. Exit 1 only for fired gates (`--fail-on-failures`, spec-diff differences, coverage budgets). Exit 0 otherwise.
- Multi-target semantics (`scan`, `run`, multi-target `explore`): exit **2 if no target could start** (all failed before execution — missing file, unsupported extension, unknown function, refusal); exit **1 if at least one target succeeded and at least one failed** (partial failure is a fired-gate class, with a summary line naming the failed targets); exit 0 when all succeed and no gate fires.
- Origin sites to tag with an error kind: `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs` target resolution (file/extension/function lookups), `shatter-cli/src/host_writes.rs:98-124` (refusal), `shatter-cli/src/commands/spec_diff.rs` spec parsing, config loading in `shatter-core/src/config.rs` callers.
- One CLI integration test per class plus the two multi-target cases in `shatter-cli/tests/` asserting the code; SPEC §2.11 updated (including the `--failure-threshold` → `--fail-on-failures` fix) and `docs-smoke` passes.

>
> - **Now exit 2 (single target):** missing file, `.py` target, unknown function, bad `--set` value, function glob, spec-diff bad JSON, missing spec, host-write refusal. `shatter-cli/src/main.rs` `error_exit_code` (`:1475`) maps any non-`GateFailure` error to 2. title: scan and run must agree on a missing frontend; print the remediation once
description:
## Problem
On the same directory with the Rust frontend absent, `scan .` warns, skips the `.rs` files and exits 0, while `run .` aborts with `Error: shatter-rust frontend not found…`, exit 1 and no report. The same ~600-character remediation paragraph is printed twice per scan (once as `[warn]`, once inside the `STATUS skipped_by_unavailable_frontend … hint=` line). Users and CI get opposite behaviour from two commands that claim the same defaults.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-cli/src/helpers.rs:497` — `check_frontend_availability` (str-bnsw) builds the structured install hint; called from `shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs:497` and `commands/explore.rs:4353`.
- `scan.rs` — on unavailable frontend emits `[warn] …hint…` and a per-target `STATUS skipped_by_unavailable_frontend … hint=<same text>`; exit 0.
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/run.rs` — no availability precheck path that degrades; errors out before producing a report.
- Live evidence: `audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md` §2 (P1 scan vs run) and §"Error messages" ("frontend-missing hint repeated").
- Related: str-a7x4 "Unify the single-target exploration path used by scan and explore" — adjacent, not the same fix.

## Acceptance checks
- Proposed default (**behaviour change for `run` — decision for maintainer, one-line confirmation needed**): `run` adopts `scan`'s behaviour — skip targets whose frontend is unavailable with one warning, continue, exit 0; exit 2 if nothing at all could run (p1-10 semantics; state 2 in the code even if p1-10 has not landed).
- Shared opt-in `--require-frontend <lang>` (repeatable; this spelling, not `--require-rust`) on both commands makes a missing frontend a hard error, exit 2.
- The remediation paragraph is printed exactly once per run, at first occurrence, as the `[warn]`; per-target `STATUS skipped_by_unavailable_frontend` lines carry `hint=see warning above (frontend:<lang>)` instead of the full text.
- CLI integration tests for scan and run with `SHATTER_RUST_FRONTEND` pointed at a nonexistent path covering default and `--require-*`.
- SPEC §2.2/§2.3 document the shared behaviour.

## Scope
In: run's degradation path, shared flag, dedup of the hint, tests, SPEC.
Out: embedding the Rust frontend / distribution model (audit item 28).

Small–medium.

title: validate-protocol-registry.py: empty source extraction must fail; point extractors at real sources
description:
## Problem
The source-parity layer of `scripts/validate-protocol-registry.py` — presented in `protocol/GOVERNANCE.md` as a required gate — is a silent no-op for TypeScript and produces false warnings for Rust. `extract_ts` regexes `type Command = …;` in a file that has only re-exported generated enums since str-1hlk.7, so every extracted set is empty and the script prints "All checks passed". The Rust extractor reads `protocol.rs` while the command literals live in `handler.rs`, so it warns that implemented commands are "not found".

## Current code facts
- `scripts/validate-protocol-registry.py:545-560` — `extract_ts` matches `type Command = …;`, `ResponseStatus`, `ErrorCode` in `shatter-ts/src/protocol.ts`; that file now only `export … from './generated/protocol-enums.js'`; all three sets come back empty and no check trips.
- Rust extractor reads `shatter-rust/src/protocol.rs`; command literals are dispatched in `shatter-rust/src/handler.rs:567-575`, so `instrument`, `prepare`, `shutdown`, `get_invocation_plan` are reported "not found in shatter-rust" though three of the four are implemented and advertised.
- `audits/2026-09-04/gates/gate-parity.log:6-7` — `python3 scripts/validate-protocol-registry.py` → "Registry: 10 commands, 11 statuses, 12 error codes" then success.
- Generated sources that should be the vocabulary extraction targets: `shatter-ts/src/generated/protocol-enums.ts`, `shatter-go/protocol/protocol_enums_gen.go`, `shatter-rust/src/generated/protocol_enums.rs` (`scripts/protocol-codegen.py --check` passes).
- Dispatch sites and the exact match shape for "implemented commands":
  - TS: `shatter-ts/src/handlers.ts:402-1046` — `case "handshake":`, `case "analyze": {`, … `case "shutdown":` → regex `^\s*case "([a-z_]+)":` inside the top-level command `switch`.
  - Go: `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go:267-285` — `case "handshake":` … `case "get_invocation_plan":` → same regex, bounded to the first `switch` on the command (later `case "unsupported"`/`case "adapter"` at :1169/:1184 and type-name cases at :2201/:2218 must be excluded by scoping to that switch block).
  - Rust: `shatter-rust/src/handler.rs:543-548` — `match req.command.as_str() { "analyze" => …, "instrument" => …, "prepare" => …, "execute" => … }` → regex `^\s*"([a-z_]+)" =>` inside that `match`; the advertised capability list at `handler.rs:567-575` (`"analyze".to_string()`, …) is the secondary source to cross-check against.
- `protocol/GOVERNANCE.md:260-281` — describes this layer as a required step.
- Related open issue str-2fjn ("Cross-validate protocol registry/schema against implementations") is the broader class fix; this issue is the minimal repair of the existing validator so it stops lying.

## Acceptance checks
- Any extractor returning an empty set makes the script exit non-zero with a message naming the file and pattern.
- TS/Go/Rust extractors read the generated enum files for vocabulary and the dispatch sites for "implemented commands"; the current false Rust warnings disappear; a deliberately removed command in a temp copy is detected (add a unit test under `scripts/` — there is already a `test_drift_patrol.py` pattern).
- Proposed default (decision for maintainer): **fix the extractors and keep the layer** — it is cheap, GOVERNANCE.md already relies on it, and codegen `--check` does not cover dispatch coverage. `task parity` still green on HEAD; GOVERNANCE.md:260-281 wording matches what the script now checks.

## Scope
In: the validator script, its tests, GOVERNANCE.md sentence.
Out: generating message shapes from `field_model` (audit item 23 / str-2fjn).

## Size
Small–medium.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 6; evidence audits/2026-09-04/frontends-protocol.md (P1 validator finding, rec. 1), gates/gate-parity.log.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (audits/2026-09-04.md, branch audit-2026-09-04)
acceptance_criteria:
- Any extractor returning an empty set makes the script exit non-zero with a message naming the file and pattern.
- TS/Go/Rust extractors read the generated enum files for vocabulary and the dispatch sites for "implemented commands"; the current false Rust warnings disappear; a deliberately removed command in a temp copy is detected (add a unit test under `scripts/` — there is already a `test_drift_patrol.py` pattern).
- Proposed default (decision for maintainer): **fix the extractors and keep the layer** — it is cheap, GOVERNANCE.md already relies on it, and codegen `--check` does not cover dispatch coverage. `task parity` still green on HEAD; GOVERNANCE.md:260-281 wording matches what the script now checks.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
Audit 2026-09-22 (finding protocol-parity-15, verified; re-checked 2026-09-23 at 56c86168): this issue was closed with its title criterion unmet.

- The fix (4cf2165f) repointed only the Rust command extractor at `handler.rs` dispatch. `extract_ts` (`scripts/validate-protocol-registry.py:545-553`) still reads `type Command/ResponseStatus/ErrorCode` unions from `shatter-ts/src/protocol.ts`. title: Docs first run: make QUICKSTART/README work under default-deny and document the host-write policy in SPEC
description:
## Problem
A new user following QUICKSTART verbatim is refused on the very first command: since str-gg9v (2026-07-09) `explore/scan/run/…` default-deny target execution unless `SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND` or `--allow-host-writes` is set, and neither QUICKSTART nor README's minimal example mentions it. SPEC.md — the CLI contract — never mentions the policy or the global flag, its changelog stops at 2026-07-03 despite six later CLI-visible changes, and its §3.6 config example cannot deserialize. (`docs-smoke` validates only flag names and YAML syntax, so none of this is caught — hardening it is split out as p1-07b.)

## Current code facts
- `QUICKSTART.md:78-88` — first command `./target/release/shatter explore shipping.ts:calculateShipping`; `grep -i 'sandbox\|allow-host' QUICKSTART.md` → no matches (also §4, §5 at `:115-125`).
- `README.md:262-266` minimal example omits the flag; `README.md:290-325` documents the policy correctly further down.
- `shatter-cli/src/host_writes.rs:14-15, 98-124` — refusal path `Err(refusal_message())` for `explore`, `scan`, `run`, `observe`, `properties`, `revalidate`, `bench` when neither `SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND` nor `--allow-host-writes`/`SHATTER_ALLOW_HOST_WRITES=1` is set.
- `SPEC.md:560-576` §2.10 Global Options lists 10 globals, no `--allow-host-writes`; `SPEC.md` §2.11 Exit Codes has no row for the refusal; `SPEC.md:3` "Last updated: 2026-07-03"; changelog `SPEC.md:1121-1127` last row 2026-07-03.
- Missing changelog rows (from `git log -- SPEC.md` and landings): 07-04 str-1fwt (init/doctor gitignore), 07-09 str-gg9v (host-write policy), 07-13 str-mktn (two-file config, doctor report), 07-24 str-yhsp (`--concolic`/`--solver-timeout` on run), 07-28 str-79t9 (invocation planner), 08-26 str-9fn2 (three-way exit-code convention).
- `SPEC.md` §3.6 example `inputs: [list]` vs `shatter-core/src/config.rs` `FunctionConfig.inputs: Option<String>` (a path).
- `scripts/docs-smoke.py` / `scripts/docs-smoke.yaml` — `smoke_commands` are `--help`/`--version` only; YAML blocks are `yaml.safe_load`ed, never deserialized against the structs; there is an existing `schemas` task.

## Acceptance checks
- QUICKSTART §2 (before the first `explore`) and README minimal example show `--allow-host-writes` as the primary form (no backend to install) and mention `export SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker` as the sandboxed alternative, with a one-sentence why; running QUICKSTART §2/§4/§5 verbatim on a fresh clone succeeds.
- SPEC: `--allow-host-writes` row in §2.10; a "Sandbox and host-write policy" subsection (gated commands, env vars, throwaway cwd, TS caveat str-02i70); §2.11 documents the *intended* refusal exit code **2** with a cross-reference to the exit-code implementation issue (p1-10) — do not wait for it; six changelog rows added; "Last updated" bumped; §3.6 `inputs` example changed to a path string (`inputs: ./inputs/validateToken/candidates.json`) — **docs-only fix**, `FunctionConfig.inputs` stays `Option<String>`.
- `task docs-smoke` still green (flag names unchanged).

## Scope
In: QUICKSTART.md, README.md, SPEC.md §2.10/§2.11/§3.6/§8.
Out: docs-smoke hardening (p1-07b), exit-code implementation (p1-10), tracker-ID removal from user docs (audit P2), the broader docs reorganisation (audit item 31).

## Size
Small (doc edits only; docs-smoke hardening is p1-07b).

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 7; evidence audits/2026-09-04/docs-accuracy.md (P1-1, P1-2, P1-3, rec. 1–4), docs-quality.md (P1-3), usability-ui.md (§6 first run).

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (audits/2026-09-04.md, branch audit-2026-09-04)
acceptance_criteria:
- QUICKSTART §2 (before the first `explore`) and README minimal example show `--allow-host-writes` as the primary form (no backend to install) and mention `export SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker` as the sandboxed alternative, with a one-sentence why; running QUICKSTART §2/§4/§5 verbatim on a fresh clone succeeds.
- SPEC: `--allow-host-writes` row in §2.10; a "Sandbox and host-write policy" subsection (gated commands, env vars, throwaway cwd, TS caveat str-02i70); §2.11 documents the *intended* refusal exit code **2** with a cross-reference to the exit-code implementation issue (p1-10) — do not wait for it; six changelog rows added; "Last updated" bumped; §3.6 `inputs` example changed to a path string (`inputs: ./inputs/validateToken/candidates.json`) — **docs-only fix**, `FunctionConfig.inputs` stays `Option<String>`.
- `task docs-smoke` still green (flag names unchanged).
notes:
Audit addendum (2026-09-13), consolidating ON-1/ON-2 into this existing in-progress documentation issue; do not open a duplicate or change its assignee/status. The old suggested parent str-ck05 is closed.

Three precise qualifications/evidence additions:
1. The acceptance text's proposed SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker alternative must be language-qualified. Current shatter-cli/src/host_writes.rs identifies this variable as the Go frontend's backend; its CLI check accepts any nonempty value except "none", without verifying a TS/Rust sandbox. Therefore setting it alone cannot be described as sandboxing the TypeScript calculateShipping Quickstart. Show a deliberate command-scoped --allow-host-writes choice for the trusted pure sample, accurately labeled unsandboxed; do not claim a throwaway cwd provides OS isolation. Arbitrary code still requires a separately established appropriate isolation choice.
2. SPEC.md §3.6 inputs must be a path relative to .shatter/, accompanied by the correct candidate-file shape. In shatter-core/src/config.rs, FunctionConfig.inputs is Option<String>; resolve_function_config_with_inputs joins it with the owning .shatter/ directory; parse_candidate_inputs returns Vec<CandidateInput>, whose args field holds positional arguments. Example: inputs: inputs/validateToken.json with .shatter/inputs/validateToken.json containing [{"args":["valid-token"]},{"args":["expired-token"]},{"args":["malformed"]}]. A bare JSON array of token strings is not the candidate schema.
3. README.md's pending TypeScript redirection caveat is stale: closed str-02i70 records merge 47a30bcfea1a91786bacb42d66ae57859115d293. In shatter-ts/src/executor.ts, the resolver adapters used by createAdapterAwareRequire install buildFsWriteRedirectShim based on SHATTER_HOST_WRITE_DIR; executor.test.ts's "fs host-write redirection (str-02i70)" group covers enabled/disabled redirection and ..-path containment. Describe the implemented shim accurately, without promoting relative-fs-write redirection into general OS containment or implying absolute paths/subprocesses are sandboxed. This supplies the already-in-scope TS caveat update, not a new engine task.

Evidence: rebuilt current core (Cargo fresh=false, reviewed e50fc399f328711cbbe237c1e3918e96c1080656) rejects the old YAML sequence: "functions.src/auth.ts:validateToken.inputs: invalid type: sequence, expected a string at line 3 column 13". Supplementary config_probe.rs/config-probe.stdout.log: /tmp/shatter-followup-numeric-f2LZz8/. Separate CLI refusal logs used preexisting debug binary SHA-256 aa2f0d04ca7d4ab23b16ff375b95e2bcff455ebe55aa0ebc7e7883c8e460da6e, not a claimed rebuild; current host_writes.rs independently confirms the guard.

Scope remains docs-only as already assigned. Executable smoke and production parser controls belong to str-qwua7.9; this note does not add them here or change the config/security schema.

Evidence-location note: /tmp paths above are ephemeral, session-local breadcrumbs and may no longer exist. They are not prerequisites; use the inline reproduction and repository entrypoints.

## Acceptance checks

1. Existing first-run documentation acceptance is qualified so the TypeScript example never treats the Go-only backend variable as proof of confinement; the trusted sample's explicit scoped opt-in is labeled unsandboxed. Replace the obsolete pending TS-redirection caveat with the implemented shim's limited guarantee.
2. The corrected inputs path example includes a matching candidate JSON object array and explicitly states the .shatter/-relative resolution; public config behavior stays unchanged.

Audit reference: shatter-review-2026-09-13/ON-DOCS

Landed on main (1589d493), merge from str-qwua7.8-quickstart-default-deny (21981b1d). Independent code review before merge found three more instances of the same class of bug this issue fixes (QUICKSTART.md CI-pin example, README.md resume-section examples missing --allow-host-writes) plus a stale claim in SPEC.md and README.md (str-02i70 already landed 2026-08-24, all three frontends redirect writes, but the docs still said TS was unsandboxed-unsafe and pending). All fixed inline and verified: task docs-smoke passes, and grepped for any remaining stale str-02i70/'does not yet redirect' references (none). Gate evidence: pre-push hook ran docs gate (skipped optional linters, no failures); land-work verifier ran 3 selected checks, status=passed, against the exact merge preview (tree 3b2d08d9); post-push docs-smoke gate (old, unhardened version still on main) passed; landed tree verified to match the verified preview.

comments.text:
Audit 2026-09-22: two of this issue's acceptance criteria are unmet on main, although the issue is closed.

1. **Sandbox remedy (docs-01, P1).** The addendum required that the TS example "never treat the Go-only backend variable as proof of confinement". title: docs-smoke: execute one real target and validate config/snapshot examples against the real structs
description:
## Problem
`scripts/docs-smoke.py` is the only documentation gate with teeth, and it only checks that flag/subcommand names in fenced shell blocks exist and that JSON/YAML blocks parse. It therefore missed a QUICKSTART first command that is refused at runtime, a SPEC §3.6 config example that cannot deserialize, and a §5.5 snapshot example with the wrong `version` type and a missing required field. The gate should execute at least one documented command for real and validate typed examples against the structs.

## Current code facts
- `scripts/docs-smoke.py` / `scripts/docs-smoke.yaml` — `smoke_commands` are `--help`/`--version` only; ` ```yaml `/` ```json ` blocks go through `yaml.safe_load`/`json.loads` only.
- `SPEC.md` §3.6 `inputs: [list]` vs `shatter-core/src/config.rs` `FunctionConfig.inputs: Option<String>` (docs-only fix in p1-07; this gate must catch the next one).
- `SPEC.md` §5.5 snapshot example: `"version": "0.1.0"` where the struct wants `u32`, and `created_at` (required) is absent (docs-accuracy.md P2).
- There is an existing `schemas` Taskfile task that emits JSON schema; `shatter-core` has `ProjectConfig`/`ShatterConfig` (`config.rs:479-558`) and the snapshot struct that can serve as validators.
- `QUICKSTART.md:78-88` first command needs `--allow-host-writes`; the audit's fixture set lives in the external examples checkout (`scripts/examples_checkout.py`, `SHATTER_EXAMPLES_DIR`), so the executed target must come from an in-repo fixture (e.g. under `examples/go` or `examples/rust`, or a tiny TS file added under `scripts/docs-smoke-fixtures/`).

## Acceptance checks
- `docs-smoke.yaml` gains at least one `smoke_commands` entry that runs `shatter explore --allow-host-writes <in-repo fixture>` and asserts exit 0 and non-empty report.
- Fenced blocks tagged (e.g. ` ```yaml config ` / ` ```json snapshot `) are deserialized against the real structs — either via a new hidden `shatter validate-example --kind config|snapshot -` subcommand or via the `schemas` task's JSON schema — and the gate fails on the pre-fix §3.6 and §5.5 examples (add a test with those two blocks).
- Decision for maintainer: proposed default is the JSON-schema route (no new CLI surface); use the subcommand only if the schema cannot express the untagged enums.
- `task docs-smoke` green on HEAD after p1-07 lands.

## Scope
In: docs-smoke script/yaml, fixture, tagging the SPEC examples, tests.
Out: the doc text fixes (p1-07), markdownlint/lychee in CI (audit item 32).

## Size
Small–medium.

## Provenance

title: Unify explorer::ExploreConfig and orchestrator::ExploreConfig behind a shared base
description:
## Problem
Two `pub struct ExploreConfig` in one crate (28 and 19 fields, 11 shared) are hand-translated field by field in the CLI. New shared fields get dropped in translation — `capture_side_effects` (p1-04) is the confirmed case — and the duplicate name is confusing at call sites. Blocked by p1-04 so the new field is part of the shared set from the start.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-core/src/explorer.rs:101` — `pub struct ExploreConfig` (28 fields; explorer-only: `budget_surplus`, `candidate_inputs`, `candidate_queue_capacity`, `capabilities`, `capture_side_effects`, `claim_policy`, …).
- `shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs:103` — `pub struct ExploreConfig` (19 fields). Shared: seed, timeouts, mocks, mock_params, execution_profile, meta_config, shrink_budget, planner, value_sources, default_execute_plan (+ capture_side_effects after p1-04).
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs:5138-5171` — manual translation.
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/properties.rs:111-140` ↔ `run.rs:540-569` — identical all-default `ExploreConfig { … }` literal (should become `Default`/constructor).
- Cycle note: `explorer.rs:175-178` embeds `scan_orchestrator::{BudgetSurplus, ClaimPolicy}` in the explorer config — keep those in the explorer-only extension, not the shared base, so the base has no scan-scheduler dependency.

## Acceptance checks
- Proposed shape (decision for maintainer, default as stated): `shatter-core/src/explore_config.rs::CommonExploreConfig` embedded in both; `orchestrator::ExploreConfig` renamed to `ConcolicExploreConfig` (the explorer keeps `ExploreConfig` as the public name); `impl From<&ExploreConfig> for ConcolicExploreConfig` copies the shared base and derives the rest.
- `explore.rs:5138-5171` becomes a single `.into()`/constructor call; the `properties.rs`/`run.rs` literals use `ExploreConfig::default()` or a shared constructor.
- Epic no-behaviour-change check: walkthrough log diff empty modulo timings; `task e2e` green.

## Scope
In: the base struct, rename, `From`, CLI call sites.
Out: engine merge; scheduler-type cycle breaking (audit item 19).

## Size
Small–medium.

Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 5 (b); evidence audits/2026-09-04/rust-quality.md (rec. 2), design-foundation.md.

title: Fix TestPlanParam_HTTPRequestBodyInvariants (mined literal vs generic seed) and purge rapid failfiles
description:
## Problem
`go test ./...` in shatter-go is red: `TestPlanParam_HTTPRequestBodyInvariants` fails under rapid with seed 14691893878190207423 — a mined literal `"a"` appears at plan[5] ranked after the same literal emitted as a generic seed at plan[1]. Either the planner emits duplicate literal plans when a mined literal collides with a generic seed, or the property does not model that overlap. A committed April failfile shows this class has happened before and left cruft in git.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-go/planner/param_test.go:574-639` — the property; assertion message at `:639` "mined literal at plan[5] ranked after generic seed at plan[1]"; draws logged at `:582` (`maxPlans: 6`), `:584` (`mined: []string{"a"}`), `:597` (`hasHint: false`).
- `audits/2026-09-04/gates/gate-go-test-novcs.log:16-23` — `--- FAIL: TestPlanParam_HTTPRequestBodyInvariants (0.02s)`, "failed after 64 tests"; repro: `-run=TestPlanParam_HTTPRequestBodyInvariants -rapid.seed=14691893878190207423`.
- `audits/2026-09-04/gates/TestPlanParam_HTTPRequestBodyInvariants-20260903160655-1138468.fail` — the failfile (`v0.4.8#14691893878190207423`).
- `shatter-go/planner/testdata/rapid/TestPlanRequirements_MethodInvariants/` — a committed failfile from April; `testdata/rapid/*.fail` is not gitignored.
- Planner composition entry point: `shatter-go/planner/compose.go` (mined-literal and generic-seed plan sources; see `constructorArgPlansForReceiver` at :240 for the file layout).

## Acceptance checks
- `cd shatter-go && go test ./planner -run TestPlanParam_HTTPRequestBodyInvariants -rapid.seed=14691893878190207423` passes, and `go test ./planner -rapid.checks=2000` passes.
- Proposed default (decision for maintainer, override if the planner's ranking contract says otherwise): on collision the **mined literal wins the rank** (it carries source evidence) and the identical generic-seed plan is **deduped**, so a literal appears once at the mined rank. The fix commit records this; the property is left as-is since it already encodes "mined ranks before generic".
- Before changing ranking, grep golden/snapshot tests in `shatter-go/planner/testdata/` for an encoded duplicate and update them deliberately.
- `testdata/rapid/**/*.fail` removed from git and added to `shatter-go/.gitignore`.
- `task go:test` green in a non-bare checkout.

## Scope
In: planner dedupe or property fix, failfile cleanup, gitignore.
Out: the `-buildvcs` / bare-checkout failure (item 1); broader rapid coverage (audit P3 item 34).

## Size
Small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 3; evidence audits/2026-09-04/gates/gate-go-test-novcs.log, gates/TestPlanParam_HTTPRequestBodyInvariants-20260903160655-1138468.fail, frontends-protocol.md.

title: Thread capture_side_effects through the concolic orchestrator
description:
## Problem
`--capture-side-effects` (and the config field of the same name) is honoured by the random explorer but ignored by the concolic orchestrator: `orchestrator::ExploreConfig` has no such field and every `Command::Execute` it builds hard-codes `capture: true` or `capture: false`. A user running `explore --concolic` cannot turn side-effect capture on or off, and the two engines silently behave differently for the same flag. This is a concrete instance of the explorer-vs-orchestrator drift hazard called out in CLAUDE.md.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-core/src/explorer.rs:2784` — `capture: config.capture_side_effects` (honoured).
- `shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs:103` — `pub struct ExploreConfig` (19 fields), no `capture_side_effects`.
- The eight `Command::Execute` construction sites in `shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs`, by phase:
  - `:1630` `capture: true` — `observe_one` (initial observation of a worklist input; results are reported).
  - `:2981` `capture: true` — fuzz fallback loop inside `explore_with_oracle` (corpus executions; results are reported).
  - `:3514` `capture: true` — shrink phase 1 "bulk shrink" candidate (`explore_with_oracle`, ~`:3496-3520`).
  - `:2314` `capture: false` — `refine_boundaries_async` boundary probes.
  - `:2632`, `:2645` `capture: false` — float-vs-floor divergence probe pairs in `explore_with_oracle` (~`:2606-2650`).
  - `:3558` `capture: false` — grouped shrink candidates; `:3612` `capture: false` — per-param shrink loop (phase 2).
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs:5138-5171` — hand-translation from `explorer::ExploreConfig` to `orchestrator::ExploreConfig`; the field is dropped here.
- `shatter-cli/src/args.rs:608-610` — `#[arg(long, default_value_t = false)] capture_side_effects` ("Disabled by default", str-28ea.1).
- E2E suites: `shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic.rs`, `e2e_concolic_go.rs`, `e2e_concolic_rust.rs` — no case exercises capture with `--concolic`.

## Acceptance checks
- `orchestrator::ExploreConfig` gains `capture_side_effects: bool`. Proposed per-phase policy (decision for maintainer, default as stated): sites whose results are **reported** honour the flag — `observe_one` (:1630) and the fuzz loop (:2981). **Probe** sites keep `capture: false` regardless of the flag, with a comment saying why — boundary refinement (:2314), float/floor divergence pairs (:2632/:2645), and all three shrink candidate sites (:3514/:3558/:3612): their outputs are compared for path/outcome equality and then discarded, capture only adds payload cost, and the accepted shrunk witness keeps the side-effect payload recorded by its original observation. Note that :3514 is currently `true` while the other shrink sites are `false` — the policy makes them consistent.
- CLI translation at `explore.rs:5138` passes the value through.
- New E2E case in `shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic.rs` (TS is enough; Go/Rust not required). Fixture: the tests resolve files via `examples_dir()` (`SHATTER_EXAMPLES_DIR` or `scripts/examples_checkout.py` → `<tmp>/shatter-examples-main/standalone/ts/`), and no standalone fixture there performs a side effect today; the only side-effecting example is `typescript/src/query-creator-short.ts:5` (`console.log("yes")`, which the protocol records as `SideEffect::ConsoleOutput`, `shatter-core/src/protocol.rs:1758`). Proposed default: add `standalone/ts/NN-console-side-effect.ts` (a branch that `console.log`s on one path) to the examples repo, then assert: capture off → `side_effects` empty on every reported call; capture on → at least one `ConsoleOutput` payload on the logging path.
- `task e2e` (or the relevant `e2e-*` task) green.

## Scope
In: the field, the eight sites, CLI threading, E2E test.
Out: unifying the two `ExploreConfig` structs (item 5) — this fix should be shaped so it folds into that later.

## Size
Small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 4; evidence audits/2026-09-04/rust-quality.md ("explorer.rs vs orchestrator.rs", rec. 1).

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (audits/2026-09-04.md, branch audit-2026-09-04)

Proposed per-phase policy (decision for maintainer, default as stated): sites whose results are **reported** honour the flag — `observe_one` (:1630) and the fuzz loop (:2981). **Probe** sites keep `capture: false` regardless of the flag, with a comment saying why — boundary refinement (:2314), float/floor divergence pairs (:2632/:2645), and all three shrink candidate sites (:3514/:3558/:3612): their outputs are compared for path/outcome equality and then discarded, capture only adds payload cost, and the accepted shrunk witness keeps the side-effect payload recorded by its original observation. Note that :3514 is currently `true` while the other shrink sites are `false` — the policy makes them consistent.
- CLI translation at `explore.rs:5138` passes the value through.
- New E2E case in `shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic.rs` (TS is enough; Go/Rust not required). Fixture: the tests resolve files via `examples_dir()` (`SHATTER_EXAMPLES_DIR` or `scripts/examples_checkout.py` → `<tmp>/shatter-examples-main/standalone/ts/`), and no standalone fixture there performs a side effect today; the only side-effecting example is `typescript/src/query-creator-short.ts:5` (`console.log("yes")`, which the protocol records as `SideEffect::ConsoleOutput`, `shatter-core/src/protocol.rs:1758`). title: Epic: explorer/orchestrator/CLI de-duplication (shrink.rs, ExploreConfig, run_explore, main.rs arms)
description:
## Problem
The random explorer and the concolic orchestrator each define a `pub struct ExploreConfig` in the same crate (28 vs 19 fields, 11 shared) that the CLI hand-translates between, so shared fields get forgotten (p1-04 is one symptom). The witness-shrink selection pass is a verbatim 36-line copy in both engines. `run_explore` is 2,658 lines at brace depth 15 — the largest function in the workspace and where random/concolic/genetic wiring diverges — and `main.rs` still carries 200–300-line command arms although its CLAUDE.md says it only dispatches. title: Repair primary checkout (core.bare=true) and add a git-state hygiene check
description:
## Problem
The primary checkout `/home/ketan/project/shatter` has `core.bare = true` in `.git/config`, so `git status`, `git checkout`, `go test` (VCS stamping) and core `scm` tests all fail there, and every AGENTS.md landing step that touches the primary checkout is broken. - `.claude/worktrees/str-umw3/` — gitignored, not in `git worktree list`, gitdir gone, issue str-umw3 closed 2026-04-11; still matches greps (it was the only place `LoopCoverageTracker` "exists").

None emit an executed/cached list.
- `.agent-plugins/bento/bento/land-work/verifier.json` → the verifier; no `executed` evidence field in the contract (bento item 48 is the contract side).
- `CLAUDE.md:19-31` test-tier table does not mention checksum caching.

## Acceptance checks
Amended by the audit 2026-09-22 comment on this issue (findings gates-01, gates-02, tests-ci-06). The CI items ("`.github/workflows/ci.yml:89` calls `task check-fresh`" and the live-run "no `Task "<leaf>" is up to date` line" assertion) moved to str-49drv.144, which requires positive per-leaf execution evidence in CI. This issue keeps the verifier and `/pre-completion` parts. `check-fresh` is viable again only once str-qwua7.3's fix lands (the `meta` stage re-poisoned the cache after deletion).

- A test (`scripts/test_ci_workflow_structure.py` or a new `scripts/test_task_fresh.py`) runs `task check-fresh --dry-run`-equivalent or inspects the Taskfile and asserts every leaf under `check` has a matching checksum removal.
- Verifier execution evidence is defined **per required leaf** from an explicit expected-leaf list: `executed` = at least one `task: [<leaf>]` command echo line and no `Task "<leaf>" is up to date` line; `cached` = an up-to-date line; `missing` = neither. The verifier fails unless every required leaf is `executed`. It uses the shared parser from str-49drv.144 (for example `scripts/task_leaf_evidence.py`), not a new regex. (Replaces "exits non-zero when the executed list is empty".)
- The verifier's final JSON line sets the bento-recognized per-check `executed` boolean (bento `land.py` validates it as a boolean on each `selected_checks[]` entry; bento-rdtn.6) to `true` only when every required leaf executed. No new top-level keys are added to Shatter's strict receipt schema (`scripts/gate-receipt.py::RESULT_KEYS`), per the str-35vtk.24 note.
- A test wired into `meta` runs the verifier against a stub `task` that emits fixture logs for each case and asserts the verdict: all required leaves executed → pass; a mixed log where dependencies are cached but every required leaf executed → pass; one required leaf cached → fail naming it; one required leaf absent → fail naming it; everything cached → fail; a required leaf executed but its command failed → fail on the exit code, with the leaf reported `executed`.

title: Explain why stage-2/3 tasks report "up to date" right after .task/checksum is deleted
description:
## Problem
During the audit, `rm -rf .task/checksum && task check` still reported twelve stage-2/3 leaf tasks as "up to date" and every checksum file was rewritten with the current timestamp. That cannot be explained from `Taskfile.yml` alone and undermines even a fresh variant of the gates (p1-02): if Task can decide "up to date" without the checksum files, deleting them is not sufficient to force execution.

## Current code facts
- `audits/2026-09-04/gates/task-check-real2.log:293-302` — after checksum deletion: `rust-rt:test`, `go:vet`, `ts:install`, `go:test`, `ts:build`, `ts:test`, `cli:test`, `rust-fe:test`, `go:build` "is up to date".
- `Taskfile.yml` — 19 leaf tasks with `sources:`; check whether any also declare `generates:`, `status:`, or `method: timestamp` (Task falls back to `generates`/timestamp comparison, and `status:` short-circuits regardless of checksum).
- Task version in use and its documented semantics for `sources` without `generates` (checksum mode) vs with (timestamp mode) — record both in the write-up.
- `scripts/gate-wrapper.sh` wraps `task <name>-governed`; confirm it does not set `TASK_*` env or `--status` flags that alter the decision.

## Acceptance checks

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
**Root cause found (audit 2026-09-22, findings gates-01 and tests-ci-01).**

**Problem.** `task check` exits 0 in a fresh worktree, but no stage-2 or stage-3 test leaf runs: each one prints `Task "X" is up to date`. The cause is the meta-stage unit test `test_every_emitted_gate_is_a_real_task`. It runs `task --list-all --json` with cwd set to the repo root. On go-task 3.50 and 3.53, computing the JSON `up_to_date` field writes `.task/checksum/*` for every task that has `sources:`. Stage 1 runs `meta` first, so stages 2 and 3 find fresh checksums and skip their work. That is why deleting `.task/checksum` did not force the leaves to execute, which is the question this issue asked.

**Evidence.** Re-verified 2026-09-23. The Taskfile and script citations below are identical on main `70465921` and on the audit snapshot `56c86168`. (Main has since changed `shatter-core/Taskfile.yml`, `shatter-core/src/cache.rs` and `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs`; none of those is cited here.)
- `scripts/test_affected_gates.py:203-212` (`test_every_emitted_gate_is_a_real_task`) runs `subprocess.run(["task", "--list-all", "--json"], cwd=ROOT, ...)`.
- `Taskfile.yml:459` runs that module in `meta` (`python3 -m unittest scripts.test_affected_gates`). `meta` is a dep of `check-static` (`Taskfile.yml:535-546`), which runs before `check-unit` (`:548`) and `check-integration` (`:564`).
- Repro with go-task 3.50.0 in a `git archive` copy of HEAD: `task --list-all` writes 0 checksum files, while `task --list-all --json` writes 39 (core-test-ignored, go-test, ts-test, cli-test, rust-fe-test, conformance, parity, ...). After that, `task sub:test` prints `is up to date` even when a source file's contents have been edited. Adding `--dry`, or running with `TASK_TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)`, avoids the writes to the repo's `.task`. A scratch repro with `includes: sub: {taskfile: ./sub, dir: ./sub}` behaves the same way.
- Durable CI evidence: in run 35756993223 (task v3.53.1), cli:test, conformance, core:test-ignored, docs-smoke, go:test, go:vet, parity, rust-fe:test, rust-rt:test, ts:install and ts:test all report up to date. All 4 `test result:` lines in the log come from the separate shatter-llm step. Retrieve with `gh run view 35756993223 --log --repo <shatter remote>`.
- Local evidence: the poisoned cache is committed on the audit branch; retrieve it with `git show 56c86168:audits/2026-09-22/gates/poisoned-task-cache-snapshot/checksum/cli-test` (and siblings; `git ls-tree 56c86168 audits/2026-09-22/gates/poisoned-task-cache-snapshot/checksum/` lists them). The audit's `check.log` is gitignored and exists only on the audit machine; it is corroborating, not required.
- Introduced 2026-08-29 in 8ae14f13 and b12e3054 (str-35vtk.8). CI wall time dropped from about 330-613 s to 154-225 s from 2026-08-30 onward.

**Fix direction.** Remove the side effect from the meta stage. The simplest options are to run the listing with `TASK_TEMP_DIR` pointed at a throwaway `mktemp -d`, or to add `--dry`. Parsing the Taskfile YAML also works. Then add a regression test to `meta` that snapshots `.task/checksum` before and after it runs.

**Effect on str-qwua7.2.** str-qwua7.2's `check-fresh` design (delete `.task/checksum`, then run) was itself defeated by this bug, because `meta` re-poisoned the cache after the deletion. Once this fix lands, `check-fresh` needs no further adjustment for this cause. The CI part of str-qwua7.2 is being moved to the audit issue `ci-executed-leaf-guard` (see the companion note on str-qwua7.2).

**Widened acceptance for this issue** (replaces "explain why"):
1. No meta-stage command mutates the repo's `.task/`: no `task --list-all --json` against the live tree without `--dry` or an isolated `TASK_TEMP_DIR`. A grep test in `meta` fails if a new unguarded `task --list*` call appears in `scripts/test_*.py` or `demo/test_*.py`.
2. A new regression test, wired into `meta`, copies the repo (or a minimal Taskfile fixture with `includes:` and a `sources:` leaf) into a temp dir, runs the listing helper there, and asserts that `.task/checksum` has no new or changed entries. It then edits the leaf's source file **contents** (not just its mtime; Task's checksum method ignores mtime) and asserts the leaf runs its command (`task: [<leaf>] ...` echo line present, no `is up to date` line). It must fail on the current tree and pass after the fix. Record both runs (command + tail of output) in the close reason.
3. Execution proof on the real repo, independent of whether the tests pass: in a fresh worktree, `rm -rf .task && task meta`, then run each stage-2 and stage-3 test leaf **individually** (`task <leaf>` for cli:test, core:test-ignored, ts:test, go:test, go:vet, rust-fe:test, rust-rt:test, conformance, parity). For each, the output shows the leaf's `task: [<leaf>]` command echo and no `Task "<leaf>" is up to date` line. A leaf whose tests fail still counts as executed for this criterion. Attach the per-leaf echo lines (or a log path) to the close reason. Because `check` is staged and stops at the first failing stage, a full `task check` run is **not** required here; getting it green is `ci-first-real-run-triage`.
4. Optional: file an upstream go-task issue describing the `--list-all --json` side effect and record its link here.

**Out of scope here.** The CI executed-leaf guard (`ci-executed-leaf-guard`) and triage of test failures that surface once leaves run (`ci-first-real-run-triage`). title: Revert unauthorized beads-hook edits from str-35vtk.4
description:
str-35vtk.4 (WS-CS concurrency-safety fixes) landed with an unintended change to scripts/setup-hooks.sh: it now installs a "BEADS HOOK ENV" block (exporting BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT=30) into all five git hooks it manages, including post-merge and post-checkout.

AGENTS.md explicitly designates post-merge and post-checkout as beads-managed and off-limits to hand-editing:

"Leave the managed git hooks alone. .git/hooks/post-merge and post-checkout run `bd hooks run <hook>` to hydrate the local DB from JSONL; they are managed by beads (do not hand-edit) and are shared by every worktree. Do not disable or core.hooksPath-bypass them except transiently for a known-hanging rebase/merge in your own worktree — never in a way that persists or affects other worktrees."

Timeline: a teammate working str-35vtk.4 correctly flagged this conflict and was told to skip item 3 and defer it. A separate concurrent interactive session working the same branch took the opposite call and restored the hook-editing feature (commits "Restore hook latency evidence" / "Restore hook timeout coverage"), and that version landed and closed the issue. The user has confirmed this was NOT a deliberate, informed policy exception.

Already done directly by an agent session (2026-08-24): the live shared .git/hooks/{pre-commit,post-merge,pre-push,post-checkout,prepare-commit-msg} files had their "SHATTER HOOK ENV" block stripped by hand, restoring them to beads-managed-only content, since the block was already actively installed and affecting every worktree on the machine.

Still needed: revert the tracked source in scripts/setup-hooks.sh (the install_hook_env function, ENV_BEGIN/END_MARKER constants, BEADS_HOOKS array, and its call site), delete scripts/test_setup_hooks.sh, remove the two Taskfile.yml references (meta task sources + cmds), and correct the "Beads hook latency and backup semantics" section of docs/perf/ws-cs-concurrency-report.md to record item 3 as deferred pending an explicit policy exception rather than claim it was completed. Keep the legitimate concurrency fixes from str-35vtk.4 (items 1/2/4: gauntlet.sh mktemp isolation, examples_checkout.py flock/freshness, BinaryRegistry persistence locking, fixed-path sweep) untouched — they are unrelated and already correctly landed.

Acceptance: scripts/setup-hooks.sh no longer touches post-merge/post-checkout/pre-commit/pre-push/prepare-commit-msg beyond what it did before str-35vtk.4; `task check` passes; AGENTS.md's hook policy is either respected as-is or, if a real exception is wanted, proposed as an explicit documented amendment in a separate follow-up rather than silently coded around.

title: (BUG) shatter-go/wrapper tests race on shared content-hash-named generated file
description: Discovered confirming CI green after str-35vtk.21 (run 33264217088). task go:test (via check-unit) fails: TestBuildWrapperTargets_ImportedValueParamUsesSafeHTTPConstructor -- vet: open ./shatter_wrapper_d21045db6b7fe526.go: no such file or directory. wrapper.go:281 generates a wrapper filename as fmt.Sprintf("shatter_wrapper_%s.go", hash) where hash is a content hash, and wrapper.go:2945 removes it (os.Remove(tmp)) after use. Because the filename is deterministic (same content -> same hash) and written into a shared working directory, two tests running concurrently (CI's GOFLAGS='-p=4' package/test parallelism) that happen to generate identical wrapper content can race: one test's cleanup deletes the file while another test (or go vet invoked on it) is still reading it, producing an intermittent 'no such file or directory'. This was invisible until now because go:test was never run by CI before str-35vtk.21 replaced the standalone test-standard/parity/conformance steps with task check (which includes go:test via check-unit). Fix: scope each test's generated wrapper file to a unique per-test temp directory (e.g. t.TempDir()) instead of a shared working directory, so concurrent tests never share a filename regardless of content-hash collisions.
close_reason: Landed on main at 2a626706 (merge of str-4doys-vet-overlay-race, head 1bd6148b). Fixed shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper_internal_test.go's TestBuildWrapperTargets_ImportedValueParamUsesSafeHTTPConstructor: its single 'go test -overlay <manifest> .' invocation (the only go-test-based overlay call in the file -- every sibling test uses go build/go run, which never trigger vet) was hitting a Go toolchain caching interaction between go test's implicit vet pass and -overlay virtual paths under CI's persisted cross-run GOCACHE (actions/cache 'Cache cargo registry and build' step), producing an intermittent 'vet: open ./shatter_wrapper_<hash>.go: no such file or directory' when a stale cache entry referenced a since-deleted t.TempDir() real path from an earlier run. Fixed by passing -vet=off, matching the established pattern in every sibling overlay-based test in the same file -- compilation (which still runs) already catches the type/syntax issues vet would add nothing further for here, since the test verifies runtime behavior via actually running the generated code. Gate evidence: go test ./... in shatter-go/wrapper -- 97/97 pass. Confirmed fix in real CI: run 33277936601 fully green (23m21s), all steps passed including Full landing gate (task check), shatter-llm clippy/tests, CI workflow structure regression test -- this was the fourth and final pre-existing bug blocking str-35vtk.21's CI-green closure requirement.

title: (BUG) test_cleanup_merged_remote_branches.sh depends on ambient init.defaultBranch=main
description: Discovered confirming CI green after str-35vtk.21/str-g1yoy landed (run 33178914256). scripts/test_cleanup_merged_remote_branches.sh's throwaway bare repo (git init --bare $BARE) inherits its HEAD symref from the ambient git config's init.defaultBranch. This dev environment has init.defaultBranch=main configured globally, so the bare repo's HEAD already points to refs/heads/main by the time 'git remote set-head origin -a' runs at line 52, and it succeeds. GitHub Actions runners do not have this global config set the same way, so the bare repo's HEAD defaults to refs/heads/master (or is unset) while only 'main' is ever pushed -- 'git remote set-head origin -a' then fails with 'error: Cannot determine remote HEAD', which is not caught (script runs under set -euo pipefail) and aborts task meta, and therefore task check, in CI. This was invisible until now because task meta was never run by CI before str-35vtk.21 replaced the standalone test-standard/parity/conformance steps with task check (which includes task meta via check-static). Fix: after 'git init --quiet --bare "$BARE"', explicitly set its HEAD symref to refs/heads/main (e.g. 'git -C "$BARE" symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main') before anything is pushed, so the test's bare repo does not depend on the invoking environment's init.defaultBranch.
close_reason: Landed on main across two commits: b314ea61 (merge of first fix, head 61fad757) and d6e7f9d0 (merge of second fix, head 39d5d5955, addressing a second bare-repo scenario in the same file added concurrently by str-vsgny after the first fix was authored). Fixed scripts/test_cleanup_merged_remote_branches.sh's two throwaway bare-repo setups (BARE and BARE2) to explicitly set 'git -C $BARE symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main' right after 'git init --bare', instead of relying on the invoking environment's init.defaultBranch config (this dev box has it globally set to main; CI runners do not, so the bare repo's HEAD defaulted to master/unset while only main was ever pushed, making 'git remote set-head origin -a' fail with 'Cannot determine remote HEAD' under set -euo pipefail). Gate evidence: red/green reproduction confirmed locally by running the test under env -i with a fake HOME (no ambient git config) -- failed before the fix (error: Cannot determine remote HEAD), passed after, for both bare-repo scenarios. land-work verifier (task test-standard + parity + conformance) passed on both exact merge candidates. Confirmed fix in real CI (run 33197380586 got past the meta step's cleanup-merged-remote-branches invocation cleanly; the go:test failure later in that same run was the unrelated str-4doys bug, fixed next).

title: Resumed scans produce reports not comparable to uninterrupted scans
description:
## Symptom
A scan resumed from a checkpoint emits a report in which every function completed
before the interruption has vanished from `completed_functions` but is still counted
in `attempted_functions`. Coverage, completion, and behavior metrics collapse in
proportion to how much work the checkpoint carried, so a resumed run reads as a large
regression rather than as an equivalent result.

## Evidence
- On a checkpoint hit the function is pushed into `skipped_functions` as `SkipCategory::Expected` with `reason: "resumed from checkpoint"`, and its behavior map is loaded only to serve as a mock for callers. It emits no `FunctionReport`. Sequential path: `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs:1583-1594`. Parallel path: `:4096-4110`.
- `shatter-core/src/report.rs:107`: `attempted = completed + failed + expected_skipped`. The resumed function stays inside `attempted` while leaving `completed`.
- Net effect on a report consumer: `completed_functions`, `lines_covered`, `branches_covered`, and every rate derived from them under-report by the resumed fraction.

## Desired behavior
One of:
1. A resumed scan reconstructs `FunctionReport` entries for checkpoint-satisfied functions from the cached behavior maps, so the report is equivalent to an uninterrupted run; or
2. The report explicitly marks itself as resumed and partial — a top-level field, not only a per-function reason string — so consumers can refuse to compare it.

Option 1 is the better outcome; option 2 is the minimum that prevents silent misreading.

## Acceptance checks
- A fixture scan interrupted and resumed produces a report whose `completed_functions` and `lines_covered` match an uninterrupted scan of the same fixture (option 1), or carries an unambiguous top-level resumed/partial marker (option 2).
- A regression test covers both the sequential and parallel orchestrator paths, since the behavior is implemented separately in each.

## Scope
In scope: report construction on the resume path.
Out of scope: checkpoint format changes, resume performance.
close_reason: landed on main as part of merge 70465921 (includes 52d9c965's Merge branch 'str-8q1b4-resume-report-parity'). Push was initially blocked by an unrelated pre-existing gate mismatch (str-6nul9, now also landed) -- not caused by this branch's diff.

title: CLI temp Git helper inherits hook env
description:
# CLI temp Git helper inherits hook env

Type: bug
Priority: P1
Labels: cli,git,test

## Symptom

A managed commit hook runs the CLI unit suite while Git repository-selection variables from the outer repository are present. Two `shatter-cli` init tests then fail at their temporary repository's `git commit` step:

- `commands::init::tests::run_implicit_init_skips_a_gitignore_already_tracked_in_git`
- `commands::init::tests::run_init_explicit_still_refreshes_a_tracked_gitignore`

Both report `git ["commit", "-q", "-m", "track gitignore"] failed in /tmp/...`. The same managed run otherwise reaches the CLI suite normally. Any branch whose commit hook runs these tests under the outer Git environment can be blocked.

## Current code facts and cause

`shatter-cli/src/commands/init.rs` has a test-only `git(dir, args)` helper at line 344. It sets `current_dir(dir)` but removes only `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE`. It does not remove `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, or `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, so a managed hook can redirect the temporary repository's index or object lookup to the outer repository.

The production SCM command boundary in `shatter-core/src/scm.rs` removes all six repository-selection variables, but `shatter-cli` is a different crate and cannot call that private core helper. The CLI test helper therefore remains independently contaminated. Use `shatter-core/src/scm.rs::tests::test_git_commands_ignore_foreign_repository_environment` and its `git_environment_isolation_child` helper as the canonical parallel-safe child-process pattern; do not expose the core helper across the crate boundary for this test-only fix. The core test-only `git_ok` helper clears only five variables, so do not copy its list literally: the new CLI helper must clear all six named below.

## Smallest deterministic reproduction

Create a foreign temporary Git repository, resolve its index and object directory to absolute paths, and run the two exact CLI init tests with those paths in the child test command. Each existing test creates its own target repository. Before the fix, its helper initializes and stages in that target but the commit consults foreign repository state and fails. After the fix, both tests pass and commit only inside their own temporary repositories.

From the repository root, a literal reproduction is:

```bash
foreign_repo=$(mktemp -d)
git -C "$foreign_repo" init -q
foreign_git_dir=$(git -C "$foreign_repo" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)
foreign_common_dir=$(git -C "$foreign_repo" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)
foreign_index=$(git -C "$foreign_repo" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)
foreign_objects=$(git -C "$foreign_repo" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path objects)
env GIT_DIR="$foreign_git_dir" GIT_COMMON_DIR="$foreign_common_dir" GIT_WORK_TREE="$foreign_repo" GIT_INDEX_FILE="$foreign_index" GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY="$foreign_objects" GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES="$foreign_objects" cargo test -p shatter-cli commands::init::tests::run_implicit_init_skips_a_gitignore_already_tracked_in_git -- --exact
```

title: Git provider inherits hook index
description:
## Symptom

SCM operations fail, read the wrong repository, or misdetect a valid repository when Shatter runs inside a managed Git hook that exports repository-selection environment variables. During a pre-commit hook, `scm::tests::test_changed_files_non_ascii_path`, `scm::tests::test_changed_files_omits_plain_deletions`, and `scm::tests::test_changed_files_staged_changes_are_subdir_scoped` failed, while the focused eight-test SCM subset passed outside the hook. The hook run reported `fatal: unable to read 48328977...` from the outer repository for temporary-repository tests, and the staged-scoping test returned an empty file list.

## Smallest known reproduction

In `shatter-core/src/scm.rs`, test setup commands use `git_ok`, which removes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` before operating on a temporary repository. Production `run_git` and `detect_provider`, however, remove only `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE`; `show_file_at_ref` removes none of them.

A deterministic regression can initialize separate `foreign` and `target` temporary repositories, obtain absolute foreign paths with `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index` and `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path objects` (or resolve returned relative paths against `foreign`), stage `src/new.ts` only in the target, then invoke the target-facing production operation from a child test process with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` set to those absolute foreign paths. Before the fix, Git consults foreign repository state despite `current_dir(target)`; afterward it must discover and use the target repository. A child process avoids mutating process-global environment while Rust tests run in parallel.

## Expected behavior

Every Git subprocess launched by the SCM module is bound to the repository discovered from its `root` argument and is unaffected by ambient repository-selection variables injected by hooks or parent Git processes. The three production launch sites are `detect_provider`, `show_file_at_ref`, and the shared `run_git` path. Centralize their `Command` construction so each removes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, and `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`. These six variables are in scope because they can redirect repository metadata, index, or object lookup; other Git configuration and behavior variables are out of scope for this focused defect.

## Acceptance checks

1. Add deterministic child-process regression coverage that uses absolute foreign Git index/object paths, fails against the current production behavior for repository-state contamination, and does not mutate the parent test process's environment.
2. Route `detect_provider`, `show_file_at_ref`, and `run_git` through one command-construction boundary that removes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, and `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, without changing public SCM contracts; preserve `run_git`'s load-bearing `-c core.quotepath=false` prefix unchanged.
3. Run `rtk cargo test -p shatter-core scm::tests::test_changed_files` with normal parallelism, then stage the issue changes and run the normal `rtk git commit -m "<issue-id>: fix Git subprocess environment isolation"`; both commands exit 0, and the managed pre-commit output contains none of the three named SCM failures.

Regression coverage must include the previously unprotected `show_file_at_ref` path as well as repository discovery or file-listing behavior.

## Scope

In scope: `shatter-core/src/scm.rs`, its tests, and the environment boundary of every Git subprocess launched there. Out of scope: changes to managed hooks, bypassing hooks, the separate test-tier implementation that exposed this defect, or broader SCM behavior changes. Expected size is one focused Rust file under 100 lines of diff.

title: Gate receipt schema and writer
description:
Task, P1, `build,landing,quality-gates`; blocked by issue11.

`python3 scripts/gate-receipt.py write --candidate TREE --base TREE --tier local|ci --gate-result RESULT.json...`; stdout `{status:"written",path,digest}`, exit0; invalid/failed64; discovery/I/O74. TREE is 40 lowercase hex, must exist locally as Git tree and equal `git rev-parse TREE^{tree}`. Gate-result v1 `{gate,argv:[strings],started_at,ended_at,exit_code}` with RFC3339 UTC second timestamps.

Normative `docs/perf/gate-receipt-v1.md`: canonical UTF8 JSON sorted keys/no whitespace/final newline. Both candidate and base must be 40 lowercase hex, exist locally as Git tree objects, and equal `git rev-parse <value>^{tree}`. Receipt v1 is exactly `{schema:int=1,candidate_tree:string,base_tree:string,tier:string local|ci,gate_results:[{gate:string,argv:[strings],started_at:string,ended_at:string,exit_code:int=0}],bindings:{code:[{path:string,sha256:string}],locks:[{path:string,present:bool,sha256:string|null}]},tools:[{name:string,version:string}],started_at:string,ended_at:string,digest:string}`. Timestamps are RFC3339 UTC seconds; top start=min gate start and end=max gate end. Gate results sort by gate and are unique. Code/lock arrays sort by path; tools sort by name.

All bound repository bytes come from candidate-tree blobs, never the working tree. Code paths are Taskfiles from sorted `git ls-tree -r --name-only <candidate>` matching `*Taskfile*.yml`, plus required `scripts/gate-wrapper.sh` and receipt script; each binding is lowercase SHA-256 of raw blob bytes. Missing required code is invalid. Locks always contain entries for `Cargo.lock,shatter-rust/Cargo.lock,shatter-rust-runtime/Cargo.lock,shatter-ts/package-lock.json,shatter-go/go.sum`; absent candidate blob is `{present:false,sha256:null}`, present is true plus raw-blob SHA-256. Dirty/untracked files have no effect. Tools are the six names `cargo,go,node,npm,rustc,task` with trimmed full stdout of their version commands. To compute digest, omit the `digest` member entirely, canonical-encode the remaining top-level object with the same sorted-key/no-whitespace rules and no final newline, SHA-256 those UTF-8 bytes, then store `digest="sha256:<64-lowercase-hex>"`; final receipt includes digest and one newline. Derive `repo_key=sha256(realpath(git rev-parse --git-common-dir))`; default path is `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/shatter-gate-receipts/v1/<repo_key>/<candidate-tree>.json`, one replaceable receipt per repository/candidate. Create directories0700 and atomically write file0600; same-candidate concurrent writers may replace only with a complete valid receipt. Writer never invokes gate.

Acceptance: golden bytes/digest and each discovery/input rejection; atomic concurrent old-or-new reads; modes/exits/stdout. Out: validator/hooks/signing.
acceptance_criteria: golden bytes/digest and each discovery/input rejection; atomic concurrent old-or-new reads; modes/exits/stdout.

title: Pressure-aware gate wait policy
description:
Task, P1, build,concurrency,resource-governance; blocked by str-35vtk.13,
str-35vtk.17, str-35vtk.18 (unchanged bd deps).

Before allocation run provider; while blocked hold no capacity. Poll
SHATTER_GATE_POLL_SECONDS default5 (positive integer or exit64). On ready
allocate then recheck; if blocked release and loop. Changed reasons print to
stderr immediately and unchanged reasons every30s; ordinary waits do not
write events. One monotonic deadline covers pressure and allocation;
SHATTER_GATE_WAIT_TIMEOUT default1800 positive integer, timeout exits75
without launch. Bypass is launch-time-only: read SHATTER_GATE_BYPASS_REASON
once at wrapper start. After Unicode trim it must be 1..256 UTF-8 bytes with
no ASCII control characters; invalid present value exits64. If valid and the
initial provider measurement is blocked, bypass pressure immediately, then
use the full normal timeout solely to wait for weighted capacity. If absent
at launch, it cannot be enabled mid-wait and pressure timeout exits75.
Provider/semaphore errors are never bypassable. Issue str-35vtk.18 is used
only for an attempted bypass. After capacity, write gate_bypass event with
reason and initial pressure reasons before launch. Failed event write
releases/refuses. Bypass does not skip allocation or infrastructure errors.

ADDITION FROM 2026-08-25 CROSS-REPO RECONCILIATION: since str-35vtk.17 is
revised to make CPU saturation blocking (new signal
`cpu_some_avg10`/`SHATTER_GATE_MAX_CPU_SOME_AVG10`, reason `above_max` when
exceeded — see that issue's revised body), this issue's existing "Before
allocation run provider... On ready allocate then recheck; if blocked
release and loop" control flow already covers CPU the same way it covers
memory/disk/IO, because it treats the provider's `status` field opaquely
(ready/blocked) rather than special-casing individual signals. No new
control-flow change is needed here, only new acceptance coverage below.
Implementation location for this wait/allocation loop is not fixed by
either the original or this revision (likely `scripts/gate-wrapper.sh`
alongside the weighted-allocation client from str-35vtk.12, but that is an
implementation decision for whoever picks this up, not specified here).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (original list, unchanged, plus one new case):
- fake clock/provider/allocator sequence including ready->blocked recheck
- cadence/deadline/invalid values
- failure-mode-by-bypass matrix and durable-before-launch
- NEW: a case where the fake pressure provider reports `blocked` due to
  `cpu_some_avg10` alone (reason `above_max`, no memory/disk/IO signal
  blocking) with no Shatter-owned process contributing to that CPU load
  (simulating a different project's overload, per the diagnostic recorded
  in str-35vtk epic notes, 2026-08-25 entry, where Kapow/PickPackIt/Bento
  processes drove host load while Shatter's own gate was idle), asserting
  the wait policy does not allocate capacity and does not bypass without an
  explicit, valid SHATTER_GATE_BYPASS_REASON.

OUT OF SCOPE (unchanged): thresholds, killing active work, cleanup, remote
audit.

CROSS-REPO DEPENDENCY STATUS: str-35vtk.12 is revised (2026-08-25) to depend
on the Bento governor epic bento-dyp7. str-35vtk.13 (gate lease lifecycle,
one of this issue's blockers) has NOT been revised as part of this
reconciliation pass — it was out of the explicitly scoped set (.12/.17/.19)
and still describes a Shatter-local worktree-lease flock file. Whether .13
also needs to depend on bento-dyp7's contract (e.g. if lease identity moves
into the governor) is an open follow-up, not resolved here — do not assume
it was already revised.
acceptance_criteria: fake clock/provider/allocator sequence including ready->blocked recheck; cadence/deadline/invalid values; failure-mode-by-bypass matrix and durable-before-launch.

title: Gate event log store
description:

Default event file `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/shatter/gate-events.jsonl`; lock is the same path plus `.lock`; create parent0700/file0600. Append first under lock; if resulting count >10000, validate every line then keep newest8000 including triggering line, tempfile same directory, atomic replace while lock held. Corruption exits74 without mutation.
