title: Gate pressure signal provider
description:
Task, P1, build,resource-governance,linux; no Shatter-internal prerequisite.
No hard cross-repo blocker either (see DEPENDENCY NOTE below) — this can
proceed independently of the Bento governor epic.

CHANGE FROM ORIGINAL: the original design made CPU saturation
(`cpu_some_avg10`) report-only ("CPU is report-only" in the original body) —
every other signal (memory, disk, I/O) was blocking, but CPU was not. The
2026-08-25 cross-repo reconciliation found this gap means a CPU-only host
overload caused entirely by a *different* project's processes (e.g. Kapow
Vitest workers and golangci-lint, both observed running concurrently with a
Shatter landing-preview build during the diagnostic recorded in str-35vtk
epic notes, 2026-08-25 entry: host load ~112.84) would NOT stop a Shatter
gate from starting, since Shatter's provider only made memory/disk/IO
blocking.

CPU saturation must become a blocking admission signal, on par with the
existing memory/disk/IO handling. Target file: `scripts/gate-pressure.py`
(per the original issue's own spec; file does not exist yet — this issue
creates it). Keep the existing signal contract structure (stable name
`cpu_some_avg10`, JSON v1 schema) but change its `ready` semantics from
always-non-blocking to blocking against a threshold override, the same
pattern already specified for `memory_full_avg10` and `io_some_avg10`:

- New override `SHATTER_GATE_MAX_CPU_SOME_AVG10`: finite nonnegative decimal
  percentage; invalid value exits 70 with reason `invalid_override`,
  consistent with `SHATTER_GATE_MAX_MEMORY_FULL_AVG10` /
  `SHATTER_GATE_MAX_IO_SOME_AVG10`. PROPOSED DEFAULT: 20.0 (matching
  `SHATTER_GATE_MAX_IO_SOME_AVG10`'s default) — confirm at implementation
  time; if a different default is chosen, document why here.
- When `cpu_some_avg10` exceeds the threshold, use reason `above_max` (same
  vocabulary already specified: below_min, above_max, unsupported, missing,
  unreadable, malformed, invalid_override) — this mirrors exactly how
  `io_some_avg10` exceeding its max is reported.

All other original behavior is unchanged: read
`${SHATTER_PROC_ROOT:-/proc}/meminfo` and pressure files; memory/disk minima
overrides (`SHATTER_GATE_MIN_MEM_BYTES` default 8589934592,
`SHATTER_GATE_MIN_DISK_BYTES` default 10737418240);
`SHATTER_GATE_MAX_MEMORY_FULL_AVG10` default 1.0,
`SHATTER_GATE_MAX_IO_SOME_AVG10` default 20.0; `SHATTER_PRESSURE_FS_PATHS`
device dedup and ancestor-stat fallback (default paths: PWD,
`${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$PWD/target}`,
`${SCCACHE_DIR:-${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/sccache}`,
`${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`); on Linux, missing/unreadable/malformed meminfo or
statvfs failure exits 70; missing PSI is unsupported/nonblocking, malformed
present PSI exits 70; on non-Linux all proc signals unsupported, disk still
evaluated, status derives from disk; no waiting; <=2s; read-only/no network.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (adds CPU-blocking cases to the existing list):
JSON schema/golden plus boundary, duplicate device, missing/malformed,
invalid override, injected roots/paths, non-Linux, timeout and mutation
tests (unchanged from original), PLUS:
- A case where `cpu_some_avg10` alone exceeds
  `SHATTER_GATE_MAX_CPU_SOME_AVG10` while memory/disk/IO are all ready,
  asserting overall `status: blocked` and reason `above_max` on the
  `cpu_some_avg10` signal.
- A boundary case at exactly the threshold.
- A case with `SHATTER_GATE_MAX_CPU_SOME_AVG10` unset, using the documented
  default (20.0, or whatever is confirmed at implementation time).
- An invalid-value case matching the existing invalid-override tests for
  the other two percentage overrides.

OUT OF SCOPE (unchanged): wait/bypass/cleanup — this issue reports
pressure, str-35vtk.19 acts on it.

DEPENDENCY NOTE (cross-repo; recorded here in body text, not a bd link):
this provider reads local host `/proc` state directly and does not itself
call the Bento host-wide governor (epic bento-dyp7), so it has no hard
blocking dependency on that epic landing and can be implemented
independently. However, once bento-dyp7 lands, str-35vtk.12's admission
call will already incorporate the governor's own multi-signal check; the
implementing agent should re-check at that point whether this provider
becomes a redundant Shatter-local duplicate of governor-side CPU admission,
or remains necessary as a pre-check before even attempting governor
admission. Flag that reconciliation rather than silently doing both
long-term.
acceptance_criteria: JSON schema/golden plus boundary, duplicate device, missing/malformed, invalid override, injected roots/paths, non-Linux, timeout and mutation tests.
close_reason: Landed on main at 29586ef0 (merge of str-35vtk.17-gate-pressure-signal, head b6cf22c1). Gate evidence: land-work verifier (scripts/land_work_verifier.sh) against exact merge candidate — task test-standard: exit 0, task parity: exit 0, task conformance: exit 0 (all 3 selected checks passed). Additionally: 30/30 scripts/test_gate_pressure.py unit tests pass (golden schema, boundary-exact, duplicate-device dedup, missing/malformed meminfo & PSI, invalid overrides incl. NaN/inf, injected proc-root/fs-paths, non-Linux behavior, CPU-blocking cases per the 'CHANGE FROM ORIGINAL' spec amendment), task smoke passed. Independent code review found 1 Important bug (resolve_fs_paths() trusted stale $PWD env var over os.getcwd(), defeating disk-pressure checks when spawned as a subprocess after a parent chdir) — fixed with 2 regression tests before landing, verified via re-run gates. SHATTER_GATE_MAX_CPU_SOME_AVG10 default 20.0 confirmed at implementation time per the issue's proposed default.

title: Gate resource-class policy
description:

title: Gate lease lifecycle
description:
Task, P1, `build,concurrency,resource-governance`; blocked by issue2.

Outer wrapper exports `SHATTER_GATE_LEASE_ID=<pid>:<proc-start-ticks>:<32-lowercase-hex>`, `SHATTER_GATE_CAPACITY`, `SHATTER_GATE_WEIGHT`, and holds shared flock `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/shatter-worktree-leases/<sha256(realpath(PWD))>` for the command. All allocation/worktree FDs are close-on-exec and never inherited. Nested passthrough requires `SHATTER_GATE_LOCK_HELD=1`, valid metadata, and live matching owner PID/start ticks; invalid/stale exits70. Nested weights are ignored with stable warning. Launch command in its own process group. TERM/INT forward to group, wait, close leases, and wrapper exits143/130 respectively; ordinary child exit is propagated. SIGKILL owner releases locks even if child survives because it inherited no lease FDs.

Acceptance: nested identity/forgery matrix; child signal receipt plus exact wrapper exits and immediate reacquisition; exclusive cleanup contender blocked during gate and admitted after. Out: cross-machine lease and deletion.

title: Weighted semaphore allocation
description:
Task, P1, build,concurrency,resource-governance; blocked by str-35vtk.11 AND
by the new cross-repo dependency below.

SUPERSEDES the original Shatter-local design. The 2026-08-25 cross-repo
tracker reconciliation found this issue's original design (a Shatter-local
flock-based weighted slot semaphore under `SHATTER_HEAVY_SLOTS`) would create
a fourth independent host-admission mechanism alongside PickPackIt, Kapow, and
Bento's existing `run-heavy` — none of which contend for the same capacity
pool. Evidence (recorded in str-35vtk epic notes, 2026-08-25 entry): a live
diagnostic found host load ~112.84 90.23 57.18 with Shatter's own semaphore
not held at all, driven by concurrent Kapow/PickPackIt/Bento processes; a
single-project semaphore cannot prevent that.

CHANGE: `scripts/gate-wrapper.sh [--weight N|--exclusive] <label> <cmd...>`
acquires weighted capacity from the host-wide governor being built in Bento
(epic bento-dyp7 "Host-wide weighted admission governor for heavy agent
jobs", client CLI/contract fixed by its child bento-dyp7.1 "Design doc:
host-wide governor contract") instead of implementing its own flock slot
directory. Shatter's job is to be a thin, correct client of that governor's
contract, not to reimplement weighted admission locally.

Preserve all weight/clamp/exclusive semantics already specified for this
issue, since they match the governor's required contract:
- N is base-10 >= 1; invalid/missing exits 64 before launch.
- Requests above capacity clamp and print
  `weight-clamped requested=N capacity=C`; `--exclusive` == capacity.
- Nesting (a heavy gate that invokes a nested heavy sub-gate) must not
  deadlock against the outer lease (re-entrancy) — this is the governor's
  responsibility to provide; this issue's job is to verify
  `gate-wrapper.sh` correctly relies on that contract rather than acquiring
  a second independent lease.
- Normal exit, SIGTERM, and SIGKILL of the gate-wrapper process must leave
  the governor's capacity immediately reacquirable (whole-DAG lease
  release) — verify against the governor's contract, do not reimplement
  flock-release logic locally.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Weight/clamp/exclusive/invalid-value behavior matches the bullet list
  above, tested via the governor's documented fake-provider/deterministic
  test harness (bento-dyp7.2), not a live multi-process capacity fixture
  against a Shatter-local flock dir, since capacity is no longer
  Shatter-local state.
- If the governor is unreachable, misconfigured, or errors,
  `gate-wrapper.sh` fails closed (refuses to launch the wrapped command)
  rather than falling back to unmanaged execution.
- Normal exit / TERM / SIGKILL of the gate-wrapper owner release capacity
  immediately, verified against the governor's lifecycle contract.

OUT OF SCOPE: task mapping, metadata, fairness beyond no-partial-hold
(unchanged from original), plus: implementing the weighted-capacity
accounting itself — that lives in bento-dyp7.2, not here.

DEPENDENCY (cross-repo; recorded here in body text since bd has no
cross-repo dependency links): blocked by Bento epic bento-dyp7 reaching a
landed, concretely-versioned client contract (specifically its design-doc
child bento-dyp7.1 — client CLI shape, weight/capacity semantics,
fail-closed behavior, whole-DAG lifecycle). Do not begin implementation
before bento-dyp7.1 lands.

Existing within-repo dependency (str-35vtk.11 blocks str-35vtk.12) is
unchanged and remains a real bd dep link.
acceptance_criteria: capacity2/slot2-held fixture proves weight2 never hoards slot1 and weight1 runs; exact exclusive/clamp/invalid/capacity tests; normal exit, TERM, and SIGKILL owner leave all flock slots immediately acquirable.

title: react-hook adapter is applied but execution overflows the stack: 183 TS functions lost
description:
## Problem

The react-hook adapter IS auto-selected and active for React components, and execution still fails
with `Maximum call stack size exceeded`. The whole file then fails, and its functions never enter
the spec at all — so they are invisible in coverage numbers rather than counted as uncovered.

This is the single largest TypeScript blocker measured in a 306-file run: 183 functions,
17,889 span lines.

## Current code facts (verified 2026-08-14, engine @ ce1d0199)

- Detection works and is automatic. `shatter-ts/src/analyzer.ts:493` calls `recognizeReactHooks`,
  and `analyzer.ts:511-528` converts any react-hook hint into
  `invocation_model = { kind: "adapter", adapter_id: REACT_HOOK_ADAPTER_ID, scenario_schema: { kind: "hook_callable_return" } }`.
- The adapter implementation exists: `shatter-ts/src/react-hook-invocation.ts` (React shims wired at
  `:394-395`; `shatter-ts/src/executor.ts:831-834` resolves `react/jsx-runtime` and
  `react/jsx-dev-runtime`).
- For the failing component the adapter was selected, with high confidence, and logged as active:

  ```
  [info]   BookmarkButton adapter [active]: ts/module-resolution/tsconfig-paths (config)
  [info]   BookmarkButton adapter [active]: react-hook (auto-applied)
  ```

  Artifact `invocation_model`:
  `{"kind": "adapter", "adapter_id": "react-hook", "scenario_schema": {"kind": "hook_callable_return"}}`
  with `adapter_hints[0].confidence: "high"` and reasons
  `["Calls useCallback imported from 'react'", "Calls custom hook useAuthStore", ...]`.

- The engine already has a root-cause bucket for the failure: `ts_root_causes` records
  `parse_jsx_or_type_runtime`.

So this is NOT a detection gap and NOT a missing adapter. The adapter runs and then blows the stack.

## Smallest reproduction

Target repo kapow (`web/`), engine @ ce1d0199:

```
web/src/components/search/BookmarkButton.tsx   (a Mantine ActionIcon + Tooltip button,
                                                useCallback + two zustand store hooks)

error: "observe stage failed: unexpected response from frontend:
        execute error (InternalError): Execute failed: Maximum call stack size exceeded"
summary: total_functions 1, completed 0, failed 1, runtime_failed 1, elapsed 4.26s
         ts_root_causes: {"parse_jsx_or_type_runtime": {"count": 1, "line_weight": 83}}
```

**First work item**: reduce to an in-repo fixture — a component that calls `useCallback` and renders
a third-party JSX element — and confirm it reproduces. Required by acceptance regardless.

## Scale across the run (306 TS files)

| ts_root_cause | Functions | Span lines |
|---|---|---|
| `parse_jsx_or_type_runtime` | 183 | 17,889 |
| `other` | 7 | 314 |
| `missing_browser_api` | 3 | 380 |

TS totals: 380 completed, 212 failed, 2 skipped; 33,796 discovered span lines of which 11,662
(34.5%) belong to functions that failed outright.

## Expected behavior

React components routed through the react-hook adapter execute without stack overflow, or — where a
component genuinely cannot be executed — the function is reported as skipped with the specific
`parse_jsx_or_type_runtime` reason and the rest of the file still completes.

## Open question for triage, with an explicit stop rule

Whether the overflow originates in the React shim/dispatcher in `react-hook-invocation.ts`, in JSX
runtime resolution in `executor.ts`, or in the component's third-party UI library (Mantine) is NOT
established. Capture the stack trace first — for an unbounded-recursion bug the repeated frame
pattern usually names the origin immediately, and it is the cheapest artifact available.

**Stop rule**: spend at most one reduction pass building the fixture. If a `useCallback` +
third-party JSX component does not reproduce, add the two zustand store hooks (the failing component
also calls `useAuthStore` and `useBookmarkStore`); if that still does not reproduce, stop, attach the
stack trace and the negative result to this issue, and split the investigation into a follow-up
rather than widening this one.

## Acceptance

- An in-repo fixture reproducing the overflow exists under the TS example/fixture set.
- That fixture executes successfully through the react-hook adapter, or is reported as a skip with
  reason `parse_jsx_or_type_runtime` without failing its whole file.
- A TS test covers the fixture.
- The 380 TypeScript functions that complete successfully today still complete — no regression.
- External confirmation (not a CI gate): re-running kapow's `web/` tier reduces the
  `parse_jsx_or_type_runtime` count from its 183-function baseline. Note that 183 is the size of a
  coarse root-cause bucket; it is NOT established that all 183 are stack overflows rather than a
  mix, so score this criterion on the direction of travel plus the fixture, not on a fixed number.

## In scope / out of scope

In scope: the overflow on adapter-routed components, and file-level survivability of one failing
component.
Out of scope: coverage attribution for adapter-owned executions — that is epic `str-j49xg`
("Adapter-owned executions return empty coverage fields"). This issue is about executions that
CRASH; that epic is about executions that succeed but report nothing.

## Size

Medium — unknown root cause behind a reduction step, with a clear stop/split rule.

## Artifacts

- `kapow/web/shatter-artifacts/explore-results/web_src_components_search_BookmarkButton.tsx/00023_BookmarkButton.json`
- `kapow/web/shatter-artifacts/explore-results/*/summary.json` (the 306-file aggregate)
- `kapow/shatter-artifacts/files/web__src__components__search__BookmarkButton.tsx.log`

title: Null return collapses to returns void, hiding an unobserved execution
description:
## Problem

Two `package main` entry helpers execute 100 iterations and record no executed lines, no return
value, and no thrown error — and are then classified `returns void`, despite the analysis stage
correctly typing the return as `complex/error`.

This is a silent false negative: the spec asserts a behavior the function cannot have. A wrong spec
is worse than a reported failure, because nothing downstream flags it for review.

There are two separable defects. This issue covers (B), which is well-defined, and timeboxes (A).

- **(A)** The execution is not observed: `lines_executed` is empty and the returned error is lost.
  Root cause NOT established.
- **(B)** The classifier cannot distinguish "returned void" from "returned null", and silently picks
  void even when the analyzed return type is non-void.

## Current code facts (verified 2026-08-14, engine @ ce1d0199)

`shatter-core/src/spec.rs:440-443` is where the classification is cemented:

```rust
match &ec.canonical_return_value {
    Some(v) if !v.is_null() => Postcondition::Returns { value: v.clone() },
    _ => Postcondition::ReturnsVoid,
}
```

Any null (or absent) canonical return value becomes `ReturnsVoid`, with no reference to the
function's analyzed return type. `Postcondition::ReturnsVoid` is defined at `spec.rs:168` and
rendered as the string `"returns void"` at `spec.rs:500` and `spec.rs:941`. A parallel collapse
exists in `shatter-core/src/compare.rs:386-388`.

For a Go function returning `error`, this also means a legitimately-nil error is indistinguishable
from a void return in the spec — a pre-existing expressiveness gap that this same fix addresses.

## Smallest reproduction (evidence is external; an in-repo fixture is part of the work)

Observed in target repo kapow:

```
api/cmd/fixtureutil/main.go::run(databaseURL, fixtureDir string, skipMigrate bool) error
inputs ("", "", false), DATABASE_URL unset
```

whose first guard makes a non-nil error unavoidable:

```go
dsn := databaseURL
if dsn == "" { dsn = os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL") }
if dsn == "" {
	return fmt.Errorf("--database-url flag or DATABASE_URL env var is required")
}
```

Recorded:

```json
{"inputs": ["", "", false], "return_value": null, "thrown_error": null, "lines_executed": []}
lines_covered: 0 / 36 · iterations: 100 · timed_out: false
return_type: {"kind": "complex", "complex_kind": "error"} · branches: 7
class: "Class 1 — returns void"
```

Same shape for `api/cmd/testlanes/main.go::run() error` (0 / 75, 100 iterations). These were the only
2 of 764 api/ observation records with `iterations > 0` and `lines_covered == 0`.

**First work item**: reduce to an in-repo fixture under `examples/go/` — a few-line `package main`
with `func run() error { return fmt.Errorf("boom") }` — and confirm whether it reproduces. That
fixture is required by the acceptance criteria regardless of the outcome.

## Leads, explicitly not a diagnosis

- Both instances are named `run`, both in `package main`, both called by `main()` which then calls
  `os.Exit`. Whether any of that is causal is NOT established.
- It is not "package main is broken": sibling functions in the same files report coverage normally —
  `printLanes` 2/12, `collectOutput` 6/15, `resolveParallelism` 4/9, `(LaneReport).print` 7/21.
- `testlanes::run()` takes no parameters and calls `flag.Parse()`; `fixtureutil::run` takes three
  parameters and does not — so a flag-parsing explanation does not cover both.

## Representation decision (state before implementing)

The no-value-observed arm needs a representation. Recommendation: add a distinct `Postcondition`
variant rather than overloading `ReturnsVoid`, and handle it at the three existing match/render
sites — `spec.rs:168` (definition), `spec.rs:500` and `spec.rs:941` (rendering). Also decide whether
`compare.rs:386-388`, which has the identical collapse, is fixed in this change; recommendation: yes,
since this repo's recurring failure mode is fixing one of two parallel paths.

Verify early that the analyzed return type is reachable at the `spec.rs:440` site. If it is not,
(B) becomes plumbing work and the size estimate below is wrong.

## Acceptance

- (B) `spec.rs` never emits `ReturnsVoid` for a function whose analyzed return type is non-void. It
  either reports the observed value (including an explicit nil/null) or, when no value was observed
  at all, a non-behavioral status — never a confident void class. Unit test in `spec.rs` covers both
  arms.
- An `examples/go/` fixture with an error-returning `run()` in `package main` is added and exercised
  by `cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go`.
- (A) Timeboxed: if the in-repo fixture reproduces the empty `lines_executed`, fix it here; if it
  does not reproduce, record the negative result in a comment and open a follow-up rather than
  expanding this issue.

## In scope / out of scope

In scope: the `spec.rs` classification rule, the matching `compare.rs` collapse, the fixture, and a
timeboxed (A) investigation. Spec output strings change, so updating affected regression snapshots
is in scope.
Out of scope: a general "every unobservable function must be reported as failed/skipped with a
reason" contract across all frontends — that is a broader reporting change; file separately if (A)
turns out to need it.

## Size

Medium — (B) is small and well-defined; (A) is an investigation with an explicit stop rule.

## Artifacts

- `kapow/api/shatter-artifacts/explore-results/api_cmd_fixtureutil_main.go/00036_run.json`
- `kapow/shatter-artifacts/files/api__cmd__fixtureutil__main.go.json`
notes:
(A) investigation result: NEGATIVE — does not reproduce in-repo.

Added examples/go/main-run-error-return/main.go: a package-main `run(name string) error`
helper called by `main` -> `os.Exit`, with an unavoidable-error empty-input guard, closely
mirroring kapow's api/cmd/fixtureutil/main.go::run and api/cmd/testlanes/main.go::run.

New e2e test shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic_go.rs::e2e_go_main_run_error_return_is_observed_and_never_void
explores both the erroring ("") and nil-returning ("alice") arms and asserts every discovered

lines_executed is populated for both paths, the guard's error message is observed
("ERROR:name is required"), and the nil-error return is observed ("null" via canonical Returns).

So the underlying empty-lines_executed / lost-return-value observability gap described in this
issue's (A) does NOT reproduce against this minimal in-repo package-main + run() + os.Exit shape.

DATABASE_URL env-var read, the specific project/module layout, or something else about kapow's
build), or has since been fixed by unrelated work. Recommend filing a follow-up issue to

(B) shipped in this same change: added Postcondition::Unobserved (spec.rs), threaded the

title: Per-function explore timeout cannot bound a single long execute: functions run 3x over budget and report timed_out=false
description:
## Problem

`--timeout-explore` is only evaluated between iterations, so it cannot bound a single slow execute
round-trip. On large Go packages one round-trip costs tens of seconds, so a function configured with
`--timeout-explore 30` and `max_iterations: 100` performs exactly ONE iteration, runs ~3x past its
stated timeout, and then reports `timed_out: false`.

The result is that a one-sample behavior class is indistinguishable from a thoroughly explored one,
and the per-function timeout does not do what its name promises.

## Current code facts (verified 2026-08-14, engine @ ce1d0199)

- `shatter-core/src/explorer.rs:1362-1370` — the budget check sits at the top of the exploration
  loop, before the Execute round-trip:

  ```rust
  if let Some(timeout) = config.timeout_explore
      && explore_start.elapsed() >= timeout
  {
      timed_out_due_to_budget = true;
      break;
  }
  ```

  Nothing cancels an execute already in flight, so elapsed time is only observed after a full
  round-trip completes.
- `explorer.rs:1317` declares `let mut timed_out_due_to_budget = false;`.
- `explorer.rs:485-493` documents the contract this feeds:
  "a successful Result with `timed_out=true` means 'exploration ran out of time mid-flight,' not
  'explored everything.'" (`ObservationOutput.timed_out`, added by str-gz8j; the CLI downgrades to
  `OutcomeStatus::TimedOut` from it.)

So the intended semantics exist; the check simply cannot fire for a function whose single execute
overruns the budget, and the loop may instead exit through a natural-termination path.

## Local reproduction

Any function whose single Execute round-trip outlasts the per-function budget shows this. Force it
with a tiny budget against any Go example that needs a real build:

```bash
shatter explore examples/go/<any-example>.go --timeout-explore 1 --spec-out /tmp/out.json
```

Then compare the recorded `wall_time_ms` against the 1-second budget and check `timed_out` in the
observation: the wall time exceeds the budget while `timed_out` stays `false`, because the check at
`explorer.rs:1362` is only reached after the round-trip returns. A dedicated slow fixture (a build or
function that reliably takes several seconds) makes the assertion deterministic for the regression
test.

## Evidence (target repo kapow, 764 observation records under api/)

Run flags: `--timeout-explore 30 --request-timeout 240 --build-timeout 240`, config
`max_iterations: 100`.

- 414 records with `iterations == 1`: median `wall_time_ms` **87,048** — roughly 3x the 30s
  per-function timeout — and `timed_out: true` in ZERO of them.
- 350 records with `iterations > 1`: median `wall_time_ms` 46,792, median 4.5 iterations.

Verbatim, `api/graph/resolver/auth.resolvers.go::(*mutationResolver).CreateTeam`:

```json
{"status": "completed", "wall_time_ms": 91043,
 "observation": {"iterations": 1, "unique_paths": 1, "timed_out": false,
                 "lines_covered": 3, "total_lines": 18}}
```

with a single `raw_results` entry.

## Explicitly unresolved

Whether each of those 414 functions stopped because of the budget or through a legitimate
natural-termination path (exhausted worklist after a first-iteration panic) is NOT established from
the artifacts — and that ambiguity is itself part of the problem: the output does not record WHY
exploration stopped. Establishing the stop reason is the first work item.

## Expected behavior

1. A function whose wall time exceeds `--timeout-explore` is not reported as a clean completion. At
   minimum the budget is re-checked after the execute returns; better, the execute is cancelled at
   the deadline.
2. The observation records why exploration stopped (budget / max_iterations / exhausted worklist /
   plateau), so a one-iteration result is self-explaining.

## Intended consequence

This deliberately reclassifies runs that previously reported `completed`. Functions that overran
their budget will start surfacing as `OutcomeStatus::TimedOut` in CLI output, which is the point —
the str-gz8j contract already says `timed_out=true` means "ran out of time mid-flight". Expect
checked-in report snapshots to move.

## Acceptance

- No observation record can carry `timed_out: false` while its wall time exceeds the configured
  `timeout_explore`; a unit test in `explorer.rs` covers a single-execute overrun.
- The observation carries a stop-reason enum, and it is surfaced in explore output.
- `cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go` passes; add or extend a case asserting the stop reason on a
  deliberately slow fixture.
- Parity: this touches spec/report output, so run `task parity` and `task conformance`; update
  `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` only if a declared capability changes.

## In scope / out of scope

In scope: the timeout check placement, the stop-reason field, and their reporting.
Out of scope: reducing the ~87s per-execute cost in the Go path. That is real but separable — file
a follow-up once a stop reason makes the slow cases identifiable.

## Size

Medium — a small explorer change plus a protocol-visible field, so parity/conformance gates apply.

## Cross-reference

`str-garn`, `str-0wxw`, `str-hrg2` cover per-iteration slowness for axum handlers — the cost half of
the same story, in a different frontend.
notes:
Investigation (2026-08-18): Confirmed root cause and found this is a parallel-parity gap, not a from-scratch fix.

ROOT CAUSE in shatter-core/src/explorer.rs (random-explore path, explore_function, main loop ~L1325-1627):
- The only timeout check is at the TOP of the loop (L1362-1371), before the Execute round-trip. Nothing rechecks elapsed wall-time immediately after a slow execute returns.
- Critically, there is NO final 'deadline already crossed' recheck after the loop exits, regardless of which branch caused the break (max_iterations exhaustion L1326-1360, natural worklist exhaustion via meta_strategy.next()==None L1492, or custom-generator unavailability L1461/1481). If the loop exits via any of THOSE paths on the same pass where wall-clock has already blown past timeout_explore (e.g. because the single execute that just completed took 3x the budget), timed_out_due_to_budget stays false and the observation is reported as a clean 'completed' run — exactly the str-gz8j contract violation the issue describes.

THIS IS A KNOWN-FIXED CLASS OF BUG IN THE SISTER PATH: shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs (concolic path) already solved this exact problem under str-jeen.65. It:
1. Has a proper TerminationReason enum (MaxIterations/MaxExecutions/CoveragePlateau/WorklistExhausted/TimeoutExplore/McdcComplete) tracking why each phase's loop exited (L302-317).
2. After the main loop AND after every subsequent phase (float-probe pre-pass, refine, shrink, fuzz), re-checks  regardless of how that phase's loop exited, and forces  if the wall clock has already passed the deadline (L3409-3420, L2967-2969, etc.) — this is the exact 'catch it even on natural termination' safety net explorer.rs is missing.
3. Final ExploreResult.timed_out = timed_out_overall || termination_reason==TimeoutExplore (L3750-3751), which pipeline.rs then maps into ObservationOutput.timed_out.

However: even orchestrator.rs's TerminationReason enum does NOT propagate as a field into ObservationOutput (shatter-core/src/explorer.rs L431-495) — only the derived bool  survives into the protocol-visible/serialized struct. So the tracker's acceptance criterion #2 ('observation carries a stop-reason enum, surfaced in explore output') is NOT satisfied by EITHER path today — this part is genuinely new, protocol-visible work spanning both explorer.rs and orchestrator.rs, not just a port of an existing pattern.

PLAN:
1. Port the str-jeen.65 'final deadline-crossed recheck regardless of exit reason' pattern into explorer.rs's main loop (and its shrink pass, which already partially has ad-hoc checks at L1711/1757/1798/1805 but no unconditional post-loop catch-all). This alone fixes the P1 correctness bug (timed_out:false while 3x over budget).
2. Add a serializable stop-reason field to ObservationOutput (new small enum, since orchestrator::TerminationReason isn't Serialize), wired from both paths, satisfying acceptance criterion #2.
3. Regression test: extend explorer.rs unit tests using the existing SHATTER_OBSERVER_EXEC_SLEEP env var on protocol/observer-recording-frontend.sh (already supports simulating one slow execute) to assert a single overrunning execute yields timed_out=true even when it's the only iteration and no other break condition naturally routes through the timeout branch.
4. cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go plus task parity / task conformance since this touches protocol-visible ObservationOutput.

Flagged to team-lead (main) that the tracker issue actually has a full, detailed description+acceptance-criteria already (contrary to the 'thin/title-only' framing in the dispatch prompt) — proceeding per the issue's own documented acceptance criteria.
Investigation (2026-08-18): Confirmed root cause and found this is a parallel-parity gap, not a from-scratch fix.

ROOT CAUSE in shatter-core/src/explorer.rs (random-explore path, explore_function, main loop ~L1325-1627):
- The only timeout check is at the TOP of the loop (L1362-1371), before the Execute round-trip. Nothing rechecks elapsed wall-time immediately after a slow execute returns.
- Critically, there is NO final "deadline already crossed" recheck after the loop exits, regardless of which branch caused the break (max_iterations exhaustion L1326-1360, natural worklist exhaustion via meta_strategy.next()==None L1492, or custom-generator unavailability L1461/1481). Confirmed empirically: with max_iterations=1 and a single execute forced to ~1s (via SHATTER_OBSERVER_EXEC_SLEEP=1 on protocol/observer-recording-frontend.sh) against a 300ms timeout_explore, the loop exits via the max_iterations-exhaustion branch (L1326-1360, textually BEFORE the timeout check at L1362) on the second top-of-loop pass, so `timed_out_due_to_budget` is never set even though wall time is already 3x over budget. With max_iterations left large (100), the same slow single-execute scenario DOES correctly surface timed_out=true, because the timeout check happens to run before any other break condition — so the bug specifically manifests whenever a function's effective per-function budget (max_iterations) is small/near-exhausted at the same moment the wall clock has already blown past timeout_explore, e.g. simple/early-return functions that only produce 1 candidate.

THIS IS A KNOWN-FIXED CLASS OF BUG IN THE SISTER PATH: shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs (concolic path) already solved this exact problem under str-jeen.65. It:
1. Has a proper TerminationReason enum (MaxIterations/MaxExecutions/CoveragePlateau/WorklistExhausted/TimeoutExplore/McdcComplete) tracking why each phase's loop exited (L302-317).
2. After the main loop AND after every subsequent phase (float-probe pre-pass, refine, shrink, fuzz), re-checks deadline_crossed() regardless of how that phase's loop exited, and forces timed_out_overall = true if the wall clock has already passed the deadline (L3409-3420, L2967-2969, etc.) - this is the exact "catch it even on natural/other-reason termination" safety net explorer.rs is missing.
3. Final ExploreResult.timed_out = timed_out_overall || termination_reason==TimeoutExplore (L3750-3751), which pipeline.rs then maps into ObservationOutput.timed_out.

However: even orchestrator.rs's TerminationReason enum does NOT propagate as a field into ObservationOutput (shatter-core/src/explorer.rs L431-495) - only the derived bool timed_out survives into the protocol-visible/serialized struct. So the tracker's acceptance criterion #2 ("observation carries a stop-reason enum, surfaced in explore output") is NOT satisfied by EITHER path today - this part is genuinely new, protocol-visible work spanning both explorer.rs and orchestrator.rs, not just a port of an existing pattern.

PLAN:
1. Port the str-jeen.65 "final deadline-crossed recheck regardless of exit reason" pattern into explorer.rs's main loop (and its shrink pass, which already has ad-hoc checks at L1711/1757/1798/1805 but no unconditional post-loop catch-all). This alone fixes the P1 correctness bug (timed_out:false while 3x over budget).
2. Add a serializable stop-reason field to ObservationOutput (new small enum, since orchestrator::TerminationReason isn't Serialize), wired from both paths, satisfying acceptance criterion #2.
3. Regression test: extend explorer.rs unit tests using the existing SHATTER_OBSERVER_EXEC_SLEEP env var on protocol/observer-recording-frontend.sh (already supports simulating one slow execute) to assert a single overrunning execute yields timed_out=true even when max_iterations=1 routes the loop through the budget-exhaustion branch instead of the timeout branch.
4. cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go plus task parity / task conformance since this touches protocol-visible ObservationOutput.

Flagged to team-lead (main) that the tracker issue actually has a full, detailed description+acceptance-criteria already (contrary to the "thin/title-only" framing in the dispatch prompt) - proceeding per the issue's own documented acceptance criteria.

title: shatter-go: filename-scoped config globs silently fail for nested relative paths
description:
The file half of a `functions:` config key is matched with filepath.Match against whatever path spelling the caller holds. TargetRelpath collapses ABSOLUTE paths to their basename, but leaves clean nested RELATIVE paths intact, and filepath.Match "*" never crosses a separator. So a filename-scoped key ("*.resolvers.go:*", "resolver.go:*") matched for callers holding an absolute path and silently failed for callers holding a repo-relative one.

Impact: the planner/hint path (frontendsetup, absolute analysis.SourceFile) resolved `mocks` entries while the prepare/execute bridge (handler.configMockConfigs, repo-relative request `file`) did not. Config mock expressions therefore appeared in planning output (artifact `mock_symbols`) but were never substituted into the built harness — the mock silently did nothing, and the real dependency ran.

Repro (kapow-jdb8): `.shatter/config.yaml` with `"*.resolvers.go:*": mocks: {"auth.GetAccount": "auth.StaticAccount()"}`; `shatter explore api/graph/resolver/auth.resolvers.go:CreateTeam` kept hitting the real auth gate ("authentication required") on every iteration. No WARN was emitted — configMockConfigs just returned nil.

Fix: matchFileGlob in shatter-go/config/loader.go — a pattern containing "/" stays anchored to the full relative path; a filename-scoped pattern (no separator) falls back to matching path.Base(relpath). Applies to all consumers of the shared key space (mocks, defaults, generators, receiver, policy), which is the point: the same key must mean the same thing regardless of path spelling.

Note this affects the safety-policy resolver too — filename-scoped policy entries now apply where they previously silently did not.
close_reason:

Anchored patterns (containing /) match the full relative path; filename-scoped patterns also match the basename, in a strictly lower specificity tier so they can never beat or tie an anchored key. The safety-policy gate uses the new MatchTargetAnchored and keeps failing closed.

title: WS-F: Batch-landing protocol for swarm leads (lands with WS-E)
description:
New .claude/skills/batch-land/SKILL.md + AGENTS.md "Batch Landing (lead agent)" section + .claude/swarm-config.md quality-gates rewrite (bento:swarm reads swarm-config.md; bento plugin skills aren't editable — repo docs carry the doctrine).

Protocol: (1) batch pushed, reviewed, non-overlapping branches, ≤5 per batch or ~30min window; a branch whose affected-gates output hit the check fail-safe lands in a batch of ≤2. (2) Lead only, one landing at a time, sequential --no-ff merges in the primary checkout; nothing pushed until green (preserves serial-merge + ancestry doctrine and the shared-checkout/beads-DB constraint). (3) Record each branch's affected-gates output pre-merge; after all merges run ONE `task check` + union of conditional gates (e2e-*, walkthrough, gauntlet) via gate-wrapper. (4) Pass: push once, letting the pre-push hook run as normal — an exact-tree local-tier receipt (str-35vtk.23/.24) from the batch check just performed lets the hook's own Shatter quality-gate re-run be satisfied by receipt reuse instead of recomputed, but the hook itself always executes, including Beads and any other non-Shatter safety hooks it runs; never pass `--no-verify` to skip the hook wholesale, since that would also skip those unrelated safety checks → verify each branch by ancestry → batch bd close → delete branches. (5) Fail — attribution ladder: (a) failing gate in exactly one branch's list → suspect; (b) re-merge all except suspect, re-run only the failing gate; (c) ambiguous → linear removal in reverse merge order; (d) rebuild integration without offender, re-run failing gate + one final check on the reduced batch (explicit skill step), land the rest, reopen offender with gate output, reassign. Worst case = 1 full check + ≤N single-gate re-runs.

Acceptance: dry-run simulation on 3 scratch branches (one intentionally breaking a unit test): batch check fails, ladder isolates offender, reduced batch lands green, offender reopened with failure output; swarm-config.md no longer instructs per-merge full checks; teammate completion messages required to include the Gates-selected row.
notes:
2026-08-24 plan refinement: str-35vtk.26 now blocks this issue. Before enabling reuse, collect 10 distinct successful non-tracker main-push shadow samples with zero false accepts and explained misses. A valid exact-tree receipt may later skip only the Shatter quality section; do not use blanket --no-verify because Beads and unrelated safety hooks must still run.
2026-09-23 str-35vtk.26 progress: scripts/receipt-shadow-threshold-check.py landed on branch str-35vtk.26-receipt-shadow-evidence-threshold. It queries the str-35vtk.18 event log for single-ref refs/heads/main|master receipt_shadow events (str-35vtk.25) whose local commit is now an ancestor of origin/main and diff_class=other, dedupes by candidate tree, and applies the zero-false_accept/zero-unexplained-unexpected_miss rule against the first 10 distinct eligible entries. Full fixture-based test coverage (dedup, beads_only exclusion, abandoned/unreachable-commit exclusion, multi-ref exclusion, deterministic first-10 selection, false_accept fail, unexplained unexpected_miss fail, linked-issue-explained pass, stubbed bd-note append) passes: 24/24 in scripts/test_receipt_shadow_threshold_check.py.
Per explicit user-approved scope, this session did NOT run the tool against the real production gate-event log expecting a pass -- the shadow check only landed today (str-35vtk.25) and the real log almost certainly does not yet have 10 eligible real main-push events. The str-35vtk.26 operational milestone (10 real clean/explained observations) has not yet accumulated and remains open for a future session to close once it has. This note's revision to the description's step (4) language above reflects the intended scope: --no-verify itself is never used; only Shatter's own quality-gate re-run inside the hook is satisfied by receipt reuse.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
Audit 2026-09-22 (finding agent-repo-19, `audits/2026-09-22/findings.json`):
this issue's premise is stale and its scope needs updating.

- The body says "bento:swarm reads swarm-config.md" and plans a
  `.claude/swarm-config.md` quality-gates rewrite. The installed bento
  swarm no longer reads it:
  `bento/plugins/claude/bento/skills/swarm/scripts/swarm-discover.py:18-22`
  reads only `swarm-config.json` (repo root), `.claude/swarm-config.json` or
  `.codex/swarm-config.json` (bento-96ua.2, closed). It validates a
  `landing` block (`mode`, `gate_scope`, `full_gate`, `max_batch_size`,
  `linger_minutes`, `batch_boundary_paths`; `:88-183`). An invalid or
  absent block degrades to serial landing. The schema is in bento
  `skills/swarm/references/landing-config.md`.
- Shatter has only `.claude/swarm-config.md` (plus an untracked
  `.codex/swarm-config.md` symlink in the primary). No `swarm-config.json`
  exists, so swarms land serially and the .md gates (`/check-all`,
  `/pre-completion`, `/walkthrough-review`) are at best read as prose.
  `/check-all` also has `disable-model-invocation: true`
  (`.claude/skills/check-all/SKILL.md:5`), so a lead cannot invoke it
  through the Skill tool. Reference `task check` directly.
- `CLAUDE.md:57` states "The lead runs one full `task check` at batch
  landing", but nothing configured implements batch landing today.

**Proposed scope update:**
- Write the config at the repo root as `swarm-config.json`, so both
  runtimes read it: `swarm-discover.py:18-22,257-270` checks the
  runtime-specific file (`.claude/` or `.codex/swarm-config.json`) and then
  the root file, and Codex never falls back to `.claude/swarm-config.json`.
  Delete `.claude/swarm-config.md` and the primary's untracked
  `.codex/swarm-config.md` symlink (or keep the `.md` only for Epic-mode
  prose that bento does not read).
- `landing` block: `full_gate: task check`, and `mode` / `max_batch_size`
  matching this issue's protocol.
- **`gate_scope` needs an adapter; `task affected` does not fit the
  contract.** bento's `landing-config.md` defines `gate_scope` as a
  "command that emits scoped gate commands for a diff", and teammates run
  the emitted commands. `task affected` (`Taskfile.yml:511-514`)
  *executes* the selected gates and prints status and logs; it emits no
  commands. Add a small executable (for example `scripts/gate-scope.sh`)
  that calls `python3 scripts/affected-gates.py --base <base> --head <head>`
  and prints one runnable command per selected gate (`task <gate>`,
  nothing for `(none)`), with no other stdout.
- **Behavioural validation, not just warning-free discovery.** A
  `gate_scope` string whose first word resolves on `PATH` passes
  `swarm-discover.py` validation whatever it prints. Acceptance: (1)
  `swarm-discover.py --runtime claude` and `--runtime codex` both report
  the same non-null `landing` block with `mode` as configured and no
  warnings; (2) a test runs the adapter on a fixture diff touching one
  crate and asserts stdout is exactly the expected `task <gate>` lines,
  and on a docs-only diff asserts it prints only the docs gates (or
  nothing); (3) every emitted line runs successfully when executed as a
  command in a scratch worktree (record the output in the close reason).
- Re-check whether the manual batch-land skill this issue plans is still
  needed, given bento swarm's built-in batch mode, and whether step (4)'s
  "push once with --no-verify" survives. Audit decision D4 and the 08-24
  note already rule out hook bypass, so drop it.
- Until batch landing is configured and validated, soften `CLAUDE.md:57`
  to say batch landing is planned (str-35vtk.9), not current.

title: WS-C: Resource governance: job budgets + heavy-tier slot semaphore + timing capture
description:
1. Checked-in repo .cargo/config.toml: `[build] jobs = 8`; `[env] RUST_TEST_THREADS = { value = "4", force = false }` (pre-set env wins; CI sets CARGO_BUILD_JOBS to uncap). Taskfile top-level env (overridable): `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=${SHATTER_BUILD_JOBS:-4}` for task-mediated builds, `GOFLAGS=-p=${SHATTER_GO_PROCS:-4}`, `GOMAXPROCS=8`, `NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS=${SHATTER_TEST_THREADS:-4}` (effective with WS-M). Jest already --runInBand. A solo human overrides the env to reclaim the box.
2. New scripts/gate-wrapper.sh (`gate-wrapper.sh <label> <cmd...>`): counting semaphore of `SHATTER_HEAVY_SLOTS` (default max(1, nproc/8) = 4 here) flock slots under ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/shatter-heavy-slots/; block with a loud periodic "waiting for slot" message (timeout → loud error, not silent hang). Then `nice -n 10 ionice -c2 -n7 <cmd>`. Re-entrancy: SHATTER_GATE_LOCK_HELD=1 → passthrough (check → conformance nesting must not deadlock). Timing: append CSV to ~/.cache/shatter/gate-times.csv (timestamp, worktree, label, wall secs, exit code, 1-min loadavg, slots held); truncate to last 10k lines.
3. Wrap top-level heavy tiers only: `check`, `check-fast`, `e2e`/`e2e-*`, `conformance`, `parity`, `gauntlet`, `walkthrough`, `core:test-ignored`. Light tasks unwrapped.
4. AGENTS.md: parallel-agent resource etiquette (slot/budget env vars); don't bypass the wrapper with bare `cargo test --test e2e_*` when an equivalent task exists.

Acceptance: rerun WS0 concurrency headline (4 × task check): bounded loadavg, responsive shell, aggregate wall ≤ serial baseline; 5th concurrent gate blocks until a slot frees (CSV timestamps); nested check acquires one slot; CSV rows have all 7 fields; `task test-quick` unaffected.
notes:
Landed on main at 0407b3dd (merge commit) via bento:land-work.

Root fix (already implemented on this branch through an earlier review round): scripts/gate-wrapper.sh — a machine-wide counting semaphore (flock-based, default max(1, nproc/8) slots under ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/shatter-heavy-slots/) wraps all top-level heavyweight gates (check, check-fast, e2e*, conformance, parity/golden, walkthrough, gauntlet, core:test-ignored) with nice/ionice and timing capture to ~/.cache/shatter/gate-times.csv; re-entrancy via SHATTER_GATE_LOCK_HELD prevents nested-task deadlock. .cargo/config.toml caps cargo jobs=8 / RUST_TEST_THREADS=4 (force=false, pre-set env wins); Taskfile defaults GOFLAGS=-p=4 / GOMAXPROCS=8. CI overrides via env (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4). AGENTS.md documents the etiquette.

Independent code review of this landing pass found and I fixed 3 additional correctness bugs beyond the prior review round:
1. SHATTER_HEAVY_SLOTS=0 passed numeric validation but the >=1 floor only applied to the *computed default*, not an explicit value — seq 1 0 iterates zero times, hanging every gate forever. Now floored to 1 for explicit values too.
2. gate-times.csv's append-then-trim was not atomic against concurrent appenders from other agents on the same machine (the exact scenario this branch governs) — a trim's tail-into-tempfile-then-mv could silently drop a concurrently-appended row. Now one critical section under a dedicated flock.
3. configure-bindgen.sh's existing-[env]-table detection (grep) was looser than its insertion pattern (awk exact match), so a CRLF/trailing-whitespace [env] header was detected but the workaround was silently never inserted while the script still printed success and exited 0. Also found while fixing this: GNU grep -E does NOT interpret \t/\r as escapes (only -P does) — my first fix attempt for this had the same latent bug; verified against real GNU grep 3.11 (not the interactive-shell's ugrep-based grep function) before landing. Both patterns now embed real tab/CR bytes.

Filed non-blocking follow-ups for two PLAUSIBLE (inherent-tradeoff) findings: str-ep8s4 (widened 30m go test timeout holds gate slot longer on hangs), str-0f6ze (monitor whether jobs=8 cap worsens the documented check-unit nested-build flake).

Gate evidence (project verifier scripts/land_work_verifier.sh, run against the exact merge candidate — itself now routes parity/conformance through the new gate-wrapper.sh, a real end-to-end exercise of this change):
  task test-standard -> passed
  task parity        -> passed
  task conformance    -> passed

Also ran directly: functional smoke tests of gate-wrapper.sh (basic run + CSV row format, re-entrancy passthrough, semaphore serialization under 1 slot with 2 concurrent jobs, SHATTER_HEAVY_SLOTS=0 no longer hangs) and configure-bindgen.sh's detection/insertion logic against a CRLF [env] header, all passing; bash -n syntax check on both scripts.

title: Build/test efficiency overhaul (caching, gate dedup, diff-scoped gating, batch landing)
description:
The build+test cycle is prohibitive: ~11.4GB of build artifacts rebuilt cold per worktree (target/ 6.4G, shatter-rust/target/ 4.7G, shatter-ts/node_modules 243M; ~24 worktrees, most carrying stale multi-GB target dirs), no cargo profile tuning, no sccache/fast linker, demo scripts compile from scratch into mktemp CARGO_TARGET_DIRs, parity/conformance/golden-test/e2e each rebuild the three frontends, e2e tests run `go build` at test time (shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic_go.rs:87, e2e_concolic.rs:1960), TS e2e_concolic.rs has no `#[ignore]` so 23 node-subprocess tests run even in `task test-quick`, and `task pre-completion` runs smoke + full `task e2e` + the ~16-subtask `check` fan-out for every issue. N concurrent agents thrash the machine, and shared mutable state (/tmp/shatter-examples-main with no lock, gauntlet's fixed /tmp paths) corrupts concurrent runs.

User-approved plan (2026-07-10, two planning sessions merged). **Child issue bodies are authoritative**; full plan text committed as docs/perf/efficiency-plan.md (mirror) by WS0. Standing constraints: quality reduction is NOT in scope — anything removed from a gate must be shown covered elsewhere on the landing path; the landing gate runs the full suite exactly once per landing; PBT case tiering approved (reduced cases inner tiers, full at landing + CI).

Waves: WS0 (baseline) → A (caching) + B (gate dedup) + CS (concurrency safety) → C (governance) + D (demos) + M (test mechanics) → E+F together (diff-scoped gating + batch landing) → H (closeout). Later phase, out of scope: TIA revival (docs/plans/str-zwgc-test-impact-analysis.md, tracker str-cl53).

Out of scope for the epic: merging shatter-rust into the root cargo workspace (rejected: generated fixture crates path-dep on shatter-rust-runtime; shared lockfile couples concurrent agents — record as decision note); sccache in GitHub CI (deferred); pnpm migration; automating host-level installs (user runs them).

Evidence: four concurrent checks took 1,611s, peak load 58.86, and only 2/4 passed; current registered worktrees carried roughly 185 GiB across about 40 Rust target directories. New work extends closed .5 governance to whole-DAG weighted/fail-closed admission, completes CI/LLM coverage, introduces exact-tree receipt shadowing, hardens cleanup, and skips deletion/tracker-only rebuilds. Embedded-Go content-addressed reuse is deliberately deferred until str-o09e closes.
2026-08-25 later live diagnostic (cross-repo host-governance reconciliation): host load average ~112.84 90.23 57.18 observed while no Shatter heavy-tier semaphore lock was held. title: [bug] config mocks schema split-brain: Rust MockOverride rejects Go frontend's expression-string form
description:
### Problem

The Rust CLI and the Go frontend parse the same `.shatter/config.yaml` `functions.<glob>.mocks` section with incompatible schemas, so the str-c8djq execute-time mock expressions are unusable in any project the CLI touches:

- Go frontend (shatter-go/config loader, str-c8djq): `mocks` values are bare STRINGS — `"auth.GetAccount": "auth.StaticAccount()"` (Go source expression substituted at the call site).
- Rust CLI (shatter-core/src/config.rs:873/933 → `crate::auto_mock::MockOverride` at auto_mock.rs:270): `mocks` values must be a STRUCT `{return_values: Option<Vec<Value>>, behavior: Option<MockBehavior>}`.

Repro (kapow, 2026-07-06): adding the Go-style string entry and running `shatter explore api/graph/resolver/auth.resolvers.go` fails before analysis with:
`Error: failed to parse config YAML '.shatter/config.yaml': functions.*.resolvers.go:*.mocks.auth.GetAccount: invalid type: string "auth.StaticAccount()", expected struct MockOverride at line 22 column 26`

Conversely, a Rust-style struct entry would fail the Go loader (map[string]string). One YAML cannot satisfy both consumers. The str-c8djq E2E (`e2e_go_mock_substitution_reaches_mock_only_branches`) missed this because its fixture config lives under examples/go/mock-subst/ where only the frontend's upward walk finds it — the CLI never parses that file.

### Requested Behavior

1. Rust `MockOverride` accepts BOTH forms: bare string (shorthand for `{expression: <s>}`) and struct, with a new optional `expression: Option<String>` field (serde untagged enum or custom deserializer normalizing to the struct). The CLI does not act on `expression` (execute-time substitution is frontend-owned); it must simply parse, preserve, and not choke.
2. Go loader (shatter-go/config): accept BOTH forms symmetrically — bare string (expression) and struct with optional `expression` / `return_values` / `behavior` keys (ignore the non-expression keys or map them to MockConfig fields where they already exist).
3. Cross-consumer test: one YAML fixture containing both a string-form and a struct-form mock entry parses successfully in BOTH the Rust config loader (unit test in shatter-core/src/config.rs tests) and the Go loader (shatter-go/config test).
4. E2E hardening: the mock-substitution E2E (shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic_go.rs, e2e_go_mock_substitution_reaches_mock_only_branches) should drive the run through a path where the RUST side also parses the fixture config (e.g. pass the fixture dir as project root / config resolution entrypoint), so schema drift between the two consumers fails the gate. If that wiring is disproportionate, add instead a dedicated cross-schema conformance test and note it in the e2e comment.
5. Parity/doc: shatter-go/CLAUDE.md hint-config section and protocol/parity-matrix.yaml hint_config_v1 notes updated to document the accepted forms.

### Acceptance

- kapow-style config (`"auth.GetAccount": "auth.StaticAccount()"` under a basename glob) parses in both consumers; `shatter explore <file>` proceeds past config load and the substitution fires (kapow-jdb8 validation unblocks).
- Struct-form entries with return_values/behavior keep existing semantics in both consumers.
- `task parity` + `task conformance` + Go/Rust unit suites green; e2e_concolic_go still passes.

### Out of Scope

- Making the CLI act on `expression` (wire-level return_values path remains str-8v66).
- TS/Rust frontend mock substitution.
close_reason:
Landed on main via merge of str-7lab0-djcv2-mock-integration.

Both consumers now accept both mocks YAML forms: Rust MockOverride deserializes from a bare string (shorthand for {expression}) or the struct form; the Go loader's MockValue unmarshals from a scalar or a mapping, tolerating CLI-owned keys. Cross-consumer tests pin one YAML parsing in both loaders.

Two follow-ups surfaced while landing:
- The acceptance-criterion repro (kapow config mocks taking effect) did NOT work from this change alone — filename-scoped config globs silently failed for nested relative paths, so the mocks resolved for planning and vanished at execute time. Fixed as str-cl19s in the same merge.
- Independent review found generate_auto_mocks gating pure-utility passthrough on overrides.contains_key, which an expression-only entry now trips; fixed in ae3b5e4f via MockOverride::has_cli_directives.
- Untagged MockOverride degrades serde parse diagnostics: filed as str-qpttz.

Gate evidence on the exact merge candidate: task test-standard exit 0; task parity exit 0; task conformance exit 0 (42/42); cargo test -p shatter-core --test e2e_concolic_go --ignored exit 0 (19 passed); go test ./... in shatter-go exit 0 (1441 passed); land-work project verifier passed with 0 unverified paths.

title: TS input generator fills array-typed params/fields with {} and degrades Date/Response/function params — 83/127 pickpackit web error_only from one root cause
description:
## Evidence (pickpackit web --all milestone scan, engine eb3681e4, artifacts scan-results/92eec168...)

127/341 functions error_only; 83 share ONE root cause — the generated input drops the prototype/shape of non-plain-object types:
- method-not-a-function (49): array/collection field filled as {} → .map/.find throw. AvatarStack input {"people": {}, "size": null} → 'TypeError: people.map is not a function'; buildEntries input {"entries": {}, ...} → 'draft.entries.map is not a function'.
- not-iterable (25): array param filled as {} → spread/for..of throw. itemIdsAlreadyOnTrip input ["tripId", {}] → 'packingItems is not iterable'; groupItemsByCategory input [{}, {}] → 'items is not iterable'.
- not-a-function (9): Date/Response/callback params degraded: shortDate gets {"getFullYear": null,...}; buildApiError's response.text missing; requestClose props.onClose null.

All 127 error_only artifacts show constraint_stats total_constraints:0 / solver_guided_inputs:0 — these die on unguided structural fills before any solver involvement.

## Relation to str-9cqde

str-9cqde recovered array-ness in TypeInfo conversion for the direct cases; its review follow-up notes list the residual conversion sites that still lose array-ness: union members (Widget[] | null), return types, tuple syntax [A,B], array-typed aliases (type Widgets = Widget[]). This bug is the input-generator-visible consequence; fix either the residual TypeInfo sites, the type→value mapper (seed [] plus a small populated T[] when the type is Array<T>/iterable), or both.

## Also

Instantiate known built-ins instead of plain-object stand-ins: Date → new Date(...), Response-like → minimal object with text()/json(), function-typed params → jest-style recording stub (frontend already has behavior-mock machinery).

## Cross-language

Go/Rust frontends already synthesize slices/Vec correctly; this is TS-specific in implementation, but the contract ('array-typed inputs are generated as arrays; built-in types are instantiated, not shape-mocked') belongs in the parity notes for any future frontend (C++/Java collections likewise).

## Acceptance

- pickpackit focused web scan of domain/bundles.ts + inventoryPicker.ts + primitives.tsx: the named functions leave error_only.
- Unit tests in shatter-ts for array/Date/function param generation; E2E case with a cross-file array param exercising solve.
- Full-corpus web error_only count drops materially (expect ~-60 to -80 of 127).

title: Plan field unsupported behavior
description:
## Problem

After typed receiver field plans and TS request typing exist, Shatter needs unsupported behavior plus conformance coverage that keeps plan-feature failures clean and consistent across frontends. Construction should not move in lockstep yet, but the wire shape and unsupported semantics should.

## Current Code Facts

- Go consumes `Command::Execute.plan`; TS/Rust currently do not.
- `protocol/PARITY.md` already tracks `ts-rust-execute-plan-not-implemented`.
- `ExecuteResult.outcome` exists in the core protocol. Go emits `outcome`; TS/Rust may not.

## Required Behavior

Implement or pin unsupported behavior for `Command::Execute.plan` with receiver field plans:

- Go returns a documented unsupported signal for an unknown receiver kind or unsupported field-plan shape.
- TS and Rust return their current clean unsupported signal for field-plan-bearing execute requests until they consume plans.
- The parity matrix and allowed-divergence docs clearly separate three states: typed wire support, Go field-plan consumption, TS/Rust non-consumption.
- Add conformance coverage for those cases.

Preferred unsupported contract when a frontend emits `ExecuteResult.outcome`:

- return `ResponseResult::Execute`, not a transport-level protocol error;
- set `outcome.status = "unsupported"`;
- set non-empty `outcome.short_reason` with a stable prefix such as `unsupported_receiver_kind:` or `unsupported_receiver_field_plan:`;
- never silently fall back to legacy shallow receiver construction when a plan explicitly requests an unsupported receiver strategy.

If a frontend cannot emit `outcome` yet, pin its existing unsupported signal and document the divergence.

## Acceptance

- `task conformance` includes field-plan-bearing execute cases, or the close note names any pre-existing unrelated conformance blocker and the cases added.
- Go's unknown/unsupported plan-feature behavior is pinned.
- TS/Rust behavior is pinned without claiming they implement receiver construction.
- `protocol/PARITY.md` and `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` reflect the exact divergence and resolution condition.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing TS/Rust plan consumption.
- Implementing Go receiver field construction beyond the unsupported cases needed for conformance.
- Changing transport-level error handling.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
**Audit 2026-09-22 note** (finding frontend-ts-08, confirmed; re-checked at 56c86168).

This issue pins clean unsupported behaviour for plan-bearing `execute` requests. A related gap is the **planner commands themselves**.

- `shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md:155-157` says conformance tests "expect TS to return a clean 'capability not supported' response" when planner commands are probed.
- In fact the TS dispatch allow-list is a hand-written literal (`shatter-ts/src/handlers.ts:1151`: `handshake, analyze, instrument, prepare, execute, setup, teardown, generate, shutdown`), so a probe returns:
  ```json
  {"id":2,"status":"error","code":"invalid_request","message":"Unknown command: get_invocation_plan"}
  ```
- The only `get_invocation_plan` conformance case (`protocol/conformance/conformance_cases.yaml:538`, `planner_runtime_value_go`) is `frontends: [go]`, so nothing checks the documented contract.

**Acceptance item to add here:** TS (and Rust, if it has the same gap) and the docs agree on the planner-command probe response. One of two things happens:
- (a) behaviour changes: a command that is in generated `ALL_COMMANDS` but not in an explicit supported-**command** set returns `not_supported`, and truly unknown commands keep `invalid_request`. The supported-command set must be separate from `SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` (`handlers.ts:56-68`), which holds `complex_type:*` entries and omits the control commands `handshake` and `shutdown`; those two are always dispatched. Using `SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` as the dispatch set would reject handshake and shutdown; or
- (b) the contract changes: `shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md:155-157` and `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` document `invalid_request`.

Either way, a TS (and Rust) conformance case for a `get_invocation_plan` probe pins it, and `task conformance` shows the case running.

Option (a) is already an acceptance criterion of <ts-request-validation id>, which derives the dispatch set from `ALL_COMMANDS`. If that lands first, this item closes by pointing to it.

title: Receiver field plan wire type
description:
## Problem

Shatter needs a typed way to express "construct this receiver with these fields populated" without inventing an opaque recipe payload. Existing `InvocationPlan` fields cover constructor and argument planning, but not receiver field injection for shapes like Kapow's `queryResolver` embedding a `*Resolver` whose `SearchBackend` field must be non-nil.

## Current Code Facts

- Rust core `InvocationPlan` is in `shatter-core/src/protocol.rs`.
- Go's mirrored `InvocationPlan` is in `shatter-go/protocol/invocation_plan.go`.
- JSON schemas define `invocation_plan` in `protocol/schemas/request.schema.json` and `protocol/schemas/response.schema.json`.
- Known schema drift to handle in this issue: `constructor_arg_plans` exists in Rust and Go protocol types but is absent from the schema files. Fix that specific drift while touching the `invocation_plan` schema.

## Required Behavior

Add this exact typed wire shape to Rust core, Go protocol types, and protocol schemas:

```text
InvocationPlan.receiver_field_plans: Vec<ReceiverFieldPlan>

ReceiverFieldPlan:
- path: Vec<String>
- kind: ValuePlanKind
- literal: Option<Value>
- type_hint: String
```

JSON field names:

- `receiver_field_plans`
- `path`
- `kind`
- `literal`
- `type_hint`

Semantics:

- `path` is the receiver field path from the receiver root, for example `["Resolver", "SearchBackend"]` or `["SearchBackend"]`.
- `kind` reuses existing `ValuePlanKind`; do not add a new value-plan kind here.
- `runtime_value` remains the way to name frontend-supplied non-JSON runtime collaborators.
- This issue only adds the typed wire/data model. It does not implement any frontend receiver construction behavior.

## Required Test / Contract Updates

- Rust protocol round-trip for `InvocationPlan` with `receiver_field_plans`.
- Go JSON round-trip for `InvocationPlan` with `receiver_field_plans`.
- Schema/golden updates for `receiver_field_plans`.
- Schema update for the already-existing `constructor_arg_plans` field; do not broaden this into unrelated schema cleanup.
- Backward-compatibility test showing existing plans without field plans preserve their JSON shape.

## Acceptance

- Rust, Go, and schemas agree on the exact `receiver_field_plans` wire shape.
- Existing `InvocationPlan` JSON without field plans remains backward-compatible.
- The known `constructor_arg_plans` schema drift is fixed as part of the same `invocation_plan` schema edit.
- `str-7zhdh` has a Beads note saying it is the Go implementation slice for typed receiver field construction and should consume `receiver_field_plans` rather than inventing an opaque recipe payload.
- No Go/TS/Rust frontend construction behavior is implemented in this issue.

## Out of Scope

- TypeScript request typing; tracked by the next child.
- Go receiver construction implementation; remains `str-7zhdh`.
- TS/Rust plan consumption.
- New mock/fake return-value search behavior.
- Arbitrary config-driven executable providers.
close_reason: Already implemented and merged into main (4b9e124a: typed receiver_field_plans wire shape added to InvocationPlan across Rust/Go/schema). Stale in_progress claim; no further work needed.

title: TS InvocationPlan request typing
description:
## Problem

The Rust core and Go protocol types already carry `Command::Prepare.plan` and `Command::Execute.plan`. TypeScript currently has no typed `InvocationPlan` surface in `shatter-ts/src/protocol.ts`, so TS can at best tolerate unknown JSON properties. That is not enough for parity docs or conformance fixtures that intentionally send plan-bearing requests.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-ts/src/protocol.ts::PrepareRequest` currently has `file`, `function`, `mocks`, `project_root`, and `execution_profile`, but no `plan`.
- `shatter-ts/src/protocol.ts::ExecuteRequest` currently has `function`, `inputs`, `mocks`, `setup_context`, `prepare_id`, `capture`, and `execution_profile`, but no `plan`.
- TypeScript does not consume `Command::Execute.plan`; this issue must not pretend it does.

## Required Behavior

Add TypeScript protocol interfaces matching the current `InvocationPlan`, `ValuePlan`, and new `ReceiverFieldPlan` wire shapes. Add:

- `plan?: InvocationPlan | null` to `PrepareRequest`;
- `plan?: InvocationPlan | null` to `ExecuteRequest`.

Behavior remains unchanged: TS may ignore `plan` until the tracked `ts-rust-execute-plan-not-implemented` divergence is resolved.

## Required Test / Contract Updates

- TypeScript protocol parsing/typing test or fixture showing a plan-bearing execute request type-checks.
- Backward-compatibility check showing no-plan requests are unchanged.
- Parity docs/matrix note, if needed, clarifying that TS has typed wire support but still does not consume plans.

## Acceptance

- `shatter-ts/src/protocol.ts` exposes typed `InvocationPlan`, `ValuePlan`, and `ReceiverFieldPlan` shapes.
- `PrepareRequest` and `ExecuteRequest` include optional `plan`.
- TS behavior remains unchanged and the non-consumption divergence remains documented.

## Out of Scope

- TS receiver construction.
- TS plan-aware execute behavior.
- Browser/React adapter changes.

title: Epic: Typed receiver construction plans
description:
## Problem

`str-7zhdh` asks for Go receiver fixture recipes so Shatter can construct receiver values with useful fields populated, especially Kapow's `queryResolver` / embedded `Resolver.SearchBackend` shape. The general problem is not Go-only, but the first executable construction work is Go-specific because Go is the only frontend that currently consumes `Command::Execute.plan`.

The rejected "stateful recipe payload" framing is too loose: an opaque recipe object would create a second protocol language interpreted independently by each frontend. Shatter already has the right carrier: `InvocationPlan`.

## Desired Shape

Extend the typed `InvocationPlan` vocabulary so receiver field construction can be expressed as data, then keep behavior honest:

- Go may implement receiver field construction in `str-7zhdh`.
- TypeScript and Rust should not implement construction until they consume `Command::Execute.plan`.
- Cross-language lockstep applies to wire typing, request type parity, and clean unsupported behavior, not to construction behavior.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/protocol.rs::InvocationPlan` already has `receiver_kind`, `argument_plans`, and `constructor_arg_plans`.
- `shatter-go/protocol/invocation_plan.go::InvocationPlan` mirrors the Go-side protocol type and already has `ConstructorArgPlans`.
- `Command::Prepare.plan` and `Command::Execute.plan` already carry `InvocationPlan` in Rust core and Go protocol types.
- `shatter-ts/src/protocol.ts::ExecuteRequest` and `PrepareRequest` currently have no typed `plan` field and no `InvocationPlan` interface.
- `protocol/PARITY.md` tracks `ts-rust-execute-plan-not-implemented`: Go consumes `Command::Execute.plan`; TypeScript and Rust do not.
- `str-c8djq` is closed/landed, so Go config mock substitution now exists and can support future fake collaborator work.
- `str-7zhdh` is already `in_progress`; this epic must not duplicate it.

## Acceptance

- Child issues add a typed receiver field-plan wire surface, a TypeScript request-typing surface, and conformance coverage for unsupported plan behavior.
- `str-7zhdh` is dependency-blocked by the wire issue and noted as the Go implementation slice for this epic.
- The epic is complete only after all children are closed, `str-7zhdh` has either landed as the Go implementation slice or been explicitly superseded, and the epic close note reassesses whether TS/Rust plan consumption should be scheduled before any TS/Rust construction issues are filed.

## Out of Scope

- Opaque `stateful_recipe` payloads.
- TS/Rust receiver construction in this slice.
- Arbitrary executable recipe providers.
- Live database, Tantivy, browser, or external-service dependencies.
- Mock outcome variation as an exploration dimension; file that later only after a concrete single mechanism is chosen.
notes:
Fresh evidence from the kapow baseline run, 2026-08-14 (engine ce1d0199, 597/704 files, 1418 fns):

Receiver-field construction is now the single largest coverage blocker in this target. 178 functions have a nil-pointer panic as their ONLY observed behavior, holding 4,791 uncovered lines; excluding them lifts kapow's Go tier from 14.5% to 16.0% and the overall figure from 18.1% to 20.2%.

The kapow config-mock path (str-c8djq) verifiably works and reaches exactly this wall: api/graph/resolver/auth.resolvers.go::(*mutationResolver).CreateTeam records mock_symbols ["auth.GetAccount"] and a branch_path showing 'acct == nil' NOT taken -- the auth gate is cleared for the first time -- then panics on the next statement at r.UserService, because go_runtime_values can construct parameters but not the fields of the receiver struct. Result: 3/18 lines. All 11 resolvers in that file show the same shape.

Artifact: kapow/api/shatter-artifacts/explore-results/api_graph_resolver_auth.resolvers.go/00016_mutationResolver_.CreateTeam.json

See also str-t3f8o (receiver reused across iterations), filed from the same run.

title: crate_bridge harness registers only the requested function; discovered non-handler pub fns misreport as completed/0%
description:
## Symptom (pickpackit pp-vb2q)

Discovered pub fns in non-handler modules (e.g. pickpackit api/src/suggestions.rs::line_status_for_quantities, score_item) report 'completed' with 0% coverage; engine emits 'function not in crate_bridge dispatch table: <name>'.

## Root cause (investigated 2026-07-05)

Two issues:
1. execute_function_crate_bridge (shatter-rust/src/executor.rs:4448) builds a single-entry dispatch table: `let compatible_fns = vec![fn_info];` (~:4492-4505), even though generate_crate_bridge_wrapper (:3826) and the dispatch match (:4133-4146) already support N functions. Deliberate at the time to avoid a non-compilable sibling poisoning the harness build (comment :4476-4478); the poisoning guard is locked by test crate_bridge_unsupported_sibling_does_not_poison_requested_function (:11620).
2. The unknown-function arm (:4141) emits not_supported as a thrown_error inside an OK execute response, so the engine's not_supported→Unsupported reclassification (shatter-core/src/explorer.rs:513-517, observe.rs:981-995 — response/error-level only) never fires; the scan records completed/0%.

## Fix shape

- Populate the crate_bridge table with all fns from extract_all_fn_contexts (:4479) filtered by non-generic + crate_bridge_unsupported_reason().is_none() (:1539-1556), mirroring the crate_backed filter (:4773-4792). Resolve compile-poisoning: per-function fallback build on CompilationFailed, or per-wrapper degradation (return side already degrades via ShatterRetW :3844-3848).
- Defense-in-depth: reclassify thrown_error.error_type==not_supported inside an ok result as Unsupported (never completed/0%).
- Bump HARNESS_CACHE_VERSION (:682).

## Tests to extend

crate_bridge_wrapper_contains_all_functions (:10584), crate_bridge_wrapper_dispatch_includes_function_names (:10671), crate_bridge_unsupported_sibling_does_not_poison_requested_function (:11620), plus integration crate_bridge_executes_private_function (:11041). Engine-side swallow test near observe.rs:981 / explorer.rs:513.

## Acceptance

- pickpackit focused scan of api/src/suggestions.rs executes line_status_for_quantities and score_item with real coverage (no 'not in crate_bridge dispatch table').
- A never-dispatchable function reports unsupported, not completed/0%.
- E2E: cargo test --test e2e_concolic_rust passes; task parity if protocol-visible.
