title: shatter-go: key mocks by resolved package identity, not source spelling
description:
### Problem

Go mock matching (str-c8djq) keys mocks by their SOURCE spelling ("qualifier.Func"), not by package identity. `instrument.normalizeMockSymbol` (shatter-go/instrument/mocksubst.go) reduces every symbol to its final qualifier+function pair, and `DedupeMocks` collapses entries by that key. Consequences:

1. Two packages with the same base name (`a/util.Do`, `b/util.Do` — util/client/models names are common) collide: DedupeMocks keeps one (expression wins / first wins), and the other's call sites get the WRONG expression substituted or the wrong mock dropped silently.
2. Aliased imports never match: `import a2 "example.com/auth"` + config mock `auth.GetAccount` doesn't rewrite `a2.GetAccount(...)` call sites even though it's the same package function.
3. DedupeMocks' wire→config "upgrade" (`out[i] = m`) discards the wire mock's ReturnValues/ShouldTrackCalls/DefaultBehavior; combined with `wireShimMocks` excluding expression mocks from shim generation, call tracking for that symbol disappears from ExecuteResult (protocol-observable). Mitigating: no generated code currently invokes ShatterMock_* shims, so tracking is already inert on main — but the field discard makes the future wiring silently lossy.

### Current Code Facts (str-c8djq branch, verified 2026-07-05)

- `resolveMockSubstitutionScopes` (shatter-go/protocol/mock_resolve.go) already walks the loaded `packages.Package` with full `TypesInfo` — the `*types.PkgName` it resolves per call site carries `Imported().Path()`, i.e. the exact package identity is ALREADY available at resolve time and is currently discarded.
- `MockSubstitution.QualifiedFunction` is a source spelling; `AllowedFuncs` is function-granular.
- `DedupeMocks` and `normalizeMockSymbol` live in shatter-go/instrument/mocksubst.go; `discoverDependencies` (executor.go) has a parallel symbol parser with a documented base-name over-suppression limit.

### Requested Behavior

Key mocks by resolved package path where type information exists:

1. Config mock spelling gains an optional path-qualified form (`example.com/pkg.Func`) documented in shatter-go/CLAUDE.md; bare `pkg.Func` stays as convenience shorthand.
2. During type resolution, match a config mock to a call site by the resolved `types.PkgName.Imported().Path()` (exact match for path-qualified spellings; base-name match for bare spellings, warning when two distinct imported paths share the base name instead of silently mis-substituting).
3. Aliased imports match automatically under type resolution (identity, not spelling).
4. DedupeMocks collapses entries only when they provably refer to the same package identity; upgrades merge fields (Expression from config; ReturnValues/ShouldTrackCalls/DefaultBehavior preserved from wire) instead of replacing wholesale.
5. `discoverDependencies` suppression reuses the same parsed-symbol representation.

### Acceptance

- Unit tests: same-base-name two-package fixture — each mock hits only its own package's call sites; ambiguous bare spelling emits a warning and (documented choice) either applies to both or neither.
- Aliased-import fixture: bare config mock rewrites aliased call sites when type-resolved.
- Dedupe merge test: wire mock fields survive an expression upgrade.
- Cross-language design note: the "value expression for an opaque/hard dependency, keyed by canonical symbol identity" concept must map to TS (module specifier + export name) and Rust (crate path) — record the shape in protocol/parity-matrix.yaml notes for hint_config_v1 (still Go-only, but the identity model must not be Go-specific).

### Out of Scope

- Position-based call-site rewriting (separate issue: shared walker).
- Making shims/call-tracking live (str-8v66 return-values path).
close_reason:
Landed on main at 58e4e03c767dd0149f565d1f51b2007d6d2ee16e (merge "Merge str-djcv2-package-identity: key Go mocks by resolved package identity, not source spelling"). Ancestry and remote-push both verified.

Gate evidence:
- task check (static+unit+integration) -> exit 0, re-run clean across 5 successive rebases as main moved during landing; final run on candidate 44ce661b green.
- go build ./... -> exit 0
- go test ./instrument/... ./protocol/... -> exit 0, full pass
- land-work-run-verifier.py on exact merge preview (base 0b5c16df2b2ee1c283bddc886db869a8f8ae6c0f, head 44ce661b) -> verifier_status: passed, 3 selected checks, unverified_paths: []
- Independent high-effort code-review workflow found 7 confirmed findings (5 correctness: rewrite-time precedence inversion, silent mergeMockConfigs conflicts, missing ImportPath in SubstitutionsFingerprint, dependency-suppression regression for single-segment colon-form symbols, plus a misleading log message and a duplicate helper) -- all fixed in commit 44ce661b with regression coverage, re-verified green before landing.
- land-work-verify-landing.py: sha_matches=true, tree_matches=true against expected_tree 692a96f1551e89c2a74a4003441d9f13a91d4b80.

An earlier duplicate/superseded attempt at this issue (branch str-djcv2-mock-package-identity, commit 7adbe75e, predating the str-n0rtz shared-call-walker refactor) was found during triage and deleted rather than landed -- it carried no unique value beyond what shipped here.

title: shatter-rust: emit enum_values for fieldless enums declared in the analyzed file
description:
### Problem

str-pjlc1 added an optional `enum_values` field to the TypeInfo `union` wire variant: a concrete value domain for named enum-like types, drawn from by the core input generator so validating decoders accept inputs and function bodies execute. Go emits it; the Rust frontend only round-trips it. Rust functions taking fieldless enums still receive generic candidates, so match arms over enum variants stay uncovered unless serde happens to accept a generated value.

### Current Code Facts (as of str-pjlc1 branch, pre-landing)

- `shatter-rust/src/analyzer.rs::convert_type_path` already detects local fieldless enums and produces `TypeInfo::Union` over variant types, with `enum_values: Vec::new()` and a comment marking extraction as a tracked follow-up (search "str-pjlc1" in that file).
- `shatter-rust/src/protocol.rs` deserializes/serializes the field (defaulted when absent).
- `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` marks rust `wire_only` on `shared_wire_types.type_info_enum_values`; `allowed_divergences.enum-value-domain-partial` has resolution_condition: "the Rust analyzer emits enum_values for fieldless enums".
- Core generation already works (`shatter-core/src/input_gen.rs::generate_union`); no core changes needed.
- Constraint from project memory: shatter-rust parses one file at a time — enums defined outside the analyzed file are Opaque (str-do53/str-1fik territory). This issue covers enums defined in the analyzed file only.

### Requested Behavior

For a parameter whose type resolves to a fieldless enum declared in the analyzed file, emit `enum_values` holding each variant's serde-facing value:
1. Default serde: variant name as string (respecting `#[serde(rename = "...")]` and `#[serde(rename_all = "...")]` when present in the analyzed source).
2. Explicit discriminants on integer-repr enums (`enum E { A = 1, B = 2 }` with `#[repr(i*)]`/serde int representation): emit the integers when that is what serde would accept; otherwise emit variant-name strings.
Cap at 64 values with a warning, matching Go's truncation pattern (one WARN-level log per truncated parameter type; see shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go enum_values handling after str-pjlc1 lands).

Governing invariant for all attribute questions: every emitted enum_values member MUST be accepted by serde deserialization of the enum as written. When the analyzer cannot prove what serde accepts (exotic attributes, ambiguous int-vs-string representation), emit no enum_values for that type — fall back to today's plain union; never guess. Variant-level `#[serde(rename)]` overrides enum-level `#[serde(rename_all)]` (serde's own precedence). This issue depends on str-pjlc1 having landed (wire field + core generation).

### Acceptance

- Analyzer unit tests: plain fieldless enum → union with string enum_values; rename/rename_all respected; enum with data-carrying variants emits NO enum_values (unchanged behavior).
- An e2e case mirroring `e2e_go_enum_value_domain_reaches_all_arms` in `shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic_rust.rs`: a match over a 3-variant enum reaches all arms.
- `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml`: flip rust to `implemented`; update/narrow `enum-value-domain-partial`; run `task parity` + `task conformance`.

### Out of Scope

- Cross-file/cross-crate enum resolution (str-do53 / str-1fik).
- Data-carrying enum variants (need structured synthesis, not a value domain).
close_reason: Landed on main (merge commit f295d950, tree verified 0cfadeb6).

title: shatter-ts: emit enum_values for TS enums and literal-union aliases
description:
### Problem

str-pjlc1 added an optional `enum_values` field to the TypeInfo `union` wire variant: a concrete value domain for named enum-like types, which the core input generator draws from so validating decoders accept inputs and function bodies execute. Go emits it (const sets of named string/int types, capped at 64). The TypeScript frontend only round-trips the field — it never emits it, so TS functions guarded by enum validation still receive generic string/number candidates and their bodies stay uncovered.

### Current Code Facts (as of str-pjlc1 branch, pre-landing)

- `shatter-ts/src/protocol.ts` TypeInfo `union` variant carries optional `enum_values?: (string | number | boolean)[]` for wire parity; no analyzer code populates it.
- `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` `shared_wire_types.type_info_enum_values` marks typescript as `wire_only`; `allowed_divergences.enum-value-domain-partial` records the divergence with resolution_condition: "The TypeScript analyzer emits enum_values for enum declarations and string/numeric literal-union aliases".
- Go's contract to match (shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go on the str-pjlc1 branch): named type → enumerate constant values of that exact type → emit as union with one base variant plus enum_values; warn-and-truncate at 64 values.
- Core behavior is already in place (`shatter-core/src/input_gen.rs::generate_union`): 85% valid member draw, 15% off-domain probe. No core changes needed.

### Requested Behavior

The TS analyzer emits `enum_values` for parameters whose declared type resolves to:
1. A TS `enum` declaration (string and numeric enums; use member values, not names).
2. A type alias whose definition is a union of string/number/boolean literal types (e.g. `type Mode = "fast" | "slow"`), including via nested alias resolution within the analyzed file's type-checker view.

The emitted TypeInfo mirrors Go's shape: `union` with the base primitive variant(s) plus `enum_values`. Cap at 64 values with a warning, same as Go (match the Go analyzer's truncation warning pattern: one WARN-level frontend log line per truncated parameter type; grep `enum_values` in shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go after str-pjlc1 lands for the reference).

Clarifications: forward member values only for numeric enums (ignore TypeScript's reverse mappings — `enum E { A = 1 }` emits `[1]`, never `"A"`). Unresolvable nesting (circular aliases, generics, conditional types) falls back to today's plain union with no enum_values — never guess. This issue depends on str-pjlc1 having landed (it defines the wire field and core generation).

### Acceptance

- Round-trip/protocol tests in `shatter-ts/src/protocol.test.ts` extended for emitted (not just parsed) enum_values.
- An analyzer unit test: a literal-union alias parameter and a TS enum parameter each produce a union with the expected enum_values.
- An e2e case mirroring `e2e_go_enum_value_domain_reaches_all_arms` (shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic.rs) with a TS fixture whose switch over a literal-union covers all arms only via valid members.
- `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml`: flip typescript to `implemented` on `type_info_enum_values`; update or narrow `enum-value-domain-partial` (rust-only afterwards) and run `task parity` + `task conformance`.

### Out of Scope

- Rust emission (separate issue).
- Object-literal const maps (`as const` objects), zod/valibot schema mining — future levers, not this issue.
close_reason: Landed on main at 0ea1d396 (merge of str-knf0v-ts-enum-values).

title: scan --changed --include-untracked drops untracked files when scan root is a repo subdirectory
description:
## Symptom

`shatter scan <subdir> --changed --include-untracked` logs 'SCM reports N changed file(s)' but then 'No supported source files found' — untracked files are silently dropped. Tracked modified files work. Reproduced in a fresh repo: untracked src/probe.ts, `shatter scan src --changed --include-untracked` → no files scanned. Discovered while verifying pickpackit pp-wcpw `make shatter-scan-changed` acceptance.

## Root cause

`GitProvider::changed_files` (shatter-core/src/scm.rs) runs `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` with cwd = scan root (a repo subdirectory). `git diff --name-only` prints repo-root-relative paths regardless of cwd, but `ls-files` prints cwd-relative paths. `parse_file_list` joins both against `repo_root`, so untracked paths from a subdir scan resolve to nonexistent paths outside the scan root and are skipped by `discovery::filter_file_list` (strip_prefix fails).

## Fix

Add `--full-name` to the ls-files invocation so output is repo-root-relative, matching the diff invocations. Add a regression test: temp git repo, untracked file in a subdir, `changed_files(subdir, true)` returns the correct absolute path.

## Acceptance

- Unit test in scm.rs: untracked file under subdir root is returned with correct absolute path (fails before fix).
- Manual repro: scratch repo scan finds the untracked function.
- pickpackit `make shatter-scan-changed` with only an untracked web/src file scans that file.
close_reason: Landed on main (merge eb3681e4, tree 6657bf60). --full-name on ls-files; regression test fails without fix. Carried 4 mechanical clippy-lint fixes unblocking the rust-fe gate. Full gate verified on the exact candidate (rust-fe flakes 'build timed out' under contention; identical tree passed 522/0 capped).

title: [bug] Go frontend discovery cache (user-global go-workspace) lacks frontend-version key — stale analyses served after frontend changes
description:
Observed 2026-07-05 on zolem with the landed str-e41w engine + zolem-cf4 config hints. Focused scan of the three provider handler files: handleMessages 34% (14/14 branches), handleChatCompletions 38% (13/13), handleGenerate 33% (12/12). Whole-repo scan, same binary and config, same session: 14%, 17%, 11% — with identical hints applied and no failures.

The salient difference: in a whole-repo scan the handlers' callees (validator.Validate, matcher.Match, renderFixtureBody, ...) are scanned in earlier topological layers and their behavior maps are then used as mocks for the callers. Many callee maps are error-dominated (66/386 functions are error_only), so mocked callees return error variants and short-circuit the callers' happy paths that the focused scan (no callee maps) explores natively.

Repro: zolem @ main (post zolem-cf4): 'make shatter-focused INCLUDE=internal/provider/anthropic/handler.go' vs 'make shatter'; compare handleMessages lines.

Direction candidates (investigate first): (a) when the caller's coverage plateaus under mocked callees, fall back to native callee execution for remaining budget; (b) bias behavior-map mock selection toward success variants for deep-path exploration (error variants already covered by the callee's own scan); (c) count mock-variant selection toward caller branch goals. Fix belongs engine-side; target projects cannot config around it.

Acceptance: whole-repo scan of zolem brings the three handlers within ~1.2x of their focused-scan line coverage without regressing total scan wall time by more than ~10%; regression test at orchestrator level with a two-function fixture (callee with error+success variants; caller gated on callee success).
notes:
Landed on main at 10cc4dfe (merge commit) via bento:land-work.

Root fix: mixed a frontend self-fingerprint (SHA-256 of the running executable, streamed via io.Copy, computed once per process via sync.OnceValue, overridable via SHATTER_FRONTEND_FINGERPRINT for tests) into shatter-go's own internal discovery cache key (ComputeDiscoveryHash, user-global ~/.config/shatter/go-workspace/analysis). Previously this cache had no dependency on the frontend build itself, so a rebuild that changed analyzer behavior (e.g. str-e41w) kept serving stale results from older builds with no version bump to catch it -- root-caused on zolem (handlers stuck at kind:unknown / 14% coverage in the primary checkout vs 33-38% in fresh worktrees).

Major dedup during rebase: the original commit ALSO duplicated a separate, already-independently-landed fix for a DIFFERENT cache layer (shatter-core's Rust-side AnalysisCache, landed via str-2cihu with an analyzer_version field/API) using an incompatible constructor-based analyzer_fingerprint design. Fully removed during rebase -- shatter-core/src/analysis_cache.rs and shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs are now byte-identical to main (verified via diff and repo-wide grep for orphaned references). Final landed diff is Go-side only: shatter-go/protocol/analysis_cache.go + its test file.

Code review (after the dedup) found and I fixed 3 issues: (1) doc comments not updated to mention the new hash input, (2) commit message still described the deduped-away Core-layer changes as if they existed -- amended to accurately describe only the Go-side fix, (3) no log signal when the self-fingerprint read fails, silently and permanently missing the cache in sandboxed environments -- added slog warnings on all three failure fallback paths. Filed 3 non-blocking follow-ups: str-o1ghm (workspace GC has no coverage for the analysis cache dir, meaningfully worse now that every rebuild orphans entries), str-xaptz (SHATTER_DISABLE_ANALYSIS_CACHE doesn't skip hash computation), str-gjsb2 (consider debug/buildinfo instead of full-binary hash for hot-path latency).

Gate evidence (project verifier scripts/land_work_verifier.sh, run against the exact merge candidate):
  task test-standard -> passed
  task parity        -> passed
  task conformance    -> passed

Also ran directly: go build ./... -> clean; go vet ./... -> clean; go test ./protocol/... (TestComputeDiscoveryHash*, TestFrontendFingerprint*) -> all passed.

title: [bug] Analysis cache has no analyzer-version key — frontend analyze-behavior changes serve stale cached results
description:
Found during str-e41w review. shatter-core's analysis cache keys entries by (path, content hash, PROTOCOL_VERSION) only. When a frontend's analyze output changes for unchanged source (str-e41w: direct *http.Request params become symbolic strings), previously-scanned projects keep serving old cached ParamInfo until the source file changes — the new behavior is silently inert, and the planner (fresh analysis) can disagree with the core (cached) in materialize_seeds, yielding empty-body requests with no diagnostic.

Fix: include a frontend analyzer version (e.g. the embedded go-frontend-source-hash printed by shatter --version) in the cache key, mirroring wrapper-side generatorVersion. Same detectability class as str-o09e; related precedent str-6jwyw.

Workaround: clear .shatter-cache/analysis when upgrading shatter across analyze-behavior changes.

Acceptance: changed analyzer contract auto-invalidates prior analysis entries; cache-layer regression test; no invalidation when frontend hash unchanged.
notes:
Landed on main at f9753e80 (merge commit) via bento:land-work.

When landing str-oqynx, its core-layer duplicate will need to be dropped/reconciled against this landed analyzer_version implementation, keeping only str-oqynx's distinct shatter-go/protocol/analysis_cache.go (Go-side discovery cache) fix.

title: [bug] Cold-cache harness-build thundering herd: parallel per-function builds all hit build timeout, scan completes 0 functions
description:
## Problem

`shatter scan --all` on a Go target with a cold host Go build cache launches every per-function harness build concurrently (parallelism defaults to CPU count). Each `go build` redundantly compiles the same dependency graph (the Go build cache does not deduplicate in-flight work across concurrent builds), the CPU is massively oversubscribed, and **every** build hits the per-function 60s build timeout. The scan burns its entire `timeout_total` budget with zero completions.

Observed on zolem (2026-07-04, main-build 2f3cb598): first `make shatter` after clearing `.shatter-cache/behavior-maps` → 62/62 attempted functions failed `timed out during build after 60s`, 324 skipped `interrupted (total scan budget exceeded)`, 0 completed. Immediately re-running the same scan with a warm cache → 386 attempted, 377 completed. A lone `go build ./...` of the module takes 16s wall / 65s CPU.

## Proposed fix

Warm the build cache before fanning out: when a scan (or explore batch) will build N>1 harnesses for the same module/workspace, run ONE synchronous warm-up build first (either the first function's harness, or `go build ./...` of the target module), then release the remaining builds at full parallelism. Alternative/complement: make the build timeout adaptive — measure the warm-up build and scale the per-function cap.

The fix must be language-generic in design: the TS frontend (node_modules/tsc incremental state) and Rust frontend (cargo target dir) have the same cold-cache stampede shape; the warm-up hook belongs in core scan orchestration (`shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs`, `build_timeout` path), with each frontend deciding what "warm-up" means.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fresh scan of zolem (or an e2e fixture module) with a deliberately cold GOCACHE completes without mass `timed out during build` failures; first-run wall time within ~2x of warm-run wall time.
- Regression test at the orchestrator level: N queued builds on a cold cache → exactly one build proceeds until the first completes, then the rest fan out.
- No regression in warm-cache scan wall time (warm-up is a no-op or trivially cheap when the cache is hot).

## Evidence

- Cold-run report: zolem shatter-report/full-scan.md @ 2026-07-04 first run (0 completed).
- Warm rerun: same command, 377/413 completed.
- rtk log: ~/.local/share/rtk/tee/1783136946_make_shatter.log
close_reason: Landed on main (merge 29378434): BuildWarmupGate serializes the first per-function harness build of a scan (default pool + function-isolation modes; gate acquired before same-file permits to avoid leader/follower deadlock; opens on leader failure too). Cold-cache acceptance on zolem: GOCACHE=empty tempdir full scan → 386 completed / 0 failed / 0 interrupted (pre-fix: 0 completed, 62 build timeouts, 324 interrupted on the same budget). Warm-cache cost: one serialized function. Gates: 3 new gate regression tests, scan_orchestrator suite 180, full core suite (2 env-dependent project tests pass with SHATTER_EXAMPLES_DIR), clippy clean (also fixed two pre-existing clippy-1.96 lints blocking the gate). Language-agnostic design: gate lives in core orchestration; TS/Rust frontends get the same protection.

title: Generator prefetch failure degrades to misleading 'unsupported extractor types'; prefetch fragile under DB pressure
description:
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust-frontend, scan, observability
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo pickpackit (~/project/pickpackit, ≥90% feature-code goal).

### Symptom

In a full `shatter scan api/src --require-rust` of pickpackit (123 attempted
functions, parallelism 6 auto-detected, default generator pool max 8), 85
functions failed with:

```
error: exploration error: unsupported: axum handler has unsupported extractor types: CurrentAccount
```

The same functions pass cleanly (native-replay markers present, behavioral
clusters produced) when scanned focused (`--include '**/handlers/tags.rs'`,
11/11 completed, 0 failed) with the same binary, config, and database — and a
full rerun with `SHATTER_PICKPACKIT_POOL_MAX=2 --parallelism 3` is expected to
mostly pass (validation in flight). The failure is load-dependent, not a
capability gap, but the error text claims a capability gap.

### Mechanism (verified in source, shatter main f64b1323)

- `execute_adapter_owned` (shatter-rust/src/adapters.rs:552 area) classifies an
  extractor param as unsupported only when the input at that param index is NOT
  a replayable native marker: `!is_replayable_native_input(inputs.get(i))`.
- The native marker comes from custom-generator prefetch. When prefetch fails,
  the scan logs a warning and continues with plain generated inputs — e.g.
  scan_orchestrator.rs:3068 `"scan concolic generator prefetch failed for {}: {err}"`
  (warn level), and the analogous random-path prefetch degrades similarly.
- Plain inputs then hit the adapter check and fail as
  "unsupported extractor types: CurrentAccount" — the root cause (generator
  prefetch error, in pickpackit's case Postgres pool exhaustion:
  6 workers x pool max 8 + per-execute lazy handler pools vs
  max_connections=100, 120s acquire timeout) is invisible in the report.
  With `--log-level warn` + report-only output, users see only the wrong story.

Second corroboration (2026-07-03, same binary): with an empty test database
(docker recreation wiped schema), every generator prefetch panicked
("native generator "current" ... panicked: shatter generator thread panicked:
Any { .. }" — 2100 warn lines, 100 per generator file), and affected handler
functions again surfaced only as unsupported-extractor failures. Note the
panic payload is also lost (`Any { .. }`) — surfacing the panic message string
when available is part of desired behavior 1.

### Desired behavior

1. **Attribution:** when an adapter-owned execution fails the extractor check
   AND a configured generator for that param/type had a failed or exhausted
   prefetch, the function failure reason must name the prefetch failure (e.g.
   "custom generator prefetch failed for CurrentAccount: PoolTimedOut ...")
   rather than "unsupported extractor types". A function whose config binds a
   generator to an extractor should never report the bare unsupported-extractor
   error without qualifying why the generator produced no value.
2. **Report surfacing:** prefetch failures should appear in the scan report
   (per-function failure reason and/or a run-level warnings section), not only
   as transient warn-level log lines.
3. Retry/concurrency limiting for generator prefetch: file as a follow-up
   issue by default; implement here only if trivially small.

Note: "the analogous random-path prefetch degrades similarly" is inferred, not
yet verified — the acceptance grep of both explorer paths settles it.

### Reproduction

Authoritative repro: the unit test in Acceptance (self-contained in this
repo). The pickpackit run below is corroborating field evidence only and
requires the external pickpackit checkout + test stack.

From ~/project/pickpackit (test stack up via docker compose project
pickpackit-api-test-pickpackit-3654118870, ports 55370/56370; see
scripts/api-integration-test.sh --print-config):

```
export SHATTER_RUST_SRC=$HOME/project/shatter/shatter-rust \
       SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=$HOME/project/shatter/shatter-rust-runtime \
       DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55370/pickpackit_test
# high pressure (default pool max 8, parallelism auto) -> mass "unsupported extractor" failures
shatter scan api/src --require-rust --timeout-total 14400 -o /tmp/rep.json
# low pressure -> passes
SHATTER_PICKPACKIT_POOL_MAX=2 shatter scan api/src --require-rust --parallelism 3 ...
```

Evidence artifact: pickpackit shatter-artifacts/baseline-20260703-api.json
(85x unsupported-extractor failures) vs focused tags.rs runs (11/11 pass).

### Acceptance

- Unit test: adapter-owned execution with a config-bound generator whose
  prefetch returned an error reports a failure reason naming the generator
  prefetch failure, not "unsupported extractor types".
- Scan report JSON carries the prefetch failure reason for affected functions.
- E2E: existing e2e_concolic_rust.rs stays green; add a case if an existing
  fixture can simulate prefetch failure cheaply (e.g. generator file that
  errors), else unit-level coverage suffices with a note.
- Grep both explorer paths (explorer.rs random / orchestrator.rs concolic) —
  parallel-path parity rule — and cover whichever consumes prefetch results.

### Out of scope

- Changing pickpackit generators or configs (target-side hygiene is tracked in
  pickpackit's tracker).
- Reworking pool management inside target generator files.

title: Props/array field types degrade to unknown when element interfaces are cross-file
description:
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo kapow.

#### Symptom

~9 kapow web functions fail every iteration with `institutions.map is not a function` (and siblings): a param or props field typed as `Institution[]` degrades to `{kind:"unknown"}` in TypeInfo, so the Rust core generates a random primitive; the body then calls `.map` on a non-array.

#### Current Code Facts (verified 2026-07-01)

- Array typing is correct when the element type resolves: `isArrayType` → `{kind:"array",element}` (shatter-ts analyzer.ts:688), tuples (:700), ArrayLike/numeric-index (:1743), `T extends X[]` generics (:783).
- Degradation source: props objects are extracted by `convertObjectType` (analyzer.ts:1725), which recurses per field (:1765-1789) but deliberately drops `sourceFile` context for field types (:1782) — a field whose array element is an interface declared in another file becomes unresolvable in context and collapses to `{kind:"unknown"}`.
- The core generates for `unknown` by falling back to random primitives (shatter-core input_gen.rs unknown arm), producing the `.map is not a function` class.

#### Change

1. shatter-ts: preserve enough context in `convertObjectType` field recursion to resolve cross-file element/interface types (thread sourceFile or use the checker's symbol location instead of dropping it at :1782); bound recursion depth as today.
2. Fallback hardening (cheap, independent): when a type is `array<unknown>` rather than bare unknown, keep the array kind so the core at least generates arrays of somethings. (Changing the core's generic `unknown`-arm value rotation is explicitly OUT of scope — file a follow-up if the fixture still mis-generates after item 1.)

#### Out of scope

- Full cross-file type resolution overhaul; only field-type context preservation.
- React recognition/leak/coverage issues (separate).

#### Acceptance

- Unit test: props interface in file A with field `items: Widget[]` where Widget is declared in file B → TypeInfo has `array` kind with resolved element fields, not unknown.
- kapow validation: `.map is not a function` failure count drops to ~0 in a web/src re-run. How to run: from ~/project/kapow, `SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=bwrap <your-built-binary> explore <web/src file> --spec` per file, or the full set via `SHATTER=<binary> bash scripts/shatter-source-set.sh explore`; count failures by grepping `is not a function` in `web/shatter-artifacts/explore-results/*/0*.json`.
- fast-check property for the recursion (no crash/no unbounded depth on cyclic types); TS suite green.
close_reason: Landed on main (merge 87b99d22). Fix: convertTypeWithNode recovers array-ness from declared AST TypeNode when the lib-less bundled frontend degrades T[]/Array<T>/ReadonlyArray<T> to unknown/empty-object; recovery gated to degraded shapes only (review fix aa1ae9f1) so with-lib behavior is untouched (optional-array nullability preserved, shadowed Array types safe). degradedType keeps array kind on cycle/depth bailout. Evidence: 906/906 shatter-ts tests incl. cross-file fixture + noLib suite + fast-check property; TS E2E 22/22 on final base; independent review verdict merge-with-fixes, fix applied. Known remaining lib-less gaps recorded as issue comment (union members, return types, tuple syntax, type aliases).

comments.author: Test User
comments.text: Review follow-up notes (non-blocking): lib-less sibling conversion sites still lose array-ness — union members (Widget[] | null), return types, tuple syntax [A,B]; array-typed aliases (type Widgets = Widget[]) also degrade. File follow-ups if these surface in target runs. degradedType change: cyclic/depth-limited arrays now yield array{unknown} with lib present (intentional).

title: Transitive require('react') from node_modules bypasses the sandbox react shim
description:
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo kapow.

#### Symptom

Components correctly recognized and executed via the react-hook adapter can still crash with real-React null-dispatcher errors when a third-party dependency (kapow: Mantine) internally calls React hooks — the dependency's own `require('react')` resolves to the real react package, not shatter's shim.

#### Current Code Facts (verified 2026-07-01)

- The react shim resolver is injected into the sandbox require chain recursively for target-code module loads (shatter-ts executor.ts:668-689, :733).
- node_modules dependencies are loaded via native createRequire (executor.ts:622-633); their internal `require('react')` uses Node's real resolution and bypasses the shim — two React instances, the real one with a null dispatcher.

#### Change

Route transitive `require('react')` (and 'react-dom', the automatic runtime entrypoints 'react/jsx-runtime', 'react/jsx-dev-runtime') from node_modules-loaded dependencies to the shim. Preferred approach: alias the react-family specifiers at sandbox module-resolution level (single choke point, covers arbitrarily deep transitive requires); fall back to extending the injected resolver through the createRequire path only if the alias approach can't intercept native createRequire resolution. Preserve native resolution for everything else (perf + fidelity). Version-mismatch note: forcing the shim onto dependencies compiled against any React version is acceptable — the shim implements the stable hook/createElement surface, and exploration fidelity (not React semantics fidelity) is the goal; document this in the code comment. Test fixture node_modules: follow existing shatter-ts test conventions (generated in test setup is fine).

#### Out of scope

- Recognition gaps (separate issue).
- Adapter-owned coverage capture (separate issue).
- Non-react module aliasing generally.

#### Acceptance

- Unit test: a fixture component importing a helper package (fixture node_modules) that itself calls useState executes under the react-hook adapter without null-dispatcher errors, with the shim's hook semantics.
- kapow validation: recognized Mantine-using components in web/src execute without `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'use...')` in a re-run. How to run: from ~/project/kapow, `SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=bwrap <binary> explore <web/src component file> --spec`; grep `web/shatter-artifacts/explore-results/*/0*.json` raw_results for the null-dispatcher message.
- TS suite green; no change to non-react module loading behavior (test that a dependency using fs/path still loads natively).
close_reason: Landed on main at b8687802 (merge of str-rzsej-react-leak, after addressing review findings).

title: React recognizer misses automatic-JSX-runtime and third-party-hook components — unrecognized components crash on real React
description:
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo kapow.

#### Symptom

~43 kapow web component functions fail every iteration with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useState'/'useMemo'/'useContext'/'useRef')`: they are NOT recognized as react-hook adapter targets, fall through to direct invocation, and execute against real React outside a renderer.

#### Current Code Facts (verified 2026-07-01)

- `recognizeReactHooks` early-returns undefined when `!hasReactImport` (shatter-ts react-hook-recognizer.ts:258); with the automatic JSX runtime (React 17+) components need no react import, so they are never recognized.
- `REACT_HOOK_MODULES` (react-hook-recognizer.ts:41) contains only react/react-dom — hooks imported from barrels or third-party hook packages (kapow uses @mantine/hooks) don't count as hook usage.
- Component recognition (`isComponentName` + `bodyContainsJsx`, react-hook-recognizer.ts:61-86, 286-305) plus `findFunctionBody` (:198) can fail to line-match arrow/HOC-wrapped components.
- Recognized targets get invocation_model react-hook at analyzer.ts:385-402 and run against the react shim (react-shim.ts) — those succeed; the failures are exactly the unrecognized remainder.
- Related but separate leak: even recognized components can crash when a node_modules dependency's transitive `require('react')` bypasses the sandbox shim resolver (executor.ts:622-689) — that is filed separately; keep this issue to recognition.

#### Change

In shatter-ts react-hook-recognizer.ts:
1. Recognize components without a react import when the file extension is .tsx/.jsx AND the body contains JSX (predicate decided: extension + JSX-in-body; do NOT consult tsconfig `jsx` settings in this issue).
2. Treat `useXxx`-named imports from any module as hook-usage signals for the component/custom-hook paths (decided: any-module signal, no config surface; keep builtin-hook detection as-is).
3. Harden findFunctionBody for arrow components assigned to const and components wrapped in memo/forwardRef (unwrap the call expression to the inner function).

#### Out of scope

- The transitive real-React leak through node_modules (separate issue).
- Adapter-owned coverage capture (separate issue).
- Class components.

#### Acceptance

- Unit tests (fast-check where an invariant fits, per TS conventions): automatic-JSX-runtime component (no react import), component using only @mantine/hooks-style third-party hooks, const-arrow component, memo-wrapped component — all recognized with invocation_model react-hook; non-component PascalCase util NOT recognized.
- kapow validation: the null-dispatcher failure count in a web/src re-run drops to ~0 for previously unrecognized components (a nonzero remainder attributable to the separately-filed transitive-React leak is acceptable). How to run: from ~/project/kapow, `SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=bwrap <binary> explore <web/src component file> --spec`; grep `web/shatter-artifacts/explore-results/*/0*.json` for `reading 'use`.
- TS test suite + `task conformance` green; parity matrix untouched unless capability text changes.

title: [epic] Adapter-owned executions return empty coverage fields — React/http/gin/axum targets contribute zero line coverage
description:
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo kapow (90% feature-code goal, 80% UI floor).

#### Symptom

Every adapter-owned invocation returns empty `lines_executed`/`branch_path`/`path_constraints`, so functions executed through invocation-model adapters contribute ZERO coverage regardless of how thoroughly they execute. In kapow this caps ALL React function components (the entire UI tier) plus any Go net/http handlers; the same contract note appears for Go gin and (per parity docs) Rust axum.

#### Current Code Facts (verified 2026-07-01)

- TS: `executeAdapterOwned` (shatter-ts handlers.ts:677 dispatch; executor.ts) returns empty instrumentation fields; the shatter-go CLAUDE.md Invocation Model Parity Contract states the same for go/http-handler and go/gin ("Instrumentation fields (branch_path, lines_executed) are empty for adapter-owned calls").
- The TS react-hook adapter executes component/hook bodies in-process (react-shim.ts stubs; react-hook-invocation.ts:580 direct call, :377 stateful rerender) — the target function body DOES run in instrumentable form; only the adapter result assembly drops instrumentation.
- The TS instrumentor already parses/instruments .tsx (instrumentor.ts:163 ScriptKind.TSX).
- Go adapters build a specialized launcher entrypoint (shatter-go protocol/adapter_launcher.go) running httptest — the target body runs inside the instrumented overlay build, so branch/line capture machinery exists in the same process.

#### Change

Make adapter-owned executions carry the same instrumentation capture as direct calls, per frontend:

1. TS (primary, unlocks kapow UI): the adapter invokes the instrumented function in-process — thread the normal coverage collection (whatever executor.ts uses for direct calls) through executeAdapterOwned instead of returning empty fields.
2. Go: adapter launcher entrypoints should link the instrumented target (as the normal wrapper path does) and propagate branch_path/lines_executed into the adapter's ExecuteResult (shatter-go protocol/adapter.go ExecuteAdapterOwned currently returns empty instrumentation fields by construction).
3. Rust: audit axum adapter for the same gap; fix or file follow-up.
4. Update parity-matrix.yaml and each frontend CLAUDE.md contract text (they currently document the empty-fields behavior as a contract — this issue changes that contract deliberately).

#### Out of scope

- New adapters or recognition changes (separate issues).
- Concolic/solver use of adapter branch paths beyond what direct calls already get.

#### Acceptance

- TS fixture: a React function component with a props-driven branch, explored via the react-hook adapter, reports non-empty lines_executed and coverage consistent with the branch taken; a two-branch component explored with varied props shows both branches in coverage.
- Go fixture: a net/http handler with a method-driven branch reports non-empty lines_executed under the go/http-handler adapter.
- E2E: add cases to e2e_concolic.rs (TS) and e2e_concolic_go.rs asserting adapter-owned targets produce coverage; `task parity` + `task conformance` green after matrix/doc updates.
- kapow validation: exec-line coverage for web/src/components feature files rises above zero in a re-run.

#### Structure

This is an EPIC. Child issues (filed alongside):
1. TS: instrument adapter-owned executions (react-hook + browser-dom) — populate lines_executed/branch_path/path_constraints identically to direct calls.
2. Go: adapter launcher coverage propagation (go/http-handler AND go/gin — acceptance covers both).
3. Rust: axum adapter audit — closable on evidence either way: if instrumentation fields are already populated, attach proof and close; if the gap exists, attach a failing fixture and file the fix as a follow-up child.

Notes for implementers: all line refs are 2026-07-01 advisory — anchor by symbol name. The kapow re-run validation is a program-level check the coordinating agent runs; it is NOT required to close individual children. Contract-text updates (parity matrix + frontend CLAUDE.mds) land with each child; a partial-parity intermediate state is expected and should be reflected honestly in the matrix per child as it lands.

One explicit 'missing_global: document (DOM)' names the browser-globals adapter (ItemImageLightbox). title: Param-decode failures misreported as completed: launcher deser errors bypass outcome classification
description:
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo kapow.

### Symptom

Functions whose generated inputs are 100% rejected at param decode report `status: completed` with 0 lines covered — total input starvation is invisible in headline status. kapow examples: `gqlScaleToService` (all inputs "not a valid RatingScale") and `runErrorMessage` (all inputs "cannot unmarshal object into Go value of type error") — both 100 iterations, 0 unique paths, 0 covered lines, status `completed` in explore-results summary.json.

### Current Code Facts (verified 2026-07-01)

- The direct/prepared launcher emits deserialization errors as `launcherResponse{Error: err.Error()}` with `ThrownError` left nil (shatter-go/launcher/launcher.go:700-703).
- `outcomeFromResult` (shatter-go/protocol/handler.go:1213) classifies only via `thrownErr`; nil → `OutcomeStatusCompleted` (handler.go:1233-1237). Per the Invocation Outcome Contract (shatter-go/CLAUDE.md, str-hy9b.A2), non-completed statuses carry `short_reason` — a body-never-entered run should not be `completed`.
- CLI summary counts these functions in `completed` / `completed_function_span_lines` with `covered_completed_lines == 0` (shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs:639-651), so target-repo rollups (e.g. kapow's shatter-artifacts) overstate explored surface.

### Change

1. Go frontend: map non-nil `launcherResponse.Error` on the deser path to a non-completed InvocationOutcome — decide between `runtime_failed` with a distinct `error_type` (e.g. `input_decode_failed`) or a new outcome enum value; prefer the existing enum + distinct error_type to avoid a protocol/parity change unless per-status wire semantics demand it (check parity-matrix `outcome` capability before adding enum values; TS/Rust would need the same status value if the enum grows).
2. Per-iteration vs per-function: a single rejected iteration is normal probing; the misreport is *all* iterations rejected with zero body entry. The per-function explore status should reflect that — use summary status name `input_starved` (check summary.json status vocabulary in explore.rs for collisions before finalizing), so summaries stop counting starved functions as explored. Fixture location: follow the existing known-answer convention (examples/go/ + e2e_concolic_go.rs cases).

### Out of scope

- Making inputs valid (enum/error/value-domain issues cover that).
- TS/Rust equivalent audits (file follow-ups if the same pattern exists there).

### Acceptance

- Fixture: function whose only param is a validating named type with no valid generated candidates → explore reports a non-completed per-function status naming input starvation; summary.json no longer counts it in `completed`.
- Mixed case: function where some iterations decode and execute → still `completed` (probing rejections don't flip status).
- Unit tests at handler (`outcomeFromResult`) and explore.rs classification; conformance (`task conformance`) green; if any wire enum changes, follow protocol/GOVERNANCE.md and update parity matrix + all three frontends' round-trip tests.

title: Enum value-domain extraction: Go const sets → protocol TypeInfo.enum_values → core generates valid variants
description:
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo kapow.

### Symptom

Functions taking named enum-like types get only generic candidates, so 100% of inputs are rejected by validating decoders and the function body never executes. kapow `gqlScaleToService(s model.RatingScale)` (api/graph/resolver/rating_helpers.go:23): gqlgen string enum with custom UnmarshalJSON→IsValid ("%s is not a valid RatingScale"); 100 iterations, 0 paths, 0/11 lines. Same for SortDirection inside `(*queryResolver).Search` (many rejected iterations mixed in).

### Current Code Facts (verified 2026-07-01)

- Go planner: `classifyParamFamily` (shatter-go/planner/param.go:250) sends any named string type to `stringFamily()` (param.go:277-278, 317-326) — candidates only zero-value/"a"/"hello". No enum awareness.
- Go analyzer resolves imported named types via `pkg.TypesInfo` (shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go:1227, 1266) — underlying kind only; never enumerates const sets. Valid values are statically reachable via the defining package's `types.Scope()` (const decls of that named type), plus gqlgen conventions (`IsValid()` method, `AllX` slice) as corroborating signals.
- Protocol `TypeInfo` (shatter-go/protocol/types.go:288) has only type_name/complex_kind — no field to carry a value domain.
- The ONLY enum-aware generation path today: TS emits `TypeInfo::Union{variants}` (see shatter-ts analyzer tests, e.g. analyzer.test.ts:696), consumed by shatter-core/src/input_gen.rs:128 → `generate_union` (:549). Go/Rust never produce Union for named enums.
- Scan-scope exclusion of the defining package (kapow excludes generated api/graph/model/) is irrelevant: type info comes from the type-checked import, not from scanning that file.
- Per-target manual workaround exists (hint_config_v1 `defaults` pinning e.g. `s: "STARS"` via config/loader.go) but does not scale and requires humans to know the domains.

### Change

1. Go analyzer: when a param's type is a named string/int type whose defining package scope contains constants of that exact type, collect those constant values as the param's value domain (cap at 64; log a warn-level truncation note when the cap trims, mirroring the config loader's warn-on-unknown pattern). Use gqlgen `IsValid`/`AllX` only as optional corroboration, not as the primary mechanism.
2. Protocol: add an optional `enum_values` field (decided name — the errors.Is sentinel follow-up shares this field, so keep it value-list-shaped with room for expression-kind entries later) to the shared TypeInfo wire type — follow protocol/GOVERNANCE.md checklist; regenerate bindings (never hand-edit); round-trip tests in all three frontends per protocol rules.
3. Core: map the new field onto the existing Union-variant generation (input_gen.rs `generate_union`) so valid variants are generated (mixed with occasional invalid probes so rejection paths stay covered — keep the current generic candidates at low weight).
4. Parity: declare the capability in protocol/parity-matrix.yaml with Go implemented; file follow-ups or mark allowed divergences for TS (emit Union/enum_values for TS enum declarations and literal-union aliases where not already) and Rust frontend (native enums) rather than implementing all three here. Language-portability note: the mechanism (named type + const/variant set → enum_values) maps directly to Java enums and C++ enum class.

### Out of scope

- errors.Is sentinel mining (separate issue; shares the TypeInfo domain field).
- Status misreporting of all-rejected runs (separate issue).
- Full TS/Rust frontend implementations (tracked as follow-ups per parity matrix).

### Acceptance

- Fixture: Go file with `type Color string`, const set of 3, a `switch` over them plus default → explore covers all 4 arms (3 valid + 1 invalid probe) under `shatter explore`.
- kapow validation: `gqlScaleToService` explores >0 paths with valid RatingScale values reaching the body. How to run: from ~/project/kapow, `SHATTER=<your-built-binary> bash scripts/shatter-source-set.sh explore` explores the whole set; for one file run `<binary> explore api/graph/resolver/rating_helpers.go --spec` from the kapow root (SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=bwrap).
- Protocol round-trip tests updated in ts/go/rust frontends; `task parity` and `task conformance` green.
- Go E2E gate green (`cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go -- --include-ignored`); add an enum-param E2E case per the shatter-go CLAUDE.md rule.
- Both explorer paths benefit (random explorer + concolic orchestrator) — verify per the parallel-path rule.

### Size signal

Multi-crate (shatter-go analyzer/planner, protocol types + bindings, shatter-core input_gen) — larger than one normal task; may warrant splitting analyzer/protocol/core into sub-issues at implementation time.
close_reason: Landed (merge 8000e68f): Go analyzer const-set extraction -> TypeInfo.enum_values -> core valid-member generation (random + boundary + default + LLM paths); 2 Go E2E cases both explorer paths; unsigned/u64 wire coverage. Follow-ups: str-knf0v (TS), str-2nfoe (Rust), str-v0yjq (remaining core paths).

title: Go wrapper cannot decode __complex_type:error params — error-typed params 100% rejected (mirror the time.Duration decode fix)
description:
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo kapow.

### Symptom

Any Go function with an `error`-typed parameter gets every generated input rejected at decode: e.g. kapow `runErrorMessage(err error)` (api/internal/chat/service.go:536) — 100 iterations, 0 unique paths, 0/8 lines, error `param err: json: cannot unmarshal object into Go value of type error`.

### Current Code Facts (verified 2026-07-01)

- The Go analyzer maps built-in `error` to `ComplexKind:"error"` (shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go:1319-1322).
- The Rust core's generator emits the cross-frontend shape `{"__complex_type":"error","class":...,"message":...}` (shatter-core/src/input_gen.rs:590, generate_error at :725-745). So the analyzer→core leg already follows the convention; only the decode side is missing.
- The generated wrapper falls through to plain `var err error; json.Unmarshal(input,&err)` (shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go:548-586), which cannot unmarshal into a bare interface.
- Precedent to mirror exactly: `writeDurationParamDeserialization` (wrapper.go:1232-1246), dispatched at the `GoType=="time.Duration"` branch near wrapper.go:559-561, which decodes the analogous legacy `{"__complex_type":"duration","ms":N}` shape with typed fallback and specific error preservation.
- `runtimeval` registry has no `error` entry (only context.Context at registry.go:68, io.Writer at :89 etc.).

### Change

Add `writeErrorParamDeserialization` in shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go mirroring the Duration helper: for params with GoType `error` (confirm the exact GoType string that reaches the wrapper for the builtin `error` interface — check what analyzer.go:1319-1322's ComplexKind mapping produces; bare builtin `error` only, named error-implementing types out of scope), decode `{"__complex_type":"error", "message": m}` to `errors.New(m)` (JSON `null` → nil error), ignoring the `class` field for now (no typed-error reconstruction), preserving the original decode error message for any other shape. Thread the `errors` import through the wrapper import block (same mechanism as str-gxjs.1 runtime-value imports).

### Out of scope

- Satisfying `errors.Is(err, pkg.ErrSentinel)` branches — sentinel mining is a separate issue (value-domain family).
- TS/Rust frontends (they already handle their own error encodings).
- Changing the misleading `completed` status for all-rejected runs (separate issue).

### Acceptance

- Regression test in shatter-go/wrapper (model on wrapper_duration_test.go: static-source guards + compile + run with the error wire shape and with null).
- A fixture function `func classify(err error) string` with `err == nil` / non-nil branches explores BOTH branches under `shatter explore`.
- Go E2E gate green: `cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go -- --include-ignored`; add a case if existing shapes don't cover an error param (per shatter-go CLAUDE.md E2E rule).
- shatter-go/CLAUDE.md gets a short wire-format note beside the Duration Parameter Wire Format section.
notes:
Non-blocking follow-ups from str-jn9r0 review (do not action now):
1. writeErrorParamDeserialization is the second near-verbatim tagged-object decode helper (after writeDurationParamDeserialization). When a third lands (str-kvzh7 / str-pjlc1), generalize to a decoder table keyed by GoType: {tag, emit fn, required imports} instead of copy #3.
2. Wrapper harness test scaffolding (temp module + overlay manifest + build + runner build/run) is now duplicated ~6x across wrapper_duration_test.go and wrapper_error_test.go. Extract a shared buildAndRunWrapperHarness helper opportunistically.

title: Docs examples smoke gate
description:
## Problem

Documentation drift is not limited to missing command inventory. README, QUICKSTART, SPEC, and docs examples can contain stale flags, removed commands, broken paths, invalid JSON snippets, or examples that no longer match the current CLI. The latest audit found SPEC.md still documenting removed or renamed flags such as `explore --timeout`, scan `--output-dir`, and global `--perf`.

str-wurp covers mechanical CLI command/flag inventory versus clap definitions. Shatter still needs executable example checks so user-facing docs cannot keep broken snippets.

## Current Code Facts

- README.md, QUICKSTART.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and docs/INDEX.md all point readers toward SPEC.md as the behavioral authority.
- str-ck05 tracks repairing stale SPEC.md content.
- str-wurp tracks a CLI inventory/gauntlet drift gate, but not general markdown example execution or JSON/schema validation.

## Desired Behavior

Add a docs smoke gate that extracts or declares user-facing command and data examples, runs the safe examples, and validates structured snippets. Documentation changes that introduce stale commands or invalid examples should fail locally before they land.

## Required Trigger

The gate must be invoked by a real command, such as `task docs-smoke` or `task drift-docs`, and be included in either `task check` or the scheduled drift patrol. A docs-only branch that changes README, QUICKSTART, SPEC, or docs command examples must have an obvious command to run and a failing path if examples are stale.

## Suggested Shape

Use a maintained allowlist/blocklist rather than trying to run every fenced block blindly:

- runnable shell examples: run with temporary output dirs and no network by default;
- `--help` examples: verify command and flag existence against the built CLI;
- JSON/YAML examples: validate parseability and schema when a schema exists;
- intentionally illustrative snippets: mark as `no-run` with a short reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A checked-in docs smoke command validates at least README.md, QUICKSTART.md, SPEC.md, and docs/INDEX.md or an explicit configured subset.
- Reintroducing one known stale flag from the audit, such as `shatter explore --timeout`, causes the docs smoke gate to fail.
- Structured examples that claim to be JSON or YAML are parsed and fail on invalid syntax.
- The gate is wired into `task check`, the scheduled drift patrol, or both.
- Contributor/agent instructions explain how to mark non-runnable examples and require a reason for each exemption.

## Out of Scope

- Rewriting SPEC.md content directly; tracked by str-ck05.
- Full end-to-end walkthrough testing; keep this smoke gate fast and deterministic.
notes: Landed on main (7bed0d90). Gate evidence: task docs-smoke (pass), python3 -m unittest scripts.test_docs_smoke (39 passed), task check-static (pass) — all run against the exact merge candidate (preview tree f7f452b3). Independent code review caught and fixed a subcommand-path-resolution bug (leading global flag before subcommand caused false-positive unknown-flag errors).

title: Scheduled drift patrol
description:
## Problem

Drift checks currently depend on an agent or human remembering to run a broad audit. That is why stale SPEC content, expired parity divergence warnings, missing docs/stories, stale in-progress issues, and invalid agent instructions can linger until a manual audit happens.

Existing issues cover several individual checks, but there is no recurring trigger that gives drift warnings a visible audience.

## Current Code Facts

- str-wurp proposes a mechanical CLI-surface drift gate.
- str-2fjn proposes protocol registry/schema/runtime cross-validation.
- str-5dx0 proposes scheduled visibility for parity divergence expiry warnings.
- The latest audit ran these current gates manually: cargo test/clippy, Go test/vet, TS test/tsc, task conformance, protocol registry validation, and protocol codegen check.
- docs/stories is absent, so story drift has no current patrol surface.

## Desired Behavior

Add a bounded drift patrol with an explicit trigger and failure path. The patrol should run often enough that drift is detected before a human starts unrelated implementation work.

## Required Trigger

Implement at least one real recurring trigger:

- preferred: a scheduled CI workflow or equivalent repository automation that runs at least weekly;
- acceptable fallback if CI is not available yet: a documented `task drift-patrol` target wired into the agent pre-completion or audit skill so agents cannot call a governance audit complete without running it.

The trigger must publish visible output: a failed check, a generated report, or an automatically filed/updated Beads issue.

## Minimum Patrol Contents

The first version should run bounded checks only:

- protocol registry/codegen checks;
- protocol conformance or a documented fast subset;
- CLI drift check once str-wurp lands, or a placeholder that fails with a clear "not implemented" message until str-wurp is closed;
- parity expiry warning check from str-5dx0 when available;
- docs/stories existence and index freshness check once the stories issue lands;
- stale tracker hygiene query for long-running in_progress issues and open children under closed epics.

For the first tracker hygiene threshold, flag:

- any `in_progress` issue older than 14 days without a recent update; and
- any open or `in_progress` child whose parent epic is closed.

The thresholds may be tuned later, but the first implementation should make
these two currently observed drift classes visible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single command, documented as the drift patrol entry point, runs the bounded drift suite.
- A recurring trigger invokes that command, or the lack of CI is explicitly handled by wiring the command into the local agent/audit completion path.
- The command fails when any enabled drift check fails and prints the responsible issue or remediation path.
- The patrol output includes enough context to create or update a Beads issue without redoing the audit.
- Documentation states the cadence, owner/audience, and what to do with failures.

## Out of Scope

- Full quality gates on every patrol run unless they are already cheap enough.
- Replacing the deeper manual audit process.
- Duplicating str-wurp, str-2fjn, or str-5dx0 implementation details.
close_reason: Landed on main at bddf2481 (merge commit; feature commits 9d52ac31, a758d94e). Gate evidence: task test-standard -> exit 0 (local, run twice: before and after the review-fix commit); 33/33 scripts/test_drift_patrol.py unit tests pass; CI ci.yml test job -> pass (PR #2, run 31210298381); CI Patrol self-test job -> pass; land-work project verifier -> passed, 3 selected checks, 0 unverified paths. Independently reviewed (Merge with fixes -> fixed: added LoadTrackerTest for the bd/jsonl fallback path; documented missing Taskfile sources: block; filed str-ny1jh as non-blocking follow-up for run_command's OSError handling).

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
Audit 2026-09-22 follow-up. This issue was closed (bddf2481) on the evidence of "CI Patrol self-test job -> pass" and the PR's ci.yml run. On pull requests, `drift-patrol.yml` skips the `patrol` job (`if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`), so that evidence could not show a scheduled patrol running.

The scheduled workflow has never executed the patrol. All 7 scheduled runs, from 2026-08-10 to 2026-09-21, failed in `actions/setup-go` with `The specified go version file at: go.mod does not exist` (for example run 35620815498). The cause is that `drift-patrol.yml:85` sets `go-version-file: go.mod`, and the repo has no root go.mod. It should be `shatter-go/go.mod`, the same bug str-wnyzy fixed in ci.yml only.

The fix, a test that every workflow's file paths exist, the missing tracker-server row in DRIFT-PATROL.md, and the requirement that the close reason cite a real scheduled or dispatched patrol run are tracked in `str-49drv.24`.

title: Epic: Drift enforcement
description:
## Problem

Shatter repeatedly accumulates drift between implementation, documentation, protocol metadata, CLI examples, agent instructions, and issue state. The latest audit found stale SPEC.md CLI content, missing docs/stories, failing conformance despite protocol validators passing, duplicated RTK instructions, and audit/issue-filing skill instructions that conflict with each other.

Several instance or surface-specific issues already exist:

- str-ck05: SPEC.md overhaul.
- str-wurp: mechanical CLI surface drift gate.
- str-2fjn: protocol registry/schema cross-validation against implementations.
- str-5dx0: scheduled parity divergence expiry warnings.
- str-qe9pp: current Rust frontend conformance/parity drift.

Those issues are necessary but not sufficient. This epic tracks the missing governance layer: drift checks must have real triggers, real enforcement, and a recurring audience.

## Desired Outcome

Shatter has a small, documented drift-governance system where high-risk drift classes are checked automatically at the right cadence, and where failures become visible before they linger for weeks.

## Child Work

Create child issues for:

- A scheduled drift patrol that runs a bounded suite and reports or files failures.
- Executable docs/example checks for README, QUICKSTART, SPEC, and docs snippets.
- Storystore/docs stories coverage so user-visible intent does not disappear.
- Agent instruction and plugin workflow drift linting.

## Acceptance Criteria

- This epic has concrete child issues for each missing enforcement surface above.
- Each child issue names at least one trigger and one failing enforcement path, not only a human checklist.
- Existing issues str-ck05, str-wurp, str-2fjn, str-5dx0, and str-qe9pp are referenced instead of duplicated.
- The epic remains open until the child enforcement mechanisms are landed or explicitly superseded.

## Out of Scope

- Fixing SPEC.md content directly; tracked by str-ck05.
- Implementing CLI inventory drift checks; tracked by str-wurp.
- Implementing protocol field/runtime cross-checks; tracked by str-2fjn.

title: Go mock substitution works
description:
Kapow's low-coverage scan shows branch-heavy importer/scraper targets where Shatter should use fake browser/fetch/LLM dependencies instead of letting target code launch real browser processes or external services.

## Evidence

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-go/CLAUDE.md` says `.shatter/config.yaml` parses `mocks`, and the planner emits `planner.MockSpec`, but execute-time substitution is "not implemented".
- The same doc says anything relying on `mocks` to take effect at runtime is currently unsupported.
- Kapow browser constructors include `tools/kapow/internal/scraper/browser.go::NewContext`, `tools/kapow/internal/deadlines/scraper.go::NewScraper`, and `tools/kapow/importer_rankings_qs.go::newQSScraperBrowser`.
- Kapow's `.shatter/config.yaml` currently has `go_runtime_values` for `*config.Config` and an `llm` local adapter, but no browser/fetch mock behavior.

## Requested Behavior

Wire Go hint-config mocks through to actual execute-time substitution for package functions/constructors that are currently unsafe or too expensive for validation scans. The first acceptance fixture should prove that a configured mock for a Go constructor prevents the real constructor body from running and returns a deterministic fake suitable for branch exploration.

## Scope

In scope:
- Go frontend build-time symbol swap, launcher-level shim, or another deterministic mechanism that makes configured Go mocks affect execution.
- Regression coverage proving a mocked constructor does not spawn a subprocess or touch the network.
- A small Kapow-oriented validation using a browser/scraper constructor shape.

Out of scope:
- Broad syscall interception.
- LD_PRELOAD/eBPF.
- Making real Chrome/LLM runs part of normal Shatter coverage.

## Acceptance

- `.shatter/config.yaml` `mocks` entries can affect Go execution, not only planning.
- A regression test proves that a mocked constructor is called instead of the real constructor and that the real side effect is absent.
- A Kapow validation run for at least one browser/scraper target completes without launching a real Chromium/Rod browser process.
- Documentation is updated so `shatter-go/CLAUDE.md` no longer says execute-time mock substitution is unimplemented.

## Anti-Hallucination Requirement

Before implementation, re-read the cited files and report JSON in the current checkout. If any path, symbol, metric, or capability claim differs, update the issue notes before coding or stop and ask. Do not rely on memory from the drafting session.
notes: 2026-07-01 investigation (kapow coverage goal): root cause confirmed — instrument.GenerateLoopMockFile emits ShatterMock_<sym> return-value tables for auto-discovered mocks (instrument/executor.go:139, build/instrumented_overlay.go:99) but NO call-site rewrite exists (instrument/visitor.go:161 rewriteSideEffectCall only matches a fixed stdlib allowlist), so mock bodies are dead code and e.g. kapow auth.GetAccount(ctx) always returns nil (every resolver dies at the auth guard, 1 path, ~3/18 lines). Fix: AST call-site rewriter matching MockConfig.Symbol via TypesInfo.Uses (pattern at wrapper.go:2420), rewriting to ShatterMock_/ShatterMockErr_ shims with typed return decode; wire through instrumented_overlay so the SAME mechanism serves config-file mocks (this issue's acceptance) and auto-discovered mocks.

title: axum crate harness reports empty lines_executed/branch_path for DB-backed handlers
description: REFRAMES str-0wxw-B. After str-wjhv, pickpackit list_tags EXECUTES via the axum crate harness (generate_axum_crate_harness -> generate_axum_harness) and RETURNS REAL DATA: return_value.body = the seeded tags, thrown_error null, access guard PASSES (Path synthesized from recipe axum.path=/test/{workspace_id}). BUT result.lines_executed=[] and branch_path=[] => 0 coverage despite full execution. shatter_rust_runtime line/branch tracking is THREAD-LOCAL (shatter-rust-runtime/src/*.rs:167 thread_local!). The axum harness runs the handler under tokio::runtime::Runtime::new() (MULTI-THREAD, executor.rs:5491) and the instrumented handler lives in the crate-shadow (a separate compiled copy of the user crate that depends on shatter-rust-runtime). Two candidate causes: (a) crate-shadow links a DIFFERENT shatter-rust-runtime instance than the driver, so line_hit writes one thread_local and flush_results reads another; (b) the DB-backed handler body executes on a tokio worker thread (await points) while flush runs on the block_on thread. The simple in-tree test crate_backed_axum_handler_reports_executed_branch_lines passes only because its handler has no real await points and is single-crate. FIX DIRECTIONS: ensure the crate-shadow and driver share ONE shatter-rust-runtime instance (cargo unification via identical path/version) AND/OR use a current-thread runtime + flush on the same thread, or aggregate thread-local counters across threads. This is the LAST gap before handler branch coverage is real.
notes:
FULLY RESOLVED across BOTH harness paths (landed: axum 0c6f8ab3, crate-bridge ba710ad2). The same relative-vs-absolute strip_prefix bug existed in execute_function_crate_bridge (non-axum path): file_path relative, crate_root absolute -> instrumented source + in-module __shatter wrapper written to bogus path -> crate-shadow compiled original -> undefined symbol shatter_crate_bridge_entry (LINK error) for every non-axum function (pure helpers, &PgPool helpers). The tags.rs file-scan runtime_failed:9 were a MIX of this link error (serial) + cargo build-lock contention (parallel, str-<contention issue>). With both staging fixes + clean cache: axum handlers ~38% lines (scenario-pinned, 0 branches); pure fns get line+BRANCH coverage (require_trimmed: 12 iters, 2 paths, 1/1 branches, 71% lines 5/7). Achievable coverage is now MUCH higher than the 3% stale-cache reading; branchy logic (validators, access helpers) covers real branches. Handler branch coverage still needs scenario diversity (str-0wxw-B).
Fix trade-off: switched generate_axum_harness's Tokio runtime to current-thread (Builder::new_current_thread()) to fix thread-local line/branch coverage loss for handlers with genuine cross-thread awaits. Caveat: current-thread runtimes cannot host tokio::task::block_in_place — any axum handler (or a dependency it calls into, e.g. a DB driver bridging a blocking call) that invokes block_in_place will panic under this harness ('can't call block_in_place from a current_thread context'). No in-tree/example axum fixture currently uses block_in_place, so nothing is known-broken today, but this is worth checking if a kapow/pickpackit target handler hits it later. Alternative fix direction (not implemented): aggregate thread-local counters across threads instead of pinning execution to one thread — see issue description's original two fix directions.
close_reason:
Landed on main at 6540f561 (merge of str-oc67-axum-threadlocal-flush).

This closes the residual gap from the earlier str-oc67 path-bug fixes
(0c6f8ab3 axum, ba710ad2 crate-bridge, already on main): the axum crate
harness's generate_axum_harness still spun up a multi-thread Tokio
runtime, so shatter-rust-runtime's thread-local line/branch coverage
recorded into a different thread than flush_results() read whenever a
DB-backed handler's await hopped onto a worker thread, silently
dropping coverage despite correct execution. Switched to a
current-thread runtime, matching every other harness generator in the
file (generate_dispatch_harness, stdout/stderr capture,
generate_crate_bridge_wrapper all already used it -- axum was the sole
outlier). Documented the resulting block_in_place trade-off at the
call site.

Gate evidence:
- cargo test --lib (shatter-rust): green across two verification
  passes as main advanced during landing; one isolated build-timeout
  flake in unrelated native-replay tests reconfirmed passing in
  isolation. New regression test
