title: Deterministic + detectable embedded-frontend builds (cargo not recompiling shatter-core; build.rs dir rerun-if-changed misses edits)
description:
## Problem

Embedded-frontend builds are non-deterministic and stale-failures are invisible,
which was the single largest time sink in the configured-input investigation
(many cycles testing a binary that did not contain the change under test).

Two concrete defects:
1. `cargo build -p shatter-cli` did not reliably recompile `shatter-core` after
   edits to `scan_orchestrator.rs` — the built binary lacked freshly-added code
   (verified via `strings <binary> | grep <probe>` = 0). Touching the `.rs` file
   forced it; the edit alone did not.
2. `shatter-cli/build.rs` uses `cargo:rerun-if-changed=<dir>` on directories
   (e.g. `shatter-go/protocol`). Cargo's directory rerun does NOT detect in-place
   edits to files already inside the directory, so editing a `.go` file does not
   reliably trigger the embedded `go build`. (Worked around all session by
   `touch shatter-cli/build.rs`.)

## Proposed fix

- `build.rs`: track explicit file globs or a content hash of the `shatter-go`
  tree instead of directory `rerun-if-changed`, so any Go edit rebuilds the
  embedded frontend.
- Make staleness DETECTABLE: `shatter --version` prints the embedded-frontend
  build hash; `shatter doctor` / a `task check` step fails loudly when the
  binary's frontend hash != current `shatter-go` source hash.

## Acceptance

- Editing any `shatter-go` source rebuilds the embedded frontend on the next
  `cargo build` (no manual `touch`).
- A stale binary is detectable from `--version`/`doctor` output.

Labels: build, debuggability. Priority: high — caused the most wasted cycles.
close_reason: Already implemented and merged into main (6bfa8057: deterministic + detectable embedded-frontend builds). Stale in_progress claim; no further work needed.

title: Crate bridge dup features
description:
Title: Crate bridge dup features

Repository/tracker: Shatter repo Beads tracker (`str-*` issue IDs). Pickpackit is the downstream repro project.

## Summary

Focused Rust Shatter scans on current Pickpackit `origin/main` fail before handler execution because the generated crate bridge writes a `crate-shadow/Cargo.toml` with duplicate `[features]` sections.

This blocks validating `.shatter` generator work such as `pp-v2rz.9` after rebasing onto current `origin/main`.

## Current Code Facts

- Pickpackit commit under test: `a19af91` (`origin/main`) plus `pp-v2rz.9-people-shatter-input-spread` generator commits.
- Current `api/Cargo.toml` has a real `[features]` section:

  ```toml
  [features]
  coverage-denominators = ["dep:syn", "dep:proc-macro2"]
  ```

- `api/.shatter/config.yaml` has no evident crate-bridge or Cargo-feature override. It only maps Shatter generators and per-function parameter generators.
- The custom Rust frontend rebuild itself succeeds:

  ```bash
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust \
  PATH=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust/target/debug:/home/ketan/project/shatter/target/debug:$PATH \
  /home/ketan/project/shatter/target/debug/shatter build-frontend rust
  ```

## Reproduction

From the Pickpackit `api/` directory on current `origin/main` or a branch rebased onto it, with the local Shatter checkout available at `/home/ketan/project/shatter`, run a focused Rust scan:

```bash
SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust \
SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust-runtime \
PATH=$(pwd)/.shatter-cache/bin:/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust/target/debug:/home/ketan/project/shatter/target/debug:$PATH \
DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:<postgres_port>/pickpackit_test \
STORAGE_BUCKET=pickpackit-images-test \
STORAGE_REGION=us-east-1 \
STORAGE_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localhost:<minio_port> \
STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID=pickpackit \
STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=pickpackit-minio \
STORAGE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<minio_port> \
STORAGE_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true \
/home/ketan/project/shatter/target/debug/shatter scan src/handlers \
  --include people.rs \
  --project-dir . \
  --language rust \
  --require-rust \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --isolation function \
  --timeout-total 420 \
  --timeout-per-fn 220 \
  --timeout-explore 120 \
  --max-iterations 2 \
  --request-timeout 220 \
  --exec-timeout 90 \
  --build-timeout 140 \
  --timing detailed \
  --timing-format json \
  --timing-output /tmp/pickpackit-people-iter2-timing.json \
  --format json \
  -o /tmp/pickpackit-people-iter2.json \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --quiet
```

Observed result from the rebased `pp-v2rz.9-people-shatter-input-spread` worktree:

```text
Scan complete: 0 completed, 4 failed, 0 unsupported, 0 skipped

error: duplicate key
  --> crate-shadow/Cargo.toml:63:2
   |
63 | [features]
   |  ^^^^^^^^
error: failed to get `pickpackit-api` as a dependency of package `shatter-exec-temp-...`

Caused by:
  failed to load source for dependency `pickpackit-api`

Caused by:
  unable to update .../crate-shadow
```

The same error appears for all four `people.rs` handlers, so Shatter fails before exercising any handler or native generator.

## Desired Behavior

Rust Shatter crate-bridge generation should handle target crates that already define `[features]`. It should either merge the required `shatter-crate-bridge` feature into the existing section or otherwise generate a valid Cargo manifest without duplicate table headers.

## Acceptance Checks

- A focused Rust scan for `api/src/handlers/people.rs` no longer fails with duplicate `[features]` in generated `crate-shadow/Cargo.toml`.
- The generated `crate-shadow/Cargo.toml` has at most one `[features]` table and preserves Pickpackit's existing `coverage-denominators` feature.
- The scan reaches handler execution; failures, if any, are real handler/generator/runtime failures rather than Cargo manifest parse errors.
- `shatter build-frontend rust` continues to succeed for Pickpackit native generators.

## In Scope

- Fixing Shatter Rust crate-bridge manifest generation or adding a documented Pickpackit `.shatter` configuration workaround if one already exists.
- Adding a regression test that covers a target Rust crate with an existing `[features]` table.

## Out of Scope

- Changing Pickpackit production API behavior.
- Removing the `coverage-denominators` feature from `api/Cargo.toml`.
- Changing the people generator input-spread work in `pp-v2rz.9`.
acceptance_criteria: Focused Pickpackit Rust scan no longer fails with duplicate [features] in generated crate-shadow/Cargo.toml; generated manifest preserves existing coverage-denominators feature; scan reaches handler execution; shatter build-frontend rust still succeeds.
notes:
Landed on main at ea27650b (merge commit) via bento:land-work.

Investigation found the actual fix (duplicate [features] table merge, section_header_insert_after) had already landed on main via a different issue, str-bphx (fix crate shadow feature injection), which had unit coverage for inject_crate_bridge_feature in isolation. This branch's single commit adds the missing full-path regression coverage: staging_then_inject_feature_with_existing_features_table exercises create_crate_staging_copy -> inject_crate_bridge_feature end-to-end against a workspace-member crate that already declares [features] (mirroring Pickpackit's coverage-denominators), asserting the staged manifest has exactly one [features] table containing both the original feature and shatter-crate-bridge.

Gate evidence (project verifier scripts/land_work_verifier.sh, run against the exact merge candidate):
  task test-standard -> passed
  task parity        -> passed
  task conformance    -> passed

Also ran directly: cargo test -p shatter-rust --lib -- --test-threads=2 -> 537 passed (default parallelism flaked with 26 failures — known build-timeout self-contention, see project memory; --test-threads=2 confirms it's environmental, not a regression); cargo clippy -p shatter-rust --lib -D warnings -> clean.

title: Configured defaults hint not applied for free functions in get_invocation_plan path (layer 3 of configured-input lever)
description:
## Problem

The configured-input coverage lever requires three layers to work end-to-end:
1. str-rd0a (LANDED): the hint-config resolver matches filename-scoped
   `defaults`/`generators` globs against the normalized SourceFile.
2. str-r2q7 (branch, HELD): scan feeds materialized planner seeds into the
   explorer (mirrors the explore CLI).
3. THIS issue: the planner must actually APPLY a configured `defaults` literal
   for a FREE FUNCTION at runtime so it becomes a materializable `Literal`
   ValuePlan / seed.

Layer 3 fails: with str-rd0a present (embedded frontend confirmed to contain
config.TargetRelpath), a configured default for a free function is NOT applied
in the get_invocation_plan path.

## Repro

shatter-cli built from str-r2q7 branch (which contains str-rd0a). Zolem worktree
`.shatter/config.yaml`:

```yaml
functions:
  "loader.go:loadOne":          # basename key — matches normalized SourceFile
    defaults:
      dir: "/home/ketan/project/zolem/testdata/fixtures/sample-anthropic"
```

`internal/fixture/loader.go::loadOne(dir string)` reads `<dir>/meta.yaml`. The
configured dir is a valid fixture directory.

EXPLORE (which already feeds planner seeds via
materialize_seeds_compatible_with_plan):

```
shatter explore "internal/fixture/loader.go:loadOne" --max-iterations 50
```

Observed: 50 iterations, **1 path, 3% coverage**, the single explored input is
`loadOne("")`. All 50 iterations hit the same `read meta.yaml: open meta.yaml:
no such file or directory` error path — the configured fixture path is NEVER
among the tried inputs. Same result under scan (with str-r2q7's seeding).

Expected: the configured `dir` is a top-priority `Literal` ValuePlan (param.go
adds the hint literal before family candidates), so the planner emits a plan
`[dir=Literal("/home/.../sample-anthropic")]`, materialize_seeds produces the
seed, and the explorer tries it — driving loadOne past the meta.yaml read.

## Analysis (where it breaks)

The match logic is correct in isolation (str-rd0a unit tests pass, including
TestHintConfigResolver_AbsoluteSourceFileMatchesFilenameGlob). The Go planner
applies hints generically for free functions: planOne (plan.go) →
paramOptionsForRequirement → opts.PerTargetHints(targetID) → HintsByName →
PlanParam emits ValuePlanKindLiteral (param.go ~193). So the chain SHOULD apply
the hint.

The break is therefore at runtime in the get_invocation_plan path: the
configured hint is not reaching the planner for this free function. Lead
hypotheses (in priority order):

1. SourceFile not populated on the cached analysis that buildTargetContext /
   lookupAnalyzedByTargetID returns for get_invocation_plan. SourceFile is only
   set during `analyze` (handler.go ~489/523/549, guarded by `if SourceFile ==
   ""`). If the analysis the planner closure sees has an empty SourceFile,
   hintConfigResolver's `config.Load(analysis.SourceFile)` fails and no hints
   resolve. CHECK FIRST.
2. targetID mismatch: hintConfigResolver does lookup(targetID) → MatchTarget on
   analysis.Name. Confirm the targetID passed by PlanRequirements resolves to
   the loadOne analysis with the right Name.
3. The planner emits the Literal but materialize_seed_for_plan rejects it, or
   the explorer does not try the seed first. (Less likely — explore tried 50
   inputs, none was the path.)

## Suggested instrumentation

Add a debug log in hintConfigResolver (shatter-go/main.go) printing
analysis.SourceFile, analysis.Name, and len(hints.Defaults) per target. Re-run
the loadOne explore and confirm whether hints.Defaults is empty (→ hypothesis
1/2) or populated (→ hypothesis 3).

## Acceptance criteria

- A configured `defaults.<param>` literal for a FREE FUNCTION is applied at
  runtime and materializes as a seed the explorer actually tries.
- With the loadOne config above, `shatter explore internal/fixture/loader.go:loadOne`
  tries `dir = "/home/.../sample-anthropic"`, reads meta.yaml, and reaches
  substantially higher coverage than 3%.
- Once green, validate str-r2q7 (scan seeding) end-to-end and run a whole-corpus
  before/after for regression, then land str-r2q7.

## Related

- str-rd0a (LANDED, config match), str-r2q7 (branch a791367c, scan seeding,
  held), str-2fui (coverage census / configured-input lever rationale).
- Artifacts: /var/tmp/r2q7-explore2.log (loadOne("") 50 iters), /var/tmp/r2q7-loadone.json.
notes: Landed on main (a6571aa0). Root cause was in shatter-cli (explore's planner consultation was flag-gated, not capability-gated like scan), not shatter-go — shatter-go's hint resolution was already correct end-to-end. Gate evidence: cargo clippy -p shatter-cli --all-targets (clean), cargo test -p shatter-cli (560 passed incl. new e2e regression test), go test ./... (992 passed), cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go --test-threads=1 --include-ignored (18 passed) — all run against the exact merge candidate. Independent code review verdict: Ready to merge, no blocking issues. Follow-ups filed: str-4i8ax (dedupe capability check). str-r2q7 (held scan-seeding branch) should be re-validated now that this layer is done.

title: Matched defaults param-literal not materialized as explored input for direct param (str-rd0a follow-on)
description:
## Problem

After str-rd0a fixed the hint-config MATCH (filename-scoped `defaults`/`generators`
globs now match an absolute SourceFile), a matched per-function `defaults` literal
for a DIRECT free-function parameter still does NOT reach the parameter's explored
inputs. The configured value never appears in `discovered_inputs`, in either the
random or `--concolic` explorer, so it does not drive coverage.

Per shatter-go/CLAUDE.md (Hint Config v1): "defaults: per-parameter literal
overrides flow into planner.ParamPlanOptions.HintsByName and become top-priority
ValuePlans, taking precedence over classifyParamFamily defaults." The match now
succeeds (config.TargetRelpath + MatchTarget, validated), but the resulting
ValuePlan literal is apparently not materialized into a concrete explored input by
the scan's explorer/orchestrator.

## Repro (with str-rd0a applied)

shatter-cli built from str-rd0a branch (587fb7c9; embedded frontend contains
config.TargetRelpath — verified via `strings`).

Zolem worktree `.shatter/config.yaml`:

```yaml
functions:
  "loader.go:loadOne":          # basename key — matches normalized SourceFile
    defaults:
      dir: "/home/ketan/project/zolem/testdata/fixtures/sample-anthropic"
```

Target: `internal/fixture/loader.go::loadOne(dir string)` reads `<dir>/meta.yaml`.
The configured fixture dir is valid (contains meta.yaml + response.json).

```
shatter scan internal/fixture --include "**/loader.go" --all \
  --parallelism 1 --scheduler-policy serial [--concolic] --no-cache -o out.json
```

Observed (both modes): loadOne stays at 3.5% (random) / 4.7% (concolic), 1/18
branches. discovered_inputs are shatter's own path-boundary values
(`""`, `"meta.yaml"`, `/tmp/shatter-enoent-dir-*`) or random strings — the
configured `dir` path is never among them.

Expected: at least the top-priority iteration uses `dir =
"/home/.../sample-anthropic"`, so loadOne reads meta.yaml, finds response.json,
and proceeds through its happy path to much higher coverage.

## Where to look

- Go planner: `planner.ParamPlanOptions.HintsByName` → does PlanParam emit a
  ValuePlan carrying the default literal for a direct primitive `string` param?
- Plan→explorer bridge: `shatter-core` planner_consumer / scan_orchestrator input
  generation — does it materialize a `defaults`/`literal` ValuePlan as a concrete
  first input, or only handle certain kinds (the docs note runtime_value is
  deserialized but "does not materialize a seed")? The random explorer clearly
  generates its own inputs and ignores plan literals; confirm whether the concolic
  orchestrator injects the literal as a seed.
- Whether `defaults` for direct params is wired at all today vs only for
  constructor/struct-field hints.

## Why it matters

Configured per-function inputs (real fixture dirs, valid structured payloads) are
the realistic "usage change" lever for the large class of Zolem functions gated
behind filesystem fixtures and valid structured inputs — the dominant
line-coverage gap (str-2fui: branch 62% >> line 26%). str-rd0a unblocked the
match; this issue is the remaining blocker to making configured inputs actually
drive coverage. Without it, the configured-input lever is unavailable and the
line-coverage ceiling stays low regardless of explorer or budget.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `functions.<glob>.defaults.<param>` literal for a direct free-function
  parameter is injected as a concrete explored input (at least the top/first
  iteration) in the explorer used by `scan` (document which modes honor it).
- With the loadOne config above, loadOne's discovered_inputs include the
  configured fixture path and its line coverage rises materially above 3.5%.
- shatter-go/CLAUDE.md Hint Config v1 section updated to state the actual,
  verified end-to-end behavior of `defaults` for direct params.

## Evidence

  config.TargetRelpath.
- /var/tmp/rd0a-loadone-final.json (random), /var/tmp/rd0a-loadone-concolic.json
  (concolic) — both show loadOne without the configured path.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE ISOLATED (precise).

scan_orchestrator.rs only calls planner_consumer::fetch_planner_seeds via
fetch_default_execute_plan_for_method (line ~5053), which:
  (a) early-returns None for FREE functions (is_method_target_name guard, ~5059) —
      so free functions like loadOne NEVER fetch planner seeds at all; and
  (b) for methods, takes only the receiver plan (.find(|p| !p.receiver_kind.is_empty()))
      and DISCARDS bundle.seeds.

So the materialized Literal/Zero seeds — including configured .shatter defaults
(now matched after str-rd0a) — are never added to scan's candidate_inputs pool.
The scan seed pool (scan_orchestrator.rs ~1675-1692, 2953) comes only from
config_function_inputs, expression-string candidates, cached behavior-map seeds,
boundary_dict, and pool_seeds — never fetch_planner_seeds.

By contrast EXPLORE (shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs ~989-1025) DOES consume
planner seeds: it selects a materializable plan and feeds
materialize_seeds_compatible_with_plan(...) into the explore seed pool. This is a
scan-vs-explore parallel-path divergence (CLAUDE.md warns about exactly this).

FIX: make scan mirror explore — fetch planner seeds for EVERY function, select a
materializable plan, and extend candidate_inputs with
materialize_seeds_compatible_with_plan(...). Preserve the existing method-only
default_execute_plan behavior. Blast radius is bounded: family candidates are
Literal/Zero (param.go ~313-339) so unconfigured primitives also yield seeds, but
scan already feeds boundary_dict seeds (~2953), so the genuinely new signal is the
configured defaults. Validate with a whole-corpus before/after for regression.

Verified: materialize_seeds handles Literal/Zero (planner_consumer.rs ~144-176);
the Go planner emits ValuePlanKindLiteral for a matched defaults hint (param.go ~193).

title: Per-function defaults param-literal override not applied to direct free-function param (blocks configured-input coverage lever)
description:
## Problem

The `.shatter/config.yaml` per-function parameter literal override
(`functions.<glob>.defaults.<param>`) does not appear to take effect for a
direct free-function string parameter. Configured values never show up in the
explored inputs, in either random or `--concolic` mode.

Per shatter-go/CLAUDE.md (Hint Config v1): "defaults: per-parameter literal
overrides flow into planner.ParamPlanOptions.HintsByName and become top-priority
ValuePlans, taking precedence over classifyParamFamily defaults."

## Repro

Target: `~/project/zolem/internal/fixture/loader.go::loadOne(dir string)` — reads
`<dir>/meta.yaml` etc. from disk; with a random `dir` it always hits
file-not-found and stays at ~3.5% line / 1-of-18 branches.

Config (in a zolem worktree `.shatter/config.yaml`):

```yaml
functions:
  "internal/fixture/loader.go:loadOne":
    defaults:
      dir: "/home/ketan/project/zolem/testdata/fixtures/sample-anthropic"
```

Scan (shatter-cli @main aa6c4499):

```
shatter scan internal/fixture --include "**/loader.go" --all \
  --parallelism 1 --scheduler-policy serial --no-cache [--concolic] -o out.json
```

Observed: `loadOne` discovered_inputs are shatter's own path-boundary values
(`""`, `"meta.yaml"`, `/tmp/shatter-enoent-dir-*`) and random strings — the
configured `dir` path is NEVER used. Coverage unchanged (3.5% random, 4.7%
concolic). Expected: `dir` = the configured fixture path on at least the
top-priority iteration, driving `loadOne` through its happy path (read meta.yaml,
detect response.json) to much higher coverage.

## Candidate causes (needs triage)

1. Match-key format: `MatchTarget` (shatter-go/config/loader.go) uses
   `filepath.Match` on `relpath:function`. The pattern `internal/fixture/loader.go`
   only matches if the resolved `relpath` is exactly that (module-relative). If
   the resolver passes an absolute path or a differently-rooted relpath, the
   entry never matches. Confirm what relpath the HINT-config resolver
   (main-side `hintConfigResolver`/`translateHintConfig`, distinct from the
   policy-side `policyTargetRelpath`) passes.
2. Plumbing: even when matched, the `defaults` literal becomes a planner
   ValuePlan. The RANDOM explorer may not consume planner ValuePlans (generates
   its own inputs), and the concolic `planner_consumer` may not materialize a
   seed for the `literal`/`runtime_value` kind. Confirm both explorer paths
   actually inject a matched `defaults` literal as a concrete first-iteration
   input.

## Why it matters

Configured per-function inputs are the realistic "usage change" lever for the
large class of Zolem functions gated behind filesystem fixtures and valid
structured payloads (the dominant line-coverage gap; see str-2fui). If
`defaults` cannot supply a direct param a concrete value that the explorer
actually uses, that lever is unavailable and the line-coverage ceiling stays
low regardless of budget or explorer choice.

## Acceptance criteria

- A regression proves a `functions.<glob>.defaults.<param>` literal for a direct
  free-function parameter is injected as a concrete explored input (first/top
  iteration) in BOTH random and concolic modes, OR the documented behavior is
  corrected to state the actual scope.
- With the loadOne config above, loadOne's discovered_inputs include the
  configured fixture path and its line coverage rises materially above 3.5%.
- shatter-go/CLAUDE.md Hint Config v1 section is updated to match actual behavior
  (which explorer modes honor `defaults`, and the required match-key format).

## Evidence

- /var/tmp/loadone-cfgfile.json (random, config file), /var/tmp/loadone-concolic-cfg.json
  (concolic, config file), /var/tmp/loadone-fixturepath.json (--set override, also no effect).
- shatter-go/config/loader.go MatchTarget/matchScore/globMatch.
- Related: str-2fui (coverage census + consolidated findings), str-e41w (symbolic request bodies).
close_reason: Landed in main d18ae000. Centralized SourceFile normalization as config.TargetRelpath; hint-config resolver now matches filename-scoped defaults/generators globs consistently with the policy resolver. Validated: config + full protocol (704) + E2E Go (9/9). NOTE: this fixes the config MATCH; making a matched defaults literal reach a direct param's explored inputs is a separate downstream issue, filed as the str-rd0a follow-on (defaults-not-materialized).

title: Coverage baseline measured under RANDOM explorer — re-baseline Zolem with --concolic (Z3 solver off by default)
description:
## Problem (high leverage)

The whole-corpus Zolem coverage baseline (19.7% line / 44.7% branch, 358
functions) and every focused scan in this goal's investigation were run with the
**random explorer**, NOT the concolic (Z3-backed) solver. `--concolic` is
`#[arg(long)] pub concolic: bool` with **no default** in
`shatter-cli/src/args.rs` (lines ~423 and ~694), so it defaults to `false` for
both `scan` and `explore`. Zolem's `shatter.config.json` / `.shatter/config.yaml`
do not enable it either. `scan.rs` does wire the flag through to
`ScanConfig.concolic` → the scan orchestrator, so `shatter scan --concolic`
engages the solver; it is simply off by default.

Consequence: the Z3 constraint solver — which exists and supports integers,
reals, and **strings** (`shatter-core/src/solver.rs` uses `z3::ast::String`) —
was never engaged when measuring coverage. Random input generation almost never
hits:

- magic string constants in `switch`/equality gates (e.g.
  `internal/fixture/sequence.go::ParseExhaustAction` switches on
  `"last"|"cycle"|"error"|"fallthrough"`; stuck at ~12%),
- precise numeric boundaries (`n < total`, `total <= 0`),
- enum/const discriminators.

Crucially, the analyzer ALREADY emits solvable symbolic conditions for these:
`switchBranches`/`switchCaseConditionText` in `protocol/analyzer.go` build
`bin_op{eq, param(s), const("last")}` conditions per switch case, and
`symextract.go` captures string literals as `const{type:str}`. So the machinery
to crack these branches exists end-to-end — it is just not exercised by a
default (random) scan.

This means a large fraction of the "low coverage" functions in the census
(str-2fui) — especially switch-on-string validators/parsers and
numeric-comparison gated logic — are likely **random-exploration artifacts, not
input-synthesis gaps**. The goal's 90% target may be far more achievable simply
by running the corpus under `--concolic`, plus targeted fixes for what concolic
genuinely cannot crack (stateful multi-call sequences like
`(*SequenceCounters).Step`, and structured JSON/YAML bodies).

## Proposed direction

1. Re-baseline: run a bounded whole-corpus (or stratified-sample) Zolem scan
   with `--concolic` (serial / low parallelism, per the load constraints) and
   compare line+branch coverage against the random baseline. Capture the delta.
2. Decide the default: if concolic materially improves corpus coverage with
   acceptable runtime, make the Zolem scan invocation use `--concolic` (a
   "usage of shatter" change, explicitly allowed by the goal) — e.g. wire it
   into `shatter.config.json` if the config supports it, or the run command.
   Consider whether `scan` should default to concolic project-wide (separate
   shatter-product decision; relates to str-yhsp "make --concolic available on
   run").
3. Re-triage str-2fui's pure-computational census under concolic: the functions
   that jump are solved; the ones that stay low reveal the REAL synthesis gaps
   (stateful sequences, structured inputs) worth fixing.

## Why this matters first

Every coverage conclusion drawn so far (str-nzn3 "no gain", str-e41w "zero gain
on local_admin", the 19.7% baseline) was measured under random exploration.
Before investing in more input-synthesis features, the corpus must be measured
under the solver that those features feed. Otherwise we risk building synthesis
machinery whose output the default explorer never exploits.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `--concolic` whole-corpus (or representative stratified-sample) Zolem scan
  is captured and its line+branch coverage compared to the random baseline,
  with the per-function deltas for the str-2fui census functions.
- A decision is recorded (issue or config change) on whether Zolem scans should
  run under `--concolic` by default, with justification.
- str-2fui is re-triaged against the concolic results so remaining low-coverage
  functions reflect genuine synthesis gaps, not explorer choice.

## Evidence

- `shatter-cli/src/args.rs` ~L423 / ~L694: `#[arg(long)] pub(crate) concolic: bool` (no default → false).
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs` L97, L808: `concolic` flows into `ScanConfig.concolic`.
- `shatter-core/src/solver.rs` L10: `use z3::ast::{... String as Z3String}` (string theory present).
- `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go` `switchBranches` / `switchCaseConditionText`: switch cases emit symbolic `param == const` conditions.
- `shatter-go/instrument/symextract.go` L138-144: string literals captured as `const{type:str}`.
- Related: str-2fui (pure-computational census), str-yhsp (--concolic on run).
notes: Closing as resolved-by-investigation. Acceptance criteria met via 2026-06-15 comments: whole-corpus re-baseline captured (25.7% line / 62.1% branch vs 19.7%/44.7% starved baseline), decision recorded — concolic REFUTED for switch-on-string functions (worse than random: 25%/2-6 branches vs 44%/6-6 with magic constants hit), real lever was per-function iteration budget not explorer type. Recommended next fixes never filed as children until now; see str-2fui for the same conclusion and the two follow-up issues filed off this investigation (structured-input seed pool, schema-aware structured-input synthesis). Found stale during bento:swarm triage (2026-08-10).

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
CORRECTION — A/B experiment REFUTES the concolic premise of this issue.

Ran focused serial scans of internal/fixture/sequence.go::ParseExhaustAction
(switch on "last"/"cycle"/"error"/"fallthrough") with a shatter-cli built from
main @118a0e27, random vs --concolic:

- RANDOM:   44% line, 6/6 branches covered, hit ALL 4 magic strings (last,
  cycle, error, fallthrough). 59 inputs.
- CONCOLIC: 25% line, 2/6 branches covered, hit ZERO magic strings. 32 inputs.

Findings:
1. The RANDOM explorer ALREADY mines and feeds the switch-case string constants
   (it discovered "last"/"cycle"/etc. by name — random text generation cannot do
   that by chance, so constant extraction exists in the random input path). It
   cracks the switch fully (6/6 branches) given adequate per-function budget.
2. --concolic is WORSE here, not better: fewer branches, no magic strings. So
   this issue's premise ("re-baseline with --concolic to lift coverage") is
   refuted for switch-on-string functions. Do NOT switch the Zolem corpus scan
   to --concolic on the strength of the str-2fui census.
3. The SAME function read 12% in the budget-constrained whole-corpus baseline
   (/tmp/zolem-whole-str-aaso.json, since lost to reboot) but 44%/6-branches in
   this focused run. The dominant variable is PER-FUNCTION ITERATION/TIME BUDGET,
   not explorer type. The whole-corpus config (timeout_total 900s across 358
   functions ≈ 2.5s/function) starves individual functions.

Revised direction (supersedes the concolic re-baseline):
- Re-baseline the whole corpus with ADEQUATE per-function budget (raise
  timeout_total / run in stratified batches so each function gets its full
  max_iterations), still random explorer. Measure how much of the 19.7% line /
  44.7% branch baseline is pure budget starvation. This is a usage/config
  change, allowed by the goal, and is likely the largest near-term lever.
- Keep --concolic OFF for the corpus pending evidence it helps any class of
  function (this experiment shows it hurting one class).

Artifacts: /var/tmp/seq-random.json (44%/6-6, magic hit),
/var/tmp/seq-concolic.json (25%/2-6, no magic).

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
NEW WHOLE-CORPUS BASELINE (supersedes the reboot-lost /tmp/zolem-whole-str-aaso.json).

Scan: shatter-cli @main 118a0e27, random explorer, `scan . --all --parallelism 4
--timeout-total 1800 --no-cache`. Artifact: /var/tmp/zolem-whole-main-118a0e27.json.

Result: 369 functions; 297 behavioral, 65 error_only, 7 skipped_by_policy, 28 unsupported.
- LINE   1576/6129 = 25.7%  (old budget-starved baseline: 19.7%)
- BRANCH 623/1004 = 62.1%  (old baseline: 44.7%)
- coverage buckets: 0%:7, <25%:92, <50%:184, <75%:70, <90%:0, >=90%:16

Interpretation (confirms this issue's corrected direction):
1. BUDGET was a real factor. Giving each function adequate iteration budget lifted
   BRANCH coverage +17.4pts (44.7→62.1) and LINE +6pts (19.7→25.7) with NO code
   change and NO concolic — just `--parallelism 4 --timeout-total 1800` so functions
   aren't starved. This is a usage change, allowed by the goal.
2. The remaining gap to 90% is dominated by LINE coverage (25.7%): branch (62%) >>
   line (26%) means functions reach their guard branches but not their bodies. The
   bodies are gated behind valid structured inputs (JSON/YAML decode), filesystem
   fixtures (loaders take paths), HTTP routing/auth (handlers), and schema validation
   — none of which random or concolic input generation can synthesize from scratch.
3. 28 unsupported functions (up from 3) are a separate lever: nested struct fields
   with no constructor (openai.MessageContent) and opaque types (jsonschema.ErrorKind)
   pre-skip their consumers. Registering generators/constructors (str-ozjv-adjacent,
   via .shatter/config.yaml `generators`) would re-enable them.

Path to 90% (in priority order):
  A. Adopt adequate-budget scanning for the corpus (done-able now; lifts branch to
     ~62%, line to ~26%).
  B. Structured-input + fixture synthesis (seeds / schema-aware bodies / filesystem
     fixtures) — the dominant LINE-coverage lever. Largest effort; overlaps str-e41w.
  C. Reduce the 28 unsupported via configured generators for no-constructor struct
     fields and opaque types.

title: Pivot to concolic-tractable pure-computational coverage gaps (52 fns, 852 lines)
description:
## Problem

Toward the Zolem 90% line+branch coverage goal, the whole-corpus baseline
(`/tmp/zolem-whole-str-aaso.json`, 358 functions) sits at 19.7% line / 44.7%
branch. Investigation (and an independent review) established that the large
HTTP-handler cluster is gated by URL-path matching, HTTP method, auth headers,
and schema validation *before* any body decode — gates that pure concolic
exploration cannot crack without seeds (tracked under str-e41w and its
follow-ups). That cluster is therefore seed-territory, not a concolic win.

The higher-ROI near-term target is the set of **pure / near-pure computational
functions** that Shatter already reaches (outcome `behavioral`) but explores
shallowly, where concolic genuinely works (real branch conditions over the
function's own inputs, not opaque stdlib/library gates). A census of the
baseline for behavioral functions with >=2 branches, <60% line coverage, and
not in handler/IO/server files yields **52 functions, 852 uncovered lines**.
Top candidates by uncovered-line gap:

| gap | branches | cov | function | file |
|-----|----------|-----|----------|------|
| 52 | 18 | 22% | `(*Loader).Load` | internal/fixture/loader.go |
| 47 | 11 | 4%  | `loadFixtures` | startup.go |
| 31 | 10 | 14% | `(*fixturesYAMLSelector).Select` | internal/fixture/selector.go |
| 27 | 10 | 10% | `validateStreamDelay` | internal/runtime/store.go |
| 26 | 6  | 7%  | `(*SequenceCounters).Step` | internal/fixture/sequence.go |
| 24 | 4  | 8%  | `ValidateTemplate` | internal/fixture/template.go |
| 23 | 6  | 8%  | `RenderBody` | internal/fixture/template.go |
| 19 | 7  | 10% | `validateFixtureNamespace` | internal/runtime/store.go |
| 18 | 8  | 22% | `validateSignature` | internal/wasmgen/generator.go |
| 17 | 6  | 19% | `validateWASMProfile` | internal/runtime/store.go |
| 14 | 6  | 12% | `ParseExhaustAction` | internal/fixture/sequence.go |

(Full list: 52 functions, 852 uncovered lines.)

These are validators, parsers, and selectors whose branches turn on their own
parameter values — exactly what concolic should drive. The shallow coverage
suggests one or more *input-synthesis* gaps (e.g. parameterized-constructor
seed shapes — see str-ozjv — struct/enum field synthesis, or string/format
constraints) prevent the explorer from reaching deeper branches.

## Proposed direction

Triage these functions to find the common input-synthesis blocker(s):
1. Run a focused serial scan of `internal/fixture` and `internal/runtime`
   (the densest clusters) and inspect `discovered_inputs` for the
   highest-gap functions — identify whether the blocker is constructor seed
   shapes (str-ozjv), unsynthesized struct/enum params, string-format
   constraints, or insufficient iteration budget.
2. File and fix the specific synthesis gap(s) found, then re-scan and measure
   the per-function coverage delta. Pure-computational functions should show a
   real (non-zero) coverage gain when the blocker is removed, unlike the
   IO-gated handlers.

This issue is the tracking anchor for the pivot away from the HTTP-handler
cluster toward concolic-tractable targets. It is investigative until the
specific synthesis blockers are filed as their own fix issues.

## Acceptance criteria

- A focused serial scan of `internal/fixture` + `internal/runtime` is captured,
  and the dominant input-synthesis blocker(s) behind the shallow coverage of
  the listed functions are identified with `discovered_inputs` evidence.
- Each distinct synthesis gap found is filed as its own fix issue (linked here)
  with a model function and a focused repro.
- After fixes, the listed pure-computational functions show measurable line +
  branch coverage gains vs the str-aaso baseline.

## Evidence

- Baseline: `/tmp/zolem-whole-str-aaso.json` (19.7% line / 44.7% branch, 358 fns)
- Census method: behavioral outcome, >=2 branches, <60% line cov, excluding
  handler/IO/server files.
- Related: str-ozjv (Go ctor seed primitives), str-e41w (symbolic http.Request
  body — the IO-handler lever, separate territory).
notes: Closing as resolved-by-investigation. Acceptance criteria met via 2026-06-15 comments: full-budget scan of internal/fixture confirmed simple functions recover with budget, but complex parsers/loaders stay low (loadOne 3.5%, wasmSelector.Select 5.2%, Loader.Load 22%) because their bodies sit behind valid structured-input parsing (YAML/JSON/struct decode) that neither random nor concolic exploration can synthesize from scratch. Concolic confirmed not helpful (see str-ior1). Filing the two recommended follow-up issues now: structured-input seed pool support, and schema-aware structured-input synthesis. Found stale during bento:swarm triage (2026-08-10).

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
VALIDATED triage results (focused full-budget scans, shatter-cli @main 118a0e27,
random explorer).

A/B on internal/fixture/sequence.go::ParseExhaustAction (switch-on-string):
- random full-budget: 43.8% line, 6/6 branches, hit all magic constants.
- --concolic: 25% line, 2/6 branches, no magic constants.
=> --concolic is WORSE for switch-on-string; the random path already does
   constant extraction. (Detailed in str-ior1.)

Full-budget scan of all internal/fixture (49 fns, parallelism 4):
- aggregate 22.4% line / 43.9% branch.
- SIMPLE functions recover with budget (ParseExhaustAction 6/6).
- COMPLEX parsers/loaders stay low even at full budget:
  loadOne 3.5% (1/18 br), (*wasmSelector).Select 5.2% (0/12 br),
  (*Loader).loadFixturesYAML 16% (4/17 br), (*Loader).Load 22% (7/18 br).
- Branch coverage (44%) >> line coverage (22%): functions cover their guard
  branches but not their bodies. The bodies sit behind valid-input parsing
  (YAML/JSON/struct decode) that random AND concolic input generation cannot
  synthesize.

Conclusion / revised pivot:
The dominant LINE-coverage gap (what the 90% goal needs) is STRUCTURED-INPUT
SYNTHESIS, not explorer type or iteration budget:
1. Concolic does not help (hurts switch-on-string). Keep it off for the corpus.
2. Budget starvation explains some simple-function under-coverage; a
   proper-budget whole-corpus re-baseline (stratified batches / higher
   timeout_total) will lift simple functions but NOT the loaders/selectors.
3. The real lever for loaders/selectors/parsers is feeding VALID structured
   inputs — either seed-driven exploration (provide example YAML/JSON; a usage
   change allowed by the goal) or schema-aware body synthesis (detect the
   decode target type and generate a structured input). This is the same class
   as str-e41w (HTTP request bodies) — generalize it to YAML/JSON/struct
   decoders.

Recommended next fixes (file as children):
- Seed pool support for structured params (YAML/JSON loaders): wire .shatter
  seeds so the explorer mutates from valid examples instead of random bytes.
- Schema-aware structured-input synthesis: when a function decodes a param/body
  into a known struct, synthesize a JSON/YAML serialization of a symbolic
  instance of that struct.

Artifacts: /var/tmp/seq-random.json, /var/tmp/seq-concolic.json,
/var/tmp/fixture-fullbudget.json.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
CONSOLIDATED VALIDATED FINDINGS — path to Zolem 90% line+branch.

Current whole-corpus baseline (main aa6c4499, /var/tmp/zolem-whole-main-aa6c4499.json,
random, --parallelism 4 --timeout-total 1800): 25.9% line / 62.1% branch, 373 fns
(295 behavioral, 71 error_only, 7 policy-skipped, 24 unsupported). Goal: 90%/90%.

LEVERS TESTED (evidence-backed):
1. ITERATION BUDGET — REAL, partial. Old starved baseline 19.7%/44.7% -> 25.9%/62.1%
   purely by giving functions adequate budget (parallelism + timeout-total). Lifts
   SIMPLE functions (switch/comparison) to full branch coverage. Usage change; already
   reflected in the current baseline. Does NOT help complex parsers/loaders.
2. CONCOLIC (--concolic) — DOES NOT HELP; WORSE for switch-on-string. A/B on
   ParseExhaustAction: random 6/6 branches (hit all magic constants via the random
   path's constant extraction) vs concolic 2/6, no constants. Keep concolic OFF for
   the corpus. (str-ior1.)
3. INPUT-REPAIR (str-kn3f, landed) — NO corpus movement (25.7->25.9 line, 62.1->62.1
   branch). Coercing malformed fields to type-valid DEFAULTS makes inputs executable
   but does not produce SEMANTICALLY valid inputs to reach bodies.
4. CONFIGURED FIXTURE PATH (.shatter/config.yaml functions.<glob>.defaults.<param>) —
   did NOT apply to a free-function string param (loadOne dir) in either random or
   concolic mode; the configured path never appeared in discovered_inputs. Either the
   match-key format (filepath.Match on relpath:function) or the defaults->ValuePlan->
   explorer plumbing does not override a direct path param. NEEDS its own investigation
   issue before relying on configured inputs as a lever.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE LINE GAP (branch 62% >> line 26%):
Functions reach their GUARD branches but not their BODIES. Bodies are gated behind
inputs the explorer cannot synthesize from scratch:
  - filesystem fixtures: loaders take dir/path args (loadOne, loadFixturesYAML, Load
    read meta.yaml/response.json from disk) -> random paths => file-not-found.
  - valid structured payloads: JSON/YAML decoders + schema validators (provider
    handlers, openapi) -> random bytes => decode/validation failure.
  - HTTP routing/auth: handlers gate on URL path, method, x-api-key before body.
  - no-constructor struct fields / opaque types: 24 unsupported (openai.MessageContent,
    jsonschema.ErrorKind) pre-skip consumers.

REALISTIC PATH TO 90% (large, multi-feature; partly in progress via str-e41w):
  A. Keep adequate-budget random scanning (done) — holds branch ~62%, line ~26%.
  B. SEMANTIC INPUT INJECTION is the dominant LINE lever. Needs EITHER:
     - working configured-input support (fix lever #4) so real fixture dirs / valid
       payloads can be supplied per function (usage change, allowed), OR
     - seed-driven exploration mutating from valid examples, OR
     - schema-aware structured-input synthesis (detect decode target type, generate a
       valid JSON/YAML instance) — generalizes str-e41w from HTTP bodies to YAML/JSON.
  C. Configured generators for the 24 unsupported (no-constructor struct fields /
     opaque types) to re-enable their consumers.

NET: 90%/90% is not reachable by explorer tuning alone. It requires semantic
input-generation infrastructure (B) plus per-function input config (B/C). Effort is
substantial and ongoing across the swarm. The corpus is correctly measured at
25.9%/62.1% on latest main.

Artifacts: /var/tmp/zolem-whole-main-{118a0e27,aa6c4499}.json, /var/tmp/seq-{random,
concolic}.json, /var/tmp/fixture-fullbudget.json, /var/tmp/loadone-*.json.

title: shatter-rust analyzer: apply serde rename_all/rename to synthesized struct field names
description: collect_struct_defs extracts RAW Rust field names (snake_case), ignoring #[serde(rename_all=...)] on the struct and #[serde(rename=...)] on fields. So a struct with #[serde(rename_all="camelCase")] (e.g. all pickpackit domain structs: Item/Trip/Person/DestinationSupply) is synthesized with snake_case JSON keys (workspace_id) but crate_bridge from_value expects camelCase (workspaceId) -> deserialization fails with missing field workspaceId. This is the DOMINANT cause of error_only/0-branches on pickpackit suggestions.rs Trip/Item pure fns (verified: errors are missing field workspaceId on full inputs; missing field id is a shrinker artifact). Fix: in collect_struct_defs (shatter-rust/src/analyzer.rs), read the struct serde rename_all convention and per-field serde rename, and emit the RENAMED field name as the Object field key. Support at least camelCase/snake_case/PascalCase/SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE/kebab-case/lowercase/UPPERCASE. Acceptance: a struct with rename_all=camelCase synthesizes camelCase keys; pickpackit suggestions.rs Trip fns reach behavioral with >0 branches. This is the key remaining blocker for engine-synthesized structs (handlers are unaffected — they use .shatter generators emitting camelCase manually).
close_reason: a8a3f33bdbe29b4e549c238b658e90b9db61dfbf landed: analyzer applies serde rename_all/rename to synthesized struct field names (verified: removed the missing field workspaceId error class on pickpackit suggestions.rs); shrink_object now drops only optional fields. 506 shatter-rust + 188 input_gen tests + parity. NOTE: the per-function acceptance (Trip fns behavioral) is NOT yet met — remaining input-erosion blocker is str-kn3f.

title: Rust whole scan budget exhaustion
description:
## Problem

A current Shatter Rust whole-handler scan of Pickpackit successfully builds the custom Rust frontend and executes a substantial prefix of the handler corpus, but it exhausts the total scan budget before reaching 90% of the target functions.

Fresh evidence from June 13, 2026:

- Scan target: `/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/pp-shatter-whole-validate/api/src/handlers`
- Current Shatter validation revision: `c1b7baa0d95e1d6fcbb508bdbb77ca3c717ffc0b`
- Custom frontend build succeeded: `.shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom`
- Whole-handler scan artifact: `/var/tmp/pickpackit-current-whole-m1-serial.json`
- Whole-handler scan log: `/var/tmp/pickpackit-current-whole-m1-serial.log`

Observed result:

- `41` completed behavioral functions.
- `0` failed functions.
- `0` unsupported functions.
- `35` interrupted functions.
- `2` expected skipped functions from config (`fetch_legs_for_workspace`, `fetch_tasks_for_workspace`).
- JSON has `78` entries in `test_order` but only `41` entries in `functions`; interrupted functions appear in the rendered log, not as completed function records.
- Completed-function coverage averaged about `25.63%`, with one discovered input per completed function in this `--max-iterations 1` baseline.

The immediate blocker is that a current full-corpus Rust scan cannot complete enough functions inside the configured total budget to support the Pickpackit goal of 90%+ execution and 80% line/branch coverage across the whole project.

## Reproduction

From `/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/pp-shatter-whole-validate/api`, after building the current Shatter CLI and custom Rust frontend:

```bash
rtk proxy bash -lc 'set -o pipefail; nice -n 19 ionice -c3 env DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55078/pickpackit_test STORAGE_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localhost:56078 STORAGE_BUCKET=pickpackit-images-test STORAGE_REGION=us-east-1 STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID=pickpackit STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=pickpackit-minio STORAGE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:56078 STORAGE_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true PICKPACKIT_S3_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:56078 PICKPACKIT_S3_BUCKET=pickpackit-images-test PICKPACKIT_S3_REGION=us-east-1 PICKPACKIT_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=pickpackit PICKPACKIT_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=pickpackit-minio SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-pickpackit-validation-current/shatter-rust SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-pickpackit-validation-current/shatter-rust-runtime PATH=$(pwd)/.shatter-cache/bin:/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-pickpackit-validation-current/shatter-rust/target/debug:/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-pickpackit-validation-current/target/debug:$PATH /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-pickpackit-validation-current/target/debug/shatter scan src/handlers --project-dir . --language rust --require-rust --parallelism 1 --scheduler-policy serial --isolation function --timeout-total 900 --timeout-per-fn 220 --timeout-explore 120 --max-iterations 1 --request-timeout 220 --exec-timeout 90 --build-timeout 140 --format json -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-current-whole-m1-serial.json --no-cache --no-seeds --quiet 2>&1 | tee /var/tmp/pickpackit-current-whole-m1-serial.log'
```

The scan reports:

```text
Scan complete: 41 completed, 0 failed, 0 unsupported, 35 interrupted, 2 expected skipped
```

The interrupted set starts at `packing_items.rs::export_packing_items_csv` and continues through the remaining packing-items, people, session, tags, tasks, trips, and workspace handlers because the total scan budget is exhausted.

## Current Code Facts

- Pickpackit validation services were healthy during the run: Postgres on `localhost:55078`, MinIO on `localhost:56078`.
- The custom Rust frontend was built from current Shatter and Pickpackit `.shatter` config before the scan.
- The scan was intentionally serial and low priority to avoid overstressing the shared machine: `--parallelism 1 --scheduler-policy serial`, `nice -n 19`, `ionice -c3`.
- Process observation during the run showed repeated Rust harness/crate builds under temporary directories such as `/tmp/shatter-audit-3671511-1/harness/rust/...`, including crate-bridge and bin-only builds.
- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs` contains two relevant harness build paths:
  - `build_and_spawn_crate_harness` around line 2860: comments say it uses a per-harness target dir for bin-only harnesses and shared target dir for crate-bridge harnesses, and skips `cargo build` if the binary exists and generated inputs are unchanged.
  - `build_and_spawn_crate_bridge_harness` around line 4160: comments say the driver binary is stable-cacheable, but the implementation still runs `cargo_check_before_build(...)` before `cargo build` whenever the local cached binary does not already match.
- `stable_crate_bridge_dir` and `crate_bridge_target_dir` around line 2999 put crate-bridge harnesses under a content-addressed cache root when `harness_cache_root()` is available; otherwise they fall back to temp dirs.
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` around line 3753 computes a `scan_deadline` from `timeout_total` and, at layer boundaries, marks all remaining functions as `SkipCategory::Interrupted` with `timed out (total scan budget exceeded)`.
- The JSON artifact already has machine-readable skipped accounting under `codebase.skipped_functions`: `35` interrupted and `2` expected skipped. This issue is not about output accounting.

## Desired Behavior

A full Rust scan over Pickpackit handlers should complete the handler corpus without exhausting total scan budget under a conservative serial configuration, or Shatter should improve Rust harness build reuse/budgeting enough that this workload completes predictably without unsafe machine load.

For this goal, completion means the scan reaches at least 90% of non-skipped handler targets.

## Scope

In scope:

- Rust frontend scan throughput and build reuse/caching inside a single scan.
- Rust scan scheduling or budgeting behavior that causes later functions to be interrupted by total budget despite successful per-function setup.
- Focused reproduction against Pickpackit handlers with serial settings.

Out of scope:

- Nontrivial Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Deleting or skipping Pickpackit feature handlers to make percentages look better.
- Increasing host load with broad parallelism as the primary fix.
- Treating the current 41/78 partial scan as success.
- JSON/report accounting for interrupted or skipped functions unless it directly affects completion throughput.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A current Pickpackit handler scan with conservative settings completes at least 90% of non-skipped handler targets without exhausting the total scan budget.
- The fix does not require nontrivial Pickpackit feature-code changes or deleting feature code.
- The validation command is documented in the issue or commit notes with the exact Shatter revision and artifact path.
- Relevant Shatter Rust/frontend tests or targeted regression tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: Current Pickpackit handler scan with conservative settings completes at least 90% of non-skipped handler targets without exhausting total scan budget; fix does not require nontrivial Pickpackit feature-code changes or deleting feature code; validation command records exact Shatter revision and artifact path; relevant Shatter Rust/frontend or targeted regression tests pass.

title: shatter-rust crate_bridge: support by-reference params (&T) by deserializing owned T and passing a borrow
description: crate_bridge harness deserializes each param via serde_json::from_value::<TYPE>(inputs[i]) using the verbatim signature type. For a by-reference param like w: &Widget it emits from_value::<&Widget>, but &T is never DeserializeOwned, so execution fails with: function parameters are not JSON-harness compatible and may not implement DeserializeOwned (executor.rs ~1535-1541). Same root cause noted for &str in e2e_concolic_rust.rs header. Impact: ALL by-reference functions are unexecutable, including every pickpackit pure domain fn (supply_applies_to_trip(&DestinationSupply,&Trip), score_item(&Item,&Trip,..), suggested_packing_items(&[Item],&[Person],&Trip,&[DestinationSupply])). With str-do53 Phase 1 these now ANALYZE as executable (Object params) but still fail at execute. Desired: in the crate_bridge wrapper param-deser loop, strip a leading & (and &[T] -> Vec<T>) from the param type, deserialize the owned base type, bind it to a local, and pass &local (or &vec) at the call site. Handle &mut similarly. Acceptance: a fn fn f(w: &Widget) where Widget: Deserialize executes and reaches branch coverage (extend the synthetic xfile e2e or add e2e_concolic_rust case); &str params also execute (lifts the documented limitation). Out of scope: references with explicit non-elided lifetimes that affect return-borrow checking. Evidence: executor.rs param-deser loops ~2160-2200, 3687+; e2e_concolic_rust.rs module doc.

title: Go CEL matcher build timeout
description:
## Problem

After current Shatter `main` resolved the primitive constructor-prefix decode failures tracked by `str-ozjv`, a focused serial Zolem scan of `internal/fixture/cel.go` still fails the representative target `(*CompiledCELMatcher).Score`, but now for a different reason: the target times out during build after 120 seconds.

This remains a Zolem coverage blocker because the target does not execute far enough to produce a useful behavior map or coverage for the matcher score path.

## Evidence

Focused scan artifact:

```text
/tmp/zolem-cel-str-ozjv-check.json
```

The scan used a bounded serial Shatter run against `~/project/zolem`:

```bash
/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter scan . \
  --project-dir . --language go --include "internal/fixture/cel.go" \
  --exclude "**/*_test.go" --exclude "**/testdata/**" \
  --exclude "**/.git/**" --exclude "**/.shatter/**" \
  --exclude "**/.shatter-cache/**" \
  --all --parallelism 1 --scheduler-policy serial --isolation function \
  --timeout-total 240 --timeout-per-fn 20 --timeout-explore 12 \
  --max-iterations 1 --request-timeout 45 --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 120 --no-cache --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false --format json \
  -o /tmp/zolem-cel-str-ozjv-check.json
```

Observed summary:

- `CompileCELMatcher` completed with outcome `error_only` and nonzero coverage.
- `(*CompiledCELMatcher).Score` failed with `timed out during build after 120s`.
- Overall result for the focused file: 1 completed, 1 failed, 0 unsupported, 0 interrupted.
- The artifact no longer contains `cannot unmarshal object into Go value of type`, so this is not the old primitive constructor-prefix decode issue.

## Desired Behavior

Shatter should build and execute the generated Go harness for `(*CompiledCELMatcher).Score` without timing out. The target should either complete and produce behavioral observations or reach a target-level runtime outcome after harness construction succeeds.

## Scope

In scope:

- Shatter-side Go build, planner, wrapper, instrumentation, or execution behavior that makes this target build too slowly or hang.
- Focused regression coverage for a receiver method with the same constructor-prefix/receiver shape if a narrow reproducer is available.
- Bounded Zolem validation for `internal/fixture/cel.go`.

Out of scope:

- Non-trivial Zolem feature-code changes.
- Deleting or weakening Zolem CEL matcher behavior.
- Re-solving the primitive constructor-prefix decode issue; that older symptom is absent in the current artifact.

## Acceptance Checks

- A focused regression or scan proves `(*CompiledCELMatcher).Score` no longer times out during build.
- A focused serial scan of `internal/fixture/cel.go` completes `Score` or reaches a target-level runtime outcome after the harness build succeeds.
- No primitive constructor-prefix unmarshal regression appears in the focused artifact.
- Relevant Go and/or Rust gates pass for the changed Shatter components.

title: Default-deny host filesystem writes: refuse unsandboxed target execution; run targets in a throwaway working directory
description:
**Evidence (downstream repo zolem, May 25 - Jun 8):** direct `shatter scan` runs (outside the repo's Docker-sandboxed wrapper) executed a target function `newJSONLRecorder(path)` that does `os.OpenFile(path, O_CREATE|...)`. Shatter's literal-mined and generated string inputs became 0-byte files in the host repo root: the error-format literal "open calls file %q: %w" plus ~20 mutation-prefix variants ("op", "ope", "open", "open c", ...), and generated values "Bob Smith", "192.168.1.42", "qelmm", "a", "ab", " ". Recurring over two weeks; users did not notice for weeks. cwd-relative writes by explored functions are a class of escape, not a one-off: any target that opens, creates, renames, or deletes by relative path will mutate the invoking repo.

**Recommendation:**
1. When no sandbox backend is configured, refuse to execute targets unless an explicit opt-in flag (e.g. `--allow-host-writes`) is passed; print the sandbox setup hint.
2. Independently, chdir each target's process to a fresh throwaway temp dir by default so relative-path writes land there and are cleaned with the run; record files created there as observed side effects (this is signal, not just mess).
3. Document the change prominently (breaking for unsandboxed workflows).

**Acceptance checks:** running a scan with no sandbox and no opt-in flag exits with an instructive error; with the flag, a target creating `./foo` leaves no file in the invoking repo (created in the run temp dir and reported as a side effect); sandboxed runs unchanged.

**Scope:** in: execution-time guard + cwd isolation + docs. Out: full syscall-level sandboxing (existing backends cover that).

---

title: Go *http.Request synthesized with fixed empty body — handlers stall at ~5% coverage
description:
## Problem

Shatter's Go frontend synthesizes every `*http.Request` parameter as a single
fixed runtime value:

```go
// shatter-go/runtimeval/registry.go:151
"*http.Request": {
    Expression: `httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/", bytes.NewReader(nil))`,
    TypeHint:   "*http.Request",
},
```

The method is always `GET`, the path always `/`, and the body is always `nil`.
Because the body is empty and fixed, any HTTP handler that decodes a request
body (`json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(...)`) immediately fails decoding and
returns an early error path (typically 400), so the handler body is never
explored. The solver has nothing symbolic to drive: the request is a constant.

This is the single largest line-coverage gap in the Zolem corpus. In the
whole-corpus baseline (`/tmp/zolem-whole-str-aaso.json`, main d8c59195),
overall line coverage is 19.7% (1189/6049). The biggest contributors to the
gap are HTTP handlers stuck at ~5%:

- `internal/provider/anthropic/handler.go::(*Handler).handleMessages` — 7/137 lines (5%), 1 iteration, inputs `[false, null]`
- `internal/provider/openai/handler.go::(*Handler).handleChatCompletions` — 5/127 lines (4%), inputs `[0, MIN_INT]`
- `internal/provider/gemini/handler.go::(*Handler).handleGenerate` — 7/139 lines (5%)
- Plus `cmd/zolem/local_admin.go` handler methods (`handleListenerResource`, `handleProfileResource`, `handleListenerCalls`) at 10-13%, and `UpsertListener`/`UpsertProfile` request-body decoders.

Together these account for >1000 uncovered lines. Driving valid request bodies
into them is the highest-leverage step toward the 90% coverage goal.

## Root cause

The fixed runtime-value synthesis for `*http.Request` provides no symbolic
surface. There is a separate `go/http-handler` adapter
(`shatter-go/protocol/nethttp_adapter.go` + `nethttp_recognizer.go`) that DOES
synthesize symbolic request attributes (`method`, `path`, `headers`, `body`),
but it does not fire for these handlers for two reasons:

1. `recognizeHTTPHandler` (nethttp_recognizer.go:15) early-returns `nil` for any
   function with a receiver (`if fn.Recv != nil { return nil }`). All the Zolem
   provider handlers are methods on `*Handler`, so they are excluded — even
   though the param-counting logic immediately below has a comment stating
   method receivers "don't interfere."
2. The adapter launcher (`adapter_launcher.go:229`) explicitly rejects receiver
   method targets, and its generated harness references `target.<Function>` as
   a package-level exported symbol, so it cannot invoke unexported methods in a
   non-main package.

Note the regular (non-adapter) wrapper path ALREADY constructs the `*Handler`
receiver and calls the unexported method — that is how these functions reach
5% rather than being pre-skipped. The only missing piece is feeding a symbolic
HTTP request (specifically a symbolic body) into the regular path instead of
the fixed empty-body runtime value.

## Proposed direction

Make the request body symbolic so the solver can synthesize valid JSON payloads
that drive handlers past their decode/validation guards. Preferred approach
(smaller surface, reuses receiver + unexported-method handling that already
works in the regular path): replace the fixed `*http.Request` runtime value
with a parameterized construction whose body is decoded from a symbolic input
prefix, e.g. `httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/", strings.NewReader(body))` where
`body` is a symbolic string input. Keep method/path fixed initially (a symbolic
method risks `httptest.NewRequest` panicking on invalid verbs); revisit
symbolic method/path/headers as a follow-up.

Alternative approach: extend the `go/http-handler` adapter to support receiver
methods (relax the recognizer receiver bailout AND teach the adapter launcher
to construct the receiver and emit the harness into the target package so it can

## Acceptance criteria

- A handler that decodes a JSON request body (model:
  `internal/provider/anthropic/handler.go::(*Handler).handleMessages`) receives
  varied symbolic request bodies and is explored to substantially higher line

  least one downstream branch are covered).
- Focused serial scan of `internal/provider/anthropic` and
  `internal/provider/openai` shows handler line coverage materially increased

- A Go-frontend regression (analyzer/wrapper or adapter, as appropriate) proves
  `*http.Request` synthesis is driven by symbolic input rather than a constant
  empty body.
- E2E Go pipeline (`cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go`) still passes.
- Parity contract updated if protocol-visible Go frontend behavior changes.

- Focused debug scan: `/tmp/anthropic-handler-debug.log` (handleMessages 5%, 1 path, no adapter)
- Registry: `shatter-go/runtimeval/registry.go:151`
- Recognizer bailout: `shatter-go/protocol/nethttp_recognizer.go:15`
- Adapter launcher receiver rejection: `shatter-go/protocol/adapter_launcher.go:229`

title: Go ctor error nil receiver
description:
Title: Go ctor error nil receiver

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,zolem,coverage

## Problem

Shatter's Go execute path can invoke a method on a nil receiver after a
parameterized receiver constructor returns `(nil, error)`. This turns a
constructor setup failure into a target-body nil pointer panic, producing
`error_only` behavior maps and low coverage for stateful receiver methods.

This is a Zolem coverage blocker after `str-q69z`: the primitive constructor
prefix decode errors are fixed, but constructor-returned errors can still leave
the receiver nil.

## Reproduction

Use Shatter `main` commit `bcb9782b` or later. This issue assumes `str-q69z`
has already landed; that fix removed the earlier primitive constructor-prefix
decode failures for Zolem.

Check out Zolem separately, then substitute its checkout path for
`/path/to/zolem` in the commands below.

Build Shatter:

```bash
cd /path/to/shatter
cargo build -p shatter-cli
```

Run a focused scan of `cmd/zolem/recording.go`:

```bash
cd /path/to/zolem
/path/to/shatter/target/debug/shatter scan . \
  --project-dir . --language go \
  --include "cmd/zolem/recording.go" \
  --exclude "**/*_test.go" --exclude "**/testdata/**" \
  --exclude "**/.git/**" --exclude "**/.shatter/**" \
  --exclude "**/.shatter-cache/**" \
  --parallelism 1 --scheduler-policy serial --isolation function \
  --timeout-total 240 --timeout-per-fn 20 --timeout-explore 12 \
  --max-iterations 1 --request-timeout 45 --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 120 --no-cache --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false --format json \
  -o /tmp/zolem-recording-jsonl-ctor-error-repro.json
```

Observed focused/whole-corpus artifacts show this shape:

```json
{
  "function_name": "(*jsonlRecorder).Close",
  "completion_outcome": "error_only",
  "coverage_pct": 12.5,
  "discovered_inputs": [{
    "inputs": [""],
    "thrown_error": "panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference",
    "lines_executed": [0,0,225,226,227,0,0,269]
  }]
}
```

`(*jsonlRecorder).Record` similarly uses inputs `["", {"Listener":"\n"}]`
and panics with a nil pointer after executing constructor lines 225-227.

## Current Code Facts

- Zolem `cmd/zolem/recording.go` defines `newJSONLRecorder(path string)
  (*jsonlRecorder, error)`.
- The constructor calls `os.OpenFile(path, os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY,
  0o644)` and returns `nil, fmt.Errorf(...)` when `path == ""`.
- The scan input prefix `[""]` means Shatter is using the constructor plan with
  a zero string path.
- The generated execution reaches constructor lines 225-227 and then method
  line 269, where `Close` dereferences `r.mu`; this implies the nil receiver
  from the failed constructor was still used for method invocation.
- Relevant Shatter areas to inspect:
  - `shatter-go/planner/compose.go` and `shatter-go/planner/plan.go` for
    constructor-backed receiver plans and constructor `ValuePlan` metadata.
  - `shatter-core/src/planner_consumer.rs` for materializing constructor prefix
    values from `ConstructorArgPlans`.
  - `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go` and `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go` for
    generated wrapper constructor invocation and execute-time receiver
    synthesis/error handling.

## Desired Behavior

For path-like Go constructor string parameters, Shatter should generate a safe
temporary file path seed instead of the empty string zero value. Zolem
`jsonlRecorder` methods should be constructed with a usable temp path so
`Close`, `Record`, `RecordWS`, and `NextCallID` execute meaningful paths on a
non-nil receiver.

As a guardrail, Shatter should also avoid invoking a target method when a
constructor still returns `(nil, error)`; such a case should be surfaced as a
structured constructor/setup failure rather than a nil receiver method panic.
The required primary behavior for this issue is the temp-path seed generation
for path-like constructor strings.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a Shatter regression for a Go method whose receiver constructor has
  signature `func newThing(path string) (*Thing, error)` and returns `nil, err`
  for the zero string.
- The regression must fail on current behavior by showing method invocation on
  a nil receiver or a nil pointer panic after the constructor error.
- Implement path-like constructor string seed generation so the generated seed
  is a usable temp path and the method reaches non-panic behavior.
- Add or preserve a guard that constructor errors do not become nil receiver
  method panics.
- A focused Zolem rerun for `cmd/zolem/recording.go` no longer reports nil
  pointer panics for `(*jsonlRecorder).Close`, `Record`, `RecordWS`, or
  `NextCallID`.
- Run relevant Go tests, `go vet`, `task smoke`, `task e2e`, and the Shatter
  pre-completion gate before landing.

## In Scope

- Constructor-prefix seed materialization for path-like Go string parameters
  when needed to make receiver setup executable.
- Go receiver constructor execution/error handling when constructors return
  `(receiver, error)`.
- Wrapper/protocol error handling so constructor errors do not lead to nil
  receiver method calls.
- Focused Zolem validation for `cmd/zolem/recording.go`.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Zolem feature-code changes.
- Deleting Zolem functions from the corpus.
- Solving unrelated Zolem gaps such as opaque `fixture.Selector`, network
  policy skips, or remote backend availability.

title: Go ctor seed primitives
description:
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,zolem,coverage

## Problem

Shatter's Go planner/wrapper path can emit parameterized-constructor plans whose
constructor arguments are decoded from an input prefix by the generated Go
wrapper. For Zolem, several such planned constructor inputs are materialized as
JSON objects (`{}`) even when the constructor parameter is a primitive Go type
such as `string`, `float64`, or `time.Duration`.

The generated Go wrapper then fails before the target method body runs because
`encoding/json` cannot unmarshal an object into the primitive constructor
argument. Those targets become `error_only` with little or no coverage, reducing
Zolem whole-corpus execution quality.

## Evidence

Current Shatter `main` at merge `0928cc0841337dccba46ace0d71a66f3a30975a0`
was built and run against `~/project/zolem` with a bounded whole-corpus
exploratory scan:

```bash
shatter scan . \
  --project-dir . --language go \
  --include "cmd/**/*.go" --include "internal/**/*.go" \
  --exclude "**/*_test.go" --exclude "**/testdata/**" \
  --exclude "**/.git/**" --exclude "**/.shatter/**" \
  --exclude "**/.shatter-cache/**" \
  --exclude "**/shatter-artifacts/**" --exclude "**/shatter-report/**" \
  --max-depth 20 --parallelism 1 --scheduler-policy serial \
  --isolation function --timeout-total 900 --timeout-per-fn 20 \
  --timeout-explore 12 --max-iterations 1 --request-timeout 45 \
  --exec-timeout 10 --build-timeout 120 --no-cache --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false --format json \
  -o /tmp/zolem-whole-m1-str-8j9k.json
```

The scan exited 0 and reported:

- 172 attempted functions
- 172 completed functions
- 118 `behavioral`
- 50 `error_only`
- 2 `dispatch_failed`
- 2 `skipped_by_policy`
- overall coverage about 52.0%

Representative failures copied from `/tmp/zolem-whole-m1-str-8j9k.json`:

```text
(*inMemoryRecorder).Record:
  inputs: [{}]
  thrown_error: function_error: param _shatterCtorArg0: json: cannot unmarshal object into Go value of type string
  coverage_pct: 0.0

(*CompiledCELMatcher).Score:
  thrown_error: function_error: param _shatterCtorArg1: json: cannot unmarshal object into Go value of type float64
  coverage_pct: 0.0

(*Generator).Generate:
  inputs: [null, {"Provider":"marshal WASM generator input: %w"}]
  thrown_error: function_error: param _shatterCtorArg1: json: cannot unmarshal object into Go value of type time.Duration
  coverage_pct: 0.0
```

The wrapper side expects primitive JSON at the constructor-prefix slot. Existing
regression coverage in `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper_receiver_arity_test.go`
asserts generated code like:

```go
json.Unmarshal(_shatterInputs[0], &_shatterCtorArg0)
NewAdapter(_shatterCtorArg0)
```

The failing shape is therefore in the seed materialization / planner consumer
path that supplies constructor prefix inputs, not in the wrapper's positional
decode.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-go/planner/compose.go::constructorArgPlansForReceiver` emits
  `ConstructorArgPlans` with `Kind: zero` and `TypeHint` derived from the Go
  constructor parameter.
- `shatter-core/src/planner_consumer.rs::materialize_constructor_value` turns
  each constructor `ValuePlan` into the input prefix sent to `Execute`.
- `shatter-core/src/planner_consumer.rs::zero_value_for_type_hint` already has
  primitive mappings for `"string"`, integer spellings, floats, booleans,
  byte slices, and `time.Duration`, but Zolem evidence shows some constructor
  primitive hints still materialize as object/null-shaped inputs.
- `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go::writeConstructorParamDeserialization`
  decodes JSON-backed constructor parameters from `_shatterInputs` before
  invoking `constructor:<FuncName>` receiver cases.

## Desired Behavior

For Go parameterized-constructor plans, Shatter should materialize constructor
prefix seed values that match the Go constructor parameter's expected JSON
shape. Primitive constructor args should receive primitive JSON zero values
(`""`, `0`, `0.0`, `false`, etc.), not `{}` or other aggregate-shaped values.

Targets whose only blocker is a primitive constructor-prefix decode error
should execute the receiver constructor and reach the target method body.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused regression proving a Go method plan with a primitive
  parameterized constructor produces executable constructor-prefix inputs for
  at least `string`, `float64`, and `time.Duration`.
- The regression must fail on the current behavior by producing a decode error
  or the wrong constructor-prefix JSON shape.
- Existing Go wrapper receiver-arity tests still pass.
- Relevant Rust planner-consumer tests pass if `shatter-core` is changed.
- A focused Zolem rerun covering at least one prior failure
  (`(*inMemoryRecorder).Record`, `(*CompiledCELMatcher).Score`, or
  `(*Generator).Generate`) no longer reports the primitive constructor
  unmarshal error and reaches nonzero line coverage or a target-level behavior
  or error after the constructor succeeds.

## In Scope

- Go planner constructor-arg `ValuePlan` metadata, core planner-consumer seed
  materialization, or execute input prefix handling.
- Focused tests in Shatter that reproduce the primitive constructor-prefix
  mismatch.
- Bounded Zolem validation for the representative failure.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Zolem feature-code changes.
- Deleting Zolem functions from the corpus.
- Solving unrelated Zolem coverage gaps such as opaque interface constructor
  dependencies, network-policy skips, or dispatch failures for receiver types
  with no available constructor.

title: Crate bridge drops locked deps
description:
Title: Crate bridge drops locked deps

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,frontend,shatter-audit,pickpackit

## Symptom

Running a bounded Rust handler scan against Pickpackit after the latest Shatter
main fixes still fails most handler targets during crate-bridge execution. The
scan exits successfully overall but only produces behavior maps for 10 of 78
discovered functions:

- Artifact: `/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-m2-after-str-2qwo.json`
- Log: `/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-m2-after-str-2qwo.log`
- Timing: `/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-m2-after-str-2qwo.timing.json`
- Result summary from the JSON `codebase` object:
  - `attempted_functions`: 78
  - `completed_functions`: 10
  - `completed_with_behavior`: 10
  - `failed_functions`: 66
  - `unsupported_functions`: 0
  - `skipped_functions_count`: 2

The repeated failure is a Rust dependency compile error inside the generated
crate-bridge harness:

```text
error[E0282]: type annotations needed
   --> .../aws-runtime-1.7.4/src/auth/sigv4.rs:278:22
    |
278 |                     .send(Box::new(SigV4MessageSigner::new(
    |                      ^^^^ cannot infer type of the type parameter `T`
```

## Smallest Known Reproduction

From Pickpackit worktree
`/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/pp-v2rz.9-people-shatter-input-spread/api`,
with Postgres on `localhost:55430` and MinIO on `localhost:56430`, a filtered
scan of just `health.rs` reproduces the failure:

```bash

  DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55430/pickpackit_test \
  STORAGE_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localhost:56430 \
  STORAGE_BUCKET=pickpackit-images-test \
  STORAGE_REGION=us-east-1 \
  STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID=pickpackit \
  STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=pickpackit-minio \
  STORAGE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:56430 \
  STORAGE_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true \
  PICKPACKIT_S3_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:56430 \
  PICKPACKIT_S3_BUCKET=pickpackit-images-test \
  PICKPACKIT_S3_REGION=us-east-1 \
  PICKPACKIT_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=pickpackit \
  PICKPACKIT_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=pickpackit-minio \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust \
```

```text
Error: scan failed: 1 function(s) attempted but 0 explored successfully
```
