title: Rust Axum CurrentAccount extractor
description:
Title: Rust Axum CurrentAccount extractor

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust-frontend,axum,pickpackit,scanner

## Problem

Pickpackit whole-corpus Shatter validation is blocked by Rust Axum handlers that
take the project-local `CurrentAccount` extractor. Shatter recognizes these
functions as Axum handlers, but then rejects execution because `CurrentAccount`
is classified as an unsupported custom extractor.

This affects a large part of Pickpackit's Rust API surface: `rg CurrentAccount
/home/ketan/project/pickpackit/api/src` shows many handlers across
`handlers/items.rs`, `handlers/packing_items.rs`, `handlers/bundles.rs`,
`handlers/trips.rs`, `handlers/tasks.rs`, `handlers/tags.rs`,
`handlers/destination_supplies.rs`, and others.

## Smallest Reproduction

From Shatter `main` at `addf2340ea9642c0b583f23a3d2ae5450bac83b7`, run:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/pickpackit \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/pickpackit \
  --include api/src/handlers/destination_supplies.rs \
  --all \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --timeout-total 120 \
  --timeout-per-fn 20 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --max-iterations 5 \
  --request-timeout 20 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 45 \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-destination-supplies-scan.json \
  --no-cache \
  --quiet
```

Observed scan summary:

```text
Scan complete: 2 completed, 7 failed, 0 unsupported, 0 interrupted, 0 expected skipped
```

The `CurrentAccount` handler failures are:

```text
/home/ketan/project/pickpackit/api/src/handlers/destination_supplies.rs::create_destination_supply:
  error: exploration error: unsupported: axum handler has unsupported extractor types: CurrentAccount

/home/ketan/project/pickpackit/api/src/handlers/destination_supplies.rs::list_destination_supplies:
  error: exploration error: unsupported: axum handler has unsupported extractor types: CurrentAccount

/home/ketan/project/pickpackit/api/src/handlers/destination_supplies.rs::update_destination_supply:
  error: exploration error: unsupported: axum handler has unsupported extractor types: CurrentAccount
```

The run artifact is:

```text
/home/ketan/project/pickpackit/shatter-artifacts/scan-results/029c379f1576ec1d1f74770583a4a318a233c1283ed47fd4d82929ac42810942/run-status.tsv
```

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-rust/src/adapters.rs::AxumHandlerRecognizer` intentionally recognizes
  custom-extractor-only handlers when the file imports Axum and the function is
  async. The recognizer test
  `axum_recognizer_high_for_custom_extractor_only_handler` covers this.
- `shatter-rust/src/adapters.rs::execute_with_adapter` still rejects mappings
  with `AxumExtractorKind::Unsupported` unless the corresponding input is a
  replayable native input. The error string is:
  `axum handler has unsupported extractor types: ...`.
- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs` already has native replay/generator plumbing
  for custom extractor values in Axum harnesses. Tests around
  `CurrentAccountLikeGen` prove native replay can insert custom extractor values
  into Axum request extensions.
- Pickpackit defines `CurrentAccount` in
  `/home/ketan/project/pickpackit/api/src/auth/current.rs`. It derives
  `Clone`, implements `FromRequestParts`, and has a test constructor:
  `CurrentAccount::test(id: Uuid) -> Self`.
- Pickpackit feature code must not be changed non-trivially for this goal.
  Shatter-side support or Pickpackit `.shatter/` usage/build-infra changes are
  acceptable if they are small and explicitly tied to this issue.

## Desired Behavior

Shatter should execute Pickpackit Axum handlers that take `CurrentAccount`
without reporting `unsupported extractor types: CurrentAccount`.

An acceptable fix can either:

- Teach the Rust scanner/input generator to supply a replayable native
  `CurrentAccount` value through existing generator/native replay plumbing when
  configured for Pickpackit, or
- Add a safe Shatter-side convention for custom Axum extractors with available
  test constructors such as `Type::test(Uuid)`, if that can be done without
  weakening unsupported-extractor diagnostics for arbitrary opaque types.

Do not silently treat every custom extractor as default-constructible.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Shatter regression using a `CurrentAccountLike` Axum extractor
  that implements `FromRequestParts` and has a `test(Uuid)`-style constructor.
  The regression must fail on current main with `unsupported extractor types`
  and pass after the fix.
- Preserve the existing unsupported custom-extractor diagnostic for custom
  extractors that have no configured generator or supported constructor path.
- Re-run the Pickpackit one-file scan above and show the three
  `CurrentAccount` handler failures no longer report
  `unsupported extractor types: CurrentAccount`.
- Run the relevant Rust frontend/core tests and the standard smoke/E2E gates
  required by Shatter pre-completion.

## In Scope

- Rust frontend Axum adapter/input-generation behavior for custom extractors.
- Native replay/generator wiring needed for `CurrentAccount`.
- Small Pickpackit `.shatter/` configuration or generator files, if needed for
  the validation goal and not feature code.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Database setup or DB-backed handler success semantics beyond getting past the
  custom extractor construction blocker.
- The separate scan-path timeouts for private helpers such as `clean_notes`,
  `require_trimmed`, and `resolve_source`.
acceptance_criteria: CurrentAccount Axum handlers no longer fail as unsupported; focused regression and Pickpackit one-file scan pass; pre-completion gates pass
notes: Investigated after Pickpackit generator-pool work. Pickpackit issue pp-bac4 landed on Pickpackit main with merge commit 82de7e6445e3831debe60b14874d6f2fb3b10224 and tracker closure commit 74d22950e9e786c8e57cfa27823d9df3bed1fc7c. Re-ran a focused destination_supplies scan against the pp-bac4 generator config using the Shatter Rust frontend: /var/tmp/pickpackit-pp-bac4-destination-supplies-m5.json reports unsupported_functions=0. The three CurrentAccount handlers no longer report unsupported extractor types; remaining failures are build/execution/task timeouts. No Shatter code change is needed for this issue; the blocker was target-project generator configuration.
close_reason: Resolved externally by Pickpackit pp-bac4 landing 82de7e6445e3831debe60b14874d6f2fb3b10224; focused scan /var/tmp/pickpackit-pp-bac4-destination-supplies-m5.json reports unsupported_functions=0 and no CurrentAccount unsupported failures.

title: Go map receiver init
description:
Title: Go map receiver init
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,zolem,receiver

## Problem

The Zolem validation sample still has a receiver-construction false positive for
a helper method whose receiver only needs initialized maps:

- `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/specs/discovery.go::(discoveryBuilder).schemaFromRef`
  completes as `dispatch_failed`.
- Completion reason:
  `receiver type discoveryBuilder requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available`.

This blocks execution and coverage for one of the sampled Zolem feature-code
methods even though Shatter should be able to synthesize a safe receiver state
for map-only helper structs.

## Evidence

Dry-run scope from current `main` (`addf2340ea9642c0b583f23a3d2ae5450bac83b7`):

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --exclude '**/*_test.go' \
  --dry-run
```

This found 57 non-test Go source files, 204 unexported functions in scan scope,
and 24 skipped functions before execution.

A deterministic 20% core sample then reproduced the gap:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --exclude '**/*_test.go' \
  --core-sample 20% \
  --seed 4242 \
  --max-iterations 5 \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --timeout-per-fn 20 \
  --timeout-total 900 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 20 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 30 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-core20-main-addf2340.json \
  --quiet
```

The sample completed 106 functions, with persisted outcomes:

```text
behavioral: 65
error_only: 26
skipped_by_policy: 14
dispatch_failed: 1
```

The lone `dispatch_failed` function was
`(discoveryBuilder).schemaFromRef`.

A targeted scan of `internal/specs/discovery.go` reproduced the same
function-level failure:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --include internal/specs/discovery.go \
  --all \
  --max-iterations 5 \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --timeout-per-fn 20 \
  --timeout-total 300 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 20 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 30 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-discovery-main-addf2340.json \
  --quiet
```

That run completed 8 functions in the file, but
`(discoveryBuilder).schemaFromRef` remained `dispatch_failed`.

## Current Code Facts

Zolem's `internal/specs/discovery.go` defines:

```go
type discoveryBuilder struct {
    all     map[string]discoverySchema
    defs    map[string]any
    visited map[string]bool
}
```

`(discoveryBuilder).schemaFromRef` reads `b.all`, writes `b.visited[name] =
true`, calls `b.convert`, and writes `b.defs[name] = def`.

The zero value of `discoveryBuilder` has nil maps, so direct zero-value
execution would panic on the map writes. However, the receiver does not contain
channels, functions, interfaces, or pointers. A generated same-package wrapper
should be able to construct an initialized receiver such as:

```go
discoveryBuilder{
    all:     map[string]discoverySchema{},
    defs:    map[string]any{},
    visited: map[string]bool{},
}
```

That receiver is safe for the method's error path and avoids the misleading
`requires_construction` dispatch failure.

## Desired Behavior

For method receivers whose dangerous unexported reference fields are map fields
only, Shatter should provide a safe initialized-map receiver strategy instead
of reporting `requires_construction`.

The fix must not weaken the guard for receiver structs that contain channels,
functions, interfaces, pointers, or other state that cannot be safely
initialized generically.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a failing Go regression for a method on a receiver with only unexported
  map fields where the method writes to those maps. The method must execute
  without `requires_construction`.
- Preserve existing true positives for receiver types containing channels,
  unguarded pointers, interfaces, or other non-map construction requirements.
- Run focused Go receiver/execute tests, then `go test ./...` and
  `go vet ./...` in `shatter-go`.
- Run bounded Zolem validation for `internal/specs/discovery.go` and confirm
  `(discoveryBuilder).schemaFromRef` no longer completes as
  `dispatch_failed`.

## In Scope

- Go receiver planning/synthesis for map-only receiver helper structs.
- Tests in `shatter-go/protocol` and related testdata.
- Use Zolem only as a validation corpus.

## Out of Scope

- Do not edit non-trivial Zolem feature code.
- Do not globally remove the `requires_construction` guard.
- Do not synthesize arbitrary initialized receiver states for channels,
  pointers, interfaces, functions, or semantically rich constructors.
acceptance_criteria: Map-only receiver helper structs get an initialized-map receiver strategy; non-map receiver construction guards remain intact; Go gates and bounded Zolem discovery validation pass.

title: Go receiver nil-slice range
description:
Title: Go receiver nil-slice range
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,zolem,receiver

## Problem

After `str-pckp` made Go receiver construction method-sensitive for safe
nil-state methods, the targeted Zolem validation still reports one remaining
receiver-construction false positive in `internal/fixture/selector.go`:

- `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/fixture/selector.go::(*fixturesYAMLSelector).Select`
  completes as `dispatch_failed` with `receiver type fixturesYAMLSelector
  requires constructor initialization`.

The validation command that exposed this was:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --include internal/fixture/fixture.go \
  --include internal/fixture/selector.go \
  --include internal/ollama/client.go \
  --all \
  --max-iterations 5 \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --timeout-per-fn 20 \
  --timeout-total 420 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 20 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 30 \
  --no-cache \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-str-pckp-preview.json \
  --quiet
```

That scan completed 21 functions with 0 failed/unsupported/interrupted, but
the JSON outcome counts still included one `dispatch_failed` function: the
selector method above.

## Current Code Facts

- `fixturesYAMLSelector` has:
  - `entries []fixturesYAMLEntry`
  - `counters *SequenceCounters`
  - `namespace string`
- `(*fixturesYAMLSelector).Select` starts by building a local `byID` map and
  then ranges `for _, e := range s.entries`.
- On a zero-value receiver, `s.entries` is nil, so the range body is skipped
  and the method returns `(nil, nil)`.
- The range body does contain unsafe receiver state use:
  `s.counters.Step(...)` when an entry has a sequence. That access is unsafe
  for a partially initialized receiver, but unreachable for the actual
  zero-value receiver Shatter would synthesize.
- `shatter-go/protocol/receiver_construction.go` currently blocks the method
  because it sees the unsafe pointer-field method call in the range body
  without recognizing that the enclosing range over a nil receiver slice field
  is zero-value-unreachable.

## Desired Behavior

The Go receiver-construction heuristic should recognize zero-value-unreachable
unsafe code inside a range over a receiver-owned slice field whose zero value is
nil. For Shatter's synthesized zero-value receiver, that range body cannot run,
so unsafe accesses inside the body should not force `requires_construction`.

This should unblock `(*fixturesYAMLSelector).Select` for zero-value execution
without weakening protection for unsafe accesses that can run on a zero-value
receiver.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a failing Go regression where a method ranges over a receiver slice field
  and the range body contains a nil-unsafe receiver pointer access; the method
  must not require construction because the zero-value slice skips the body.
- Preserve existing true-positive regressions for map writes, channel use, and
  unguarded pointer/interface access that can run on a zero-value receiver.
- Run focused Go tests, then `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` in
  `shatter-go`.
- Run bounded Zolem validation for `internal/fixture/selector.go` and confirm
  `(*fixturesYAMLSelector).Select` no longer completes as `dispatch_failed`
  for `requires_construction`.

## In Scope

- Refine Shatter's Go receiver-construction static analysis and tests.
- Use Zolem only as a validation corpus.

## Out of Scope

- Do not edit non-trivial Zolem feature code.
- Do not remove the `requires_construction` guard globally.
- Do not treat arbitrary initialized receiver states as safe; this issue is
  specifically about Shatter's synthesized zero-value receiver path.
acceptance_criteria: Receiver construction allows nil-slice receiver range bodies that are unreachable for synthesized zero-value receivers; existing unsafe receiver true positives remain blocked; Go gates and bounded Zolem selector validation pass.

title: Receiver init method sensitivity
description:
Title: Receiver init method sensitivity
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,zolem,receiver

## Problem

Zolem scans still report several safe receiver methods as `dispatch_failed`
because Shatter's Go receiver construction guard is type-wide instead of
method-sensitive. The guard currently rejects a method receiver when the
receiver type has any unexported reference-typed field, even when the method
does not read/call/dereference that field and a zero-value receiver would
exercise meaningful behavior.

Observed in the post-`str-pd80` Zolem scan:

- `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/fixture/fixture.go::(*Fixture).SetResponseTemplate`
  failed with `receiver type Fixture requires constructor initialization`.
- `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/fixture/selector.go::(fixturesYAMLEntry).label`
  failed with `receiver type fixturesYAMLEntry requires constructor initialization`.
- `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/ollama/client.go::(*Client).SelectedModel`
  failed with `receiver type Client requires constructor initialization`.
- `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/specs/discovery.go::(discoveryBuilder).schemaFromRef`
  and `.convert` failed with the same receiver-construction reason.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-go/protocol/receiver_construction.go` implements
  `ReceiverRequiresConstruction(pkg, target)` by scanning the receiver type's
  fields. It returns true if any unexported field is a map, channel, function,
  interface, or pointer.
- `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go` uses that boolean in both
  `buildTargetContext` and `synthesizeExecuteReceiverKind`; when it is true
  and no constructor is usable, direct execution returns
  `requires_construction` instead of the wrapper's `zero_value` receiver kind.
- Zolem `Fixture` has an unexported `templateBody *template.Template`, but
  `(*Fixture).SetResponseTemplate` assigns that field after parsing the input
  body; it does not require the field to be initialized before the call.
- Zolem `Client` has an unexported `run commandRunner`, but
  `(*Client).SelectedModel` only returns the primitive `model` string.
- Zolem `fixturesYAMLEntry.label` only checks whether `sequence` is nil and
  returns either `"sequence:" + e.sequence.id` or `fixtureID`; its zero value
  is safe and meaningful.
- `shatter-go/protocol/testdata/requires_construction.go` currently uses
  `LocalControlPlane.ListProfiles` as the true-positive regression, but that
  method only ranges a nil map and is actually safe under a method-sensitive
  rule. The fixture should be updated with an actually unsafe method, such as
  a method that writes to the nil `counters` map or sends on/receives from the
  nil `listeners` channel, and that method should remain rejected.

## Desired Behavior

Make the Go receiver-construction guard method-sensitive enough that a method
is rejected only when that method body actually depends on uninitialized
unexported reference state in a dangerous way. Safe zero-value receiver methods
should get a `zero_value` receiver plan/kind and proceed to execution.

This should preserve the original protection for true nil-state methods, such
as a `LocalControlPlane` method that writes through a nil map or uses a nil
channel, while unblocking safe Zolem methods like `Fixture.SetResponseTemplate`,
`fixturesYAMLEntry.label`, and `Client.SelectedModel`.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add failing Go tests before the fix for method-sensitive receiver analysis:
  one safe method on a type with an unexported reference field must not require
  construction, and one unsafe method in the construction testdata must still
  require construction. If needed, add the unsafe testdata method first so the
  true-positive assertion reflects a real dangerous zero-value access.
- Update the receiver-construction logic and every caller needed so planner and
  direct-execute synthesis agree on the same decision.
- Run focused Go tests for the new regression(s), then `go test ./...` and
  `go vet ./...` in `shatter-go`.
- Run protocol/conformance checks required for Go protocol behavior changes.
- Run bounded Zolem validation for at least `internal/fixture/fixture.go`,
  `internal/fixture/selector.go`, and `internal/ollama/client.go`, confirming
  the listed methods no longer complete as `dispatch_failed` for
  `requires_construction`.

## In Scope

- Refine Shatter's Go receiver construction heuristic and tests.
- Use only Shatter feature-branch/worktree changes.
- Treat Zolem as a validation corpus.

## Out of Scope

- Do not edit non-trivial Zolem feature code.
- Do not unblock `httpLocalServer` by calling constructors that open network
  listeners or start goroutines.
- Do not remove the `requires_construction` guard entirely; false positives
  should be fixed without regressing the true-positive protection.
acceptance_criteria: Method-sensitive receiver construction tests pass; safe Zolem receiver methods no longer dispatch_fail with requires_construction; true unsafe nil-state receiver methods remain blocked; Go/protocol gates pass.

title: Go ctor zero-value params
description:
After landing `str-pd80`, a serial whole-corpus Zolem scan still leaves method
targets unexecuted because receiver construction refuses same-package
constructors whose parameters are local non-primitive types.

Scan command:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --max-iterations 5 \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --timeout-per-fn 20 \
  --timeout-total 1200 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 20 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 30 \
  --no-cache \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-main-post-pd80-20260608.json \
  --quiet
```

Observed JSON outcome summary:

```text
behavioral: 223
error_only: 80
dispatch_failed: 25
skipped_by_policy: 30
```

Largest dispatch-failed bucket:

```text
9 dispatch_failed: receiver type localControlPlane requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
4 dispatch_failed: receiver type LegacySelector requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
2 dispatch_failed: receiver type Client requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
2 dispatch_failed: receiver type detector requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
2 dispatch_failed: receiver type discoveryBuilder requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
2 dispatch_failed: receiver type httpLocalServer requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
```

Example affected targets:

```text
/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/local_admin.go::(*localControlPlane).ListProfiles
/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/local_admin.go::(*localControlPlane).DeleteProfile
/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/local_admin.go::(*localControlPlane).ListListeners
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/fixture/selector.go::(*LegacySelector).Select
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/fixture/selector.go::(*LegacySelector).HasMatcher
```

## Current Code Facts

- `cmd/zolem/local_admin.go` defines `newLocalControlPlane(opts localAdminOptions, deps startupDeps) *localControlPlane`.
- `newLocalControlPlane` initializes the receiver fields that make the zero value unsafe: `store`, `startServer`, `counters`, and `listeners`.
- `localAdminOptions` and `startupDeps` are same-package struct parameters whose zero values are acceptable to this constructor; `startupDeps.withDefaults()` fills default functions.
- `internal/fixture/selector.go` defines `NewLegacySelector(runner *Runner) *LegacySelector`.
- `NewLegacySelector(nil)` produces a usable selector for non-WASM paths because it initializes the `cel` map and the scoring path already guards `s.runner != nil`.
- Shatter planner code already has `constructorArgPlansForReceiver` support for aggregate constructor params in `shatter-go/planner/compose.go`.
- Shatter wrapper code can deserialize constructor input slots and can also emit runtime-value constructor arguments via `ConstructorParam.RuntimeValueExpr`.
- Current admissibility checks reject constructor params that are not primitive, aggregate-synthesizable, registered runtime values, or discovered interface implementations:
  - `shatter-go/planner/constructor.go:isParamSatisfiable`
  - `shatter-go/planner/receiver.go:allParamsSatisfiable`
  - `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go:constructorParamDirectExecuteSatisfiable`

## Desired Behavior

For constructor-only parameters that are not part of the target function's
behavior input surface, Shatter should be able to pass an assignable Go zero
value when that lets a same-package constructor initialize an otherwise unsafe
receiver. Prepared plan generation and direct execute receiver synthesis must
agree on the same constructor admissibility rule.

This should let `localControlPlane` methods use `constructor:newLocalControlPlane`
instead of dispatch failing, without requiring any non-trivial changes to
Zolem feature code.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Go planner/protocol regression showing a receiver constructor
  with same-package struct parameters is selected and its constructor
  arguments do not consume target JSON input slots.
- Add or update a direct-execute regression showing the same constructor is
  synthesized instead of reporting `RequiresConstruction`.
- Verify the generated wrapper compiles for a constructor with same-package
  struct and pointer parameters using zero-value runtime expressions.
- Run `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` in `shatter-go`.
- Run `task protocol-codegen-check`, `task conformance`, `task smoke`, and
  `task e2e`.
- Run a bounded Zolem scan for at least `cmd/zolem/local_admin.go` and confirm
  `(*localControlPlane).ListProfiles` no longer reports `dispatch_failed`.

## Scope

In scope:

- Go receiver constructor admissibility for constructor-only zero-value
  parameters.
- Planner/direct-execute/wrapper alignment for that constructor parameter
  treatment.
- Focused Zolem validation for the affected receiver construction bucket.

Out of scope:

- Network/subprocess policy skips such as `http.Get`, `net.Listen`, or
  `exec.CommandContext`.
- Changing Zolem feature code.
- Broadly relaxing the `ReceiverRequiresConstruction` zero-receiver guard.
acceptance_criteria: Planner/direct-execute/wrapper regressions cover same-package zero-value constructor params; Go gates and Shatter protocol/e2e gates pass; bounded Zolem local_admin scan no longer dispatch-fails (*localControlPlane).ListProfiles

title: Scan explore timeout ignored
description:
Title: Scan explore timeout ignored

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: pickpackit,rust,scan,timeout,coverage

## Symptom

A bounded Pickpackit Rust scan was invoked with a shorter exploration timeout
than the per-function timeout, but slow handler execution still consumed the
full per-function timeout. This wastes the whole-corpus scan budget and blocks
the larger Pickpackit goal because a few slow handlers prevent most exported
handlers from being attempted.

The broad Pickpackit scan used:

```bash
# cwd: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation
shatter scan api/src/handlers --project-dir api --require-rust \
  --parallelism 1 --parallelism-min 1 --parallelism-max 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 --scheduler-policy serial --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 300 --timeout-per-fn 60 --timeout-explore 20 \
  --request-timeout 60 --exec-timeout 30 --build-timeout 90 \
  --progress --color never \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-str-7sdw-broad.json \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-str-7sdw-broad.md
```

Observed result:

```text
Scan complete: 6 completed, 3 failed, 0 unsupported, 64 interrupted, 2 expected skipped
```

The failed functions ignored the requested `--timeout-explore 20` and used a
60s execution limit instead:

```text
assistant.rs::apply_assistant_action: timed out during execution after 60s
assistant.rs::assistant_message: timed out during task after 155s
bundles.rs::apply_bundle: timed out during execution after 60s
```

`assistant_message` hit the shared-pool task watchdog at `90 + 60 + 5 = 155s`,
which further shows that the scan task was still budgeted around
`timeout_per_fn` rather than the explicit exploration timeout.

A shorter assistant-only reproduction on Shatter `main` also shows execution
timeouts being reported from the per-function timeout rather than
`--timeout-explore`:

```bash
# cwd: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation
# Adapt the Shatter binary/runtime paths to the active Shatter worktree.
env SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust-runtime \
  SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/var/tmp/shatter-pickpackit-current-assistant/harness-cache \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter \
  scan api/src/handlers --project-dir api --require-rust --include assistant.rs \
  --parallelism 1 --parallelism-min 1 --parallelism-max 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 --scheduler-policy serial --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 90 --timeout-per-fn 10 --timeout-explore 5 \
  --request-timeout 10 --exec-timeout 5 --build-timeout 20 \
  --progress --color never \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-assistant-current-short.json \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-assistant-current-short.md
```

Observed failures:

```text
apply_assistant_action: timed out during execution after 10s
assistant_message: timed out during execution after 10s
```

The expected execution limit for that command is 5s, not 10s.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs::scan_explore_timeout` already resolves
  the intended exploration budget as `config.timeout_explore.or(Some(config.timeout_per_fn))`.
- The CLI scan path builds `ExploreConfig` with `timeout_explore:
  scan_explore_timeout(config)`.
- In the shared-pool scan task loop in `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs`,
  the local `timeout` variable is currently set to `config.timeout_per_fn`.
- That local `timeout` is passed into `run_phased` as the `explore_timeout`
  argument.
- `run_phased` enforces its `explore_timeout` argument with
  `tokio::time::timeout(explore_timeout, explore_single_function(...))` and
  reports `PhasedOutcome::ExploreTimedOut(explore_timeout)`.
- The shared-pool task watchdog is computed by
  `shared_pool_task_watchdog(config.build_timeout, config.timeout_per_fn)`, so
  task-level backstops also ignore an explicit lower `--timeout-explore`.
- Existing tests cover the defaulting behavior of `scan_explore_timeout`, but
  they do not prove the shared-pool phased scan path passes that resolved value
  into `run_phased` or into the task watchdog.

## Desired Behavior

When `scan` is run with `--timeout-explore N`, the shared-pool phased scan path
should enforce that value for execution/exploration timeouts. Slow individual
handlers should not consume the larger `--timeout-per-fn` budget when a smaller
exploration budget was explicitly configured.

The task watchdog should remain a final cleanup backstop, but it should be sized
from the build timeout plus the effective exploration timeout, not always from
`timeout_per_fn`.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add focused Shatter regression coverage showing the shared-pool scan path
  reports `timed out during execution after 5s` when configured with
  `timeout_per_fn=10s` and `timeout_explore=5s`.
- Add or update a unit test proving the shared-pool task watchdog uses the
  effective exploration timeout when it is lower than `timeout_per_fn`.
- Re-run the focused Pickpackit assistant-only scan above and show its failures
  report `timed out during execution after 5s`, not 10s.
- Re-run a bounded broader Pickpackit handlers scan with serial settings and
  `--timeout-explore 20`; show execution timeout failures use 20s and that more
  functions are attempted/completed before the 300s total budget expires, or
  record the next narrower blocker as a Beads issue containing the scan command,
  final counts, failed functions, and the relevant structured per-function
  artifact fields.
- Preserve the two intentional Pickpackit config skips:
  `fetch_legs_for_workspace` and `fetch_tasks_for_workspace`.
- Run relevant Rust gates plus `task smoke` and `task e2e`.

## In Scope

- Shared-pool scan timeout plumbing in `shatter-core`.
- Focused tests proving `timeout_explore` is honored in phased scan execution
  and task watchdog sizing.
- Bounded Pickpackit validation runs.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Deleting Pickpackit handlers or weakening scan coverage goals.
- Solving all Pickpackit branch coverage in this single issue.
- Changing build-timeout semantics for the prepare phase.
acceptance_criteria: Shared-pool scan honors timeout_explore for execution timeout and task watchdog sizing; focused regression passes; focused Pickpackit assistant scan reports 5s execution timeouts with timeout_explore=5; bounded broader Pickpackit scan shows execution timeout failures use 20s or files a narrower blocker; configured skips remain preserved; Rust gates plus task smoke and task e2e pass

title: Go ctor interface params
description:
Title: Go ctor interface params

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,zolem,dispatch,coverage

## Symptom

A low-load whole-corpus Go scan of `~/project/zolem` on Shatter `main` at
`e6e9966722707902dac662016c35b22e5520dcec` completed without hard failures, but
still left 41 function entries with `completion_outcome: dispatch_failed` and
24 skipped functions. The largest dispatch-failed bucket is provider `Handler`
methods in Zolem's OpenAI, Gemini, and Anthropic packages.

Representative failed entries:

```text
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/provider/openai/handler.go::(*Handler).ServeHTTP
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/provider/openai/handler.go::(*Handler).handleChatCompletions
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/provider/anthropic/handler.go::(*Handler).handleMessages
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/provider/gemini/handler.go::(*Handler).handleGenerate
```

Each reports:
