
This prevents Shatter from entering substantial provider feature logic. For
example `openai/handler.go::(*Handler).handleChatCompletions` has 127 lines and
16 detected branches, but the scan covered 0 lines and 0 branches because
receiver dispatch never succeeded.

## Reproduction Evidence

Run from Shatter `main` worktree:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --max-iterations 5 \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --timeout-per-fn 20 \
  --timeout-total 1200 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 20 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 30 \
  --no-cache \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-main-e6e99667-m5-20260608.json \
  --quiet
```

Observed scan summary:

```text
382 discovered
358 attempted
358 completed
0 failed
24 skipped / unsupported
41 function entries with completion_outcome == dispatch_failed
overall_coverage = 38.52376137512639
```

A lower-cost provider-focused validation command after the fix can use the same
serial settings with explicit provider includes:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --include internal/provider/openai/handler.go \
  --include internal/provider/anthropic/handler.go \
  --include internal/provider/gemini/handler.go \
  --all \
  --max-iterations 5 \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --timeout-per-fn 20 \
  --timeout-total 600 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 20 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 30 \
  --no-cache \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-provider-handlers-ctor-interface.json \
  --quiet
```

Dispatch failures grouped by receiver type:

```text
16 Handler
 8 localControlPlane
 4 LegacySelector
 2 Client
 2 detector
 2 discoveryBuilder
 2 httpLocalServer
 1 Fixture
 1 fixturesYAMLEntry
 1 fixturesYAMLSelector
 1 wasmSelector
```

Skipped functions grouped by opaque/no-constructor parameter type:

```text
9 fixture.Selector
5 main.startupDeps
4 main.Recorder
3 http.Handler
2 jsonschema.ErrorKind
1 main.specFetcher
```

## Current Code Facts

- Zolem provider handlers define same-package constructors:

  ```go
  func NewHandler(
      validator *specs.Validator,
      matcher *fixture.Matcher,
      generator response.Generator,
      ollamaClient backend.TextGenerator,
      ollamaHTTP backend.ChatGenerator,
      wasmGenerator ...*wasmgen.Generator,
  ) *Handler
  ```

  in:

  ```text
  internal/provider/openai/handler.go
  internal/provider/anthropic/handler.go
  internal/provider/gemini/handler.go
  ```

- Zolem already exposes deterministic constructor helpers for several of those
  interface parameters:

  ```go
  response.NewFakerGenerator() response.Generator
  backend.NewNoopTextGenerator() backend.TextGenerator
  backend.NewNoopChatGenerator() backend.ChatGenerator
  fixture.NewEmptyMatcher() *fixture.Matcher
  ```

- Shatter already has ordinary function-parameter interface implementation
  planning:

  - `shatter-go/protocol/interface_discovery.go::discoverInterfaceImplCandidates`
    discovers parameterless constructors for imported interface parameters.
  - `shatter-go/planner/param.go::PlanParam` consumes
    `InterfaceImplsByParam`.
  - `shatter-go/planner/param_test.go::TestPlanParam_InterfaceImplCandidates_ProducesRuntimeValuePlan`
    covers an ordinary `response.Generator` parameter producing
    `response.NewFakerGenerator()`.

- Receiver constructor satisfiability does not currently receive equivalent
  interface implementation context. `shatter-go/planner/receiver.go` calls
  `allParamsSatisfiable`, which delegates to `isParamSatisfiable`; that path
  checks primitive families, aggregate synthesis, and runtime-value registry
  plans, but it has no interface-implementation candidate input for constructor
  parameters.

- The likely Shatter-side data-flow change is to discover interface
  implementation candidates for constructor parameters as well as ordinary
  function parameters, then thread that constructor-parameter context into
  receiver planning and `constructorArgPlansForReceiver`. This should reuse the
  existing `PlanInterfaceImpls` ranking and runtime-value expression shape
  rather than invent a Zolem-specific registry.

- The direct-execute receiver synthesis path also has a separate constructor
  parameter satisfiability check in `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go` and must
  stay consistent with planner behavior. A focused direct-execute regression
  should assert that receiver synthesis returns `constructor:NewHandler` (with
  no `RequiresConstruction` unsatisfied requirement) for the same constructor
  shape.

## Desired Behavior

When a method receiver has a same-package constructor whose parameters include
imported interfaces with discovered parameterless implementor constructors,
Shatter should treat those constructor parameters as satisfiable and emit
constructor argument plans using the chosen implementor constructor expression.

For the Zolem provider `Handler` constructors, Shatter should be able to select
`constructor:NewHandler` and supply deterministic values for `response.Generator`,
`backend.TextGenerator`, and `backend.ChatGenerator` using existing no-op/faker
constructors, while preserving existing aggregate and runtime-value constructor
parameter behavior.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused planner regression where a method receiver constructor has one
  or more imported-interface constructor parameters with discovered implementor
  constructors, and `PlanRequirements` emits a `constructor:<name>` receiver
  plan instead of `NoConstructor`.
- Add wrapper or composed-plan coverage proving constructor argument plans for
  interface parameters are emitted as runtime-value expressions and do not
  consume ordinary method argument slots incorrectly.
- Add or update direct-execute receiver synthesis coverage so the same
  constructor shape is selected instead of returning `RequiresConstruction`.
- Run `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` in `shatter-go`.
- Re-run a bounded Zolem provider slice scan and show representative OpenAI,
  Anthropic, and Gemini `Handler` methods no longer report `dispatch_failed`
  for missing receiver construction.

## In Scope

- Go planner/direct-execute receiver constructor parameter satisfiability for
  imported interface parameters with discovered implementor constructors.
- Constructor argument plan emission for those interface parameters.
- Focused Shatter tests and bounded Zolem provider validation.

## Out of Scope

- Broad Zolem feature-code rewrites.
- Deleting or weakening Zolem provider logic.
- Solving all remaining skipped Zolem functions in this issue.
- Raising whole-project Zolem coverage to 80% in this single issue.
acceptance_criteria: Planner/direct-execute receiver constructor parameter satisfiability handles imported interface params with discovered implementor constructors; constructor arg plans emit runtime-value expressions without shifting method args; go test ./... and go vet ./... pass; bounded Zolem provider scan shows representative Handler methods no longer dispatch-fail for missing receiver construction

title: Pickpackit Rust scan timeouts
description:
Title: Pickpackit Rust scan timeouts

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: pickpackit,rust,scan,coverage

## Symptom

After `str-u52n` fixed project-local custom Rust frontend discovery, a bounded Pickpackit handler scan from the Pickpackit repository root no longer emits native-generator custom-build warnings, but it still consumes the total scan budget after only a few real handler attempts. The scan cannot reach enough of the corpus to measure or improve the project goal of 90% successful execution and 80% line/branch coverage.

The current run completed only 2 of 75 exported handler functions before the total budget expired:

```text
Scan complete: 2 completed, 4 failed, 0 unsupported, 67 interrupted, 2 expected skipped
```

The failures are slow execution/task/build timeouts, not unsupported target shapes:

```text
assistant.rs::apply_assistant_action: timed out during execution after 60s
assistant.rs::assistant_message: timed out during task after 155s
bundles.rs::create_bundle: timed out during execution after 60s
health.rs::health: timed out during build after 180s
```

This blocks `str-bphx` and the larger Pickpackit objective because most functions are marked interrupted by total scan budget rather than explored, and even a trivial `health` handler can become a build-timeout casualty in the broader scan.

## Reproduction Evidence

Shatter main at:

```text
9a5ef67404e74abd7b5ad204306d63b0833ee2c5
```

Pickpackit validation worktree:

```text
/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation
```

Focused repo-root health scan with the same `--project-dir api` shape completed without custom frontend warnings:

```bash
env SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust-runtime \
  SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/var/tmp/shatter-pickpackit-str-u52n-main/harness-cache \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter \
  scan api/src/handlers --project-dir api --require-rust --include health.rs \
  --parallelism 1 --parallelism-min 1 --parallelism-max 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 --scheduler-policy serial --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 180 --timeout-per-fn 90 --timeout-explore 30 \
  --request-timeout 90 --exec-timeout 45 --build-timeout 90 \
  --progress --color never \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-health-str-u52n-main.json \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-health-str-u52n-main.md
```

Focused result:

```text
Scan complete: 1 completed, 0 failed, 0 unsupported, 0 interrupted, 0 expected skipped
```

Bounded broader scan from the Pickpackit repo root:

```bash
env SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust-runtime \
  SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/var/tmp/shatter-pickpackit-main-broad/harness-cache \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter \
  scan api/src/handlers --project-dir api --require-rust \
  --parallelism 1 --parallelism-min 1 --parallelism-max 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 --scheduler-policy serial --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 300 --timeout-per-fn 60 --timeout-explore 20 \
  --request-timeout 60 --exec-timeout 30 --build-timeout 90 \
  --progress --color never \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-main-broad.json \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-main-broad.md
```

Reports:

```text
/var/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-main-broad.json
/var/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-main-broad.md
```

Per-function failure artifacts under Pickpackit:

```text
api/shatter-artifacts/scan-results/729280c7b7d85ef1e403fb7045e18c9dc10a6395348c433937cd7199cc64073f/functions/
```

These artifacts preserve only `status`, `reason`, `current`, and `total` for failures. Example `jq '{function_name,status,reason,current,total}'` outputs:

```json
{"status":"failed","reason":"timed out during execution after 60s","current":1,"total":75}
{"status":"failed","reason":"timed out during task after 155s","current":2,"total":75}
{"status":"failed","reason":"timed out during execution after 60s","current":4,"total":75}
{"status":"failed","reason":"timed out during build after 180s","current":18,"total":75}
```

## Current Code Facts

- `str-u52n` already landed custom frontend lookup through the effective project directory, so this issue should not revisit custom binary discovery.
- The broader run used serial scan settings: `--parallelism 1`, `--workers-per-fn 1`, and `--scheduler-policy serial`, to avoid overstressing the system.
- The focused `health.rs` scan succeeds under a 180s total budget, but the broader scan records `health.rs::health` as `timed out during build after 180s`, suggesting broader Rust scan build/setup reuse or timeout accounting is wasting budget.
- Failed scan artifacts currently omit detailed build/execute diagnostics beyond a short reason string, making the next blocker harder to diagnose from the JSON behavior outputs alone.

## Desired Behavior

Bounded whole-corpus Pickpackit Rust scans should make steady progress through exported handlers instead of spending most of the total budget on repeated build/setup or opaque timeout states. At minimum, Shatter should preserve enough structured timeout/build diagnostics in failed scan artifacts to identify whether time is going to frontend build, harness compile, task scheduling, handler execution, or timeout accounting.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add focused Shatter regression coverage for the diagnosed timeout/build-budget issue or for preserving structured timeout diagnostics in failed Rust scan artifacts, depending on the root cause found during implementation.
- Re-run the focused Pickpackit `health.rs` repo-root scan and show it still completes with 0 failed and no custom-frontend warnings.
- Re-run a bounded broader Pickpackit handlers scan from the repo root with serial settings and show one of:
  - at least 10 exported handler functions complete before the 300s total budget expires, with no `health.rs::health` build-timeout failure, or
  - the scan artifacts contain structured enough timeout/build diagnostics to file the next narrower executable issue without relying on terminal-only output.
- Preserve the two intentional config skips for `fetch_legs_for_workspace` and `fetch_tasks_for_workspace`.
- Run the relevant Rust quality gates for any touched crates plus `task smoke` and `task e2e`.

## In Scope

- Shatter Rust scan scheduling, timeout accounting, harness build reuse, failed-artifact diagnostics, or narrowly related CLI/report plumbing needed to make the Pickpackit blocker diagnosable or measurably better.
- Focused tests and bounded Pickpackit validation runs.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Reworking Pickpackit handler logic or deleting feature code.
- Reopening custom frontend discovery fixed by `str-u52n`.
- Raising Pickpackit corpus coverage to 80% in this single issue.
acceptance_criteria: Focused regression for diagnosed timeout/build-budget issue or structured timeout diagnostics; focused Pickpackit health scan still completes without custom frontend warnings; bounded broader handlers scan either completes at least 10 handlers before 300s without health build-timeout or emits structured diagnostics sufficient for next issue; two configured skips remain justified; relevant Rust gates plus task smoke and task e2e pass.

title: Go aggregate ctor params
description:
Title: Go aggregate ctor params

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,zolem,dispatch,coverage

## Symptom

A bounded whole-corpus Go scan of `~/project/zolem` from Shatter `main` still leaves methods unsupported through `dispatch_failed` when their receiver has a same-package constructor whose parameters are Shatter-synthesizable but not primitive or runtime-value types.

The smallest current example is Zolem's `recordingResponseWriter` receiver:

```text
/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/recording.go::(*recordingResponseWriter).Flush
/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/recording.go::(*recordingResponseWriter).Write
/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/recording.go::(*recordingResponseWriter).WriteHeader
/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/recording.go::(*recordingResponseWriter).captureBody
```

Each currently reports:

```text
receiver type recordingResponseWriter requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
```

## Reproduction Evidence

Run from the Shatter main landing worktree at commit `c3b76bac31a9efd9623c3a8fe1fdf09cf0c07b1e`:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --max-iterations 5 \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --timeout-per-fn 20 \
  --timeout-total 900 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 20 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 30 \
  --no-cache \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-main-bounded-post-nb3e-20260608.json \
  --quiet
```

Observed scan summary:

```text
357 completed
1 failed
24 unsupported
0 interrupted
0 expected skipped
completion_outcome.dispatch_failed = 46
completion_outcome.behavioral = 210
overall_coverage = 38.01820020222447
```

The dispatch-failed bucket includes 4 `recordingResponseWriter` methods with the constructor-initialization reason above.

## Current Code Facts

- `cmd/zolem/recording.go` defines `type RecordCaps struct { RequestBodyCapBytes int; ResponseBodyCapBytes int; StreamEventCap int }`.
- `cmd/zolem/recording.go` defines `func newRecordingResponseWriter(w http.ResponseWriter, caps RecordCaps) *recordingResponseWriter`.
- Shatter already supports `http.ResponseWriter` as a Go runtime-value constructor parameter through the runtime-value registry.
- `shatter-go/protocol/constructor.go::classifyConstructor` accepts constructors with composite-literal returns even when the function name is lowercase, so `newRecordingResponseWriter` should be discoverable.
- `shatter-go/planner/aggregate.go::PlanAggregate` can synthesize struct aggregate parameter plans such as a `RecordCaps` composite literal or JSON-backed aggregate plan for ordinary function parameters.
- `shatter-go/planner/constructor.go::isParamSatisfiable`, `shatter-go/planner/receiver.go::allParamsSatisfiable`, `shatter-go/planner/compose.go::constructorArgPlansForReceiver`, and `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go::constructorParamDirectExecuteSatisfiable` currently treat constructor params as satisfiable only through primitive families and runtime-value registry entries.
- The wrapper already has parameterized constructor argument deserialization and runtime-value constructor parameter binding; registry-backed constructor args do not consume JSON input slots.

## Desired Behavior

The Go receiver-constructor planner and direct-execute receiver selection should treat aggregate constructor parameters as satisfiable when the existing aggregate planner can synthesize a value. A constructor like:

```go
func newRecordingResponseWriter(w http.ResponseWriter, caps RecordCaps) *recordingResponseWriter
```

should be eligible because `w` is a runtime value and `caps` is a synthesizeable same-package struct aggregate.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused failing regression where a method receiver has a parameterized constructor with one runtime-value arg and one struct aggregate arg; the planner emits a `constructor:<name>` receiver plan and the constructor arg plans include the aggregate JSON-backed/runtime-value expression without consuming the runtime-value slot.
- Add or update direct-execute coverage so the same constructor shape is selected instead of returning `RequiresConstruction`.
- Run `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` in `shatter-go`.
- Run a bounded Zolem slice scan for `cmd/zolem/recording.go` and show the four `recordingResponseWriter` methods no longer report `dispatch_failed` for missing constructor initialization.

## In Scope

- Go planner/direct-execute constructor parameter satisfiability for aggregate params already supported by `PlanAggregate`.
- Focused tests in `shatter-go` covering planner and direct-execute behavior.
- Minimal wrapper adjustments only if emitted aggregate constructor plans expose a compile/runtime mismatch.

## Out of Scope

- Broad Zolem feature-code changes.
- Provider `Handler` receiver construction and other domain-interface constructors.
- The remaining single hard timeout on `(*httpLocalServer).Close`.
- Raising whole-project Zolem coverage to 80% in this single issue.
acceptance_criteria: Planner/direct-execute treat aggregate constructor params as satisfiable when PlanAggregate can synthesize them; focused shatter-go tests pass; go test ./... and go vet ./... pass; bounded Zolem recording.go scan shows recordingResponseWriter methods no longer dispatch-fail for missing constructor initialization

title: Rust custom frontend project dir
description:
Title: Rust custom frontend ignores project dir

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,scan,pickpackit

## Symptom

After building a custom Rust frontend for a project, `shatter scan --project-dir <project>` does not find that custom frontend unless the caller's current working directory is also the project directory. Native Rust generators then fail with:

```text
native generator "State" requires a custom build (run `shatter build-frontend rust`)
native generator "current" requires a custom build (run `shatter build-frontend rust`)
```

This makes cross-directory scans of Rust projects with native generators silently fall back to the non-custom `shatter-rust` frontend and produce poor or misleading inputs.

## Evidence

Pickpackit validation worktree:

```text
/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api
```

Custom frontend build from that directory succeeded:

```bash
env SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter build-frontend rust
```

Output:

```text
[info] custom Rust frontend built: .shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom
```

The binary exists:

```text
/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api/.shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom
```

Running the scan from the Pickpackit repository root with `--project-dir .../api` still emitted the native-generator warnings above. Running the same scan from the `api/` directory stopped those warnings, which shows the custom binary lookup is tied to process CWD rather than the effective project directory.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-cli/src/helpers.rs::find_custom_binary` checks `.shatter-cache/bin/shatter-{lang}-custom` relative to the current process directory.
- The same helper only uses the `shatter_dir` argument for the legacy `.shatter/bin/` fallback.
- `scan --project-dir` supplies the intended project root elsewhere in the scan flow, but the custom frontend lookup does not use the project root's `.shatter-cache/bin`.
- `build-frontend rust` writes the binary to `<project>/.shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom`.

## Desired Behavior

When `--project-dir <project>` is supplied, Shatter should find `<project>/.shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom` regardless of the caller's CWD. The same principle should hold for Go custom frontend lookup if it shares the helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A scan launched outside a Rust project with `--project-dir <project>` uses `<project>/.shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom` when present.
- Existing CWD-relative custom frontend discovery still works for users running from the project root.
- Legacy `.shatter/bin/shatter-{lang}-custom` fallback remains intact.
- Add a focused test covering custom frontend discovery from a non-project CWD with a project `.shatter-cache/bin` custom binary.

## In Scope

- Custom frontend discovery logic in Shatter.
- Focused unit tests for the helper/config path.
- Minimal scan/frontend plumbing needed to pass the effective project directory into the lookup.

## Out of Scope

- Changing Pickpackit feature code.
- Tuning Pickpackit generators or coverage thresholds.
- Changing scan scheduling, timeout, or throughput behavior.
acceptance_criteria: scan --project-dir finds project-local .shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom from a non-project CWD; CWD-relative and legacy .shatter/bin custom frontend discovery still work; focused tests cover project-dir custom binary lookup

title: Scan budget leaves unrun funcs failed
description:
Title: Scan budget leaves unrun funcs failed

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: scan,reporting,pickpackit

## Symptom

When a scan's total budget expires, Shatter records functions that were not actually explored because of the total scan deadline as error-category skipped entries. The final codebase report routes those entries into `codebase.failed`, so a corpus run can look like dozens of real function failures even though most functions were never attempted after the scan budget was exhausted.

## Evidence

A Pickpackit handlers scan on Shatter `origin/main` at `f7ab2178fea168192cd4f892577eac69fcc251aa` scanned 75 exported functions with one worker and a 900s total budget:

```bash
shatter scan ~/.../pickpackit/.../api/src/handlers \
  --project-dir ~/.../pickpackit/.../api \
  --require-rust \
  --parallelism 1 --parallelism-min 1 --parallelism-max 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 3 \
  --timeout-total 900 \
  --timeout-per-fn 120 \
  --timeout-explore 90 \
  --request-timeout 120 \
  --exec-timeout 60 \
  --build-timeout 120 \
  --progress --color never --no-cache \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-main-f7ab.json \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-main-f7ab.md
```

Observed result:

- 14 functions completed.
- 3 functions had real per-task watchdog timeouts: `assistant.rs::assistant_message`, `bundles.rs::apply_bundle`, and `bundles.rs::create_bundle_entry`.
- 56 later functions were recorded with reason `timed out (total scan budget exceeded)`.
- The Markdown/JSON report summarized the run as 59 failed functions, obscuring the fact that most "failures" were unrun due to the global deadline rather than function-specific exploration failures.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` defines `TOTAL_SCAN_TIMEOUT_REASON` as `timed out (total scan budget exceeded)`.
- At the layer-boundary total-timeout path, and in the active-layer `FunctionOutcome::TotalTimeout` path, the orchestrator records these entries with `SkipCategory::Error`.
- `shatter-core/src/report.rs::split_skipped_into_failed` routes skipped entries with `SkipCategory::Error` into `codebase.failed`.
- Existing tests assert total-budget entries have the total-timeout reason, but they do not protect the user-facing distinction between real function failures and unattempted functions skipped because the run-level budget ended.

## Desired Behavior

The final report should distinguish functions not attempted due to total scan budget exhaustion from real per-function failures. A total-budget interruption may still mark the overall run as interrupted, but unrun functions should not inflate `codebase.failed` as if their own exploration failed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A total-scan-budget interruption still marks the scan/run status as interrupted.
- Functions skipped solely because the total scan budget was exhausted are represented separately from real function failures in the JSON and Markdown report, or at minimum are not counted in `codebase.failed` / failed-function totals.
- Real per-function timeouts, frontend errors, unsupported functions, and explicit expected skips keep their existing classifications.
- Add focused tests covering both layer-boundary and active-layer total-budget exhaustion so future reports do not regress.

## In Scope

- Shatter scan orchestration/report classification changes.
- Summary/report wording or bucket changes needed to make total-budget-unattempted functions clear.
- Focused unit/integration tests in Shatter.

## Out of Scope

- Changing Pickpackit feature code.
- Tuning Pickpackit handler inputs or coverage.
- Changing the shared-pool task watchdog duration for real in-flight function work.

title: Native generator CWD wrong
description:
Title: Native generator CWD wrong

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,input-generation,pickpackit

## Symptom

Rust native generators compiled into a custom `shatter-rust` frontend are invoked with the frontend process current working directory instead of the target project's root. A generator that reads a project-relative fixture or opens project-relative support files can fail when Shatter is launched from another directory.

This blocks Pickpackit item-image handler coverage: the configured item-image generator reads `tests/fixtures/images/sample.png`, which exists in Pickpackit's `api/` project, but a Shatter scan launched from a temporary run directory reported:

```text
generator error for current (.../.shatter/generators/pickpackit_item_image.rs): native generator "current" ... panicked: read Pickpackit sample PNG fixture: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: "No such file or directory" }
```

The generator then falls back to built-in input generation, reducing input spread for `delete_item_image` and likely preventing meaningful `upload_item_image` exploration.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/input_gen.rs::prefetch_custom_values` sends `Command::Generate` with `project_root: None` for every custom generator prefetch.
- `shatter-core/src/explorer.rs` has `ExploreConfig.project_root`, and both generator prefetch call sites run inside functions that already receive `config`.
- `shatter-rust/src/protocol.rs::Request` already has a `project_root: Option<String>` field for generate requests.
- `shatter-rust/src/handler.rs::handle_generate` and `generate_response` parse the request but do not pass `project_root` to native generator invocation.
- `shatter-rust/src/generators.rs::NativeRegistry::invoke` calls the registered Rust function directly, so any relative filesystem access uses the frontend process CWD.
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/build_frontend.rs` registers native generator files by canonical file path, so changing invocation CWD should not break file-specific registry lookup.

## Desired Behavior

When Shatter has detected a project root, custom generator prefetch should include that root in `Generate` requests. The Rust frontend should invoke `.rs` native generators with that project root as the temporary working directory so project-relative fixture and support-file access works regardless of where the scan command was launched.

If no project root is available, existing behavior should remain unchanged. If changing CWD fails, the generate response should use the existing generate error shape (`status: "error"`, `code: "internal_error"`) with a message that identifies the failed project-root CWD change.

Native generator invocation must restore the frontend process CWD after the generator returns or panics. Because CWD is process-global, the CWD change and generator call should be serialized within a frontend process rather than allowing overlapping native generator calls to race. The current handler processes protocol requests sequentially, but the implementation should keep the restoration/serialization guarantee local to the native invocation path.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused `shatter-core` regression proving custom-generator prefetch serializes `project_root` on outgoing `Generate` requests.
- Add a focused `shatter-rust` regression proving a native `.rs` generator observes `req.project_root` as its working directory during generation and that the caller's CWD is restored afterward.
- Rebuild the custom Rust frontend and rerun a focused Pickpackit item-image scan or generate path from outside the Pickpackit project, proving the `sample.png` generator no longer reports `No such file or directory`. A bounded validation target is `api/src/handlers/item_images.rs` with `--project-dir <pickpackit>/api`, `--require-rust`, serial parallelism, and a small `--max-iterations` value from a non-project working directory.

## Scope

In scope:

- Core generator prefetch plumbing for `project_root`.
- Rust frontend native generator invocation CWD handling.
- Focused tests and a bounded Pickpackit validation rerun.

Out of scope:

- Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Broad generator API redesign.
- Coverage improvements unrelated to native generator project-relative file access.
acceptance_criteria: Core Generate prefetch includes project_root; Rust native generators run under project_root and restore CWD; focused Pickpackit item-image validation no longer reports sample.png NotFound

title: Go ENOENT path feedback seeds files
description:
## Problem

Go local filesystem readers in Zolem fixture loader functions executed after earlier policy and receiver fixes, but path-like string inputs still came only from generic boundary/random values. Calls such as `os.ReadFile`, `os.ReadDir`, and `os.Stat` stopped at ENOENT and produced shallow behavior maps.

## Desired Behavior

For Go functions using allowed local filesystem reads, Shatter should inspect ENOENT feedback for paths attributable to the current input vector, create Shatter-owned scratch file or directory seeds, and schedule follow-up inputs without writing into the target project.

## Acceptance

- File path ENOENT feedback schedules a Shatter-owned empty temp file and reaches behavior beyond the initial missing-file error.
- Directory path ENOENT feedback schedules a Shatter-owned empty temp directory and reaches behavior beyond the initial missing-directory error.
- The feedback loop is scoped to Go local filesystem reads and does not modify the target checkout.
- Rust core/CLI gates, Go frontend tests, smoke, conformance, E2E, and bounded Zolem loader validation pass.
acceptance_criteria: Go path-string file and directory readers get isolated empty temp file/dir follow-up seeds after attributed ENOENT; tests and bounded Zolem loader scan show progress beyond prior ENOENT-only behavior.

title: Go Execute uses parameterized receiver ctors
description:
Title: Go Execute uses parameterized receiver ctors

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,planner,zolem,coverage

## Problem

Shatter's Go planning path can construct method receivers with parameterized
same-package constructors when the constructor parameters are primitive-
satisfiable, but direct Execute receiver-kind synthesis still skips every
parameterful constructor. As a result, methods on receiver types that require
constructor initialization are reported as unsupported even when the package
provides a usable constructor such as `NewLoader(dir string) *Loader`.

This blocks Zolem fixture-loader coverage after OS local filesystem policy
skips were fixed.

## Smallest Known Reproduction

Using landed Shatter `main` at merge `64c0f60c5895393e83b21f96b2aef00d892c5809`,
run:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --include internal/fixture/loader.go \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 20 \
  --timeout-per-fn 5 \
  --timeout-explore 5 \
  --timeout-total 240 \
  --request-timeout 30 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 60 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --progress \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-fixture-loader-os-policy-preview.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

The scan completes with zero policy skips, but six methods in
`internal/fixture/loader.go` still have `completion_outcome: dispatch_failed`
and zero covered lines. Their discovered inputs report:

```text
receiver type Loader requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
```

Affected methods include:

- `(*Loader).WithNamespace`
- `(*Loader).WithRunner`
- `(*Loader).WithSequenceCounters`
- `(*Loader).loadFixturesYAML`
- `(*Loader).loadSelectorWASM`
- `(*Loader).Load`

## Current Code Facts

- Zolem defines `type Loader struct` in
  `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/fixture/loader.go` with unexported
  reference-typed fields such as `counters *SequenceCounters` and
  `runner *Runner`.
- The same file defines `func NewLoader(dir string) *Loader`, so the receiver
  has a same-package constructor with one primitive-satisfiable `string`
  parameter.
- `shatter-go/planner/receiver.go` already allows parameterized constructors
  when `allParamsSatisfiable(c)` is true and stores `ConstructorParams` on the
  receiver plan.
- `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go` already emits constructor receiver cases for
  parameterized constructors by calling `constructorCallExpr(c)`, which uses
  Go zero-value literals such as `""` for string parameters.
- `shatter-go/protocol/prepared_launcher.go` already converts constructor
  parameters into wrapper constructor metadata via `toWrapperConstructors`.
- `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go` function `synthesizeExecuteReceiverKind`
  still skips all constructors where `len(c.Parameters) > 0`, then refuses
  zero-value fallback when `ReceiverRequiresConstruction(pkg, &target)` is
  true. That produces the unsupported outcome above.

## Desired Behavior

Direct Execute receiver-kind synthesis should mirror the planner/wrapper
capability for same-package constructors:

- If a method receiver requires construction and a same-package constructor
  for that receiver has primitive-satisfiable parameters, synthesize
  `receiver_kind: "constructor:<FuncName>"`.
- The generated wrapper should then call that constructor with zero-value
  literals for the constructor parameters, as it already does for prepared
  invocation plans.
- Constructors with unsatisfiable parameters, interface receivers, generic
  unconstrained receivers, and receiver types with no usable constructor should
  continue to fail closed with the existing unsupported outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a failing Go regression test showing `synthesizeExecuteReceiverKind`
  chooses `constructor:NewLoader` for a method on a receiver that requires
  construction when `NewLoader(dir string) *Loader` exists.
- Preserve or add a regression showing constructors with unsatisfiable
  parameters are still skipped and construction-required receivers remain
  unsupported.
- Implement the direct Execute synthesis change narrowly in the Go frontend.
- Run focused Go protocol/planner tests, then `go test ./... -timeout 20m`
  and `go vet ./...` in `shatter-go`.
- Re-run the bounded Zolem `internal/fixture/loader.go` scan and verify the
  `Loader` methods above no longer fail with the parameterless-constructor
  unsupported reason.

## In Scope

- Go direct Execute receiver-kind synthesis.
- Same-package constructor selection for primitive-satisfiable constructor
  parameters.
- Focused Zolem fixture-loader validation.

## Out of Scope

- Zolem feature-code changes.
- Whole-corpus Zolem coverage scanning.
- General fixture directory seeding or filesystem sandbox changes.
- Supporting arbitrary opaque constructor parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Direct Execute chooses primitive-satisfiable same-package parameterized receiver constructors; unsatisfiable constructors still fail closed; focused tests and bounded Zolem loader scan pass.

title: Go OS policy symbol qualifier
description:
Title: Go OS policy symbol qualifier

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,policy,zolem,coverage

## Problem

Shatter's Go execution policy is supposed to allow local filesystem operations by default (`ClassLocalFS`), but current Go dependency analysis can report standard-library OS calls with qualified symbols such as `os.ReadFile`, `os.Stat`, and `os.ReadDir`. The policy table checks for unqualified names like `ReadFile`, `Stat`, and `ReadDir`, so those calls are incorrectly classified as `unknown_high` and denied before execution.

This blocks Zolem coverage for local file/fixture loading code that should be policy-allowed.

## Current Evidence

Focused current scan from landed Shatter `main`:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --include 'internal/fixture/loader.go' \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 20 \
  --timeout-per-fn 5 \
  --timeout-explore 5 \
  --timeout-total 240 \
  --request-timeout 30 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 60 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --progress \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-fixture-loader-current.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

The JSON report still contains five `skipped_by_policy` functions in `internal/fixture/loader.go`, accounting for 258 lines and 60 branches:

- `fileExists`: `os.Stat`, 11 lines, 3 branches
- `(*Loader).loadFixturesYAML`: `os.ReadFile`, 75 lines, 17 branches
- `(*Loader).loadSelectorWASM`: `os.ReadFile`, 19 lines, 4 branches
- `loadOne`: `os.ReadFile`, 86 lines, 18 branches
- `(*Loader).Load`: `os.ReadDir`, 67 lines, 18 branches

Representative reason:

```text
skipped: side effect class=unknown_high (component=os.ReadFile, evidence=dependency os.ReadFile (os)) not in policy.allow
```

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-go/protocol/policy.go` documents the default allow set as `ClassPure` and `ClassLocalFS`.
- `moduleClass` in `shatter-go/protocol/policy.go` handles `module == "os"` by checking `isProcessGlobalOsSymbol(symbol)` and `isLocalFSOsSymbol(symbol)`.
- `isLocalFSOsSymbol` contains unqualified local filesystem names including `Open`, `OpenFile`, `ReadFile`, `WriteFile`, `Stat`, `ReadDir`, and `MkdirAll`.
- The focused Zolem report shows the frontend dependency symbol includes the package qualifier (`os.ReadFile`, `os.Stat`, `os.ReadDir`), so the current unqualified comparison misses allowed local filesystem symbols and falls through to `ClassUnknownHigh`.
- Genuine process-global OS calls such as `os.Setenv`, `os.Chdir`, and `os.Exit` must remain denied by default.

## Desired Behavior

Go policy classification should normalize standard-library dependency symbols consistently before checking the `os` allow/deny tables. Qualified and unqualified OS symbols should classify the same way:

- `ReadFile`, `os.ReadFile` -> `ClassLocalFS`
- `Stat`, `os.Stat` -> `ClassLocalFS`
- `ReadDir`, `os.ReadDir` -> `ClassLocalFS`
- `Setenv`, `os.Setenv` -> `ClassProcessGlobal`

The normalization should be narrow enough that genuine unknown or dangerous `os` calls still fail closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add failing policy regression tests showing `ExternalDependency{SourceModule: "os", Symbol: "os.ReadFile"}` and `os.Stat` classify as `ClassLocalFS`, not `ClassUnknownHigh`.
- Add or preserve a regression showing qualified process-global symbols such as `os.Setenv` classify as `ClassProcessGlobal`.
- Implement narrow symbol normalization for `module == "os"` policy classification.
- Run focused Go protocol tests and full `go test ./...` / `go vet ./...` for `shatter-go`.
- Re-run the bounded Zolem `internal/fixture/loader.go` scan above and verify the five OS local filesystem rows are no longer skipped for `unknown_high` OS policy reasons.

## In Scope

- Go frontend policy classification for standard-library `os` dependency symbols.
- Focused tests for qualified vs unqualified `os` symbols.
- Bounded Zolem fixture-loader validation.

## Out of Scope

- Allowing process-global OS operations by default.
- Changing local filesystem sandbox semantics.
- Zolem feature-code changes.
- Whole-corpus scanning beyond the bounded validation target.
acceptance_criteria: Qualified os.ReadFile/os.Stat/os.ReadDir classify as local_fs; qualified process-global os symbols remain denied; focused Go tests and bounded Zolem fixture-loader scan pass.

title: Rust Axum coverage shallow
description:
Title: Rust Axum coverage shallow

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,axum,coverage,pickpackit

## Symptom

After Shatter applies Pickpackit's function-specific Rust generators, several `api/src/handlers/bundles.rs` Axum handlers now execute successfully and return HTTP 200 responses, but Shatter still reports very low handler line and branch coverage. This blocks the whole-corpus Pickpackit validation goal because the scan is no longer stopped at router-level 404, yet completed handlers still appear to cover only a small prefix of the function body.

Example from a bounded scan of Pickpackit `bundles.rs`:

```text
Scan complete: 8 completed, 1 failed, 0 unsupported, 0 skipped
Overall coverage (completed-functions subset): 18.3%
```

Completed functions with successful behavior still report shallow coverage:

```text
create_bundle_entry: 0/6 branches, 1/16 lines, 3 iterations, returns HTTP 200 body with entryKind/task id
get_bundle: 0/2 branches, 1/10 lines, 3 iterations, returns HTTP 200 bundle body
update_bundle_entry: 6/21 branches, 7/79 lines, 3 iterations, returns HTTP 200 entry body
```

The same scan artifacts show native replay recipes using the intended Pickpackit generators and concrete route ids, so the remaining low coverage is not explained by the prior config-separator mismatch.

## Smallest Known Evidence

Repository under test: `~/project/pickpackit`, validation worktree `~/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation`.

Shatter branch used for evidence: `str-uk4o-rust-config-separators`, after the config separator fix.

Prerequisites:

```bash
docker compose up -d postgres
DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
  cargo run --manifest-path api/Cargo.toml --bin pickpackit-migrate
```

Bounded scan command, run from Pickpackit `api/`:

```bash
SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-uk4o-rust-config-separators/shatter-rust-runtime \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-uk4o-rust-config-separators/target/debug/shatter \
  scan src/handlers \
  --include bundles.rs \
  --project-dir . \
  --require-rust \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --parallelism-min 1 \
  --parallelism-max 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 3 \
  --timeout-total 420 \
  --timeout-per-fn 90 \
  --timeout-explore 60 \
  --request-timeout 120 \
  --exec-timeout 60 \
  --build-timeout 120 \
  --progress \
  --color never \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-api-bundles-str-uk4o-m3.json \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-api-bundles-str-uk4o-m3.md
```

Generated scan artifact directory:

```text
api/shatter-artifacts/scan-results/4bc304bc96e41deb46522f99b6a6e3c09bf52e558a58725b5f22182495911f31/
```

Concrete artifact facts:

- `functions/00003_...__create_bundle_entry.json` contains `.shatter/generators/pickpackit_bundle.rs`, concrete `bundle_id` values, status `200`, and top-level status `completed`, but the markdown report shows only `1/16` lines and `0/6` branches.
- `functions/00006_...__get_bundle.json` contains `.shatter/generators/pickpackit_bundle.rs`, concrete `bundle_id` values, status `200`, and top-level status `completed`, but the markdown report shows only `1/10` lines and `0/2` branches.
- `functions/00009_...__update_bundle_entry.json` contains `.shatter/generators/pickpackit_bundle_entry.rs`, concrete `bundle_id` and `entry_id` values, repeated status `200`, and top-level status `completed`, but the markdown report shows only `7/79` lines and `6/21` branches.

There was also one failure in the same bounded run:

```text
delete_bundle: timed out during task after 215s
```

That timeout should be tracked separately if it is not caused by the same coverage accounting bug. This issue is specifically about successful Axum executions producing shallow coverage data.

## Current Code Facts

- Rust Axum handler execution is implemented in `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs`.
- Rust source instrumentation is implemented in `shatter-rust/src/instrument.rs`.
- The scan report line and branch totals are aggregated by Shatter from Rust frontend execution results; the completed Pickpackit handlers have observed HTTP 200 behavior but line counts still look like entry-line-only or wrapper-level coverage.
- Existing issue `str-ltq0` covers Axum path default generation and execution-level tuple path tests. It does not cover coverage accounting after a handler has already reached and returned from handler logic.

## Desired Behavior

When a Rust Axum handler executes successfully, Shatter should report line and branch coverage for the handler body that actually ran, not only the wrapper/entry point or a shallow prefix. Pickpackit handlers returning HTTP 200 should show coverage consistent with executed validation, database, and response-construction code.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Rust frontend regression with an Axum handler that returns successfully after executing multiple handler-body lines and at least one branch; verify Shatter reports those executed lines and branches.
- Fix Rust instrumentation/execution/coverage mapping so Axum handler body coverage is not collapsed to entry-line-scale coverage after successful execution.
- Preserve existing Axum route generation behavior and existing path extractor behavior.
- Re-run the bounded Pickpackit `bundles.rs` scan above and show successful handlers such as `create_bundle_entry`, `get_bundle`, and `update_bundle_entry` report materially more accurate line/branch coverage, or document a more precise follow-up if another blocker is exposed.

## Scope

In scope:

- Rust frontend instrumentation, execution result coverage payloads, and scan aggregation for Axum handler executions.
- Focused Rust frontend regression tests for handler body line and branch coverage.
- Pickpackit validation scan as proof of improvement.

Out of scope:

- Non-trivial Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Broad generator rewrites.
- The `delete_bundle` timeout unless investigation proves it has the same root cause.
- Axum path parsing/default-value gaps already tracked by `str-ltq0`.
acceptance_criteria: Focused Rust frontend Axum coverage regression passes; successful Axum handler body line/branch coverage is not entry-line-scale; bounded Pickpackit bundles scan shows materially improved successful-handler coverage or a precise follow-up blocker.
notes: Implementation note: added statement-level Rust line_hit instrumentation plus a crate-backed Axum regression. Validation: focused explore of Pickpackit create_bundle_entry with the patched custom frontend reports lines_executed [292, 298, 300, 301, 302, 303, 305, 306], improving from entry-line-only [292]. Bounded bundles.rs scan with max-iterations=3 improved completed handler line coverage materially: create_bundle_entry 1/16 -> 8/16, get_bundle 1/10 -> 3/10, list_bundles 9/97 -> 23/97, update_bundle 9/81 -> 26/81, delete_bundle_entry 2/20 -> 8/20. Residual: branch/input diversity and total scan budget starvation remain separate triage findings; a draft issue was reviewed as triage-only because the repro depends on a local Pickpackit database checkout and needs a portable fixture.

title: Rust config separators mismatch
description:
Title: Rust config separators mismatch

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,config,input-generation,pickpackit,coverage

## Symptom

Pickpackit API uses Rust-style function override keys in `api/.shatter/config.yaml`, for example:

```yaml
functions:
  "**/bundles.rs::create_bundle_entry":
    param_generators:
      current: generators/pickpackit_bundle.rs
```

When Shatter explores the same Rust handler through the CLI target syntax `src/handlers/bundles.rs:create_bundle_entry`, the function-level `param_generators.current` override is not applied. The generated native replay uses the default `current` generator instead of the configured bundle-aware generator, so the Axum request path lacks `bundle_id` and returns a shallow router-level `404`.

This keeps Pickpackit bundle handlers from reaching meaningful branch logic and blocks the current whole-corpus validation goal.

## Smallest Known Reproduction

Repository under test: `~/project/pickpackit`, validation worktree `~/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation`.

Prerequisites used in the repro:

```bash
docker compose up -d postgres
DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
  cargo run --manifest-path api/Cargo.toml --bin pickpackit-migrate
```

Focused command, run from Pickpackit `api/`:

```bash
SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust-runtime \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter \
  explore src/handlers/bundles.rs:create_bundle_entry \
  --project-dir . \
  --require-rust \
  --workers 1 \
  --observer-pool 1 \
  --max-iterations 3 \
  --timeout-explore 60 \
  --time-limit 120 \
  --request-timeout 120 \
  --exec-timeout 60 \
  --build-timeout 120 \
  --color never \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-create-bundle-entry-explore-m3.json \
  -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-create-bundle-entry-explore-m3.md
```

Observed result:

- Explore completed in about 54 seconds.
- `create_bundle_entry` reported 3 iterations, 1 path, and 0/6 branches.
- The artifact under `api/shatter-artifacts/explore-results/src_handlers_bundles.rs/00292_create_bundle_entry.json` shows the raw native replay for `current` used `.shatter/generators/pickpackit.rs`.
- The same replay recipe had `axum.path: /test/{workspace_id}` and did not include `bundle_id`.
- The handler returned HTTP 404 with `{ "error": "not found" }` and only line 292 executed.

Expected for this config: `current` should use `.shatter/generators/pickpackit_bundle.rs` for `create_bundle_entry`, because that function override is explicitly configured.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/config.rs` resolves function overrides in `resolve_from_merged` and `resolve_function_config_with_inputs`.
- Both functions currently compile each config `functions` key as a glob and call `matcher.is_match(function_id)` directly.
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs` builds the per-function config id as `format!("{}:{}", file_str, func.name)`.
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` calls `load_config_function_inputs`, which passes its `func_name` straight into `resolve_function_config_with_inputs`.
- Existing config docs from `shatter-cli/src/commands/init.rs` describe per-function keys as `relative/path.<ext>:functionName`.
- Existing `shatter-core/src/config.rs` test `resolve_function_config_matches_scan_function_ids` proves exact Rust-style keys match exact Rust-style ids like `/repo/src/handlers/legs.rs::fetch_legs_for_workspace`.
- There is no regression proving a Rust-style config key like `**/bundles.rs::create_bundle_entry` also applies when the caller supplies the documented CLI/explore id `src/handlers/bundles.rs:create_bundle_entry`.

## Desired Behavior

Per-function config matching should tolerate the separator mismatch between documented Shatter target ids (`file:function`) and Rust-qualified function keys (`file::function`) when the file suffix and function name are otherwise the same.

Both scan and explore must honor the same matching semantics because both paths resolve inputs and generators through `resolve_function_config_with_inputs`.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused failing regression in `shatter-core` showing a config key such as `**/bundles.rs::create_bundle_entry` resolves function-level `param_generators.current` for a function id such as `src/handlers/bundles.rs:create_bundle_entry`.
- Implement the matching fix in Shatter config resolution so both `file:function` and `file::function` forms can match equivalent file/function targets without breaking existing glob behavior.
- Run the focused regression test and the relevant `shatter-core` config tests.
- Re-run the focused Pickpackit `create_bundle_entry` explore command and verify the native replay uses `.shatter/generators/pickpackit_bundle.rs` rather than `.shatter/generators/pickpackit.rs`, with an Axum path that includes both `workspace_id` and `bundle_id`.
- Re-run a bounded Pickpackit `bundles.rs` scan and verify function-specific generators are applied for configured bundle handlers; if coverage is still shallow, document the next blocker in Beads instead of changing Pickpackit feature code.

## Scope

In scope:

- Shatter `.shatter/config.yaml` per-function matching logic.
- Focused Shatter regression tests for separator compatibility.
- Pickpackit validation commands that prove the configured generators are applied.

Out of scope:

- Non-trivial Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Broad generator rewrites.
- Changing the documented `file:function` CLI target syntax.
- Relaxing skip or failure reporting for unsupported functions.
acceptance_criteria: Focused shatter-core regression proves Rust-style config keys match CLI/explore file:function ids; config matching fix preserves existing glob behavior; focused Pickpackit explore uses bundle-aware generator; bounded bundles scan rerun documents next blocker if any.

title: Go HTTP writer policy skip
description:
Title: Go HTTP writer policy skip

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,policy,zolem

## Problem

Shatter's Go frontend currently skips functions that accept `http.ResponseWriter` under the default execution policy, even though the same frontend already treats `http.ResponseWriter` as a synthesizable in-memory runtime value.

This blocks broad Zolem coverage for HTTP response helpers and handler-like paths. In the latest whole-corpus Zolem report, 57 functions were `skipped_by_policy` because of:

`skipped: side effect class=network (component=http.ResponseWriter, evidence=param "w" type http.ResponseWriter) not in policy.allow`

Those 57 skipped functions account for 1476 lines and 159 branches.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-go/runtimeval/registry.go` registers `http.ResponseWriter` as `httptest.NewRecorder()` with import `net/http/httptest`, which is an in-memory recorder and does not bind a network socket.
- `shatter-go/runtimeval/registry.go` registers `*http.Request` as `httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/", bytes.NewReader(nil))`.
- `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer_test.go` has `TestAnalyzeSynthesizableStdlibTypes`, documenting that `http.ResponseWriter` and `*http.Request` should be emitted as `Kind="unknown"` with `TypeName` so the planner can resolve safe runtime values instead of skipping before planning.
- `shatter-go/protocol/policy.go` currently maps `http.ResponseWriter` and `http.Request` in `paramTypeClass` to `ClassNetwork`, so `evaluateExecutePolicy` denies these non-adapter functions before planning can use the runtime-value registry.
- `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go` already bypasses the policy gate for exact adapter-owned HTTP handlers (`InvocationModel.Kind == "adapter"`). This issue is about direct-execution functions and helpers whose parameters can be safely synthesized, not about bypassing the policy for arbitrary outbound network dependencies.

## Smallest Reproduction

Use the existing Go protocol test fixture:

- File: `shatter-go/protocol/testdata/opaque.go`
- Function: `AcceptsResponseWriter(w http.ResponseWriter)`

Expected behavior: default policy should allow execution to proceed past the policy gate because the parameter has a safe runtime value (`httptest.NewRecorder()`).

Current behavior to capture with a red regression test: executing `AcceptsResponseWriter` through `runExecuteWithLoader` returns `outcome.status == "skipped_by_policy"` with the `http.ResponseWriter` network reason.

## Desired Behavior

The default policy should not classify safe runtime-value parameter types as denied network side effects when the runtime-value registry owns an in-memory constructor.

At minimum, `http.ResponseWriter` should no longer be policy-denied. If the implementation touches the same policy table, verify whether `*http.Request` has the same mismatch and keep it aligned with the existing runtime registry and analyzer tests.

Genuine outbound network operations must still be denied by default, including `net.Conn`, `net.Listener`, `http.Client`, `net/http` dependency calls such as `http.NewRequestWithContext`, and other non-runtime-value network resources.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a failing regression test showing `AcceptsResponseWriter` is currently skipped by policy despite being a registered runtime value.
- Update the Go policy classification so safe `httptest`-backed runtime values for HTTP writer/request parameters are allowed to reach planning/execution by default.
- Keep existing policy tests for database, subprocess, browser, `net.Conn`, `net.Listener`, `http.Client`, and outbound `net/http` dependencies passing.
- Run focused Go protocol tests.
- Run this bounded Zolem scan and show at least one previously skipped helper, such as `writeJSON` in `cmd/zolem/local_admin.go`, no longer has `completion_outcome == "skipped_by_policy"` for the writer policy reason:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
```

title: Go unsupported receiver behavioral
description:
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go, scan, reporting, zolem, coverage

## Symptom

The current Zolem whole-corpus scan still counts Go receiver methods as
`completion_outcome == "behavioral"` even when every discovered input is
`outcome_status == "unsupported"` and no source lines or branches execute.
This makes the behavior maps and coverage/progress summary overstate successful
execution.

Whole-corpus evidence from the latest available Zolem report:

```text
report: /var/tmp/zolem-shatter-str-cir6-corpus.json
attempted_functions: 358
completed_functions: 358
completed_with_behavior: 234
completed_error_only: 38
completed_skipped_by_policy: 86
unsupported_functions: 24
overall_coverage: 33.16481294236603
```

Outcome rollup from that report:

```text
behavioral       234 functions, 622 / 2882 lines, 224 / 471 branches
error_only        38 functions, 145 / 814 lines, 104 / 172 branches
skipped_by_policy 86 functions,   0 / 2353 lines, 0 / 346 branches
```

Representative false behavioral rows from that report:

```text
105 lines, 13 branches, behavioral, unsupported:
  /home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/local_admin.go::(*localControlPlane).UpsertListener

  /home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/ollama/client.go::(detector).detect
  receiver type detector requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
```

## Focused Reproduction

From the current Shatter `main` worktree:

```bash
target/debug/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --include 'cmd/zolem/local_admin.go' \
```
