```bash
  --progress \
  --format json \
  -o /var/tmp/zolem-local-admin-receiver-gap.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

Observed focused aggregate:

```json
{
  "attempted": 20,
  "completed": 20,
  "behavioral": 13,
  "unsupported": 5,
  "skipped": 5,
  "coverage": 4.225352112676056
}
```

Observed focused rows with zero executed lines:

```text
behavioral  (*localControlPlane).ClearCalls     12 lines  2 branches  unsupported receiver initialization
behavioral  (*localControlPlane).Close          18 lines  3 branches  unsupported receiver initialization
behavioral  (*localControlPlane).DeleteListener 18 lines  3 branches  unsupported receiver initialization
behavioral  (*localControlPlane).ListCalls      12 lines  2 branches  unsupported receiver initialization
behavioral  (*localControlPlane).ListListeners  23 lines  1 branch    unsupported receiver initialization
behavioral  (*localControlPlane).UpsertProfile  30 lines  4 branches  unsupported receiver initialization
behavioral  (*localControlPlane).UpsertListener 105 lines 13 branches unsupported receiver initialization
```

The shared reason is:

```text
receiver type localControlPlane requires constructor initialization; no parameterless constructor available
```

## Current Code Facts

- The focused scan writes per-function artifacts under
  `shatter-artifacts/scan-results/<scan-id>/functions/*.json`.
- The false behavioral functions have `lines_covered == 0`,
  `branches_covered == 0`, and discovered inputs whose unique
  `outcome_status` set is only `["unsupported"]`.
- The scan report still increments `completed_with_behavior` and
  `completed_functions` for those rows.
- This is distinct from policy skips: the same focused scan correctly reports
  HTTP/network surfaces such as `handleListenerResource` as
  `completion_outcome == "skipped_by_policy"`.
- Older issue `str-2x4u` fixed an all-execute-skip behavioral classification
  path, but this current Go receiver-initialization unsupported path still
  reaches `behavioral`.

## Desired Behavior

If a function has no successful observations, no executed source lines, and
all discovered inputs are unsupported because Shatter cannot construct the
receiver or parameters, scan output must not classify it as a behavioral
success.

It should be reported as unsupported or another non-success outcome with the
existing constructor diagnostic preserved. The exact bucket can follow current
Shatter semantics, but the report must not count these functions as
`completed_with_behavior`, must not emit a misleading behavior map, and must
not make Zolem execution-success metrics look better than they are.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Shatter regression for a Go receiver method whose only
  discovered input has `outcome_status == "unsupported"` and zero covered
  lines/branches, proving it is not reported as
  `completion_outcome == "behavioral"`.
- Preserve the receiver-constructor diagnostic in the report or function
  artifact.
- Re-run the focused Zolem `cmd/zolem/local_admin.go` scan above and verify
  `(*localControlPlane).UpsertListener` and the other all-unsupported receiver
  methods are no longer counted as behavioral completion.
- Re-run the Zolem whole-corpus report summary or a bounded equivalent and
  verify all-unsupported zero-line functions are excluded from
  `completed_with_behavior`.
- Preserve genuine behavioral, error-only, and `skipped_by_policy`
  classifications.
- Keep Zolem feature code unchanged.

## Scope

In scope:

- Scan result classification/reporting for Go functions where all discovered
  inputs are unsupported receiver/parameter construction failures.
- Focused Shatter tests and a bounded Zolem validation rerun.

Out of scope:

- Teaching Shatter to synthesize complex receiver constructors.
- Allowing network or filesystem side effects that are currently skipped by
  policy.
- Broad coverage improvements beyond making unsupported-result reporting
  truthful.
- Non-trivial Zolem feature-code changes.
acceptance_criteria: All-unsupported zero-line Go receiver methods are not counted as behavioral completion; diagnostic is preserved; focused Zolem local_admin scan verifies affected methods; genuine behavioral/error-only/skipped_by_policy classifications remain intact.
close_reason: Resolved on pushed main 7139ed1c7c2cb0b37ece88332f044ce31aa05fc6. All-unsupported Go receiver/parameter construction outcomes now classify as dispatch_failed instead of behavioral, preserving the frontend constructor diagnostic. Focused Zolem local_admin scan now reports 2 behavioral, 11 dispatch_failed, 7 skipped_by_policy; UpsertListener is dispatch_failed with the receiver-constructor reason.

title: Go scan stalls on one fn
description:
Title: Go scan stalls on one function

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go, scan, timeout, zolem

## Symptom

A fresh serial Shatter scan of Zolem on Shatter `main` commit
`877e9625` can spend many minutes inside one Go function without producing a
per-function timeout, failed-function artifact, or progress event. This blocks
whole-corpus Zolem validation because the scan cannot reliably reach the final
summary.

The current blocker was observed on:

```text
target repo: /home/ketan/project/zolem
target branch: main
shatter repo: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi
shatter commit: 877e9625
scan artifact dir:
  /home/ketan/project/zolem/shatter-artifacts/scan-results/47a6994904dfe0c5ea582a492b21b2f60c7aafec8571f5c8c80bfba59d1de35f
```

Command:

```bash
env \
  SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
  SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
  ZOLEM_SHATTER_REPO_WRITE_GUARD=/home/ketan/project/zolem/.shatter/sandbox-host-write-guard.codex-20260608 \
  ZOLEM_SHATTER_TMP_WRITE_GUARD=/tmp/zolem-shatter-sandbox-host-write-guard.codex-20260608 \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter scan \
    --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
    --language go \
    --all \
    --progress \
    --parallelism 1 \
    --parallelism-min 1 \
    --parallelism-max 1 \
    --scheduler-policy serial \
    --workers-per-fn 1 \
    --request-timeout 120 \
    --build-timeout 120 \
    --timeout-total 1800 \
    --fail-on-failures=100 \
    -o /var/tmp/zolem-shatter-877e9625-serial.json \
    -o /var/tmp/zolem-shatter-877e9625-serial.md \
    /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

The scan reported:

```text
Discovered 57 source file(s)
Including 204 unexported function(s) in scan scope
Skipped 69 function(s) (unexecutable parameter types)
Scanning 313 function(s) in dependency order...
```

It made progress through 107 completed function artifacts, then started:

```text
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/specs/openapi.go::lookupRequestSchema
```

No artifact was written for that function:

```text
missing:
/home/ketan/project/zolem/shatter-artifacts/scan-results/47a6994904dfe0c5ea582a492b21b2f60c7aafec8571f5c8c80bfba59d1de35f/functions/00233_home_ketan_project_zolem_internal_specs_openapi.go__lookupRequestSchema.json
```

After several minutes with no new scan progress, process inspection showed one
live Docker sandbox container and one `/shatter-bin/launcher` inside it.
`docker logs` for the container showed many JSON execution results for this
same function, mostly fast target-returned errors such as:

```text
no supported openapi operation configured for <generated source key>
param doc: json: cannot unmarshal string into field Components.callbacks of type openapi3.PathItem
```

The scan was interrupted manually with SIGINT after the function had consumed
many minutes. The command exited with code 130, so no final
`/var/tmp/zolem-shatter-877e9625-serial.{json,md}` summary was produced.

## Current Code Facts

The Zolem target function is:

```go
func lookupRequestSchema(doc *openapi3.T, source ContractSource) (*openapi3.SchemaRef, error)
```

from `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/specs/openapi.go`. It first calls
`supportedOpenAPIOperation(source)`, then looks up the OpenAPI path, method,
request body, and JSON/octet-stream schema. Invalid `ContractSource` values
return a normal Go error quickly.

The previous stale Zolem report from May 29, before recent Shatter fixes,
showed:

```text
Functions discovered: 360
Functions attempted: 271
Functions completed: 245
Functions failed: 26
Functions skipped: 89
Overall coverage (completed-functions subset): 35.1%
```

The fresh scan improved discovery/attempt shape but still cannot be used as
whole-corpus evidence while a single function can monopolize the run:

```text
Discovered executable attempts: 313
Skipped as unexecutable parameter types: 69
Completed artifacts before manual interrupt: 107
```

## Desired Behavior

Whole-corpus scans should make bounded progress even when one Go function
generates many error-only executions or solver candidates. A single target
function should eventually complete, fail with a specific timeout/exploration
diagnostic, or be classified as error-only. It should not run for many minutes
without a per-function artifact or progress update when the user provided
`--request-timeout`, `--build-timeout`, `--timeout-total`, and the scan has a
documented per-function timeout mechanism.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Shatter regression that reproduces this class of Go scan stall
  without depending on Zolem feature code. The test should cover a function
  that returns quick errors for many generated inputs or otherwise keeps the
  explorer busy past the intended per-function budget.
- Fix scan/exploration timeout enforcement so the affected function produces a
  completed/error-only/failed artifact instead of silently monopolizing the
  serial scan.
- Re-run a targeted Zolem scan for
  `internal/specs/openapi.go::lookupRequestSchema` and verify it terminates
  with an artifact and actionable outcome.
- Re-run the low-parallel whole-corpus Zolem scan far enough to pass this
  function and reach later functions. If another blocker appears, file the next
  smaller issue with report/artifact evidence.

## Scope

In scope:

- Go scan/exploration timeout enforcement.
- Progress and artifact behavior when one function consumes its budget.
- Focused Shatter tests and targeted Zolem validation.

Out of scope:

- Non-trivial Zolem feature-code changes.
- Broad improvements to Zolem input quality or the 69 unexecutable parameter
  skips; those should be separate issues.
- Treating target-returned errors from `lookupRequestSchema` as Shatter
  failures when they are valid function behavior.

title: Policy skips reported behavioral
description:
Go execute responses with `outcome.status == "skipped_by_policy"` can be flattened by `shatter scan` into a behavioral discovered input with `return_value: null`, `thrown_error: null`, and `lines_executed: []`. This makes policy-blocked executions look like successful null-return behavior and obscures why coverage is zero.

Observed evidence:
- While validating `str-5qi1`, direct `shatter-go` execution of Zolem `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/runtime/store.go::ValidateLoopbackAddr` with input `"192.168.1.42"` returned:
  - top-level `status: "execute"`
  - `outcome.status: "skipped_by_policy"`
  - `outcome.short_reason: "skipped: side effect class=network (component=net.SplitHostPort, evidence=dependency net.SplitHostPort (net)) not in policy.allow"`
- A targeted scan of the same file written to `/tmp/zolem-runtime-str-5qi1.json` reported the same function as:
  - `completion_outcome: "behavioral"`
  - discovered input `"192.168.1.42"`
  - `return_value: null`
  - `thrown_error: null`
  - `lines_executed: []`
- The same targeted scan correctly reports pure target-returned errors such as `validateErrorType("")` as `completion_outcome: "error_only"` with `thrown_error: "function_error: error_type is required when backend is error"` and line traces. The gap is specific to skipped-by-policy outcomes being represented as successful behavior in scan output.

Current code facts:
- Go policy evaluation and execute outcome synthesis live under `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go` and `shatter-go/protocol/policy.go`.
- Rust-side scan/report aggregation consumes frontend execute responses and writes per-function `completion_outcome`, `discovered_inputs`, `return_value`, `thrown_error`, and `lines_executed` in the scan JSON report.
- The current scan JSON schema has no visible per-input field for `outcome.status`, so skipped-by-policy may need to map to an existing non-behavioral representation or the report schema may need an explicit outcome/status field.

Desired behavior:
Policy-skipped Go executions should not be counted or displayed as behavioral null successes. Scan output should preserve enough information for users and agents to distinguish policy skips from successful executions, including the skip reason where available.

Acceptance checks:
- Add a focused regression that feeds a frontend execute response with `outcome.status == "skipped_by_policy"` through the scan/report aggregation path and proves it is not emitted as a plain behavioral null-success input.
- Verify the regression preserves or exposes the policy skip reason.
- Re-run a targeted Zolem scan for `internal/runtime/store.go::ValidateLoopbackAddr` or the containing file and verify the policy skip is distinguishable from successful null behavior.

In scope:
- Scan/report aggregation of frontend `skipped_by_policy` outcomes.
- Minimal Go/Rust protocol mapping changes needed to preserve skip reason in reports.

Out of scope:
- Relaxing the default Go side-effect policy.
- Making `net.SplitHostPort` executable under the default policy.
- Broad input-generation or coverage strategy changes.

title: Go error returns surface as behavior
description:
Shatter's generated Go wrapper currently treats target functions that return `error` as ordinary successful return values, and drops secondary return values entirely. This makes functions with signatures like `func F(...) error` and `func F(...) (T, error)` appear successful even when the target returned a non-nil error.

Observed impact:
- A full Zolem scan from Shatter `main` commit `99c8db9a5c7129b11eba2701c6f69362e66e0b19` completed 358 functions with 0 failed and 24 unsupported, but reported 354 behavioral and 4 error-only functions at `--max-iterations 1`.
- A targeted Zolem scan of `internal/runtime/store.go` with `--max-iterations 20` completed 22 functions with 0 failed/unsupported, but still reported 0% coverage and no thrown error for validation functions that should reject invalid inputs.
- Example evidence from `/tmp/zolem-runtime-20.json`: `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/runtime/store.go::ValidateLoopbackAddr` was explored with inputs including `""`, `"192.168.1.42"`, and `" "`; every discovered input reported `return_value: null`, `thrown_error: null`, and `lines_executed: []`.

Current code facts:
- `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go` `writeCall` currently emits `_result, _ := call` for multi-return targets by creating blank assignments for every result after the first, then emits `return _result, nil`. This drops the conventional trailing `error` from `(T, error)`.
- The same `writeCall` path emits `_result := call` and `return _result, nil` for single-result targets. For `func F(...) error`, this returns a non-nil target error as the wrapper's ordinary return value rather than as the wrapper's `error`.
- `shatter-go/build/instrumented_overlay.go` already maps a non-nil `_invokeErr` from `ShatterInvoke` into `ThrownError` with `ErrorType: "function_error"`, so the wrapper should pass target-returned errors through `_invokeErr` when the target's return shape includes a conventional error result.
- Zolem source confirms the observed inputs should not be all-successful: `internal/runtime/store.go` `validateLoopbackAddr` returns errors for malformed `host:port` values and non-loopback hosts, and `ValidateLoopbackAddr` returns that helper's error directly.

Desired behavior:
- For single-result targets whose result type is `error`, generated wrappers should return `(nil, err)` when the target returns a non-nil error and `(nil, nil)` when it returns nil.
- For multi-result targets whose final result type is `error`, generated wrappers should return `(primaryResult, nil)` when the error is nil and `(nil or primaryResult, err)` when the error is non-nil, using the existing `_invokeErr` path so scan reports expose `thrown_error: function_error`.
- Non-error multi-result functions should keep their existing compile-safe behavior unless intentionally expanded in a separate issue.

Acceptance checks:
- Add a failing Go wrapper regression test before the fix. The test must exercise at least `func Validate(s string) error` and `func Parse(s string) (int, error)` through generated `ShatterInvoke`, and assert non-nil returned target errors become the `error` return from `ShatterInvoke`.
- After the fix, the focused regression test passes.
- `go test ./...` passes in `shatter-go`.
- A targeted Zolem scan for `internal/runtime/store.go` shows invalid `ValidateLoopbackAddr` inputs no longer appear as `return_value: null`, `thrown_error: null` successes.

In scope:
- Go wrapper generation and directly related Go wrapper tests.
- Generator hash/version update if generated wrapper output changes.

Out of scope:
- Broad input-generation strategy changes.
- Broad Zolem source changes.
- New multi-return JSON output schema for non-error secondary return values.
notes: Merge 97c0bc67180e74cb192f1ef37c910790e263ae43 landed the Go wrapper/protocol error-return fix. The ValidateLoopbackAddr acceptance symptom remains open because execution currently returns skipped_by_policy before the target error can surface in scan reports; follow-up str-0vko tracks that policy-skip reporting gap.

title: CompiledModule fields stay nil
description:
Title: CompiledModule fields stay nil

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,wrapper,zolem,regression

## Symptom

After landing Shatter `main` commit `6bfcaa1c` (`bd sync: close str-yppa`),
a fresh whole-corpus Zolem scan completed all executable functions but still
classified 6 functions as `error_only`.

Four of the remaining rows share one Shatter-side shape: generated JSON inputs
assign scalar/string values to a Go struct field whose type is
`fixture.CompiledModule` or `*fixture.CompiledModule`. Go's typed
`encoding/json` decode cannot unmarshal those values into the generated wrapper
parameter, so execution never reaches the target behavior.

Evidence from `/tmp/zolem-main-str-yppa-scan.json`:

- `internal/fixture/template.go::templateContext`:
  `function_error: param f: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field Fixture.Module of type fixture.CompiledModule`
- `internal/fixture/matcher.go::(*Matcher).Swap`:
  `function_error: param fixtures: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field Fixture.Module of type fixture.CompiledModule`
- `internal/fixture/template.go::ValidateTemplate`:
  `function_error: param f: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field Fixture.Module of type fixture.CompiledModule`
- `internal/provider/openai/handler.go::renderFixtureBodyBytes`:
  `function_error: param f: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field Fixture.Module of type fixture.CompiledModule`

The same scan reported `358 completed`, `0 failed`, `24 unsupported`,
`352 completed_with_behavior`, `6 completed_error_only`, and
`24.3680485338726` overall coverage.

## Current Code Facts

- Zolem defines `internal/fixture.Fixture` in
  `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/fixture/fixture.go`; its `Module` field
  is `*CompiledModule` and is documented as nil when no `match.wasm` is
  present.
- Zolem defines `internal/fixture.CompiledModule` in
  `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/fixture/wasm.go`; it wraps an unexported
  `wazero.CompiledModule` field and is not JSON-representable.
- Shatter's Go analyzer has special handling for `CompiledModule` in
  `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go` so the type is recognized as
  `wazero.CompiledModule` rather than a generic opaque blocker.
- Shatter's runtime-value registry in `shatter-go/runtimeval/registry.go`
  contains a constructor expression for `wazero.CompiledModule`.
- Shatter planner tests in `shatter-go/planner/composite_test.go` already cover
  expression-based planning for `wazero.CompiledModule` and
  `fixture.CompiledModule` fields.
- The failure still occurs in generated wrapper typed decoding: random JSON
  reaches `json.Unmarshal(raw, &param)` with a non-null value at a nested
  `Fixture.Module` field before target execution.

## Reproduction

From a landed Shatter main worktree with `target/debug/shatter` built and Zolem
checked out at `/home/ketan/project/zolem`, run a focused scan:

```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/zolem-compiled-module-artifacts \
SHATTER_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/zolem-compiled-module-cache \
SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR=/tmp/zolem-compiled-module-seeds \
target/debug/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --include internal/fixture/template.go \
  --include internal/fixture/matcher.go \
  --include internal/provider/openai/handler.go \
  --all \
  --resume off \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 300 \
  --timeout-per-fn 60 \
  --timeout-explore 45 \
  --request-timeout 60 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 60 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false \
  --progress \
  --color never \
  --format json \
  --fail-on-failures=0 \
  -o /tmp/zolem-compiled-module-scan.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

Then inspect `/tmp/zolem-compiled-module-scan.json` for the four affected
functions above.

## Required Behavior

Generated Go wrappers should not feed non-null JSON values into nested fields
whose Go type is satisfied by Shatter runtime-value handling and cannot be
represented in JSON, specifically `fixture.CompiledModule` /
`wazero.CompiledModule`. Those fields should decode as nil/zero or be replaced
by the existing runtime-value expression before target execution, while ordinary
sibling fields still decode from the generated JSON input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a failing Go-side regression test first for a generated wrapper target
  whose input struct contains a nested `*CompiledModule`-like field plus at
  least one ordinary sibling field. The pre-fix behavior must fail during
  `json.Unmarshal` with a `cannot unmarshal ... into Go struct field ...`
  error for that field.
- Implement the smallest Shatter-side fix so generated wrappers leave nested
  `fixture.CompiledModule` / `wazero.CompiledModule` fields nil/zero or bind
  them through the existing runtime-value mechanism before typed unmarshal.
- Preserve ordinary sibling fields and existing normalizers for map sentinels,
  `time.Time`, and function-valued fields.
- Run focused Go wrapper/planner tests for the new behavior and adjacent
  normalizer paths.
- Run `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` under `shatter-go`.
- Re-run the focused Zolem scan above and confirm the four affected functions
  are no longer `error_only` from `Fixture.Module` / `CompiledModule` JSON
  decode errors.

## In Scope

- Go generated wrapper normalization or runtime-value binding for nested
  `fixture.CompiledModule` / `wazero.CompiledModule` fields.
- Tests that prove the opaque module field stays nil/zero or is runtime-bound
  while ordinary sibling fields still decode.

## Out of Scope

- Zolem feature-code changes.
- General synthesis of arbitrary opaque resource values.
- The remaining nil-pointer target panics from
  `cmd/zolemc/main.go::flagWasSet` and
  `internal/fixture/wasm_selector.go::newWASMSelector`.

title: Go func fields stay nil
description:
Title: Go func fields stay nil

## Symptom

After landing Shatter main commit `25adf3b2` (`bd sync: close str-hhly`), a fresh Zolem corpus scan completed all executable functions but still classified 7 functions as `error_only`.

Two remaining errors have the same Shatter-side shape: generated JSON inputs assign scalar values to Go struct fields whose type is a function. Go's typed `encoding/json` decode cannot unmarshal those values into `func` fields, so execution never reaches the target behavior.

Evidence from `/tmp/zolem-main-str-hhly-scan.json`:

- `cmd/zolemc/main.go::flagWasSet` has `function_error: param fs: json: cannot unmarshal number into Go struct field FlagSet.Usage of type func()`.
- `internal/admincli/admincli.go::NewClient` has `function_error: param httpClient: json: cannot unmarshal bool into Go struct field Client.CheckRedirect of type func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error`.

The same scan command reported `358 completed`, `0 failed`, `24 unsupported`, and `7 completed_error_only`. The earlier rounded-number failures from `templateContext`, `ValidateTemplate`, and `ineligibilityReasons` are now behavioral with no thrown error.

## Current Code Facts

- `flagWasSet` takes a `*flag.FlagSet`; the stdlib `flag.FlagSet` type includes `Usage func()`.
- `NewClient` takes an `*http.Client`; the stdlib `http.Client` type includes `CheckRedirect func(req *http.Request, via []*http.Request) error`.
- Function values cannot be represented by JSON. For Shatter's Go wrapper path, function-valued struct fields should be left absent or decoded as nil rather than receiving synthesized bool/number/string/object values.
- The likely Shatter implementation surface is `shatter-go/planner/aggregate.go`, where `PlanAggregate` synthesizes value plans for slices, maps, and structs, with final typed decode happening in generated wrappers from `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go`.
- Top-level function-typed parameters already have fallback planner coverage in `shatter-go/planner/fallback_test.go` (`TestPlanParam_Func_EmitsNil`). This issue is specifically about function-valued fields nested inside otherwise synthesizable structs.
- Existing wrapper regression tests live under `shatter-go/wrapper/`; existing planner/input synthesis tests live under `shatter-go/planner/`. A focused test command should target the package that receives the new regression, for example `go test ./planner -run '<new test name>' -count=1` and/or `go test ./wrapper -run '<new test name>' -count=1`.
- This should be handled in Shatter, not by changing Zolem feature code.

## Reproduction

From a landed Shatter main worktree with `target/debug/shatter` built and Zolem checked out at `/home/ketan/project/zolem`, run a focused scan:

```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/zolem-func-field-artifacts \
SHATTER_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/zolem-func-field-cache \
SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR=/tmp/zolem-func-field-seeds \
target/debug/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --include cmd/zolemc/main.go \
  --include internal/admincli/admincli.go \
  --all \
  --resume off \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 300 \
  --timeout-per-fn 60 \
  --timeout-explore 45 \
  --request-timeout 60 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 60 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false \
  --progress \
  --color never \
  --format json \
  --fail-on-failures=0 \
  -o /tmp/zolem-func-field-scan.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

Then inspect `/tmp/zolem-func-field-scan.json` for `flagWasSet` and `NewClient`.

## Required Behavior

Generated Go inputs and wrappers must not emit non-null JSON values for function-valued fields nested inside otherwise synthesizable struct inputs. Those fields should remain nil/absent so typed JSON decoding can succeed and the target function can execute.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a failing Go-side regression test first for a generated wrapper target whose input struct contains a `func` field plus at least one ordinary field. The pre-fix behavior must fail with `json: cannot unmarshal ... into Go struct field ... of type func...`.
- Implement the smallest Shatter-side fix so generated Go inputs leave function-valued struct fields nil/absent while preserving ordinary sibling fields.
- Add coverage for a pointer-to-struct input or stdlib-like struct shape so the fix covers `*flag.FlagSet` / `*http.Client`-style parameters, not only an anonymous flat struct.
- Run focused Go wrapper/input-generation tests for the new behavior.
- Run `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` under `shatter-go`.
- Re-run the focused Zolem scan above and confirm `flagWasSet` and `NewClient` are no longer `error_only` from function-field JSON decode errors.

## In Scope

- Shatter Go input synthesis and/or generated wrapper normalization behavior for function-valued struct fields.
- Tests that prove function fields remain nil/absent while sibling fields still decode.

## Out of Scope

- Zolem feature-code changes.
- General support for synthesizing callable Go function values.
- The other 5 remaining `error_only` rows from `/tmp/zolem-main-str-hhly-scan.json`, including `fixture.CompiledModule` decode errors and nil pointer panics.

title: Go normalizers preserve large numbers
description:
## Symptom

After landing `str-e07l` on Shatter main at merge `c2780df04503712037ad1f36d5a9a5d3474cf59a`, a whole-corpus Zolem scan still completed all executable functions but showed new parameter decode errors in functions whose inputs combine Shatter wrapper normalization with large integer fields.

Examples from `/tmp/zolem-main-c2780df-scan.json`:

- `internal/fixture/template.go::templateContext` became `error_only` with `function_error: param f: json: cannot unmarshal number 18446744073709552000 into Go struct field Fixture.TemplateSeed of type uint64`.
- `internal/fixture/template.go::ValidateTemplate` failed the same way.
- `internal/ollama/client.go::ineligibilityReasons` failed with `json: cannot unmarshal number 9223372036854776000 into Go struct field modelInfo.ContextLength of type int`.

The printed input values include exact boundary integers such as `18446744073709551615` and `9223372036854775807`, but the error messages show rounded JSON numbers. That indicates wrapper-side JSON normalization is decoding through `interface{}` with default `float64` numbers and then re-marshaling, which changes integer lexemes before the final typed `json.Unmarshal`.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go` now emits `shatterNormalizeTimeInput` for parameters whose Go type tree contains `time.Time`.
- The existing `shatterNormalizeMapInput` and the new `shatterNormalizeTimeInput` both call `json.Unmarshal(raw, &decoded)` into `any` and then `json.Marshal(normalized)`.
- Go's default `encoding/json` decoding into `any` represents JSON numbers as `float64`, which cannot preserve all large `int64`/`uint64` boundary values exactly.
- The whole-corpus scan command that exposed this issue was run from landed main with `--max-iterations 1`, output `/tmp/zolem-main-c2780df-scan.json`, and produced 358 completed / 0 failed / 24 unsupported / 10 error_only with overall coverage `27.30030333670374`.

## Focused Reproduction Command

This repo expects the Zolem checkout at `/home/ketan/project/zolem`. From a Shatter worktree with `target/debug/shatter` built, run:

```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/zolem-template-number-artifacts \
SHATTER_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/zolem-template-number-cache \
SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR=/tmp/zolem-template-number-seeds \
target/debug/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --include internal/fixture/template.go \
  --all \
  --resume off \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 300 \
  --timeout-per-fn 60 \
  --timeout-explore 45 \
  --request-timeout 60 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 60 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false \
  --progress \
  --color never \
  --format json \
  --fail-on-failures=0 \
  -o /tmp/zolem-template-number-scan.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

Then inspect `/tmp/zolem-template-number-scan.json` for the entry whose `file_path` ends with `internal/fixture/template.go` and whose `function_name` is `templateContext`.

## Required Behavior

Generated Go wrapper normalizers must preserve JSON number lexemes while normalizing map sentinels or date/date_time complex markers. Normalization must not turn valid large integer inputs into rounded values that typed Go `json.Unmarshal` rejects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a failing wrapper regression test first in `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper_duration_test.go` for a generated wrapper target like `func SeedAfterDate(cfg struct{ Now time.Time; Seed uint64 }) uint64 { return cfg.Seed }`, invoked with `{"Now":{"__complex_type":"date","value":2147483647000},"Seed":18446744073709551615}`. The pre-fix runner should fail with `json: cannot unmarshal number 18446744073709552000 into Go struct field .Seed of type uint64` or the same rounded-number error wrapped with the parameter name.
- Implement the smallest wrapper-side fix so generated normalizers preserve large JSON number lexemes while still converting date/date_time markers and map sentinel objects.
- Add or update focused map-normalizer coverage in `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper_test.go` so map sentinel normalization also preserves a large integer value in the same input object.
- Run focused wrapper tests:
  - `go test ./wrapper -run 'TestWrapper_StructWithTimeFieldAcceptsDateMarker|TestWrapper_StructWithTimeFieldPreservesLargeInteger' -count=1`
  - `go test ./wrapper -run 'TestGeneratedWrapperNormalizesSentinelMapInput|TestGeneratedWrapperNormalizesSentinelMapInputInsideStruct|TestGeneratedWrapperPreservesKeyValueStructWithoutMap' -count=1`
  - `go test ./wrapper -run 'TestWrapper_(DurationParam|StructWithDurationField|DurationParam_RejectsInvalidObject)$' -count=1`
- Run `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` under `shatter-go`.
- Re-run the focused Zolem scan command above and confirm `internal/fixture/template.go::templateContext` is no longer `error_only` from rounded `TemplateSeed` decoding.

## In Scope

- Go generated wrapper JSON normalization helpers and wrapper tests.
- Preserving exact numeric JSON lexemes during wrapper-side normalization.

## Out of Scope

- Zolem feature-code changes.
- Broad changes to Rust input generation or exploration policy.
- Fixing unrelated nil pointer panics, Anthropic union shape errors, or unsupported opaque parameter types.

title: Go time fields decode dates
description:
## Symptom

A whole-corpus Go scan of Zolem on Shatter main at merge `ed22e83b80bd3c571c00b8cb0d5a60e189ec052f` completed all 358 executable functions but left `internal/fixture/template.go::templateContext` as `error_only` with:

`function_error: param input: Time.UnmarshalJSON: input is not a JSON string`

The failing input contains a nested `time.Time` field encoded by Shatter as a complex date marker:

```json
{"Now":{"__complex_type":"date","value":2147483647000}}
```

Go `encoding/json` expects `time.Time` values to decode from JSON strings, so the generated wrapper rejects the input before the target function can execute.

## Focused Reproduction Command

This repo expects the Zolem checkout at `/home/ketan/project/zolem`. From a Shatter worktree with `target/debug/shatter` built, run:

```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/zolem-template-time-artifacts \
SHATTER_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/zolem-template-time-cache \
SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR=/tmp/zolem-template-time-seeds \
target/debug/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --include internal/fixture/template.go \
  --all \
  --resume off \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 300 \
  --timeout-per-fn 60 \
  --timeout-explore 45 \
  --request-timeout 60 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 60 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false \
  --progress \
  --color never \
  --format json \
  --fail-on-failures=0 \
  -o /tmp/zolem-template-time-scan.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

Then inspect `/tmp/zolem-template-time-scan.json` for the entry whose `file_path` ends with `internal/fixture/template.go` and whose `function_name` is `templateContext`.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go` maps Go `time.Time` to `ComplexKind="date"`.
- `shatter-core/src/input_gen.rs` emits `ComplexKind::Date` and `ComplexKind::DateTime` as `{"__complex_type":"date","value":...}` when the frontend advertises support.
- `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go` currently has special wrapper-side decoding for top-level `time.Duration` and map sentinel normalization, but ordinary parameter decoding still calls `json.Unmarshal(raw, &param)` directly for structs that contain `time.Time` fields.
- `shatter-go/reconstruct/reconstruct.go` can convert date markers to `time.Time`, but the generated wrapper path does not use that reconstruction before typed `json.Unmarshal`.
- `internal/fixture/template.go::templateContext` copies `input.Now` into the returned `TemplateContext.Now`, so a focused scan can confirm the function executes after parameter decoding succeeds.

## Required Behavior

Generated Go wrappers should accept Shatter date/date_time complex markers when they appear inside typed parameters containing `time.Time`, converting them into a JSON shape that Go `time.Time` fields can unmarshal. This should happen before the target call and should not require any Zolem source changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a failing wrapper regression test first for a function like `func UnixMillis(cfg struct{ Now time.Time }) int64 { return cfg.Now.UnixMilli() }` invoked through the generated wrapper with `{"Now":{"__complex_type":"date","value":2147483647000}}`; verify it fails with the existing `Time.UnmarshalJSON: input is not a JSON string` behavior before the fix.
- Implement the smallest wrapper-side fix so that the regression reaches the target function and returns `2147483647000`.
- Preserve existing duration and map sentinel behavior; run the existing focused wrapper tests that cover those paths.
- Run `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` under `shatter-go`.
- Re-run the focused Zolem scan command above and confirm `internal/fixture/template.go::templateContext` is no longer `error_only` from parameter decoding.

## In Scope

- Go wrapper generation and wrapper type detection/normalization needed for typed `time.Time` fields.
- Focused tests in `shatter-go/wrapper` or adjacent Go wrapper test files.

## Out of Scope

- Zolem feature-code changes.
- Broad input-generation policy changes for every complex kind.
- Fixing unrelated remaining Zolem `error_only` functions such as nil pointer panics, negative length panics, Anthropic union decode shape, or OpenAPI typed string fields.

title: Go nested map sentinel inputs
description:
Title: Go nested map sentinel inputs

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,input-generation,zolem,coverage

## Symptom

After Shatter `main` commit `4c9aac4c574a036b83b433beafd66d1c05465e5d`,
a low-load whole-corpus Zolem scan completed without frontend failures but still
reported ten `error_only` functions and only 23.56% overall codebase coverage.

The scan command was:

```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/zolem-current-artifacts-4c9aac4 \
SHATTER_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/zolem-current-cache-4c9aac4 \
SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR=/tmp/zolem-current-seeds-4c9aac4 \
target/debug/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --resume off \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 1200 \
  --timeout-per-fn 60 \
  --timeout-explore 45 \
  --request-timeout 60 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 60 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false \
  --progress \
  --color never \
  --format json \
  --fail-on-failures=0 \
  -o /tmp/zolem-current-scan-4c9aac4.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

Summary from `/tmp/zolem-current-scan-4c9aac4.json`:

```text
total_discovered_functions: 382
attempted_functions: 358
completed_functions: 358
completed_with_behavior: 348
completed_error_only: 10
failed_functions: 0
unsupported_functions: 24
overall_coverage: 23.559150657229523
```

Several remaining `error_only` functions fail before handler/body execution
because generated `_key` / `_value` map sentinels appear inside struct fields,
not as the top-level parameter itself.

Representative failures:

```text
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/specs/discovery.go::schemaType
completion_outcome: error_only
coverage_pct: 0.0
thrown_error: function_error: param schema: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field discoverySchema.properties of type specs.discoverySchema
input excerpt:
{
  "Properties": {
    "_key": "0",
    "_value": {}
  }
}
```

```text
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/ollama/client.go::ineligibilityReasons
completion_outcome: error_only
coverage_pct: 0.0
thrown_error: function_error: param info: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field modelInfo.Capabilities of type bool
input excerpt:
{
  "Capabilities": {
    "_key": "test",
    "_value": true
  },
  "ContextLength": -925,
  "Name": "lcpszrrpluhxguof",
  "ParameterCount": 255
}
```

```text
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/fixture/static_selector.go::(staticSelector).Select
completion_outcome: error_only
coverage_pct: 0.0
thrown_error: function_error: param candidates: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field Fixture.Module of type fixture.CompiledModule
input excerpt:
[
  -1,
  {"Body": [], "Labels": {"_key": "true", "_value": "test"}, ...},
  [
    {"Tags": {"_key": "0", "_value": "true"}, ...}
  ]
]
```

## Current Code Facts

- `str-eh5g` fixed top-level Go map parameters by adding wrapper-side
  normalization in `shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go`.
- The current wrapper generator only calls `shatterNormalizeMapInput` for a
  parameter when `wrapperParamNeedsMapInputNormalizer` sees `map[` in the
  parameter's top-level Go type string.
- Struct parameters such as `discoverySchema`, `modelInfo`, and `Fixture` can
  contain map fields. Their top-level wrapper parameter type string does not
  contain `map[`, so their raw JSON input still reaches `encoding/json` with
  nested `_key` / `_value` sentinel objects.
- Go's `encoding/json` expects map fields to be normal JSON objects whose field
  names are map keys and whose values match the map value type.

## Desired Behavior

Go frontend execution should canonicalize generated map sentinels wherever they
appear in a parameter input tree when the target parameter or one of its nested
fields contains a Go map. Shatter should not feed nested `_key` / `_value`
objects into Go struct fields that are maps.

For the Zolem examples above, generated inputs should reach the function body
or produce target-level behavior observations instead of failing during
parameter reconstruction.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused regression for a Go function taking a struct parameter with a
  nested map field whose value type is a struct, proving generated sentinel map
  input is normalized before `json.Unmarshal`.
- Fix Go input reconstruction/generation so nested map sentinels inside struct,
  slice, array, pointer, or nullable parameter shapes are represented as normal
  JSON objects before Go unmarshalling.
- Preserve ordinary structs that legitimately contain `_key` and `_value`
  fields when they are not map sentinel payloads, or document and test the
  chosen heuristic if exact structural disambiguation is not currently
  available.
- Rerun a focused Zolem repro for at least `schemaType` or
  `ineligibilityReasons` and verify it no longer fails during parameter
  reconstruction due to nested map sentinel JSON.
- Run Go quality gates for touched code: `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` in
  `shatter-go/`.

## In Scope

- Go wrapper/input reconstruction for nested map fields.
- Focused Go frontend tests for nested maps inside structs and arrays/slices.
- Focused Zolem validation for at least one of the failing targets above.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Zolem feature-code changes.
- Solving all remaining low-coverage functions.
- Native construction of unrelated opaque values such as `fixture.CompiledModule`
  beyond avoiding nested map sentinel unmarshal failures in fields that are maps.
acceptance_criteria: Nested-map Go regression passes; focused Zolem schemaType or ineligibilityReasons no longer fails during nested map parameter reconstruction; go test ./... and go vet ./... pass in shatter-go

title: Go map inputs use key/value sentinel
description:
Title: Go map inputs use key/value sentinel

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,input-generation,zolem,coverage

## Symptom

After fixing `str-si7k`, a bounded whole-corpus Zolem validation scan from
Shatter `main` completed without failed functions, but still produced seven
`error_only` function entries and only about 28.4% overall coverage at
`--max-iterations 1`.

One of the clearest remaining Shatter input-shape failures is:

```text
/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/specs/discovery.go::collectDiscoveryMethods
completion_outcome: error_only
coverage_pct: 0.0
thrown_error: function_error: param resources: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type specs.discoveryResource
lines_executed: []
```

The discovered input for that function used a sentinel-style map shape:

```json
{
  "_key": "ytcvezulkygtjb",
  "_value": {
    "Methods": {
      "_key": "null",
      "_value": {
        "ID": "gdvnigb",
        "Request": {
          "Ref": "ynjbmksdait"
        }
      }
    },
    "Resources": {
      "_key": "test",
      "_value": {}
    }
  }
}
```

Go then unmarshaled that JSON directly into
`map[string]discoveryResource`. The JSON object field `_key` became a real map
entry whose value is the string `"ytcvezulkygtjb"`, which cannot unmarshal into
`discoveryResource`.

## Reproduction

Build current Shatter `main`, then run a focused low-load Zolem scan:

```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/zolem-go-map-input-artifacts \
SHATTER_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/zolem-go-map-input-cache \
SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR=/tmp/zolem-go-map-input-seeds \
target/debug/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --include 'internal/specs/discovery.go' \
  --resume off \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 300 \
  --timeout-per-fn 60 \
  --timeout-explore 45 \
  --request-timeout 60 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 60 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false \
  --progress \
  --color never \
  --format json \
  --fail-on-failures=0 \
  -o /tmp/zolem-go-map-input-scan.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

Inspect the result:

```bash
jq -r '.functions[]
  | select(.function_name == "collectDiscoveryMethods")
  | {completion_outcome, coverage_pct, discovered_inputs}' \
  /tmp/zolem-go-map-input-scan.json
```

Expected current behavior: `collectDiscoveryMethods` is `error_only`, has no
executed lines, and the thrown error contains
`json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type specs.discoveryResource`.

## Current Code Facts

- Zolem `internal/specs/discovery.go` defines:

  ```go
  type discoveryResource struct {
      Methods   map[string]discoveryMethod   `json:"methods"`
      Resources map[string]discoveryResource `json:"resources"`
  }

  func collectDiscoveryMethods(resources map[string]discoveryResource) map[string]discoveryMethod
  ```

- The target parameter is a normal Go map: `map[string]discoveryResource`.
- Go's `encoding/json` expects map JSON as an object whose field names are map
  keys and whose field values are `discoveryResource` JSON objects.
- The observed Shatter-generated input uses `_key` / `_value` sentinel fields
  for maps instead of producing an object like:

  ```json
  {
    "resourceName": {
      "methods": {
        "methodName": {
          "id": "method-id",
          "request": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Request"}
        }
      },
      "resources": {}
    }
  }
  ```

## Desired Behavior

Go frontend execution should reconstruct generated map inputs into JSON that
`encoding/json` can unmarshal into Go map parameters. Shatter should not feed
`_key` / `_value` sentinel objects directly into Go map arguments.

For this Zolem target, at least one generated input should reach
`collectDiscoveryMethods` body lines and produce a behavior observation instead
of failing during parameter reconstruction.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Shatter regression for a Go function taking a map parameter
  with struct values, proving generated map inputs execute past parameter
  reconstruction.
- Fix Go input reconstruction or generation so map inputs are represented as
  normal JSON objects for Go map parameters.
- Rerun the focused Zolem repro above and verify
  `internal/specs/discovery.go::collectDiscoveryMethods` is no longer
  `error_only` due to `_key` / `_value` map JSON.
- Run Go quality gates for the touched code (`go test ./...` and `go vet ./...`
  in `shatter-go/`).

## In Scope

- Go map parameter input generation or reconstruction.
- Focused Go frontend tests for map inputs.
- Focused Zolem validation for `collectDiscoveryMethods`.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Zolem feature-code changes.
- Solving all remaining Zolem coverage gaps.
- Native factories for unrelated opaque values such as `*flag.FlagSet`,
  `fixture.CompiledModule`, or WebSocket connections.
acceptance_criteria: Map-parameter Go regression passes; focused Zolem collectDiscoveryMethods no longer fails during map parameter reconstruction; go test ./... and go vet ./... pass in shatter-go
