```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
ZOLEM_SHATTER_REPO_WRITE_GUARD=/home/ketan/project/zolem/.shatter/sandbox-host-write-guard.codex-current \
ZOLEM_SHATTER_TMP_WRITE_GUARD=/tmp/zolem-shatter-sandbox-host-write-guard.codex-current \
target/debug/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --resume off \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --workers-per-fn 1 \
  --scheduler-policy serial \
  --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-total 900 \
  --timeout-per-fn 60 \
  --timeout-explore 45 \
  --request-timeout 60 \
  --exec-timeout 10 \
  --build-timeout 60 \
  --no-cache \
  --no-seeds \
  --set llm.enabled=false \
  --progress \
  --color never \
  --format json \
  --fail-on-failures=0 \
  -o /tmp/zolem-current-scan-1iter.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

The scan discovered 382 functions, attempted 358, completed 355, failed 3, and
reported 24 unsupported targets. The failed functions were:

- `/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/local_admin.go::handleListenerCalls`
- `/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/local_admin.go::handleListenerResource`
- `/home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem/local_admin.go::handleProfileResource`

All three failures had the same launcher build shape:

```text
error: exploration error: unexpected response from frontend: execute error (InternalError): adapter go/http-handler invoke failed: http handler execution: build adapter launcher: launcher: go build: exit status 1
.shatter-launchers/<id>/main.go:13:2: found packages main (integration_helpers_test.go) and shattertarget (local_admin.go) in /home/ketan/project/zolem/cmd/zolem
.shatter-launchers/<id>/main.go:13:2: import "zolem.dev/zolem/cmd/zolem" is a program, not an importable package
```

## Current Code Facts

- The failing zolem targets are in `cmd/zolem/local_admin.go`, which belongs to
  package `main`.
- The Go toolchain rejects importing `zolem.dev/zolem/cmd/zolem` because it is a
  command package, so a generated launcher for package-main targets cannot use
  ordinary import-based invocation.
- The failure happens in Shatter's Go HTTP handler adapter launcher path, after
  target discovery and scheduling have already accepted these functions.
- The same validation run successfully completed receiver-method HTTP handler
  targets in importable internal packages, including provider handlers under
  `internal/provider/...`.

## Desired Behavior

Go HTTP-handler execution should handle package-main targets without generating
an import of the command package. Shatter should either execute the target via a
same-package overlay launcher or classify the target as unsupported with a clear
reason before execution. It should not fail the scan with an InternalError
caused by `import ".../cmd/..." is a program, not an importable package`.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused regression covering a Go HTTP handler target in a `package main`
  directory that would fail if the launcher imports the command package.
- Make the regression pass by executing package-main HTTP handler targets or by
  producing a deterministic unsupported classification before execution.
- Rebuild Shatter and rerun a focused zolem repro for at least one failing
  target, such as
  `cmd/zolem/local_admin.go::handleProfileResource`.
- Rerun the bounded zolem whole-corpus scan above and verify these three targets
  no longer appear as failed InternalError entries.

## In Scope

- Go frontend or orchestrator launcher generation for HTTP handler targets in
  `package main`.
- Focused regression tests for command-package HTTP handler execution or
  classification.
- Revalidation against zolem using external output/cache paths and low
  parallelism.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial zolem feature-code changes.
- Broad input-generation improvements needed to raise zolem coverage after the
  execution failure is removed.
- Opaque parameter support for the 24 currently unsupported zolem targets.
acceptance_criteria: Package-main Go HTTP handler regression exists and passes; focused zolem repro for cmd/zolem/local_admin.go::handleProfileResource no longer fails with command-package import InternalError; bounded zolem whole-corpus scan no longer reports the three local_admin.go HTTP handler targets as failed InternalError entries.

title: Concolic native seeds run first
description:
Title: Concolic native seeds run first

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,axum,concolic,pickpackit,scan

## Symptom

After `str-itp2` landed, a Pickpackit `src/handlers` scan from Shatter `main`
now produces behavior maps for most Rust/Axum handlers, but two handlers still
record `dispatch_failed` with zero observations:

```text
create_bundle  dispatch_failed  no successful observations recorded after 5 attempted execution(s)
update_person  dispatch_failed  no successful observations recorded after 5 attempted execution(s)
```

The scan output was:

```text
/var/tmp/pickpackit-main-str-itp2-handlers-1iter/report.json
```

Relevant aggregate result from that report:

```text
70 behavior-map entries
2 dispatch_failed entries: create_bundle, update_person
```

Both failing handlers are normal Axum handlers with native generator-backed
`State<AppState>` and `CurrentAccount` params:

```rust
pub async fn create_bundle(
    State(state): State<AppState>,
    current: CurrentAccount,
    Path(workspace_id): Path<Uuid>,
    Json(payload): Json<CreateBundleRequest>,
) -> ApiResult<Json<BundleDetail>>

pub async fn update_person(
    State(state): State<AppState>,
    current: CurrentAccount,
    Path((workspace_id, person_id)): Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
    Json(payload): Json<UpdatePersonRequest>,
) -> ApiResult<Json<Person>>
```

## Smallest Known Reproduction

From the Pickpackit API validation worktree:

```bash
cd /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api

env \
  DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
  SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust-runtime \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter \
  scan src/handlers \
    --project-dir . \
    --language rust \
    --require-rust \
    --concolic \
    --timeout-total 3600 \
    --timeout-per-fn 300 \
    --timeout-explore 240 \
    --request-timeout 300 \
    --exec-timeout 240 \
    --build-timeout 300 \
    --max-iterations 1 \
    --parallelism 1 \
    --progress \
    --color never \
    --no-seeds \
    --no-cache \
    --format json \
    --fail-on-failures=0 \
    -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-main-str-itp2-handlers-1iter/report.json
```

Then inspect:

```bash
jq -r '.functions[]
  | select(.completion_outcome != "behavioral")
  | [.function_name, .completion_outcome, .completion_reason]
  | @tsv' /var/tmp/pickpackit-main-str-itp2-handlers-1iter/report.json
```

Expected current failing rows:

```text
create_bundle  dispatch_failed  no successful observations recorded after 5 attempted execution(s); frontend likely skipped or rejected every execute attempt
update_person  dispatch_failed  no successful observations recorded after 5 attempted execution(s); frontend likely skipped or rejected every execute attempt
```

If the local paths above are stale, recreate the environment from current
`main` rather than depending on the original session:

```bash
# Shatter
cd /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi
git checkout main
git pull --ff-only origin main
cargo build --bin shatter

# Pickpackit validation database
cd /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation
docker compose up -d postgres
env DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
  cargo run --manifest-path api/Cargo.toml --bin pickpackit-migrate
```

Then rebuild Pickpackit's custom Rust frontend before scanning:

```bash
cd /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api
env SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter \
  build-frontend rust \
    --project-dir . \
    --config .shatter \
    --output .shatter-cache/bin \
    --color never
```

## Current Code Facts

- Pickpackit `.shatter/config.yaml` defines default native generators:
  - `generators.State: generators/pickpackit.rs`
  - `generators.CurrentAccount: generators/pickpackit.rs`
  - `param_generators.current: generators/pickpackit.rs`
- `.shatter/generators/pickpackit.rs` exports `State`, `CurrentAccount`, and
  `current`; `CurrentAccount` returns a native replay marker with a seeded
  `workspace_id` and an `axum.path` hint.
- Focused `explore` runs for these functions show the adapter-level rejection
  when a candidate reaches execute without native replay input for
  `CurrentAccount`:

```text
frontend error during execute: axum handler has unsupported extractor types: CurrentAccount
```

- In `shatter-rust/src/adapters.rs`, `execute_adapter_owned` rejects
  `AxumExtractorKind::Unsupported` params unless the corresponding input slot
  is a native replay marker.
- In `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs`,
  `observe_with_optional_concolic` currently builds concolic inputs in this
  order:
  - `seed_inputs = boundary_dict::generate_boundary_inputs(&analysis.params)`
  - `user_inputs = user_seeds + candidate_inputs`
  - `generated_inputs = prefetch_concolic_generator_inputs(...)`
  - `user_inputs.extend(generated_inputs)`
- The same function sets `max_executions` to `max_iterations * 5`. With
  `--max-iterations 1`, invalid built-in boundary seeds for native Axum params
  can consume all 5 executions before generated native seeds are observed.
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` already has a unit test named
  `concolic_generator_inputs_seed_custom_values`, but it only proves generated
  native inputs can be produced. It does not prove concolic scan prioritizes
  generated native seeds ahead of invalid built-in boundary seeds.

## Desired Behavior

For concolic scans of functions with custom/native generator-backed params,
Shatter should execute generated native seed inputs before invalid built-in
boundary inputs can exhaust the small execution budget. Pickpackit
`create_bundle` and `update_person` should produce behavior maps rather than
`dispatch_failed`.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Shatter test showing concolic scan/orchestration orders native
  generator seed inputs before generic boundary seeds, or otherwise guarantees
  at least one native generated input is executed for a function with native
  generator-backed params under `max_iterations = 1`.
- The focused Pickpackit repro for `create_bundle` and `update_person` no
  longer produces `dispatch_failed`.
- A `src/handlers` Pickpackit scan with `--max-iterations 1` produces behavior
  maps for these two handlers.
- Existing Rust frontend tests pass, including the Axum custom extractor tests
  added for `str-itp2`.
- Rust clippy passes with `-D warnings`.

## Scope

In scope:

- Concolic scan input ordering and execution budget handling for
  native/custom-generator params.
- Rust/Axum behavior where invalid JSON boundary seeds currently run before
  native replay seeds.
- Focused tests in Shatter plus Pickpackit validation.

Out of scope:

- Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Broad branch coverage improvement beyond ensuring generated native seeds are
  actually observed.
- Go smoke observe timeout work; that is tracked separately by `str-aof7`.
acceptance_criteria: Native/custom generator-backed concolic inputs execute before invalid boundary seeds can exhaust max_iterations=1; Pickpackit create_bundle and update_person produce behavior maps; Rust tests and clippy pass.

title: Pickpackit apply_bundle timeout
description:
Title: Pickpackit apply_bundle timeout

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,axum,pickpackit,scan,timeout

## Symptom

After `str-itp2` landed, Shatter can execute the Pickpackit `session`
custom-extractor endpoint and most Pickpackit Rust/Axum handlers, but a
whole-handler scan still fails one handler:

```text
Scan complete: 72 completed, 1 failed, 0 unsupported, 2 skipped (1 worker(s))

Errors:
- /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api/src/handlers/bundles.rs::apply_bundle: timed out during task after 605s
```

The scan wrote its completed-function report to:

```text
/var/tmp/pickpackit-main-str-itp2-handlers-1iter/report.json
```

That report contains 72 completed function behavior maps. It does not contain
`apply_bundle`, because the task timed out before producing a completed entry.

## Reproduction

Use the Pickpackit validation worktree:

```text
repo root: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation
api cwd:   /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api
```

From the Pickpackit repo root, start the shared validation database if needed:

```bash
docker compose up -d postgres
DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit make api-migrate
```

The local Pickpackit docs map Postgres to host port `55432`. Then build
Shatter and the Pickpackit custom Rust frontend from current Shatter `main`.
The commands below use `/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi`;
substitute the current Shatter checkout/worktree path if different:

```bash
cargo build -p shatter-cli
cargo build --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml

env PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug:/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust/target/debug:$PATH \
  DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust \
  SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust-runtime \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter build-frontend rust
```

Then run a focused reproduction from the Pickpackit API cwd:

```bash
env PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug:/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust/target/debug:$PATH \
  DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust \
  SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/shatter-rust-runtime \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/main-land-str-puqi/target/debug/shatter scan src/handlers/bundles.rs \
    --project-dir . \
    --language rust --require-rust --concolic \
    --include '**/bundles.rs' \
    --timeout-total 1200 --timeout-per-fn 300 --timeout-explore 240 \
    --request-timeout 300 --exec-timeout 240 --build-timeout 300 \
    --max-iterations 1 --parallelism 1 \
    --progress --color never --no-seeds --no-cache --format json \
    --fail-on-failures=0 --log-level info \
    -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-apply-bundle-timeout/report.json
```

If the focused command does not select only `apply_bundle`, add the function
target explicitly:

```bash
src/handlers/bundles.rs:apply_bundle
```

## Current Code Facts

Pickpackit `api/src/handlers/bundles.rs` defines:

```rust
pub async fn apply_bundle(
    State(state): State<AppState>,
    current: CurrentAccount,
    Path((workspace_id, bundle_id)): Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
    Json(payload): Json<ApplyBundleRequest>,
) -> ApiResult<Json<ApplyBundleResponse>>
```

`ApplyBundleRequest` contains:

```rust
pub struct ApplyBundleRequest {
    pub trip_id: Uuid,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub entry_keys: Option<Vec<Uuid>>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub preparation_task_keys: Option<Vec<Uuid>>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "deserialize_three_state_uuid")]
    pub person_override: ThreeState,
}
```

The handler opens a SQLx transaction, validates workspace/trip/bundle/person
relationships, loads bundle item/task/preparation rows, filters optional entry
and preparation-task IDs, inserts `trip_packing_items` and `trip_tasks`, commits,
and returns `ApplyBundleResponse`.

The latest successful whole-handler scan also proves adjacent Pickpackit
surfaces now work:

- `session.rs::session` completed with one path, HTTP 200 account JSON, and 33%
  coverage.
- `item_images.rs::upload_item_image` completed with one path and a generated
  multipart/image native replay input.
- Most other `State<AppState> + CurrentAccount + Path/Json` handlers completed
  with one path and nonzero coverage.

The two skipped functions in that scan are known direct `&PgPool` helpers:

- `legs.rs::fetch_legs_for_workspace`
- `tasks.rs::fetch_tasks_for_workspace`

Those are already tracked by `str-02br` and are not part of this issue.

## Desired Behavior

Shatter should handle the `apply_bundle` handler without allowing one
function-level task to run for about 605 seconds and fail the whole Pickpackit
handler scan. Acceptable outcomes include:

- `apply_bundle` executes and produces a behavior-map entry; or
- Shatter records a controlled timeout/skip/failure for `apply_bundle` within
  the configured per-function/task timeout and still writes aggregate outputs
  promptly.

The broader Pickpackit scan should not require an external process killer or
lose already-completed behavior maps because one DB-heavy Axum handler has a
large search/task surface.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Shatter regression for a Rust/Axum handler or scan task that
  previously could overrun the configured per-function/task budget.
- Fix the timeout/accounting or input/task bounding path so `apply_bundle` no
  longer fails as `timed out during task after 605s` in a one-iteration
  Pickpackit handler scan.
- Re-run a focused Pickpackit `bundles.rs::apply_bundle` scan and show it either
  completes behaviorally or produces controlled timeout/skip/failure accounting
  within the configured timeout.
- Re-run the Pickpackit `src/handlers` scan and show `apply_bundle` no longer
  appears as the sole long task timeout.
- Preserve the existing successful behavior for `session.rs::session` and other
  custom-extractor Axum handlers.
- `cargo test --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml`, Rust frontend clippy,
  `task smoke`, `task e2e`, and `task conformance` pass for the Shatter change.

## Scope

In scope:

- Shatter Rust/Axum scan task timeout/accounting for DB-backed handlers.
- Bounding concolic/task work for handler functions like `apply_bundle`.
- Focused Pickpackit validation using existing native generators and database
  setup.

Out of scope:

- Non-trivial Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- The direct `&PgPool` helper support tracked by `str-02br`.
- Broad branch-spread improvements beyond making this handler controlled and
  reportable.
- Deleting or weakening existing Pickpackit feature behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Focused apply_bundle scan no longer reports timed out during task after 605s; whole Pickpackit handlers scan records apply_bundle as completed or controlled promptly; listed Shatter gates pass.
close_reason: e2db5fe1 verified on main; no code change required; Pickpackit handlers scan /var/tmp/pickpackit-str-75hw-handlers-current/report.json completed 73, failed 0, unsupported 0, skipped 2 with apply_bundle behavioral

title: Go scan OpenAPI type blow-up
description:
Title: Go scan OpenAPI type blow-up

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,scan,timeout,memory

## Problem

After Zolem issue `zolem-n0a` added scan-only Wazero runtime value factories,
Shatter can dry-run more Zolem functions and can execute the newly unlocked
Wazero API functions. However, a whole-corpus Zolem scan still wedges in the
OpenAPI region and ignores the configured total/per-function timeouts while
memory grows until the run becomes unsafe.

This is a Shatter scan timeout/accounting and input/model-size bug, not a
Zolem Wazero factory bug.

## Current Facts

- Zolem root: `/home/ketan/project/zolem`
- Shatter root used for verification: `/home/ketan/project/shatter`
- Shatter checkout used for verification:
  - branch: `str-8124-clean`
  - commit: `5fe29abe3892c691adee0640eb324d67b604d82d`
- Zolem checkout used for verification:
  - branch: `main`
  - commit: `f8175d26b229b8e47bb312e5b4cecd95121c12c6`
- Zolem main includes `zolem-n0a` completion commits, including
  `2beab60 Add Shatter Wazero runtime value factories` and
  `f8175d2 Record zolem-n0a outcome`.
- Docker image used by the repro:
  `golang:1.26-bookworm`, local digest
  `golang@sha256:5d2b868674b57c9e48cdd39e891acce4196b6926ca6d11e9c270a8f85106203d`.
- Zolem `.shatter/config.yaml` now registers `go_runtime_values` for:
  - `fixture.CompiledModule`
  - `api.FunctionDefinition`
  - `api.Function`
- A fresh dry-run with Shatter release binary selected 331 functions and skipped
  32 unsupported functions, down from the old 34-skip baseline. The skipped
  set contained no `api.Function`, `api.FunctionDefinition`, `interface{}`,
  `any`, or `parse.Node` unsupported reason.
- A focused execution scan of `internal/wasmgen/generator.go` completed all 7
  selected functions with 0 failed, 0 unsupported, and 0 skipped. It completed
  the formerly unsupported Wazero functions:
  - `callU32`: 3 paths, 46% coverage
  - `validateSignature`: 6 paths, 39% coverage
- No Go frontend or Docker sandbox process was left after the focused Wazero
  scan.
- A smaller focused OpenAPI reproduction exists and is preferred over the
  whole-corpus command for implementation work. See the next section.

## Smallest Known Reproduction

Build Shatter release, then run:

```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/zolem-shatter-artifacts-n0a-openapi-focused \
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/zolem-shatter-harness-n0a-openapi-focused \
SHATTER_GO_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/tmp/shatter-go-workspaces-n0a-openapi-focused \
/home/ketan/project/shatter/target/release/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --no-cache \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --timeout-total 360 \
  --timeout-per-fn 120 \
  --timeout-explore 120 \
  --request-timeout 120 \
  --build-timeout 120 \
  --exec-timeout 30 \
  --include 'internal/specs/openapi.go' \
  --progress \
  --output /tmp/zolem-n0a-openapi-focused.md \
  --output /tmp/zolem-n0a-openapi-focused.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

Focused repro observed on the commits above:

- Shatter discovered 1 source file and selected 6 functions.
- It completed:
  - `loadOpenAPIDocument`
  - `supportedOpenAPIOperation`
  - `normalizeSchemaRef`
- It then started `lookupRequestSchema` as 4/6 at elapsed ~55s and produced no
  further progress.
- The process remained live past `--timeout-per-fn 120`, `--request-timeout 120`,
  and `--timeout-total 360`.
- At about 7m09s elapsed, process state was:
  - Shatter scan: ~2.18 GiB RSS, ~82% CPU
  - Docker sandbox command: ~30 MiB RSS, 0% CPU
  - Docker container `golang:1.26-bookworm`: alive but idle
- The outer `timeout 540` killed the command with exit code 124.
- Shatter wrote no aggregate outputs at `/tmp/zolem-n0a-openapi-focused.json`
  or `/tmp/zolem-n0a-openapi-focused.md`.
- After the outer timeout killed the process group, no matching Go frontend,
  harness, or Docker sandbox container remained.

This smaller repro is sufficient to investigate timeout/accounting and avoids
the unsafe whole-corpus memory growth described below.

## Whole-Corpus Reproduction

Build Shatter release, then run:

```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/zolem-shatter-artifacts-n0a-full \
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/zolem-shatter-harness-n0a-full \
SHATTER_GO_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/tmp/shatter-go-workspaces-n0a-full \
/home/ketan/project/shatter/target/release/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --no-cache \
  --parallelism 1 \
  --timeout-total 1800 \
  --timeout-per-fn 180 \
  --timeout-explore 180 \
  --request-timeout 180 \
  --build-timeout 180 \
  --exec-timeout 30 \
  --progress \
  --output /tmp/zolem-n0a-full.md \
  --output /tmp/zolem-n0a-full.json \
  /home/ketan/project/zolem
```

## Whole-Corpus Observed Behavior

- The run discovered 54 source files, included 208 unexported functions, skipped
  32 unsupported functions, and began scanning 331 functions.
- It completed through `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/specs/openapi.go::loadOpenAPIDocument`
  as function 277/331.
- It then started `/home/ketan/project/zolem/internal/specs/openapi.go::lookupRequestSchema`
  as function 278/331 and stopped making progress.
- The run remained alive well past the configured `--timeout-per-fn 180`,
  `--request-timeout 180`, and `--timeout-total 1800`.
- At roughly 32 minutes elapsed, process state was:
  - top-level Shatter scan: about 25.9 GiB RSS, about 58% CPU
  - Go frontend: about 5.6 GiB RSS, about 16% CPU
  - Docker sandbox command: still alive, 0% CPU
  - system memory: about 420 MiB free, about 4.4 GiB available, swap in use
- No aggregate outputs were written at `/tmp/zolem-n0a-full.json` or
  `/tmp/zolem-n0a-full.md`.
- The run had to be terminated to protect the machine. After termination, no
  matching Go frontend or Docker sandbox container remained.

## Expected Behavior

Shatter should not grow unbounded memory or remain live past the configured
scan timeout while processing a single Go function with a large static type
graph. One of these outcomes would be acceptable:

- `lookupRequestSchema` completes and the scan continues;
- `lookupRequestSchema` is failed or skipped with explicit timeout/model-size
  accounting and aggregate reports are written; or
- the whole scan aborts at `--timeout-total`, cleans up child processes, and
  writes final failure accounting.

## Likely Area

The stuck work appears to be in-process Shatter/Go frontend value or type-model
handling for large OpenAPI objects, not active Docker execution:

- Docker sandbox was idle at 0% CPU.
- Shatter and the Go frontend were the high-memory processes.
- The failure point was the same OpenAPI function region that previously
  exposed large generated `openapi3.T` value/type behavior.

## Acceptance Checks

- A whole-corpus Zolem scan with the reproduction command exits without manual
  intervention.
- The scan either completes or records timeout/model-size failure accounting for
  `lookupRequestSchema`.
- `--timeout-total 1800` is honored even when the active layer is doing
  expensive in-process type/value work.
- The smaller focused OpenAPI reproduction exits under Shatter's own
  `--timeout-total 360` without requiring an outer process killer.
- No matching Go frontend, harness, or Docker sandbox process remains after
  completion or timeout.
- Aggregate Markdown and JSON outputs are written on completion or controlled
  timeout.
- Add or update an automated regression check that exercises the
  timeout/accounting path without requiring the unsafe whole-corpus memory run.

## In Scope

- Timeout enforcement around active in-process scan layers.
- Bounding or short-circuiting random input generation / type-value handling
  for huge Go static type graphs.
- Final accounting and cleanup for this failure mode.
- Adding a reduced Shatter-side fixture or regression harness that reproduces
  the timeout/accounting failure without scanning the whole Zolem corpus.

## Out of Scope

- Changing Zolem feature code.
- Reverting or redesigning the `zolem-n0a` Wazero value factories.
- Improving coverage for unrelated opaque types such as `fixture.Selector`,
  `http.Handler`, or provider generator interfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Focused OpenAPI repro exits under Shatter's own timeout with failure accounting and aggregate outputs; no Go frontend or Docker sandbox remains after timeout/completion

title: Go browser ctor policy
description:
During whole-corpus Shatter validation against `~/project/kapow`, browser helper dependencies were already mocked/skipped well enough for a one-iteration run, but a higher-intensity run still launched a real Rod/Chromium browser when scanning the browser constructor target itself.

Observed evidence:

- Command was a whole-corpus Go scan of `/home/ketan/project/kapow` from Shatter branch `str-kuc0-kapow-build-timeouts`.
- Higher-intensity validation command used `--max-iterations 5 --timeout-explore 20 --timeout-total 4800 --parallelism 4 --exec-timeout 5 --build-timeout 30 --progress`.
- At roughly target 1126 of 1198, progress showed:
  - `/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow/internal/scraper/browser.go::New`
  - display name `New`
  - status completed after the same interval where Chromium appeared.
- Process table showed a real browser process:
  - `/home/ketan/.cache/rod/browser/chromium-1321438/chrome --headless ... --dump-dom ... about:blank`
  - plus `chrome_crashpad_handler`, zygote, and gpu-process children.
- The scan and browser process tree were stopped immediately.

Current code facts:

- Kapow target function is `/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow/internal/scraper/browser.go::New`.
- `New(opts ...Option) (*Browser, error)` calls `NewContext(context.Background(), opts...)`.
- `NewContext` constructs `launcher.New()...` and calls `l.Launch()`, then `rod.New().ControlURL(...).Connect()`.
- The local `Browser` type wraps `*rod.Browser` and `*launcher.Launcher`.
- Existing Shatter Go policy code in `shatter-go/protocol/policy.go` classifies browser automation dependencies and browser helper return types such as `scraper.Browser`, `rod.Browser`, and `launcher.Launcher` as `subprocess`.
- Existing tests cover browser automation dependencies, browser return types, and local browser helper chains, but the higher-intensity validation demonstrates that the direct constructor target `scraper.New` was still allowed to execute and launch Chrome.

## Desired Behavior

The Go frontend default policy must prevent direct execution of browser constructor targets that launch Rod/Chromium. Such targets should be skipped/unsupported under the default scan policy, or otherwise classified so scan prepare/execute does not run the real browser constructor.

Browser windows/processes must not be spawned by Shatter validation unless the user explicitly opts into subprocess/browser execution.

## Reproduction

Use Shatter after the existing Kapow fixes from `str-kuc0-kapow-build-timeouts`
are available on the working branch (or after that branch has landed on `main`),
then run a whole-corpus Kapow scan with more than one iteration:

```bash
SHATTER_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/shatter-kapow-browser-repro/cache \
SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR=/tmp/shatter-kapow-browser-repro/seeds \
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/kapow \
  --language go --log-level warn --color never --format json \
  --output /tmp/shatter-kapow-browser-repro/report.json \
  --stdout --no-cache --no-seeds --max-iterations 5 \
  --timeout-explore 20 --timeout-total 4800 --parallelism 4 \
  --exec-timeout 5 --build-timeout 30 --progress
```

Monitor for browser processes during the run:

```bash
pgrep -af '(/home/ketan/.cache/rod/browser/chromium|/tmp/leakless|chrome --.*dump-dom|chrome --.*rod)'
```

The observed failure occurred when the scan reached `tools/kapow/internal/scraper/browser.go::New`.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a failing Go frontend policy test showing that a direct function returning or constructing the local browser wrapper, equivalent to `func New(...) (*Browser, error)`, is classified as `subprocess`/policy-skipped under default policy.
- Implement the policy fix without modifying Kapow feature code.
- The new test passes.
- Existing Go frontend tests pass with `go test ./...` in `shatter-go/`.
- A targeted or whole-corpus Kapow validation reaches the browser constructor marker
  `/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow/internal/scraper/browser.go::New`
  without spawning a process matching `/home/ketan/.cache/rod/browser/chromium`,
  `/tmp/leakless`, or `chrome --.*dump-dom`.
- `task conformance` still passes because this is a Go frontend behavior/policy change.

## Scope

In scope:

- Go frontend policy classification and tests.
- Default scan behavior for browser constructor targets and local browser wrappers.

Out of scope:

- Non-trivial Kapow feature-code changes.
- Allowing actual browser execution during unattended validation.
- Broad generator support for every skipped opaque browser type.

title: Rust Axum tests build timeout
description:
Title: Rust Axum tests build timeout

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust-frontend, tests, axum, build-timeout

## Symptom

The full Rust frontend gate can hang long enough to make completion ambiguous
and then fail several Axum executor tests with `CompilationFailed("build timed
out")`.

Observed while validating `str-puqi-rust-exit-diagnostics` from Shatter commit
`095a28c9a0e66a86e83cbc7bc280cc18d05792ae`:

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml
```

The run emitted these failures before the command was interrupted after several
additional minutes with no final summary:

```text
executor::tests::execute_axum_handler_replays_native_state_and_extension_values
panicked at src/executor.rs:6017:25:
execute failed: CompilationFailed("build timed out")

executor::tests::execute_axum_handler_replays_native_state_inside_request_runtime
panicked at src/executor.rs:6114:25:
execute failed: CompilationFailed("build timed out")

executor::tests::execute_axum_handler_defaults_null_json_body_to_valid_payload
panicked at src/executor.rs:6457:25:
execute failed: CompilationFailed("build timed out")

executor::tests::execute_axum_handler_sends_literal_null_json_body_for_option_payload
panicked at src/executor.rs:6520:25:
execute failed: CompilationFailed("build timed out")
```

## Current Code Facts

- The failing tests are in `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs`.
- The command is the documented Rust frontend gate for changes under
  `shatter-rust/`.
- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs` defines `DEFAULT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECS` as 30,
  and the harness build paths read `SHATTER_BUILD_TIMEOUT` before returning
  `CompilationFailed("build timed out")`.
- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs` reads `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE` and
  `SHATTER_HARNESS_SCRATCH` to choose persistent harness cache and scratch
  roots; the named failing tests construct fresh `HarnessCache`,
  `CrateHarnessCache`, and `CrateBridgeHarnessCache` values locally.
- The same validation session passed the focused generator panic regression:

  ```bash
  cargo test --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml \
    native_registry_generator_panic_returns_error -- --nocapture
  ```

- The same validation session passed Rust frontend clippy:

  ```bash
  cargo clippy --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings
  ```

## Desired Behavior

`cargo test --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml` should complete
deterministically enough for agents to use it as a pre-completion gate. Axum
executor tests that compile harnesses should not fail because the harness build
timeout is too low, cache contention-prone, or shared-state dependent.

## Acceptance Checks

- Reproduce at least one of the named Axum executor test build timeouts or
  explain why the full-suite run can time out while focused runs pass.
- Add or adjust focused coverage so this timeout mode is deterministic enough
  to guard in CI or local pre-completion runs.
- Fix the timeout/cache/test setup so the full command
  `cargo test --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml` completes successfully.
- Verify `cargo clippy --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings`
  still passes.

## Scope

In scope:

- `shatter-rust` Axum executor test harness build timeouts.
- Test cache/scratch isolation or timeout configuration needed to make the
  Rust frontend gate reliable.

Out of scope:

- Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- The native generator panic handling fixed by `str-puqi`.
- Broad Axum extractor support gaps such as `CurrentAccount` or `Multipart`.
close_reason: Resolved on main 9c44d5c987d79919acbd5813a63a0e689f19020e; raised Rust harness build timeout to 120s with regression coverage, and full Rust frontend tests/clippy plus smoke/e2e passed on the merge candidate.

title: Go smoke observe hang
description:
Title: Go smoke observe hang

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go, smoke, frontend, diagnostics

## Symptom

The required Shatter pre-completion smoke gate currently hangs on the Go standalone smoke target and eventually reports only a frontend request timeout:

```text
task smoke
...
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- explore --max-iterations 3 --timeout-explore 10 /tmp/shatter-examples-main/standalone/go/smoke-main.go:SmokeClassify
...
[progress] failed 1/1: SmokeClassify (30.0s)
[error] Exploration error for SmokeClassify: observe stage failed: frontend error: request timed out after 30s
Error: explore: all 1 attempted target(s) failed (build_failed=0, runtime_failed=0, timed_out=1); no completed functions
```

Retrying the same target with a larger request timeout still hangs and times out:

```bash
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- explore \
  --max-iterations 3 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 300 \
  --no-cache \
  /tmp/shatter-examples-main/standalone/go/smoke-main.go:SmokeClassify
```

Observed result:

```text
[progress] failed 1/1: SmokeClassify (300.0s)
[error] Exploration error for SmokeClassify: observe stage failed: frontend error: request timed out after 300s
```

This blocked landing `str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path`, which otherwise had passing focused regressions, full `cargo test`, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`.

## Reproduction Evidence

Shatter checkout:

```text
repo: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path
branch: str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path
head: 67ba7285 str-8hui: Export behavior input witnesses
base main: 7fedfed5 Merge branch 'str-2rh9-concolic-frontend-retry-gap'
```

The `/tmp/shatter-examples-main` checkout is produced by the repo's `scripts/examples_checkout.py` helper. `Taskfile.yml::smoke` calls that helper before running the Go smoke target, so a fresh reproduction can either run `task smoke` or run:

```bash
python3 scripts/examples_checkout.py
```

before invoking the direct `cargo run ... /tmp/shatter-examples-main/...` command.

Commands run from the Shatter worktree:

```bash
task smoke
task smoke
env SHATTER_LOG_LEVEL=debug cargo run -p shatter-cli -- explore \
  --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 45 \
  --no-cache \
  /tmp/shatter-examples-main/standalone/go/smoke-main.go:SmokeClassify
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- explore \
  --max-iterations 3 \
  --timeout-explore 10 \
  --request-timeout 300 \
  --no-cache \
  /tmp/shatter-examples-main/standalone/go/smoke-main.go:SmokeClassify
```

All timed out in the observe stage. The TypeScript half of `task smoke` passed.

The same direct command could not be re-run from the local `/tmp/shatter-main-land` main preview because that Git worktree path is stale/missing. The failure is therefore proven on the `str-8hui` branch where it blocks landing; a follow-up agent should reproduce on current `main` after creating or using a valid main worktree.

After a timed-out run, the branch-local Go workspace had no final launcher binary and no build diagnostics:

```text
.shatter-cache/go-workspace/binaries/ was empty
.shatter-cache/go-workspace/runs/20260604T003446Z/build_1576a0bd1a155d6e-838d3a9b.log existed but had size 0
pgrep -af 'shatter_launcher_1576a0bd1a155d6e|go build|shatter-go' found no leftover build/frontend process
```

One earlier 30s timeout left generated cache files:

```text
.shatter-cache/go-workspace/binaries/shatter_launcher_1576a0bd1a155d6e-838d3a9b.lock
.shatter-cache/go-workspace/binaries/shatter_launcher_1576a0bd1a155d6e-838d3a9b.tmp-1214481-1780533286808637941
```

Those files were removed manually and the 300s repro still timed out, so stale lock cleanup alone is not sufficient.

## Current Code Facts To Verify

- `Taskfile.yml::smoke` runs the Go smoke command without an explicit `--request-timeout`, so it uses the CLI default request timeout.
- The Go frontend build path writes launcher build logs under `.shatter-cache/go-workspace/runs/<timestamp>/build_*.log`.
- The observed Go smoke build log for launcher hash `1576a0bd1a155d6e-838d3a9b` was empty, which means the failure did not surface useful `go build` output.
- The reported category is `timed_out`, not `build_failed`, even though no launcher binary was produced.
- `shatter-go/build/builder.go::Builder.compileLauncher` accepts a `context.Context` parameter but currently discards it before calling `launchBuildWithLog`.
- `shatter-go/launcher/launcher.go::BuildLauncher` runs `go build` through `exec.Command("go", buildArgs...)` rather than a context-aware command, so build cancellation/timeout is not directly wired to the Go build subprocess.
- `shatter-go/launcher/launcher.go::acquireLauncherBuildLock` owns launcher `.lock` files, and `BuildLauncher` owns same-directory `.tmp-*` launcher binaries before publishing the final binary.

## Desired Behavior

The Go standalone smoke target should complete reliably or fail with a specific actionable build/frontend diagnostic. It should not hang until the generic request timeout with an empty build log and no final launcher binary.

If a launcher build is still in progress when a request is cancelled or times out, Shatter should clean up the lock/temp state and report whether the wait was for a build lock, a build command, or launcher execution.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused regression or integration test for the Go smoke/launcher path that reproduces either the hang, stale lock, or empty-diagnostic timeout failure mode without depending on Pickpackit.
- Fix the Go frontend/build path so `/tmp/shatter-examples-main/standalone/go/smoke-main.go:SmokeClassify` completes under `task smoke`, or fails with a concrete build/launcher error rather than a generic observe request timeout.
- Ensure timed-out/cancelled Go launcher builds do not leave stale `.lock` or `.tmp-*` files that can poison later runs.
- Preserve existing successful Go frontend execution behavior.
- `task smoke` passes from a clean Shatter worktree after the fix.

## Scope

In scope:

- Go frontend observe/build timeout handling.
- Launcher build lock/temp cleanup on timeout or cancellation.
- Diagnostics for Go launcher build waits and empty build logs.
- Focused Shatter tests and the `task smoke` gate.

Out of scope:

- Pickpackit feature-code changes. Pickpackit is a separate downstream Rust/Axum validation repository used by the broader Shatter validation goal; this issue should be reproducible without it.
- Rust concolic generator behavior from `str-8hui`.
- Kapow whole-corpus Go validation improvements beyond whatever is needed to keep the smoke target healthy.
close_reason: Resolved on main ac8655b56a0bc05f4c2ae1d5eced1228e99421cc; fresh direct Go smoke explore passed with --clean/temp caches, and task smoke passed on rebased issue branch.

title: Rust frontend exit diagnostics
description:
Title: Rust frontend exit diagnostics

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust, frontend, diagnostics, scan, concolic

## Symptom

When the Rust custom frontend subprocess exits before replying, Shatter reports only an opaque process-level message such as:

```text
frontend subprocess exited before responding: .shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom (exit status: 101)
```

The scan/report failure record does not preserve the child stderr, panic message, or backtrace. This makes target panics, harness panics, database race failures, and frontend bugs indistinguishable.

## Reproduction Evidence

Observed during Pickpackit Rust/Axum concolic validation on a Shatter candidate built from `main` plus `str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path`:

```text
Scan complete: 67 completed, 6 failed, 0 unsupported, 2 skipped
```

Each failed function had the same opaque error shape:

```text
error: concolic exploration error: frontend error: frontend subprocess exited before responding: .shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom (exit status: 101)
```

Examples from `/var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-candidate-full/report.json`:

```text
item_categories.rs::list_item_categories
items.rs::update_item_home_location
legs.rs::reorder_legs
next_time_notes.rs::list_next_time_notes
tags.rs::create_tag_category
trips.rs::archive_trip
```

A narrowed parallel rerun over the same handler files failed a different set of functions with the same opaque status-101 message, while several full-run failures completed successfully. That evidence points to a real instability, but the current reporting blocks root-cause work because it drops the child process failure text.

## Current Code Facts To Verify

- The Rust frontend transport path that spawns `shatter-rust-custom` returns a frontend error when the subprocess exits before responding.
- The scan report failed-function record currently stores only the process exit summary, not child stderr/backtrace text.
- Existing scan report fields can already carry an `error_message`; the missing behavior is preserving enough child diagnostics in that message or an adjacent structured field.

## Desired Behavior

When a Rust frontend subprocess exits before responding, Shatter should capture bounded child stderr and include it in the per-function failure details and scan log. If `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` or equivalent produces a panic backtrace, the report should preserve enough of it to identify the panic site without requiring external logs.

## Smallest Acceptable Reproduction

Add a Shatter-local test or fixture that uses a fake/minimal frontend process or harness command which writes a panic-like message to stderr and exits with code 101 before sending a response. The scan/execution path should report a failure that includes the stderr snippet instead of only `exit status: 101`.

This test should not depend on Pickpackit.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add focused regression coverage for a Rust frontend child process that writes stderr and exits before responding.
- The resulting scan/execution error includes bounded stderr text in the report failure detail or structured diagnostic field.
- Existing successful Rust frontend execution behavior is unchanged.
- Re-run a focused Pickpackit validation that previously showed opaque status-101 failures and verify any remaining frontend exits include actionable stderr/backtrace detail.
- Keep Pickpackit feature code unchanged.

## Scope

In scope:

- Rust frontend subprocess error capture.
- Scan/report failure diagnostics for frontend child exits.
- Bounded stderr/backtrace retention so reports stay well-formed.

Out of scope:

- Fixing the underlying Pickpackit parallel instability once the panic text is visible.
- Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Adding skips for mutation-heavy handlers.
- Reworking the already-fixed solver unknown-param behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Regression coverage preserves bounded stderr/backtrace for Rust frontend child exit 101; successful frontend execution unchanged; focused Pickpackit rerun exposes actionable diagnostics without Pickpackit feature-code changes.

title: Concolic frontend retry gap
description:
Title: Concolic frontend retry gap

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,concolic,scan,pickpackit
Discovered from: str-8hui
Blocks: str-8hui

## Problem

The worker-pool scan retry budget added for transient frontend transport failures does not cover concolic exploration errors. In `scan --concolic`, the same frontend subprocess exit can be wrapped as `ScanError::Concolic(crate::orchestrator::ExploreError::Frontend(_))` instead of `ScanError::Explore(ExploreError::Frontend(_))`. The retry predicate does not recognize that nested concolic frontend error, so Shatter still marks otherwise executable Pickpackit functions failed with raw exit-101 transport errors.

Representative final error from a whole Pickpackit `src/handlers` run:

```text
error: concolic exploration error: frontend error: frontend subprocess exited before responding: .shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom (exit status: 101)
```

## Reproduction Evidence

Shatter checkout:

```text
repo: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path
branch: str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path
head: 89dd3767 str-8hui: Export behavior input witnesses
base includes: 9cb005b5 Merge branch 'str-92ie-frontend-retry-budget'
```

Pickpackit checkout:

```text
repo/API cwd: /tmp/pickpackit-main-shatter-concolic/api
database: postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit
```

Build the custom frontend:

```bash
env \
  RUST_BACKTRACE=1 \
  SHATTER_SKIP_CHECK=1 \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust \
  SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust-runtime \
  DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
  PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust/target/debug:/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/target/debug:$PATH \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/target/debug/shatter build-frontend rust
```

Run the whole handler corpus:

```bash
env \
  RUST_BACKTRACE=1 \
  SHATTER_SKIP_CHECK=1 \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust \
  SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust-runtime \
  DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
  PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust/target/debug:/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/target/debug:$PATH \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/target/debug/shatter scan src/handlers \
    --language rust --require-rust --concolic \
    --parallelism 3 --parallelism-min 3 --parallelism-max 3 --workers-per-fn 1 \
    --max-iterations 5 --timeout-per-fn 420 --timeout-total 7200 \
    --request-timeout 180 --exec-timeout 60 --build-timeout 600 \
    --cache-dir /var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-after-92ie-full/scan-cache \
    --no-seeds --format json \
    -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-after-92ie-full/report.json \
    --fail-on-failures=0
```

Observed aggregate from `/var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-after-92ie-full/report.json`:

```json
{
  "attempted": 75,
  "completed": 50,
  "failed": 23,
  "unsupported": 0,
  "skipped": 2,
  "total_clusters": 344,
  "total_inputs": 346
}
```

The two skipped functions are the configured helper skips:

- `src/handlers/legs.rs::fetch_legs_for_workspace`
- `src/handlers/tasks.rs::fetch_tasks_for_workspace`

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs::ScanError` has both `Explore(#[from] ExploreError)` and `Concolic(#[from] crate::orchestrator::ExploreError)` variants.
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs::retryable_frontend_transport_failure_source` currently recognizes:
  - `PhasedOutcome::Failed(ScanError::Frontend(error))`
  - `PhasedOutcome::Failed(ScanError::Explore(ExploreError::Frontend(error)))`
- It does not recognize `PhasedOutcome::Failed(ScanError::Concolic(crate::orchestrator::ExploreError::Frontend(error)))`.
- `shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs::ExploreError` has a `Frontend(#[from] FrontendError)` variant whose display text is `frontend error: ...`.
- The self-contained `str-92ie` regression test covers repeated frontend exits through the non-concolic `ExploreError::Frontend` path, not the concolic wrapper path.

## Expected Behavior

The default worker-pool scan path should apply the same bounded retry budget to retryable frontend transport failures whether they originate from non-concolic exploration or concolic exploration.

Policy:

- Treat `ScanError::Concolic(crate::orchestrator::ExploreError::Frontend(error))` as retryable when `error` is `FrontendError::Write`, `FrontendError::Read`, or `FrontendError::SubprocessExited`.
- Preserve the existing 3 total attempts per function: initial attempt plus 2 fresh-frontend retries.
- Keep non-transport concolic errors non-retryable.
- If the concolic transport failures exhaust the budget, return the existing retry-budget-exhausted diagnostic rather than the raw frontend error.

## Acceptance

- Add a self-contained Shatter regression test that fails before the fix because a concolic frontend transport error is not retried.
- The test must exercise `PhasedOutcome::Failed(ScanError::Concolic(crate::orchestrator::ExploreError::Frontend(_)))` through the worker-pool retry predicate or a focused helper-level assertion, and verify it is treated as retryable with the same source text behavior as non-concolic frontend errors.
- Existing retry tests still pass:
  - `parallel_scan_retries_repeated_execute_frontend_exits`
  - `parallel_scan_retries_dead_idle_frontend_before_failing_function`
- Re-run the Pickpackit whole-corpus `src/handlers` concolic scan after the fix. It should no longer report raw exit-101 failures for concolic frontend transport loss. If another failure class remains dominant, file the next smaller blocker with report evidence.
- Keep Pickpackit feature code unchanged.

## In Scope

- Worker-pool retry classification for concolic frontend transport errors.
- Focused Shatter regression coverage in or near `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs`.
- Pickpackit validation rerun using the existing validation checkout.

## Out of Scope

- Pickpackit application feature-code changes.
- Broad changes to frontend process lifetime management.
- Changing configured skip entries.
- Solving branch diversity or coverage quality beyond removing this retry-classification gap.

title: Frontend retry budget
description:
Title: Frontend retry budget

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,concolic,scan
Discovered from: str-8hui
Blocks: str-8hui

## Problem

The scan worker-pool path only gives a function one retry after a frontend transport failure. In large concolic scans a reused frontend can exit transiently before responding, and the same function can succeed if it is rerun with a fresh frontend. One retry is not enough for the observed failure mode, so Shatter can mark otherwise executable functions failed with an opaque transport error.

Observed Pickpackit symptom:

```text
concolic exploration error: frontend error: frontend subprocess exited before responding: .shatter-cache/bin/shatter-rust-custom (exit status: 101)
```

## Durable Reproduction To Add

Add a Shatter regression test that does not depend on Pickpackit:

1. Create a protocol test frontend script under `protocol/` that:
   - completes handshake normally,
   - for the first two execute or prepare/explore requests for a given function, exits before writing a response,
   - records attempts in a temp flag/counter path from an env var,
   - on the third attempt, returns a normal successful execute response compatible with existing scan tests.
2. Add a `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` test using `parallel_scan` with:
   - `parallelism: 1`,
   - `IsolationMode::None`,
   - a single exported no-dependency function,
   - `max_iterations_per_function: 1`,
   - the new test frontend script,
   - an env var pointing at a temp counter file.
3. The test should assert the scan succeeds with one `function_result`, no skipped functions, and no failed function outcome.

This test should fail before the fix because the current worker-pool implementation retries only once.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` defines `retryable_frontend_transport_failure` for `FrontendError::Write`, `FrontendError::Read`, and `FrontendError::SubprocessExited`.
- The default worker-pool path in `parallel_scan_with_progress` retries a transport failure once with a fresh frontend, then fails the function if the replacement frontend also dies.
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` already has `parallel_scan_retries_dead_idle_frontend_before_failing_function`, but that covers a one-time dead frontend and does not cover repeated transient frontend loss for the same function.
- `IsolationMode::Function` is not the target behavior for this issue; the fix must cover the default worker-pool path (`IsolationMode::None`).

## Expected Behavior

The default worker-pool scan path should make a bounded number of fresh-frontend attempts for retryable transport failures before failing the function.

Policy for this issue:

- Allow up to 3 total attempts per function for retryable frontend transport failures: the initial attempt plus 2 fresh-frontend retries.
- Respawn a fresh frontend for each retry attempt.
- Do not retry non-transport errors, unsupported-function errors, build timeouts, or exploration timeouts.
- If all attempts fail with retryable transport failures, return a failure that states the retry budget was exhausted and includes the final transport error text.

## In Scope

- Add the self-contained test frontend script.
- Add the failing regression test first.
- Implement the bounded retry budget in the worker-pool scan path.
- Keep function-isolation behavior unchanged except for any shared helper needed by the worker-pool code.

## Out of Scope

- Pickpackit application code changes.
- Adding support for Pickpackit `CurrentAccount` extractor execution.
- Broad Rust frontend protocol redesign.
- Making frontend stderr non-empty when a child exits silently.
- Changing configured scan skips.

## Acceptance

- The new regression test fails before the fix for the current one-retry behavior.
- The new regression test passes after the fix.
- Existing scan retry tests still pass, including `parallel_scan_retries_dead_idle_frontend_before_failing_function`.
- A reduced Pickpackit validation run may be used as extra evidence for `str-8hui`, but this issue is complete based on the self-contained Shatter test and worker-pool behavior above.

title: Solver unknown params panic
description:
Title: Solver unknown params panic

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: solver, concolic, rust, scan, pickpackit

## Symptom

During Pickpackit whole-corpus `shatter scan --concolic` validation, Shatter's debug build repeatedly panics in the solver when a collected path constraint references a parameter name that is not present in the top-level `ParamInfo` list.

Representative log excerpt from `/var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-clean-final/scan.log`:

```text
thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at shatter-core/src/solver.rs:916:21:
constraint references unknown param "owner_filter", known params: {"_", "current"}
```

The scan continues for some functions but emits repeated worker panics instead of treating the unsupported constraint as solver-ineligible input.

## Reproduction

Shatter checkout:

- repo root: `/var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean`
- commit: `da8c22cfc94478aab7a835769c66c56bd9fd2f60`
- branch source: `str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path`
- build mode: debug (`cargo build --bin shatter`)

Pickpackit checkout:

- repo root: `/var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-validation`
- commit: `7cdad43c942d824777097a18802fee1ea1674667`
- API working directory: `/var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-validation/api`
- custom frontend built with:

```bash
env \
  DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit_str_8hui_clean \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/shatter-rust \
  SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/shatter-rust-runtime \
  PATH=/var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/shatter-rust/target/debug:/var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/target/debug:$PATH \
  /var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/target/debug/shatter build-frontend rust
```

Scan command:

```bash
env \
  DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit_str_8hui_clean \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/shatter-rust \
  SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/shatter-rust-runtime \
  SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-clean-final/harness-cache \
  SHATTER_HARNESS_SCRATCH=/var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-clean-final/harness-scratch \
  PATH=/var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/shatter-rust/target/debug:/var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/target/debug:$PATH \
  /var/tmp/shatter-str-8hui-clean/target/debug/shatter scan src/handlers \
    --language rust --require-rust --concolic \
    --parallelism 2 --parallelism-min 2 --parallelism-max 2 --workers-per-fn 1 \
    --max-iterations 5 --timeout-per-fn 420 --timeout-total 7200 \
    --request-timeout 180 --exec-timeout 60 --build-timeout 600 \
    --cache-dir /var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-clean-final/scan-cache \
    --no-seeds --format json \
    -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-clean-final/report.json
```

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/solver.rs::solve_for_new_path` has a debug-only validation block under `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`.
- That block calls `crate::sym_expr::extract_param_names(constraint)` and `debug_assert!`s that each non-dotted parameter name exists in `param_infos`.
- In debug builds, constraints such as `SymExpr::Param { name: "owner_filter", .. }` with `param_infos` containing only `"_"` and `"current"` panic instead of returning a `SolverError`.
- This is especially visible in Rust/Axum native-generator scans, where path constraints can include request/body/query-derived symbolic names that are not top-level handler parameters.

## Expected Behavior

Solver-ineligible constraints that reference unknown top-level params should be handled as an unsupported solve attempt, not as a panic. A concolic scan should continue without worker panics and still report behavior maps for executable inputs.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Rust regression test that calls `solve_for_new_path` with a constraint referencing an unknown non-dotted param and verifies it returns a recoverable error instead of panicking.
- Fix `solve_for_new_path` so debug builds do not panic for unknown constraint params.
- Re-run the Pickpackit concolic validation far enough to confirm the `owner_filter` panic no longer appears in the scan log.
- Keep Pickpackit feature code unchanged.

## Scope

In scope:

- Solver validation for unknown top-level constraint params.
- Concolic scan robustness when Rust/Axum instrumentation emits request-derived symbolic names.

Out of scope:

- Solving `owner_filter` correctly.
- Broad symbolic naming redesign.
- Pickpackit feature-code changes.

title: Solver unknown param panic
description:
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: concolic, solver, rust, scan, pickpackit

## Problem

A Pickpackit whole-corpus `shatter scan --concolic` validation run on Shatter branch `str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path` panics inside Shatter's solver when it sees a constraint whose symbolic name is not one of the executable function parameters passed to the solver.

Representative stderr from the run:

```text
thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at shatter-core/src/solver.rs:916:21:
constraint references unknown param "owner_filter", known params: {"current", "_"}
```

The panic repeats for the same handler shape while the scan continues, which makes the concolic validation unreliable and risks losing solver-driven input generation for handlers whose branch constraints mention destructured request/query fields rather than top-level executable parameters.

## Reproduction

Shatter checkout:

```text
repo: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path
branch: str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path
head at observation: c852f0c8 str-8hui: Seed concolic scan from generators
```

Pickpackit checkout:

```text
repo: /tmp/pickpackit-main-shatter-concolic
commit: 08d69c9cb894633a38c1c0c2537e9549ab03c29b
api working directory: /tmp/pickpackit-main-shatter-concolic/api
```

Prerequisite: build the Pickpackit custom Rust frontend from the API directory:

```bash
env \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust \
  SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust-runtime \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/target/debug/shatter build-frontend rust
```

Run a whole-corpus concolic scan from the Pickpackit API directory:

```bash
env \
  SHATTER_SKIP_CHECK=1 \
  SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust \
  SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust-runtime \
  SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-concolic-custom/harness-cache \
  SHATTER_HARNESS_SCRATCH=/var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-concolic-skip/harness-scratch \
  DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
  PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/shatter-rust/target/debug:/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/target/debug:$PATH \
  /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-8hui-axum-concolic-generator-path/target/debug/shatter scan src/handlers \
    --language rust --require-rust --concolic \
    --parallelism 3 --parallelism-min 3 --parallelism-max 3 --workers-per-fn 1 \
    --max-iterations 5 --timeout-per-fn 420 --timeout-total 7200 \
    --request-timeout 180 --exec-timeout 60 --build-timeout 600 \
    --cache-dir /var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-concolic-skip/scan-cache \
    --no-seeds --format json \
    -o /var/tmp/pickpackit-str-8hui-concolic-skip/report.json
```

The panic was observed after bundle handlers began executing; the run was stopped after the panic to avoid accepting a corrupted validation artifact.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/solver.rs` panics at the unknown-param path instead of returning an unsolved or unsupported constraint result.
- In this scan path, executable parameters for the affected Axum handler are adapter-level values such as `current` and `_`, while the collected branch constraint can reference request/query-derived names such as `owner_filter`.
- This issue is blocking `str-8hui` whole-corpus validation, but it is distinct from generator seeding: the custom frontend was built and the concolic scan had started producing artifacts before this panic appeared.

## Desired Behavior

The solver must not panic when a constraint references a symbolic name that is absent from the executable parameter map. It should treat that constraint as unsolved, unsupported, or otherwise skip it with structured diagnostics while allowing scan/concolic exploration to continue and report a well-formed behavior map.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Shatter regression test that constructs or solves a constraint referencing an unknown symbolic parameter and proves it does not panic.
- Fix the solver/concolic path so unknown-parameter constraints are reported as unsolved/unsupported instead of panicking.
- Re-run the Pickpackit concolic whole-corpus validation command, or the current `str-8hui` acceptance command, and verify no `constraint references unknown param` panic appears.
- Keep Pickpackit feature code unchanged.

## Scope

In scope:

- Shatter solver/concolic handling for constraints whose symbolic references are not top-level executable parameters.
- Focused Shatter unit/regression coverage.
- Re-running enough Pickpackit validation to prove the panic is gone.

Out of scope:

- Improving branch coverage quality beyond preventing this panic.
- Changing Pickpackit feature code.
- Redesigning Axum extractor modeling or query-field symbolic naming beyond the minimal non-panicking behavior.

title: Go browser deps stay mocked
description:
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,scan,policy,kapow

## Symptom

Whole-corpus Kapow validation can execute Go browser automation helpers and launch Rod/Chromium subprocesses. This happened while scanning `tools/kapow/internal/scraper/browser.go` targets such as `New` and `NewContext`.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-go/protocol/policy.go` classifies `os/exec` and similar modules as `subprocess`, but did not classify browser automation modules such as `github.com/go-rod/rod`, `github.com/go-rod/stealth`, `github.com/playwright-community/playwright-go`, `github.com/chromedp/chromedp`, or `github.com/tebeka/selenium`.
- `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go` applied the execution policy in `handleExecute`, after `handlePrepare` could build a harness for the target.
- Analyzer output for `/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow/internal/scraper/browser.go::New` shows a local dependency on `NewContext`, while `NewContext` directly depends on `launcher.New` and `rod.New`. Policy classification must therefore account for same-file local helper calls.

## Smallest Reproduction / Evidence

Run a targeted scan from Shatter against Kapow:

```bash
SHATTER_CACHE_DIR=/home/ketan/tmp/shatter-kapow-validation/str-kuc0-browser-policy/cache \
SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR=/home/ketan/tmp/shatter-kapow-validation/str-kuc0-browser-policy/seeds \
cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/kapow \
  --language go \
  --include 'tools/kapow/internal/scraper/browser.go' \
  --format json \
  --output /home/ketan/tmp/shatter-kapow-validation/str-kuc0-browser-policy/report.json \
  --stdout --no-cache --no-seeds --max-iterations 1 \
  --timeout-explore 10 --timeout-total 120 --parallelism 2 \
  --exec-timeout 5 --build-timeout 30
```

Before the fix, `pgrep -af '(/home/ketan/.cache/rod/browser/chromium|/tmp/leakless)'` showed Rod/Chromium subprocesses during this scan.

## Acceptance Checks

- Browser automation dependencies are classified as unsafe subprocess-like dependencies for policy/mocking decisions.
- Same-file helper calls are considered when policy evaluates a target, so wrappers like `New -> NewContext -> launcher.New` inherit the unsafe dependency.
- `handlePrepare` does not build direct harnesses for policy-denied targets before the execution policy has a chance to run.
- The targeted Kapow browser wrapper scan completes without Rod/Chromium/leakless subprocesses.
- Focused Go policy tests cover direct browser automation dependencies and the transitive local-helper path.

## In Scope

- Shatter Go frontend policy/analyzer/handler changes needed to keep browser automation from launching during scan execution.
- Tests in `shatter-go/protocol`.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Kapow feature-code changes.
- Deleting or excluding Kapow browser feature code from discovery.
- Browser/UI tooling or Playwright visual review.
acceptance_criteria: Browser automation dependencies are classified as subprocess-like policy dependencies; same-file helper calls inherit unsafe dependencies; prepare does not build policy-denied direct harnesses; targeted Kapow browser wrapper scan completes without Rod/Chromium/leakless subprocesses; focused Go policy tests cover direct and transitive browser dependencies.

title: Kapow build timeouts block 90%
description:
Title: Kapow build timeouts block 90%

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: scan, go, kapow, timeout, build

## Symptom

After `str-0agd` landed, a whole-corpus Kapow Go scan no longer stalls at a
handful of 90-second task timeouts. The scan now reaches every attempted target
and writes a report, but it still misses the requested 90% successful execution
threshold.

Latest whole-corpus validation from Shatter `main` commit
`14f3585b09b745b13fedc62b2aead8a5530a7688`:

```json
{
  "attempted": 1197,
  "completed": 1063,
  "completed_with_behavior": 985,
  "failed": 134,
  "skipped_count": 102,
  "total_discovered": 1299,
  "functions": 1063,
  "coverage": 30.971374941342095,
  "total_branches": 2131
}
```

`1063 / 1197` completed is about 88.8%, just below the 90% target. The dominant
remaining failure category is build timeout:

```text
117 timed out during build after 30s
  9 execute error (ExecutionTimeout): launcher: execution timed out after 5s
  7 timed out during execution after 30s
  1 instrumentation build failure from duplicate ShatterMock_NewService symbols
```

## Reproduction Evidence

Run from Shatter `main`:

```bash
env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/shatter-target-kapow-after-0agd \
  SHATTER_CACHE_DIR=/home/ketan/tmp/shatter-kapow-validation/full-scan-20260602-3/cache \
  SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR=/home/ketan/tmp/shatter-kapow-validation/full-scan-20260602-3/seeds \
  cargo run -p shatter-cli -- scan /home/ketan/project/kapow \
  --language go --include '**/*.go' \
  --exclude '**/.claude/**' --exclude '**/.shatter/**' \
  --exclude '**/.shatter-cache/**' --exclude '**/shatter-artifacts/**' \
  --exclude '**/shatter-artifacts-j3/**' --exclude '**/.worktrees/**' \
  --exclude '**/.cache/**' --exclude '**/api/tools.go' \
  --exclude '**/api/ui/embed.go' --exclude '**/api/ui/stub.go' \
  --log-level warn --color never --format json \
  --output /home/ketan/tmp/shatter-kapow-validation/full-scan-20260602-3/report.json \
  --stdout --no-cache --no-seeds --max-iterations 5 \
  --timeout-explore 20 --timeout-total 1800 --parallelism 8 \
  --exec-timeout 5 --build-timeout 30 --progress \
  > /home/ketan/tmp/shatter-kapow-validation/full-scan-20260602-3/stdout.json \
  2> /home/ketan/tmp/shatter-kapow-validation/full-scan-20260602-3/stderr.log
```

The scan reached `current: 1197, total: 1197` and wrote the report. It did not
hit the total scan timeout sweep, and there were no remaining 90-second task
watchdog failures.

Representative build-timeout targets include:

```text
/home/ketan/project/kapow/api/internal/otel/middleware.go::Middleware
/home/ketan/project/kapow/api/internal/posthog/posthog.go::New
/home/ketan/project/kapow/api/internal/priority/service.go::(*Service).Clear
/home/ketan/project/kapow/api/internal/scorecard/service.go::NewService
/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/dbverify/fingerprint.go::(*fingerprint).MarshalIndented
/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow/admissions.go::(*admissionsImporter).Dependencies
/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow/extract_cds.go::(*cdsExtractImporter).Run
/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow/importer_climate_normals.go::(*climateNormalsImporter).Run
/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow/importer_deadlines.go::(*deadlinesImporter).Scrape
/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/nleval/eval/cache.go::NewResponseCache
```

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-cli/src/args.rs` exposes `scan --build-timeout`; default is 30s.
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs` carries `build_timeout` into
  `ScanConfig.build_timeout`.
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` passes `build_timeout` to
  `run_scan_task_with_phase_timeouts`.
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` reports `BuildTimedOut` as
  `timed out during build after Ns`.
- `shatter-core/src/report.rs` classifies reasons beginning with
  `timed out during build` as `build_timeout`.
- `shatter-go/instrument/executor.go` generates `ShatterMock_<safeName>`
  functions; one non-dominant failure in the broad run is duplicate
  `ShatterMock_NewService` declarations for `api/internal/router`.

## Desired Behavior

Whole-corpus Kapow execution should complete at least 90% of attempted feature
code without non-trivial Kapow feature-code changes. The fix should focus on
Shatter-side behavior that turns currently failed build-timeout targets into
completed attempts while preserving honest reporting for genuinely unbuildable
or unsupported targets.

Potential directions include improving Go harness build reuse, reducing
unnecessary per-target build work, applying a more appropriate build timeout
only where build latency dominates, or otherwise making the build phase bounded
but capable of completing these Kapow targets. Do not merely hide failures as
skips unless the skip is justified by a clear policy and recorded honestly.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused regression or fixture test that reproduces the build-timeout
  failure mode or proves the selected Shatter-side build-timeout mitigation.
- Re-run a reduced Kapow validation containing several representative
  build-timeout targets and show that at least some previously build-timeout
  targets now complete or fail for a more specific honest reason.
- Re-run the whole-corpus Kapow scan and show completed attempted functions
  reaches at least 90%, or file the next smaller blocker issue with evidence if
  another category becomes dominant.
- Preserve `str-gi10` total-timeout behavior and `str-0agd` per-target timeout
  behavior: whole-corpus scans must still write reports and must not regress to
  90-second task-watchdog stalls.
- Run relevant Rust/Go gates, plus `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `task smoke`,
  and `task --force e2e` before landing.

## In Scope

- Shatter Go harness build behavior, build timeout handling, and scan
  orchestration/reporting needed to improve Kapow successful execution.
- Small Kapow build-usage or infrastructure adjustments only if they do not
  change feature behavior.
- Filing a separate follow-up for the one duplicate `ShatterMock_NewService`
  instrumentation failure if it remains after the dominant build-timeout issue
  is addressed.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Kapow feature-code changes.
- Deleting Kapow feature code.
- Silently reclassifying real failures as success.
- Solving branch-input diversity after successful execution is still below 90%.
acceptance_criteria: Whole-corpus Kapow scan completes at least 90% of attempted functions, or the next dominant blocker is filed with evidence; reduced build-timeout validation and Rust/clippy/smoke/e2e gates pass.

title: TS e2e classify flake
description:
Title: TS e2e classify flake

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: typescript,concolic,tests,flake

## Symptom

The exact landing preview for an unrelated one-line Rust Z3 unit-test seed
change failed in the TypeScript concolic e2e test
`concolic_classifynumber_discovers_all_branches` in
`shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic.rs`.

The test expects TypeScript concolic exploration of `classifyNumber` to
discover the branch returning `"positive-even"`. In the failing full Rust gate,

```text
thread 'concolic_classifynumber_discovers_all_branches' (...) panicked at shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic.rs:204:5:
should discover 'positive-even' branch; found: {"\"positive-odd\"", "\"negative\"", "\"zero\""}
```

tracked by `str-rf8o`. This issue is only for the TypeScript e2e test.

normal Rust gate. It should either reliably discover the even positive branch
