title: Instrument TMPDIR race
description:
Title: Instrument TMPDIR race

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust, tests, tmpdir, instrumentation

## Problem

The required Shatter Rust gate `cargo test` can still fail under the default
parallel test runner because a Shatter scan with caller-provided `TMPDIR`
created direct host `/tmp/shatter-instrument-*` directories.

Observed failure from a full workspace `cargo test` run on the rebased
`str-bphx-pickpackit-seed-diversity` branch:

```text
shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs::explore_respects_tmpdir_no_host_tmp_pollution

TMPDIR=/tmp/.tmpq8Ccct was set but Shatter created shatter-* entries in /tmp:
[
  "/tmp/shatter-instrument-3984259",
  "/tmp/shatter-instrument-3984367",
  "/tmp/shatter-instrument-3984368",
  "/tmp/shatter-instrument-3984258",
  "/tmp/shatter-instrument-3984263",
  "/tmp/shatter-instrument-3984262"
]

shatter status: ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(0))
stderr=
[info] Discovered 1 source file(s) in /tmp/.tmpoqdYNs
[info] Scanning 1 function(s) in dependency order...
[info] [1/1] /tmp/.tmpoqdYNs/toy.go::Add (16.1s elapsed)
[info] Wrote report to /tmp/.tmpvh4E0P/scan.json
```

The child `shatter scan` completed successfully and wrote its report, so the
failure is direct host `/tmp` pollution rather than a scan crash.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs` documents the contract that when
  `TMPDIR` is set, Shatter must not create direct host `/tmp/shatter-*`
  entries. Its header explicitly lists `shatter-instrument-*` as one historical
  pollution class.
- The regression invokes the real `shatter` binary against a small Go fixture,
  sets `TMPDIR` to a sentinel tempdir, snapshots direct `/tmp/shatter-*`
  entries before and after the child process, and fails on any new entries.
- `shatter-rust/src/handler.rs` currently constructs an instrumentation
  directory with:

  ```rust
  std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("shatter-instrument-{}", std::process::id()))
  ```

  That path shape matches the failing `/tmp/shatter-instrument-*` entries.
- `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go` creates Go instrumentation directories under
  `ws.GeneratedDir()` with `os.MkdirTemp(ws.GeneratedDir(), "instrument-*")`,
  which does not match the observed direct host `/tmp/shatter-instrument-*`
  paths.

## Desired Behavior

The TMPDIR regression test should only fail when the Shatter process under test
violates the TMPDIR contract. Rust instrumentation temp directories should be
created under the caller-provided `TMPDIR` or another Shatter-controlled
workspace/cache directory, not directly under host `/tmp` when `TMPDIR` is set.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add or adjust a focused regression proving Rust instrumentation does not
  create direct host `/tmp/shatter-instrument-*` entries when `TMPDIR` is set.
- `shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs::explore_respects_tmpdir_no_host_tmp_pollution`
  still proves the child `shatter scan` honors a caller-provided `TMPDIR` and
  writes at least one temp entry under the sentinel.
- A full workspace `cargo test` run passes with default Rust test parallelism.
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes.
- The fix does not weaken or skip the TMPDIR regression assertion.

## Scope

In scope:

- Rust instrumentation temporary directory placement and cleanup.
- Minimal test-harness isolation if needed to make the existing TMPDIR
  regression deterministic.

Out of scope:

- Changing Pickpackit feature code.
- Weakening the host `/tmp` pollution check.
- Broad refactors of frontend workspace/cache management beyond what is needed
  to honor `TMPDIR` for instrumentation temp directories.
acceptance_criteria: Rust instrumentation does not create direct /tmp/shatter-instrument-* entries when TMPDIR is set; tmpdir_regression still proves sentinel TMPDIR usage; full workspace cargo test passes; cargo clippy -- -D warnings passes; TMPDIR regression is not weakened.

title: Observer logs TMPDIR race
description:
Title: Observer logs TMPDIR race

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust, tests, tmpdir

## Problem

The required Shatter Rust quality gate `cargo test` can fail nondeterministically
because `shatter-core` observer-pool tests write log files directly under
`std::env::temp_dir()` with names matching `/tmp/shatter-observer-*.log`, while
the `shatter-cli` TMPDIR regression integration test watches global `/tmp` for
new `shatter-*` entries.

Observed failure from a full workspace `cargo test` run after the external-audit
TMPDIR race fix was merged:

```text
shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs::explore_respects_tmpdir_no_host_tmp_pollution

TMPDIR=/tmp/.tmpxjZrbA was set but Shatter created shatter-* entries in /tmp:
[
  "/tmp/shatter-observer-dedup-3438486-1780364522922511067.log",
  "/tmp/shatter-observer-timeout-3438486-1780364522819185691.log",
  "/tmp/shatter-observer-budget-3438486-1780364522819042291.log",
  "/tmp/shatter-observer-setup-3438486-1780364522828839179.log",
  "/tmp/shatter-observer-pool-3438486-1780364522896045255.log"
]
```

The child `shatter scan` process in the TMPDIR regression completed
successfully and wrote its report, which indicates the failure came from
concurrent test pollution rather than the child scan itself.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs` runs the real `shatter` binary with a
  sentinel `TMPDIR`, snapshots direct `/tmp/shatter-*` entries before and after
  the child process, and fails if any new host `/tmp` entries appear.
- `shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs` already takes the cross-test lock
  `common::host_tmp_shatter_lock()` before snapshotting `/tmp`.
- `shatter-cli/tests/common/mod.rs::host_tmp_shatter_lock` currently serializes
  CLI integration tests that are known to create host `/tmp/shatter-*` entries.
- `shatter-core/src/explorer.rs` has five observer-pool tests that create log
  paths with `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("shatter-observer-..."))`:
  `explore_function_observer_pool_uses_multiple_frontend_processes`,
  `explore_function_observer_pool_runs_function_setup_per_observer`,
  `explore_function_observer_pool_drains_in_flight_on_timeout`,
  `explore_function_observer_pool_suppresses_duplicate_candidates`, and
  `explore_function_observer_pool_budget_counts_executed_not_enqueued`.
- Those observer-pool tests do not currently share the `host_tmp_shatter_lock`
  used by the CLI integration tests.

## Desired Behavior

The TMPDIR regression test should only fail when the Shatter process under test
violates the TMPDIR contract. Observer-pool tests should not create global
`/tmp/shatter-*` entries that can race with that assertion during a normal
parallel workspace `cargo test` run.

## Acceptance Checks

- The observer-pool tests no longer create direct `/tmp/shatter-observer-*`
  files that can be observed by `shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs`.
- `shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs::explore_respects_tmpdir_no_host_tmp_pollution`
  still proves that the child `shatter scan` honors a caller-provided `TMPDIR`
  and writes at least one temp entry under the sentinel.
- A full workspace `cargo test` run passes with default Rust test parallelism.
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes.

## Scope

In scope:

- Test-harness isolation for observer-pool log files in `shatter-core`.
- Minimal shared test helper code if needed to coordinate with the CLI TMPDIR
  regression test.

Out of scope:

- Changing Pickpackit feature code.
- Skipping or weakening the TMPDIR regression assertion.
- Changing Shatter production observer behavior unless a focused reproduction
  shows production code ignores `TMPDIR`.
acceptance_criteria: Observer-pool tests do not create direct /tmp/shatter-observer-* files; tmpdir_regression still proves sentinel TMPDIR usage; full workspace cargo test passes; cargo clippy -- -D warnings passes.

title: External audit TMPDIR race
description:
Title: External audit TMPDIR race

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust, tests, tmpdir, scan

## Problem

The workspace `cargo test` gate can fail nondeterministically because the
integration test that asserts Shatter honors `TMPDIR` watches global `/tmp`
while another integration test can create `shatter-audit-*` directories there
at the same time.

Observed failure from a full Shatter `cargo test` run after building the
TypeScript frontend with `npm run build` from `shatter-ts/`:

```text
shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs::explore_respects_tmpdir_no_host_tmp_pollution

TMPDIR=/tmp/.tmpH19hLD was set but Shatter created shatter-* entries in /tmp:
["/tmp/shatter-audit-2843165-1", "/tmp/shatter-audit-2843165-0"]
```

A focused concurrent reproduction also fails when these two commands are run
at the same time from the same worktree:

```bash
cargo test -p shatter-cli --test tmpdir_regression -- --nocapture
cargo test -p shatter-cli --test scan_no_side_effects -- --nocapture
```

The `tmpdir_regression` command failed with new entries such as
`/tmp/shatter-audit-2870129-0` and `/tmp/shatter-audit-2870129-1`, while the
`scan_no_side_effects` command passed.

This blocks using the normal Rust quality gate to land fixes needed for the
Pickpackit validation work.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs` runs the real `shatter` binary with
  `TMPDIR` set to a sentinel tempdir, snapshots `/tmp` before and after the
  child process, and fails if any new direct `/tmp/shatter-*` entries appear.
- The same test also checks that `std::fs::read_dir(&sentinel_path)` contains
  at least one entry, which prevents a vacuous pass where the scan never
  exercised a temp-creation path under the sentinel.
- `shatter-cli/tests/scan_no_side_effects.rs` also runs the real `shatter`
  binary in external-audit mode (`-o <external> --no-cache --no-seeds`) but does
  not set `TMPDIR`, so its child process may create `/tmp/shatter-audit-*`
  directories during a parallel test run.
- External-audit storage is created by
  `shatter-cli/src/helpers.rs::apply_external_audit_storage`, which uses
  `std::env::temp_dir().join("shatter-audit-<pid>-<counter>")`.
- The explore command has a parallel external-audit setup in
  `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs` with the same
  `std::env::temp_dir().join("shatter-audit-<pid>-<counter>")` shape.
- Cargo can run integration test binaries concurrently by default, so one
  test binary's global `/tmp` writes can be observed by another test binary.

## Desired Behavior

The TMPDIR regression test should only fail when the Shatter process under test
violates the TMPDIR contract. Other integration tests should not create global
`/tmp/shatter-*` entries that can race with that assertion.

## Acceptance Checks

- The external-audit integration tests isolate their temporary roots so that
  `scan_no_side_effects` cannot create `/tmp/shatter-audit-*` during a normal
  parallel `cargo test` run.
- `shatter-cli/tests/tmpdir_regression.rs::explore_respects_tmpdir_no_host_tmp_pollution`
  still proves that the child `shatter scan` honors a caller-provided `TMPDIR`
  and writes at least one temp entry under the sentinel.
- A full workspace `cargo test` run passes with the default Rust test
  parallelism after the TypeScript frontend is built.
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes.

## Scope

In scope:

- Test-harness isolation for external-audit/TMPDIR integration tests.
- Minimal helper code in tests if needed to set per-test `TMPDIR` values.

Out of scope:

- Changing Pickpackit feature code.
- Changing Shatter's production external-audit storage semantics unless a
  focused reproduction shows production code ignores `TMPDIR`.
- Skipping the TMPDIR regression assertion or weakening it to ignore unrelated
  `/tmp/shatter-*` entries.
acceptance_criteria: External-audit integration tests isolate TMPDIR; tmpdir_regression still proves sentinel TMPDIR usage; full workspace cargo test passes after npm run build in shatter-ts; cargo clippy -- -D warnings passes.

title: Embedded extract tests race
description:
Title: Embedded extract tests race

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust, tests, embedded-frontend

## Problem

The required Shatter Rust quality gate `cargo test` can fail under the default
parallel test runner because embedded frontend extraction tests share fixed
directories under `/tmp`. A qlec verification run from the feature worktree
failed 8 tests after the code compiled successfully.

The failures all came from embedded frontend extraction tests trying to rename
or chmod temp files under shared test directories that no longer existed:

```text
embedded_frontend::tests::extract_to_cleans_up_old_bundles
embedded_frontend::tests::extract_to_is_idempotent
embedded_frontend::tests::extract_to_refreshes_stale_worker_when_bundle_hash_changes
embedded_frontend::tests::extract_to_writes_bundle_to_cache
embedded_frontend::tests::extract_to_writes_worker_bundle
embedded_go_frontend::tests::extract_to_cleans_up_old_binaries
embedded_go_frontend::tests::extract_to_is_idempotent
embedded_go_frontend::tests::extract_to_writes_binary_to_cache
```

Representative errors:

```text
failed to rename /tmp/shatter-test-extract/worker.js.<pid>.<n>.tmp -> /tmp/shatter-test-extract/worker.js: No such file or directory (os error 2)
failed to set permissions on go frontend binary: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

## Current Code Facts

- The affected tests live in `shatter-cli/src/embedded_frontend.rs` and
  `shatter-cli/src/embedded_go_frontend.rs`.
- The tests use deterministic `/tmp/shatter-test-*` directories.
- The failure occurs with ordinary `cargo test` in the workspace root, which is
  the required pre-completion gate for Shatter Rust changes.

## Desired Behavior

The embedded frontend extraction tests must be safe under the default parallel
Rust test runner. Each test should use an isolated temporary directory or other
race-free cleanup strategy so concurrent tests cannot delete another test's
working directory.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add or adjust tests/helpers so each embedded frontend and embedded Go frontend
  extraction test uses an isolated temp directory.
- `cargo test` passes from the Shatter workspace root with the default test
  thread count.
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes.
- The fix does not weaken production extraction behavior or skip the affected
  assertions.

## Scope

In scope:

- Test isolation and any tiny helper needed to create unique temp directories.
- The embedded frontend and embedded Go frontend extraction test modules.

Out of scope:

- Changing Pickpackit validation behavior.
- Changing Shatter runtime extraction semantics beyond what is required to keep
  the existing tests deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Embedded frontend and Go frontend extraction tests use isolated temp dirs; cargo test and cargo clippy -- -D warnings pass; production extraction behavior is unchanged.

title: Scan cleans stale function artifacts
description:
Title: Scan cleans stale function artifacts

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: scan, artifacts, pickpackit

## Problem

`shatter scan` can reuse the same deterministic scan artifact directory for a
later run over the same target corpus, while leaving function artifacts from an
earlier incomplete or invalid run in place. During Pickpackit validation this
made the artifact directory contain stale failures from a previous disk-full
run while a newer run was still in progress and overwriting only the functions
it had reached.

This makes whole-corpus validation ambiguous: a future agent reading
`shatter-artifacts/scan-results/<scan-id>/functions/*.json` can mistake stale
failures for current-run results, and a final report risks including stale
artifacts if cleanup/finalization reads the directory rather than only the
current run's completed work.

## Evidence

From the Pickpackit validation worktree:

```bash
cd /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api

PATH=/home/ketan/project/shatter/target/release:\
/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-bphx-pickpackit-seed-diversity/shatter-rust/target/release:$PATH \
DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-bphx-pickpackit-seed-diversity/shatter-rust \
SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-bphx-pickpackit-seed-diversity/shatter-rust-runtime \
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-cache-fe31829-bphx \
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 SHATTER_BUILD_TIMEOUT=300 \
shatter scan src/handlers --project-dir . --require-rust \
  --timeout-total 7200 --timeout-per-fn 300 --timeout-explore 240 \
  --request-timeout 300 --exec-timeout 240 --build-timeout 300 \
  --parallelism 1 --max-iterations 5 --progress --color never \
  -o /tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-handlers-fe31829-bphx-p1-m5.json
```

The run used scan artifact directory:

```text
shatter-artifacts/scan-results/729280c7b7d85ef1e403fb7045e18c9dc10a6395348c433937cd7199cc64073f/functions
```

That same directory already contained 75 function artifact files from an
earlier invalid run. While the new run had live progress through only about 36
functions, this command already returned `75`:

```bash
find shatter-artifacts/scan-results/729280c7b7d85ef1e403fb7045e18c9dc10a6395348c433937cd7199cc64073f/functions -name '*.json' | wc -l
```

Several unread functions still had stale errors from the earlier run, including
`No space left on device` paths under:

```text
api/.shatter/cache/harness/rust/crate-bridge/target/debug/deps
```

Those errors were not from the current run: live process inspection showed the
current crate-bridge builds were using the requested external cache root:

```text
/tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-cache-fe31829-bphx/rust/crate-bridge/target/debug/deps
```

## Desired Behavior

A scan run should not expose stale per-function artifacts as if they belonged
to the current run. Before writing current-run function artifacts for a
deterministic scan ID, Shatter should either:

- clean the previous `functions/` directory for that scan ID, or
- write each run into a unique attempt directory and make reports read only the
  selected attempt.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a regression test that creates a stale function artifact under a reused
  scan artifact directory, runs a scan that does not visit that function, and
  verifies the stale artifact is not present in the current run's function
  artifact set or final report.
- Preserve resume behavior if any scan mode intentionally reuses prior state:
  explicit resume/cache data must remain separate from current-run
  per-function result artifacts.
- Re-run a Pickpackit handler scan after the fix and verify the function
  artifact count and failed-function set match live current-run output rather
  than stale artifacts from a previous attempt.

## In Scope

- Scan artifact directory cleanup or attempt scoping.
- Report/finalization logic that enumerates per-function scan artifacts.
- Tests around stale artifact isolation.

## Out of Scope

- Fixing the separate Rust frontend broken-pipe/hang failures; those are
  tracked by `str-qlec`.
- Changing Pickpackit feature code.
- Changing deterministic codebase scan IDs unless that is the smallest safe
  way to isolate attempts.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test proves stale per-function artifacts from a reused scan artifact directory are absent from the current run artifact set or final report; intentional resume/cache state remains separate; Pickpackit scan validation, when available, matches current-run outputs rather than stale files.

title: Scan honors harness cache env
description:
## Problem

`shatter scan` currently overwrites a caller-provided `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE`
when project storage is applied to the Rust frontend. This prevents large
external validation runs from moving generated Rust crate-bridge harness builds
off the project filesystem.

During Pickpackit whole-handler validation, `/home` filled because crate-bridge
build outputs were forced into:

`api/.shatter/cache/harness/rust/crate-bridge/target`

even when the scan command was launched with:

`SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/shatter-pickpackit-harness-cache`

The rustc command line still used:

`.../api/.shatter/cache/harness/rust/crate-bridge/target/debug/deps`

The resulting full-corpus run failed with many `No space left on device (os
error 28)` compilation errors after the harness cache reached about 59G on
`/home`.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-cli/src/helpers.rs::apply_project_storage` constructs
  `HarnessStorage::for_project(project_root)` and appends its env vars to the
  frontend config whenever a project root is present.
- `shatter-core/src/harness_storage.rs::HarnessStorage::for_project` always
  uses `<project_root>/.shatter/cache/harness` for the cache root.
- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs::harness_cache_root` does honor
  `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE`, but the frontend receives the project default because
  the CLI appends that value after constructing project storage.
- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs::crate_bridge_target_dir` correctly places the
  shared crate-bridge target under the effective harness cache root, so the bug
  is in CLI storage-env resolution/propagation rather than crate-bridge target
  layout.

## Smallest Reproduction

1. Run a Rust `shatter scan` or execution path that uses crate-bridge harnesses
   with `--project-dir .` and `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/some-cache`.
2. Inspect the child Cargo/rustc command or generated paths.
3. Actual: build outputs still land under `<project>/.shatter/cache/harness`.
4. Expected: build outputs land under `/tmp/some-cache`.

The Pickpackit validation command that exposed this:

```bash
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/shatter-pickpackit-harness-cache \
DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-bphx-pickpackit-seed-diversity/shatter-rust \
SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/str-bphx-pickpackit-seed-diversity/shatter-rust-runtime \
shatter scan src/handlers --project-dir . --require-rust \
  --timeout-total 7200 --timeout-per-fn 300 --timeout-explore 240 \
  --request-timeout 300 --exec-timeout 240 --build-timeout 300 \
  --parallelism 1 --max-iterations 5 --progress --color never \
  -o /tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-handlers-str-bphx-p1-m5-harness-tmp.json
```

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused test proving project storage honors a pre-existing
  `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE` instead of overwriting it.
- Preserve default behavior when `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE` is unset: project scans
  should still use `<project>/.shatter/cache/harness`.
- Verify the Pickpackit scan can start crate-bridge compilation with rustc/Cargo
  output paths under the requested external cache root.

## In Scope

- CLI/core storage-env resolution for harness cache override behavior.
- Tests around `apply_project_storage` or `HarnessStorage` env resolution.
- This issue only needs to define precedence for `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE`;
  changing precedence for scratch or artifact env vars is out of scope unless
  it naturally falls out of a small shared helper and is covered by tests.

## Out of Scope

- Changing Pickpackit feature code.
- Reworking crate-bridge build caching semantics beyond honoring the existing
  `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE` knob.
- Solving separate frontend broken-pipe failures; those are tracked separately
  by `str-qlec`.

title: Rust frontend parallel broken pipe
description:
Pickpackit whole-corpus Rust handler scans with a custom native-generator frontend fail under moderate scan parallelism. The same handlers complete when scanned serially, so this appears to be a Shatter Rust frontend/orchestrator reliability gap under concurrent custom-frontend workload rather than a Pickpackit handler bug.

Observed command from `api/` in Pickpackit:
`shatter scan src/handlers --project-dir . --require-rust --timeout-total 3600 --timeout-per-fn 300 --timeout-explore 240 --request-timeout 300 --exec-timeout 240 --build-timeout 300 --parallelism 6 --max-iterations 5 --progress --color never -o /tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-handlers-str-bphx-m5.json`

Observed result:
- 75 exported handlers discovered.
- 60 completed, 13 failed, 0 unsupported, 2 skipped.
- All 13 failures reported `error: exploration error: frontend error: failed to write to frontend stdin: Broken pipe (os error 32)`.
- Failed functions included `item_images.rs::upload_item_image`, `items.rs::update_item_home_location`, several `legs.rs`, `packing_items.rs`, `tags.rs`, `tasks.rs`, and `workspaces.rs::workspaces`.

Control evidence:
- `workspaces.rs::{update_workspace,workspaces}` completed with 0 failures when scanned with the same timeouts and `--parallelism 1`.
- Earlier focused `item_images.rs` scans also completed with `--parallelism 1`.

Current workaround:
Run Pickpackit whole-corpus validation with `--parallelism 1` to avoid custom frontend broken pipes.
acceptance_criteria: Re-run a Pickpackit whole-corpus scan at --parallelism 6 --max-iterations 5 and verify that the observed broken-pipe failure set no longer occurs, or document a principled lower parallelism limit with an explicit diagnostic.
notes: 2026-06-01 update from Pickpackit full serial validation: after landing str-yoqb and running the full exported-handler scan with --parallelism 1 --max-iterations 5 and SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-cache-fe31829-bphx, the run still reproduced broken-pipe/timeout behavior. Live progress reached upload_item_image, which failed with 'frontend error: failed to write to frontend stdin: Broken pipe (os error 32)'. Later legs.rs::delete_leg failed/timed out, after which the parent shatter scan process slept in futex_wait_queue with no child cargo/rustc/frontend process and no further progress until interrupted with SIGINT. This expands the issue beyond parallelism 6: at least one whole-corpus serial run can broken-pipe and then hang after a function failure. The run was interrupted before a final report because the parent was idle with no child process.
close_reason: 4dbe6947 landed on main; Pickpackit full p6 m5 scan completed 73/75 handlers with 0 failed, 0 unsupported, and 2 config skips

title: Pickpackit seed diversity
description:
## Problem

Shatter can now execute the exported Rust handler corpus in `~/project/pickpackit/api/src/handlers`, but the generated behavior maps are too shallow to satisfy the project goal of exercising many branches with a good spread of inputs.

Evidence from the branch validation artifact `/tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-handlers-str-ounl.json`:

- `version: 6`
- 73 function entries, all `completion_outcome: behavioral`
- 73 discovered inputs total: exactly 1 input for each function
- 548 total detected branches
- only 1 covered branch total
- `upload_item_image` now reaches an HTTP handler result (`403 {"error":"forbidden"}`) instead of the old empty router 404, but still covers no branches in the full scan

The important evidence is copied above because `/tmp` artifacts are ephemeral.

The run command used for the artifact was:

```bash
shatter scan src/handlers --project-dir . --require-rust \
  --timeout-total 3600 --timeout-per-fn 300 --timeout-explore 240 \
  --request-timeout 300 --exec-timeout 240 --build-timeout 300 \
  --max-iterations 1 --progress --color never \
  -o /tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-handlers-str-ounl.json
```

The two skipped functions are intentional config skips:

- `src/handlers/legs.rs::fetch_legs_for_workspace`
- `src/handlers/tasks.rs::fetch_tasks_for_workspace`

Both are resource-bound SQL helpers covered by wrapper handlers.

## Desired Behavior

Shatter's Pickpackit validation setup should generate or retain multiple useful input variants for the exported handler corpus so behavior maps show meaningful branch and path diversity, not just one shallow authorization or not-found result per handler.

## In Scope

- Improve Shatter-side handling of native-generator recipes, replayed native values, seed reuse, or validation infrastructure so Pickpackit handlers get coherent workspace/account/path/body combinations.
- Add focused tests or validation checks that prove multiple inputs are emitted for representative Pickpackit-style Axum handlers. Good representative handlers from the current corpus include:
  - `src/handlers/item_images.rs::upload_item_image`
  - `src/handlers/bundles.rs::get_bundle`
  - `src/handlers/people.rs::create_person`
- Preserve the existing rule that Pickpackit feature code must not receive non-trivial changes.

## Out of Scope

- Rewriting Pickpackit handler feature logic.
- Removing handler code from the corpus.
- Counting sampled exploratory coverage as final success for the overall project goal.

## Acceptance

- A whole-corpus exported-handler run over `~/project/pickpackit/api/src/handlers` still completes with 0 failed and 0 unsupported functions, with only the two justified config skips.
- The resulting JSON behavior map contains more than one discovered input for at least two representative stateful handlers, or the issue documents a narrower next blocker with a reproducible Shatter failure.
- Aggregate branch coverage improves from the current baseline of 1 covered branch out of 548 detected branches to at least 25 covered branches, with the new baseline recorded in the issue closeout.

## Current Code Facts

- The Rust frontend native generator registry and replay support live under `shatter-rust/src/generators.rs` and `shatter-rust/src/handler.rs`.
- Axum harness request synthesis and native recipe path handling live in `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs`.
- Pickpackit validation uses native generators declared in `api/.shatter/config.yaml` and implemented under `api/.shatter/generators/`.
notes:
Landed partial seed-diversity fix on main in merge 91ffa5b9a735b05aca1483ad3181d79d1f880490. Scope: generator-backed concolic scans now honor the iteration budget, random prefetch scales with max_iterations for native generator sources, and reports preserve native replay raw executions as discovered inputs. Verified on rebased merge preview tree 65203c4aaa41bf66f403a73533a2d35e35047585 with npm ci, npm run build, cargo test (3778 passed, 21 ignored), cargo clippy -- -D warnings, task smoke, and task e2e (TS 20, Rust 3, Go 8 passed). Pickpackit samples improved: item_images m3 produced 6 inputs across 2 handlers with both handlers multi-input; bundles m3 produced 25 inputs across 9 handlers with 8/9 multi-input and 32 total line hits. str-bphx remains open because whole-corpus branch coverage acceptance is not yet met.
Post str-u52n validation from Shatter main dd8c66b71c785e1b04515933da971a7e55985430: Pickpackit repo-root scan with `--project-dir api` now finds the project-local Rust custom frontend; no native-generator custom-build warnings appeared. Focused health scan completed: 1 completed, 0 failed, 0 unsupported, 0 interrupted, 0 expected skipped; reports `/var/tmp/pickpackit-health-str-u52n-main.json` and `.md`.

Bounded broader handlers scan from repo root: `scan api/src/handlers --project-dir api --require-rust --max-iterations 1 --parallelism 1 --timeout-total 300 --timeout-per-fn 60 --timeout-explore 20 ...`. Final counts: 2 completed, 4 failed, 0 unsupported, 67 interrupted, 2 expected skipped. Reports: `/var/tmp/pickpackit-handlers-main-broad.json` and `.md`. Completed functions were `catalog.rs::apply_catalog_kit` (1 path, 16% coverage) and `destination_supplies.rs::create_destination_supply` (1 path, 0% coverage). Failed functions: `assistant.rs::apply_assistant_action` timed out during execution after 60s; `assistant.rs::assistant_message` timed out during task after 155s; `bundles.rs::create_bundle` timed out during execution after 60s; `health.rs::health` timed out during build after 180s. Remaining 67 were interrupted by total scan budget. Narrower next blocker: bounded Pickpackit scans need much better per-function throughput/build reuse or targeted timeout handling before whole-corpus branch/input diversity acceptance can be measured.
str-7sdw landed on main (merge 0cdc51167b208c20c4cfcbb6cf46713ecb535ea3; main now 7f531f5b). Focused Pickpackit health repo-root scan still completed 1/1 with 0 failed and no custom frontend warnings. Bounded broader serial handlers scan completed 6, failed 3, interrupted 64, expected-skipped 2; the two configured skips remained fetch_legs_for_workspace and fetch_tasks_for_workspace. The remaining failures now write structured timeout diagnostics in per-function artifacts, e.g. {kind: timeout, phase: execution, elapsed_secs: 60} for apply_assistant_action/apply_bundle and {kind: timeout, phase: task, elapsed_secs: 155} for assistant_message. This satisfies the diagnostic branch of str-7sdw and leaves the next narrower work as execution/task timeout root-cause fixes rather than artifact/report ambiguity.
Post str-plr2 validation from branch str-plr2-scan-explore-timeout-ignored / merge 14bf9814b5ae716319700882c9b80a5723308a36: shared-pool scan now honors explicit timeout_explore. Focused assistant-only Pickpackit scan with --timeout-per-fn 10 --timeout-explore 5 reported both exported assistant handlers as timed out during execution after 5s instead of 10s. Bounded broader handlers scan with --timeout-total 300 --timeout-per-fn 60 --timeout-explore 20 attempted 14/75 functions, completed 1 (health), failed 11, interrupted 61, expected-skipped 2, unsupported 0. Execution-timeout failures now report 20s; task-watchdog failures now report 115s (90 build + 20 explore + 5 cleanup), confirming watchdog sizing also uses the effective explore timeout. The two configured skips remain fetch_legs_for_workspace and fetch_tasks_for_workspace. This fixes the timeout-plumbing bug, but str-bphx remains blocked on throughput/build reuse or targeted timeout strategy because a 20s explore cap improves budget enforcement while still leaving whole-corpus completion and coverage far below acceptance.

comments.author: Test User
comments.text: Mechanism identified (2026-07-06, via pickpackit pp-v2rz.9 validation): the concolic scan path invokes a native generator ONCE, captures one recipe, and replays it symbolically for all iterations — SEED_COUNTER-style per-invocation variation in generators never advances (every captured recipe carries sequence:0), so scenario spread written into generators is inert under scan. The 40+ behavior clusters observed come from symbolic mutation of mocked body fields, not generator variation. Uncovered branches are exactly the ones needing FK-valid/membership-checked UUIDs the solver cannot fabricate (e.g. pickpackit ensure_account_in_workspace arms). Fix direction: engine-side per-draw generator re-invocation — re-invoke the generator (or honor a per-draw recipe parameter like 'sequence') for each concrete draw, so native-replay generators can supply a scenario STREAM instead of a pinned value. Cross-language: generators-as-streams generalizes to TS/Go/Rust factories and would map to C++/Java factory interfaces; protocol change is a per-draw index/recipe field in the generate/execute exchange.

title: Axum recipe path arity mismatch
description:
Title: Axum recipe path arity mismatch

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: rust,axum,pickpackit,input-generation

## Problem

Shatter's Rust Axum harness can prefer a native generator's `recipe.axum.path`
even when that path has fewer segments than the handler's `Path<T>` extractor
requires. For tuple path handlers this can route the request to no handler at
all, returning Axum's empty HTTP 404 and recording no executed handler lines or
branches. The function is then reported as `behavioral`, but the behavior map
is shallow and does not exercise the handler body.

## Current Evidence

From `/home/ketan/project/shatter` at `main` commit `82690a3e`
(`bd sync: close str-62pj`), the landed Pickpackit exported-handler scan was:

```bash
cd /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api

PATH=/tmp/shatter-target-pickpackit-main-final/release:/tmp/shatter-target-pickpackit-rust-main-final/release:$PATH \
DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust \
SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust-runtime \
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/shatter-harness-pickpackit-main-final \
SHATTER_BUILD_TIMEOUT=300 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 \
shatter scan src/handlers --project-dir . --require-rust \
  --timeout-total 3600 --timeout-per-fn 300 --timeout-explore 240 \
  --request-timeout 300 --exec-timeout 240 --build-timeout 300 \
  --max-iterations 1 --progress --color never \
  -o /tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-handlers-main-final.json
```

The scan completed the exported handler corpus:

```text
Scan complete: 73 completed, 0 failed, 0 unsupported, 2 skipped (8 workers)
```

The two skips are intentional `skip=true` config entries for SQL resource
helpers already covered through wrapper handlers:

- `src/handlers/legs.rs::fetch_legs_for_workspace`
- `src/handlers/tasks.rs::fetch_tasks_for_workspace`

However, the `upload_item_image` behavior map shows a router-level 404 rather
than handler execution:

```json
{
  "display_name": "upload_item_image",
  "completion_outcome": "behavioral",
  "branch_count": 13,
  "branches_covered": 0,
  "coverage_pct": 0.0,
  "discovered_inputs": [
    {
      "inputs": [
        "State native handle",
        "current native handle with recipe.axum.path=/test/<workspace_id>",
        null,
        null
      ],
      "return_value": {"body": "", "headers": {}, "status": 404},
      "lines_executed": []
    }
  ]
}
```

The Pickpackit handler signature needs two path segments:

```rust
pub async fn upload_item_image(
    State(state): State<AppState>,
    current: CurrentAccount,
    Path((workspace_id, item_id)): Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
    mut multipart: Multipart,
) -> ApiResult<Json<Item>>
```

The native `current` generator recipe supplies only a workspace path:

```json
{
  "account_id": "...",
  "workspace_id": "...",
  "axum": {
    "path": "/test/<workspace_id>"
  }
}
```

Because the generated route pattern for `Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>` is
`/test/{p0}/{p1}`, using `/test/<workspace_id>` cannot match the route. The
result is Axum's empty 404 before the handler body runs.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs::axum_route_pattern_for_path` maps tuple path
  extractors to a matching number of route placeholders, e.g.
  `Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>` becomes `/test/{p0}/{p1}`.
- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs::axum_default_path_value_for_path` can generate
  a parseable default path with the same tuple arity, e.g. two UUID segments.
- `generate_axum_harness` currently reads `axum_recipe_field("path")` before
  falling back to generated `Path` input/defaults.
- The existing unit test
  `generate_axum_harness_prefers_recipe_path_over_generated_path_input`
  explicitly asserts that recipe path lookup precedes generated path lookup,
  but it does not check whether the recipe path matches the route pattern's
  required segment count.
- `generate_axum_harness_with_tuple_path_uses_matching_route_segments` already
  protects route/default arity for tuple `Path`, so the gap is specifically the
  unchecked native recipe override.

## Desired Behavior

The Axum harness should not let a native recipe path with the wrong segment
arity bypass handler execution. For a handler route such as `/test/{p0}/{p1}`,
a recipe path like `/test/<workspace_id>` should either be extended with safe
generated defaults for missing path segments or rejected in favor of the
generated full-arity path. In either case the request should route to the
handler instead of returning a router-level 404.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused Rust frontend regression for an Axum handler with
  `Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>` and a native replay recipe containing
  `{"axum":{"path":"/test/<one-uuid>"}}`; before the fix it returns the
  router-level empty 404 or records no handler execution, and after the fix the
  handler body is invoked.
- Preserve support for valid full-arity recipe paths, e.g.
  `/test/<uuid-a>/<uuid-b>` should still win over generated defaults.
- Preserve tuple path route/default generation tests for
  `Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>`.
- Re-run a focused Pickpackit validation for
  `src/handlers/item_images.rs::upload_item_image` and verify the artifact no
  longer has `return_value.status == 404` with empty body and
  `lines_executed == []` from router miss.
- Re-run the exported `src/handlers` Pickpackit scan and verify it still has
  0 failed and 0 unsupported functions, with the same two configured skips
  justified.

## In Scope

- Rust Axum harness path synthesis and native recipe path validation/fallback.
- Tests in `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs` or nearby Rust frontend tests.
- Pickpackit validation using the existing validation worktree and database.

## Out of Scope

- Non-trivial Pickpackit feature-code changes.
- Exhaustive branch/input spread tuning for all handlers.
- Browser-equivalent multipart fuzzing for every possible multipart schema.
acceptance_criteria: Regression covers one-segment native recipe path for tuple Path; valid full-arity recipe paths still win; focused Pickpackit upload_item_image no longer router-404s with no lines; exported handler scan remains 0 failed/unsupported with justified skips

title: Go overlay build generation races
description:
Title: Go overlay build generation races

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,kapow,concolic,overlay

## Symptom

Fresh current-main Kapow scan of /home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow with parallelism 8 produced 333 completed, 637 failed, 160 unsupported out of 1130 discovered functions. The dominant failures are total-budget timeouts, but the actionable build failures include corrupted generated overlay sources: empty files, EOF syntax errors, invalid inserted statements, mixed main/shattertarget package errors, and instrumented files reporting package shattertarget where Go expected package main.

Representative current artifact: /tmp/str-np0w-kapow-full-current.json

Representative errors:
- workspace: materialized source file is empty: .../instrumented/fields.go
- loghandler.go:1:1: expected 'package', found 'EOF'
- importer_climate_normals.go:1:1: expected 'package', found 'EOF'
- .shatter-launchers/.../main.go:7:2: found packages shattertarget (admissions.go) and main (importer_climate_normals.go)
- instrumented/importer_deadlines_bigfuture.go:1:1: package shattertarget; expected package main

## Current Code Facts

- shatter-go/protocol/prepared_launcher.go calls build.NewBuilder(ws).Build(...) for each direct execution preparation.
- build.Builder.Build has a mutex, but it is per Builder instance.
- The cache key for a package build is shared across many targets in the same package. In the Kapow failures the common base is 741b71f36db823e8 with mock-sensitive suffixes.
- Builder.Build writes generated wrapper, instrumented package files, test stubs, runtime helpers, and overlay manifests under the shared workspace generated directory for the cache key before launcher.BuildLauncher's binary lock is acquired.
- Therefore separate Builder instances can concurrently write and rewrite the same generated files for the same cache key during a parallel scan.

## Desired Behavior

For a given cache key, only one process/goroutine should generate overlay files and build/register the launcher binary at a time, even when separate Builder instances prepare targets concurrently. Other callers should wait and then reuse the registered binary. Generated source files should not be truncated, partially rewritten, or observed mid-write by peer builders.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add or update a focused Go test that exercises concurrent Build calls through separate Builder instances for the same request/cache key.
- The test demonstrates the pre-fix race or otherwise verifies the cross-builder serialization contract.
- Fresh focused Kapow validation no longer emits generated-source corruption errors (empty materialization, EOF package errors, mixed main/shattertarget, or package shattertarget expected main) for the previously failing class under parallelism.
- Focused Go package tests pass.

## In Scope

- shatter-go build/launcher generation locking and registry recheck behavior.
- Tests in shatter-go/build or directly adjacent packages.

## Out of Scope

- Overall Kapow total-budget timeout throughput.
- Semantic coverage improvements or branch input spread.
- Unrelated AST instrumentation placement bugs that reproduce deterministically without concurrent generated-file races.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent same-cache-key Go builds are serialized across Builder instances; focused parallel Kapow validation no longer emits generated-source corruption or mixed package errors.
notes: Focused current-main validation did not reproduce the mixed package class. Single-worker cache_compress.go scan completed 5/5 with 0 failed. Parallel subset scan including admissions*.go, colorhandler.go, cmd_scraper_inspect.go, and cache_compress.go completed 23 functions with 0 failed and 7 unsupported. tools/kapow is a module root (module github.com/ketang/kapow/tools/kapow), not a module subdirectory as initially drafted. Leaving open for future evidence rather than implementing against stale artifact evidence.

title: Rust while-let instrumentation
description:
## Context

The Pickpackit image upload route still cannot execute after Axum `Multipart`
extractor classification/request synthesis work begins, because the Rust
instrumenter emits invalid Rust for an async `while let` condition.

This is a separate gap from multipart request construction: the generated Axum
harness reaches compilation, but the instrumented source fails because the
`while let Some(field) = ...` condition is transformed into a plain expression
that starts with `let`, and the loop body then references a pattern binding that
was never introduced.

## Reproduction

From a Shatter worktree, run the multipart harness regression test introduced
while working on `str-62pj`. At filing time, this regression test exists only
on the `str-62pj-axum-multipart-extractor` feature branch; the smaller
instrumentation regression for this issue should be added on this issue's own
branch before or alongside the fix.

```bash
SHATTER_BUILD_TIMEOUT=300 cargo test --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml multipart -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture
```

Observed failing test:

```text
executor::tests::execute_axum_handler_sends_default_multipart_file_part
```

The temporary handler used by that test contains:

```rust
use axum::extract::Multipart;

pub async fn upload(mut multipart: Multipart) -> String {
    while let Some(field) = multipart.next_field().await.unwrap() {
        let name = field.name().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let filename = field.file_name().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let bytes = field.bytes().await.unwrap();
        return format!("{}:{}:{}", name, filename, bytes.len());
    }
    "empty".to_string()
}
```

The generated temporary crate fails with errors like:

```text
error: expected expression, found `let` statement
while { let __shatter_cond = let Some (field) = multipart.next_field().await.unwrap(); ... }

error[E0425]: cannot find value `field` in this scope
```

## Pickpackit Evidence

Pickpackit has the same shape in `api/src/handlers/item_images.rs`:

```rust
async fn read_file_part(multipart: &mut Multipart) -> ApiResult<Vec<u8>> {
    while let Some(field) = multipart
        .next_field()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| ApiError::BadRequest(format!("invalid multipart: {e}")))?
    {
        if field.name() == Some("file") {
            ...
        }
    }
    ...
}
```

That helper is called by `upload_item_image`, so the whole-corpus Pickpackit
handler scan cannot complete this route until `while let` instrumentation
preserves the pattern binding and emits compilable code.

## Desired Behavior

The Rust frontend should instrument `while let` conditions without converting
the `let` pattern into an invalid expression. The generated code should compile,
preserve the pattern binding inside the loop body, and still record loop/branch
execution consistently with ordinary `while` loops.

## Protocol-Visible Behavior

- Does this change protocol message shape? no
- Is cross-frontend protocol parity affected? no
- Is this Rust frontend behavior only? yes

## Scope

In scope:

- Fix Rust instrumentation for `while let` loop conditions.
- Add a regression test that fails on current invalid generated code and passes
  after the fix.
- Verify the multipart harness regression from `str-62pj` can compile past the
  `while let` handler shape.

Out of scope:

- Full multipart support or request construction changes; those remain covered
  by `str-62pj`.
- Reworking all loop instrumentation.
- Non-trivial Pickpackit feature-code changes.

## Acceptance Checks

- A focused Rust test covers an async or non-async function containing
  `while let Some(x) = ...` and proves Shatter emits compilable instrumented
  code with `x` visible in the loop body and a `loop_enter` event still emitted
  for the loop.
- `SHATTER_BUILD_TIMEOUT=300 cargo test --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml multipart -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture` no longer fails with `expected expression, found let statement` or missing `field` binding.
- The fix is limited to Rust frontend instrumentation/harness test code and
  does not modify Pickpackit feature behavior.

title: Go overlay go.mod update fails
description:
Title: Go overlay go.mod update fails

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,kapow-validation,overlay

## Problem

Broad Shatter scans of Kapow Go modules fail many otherwise-discovered functions during launcher build with:

```text
go: updates to go.mod needed, but go.mod is part of the overlay specified with -overlay
```

This is a Shatter-owned Go launcher/build failure. It prevents Kapow whole-corpus validation from approaching the requested 90% execution target and turns large parts of the corpus into `InstrumentationFailed` results before behavior exploration can run.

## Current Evidence

After building `/home/ketan/project/shatter/target/release/shatter`, run from the target module root:

```bash
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/kapow-tools-kapow-artifacts-20260531 \
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/kapow-tools-kapow-harness-20260531 \
SHATTER_GO_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/tmp/kapow-tools-kapow-workspace-20260531 \
/home/ketan/project/shatter/target/release/shatter scan . \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/kapow \
  --language go --all --no-cache --parallelism 8 \
  --request-timeout 180 --timeout-total 1800 \
  --exclude '**/.shatter/**' --exclude '**/.shatter-cache/**' \
  --exclude '**/.shatter-launchers/**' --exclude '**/shatter-artifacts/**' \
  --exclude '**/*.pb.go' --exclude '**/*_gen.go' \
  --exclude '**/zz_generated*.go' --exclude '**/generated.go' \
  --output /tmp/kapow-tools-kapow-scan-20260531.md \
  --output /tmp/kapow-tools-kapow-scan-20260531.json \
  --timing summary --timing-output /tmp/kapow-tools-kapow-timing-20260531.json \
  --timing-format json --log-level warn
```

Observed result in `/tmp/kapow-tools-kapow-scan-20260531.json`:

- `total_discovered_functions`: 1130
- `completed_functions`: 342
- `failed_functions`: 628
- `unsupported_functions`: 160
- The dominant failure text appears about 430 times in the failed reasons:
  `go: updates to go.mod needed, but go.mod is part of the overlay specified with -overlay`

A smaller module reproduces the same failure class:

```bash
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/kapow-tools-dbverify-artifacts-20260531 \
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/kapow-tools-dbverify-harness-20260531 \
SHATTER_GO_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/tmp/kapow-tools-dbverify-workspace-20260531 \
/home/ketan/project/shatter/target/release/shatter scan . \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/dbverify \
  --language go --all --no-cache --parallelism 4 \
  --request-timeout 120 --timeout-total 600 \
  --exclude '**/.shatter/**' --exclude '**/.shatter-cache/**' \
  --exclude '**/.shatter-launchers/**' --exclude '**/shatter-artifacts/**' \
  --output /tmp/kapow-tools-dbverify-scan.json
```

Observed result from the module batch summary:

- `total_discovered_functions`: 87
- `completed_functions`: 2
- `failed_functions`: 82
- Representative failed function: `/home/ketan/project/kapow/tools/dbverify/content.go::ensureOnPath`
- Representative failed reason:

```text
error: exploration error: unexpected response from frontend: execute error (InstrumentationFailed): build failed: build: compilation failed for <hash>: launcher: go build: exit status 1
go: updates to go.mod needed, but go.mod is part of the overlay specified with -overlay
```

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-go/launcher/launcher.go` builds launchers with `go build -mod=mod -buildvcs=false` and appends `-overlay <overlayPath>` when a wrapper or augmented `go.mod` overlay is needed.
- The same file's `buildCombinedOverlay` overlays the target module's `go.mod` with an augmented copy when `UseHarnessLoop` is enabled.
- `writeAugmentedGoMod` currently adds `require shatter-harness v0.0.0`, adds a `replace shatter-harness => <HarnessRuntimeDir>`, and bumps the `go` directive high enough for the harness module. It does not ensure that the overlaid module graph is otherwise tidy for modules whose original `go.mod` needs updates under `-mod=mod`.
- The failure happens before function execution, so it is not caused by Kapow feature logic.

## Desired Behavior

Shatter should build Go launchers without asking the Go tool to update an overlaid `go.mod`, or should generate an augmented module overlay that is already acceptable to `go build`. Kapow modules that currently fail with this `go.mod` overlay error should proceed to execution or fail for more specific function-level reasons.

## Acceptance Checks

- Add a focused regression fixture or test that reproduces a launcher build where `go build -mod=mod -overlay <go.mod overlay>` would try to update the overlaid `go.mod`.
- The fix makes that fixture pass without modifying the target module's real `go.mod` or `go.sum`.
- A targeted Kapow scan of `tools/dbverify` no longer has the `go: updates to go.mod needed, but go.mod is part of the overlay specified with -overlay` failure class.
- A targeted Kapow scan of `tools/kapow` has zero occurrences of the failure text `go: updates to go.mod needed, but go.mod is part of the overlay specified with -overlay`; any remaining build failures must have different, more specific root causes.

## In Scope

- Go launcher build arguments and overlay generation.
- Augmented `go.mod` / module graph handling in generated Shatter workspace files.
- Tests in `shatter-go` that cover the failure without depending on Kapow.
- Targeted Kapow validation runs after the fix.

## Out of Scope

- Changing Kapow feature code.
- Solving unrelated execution timeouts or unsupported opaque parameter types.
- Solving the separate target-working-directory side effect where executed functions write fuzz output into the target repo.
- Solving the separate API generated enum corruption failures around `internal/search/field_name_gen.go`.

title: Go scan sandbox fan-out hang
description:
Title: Go scan hangs on sandbox fan-out

Type: bug
Priority: 1
Labels: go,sandbox,scan

## Problem

A whole-corpus Go scan of Zolem can stop making progress while Shatter and Go
frontend subprocesses remain alive. Per-function/request timeouts do not cleanly
finish the scan, and stale Docker sandbox containers remain running until the
operator interrupts the run.

## Reproduction

From `/home/ketan/project/shatter` on main commit
`fdd809731ff2e84ed9ff9ca3aad1059e1cb957a8`, after building
`shatter-cli` release, run:

```bash
SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker \
SHATTER_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE=golang:1.26-bookworm \
SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/zolem-shatter-artifacts-main-proof2 \
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/zolem-shatter-harness-main-proof2 \
SHATTER_GO_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/tmp/shatter-go-workspaces-main-proof2 \
/tmp/shatter-target-zolem-main-proof/release/shatter scan \
  --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem \
  --language go \
  --all \
  --no-cache \
  --timeout-total 7200 \
  --timeout-per-fn 180 \
  --timeout-explore 180 \
  --request-timeout 180 \
  --build-timeout 180 \
  --exec-timeout 30 \
  --output /tmp/zolem-main-proof2.md \
  --output /tmp/zolem-main-proof2.json \
  .
```

## Observed Evidence

- The scan discovered 360 functions, selected 326, and skipped 34 unsupported
  signatures.
- Artifacts were written through index 00281; `sleepContext` and
  `loadOpenAPIDocument` both wrote artifacts in this run.
- The artifact directory contained 280 per-function JSON files:
  `/tmp/zolem-shatter-artifacts-main-proof2/scan-results/f567f4913aa8e0851e9373cffbe6e3254468c7e6aab90ea2a4aa9856c329dc4a/functions`.
- No aggregate outputs were written at `/tmp/zolem-main-proof2.json` or
  `/tmp/zolem-main-proof2.md`.
- Artifact timestamps stopped advancing for roughly 40 minutes while the
  top-level `shatter scan` process, Go frontend subprocesses, and 13 Docker
  sandbox containers remained alive.
- `pstree -ap <shatter-pid>` showed the top-level scan waiting under multiple
  `go-frontend-b8a...` children with Docker sandbox children.
- Manual interruption and container cleanup were required.

## Expected Behavior

When a Go function, frontend request, build, or sandbox execution exceeds the
configured timeout, Shatter should record the function as failed/skipped,
terminate associated frontend/sandbox subprocesses, continue the scan, and
eventually write aggregate Markdown/JSON outputs. `--timeout-total` should also
abort the run and clean child processes instead of leaving a silent live scan.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reproduction run with Docker sandboxing and explicit timeouts exits without
  manual intervention, even if tail functions hang or exceed timeout.
- Timed-out functions are represented in the final scan JSON/Markdown failure
  accounting.
- No Docker sandbox containers or orphan Go frontend/harness subprocesses remain
  after timeout or scan completion.

## In Scope

- Timeout propagation and cleanup for Go frontend requests and Docker sandbox
  executions.
- Scan finalization when a worker/frontend child is stuck.
- A focused regression test or harness-level test that proves cleanup/final
  accounting for a hung Go execution path.

## Out of Scope

- Improving Zolem coverage or adding new type factories.
- Changing Zolem feature code.
- Broad redesign of the scan scheduler beyond what is needed to make timeout
  and cleanup behavior reliable.
acceptance_criteria: No Docker sandbox containers or orphan Go frontend/harness subprocesses remain after timeout or completion
notes: Additional evidence from a second run: reran from /home/ketan/project/zolem with --parallelism 1 and fresh proof3 temp directories. The run again selected 326/360 functions and skipped the same 34 unsupported signatures. It wrote 276 per-function artifacts and reached internal/specs/openapi.go::loadOpenAPIDocument, but no aggregate /tmp/zolem-main-proof3.json or .md was written. The top-level command exited with signal 9 before --timeout-total 7200, after the same late OpenAPI/spec region. No Docker containers were left behind in this second run; the remaining visible go-frontend processes belonged to a separate Kapow workspace and were left untouched.

title: Pickpackit resource helper skips
description:
Title: Pickpackit resource helper skips
Type: task
Labels: rust,pickpackit,scan

## Context

The whole-corpus Pickpackit handler scan includes public SQL helper functions in handler modules as exported scan targets. Two of these helpers take `&PgPool` and are not standalone request entrypoints, so Shatter reports them as JSON-harness failures even though the route handlers that call them execute.

## Reproduction

From the Pickpackit validation worktree:

```bash
cd /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api
PATH=/tmp/shatter-target-pickpackit-root/release:/tmp/shatter-target-pickpackit-rust/release:$PATH \
DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust \
SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust-runtime \
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/shatter-harness-pickpackit-full-main-1 \
SHATTER_BUILD_TIMEOUT=300 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 \
shatter scan src/handlers --project-dir . --require-rust \
  --timeout-total 3600 --timeout-per-fn 300 --timeout-explore 240 \
  --request-timeout 300 --exec-timeout 240 --build-timeout 300 \
  --max-iterations 1 --progress --color never \
  -o /tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-handlers-main-1.json
```

Observed failures:

```text
src/handlers/legs.rs::fetch_legs_for_workspace
unsupported: crate_bridge: function fetch_legs_for_workspace is not JSON-harness compatible: function parameters are not JSON-harness compatible and may not implement DeserializeOwned

src/handlers/tasks.rs::fetch_tasks_for_workspace
unsupported: crate_bridge: function fetch_tasks_for_workspace is not JSON-harness compatible: function parameters are not JSON-harness compatible and may not implement DeserializeOwned
```

## Current Code Facts

- Pickpackit validation config path: `/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api/.shatter/config.yaml`.
- Shatter config supports per-function `skip: true` through `FunctionConfig.skip` in `shatter-core/src/config.rs`; the scan path checks `resolved.skip` in `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs` and logs `Skipping ... (skip=true in config)`.
- Existing Pickpackit validation config uses scan-style function keys under `functions:`, for example `"**/bundles.rs::get_bundle"`.
- `src/handlers/legs.rs::fetch_legs_for_workspace` signature:

```rust
pub async fn fetch_legs_for_workspace(
    pool: &PgPool,
    workspace_id: Uuid,
) -> sqlx::Result<Vec<TripLeg>>
```

- The route handler `list_workspace_legs` calls `fetch_legs_for_workspace(&state.pool, workspace_id)` and completed in the same full scan.
- `src/handlers/tasks.rs::fetch_tasks_for_workspace` signature:

```rust
pub async fn fetch_tasks_for_workspace(
    pool: &PgPool,
    workspace_id: Uuid,
) -> ApiResult<Vec<TripTask>>
```

- The route handler `list_workspace_tasks` calls `fetch_tasks_for_workspace(&state.pool, workspace_id)` and completed in the same full scan.
- These helpers are public because application code reuses them, but they are resource-bound helper functions rather than independently callable request entrypoints.

## Desired Behavior

The Pickpackit validation setup should avoid counting these resource-bound public helpers as failed feature-code entrypoints. A justified Shatter config skip is acceptable for this issue if it records that the code is covered indirectly by the corresponding route handlers. A Shatter-side classification improvement is also acceptable if it is narrow and well tested.

## Protocol-Visible Behavior

- Does this change the wire format or semantics of any protocol message? no
- If yes, which commands or fields are affected: N/A
- Is this change backward-compatible? N/A

## Parity Impact

- [ ] `buildSymExpr` (instrumentor.ts) - N/A
- [ ] `buildSymExprWithFlow` (instrumentor.ts) - N/A
- [ ] Random explorer (`shatter-core/src/explorer.rs`) - N/A
- [ ] Concolic orchestrator (`shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs`) - N/A
- [ ] CLI wiring in `main.rs` - verify no new CLI/config option is required, or wire both paths if one is added

## Default Behavior

- Is new functionality enabled by default? N/A for config-only skip; yes if implemented in Shatter classification
- If no, what flag or config option enables it: Pickpackit `.shatter/config.yaml` skip entries if config-only

## Required Test Updates

- [ ] Config-only path: run a whole Pickpackit handler scan showing these helpers are skipped/excluded with documented reasons, not failed
- [ ] Shatter-code path: unit tests added or updated for the scan classification change
- [ ] E2E concolic tests verified where relevant
- [ ] Conformance tests verified if protocol-visible behavior changes

## Contract Updates

- Are runtime contracts needed? no
- If yes, identify the trust boundary that justifies them: N/A
- Confirm all three qualifying criteria are met: N/A

## Acceptance Checks

- `fetch_legs_for_workspace` and `fetch_tasks_for_workspace` are no longer counted as failed functions in the whole Pickpackit `src/handlers` scan.
- Any skip/exclusion is documented with a reason tying each helper to its covering route handler.
- No Pickpackit feature code is deleted or behaviorally changed.

title: Axum multipart extractor support
description:
Title: Axum multipart extractor support
Type: feature
Labels: rust,axum,pickpackit,input-generation

## Context

The whole-corpus Pickpackit handler scan now reaches most exported handler code, but the image upload route still fails before execution because Shatter's Rust Axum adapter reports `Multipart` as an unsupported extractor.

## Reproduction

From the Pickpackit validation worktree:

```bash
cd /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api
PATH=/tmp/shatter-target-pickpackit-root/release:/tmp/shatter-target-pickpackit-rust/release:$PATH \
DATABASE_URL=postgres://pickpackit:pickpackit@localhost:55432/pickpackit \
SHATTER_RUST_SRC=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust \
SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH=/home/ketan/project/shatter/shatter-rust-runtime \
SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=/tmp/shatter-harness-pickpackit-full-main-1 \
SHATTER_BUILD_TIMEOUT=300 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 \
shatter scan src/handlers --project-dir . --require-rust \
  --timeout-total 3600 --timeout-per-fn 300 --timeout-explore 240 \
  --request-timeout 300 --exec-timeout 240 --build-timeout 300 \
  --max-iterations 1 --progress --color never \
  -o /tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-handlers-main-1.json
```

Observed summary:

```text
Scanning 75 exported functions
Scan complete: 71 completed, 4 failed, 0 unsupported, 0 skipped
```

The multipart-specific failure is:

```text
src/handlers/item_images.rs::upload_item_image
unsupported: axum handler has unsupported extractor types: Multipart
```

## Current Code Facts

- Shatter's Axum extractor recognizer includes `"Multipart"` in `AXUM_EXTRACTOR_TYPES` at `shatter-rust/src/adapters.rs`, but `execute_with_adapter` rejects mappings whose kind is `Unsupported` with the message `axum handler has unsupported extractor types: ...`.
- The existing adapter test coverage in `shatter-rust/src/adapters.rs` currently asserts that `Multipart` is reported as unsupported, so this issue should update that expectation or add replacement coverage.
- Pickpackit route signature:

```rust
pub async fn upload_item_image(
    State(state): State<AppState>,
    current: CurrentAccount,
    Path((workspace_id, item_id)): Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
    mut multipart: Multipart,
) -> ApiResult<Json<Item>>
```

- The handler expects multipart/form-data with a `file` part, processes the uploaded bytes through Pickpackit's image pipeline, stores WebP renditions, updates the item row, and enqueues the previous image prefix for cleanup.
- Other routes in `src/handlers/item_images.rs`, including `delete_item_image`, are now executable by Shatter.

## Desired Behavior

Shatter's Rust Axum harness should support enough multipart request construction to execute handlers that use `axum::extract::Multipart`, including a generated or recipe-provided file part. A minimal image upload payload is acceptable if it exercises the handler without requiring external feature-code changes in Pickpackit.

- If yes, which commands or fields are affected: N/A

- [ ] Property tests added if a new public helper is introduced

Title: Rust direct native params
Type: feature

## Context

The whole-corpus Pickpackit handler scan fails on the `session` route because Shatter classifies it as a direct Rust function and requires JSON-deserializable parameters. The route takes Pickpackit's `CurrentAccount` auth extractor directly, and the validation config already has a native generator for `CurrentAccount`.

## Reproduction

From the Pickpackit validation worktree:

```bash
cd /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api

  --timeout-total 3600 --timeout-per-fn 300 --timeout-explore 240 \
  --request-timeout 300 --exec-timeout 240 --build-timeout 300 \
  --max-iterations 1 --progress --color never \
  -o /tmp/shatter-pickpackit-full-handlers-main-1.json
```

Observed failure:

```text
src/handlers/session.rs::session
unsupported: crate_bridge: function session is not JSON-harness compatible: function parameters are not JSON-harness compatible and may not implement DeserializeOwned
```

## Current Code Facts

- Pickpackit validation config path: `/home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/pickpackit/shatter-str-l5ru-validation/api/.shatter/config.yaml`.
- Relevant config defaults:

```yaml
defaults:
  generators:
    State: generators/pickpackit.rs
    CurrentAccount: generators/pickpackit.rs
  param_generators:
    current: generators/pickpackit.rs
```

- Shatter resolves param/type generator config into `ExploreConfig.value_sources` in `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs`, but direct JSON-harness compatibility can still reject non-Deserialize params before a native generator constructs them.
- Pickpackit route source:

```rust
use axum::Json;
use crate::{auth::CurrentAccount, domain::Account, error::ApiResult};

pub async fn session(current: CurrentAccount) -> ApiResult<Json<Account>> {
    Ok(Json(Account::from(current)))
}
```

- Axum handlers with explicit `State`, `Path`, and `Json` extractors can now use native generators, but direct Rust function execution still rejects non-JSON params before native generation can construct them.

Shatter should be able to execute direct Rust functions whose parameters are supplied by configured native generators, or otherwise classify this common auth-extractor-only Axum route shape into the Rust Axum harness path.
