title: Parity enforcement: buildSymExprWithFlow must handle all node types that buildSymExpr handles
description:
instrumentor.ts has two functions that build symbolic expressions: buildSymExprWithFlow() (lines 278-352, used during data flow analysis) and buildSymExpr() (lines 860-951, used during branch condition analysis). They handle different sets of AST node types, causing silent data loss.

buildSymExpr() handles: Identifier, PropertyAccessExpression, CallExpression, PrefixUnaryExpression, BinaryExpression, ParenthesizedExpression, StringLiteral, NumericLiteral, and more.

buildSymExprWithFlow() handles: Identifier, PropertyAccessExpression, PrefixUnaryExpression, BinaryExpression, StringLiteral, NumericLiteral, and more — but NOT CallExpression.

This gap means any variable assigned from a method call becomes unknown in the flow map, and all subsequent references to it in branch conditions also become unknown. This is the root cause of str-sg5d.

Fix approach: Either refactor into a single shared function with a flag for context, or add a test that programmatically verifies both functions handle the same set of node types. The test approach is more robust since the two functions have legitimately different contexts (flow analysis vs. branch rewriting).

Add a unit test in instrumentor.test.ts that instruments a function with 'const x = s.indexOf("@"); if (x === -1) { ... }' and asserts the branch condition is NOT unknown.

title: E2E concolic test for string-heavy function (email validator)
description:
Add an integration test in shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic.rs that runs the full concolic pipeline on examples/standalone/ts/15-email-validator.ts. This is the primary regression gate for the string ops → Z3 solver path.

The test should:
1. Spawn the real TS frontend
2. Analyze validateEmail to get 19 branches and string-method conditions
3. Instrument the function for symbolic tracking
4. Run concolic exploration with seed inputs including structurally valid emails (e.g. 'test@example.com', '@domain.com', 'user@', '.dot@x.com', 'user+tag@x.com')
5. Assert minimum path coverage — initially modest (e.g. ≥6 distinct paths) given known limitations (str-sg5d, str-omrx), with TODOs to raise the bar as those are fixed

Why this test matters:
- str-sg5d (data flow drops CallExpression) means most branch conditions are unknown → solver can't help
- str-omrx (cold-start problem) means concolic gets stuck without good seeds
- str-emw6 (candidate inputs ignored) means hand-crafted seeds don't reach the random explorer
- This single test would have caught ALL THREE bugs before they accumulated

The test should be tagged with #[ignore] initially if it requires str-sg5d to be fixed first, with a clear comment explaining why and which issue unblocks it. Pattern after existing concolic_classifynumber_discovers_all_branches test.

When str-sg5d and str-omrx are fixed, the threshold should be raised to ≥12 distinct paths (the 12 branches reachable without regex/for-loop analysis).

title: Data flow analysis drops CallExpression assignments to unknown
description: buildSymExprWithFlow() in instrumentor.ts:278-352 has no case for ts.isCallExpression(), so any local variable assigned from a method call (e.g. 'const local = email.slice(0, atIdx)') falls through to {kind: 'unknown'} at line 351. Since visitStatementsForDataFlow() filters out unknowns (line 236), these variables are never stored in the dataFlowMap. All subsequent branch conditions referencing these locals (local.length, domain.startsWith, labels.length, etc.) also become unknown, making them invisible to the Z3 solver. This is the primary reason the email validator gets only 4/20 branches — 13 of 19 branch conditions contain unknown nodes. Fix: add CallExpression handling to buildSymExprWithFlow() that mirrors buildSymExpr()'s call handling (lines 936-948), producing symbolic call nodes for method invocations on tracked expressions.

title: Wire string method calls to Z3 string theory in solver
description:
The z3 Rust crate (v0.19) fully supports the Seq sort with contains, prefix, suffix, substr, length, at, concat, and indexof operations. Frontends already capture string method calls as SymExpr::Call { name, receiver, args }. The solver rejects all Call expressions at solver.rs line 248 with SolverError::Unsupported.

Implement ~10 match arms in to_z3_expr() mapping Call names to Z3 string operations:
- contains/includes → z3 String::contains
- indexOf/Index → z3 indexof (with -1 sentinel for not-found)
- startsWith/HasPrefix → z3 String::prefix (note: arg order flip)
- endsWith/HasSuffix → z3 String::suffix
- length/len → z3 String::length
- charAt/at → z3 String::at
- slice/substring/substr → z3 String::substr
- concat → z3 String::concat

Each frontend uses different method names for the same operation. Initially hard-code mappings for TS and Go (the two working frontends). This unblocks Z3-guided input generation for string-heavy functions like validateEmail.

This is the prerequisite for build-time table generation (separate issue) but delivers immediate value.

title: TS frontend: intra-package module resolution fails (Cannot find module)
description:
The TS frontend uses ts.transpileModule per-file + vm.createContext with the host process's require. Relative imports to sibling modules within the target package fail with 'Cannot find module'. This is the #1 error source — 365 of 366 total errors across all TS holdout targets. Causes complete failure for ts-pattern (0/35 functions) and partial failure for remeda (48/561) and es-toolkit.

Root cause: there is no bundling step. Target files are transpiled individually and executed in a VM sandbox. Relative require() calls fail because module resolution doesn't account for the target project's directory structure.

Design questions that need answering before implementation:
- How does bundling interact with per-function instrumentation?
- Would bundling break the per-function isolation model?
- How to handle tsconfig.json paths/aliases?
- Should we bundle at analysis time, execution time, or both?

Needs design work before implementation.

**Requirement: Reproduction test first.** Before attempting any fix, write an automated test that reproduces the bug (demonstrating the 'Cannot find module' failure for relative imports in the VM sandbox). The test must fail before the fix and pass after.
design:
## Root Cause

The TS frontend uses ts.transpileModule per-file + vm.createContext with the **host process's require**. Three distinct bugs:

1. **executeInstrumented** (executor.ts ~line 289): sandbox is missing __filename and __dirname entirely, and uses host require. The vm.runInContext filename is 'instrumented.js' (fake).
2. **loadModule** (executor.ts ~line 69): sets __dirname correctly but still uses the host require — so require('./sibling') resolves against shatter-ts install dir.
3. **loadAndTranspile** (setup-loader.ts ~line 45): same issue as loadModule.

The instrumented code preserves all imports (ts.transpileModule with CommonJS converts them to require() calls), so require('./purry') etc. always fails.

## Fix Design

Use Node.js `module.createRequire(filename)` (stable since Node 12) to create a require anchored to the target file's directory.

### Changes Required

**executor.ts:**
- Add `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'`
- loadModule: replace `require` with `createRequire(absolutePath)` in sandbox
- executeInstrumented: add `sourceFilePath: string` parameter; use `createRequire(sourceFilePath)` + set __filename/__dirname in sandbox; pass sourceFilePath to vm.runInContext filename option; add `fileName: sourceFilePath` to ts.transpileModule options

**handlers.ts:**
- Pass `fileForExec` (already resolved at line ~161) as 5th argument to executeInstrumented

**setup-loader.ts:**
- Add `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'`
- Replace host require with `createRequire(absolutePath)` in loadAndTranspile sandbox

### Test Plan
- Existing fixture `__fixtures__/dependencies.ts` imports from `./deps-helper` — verify it works after fix
- Add integration test: target file importing sibling module in a temp directory outside shatter-ts
- Verify ts-pattern-style scenarios (deep internal imports like './internals/helpers')
close_reason: Fixed with module.createRequire() in executor.ts, handlers.ts, setup-loader.ts

title: Make-friendly per-file specs with fingerprint-based incremental exploration
description:
## Problem

Shatter's CLI currently bundles discovery, analysis, and exploration into monolithic commands (scan, run) with outputs going to hidden .shatter/cache/ or shatter-report/. This makes it unusable with Make, which needs predictable input→output file relationships with timestamp-based staleness.

The lasting output of Shatter is behavioral specifications — not human reports. Specs are the precise, complete, machine-diffable records of observed behavior. They should be first-class project artifacts, not hidden cache.

## Design

### Two first-class artifacts, per-source-file granularity

1. **Spec files** (FunctionSpec[]) — the lasting, diffable behavioral specification. Versioned in git. Used by spec-diff for regression detection.
2. **Behavior map files** (BehaviorMap[]) — input→output mappings for compositional mocking. Stored separately, may or may not be versioned.

Both are per-source-file: specs/src/math.ts.json contains specs for all functions in math.ts.

### Internal function fingerprinting for performance

When a source file changes, Shatter doesn't blindly re-explore all functions:
1. Run cheap analyze phase → extract function signatures/ASTs
2. Compute per-function fingerprint (hash of source text, parameter types, branch structure)
3. Compare against fingerprints stored in existing output
4. Only re-explore functions with changed fingerprints
5. Merge results: preserve unchanged specs, update changed ones

Fingerprints should compose across the call graph: if B's behavior changes, A (which calls B) needs re-exploration even if A's source is unchanged.

### CLI changes needed

1. **explore --output <path>** — write spec to explicit path (Make target)
2. **explore accepts file-level targets** — shatter explore src/math.ts explores all functions in the file
3. **shatter stale** — lightweight staleness check (exit code 0/1) using fingerprints, for non-Make incremental workflows
4. **explore --clean** — ignore existing specs/fingerprints and force full re-exploration from scratch. Escape hatch for when fingerprints are stale, cache is corrupted, or exploration heuristics have changed.
5. **explore --dry-run** — run analyze + fingerprint comparison, print what would be explored (which functions are stale, which would be skipped), but don't actually run the concolic engine. Useful for understanding what Make would trigger, debugging fingerprint behavior, and CI cost estimation.

### Makefile usage

```makefile
SPECS_DIR := specs

$(SPECS_DIR)/src/math.ts.json: src/math.ts
    shatter explore src/math.ts -o $@

$(SPECS_DIR)/src/utils.ts.json: src/utils.ts
    shatter explore src/utils.ts -o $@
```

### What stays the same

- scan and run remain as batteries-included commands for users not using Make
- .shatter/cache/ remains for internal caching (behavior maps for compositional mocking during exploration)
- export-tests unchanged — reads from specs or cache

### Key files that will need changes

- shatter-core/src/cache.rs — fingerprint storage, staleness checks
- shatter-core/src/spec.rs — per-file spec bundles (array of FunctionSpec)
- shatter-core/src/behavior.rs — per-file behavior map bundles
- shatter-cli/src/main.rs — --output flag, --clean flag, --dry-run flag, file-level targets, stale command
- shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs — fingerprint-aware incremental exploration
close_reason: All features implemented in commit 1560cd5: --output, --clean, --dry-run, stale command, fingerprinting, incremental merge. Only str-w8d (call-graph fingerprints) remains.

title: Date/DateTime/Duration support end-to-end
description:
Full support for temporal types: generators, analyzer recognition, reconstruction, and integration test.

## What
1. Core generators (input_gen.rs): generate_date and generate_duration with boundary-biased values
   - Date boundaries: epoch 0, negative epoch, Y2K38 (2038-01-19), 2024-01-01, month/year boundaries, far future (9999-12-31), far past (0001-01-01)
   - Duration boundaries: 0, negative, 1ms, 1s, 1min, 1hr, 1day, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
   - Wire format: {"__complex_type": "date", "value": <epoch_ms>}, {"__complex_type": "duration", "ms": <millis>}

2. TS analyzer (shatter-ts/src/analyzer.ts): Recognize Date type in convertType/convertObjectType by checking type symbol name
3. TS reconstruction (new shatter-ts/src/reconstruct.ts): reconstructValue() infrastructure + Date case (new Date(epoch_ms))
4. Go analyzer (shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go): Recognize time.Time and time.Duration
5. Go reconstruction (new shatter-go/reconstruct/reconstruct.go): time.UnixMilli(ms) and time.Duration(ms)*time.Millisecond

6. Integration test: isWeekend(date: Date): boolean — function with two paths (weekday/weekend), verify solver generates dates hitting both paths

## Solver
ConstValue::Complex { kind: Date, repr: Int(epoch_ms) } — solver unwraps to integer comparison. Already handled by the generic Complex unwrap from str-t8b.

## Priority
Highest real-world impact — Date appears in nearly every business application.

## Files
- shatter-core/src/input_gen.rs
- shatter-ts/src/analyzer.ts
- shatter-ts/src/reconstruct.ts (new)
- shatter-ts/src/executor.ts (call reconstructValue before execution)
- shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go
- shatter-go/reconstruct/reconstruct.go (new)
- examples/typescript/src/ (isWeekend test function)
close_reason: Date/DateTime/Duration generators added to input_gen.rs with boundary-biased values. TS analyzer recognizes Date, RegExp, URL, Error, Buffer, BigInt, Symbol via complexKindFromSymbol(). Go analyzer recognizes time.Time, time.Duration, url.URL, regexp.Regexp, net.IP, big.Int/Rat/Float via complexKindFromNamed(). reconstruct.ts and reconstruct.go created with full value reconstruction. Both frontends declare complex_type capabilities in handshake. 433 core + 142 TS + all Go tests pass. Clippy and go vet clean.

title: Wire invariant detection into pipeline
description: The invariants.rs module exists but is not wired into the exploration pipeline. Implement Daikon-style invariant detection: after collecting execution records for a function, derive candidate properties (e.g. 'for all x > 100, shipping is free', 'return value is always non-negative when input is positive'). Use proptest to validate candidate invariants against the observed execution set. Properties should be classified as: (1) proven (Z3-confirmed necessary and sufficient), (2) observed (held for all samples, not formally verified), (3) likely (held for >95% of samples). Output feeds into the specification format.

title: Behavioral equivalence classes for path grouping
description: Replace return-value-based path deduplication with branch-path-based behavioral equivalence classes. Executions that follow the same branch sequence belong to the same class, regardless of output value. Within each class: pick the simplest concrete example as the canonical representative, derive common preconditions from all inputs in the class. This fixes the fundamental issue in str-798 (every distinct return value treated as unique path) at the conceptual level and is prerequisite for meaningful specification generation.

title: Design specification output format
description: Define the concrete output artifact for behavior specifications. Each function gets a spec with: (1) behavioral equivalence classes grouped by branch path, (2) preconditions for each class derived from constraints, (3) postconditions (return value pattern, side effects), (4) at least one concrete example per class, (5) distinction between proven properties (Z3-confirmed) and observed properties (seen in all samples but not formally verified). The format must be both human-readable (markdown) and machine-readable (JSON). This is the core deliverable users interact with — build backward from this.

title: E2E concolic test on real TS function
description: Add an integration test that runs the FULL concolic pipeline on a real TypeScript example function (e.g. classifyNumber): analyze → instrument → explore with concolic orchestrator → Z3 solve → verify that Z3 discovers a branch that random alone cannot. This is the single most important validation that the core value proposition works end-to-end. Must use the real TS frontend subprocess, not a mock.

title: path_hash fallback treats every distinct return value as a unique path
description: When branch_path is empty, path_hash() in explorer.rs falls back to hashing the serialized return value. For numeric functions like safeDivide, every different input pair produces a different float result, so 100 iterations yield 68 'unique paths' through a 4-path function. Fix: use lines_executed as the fallback path signature instead of return value. All executions through the same code path hit the same lines regardless of input values.

title: Explorer should instrument functions before executing
description: explore_function() in explorer.rs sends Analyze then immediately loops Execute commands, but never sends an Instrument command. Without instrumentation, the TS frontend (and Go frontend) return empty branch_path arrays, so the explorer never gets branch decision data. Fix: after receiving FunctionAnalysis, send an Instrument command and store the result before entering the execution loop.

title: Single-command repo exploration: shatter run <repo-url>
description: Add a top-level CLI command that takes a repo URL (or local path), clones it if needed, discovers all supported files (TS, Go), runs the full pipeline (analyze → explore → report), and outputs a specification report. This is the 'just give me a URL' UX goal. Steps: clone/validate repo, discover files by language, batch analyze all files, build call graph, run concolic exploration (respecting dependency order), generate markdown specs, output combined report. Should support --output-dir for writing per-function spec files.

When exploring a caller, inject these behavior maps as mocks for the callee — so the caller is tested with realistic (discovered) behavior rather than arbitrary stubs. Store behavior maps in .shatter-cache/ for reuse across runs.

title: [bug] Rust crate-bridge harness: captured stderr is lost when the target aborts or times out, and capture files are unbounded
description:
Type: bug, priority P2. Parent epic: str-49drv (Audit 2026-09-22 findings). Follow-up to str-49drv.116 (closed; merged to main as 779c02d7), found by its independent code review. Related: str-49drv.212 (Axum harness has no capture at all).

## Problem

str-49drv.116 moved the crate-bridge harness onto `shatter_rust_runtime::ProtocolChannel`, which points the process's stdout and stderr at temp capture files and drains them into `console_output` side effects after each call returns normally. That fixed protocol corruption but introduced two weaknesses in the capture files themselves.

1. **Stderr is lost when the process dies before a drain.** Before str-49drv.116 the host spawned the crate-bridge child with `.stderr(Stdio::inherit())`, so a panic message or other stderr from a target that aborts (`panic = "abort"`, stack overflow, SIGSEGV, `std::process::exit`) or that the host kills on timeout reached the host's stderr. Now that output goes into a capture file that was unlinked at creation (Unix) or delete-on-close (Windows). It is only read by `take_console_output()` after a call returns, so on an abnormal exit or a timeout kill it is lost with the process, and the host sees only a dead harness or "execution timed out" with no diagnostic.
2. **Capture files and their read are unbounded.** Only each individual console message is capped (4096 characters). Nothing caps the total bytes a target can write between drains, and `take_console_output()` reads the whole file into memory. A target that prints in a loop until the timeout, or writes a huge blob with no newlines, grows a file in the temp directory without limit (disk exhaustion), and the drain then copies it into memory (`read_to_end` plus `String::from_utf8_lossy`), which can OOM the harness. The response then carries one `console_output` effect per line, so its JSON line can be enormous.

## Current code facts (main at 779c02d7)

- shatter-rust-runtime/src/protocol_channel.rs: `pub const MAX_CONSOLE_MESSAGE_CHARS: usize = 4096` (:33) is the only cap, applied per message in `console_output_effects` (:100-106). `take_console_output` (:72) calls the file-drain helper at :137-141: `seek(0)`, `read_to_end`, `set_len(0)`, `seek(0)`, `String::from_utf8_lossy`. Capture files are created under `std::env::temp_dir()` (:152-) and unlinked right away on Unix (`remove_file`, :169) or opened `FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE` on Windows (:162), so no path survives for the host to read after a kill.
- shatter-rust/src/executor.rs: the persistent-harness timeout path (:648-660) does `self.child.kill()` and `self.child.wait()` and returns an ExecuteResult whose error is `"execution timed out after {timeout_ms}ms"`; it has no captured output to attach. The crate-bridge spawn is at :5472-5476 with `.stderr(Stdio::inherit())`, which is now bypassed because the child re-points its own fd 2 at startup.
- The standalone and dispatch harnesses (`generate_harness` executor.rs:2365 and the dispatch generator) also redirect fds 1 and 2 to capture files and read them with a bare `read_to_string` and no size cap, and also lose captures on kill. So the unbounded read is not new to crate-bridge; this issue is scoped to the crate-bridge path (the shared ProtocolChannel code), and the other two harnesses are related but out of scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Stderr survives abnormal exit.** A regression test drives a crate-bridge target that writes a recognizable line to stderr (`eprintln!("boom-marker")`) and then either aborts (`std::process::abort()`) or sleeps past the per-execution timeout. The resulting error/diagnostic surfaced to the caller (the ExecuteResult error message, or the host's own stderr) contains `boom-marker`. It fails on main before the fix. Choose and document a mechanism; acceptable ones include not unlinking the capture files and having the host read them by a path passed to the child through an environment variable, or forwarding stderr to the host's stderr as well as capturing it.
- [ ] **Bounded capture.** A regression test drives a target that writes at least 64 MiB of output (a tight `println!` loop and a single no-newline blob) in one call and asserts the harness neither exhausts memory nor returns an oversized response: the returned `console_output` total size is at most a documented constant cap (choose a default, for example 1 MiB total per call), excess output is dropped, and the response includes an explicit truncation marker so a reader knows output was cut. The on-disk capture size must also be bounded (or the test must show it stays below a documented limit); document how.
- [ ] Normal behavior is unchanged: the five existing `crate_bridge_*` regression tests from str-49drv.116 and `e2e_rust_crate_bridge_printing_target` still pass.
- [ ] No new dependency is added to the user's crate (ProtocolChannel stays std-only).
- [ ] shatter-rust/CLAUDE.md and the `console_output` notes in protocol/parity-matrix.yaml state the new cap and the abnormal-exit behavior; `task parity` and `task conformance` pass.
- [ ] `cargo test --test e2e_concolic_rust` and the crate-bridge unit tests pass. Run heavy builds via the launch-work skill's `scripts/run-heavy` wrapper and cap `--test-threads` at 2, because Rust crate-building tests contend and time out at default parallelism.

## Out of scope

- The standalone and dispatch harnesses' identical unbounded read and loss-on-kill (file separately if wanted).
- The Axum harness, which has no capture at all (str-49drv.212).
- Windows execution of harnesses in CI (str-49drv.209).
- Redesigning how `console_output` is reported to consumers.

## Size

One normal task, with a design choice inside it (how the host recovers stderr, and how the cap is enforced), so a short design note in the PR or issue comments is expected.

title: [bug] Rust Axum harness shares stdout with handler code: a handler that prints corrupts the protocol response
description:
Type: bug, priority P2. Parent epic: str-49drv (Audit 2026-09-22 findings). Sibling of str-49drv.116 (closed: crate-bridge stdout isolation, landed on main as merge 779c02d7) and str-49drv.209 (Windows harness execution).

## Problem

The generated Axum harness runs the user's handler in the same process whose stdout carries the JSON-line protocol to the frontend. Nothing redirects stdout or stderr while the handler runs, so any `println!`, `print!` (with or without a trailing newline) or `eprintln!` from handler code, or code it calls, is interleaved with the response line. The frontend reads the first stdout line as the response, fails to parse it, and reports an output-parse failure instead of the handler's result. This is the failure str-49drv.116 fixed for crate-bridge harnesses.

## Current code facts (main at 779c02d7)

- shatter-rust/src/executor.rs:6516 `fn generate_axum_harness(` emits the harness source. At :6549 it emits a call to `shatter_rust_runtime::run_harness_loop(mocks_json, |inputs| { ... })`.
- shatter-rust-runtime/src/lib.rs:544 `pub fn run_harness_loop` reads one request line from stdin, runs the handler under `catch_unwind`, then writes the response with `println!("{output}")` (lib.rs:588) followed by a stdout flush. It does no fd redirection. (`run_dispatch_loop` in the same file does the same at :643.)
- The standalone harness (`generate_harness`, executor.rs:2365, which also calls `run_harness_loop` at :2397) and the dispatch harness avoid the problem only because their generated handler bodies `libc::dup2` fds 1 and 2 to capture files (executor.rs around :2541-2561 and :2720-2721). `generate_axum_harness` emits no such code.
- The mechanism to reuse is on main: `shatter_rust_runtime::ProtocolChannel` in shatter-rust-runtime/src/protocol_channel.rs. `ProtocolChannel::install() -> io::Result<Self>` takes a private close-on-exec copy of stdout for responses, then points stdout and stderr at capture files for the rest of the process; `take_console_output(&mut self) -> Vec<Value>` drains the captures into `console_output` side-effect values; `respond(&mut self, response: &Value) -> io::Result<()>` is the only writer to the protocol pipe; free functions `console_output_effects(stdout, stderr)` and `attach_console_output(result, console)` build and attach the effects. It is std-only (Unix: dup2 via a local `extern "C"`; Windows: `SetStdHandle`). The crate-bridge driver is the worked example of how to call it: see executor.rs around :5161 (`ProtocolChannel::install()`), :5207 (`take_console_output()`), :5209 (`attach_console_output(&mut exec_result, __console)`).
- Existing Axum E2E to model the new test on: `e2e_rust_crate_backed_axum_resolves_super_and_external_extractor_types` at shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic_rust.rs:1151. The crate-bridge printing E2E to copy the harness-mode assertion from is `e2e_rust_crate_bridge_printing_target` in the same file (:1641).
- Parity contract: protocol/parity-matrix.yaml `side_effect_capabilities.console_output` (status: required) currently says Rust captures in "standalone, dispatch, and crate-bridge harnesses" (frontend line `rust: captured   # standalone, dispatch, and crate-bridge harnesses`, and a notes paragraph about crate-bridge). Axum is not named anywhere in that row or in shatter-rust/CLAUDE.md's console_output line (line 23) and "Crate-bridge protocol channel" paragraph (line 27), so the doc task is to add Axum to those statements once it is true.

Line numbers above are for main at 779c02d7 and will drift; locate the same code by searching for the named functions, and for `console_output` in protocol/parity-matrix.yaml and shatter-rust/CLAUDE.md. For the parity-matrix edit, use the existing crate-bridge sentence in the `console_output` notes and the `rust: captured` comment as the template.

## Reproduction

2. Add `println!("hello from handler");` as the first statement of the handler.
3. Run the same explore/execute that test uses.
4. Expected: the handler's real response is returned and the printed text appears as `console_output`. Suspected actual (inferred from the code above, not yet observed for Axum): an output-parse failure whose `line:` is `hello from handler`.

The first acceptance item confirms or refutes the suspicion; if the test passes on main, close this as not reproducible and record why.

## Acceptance criteria

It fails on main before the fix (if it does not, see Reproduction).
- [ ] The fix reuses `ProtocolChannel` rather than adding a second mechanism.

## Out of scope

title: [bug] Non-ASCII values panic 8 more preview truncators that slice serialized JSON at a fixed byte offset (same defect as str-wlban)
description:
Type: bug, priority P2. Parent epic: str-49drv (Audit 2026-09-22 findings). Blocked by str-wlban (in progress; branch str-wlban-spec-utf8-boundary, commit e7ae313b), which fixes only `shatter-core/src/spec.rs::format_value_short` and explicitly leaves other modules out of scope. Do not start until str-wlban is closed, so the reference fix and its tests are on main.

## Problem

Eight preview helpers shorten a serialized value with `&s[..N]` (a byte-offset slice) when `s.len() > M`. Rust panics with "byte index N is not a char boundary" when byte N falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character. The serialized text comes from `serde_json::Value::to_string()` (or a comma-joined list of such strings), so any function whose return value or argument is a JSON string with a non-ASCII character straddling the cut offset crashes the command that renders it, instead of printing a truncated preview. This is the exact failure str-wlban fixed in `spec.rs`.

## Current code facts (main at 951a6821)

Each site builds `s` (or `joined`) from a serialized `serde_json::Value`, and if its byte length exceeds a limit, slices up to a smaller fixed offset and appends "...":

| File:line | Helper | Slices at | When len exceeds |
|---|---|---|---|
| shatter-core/src/spec_diff.rs:491 | `format_postcondition_short` (Returns arm) | [..37] | 40 |
| shatter-core/src/explorer.rs:3279 | `format_value_short` | [..37] | 40 |
| shatter-cli/src/render.rs:280 | `value_short` | [..37] | 40 |
| shatter-core/src/report.rs:2599 | `format_json_compact` | [..57] | 60 |
| shatter-core/src/reporter.rs:455 | `format_json_short` | [..57] | 60 |
| shatter-core/src/export.rs:792 | `format_value_short` | [..27] | 30 |
| shatter-core/src/export.rs:803 | `format_args_short` (joined args) | [..47] | 50 |
| shatter-core/src/snapshot.rs:310 | postcondition preview | [..57] | 60 |

- The reference fix is in `shatter-core/src/spec.rs::format_value_short` (landed by str-wlban): cut at the greatest char boundary at or before the offset, `(0..=37).rev().find(|&i| s.is_char_boundary(i)).unwrap_or(0)`, keeping the same byte budget including the "..." suffix. The toolchain in use (rustc 1.96) also has stable `str::floor_char_boundary`; no minimum supported Rust version is pinned in Cargo.toml, so either form works, but use one shared helper for all sites.
- shatter-core/src/snapshot.rs belongs to the snapshot module that str-49drv.15 plans to retire. As of this filing str-49drv.15 is still open, so the site exists and is in scope. If str-49drv.15 is closed by the time you start (`bd show str-49drv.15`), skip that row.
- No shared string/preview utility module exists in shatter-core/src yet (no util, text, fmt or preview module). `proptest = "1"` is already a shatter-core dev-dependency.
- Inputs that trigger the panic: a JSON string of 35 ASCII characters, then `é`, then 10 ASCII characters. `serde_json::json!(format!("{}é{}", "a".repeat(35), "b".repeat(10))).to_string()` is 49 bytes and byte 37 is inside `é`, so it panics at every `[..37]` site above. Use a value scaled to each site's offset for the others (put a two-byte character across the offset).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add one shared helper in a new module `shatter-core/src/preview.rs` (declare it in shatter-core/src/lib.rs; shatter-cli already depends on shatter-core): `pub fn truncate_preview(s: &str, max_len: usize) -> String`. Contract: if `s.len() <= max_len`, return `s` unchanged (no ellipsis). Otherwise cut at the greatest char boundary at or before `max_len - 3` and append the fixed ASCII suffix "...", so the result is at most `max_len` bytes. `max_len` is the total budget including the suffix, i.e. the existing limits: 40, 60, 30 and 50 in the table above. For ASCII input this produces exactly what the current code produces (for example limit 40 gives the first 37 bytes plus "..."), so only strings with a multi-byte character across the cut change.
- [ ] Replace the eight fixed-offset slices with calls to it; each site keeps building its own input string (for example export.rs:803 still joins arguments first, then truncates the joined text).
- [ ] The existing str-wlban tests in `spec.rs` still pass unchanged. Migrating `spec.rs::format_value_short` to the helper is optional; if you do, those tests are the proof of equivalence.
- [ ] A `proptest` property test (shatter-core is already using proptest; put it beside the helper in `preview.rs`) generates arbitrary Unicode strings and budgets of at least 3, and asserts: no panic; result length is at most `max_len`; the result is valid UTF-8 (guaranteed by the `String` return type); an untruncated result equals the input; a truncated result is a prefix of the input followed by "...".
- [ ] Each migrated site has a direct regression test in its own module's existing `#[cfg(test)]` block. Input: a JSON string whose serialized form has a two-byte character (for example `é`) beginning one byte before the cut offset, so the offset lands inside the character. For a site with offset N (37, 57, 27 or 47), build `format!("{}é{}", "a".repeat(N - 2), "b".repeat(20))` as a JSON string value; its serialized form has the opening quote at byte 0, so `é` occupies bytes N-1 and N. The test asserts no panic and that the result ends with "...". Each such test must fail on main before the change.
- [ ] Stored data and JSON output are unchanged; only display previews change. No protocol/schema change.
- [ ] `task test-standard` passes. Because shatter-cli/src/render.rs and report output are touched, run the repo's `/walkthrough-review` skill (it runs the demo walkthrough, `task walkthrough`, and judges the output); its ASCII output must be unchanged from before your change.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning previews for display width or grapheme clusters (byte-budget truncation stays).
- Fixing any other panics outside truncation.
- Changing the numeric limits (30/40/60 and so on).

## Size

One normal task: one helper plus eight mechanical call-site changes and tests.

title: [investigate] Rust frontend: crate-private fn in a single-file crate records 0 executions with no error
description:
Type: task (time-boxed investigation), priority P2. Parent epic: str-49drv (Audit 2026-09-22 findings). Found while writing the E2E test for str-49drv.116 (Rust crate-bridge stdout isolation).

## Observation (unverified beyond one incidental run)

While building a fixture for an E2E test, a first version used a private (non-`pub`) function in a single-file crate. Exploring it did not route through the crate-bridge harness: only a bin-only harness was built. `explore` recorded 0 executions and reported no error. The fixture was then changed to a `pub fn` inside a module that uses `use crate::...` imports, which does route to crate-bridge, so the incidental run was never investigated further and was not saved.

A target that cannot be executed yet produces no error and no explicit "skipped, because ..." result is a silent coverage loss: the user sees zero paths for the function and cannot tell whether it is untestable or the tool is broken.

## Current code facts (main at 864e588a; work from current main, the relevant code is unchanged by other open work)

- shatter-rust/src/executor.rs defines `ExecuteError::NonExecutable(String)` at :166 (displayed at :177) and returns it from several routing checks (for example :254-291, :1577, :1713, :5541-5552, :5728, :5788, :5854).
- Routing rule (from str-49drv.116's description of executor.rs ~:6292-6300): a file inside a crate tries the bin-only harness first and falls back to the crate-bridge harness only when the caller has not requested a harness mode and bin-only returns `NonExecutable`. The suspected gap is the case where no error surfaces at all, not a wrong fallback decision; hypothesis (b) below covers "fallback not attempted", (a) covers "correctly declined but reported as 0 executions".
- Existing E2E helper: `write_temp_crate(dir, func_src)` in shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic_rust.rs:489 writes this Cargo.toml and puts `func_src` in `src/lib.rs`:
  `[package] name = "shatter_ddxe_fixture" version = "0.0.0" edition = "2021"` and `[lib] path = "src/lib.rs"`.
- CLI form: `shatter explore <file>:<function>` (`shatter explore --help`); the language frontend is chosen from the `.rs` extension. Build the CLI with `cargo build -p shatter-cli` (run heavy builds through the launch-work `run-heavy` wrapper); the binary is `target/debug/shatter`.

## Terms

- **bin-only harness**: the Rust frontend compiles the target function into a standalone harness binary from the target file alone, with no access to the rest of the user's crate.
- **crate-bridge harness**: the harness is built as a shadow of the user's whole crate so that `use crate::...` imports and sibling modules resolve. The existing E2E asserts this mode by pinning `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE` to a directory and requiring a build under `rust/crate-bridge/<key>/crate-shadow` in it (shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic_rust.rs, `e2e_rust_crate_bridge_printing_target`, on branch str-49drv-116-crate-bridge-stdout until it lands).
- **beads / `bd`**: this repo's issue tracker CLI (`bd show <id>`, `bd create`, `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>`).
- **"0 executions"**: the explore summary reports zero executions and zero paths for the function, with exit code 0 and nothing on stderr.

## How to tell (a), (b), (c) apart

Set `SHATTER_HARNESS_CACHE=<scratch>/harness-cache` for the run, then list that directory afterwards:
- Only a `rust/bin-only/...` build exists and the run reports 0 executions: crate-bridge was never built. That is (b) if the function could run under crate-bridge (compare with the `pub fn` control, which should build under `rust/crate-bridge/...`), or (a) if crate-bridge also cannot call a private function.
- A `rust/crate-bridge/...` build exists but the run still reports 0 executions: the fallback ran and the failure is later; record the debug log (`--log-level debug`) and treat it as a new finding rather than (a) or (b).
- The private-function run executes and reports paths: (c).

## Task

1. Reproduce, in a scratch directory outside the repo such as `/tmp/shatter-repro-private-fn` (do not commit the fixture):
   - `Cargo.toml` exactly as above.
   - `src/lib.rs`:
     ```rust
     fn classify(n: i64) -> i64 {
         if n < 0 { -1 } else if n == 42 { 99 } else { 0 }
     }
     ```
   - Run `target/debug/shatter explore <scratch>/src/lib.rs:classify` and paste the raw terminal output, exit code, and the path count / executions figure into a comment on this issue.
   - Repeat with `pub fn classify` and compare. The `pub fn` run is the control and is expected to execute.
2. Determine which of these is true, with the pasted output as evidence:
   a. The function is correctly non-executable (a private fn cannot be called from a separate bin harness) and the tool should report an explicit skipped/non-executable result instead of "0 executions".
   b. Routing wrongly declines to attempt the crate-bridge fallback for a case it could execute (bin-only returned non-executable but crate-bridge was never tried).
   c. Not reproducible: the private-fn run executes normally, so the earlier observation was a fixture mistake. Treat as not reproducible after 3 clean attempts on current main.
3. If (a) or (b), file one follow-up fix issue in this same beads tracker containing the failing test and acceptance criteria, and link it here (`bd dep add`). Do not fix it in this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A comment on this issue records the scratch fixture, the exact commands, and the raw output of both the private-fn run and the `pub fn` control run.
- [ ] The issue states which of (a), (b), (c) holds, quoting the output that shows it.
- [ ] For (a) or (b), a follow-up fix issue is filed and linked; for (c), the three attempts are recorded and this issue is closed.

## Out of scope

- Fixing routing or reporting behavior here.
- Windows, Axum, and the console-capture work from str-49drv.116.

## Size

Small: a time-boxed investigation (about an hour) whose deliverable is a written finding.

title: Rust frontend harnesses never execute on Windows in CI; standalone/dispatch harnesses are Unix-only
description:
## Problem

The release matrix ships `shatter-rust.exe` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. Maintainer decision D1 (2026-09-23, audits/2026-09-22.md) keeps Windows in that matrix. But no CI job ever runs a Rust frontend harness on Windows, and two of the three harness generators emit Unix-only code:

- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs only on `ubuntu-latest`. `.github/workflows/release.yml` (matrix row at about line 91: `target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `os: windows-latest`) builds `shatter-rust.exe`, but it runs no harness. The smoke in str-49drv.21 runs only the Go frontend.
- Standalone harness generator (`shatter-rust/src/executor.rs`, the generator that emits `shatter_rust_runtime::run_harness_loop`, console capture near lines 2524-2577) and dispatch harness generator (`run_dispatch_loop`, capture near lines 2714-2881). Both emit `libc::dup`/`libc::dup2` and `use std::os::unix::io::AsRawFd` with no `cfg(windows)` branch. On Windows, the generated harness `main.rs` does not compile. The generated harness Cargo.toml adds `libc = "0.2"` (executor.rs lines ~989 and ~1626).
- The crate-bridge harness became platform-neutral in str-49drv.116. Its protocol channel is `shatter_rust_runtime::ProtocolChannel` in `shatter-rust-runtime/src/protocol_channel.rs`: `dup2` through a local `extern "C"` on Unix, `SetStdHandle` on Windows. That code has only been verified with `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` on a generated crate-bridge crate. It has never run on Windows.

The result: on Windows, standalone and dispatch execution fail to build. Crate-bridge execution has never been exercised, so Windows-only runtime bugs (handle semantics, delete-on-close capture files, path handling) would go unseen.

## Resolved lookups

- D1 (audits/2026-09-22.md, 2026-09-23): the maintainer keeps the Windows and aarch64 release targets. No fix may drop a target from the matrix, set continue-on-error on it, or skip it with an if: guard.
- Existing Windows CI: `.github/workflows/release.yml` has the only `windows-latest` job, the release build matrix row. `ci.yml` has no Windows job. Neither workflow runs `cargo test` on Windows today.
- `libc` requirement: the generated harness Cargo.toml adds `libc = "0.2"` unconditionally. On Windows, the libc crate compiles, but `libc::dup`/`dup2` and `std::os::unix` are not available, so the generated `main.rs` fails to compile. The fix must make the generated code compile and capture output on Windows. Keeping `libc` as a `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]` entry is fine.

## Recommended approach

Reuse `shatter_rust_runtime::ProtocolChannel` (or factor its per-call capture into a shared runtime helper) instead of adding a second set of `cfg(windows)` branches to generated strings. Then the platform code exists once, in a compiled and unit-tested crate. With this approach, the standalone and dispatch harnesses also stop sharing stdout with user code between calls.

## Desired behavior

On Windows, the Rust frontend executes functions through every harness mode it auto-selects. A CI job proves it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The standalone and dispatch generators emit console capture that compiles and works on Windows. Either reuse `shatter_rust_runtime::ProtocolChannel` / a shared runtime capture helper, or add `cfg(windows)` branches. The harness must not require `libc` on Windows.
- [ ] A Windows CI job (in `ci.yml`, or a `release.yml` smoke step that runs before publish) runs, on `windows-latest`, at least: the crate-bridge stdout regression tests in `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs` (`crate_bridge_println_before_return_keeps_return_value`, `crate_bridge_print_without_newline_keeps_return_value`, `crate_bridge_user_output_imitating_a_response_is_not_the_response`, `crate_bridge_stderr_writes_keep_return_value`, `crate_bridge_alternating_printing_calls_do_not_shift_responses`), and one standalone-harness execute test (e.g. `crate_backed_execute_basic`). The job must pass, with no continue-on-error and no skip guard (D1).
- [ ] The close note links a passing run URL of that job.

## Out of scope

- The shatter-cli Windows build (Z3, embedded Go binary): tracked by str-49drv.21.
- Axum harness stdout isolation. It also emits responses on the user's stdout through `run_harness_loop`. File that separately if needed.

## Size

M to L. Most of the cost is Windows CI setup: toolchain, cargo cache, and the build time of the fixture crates.

title: Sized ints get out-of-range inputs: int_range() returns None for unsigned 64/128-bit, and boundary seeding ignores int_range (usize/u64/u128 get negatives, u8 gets -1)
description:
Step 1 of epic `int-width-signedness-epic`. This is the minimal core fix on the existing i64 data
path. Exact `u64` ranges come in step 2, `core-int-range-i128`. All paths are relative to the
shatter repo root (github.com/shatterproof-ai/shatter). Line numbers were verified at 16794cef.

## Problem

Closed str-ddxe added `int_width`/`int_signed` and the helper `shatter_core::types::int_range`. By
design, that helper returns `None` for any width whose range does not fit in `i64`, including
`u64`, `u128` and `usize` (`types.rs:311-345`). Every consumer treats `None` as "full i64".

Separately, boundary seeding never consults the helper. `boundary_dict::get_boundary_values`
(`boundary_dict.rs:54`) returns `int_boundaries()` (`:109`) for every `TypeInfo::Int`. That list
includes `0`, `±1`, `±2`, `±3`, `i64::MAX`, `i64::MIN` and powers of two. As a result:

- `usize`/`u64`/`u128` params receive negative values, including `i64::MIN`.
- `u8` params receive `-1` and `-2` from the boundary seeds, even though `int_range` covers `u8`.

The Rust harness rejects these values at deserialization, before the target runs. That wastes
budget. The rejections are also currently reported as target `throws runtime_error` rows, but that
reporting problem is a separate, related issue (`rust-input-deserialize-classification`). This
issue is only about the values generated.

## Expected bounds after this issue

The proof asserts these exact bounds:

| TypeInfo `(int_width, int_signed)` | Rust types | Bounds every generated or solved value must satisfy | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(8, false)` | `u8` | `[0, 255]` | `int_range` unchanged; boundary seeding newly filtered |
| `(8, true)` | `i8` | `[-128, 127]` | as above |
| `(16, false)` | `u16` | `[0, 65535]` | as above |
| `(16, true)` | `i16` | `[-32768, 32767]` | as above |
| `(32, false)` | `u32` | `[0, 4294967295]` | as above |
| `(32, true)` | `i32` | `[-2147483648, 2147483647]` | as above |
| `(64, false)` | `u64`, `usize` | `[0, i64::MAX]` | **new** clamp |
| `(128, false)` | `u128` | `[0, i64::MAX]` | **new** clamp |
| `(64, true)` | `i64`, `isize` | `[i64::MIN, i64::MAX]` | unchanged |
| `(128, true)` | `i128` | `[i64::MIN, i64::MAX]` | unchanged |
| width or signedness absent | Go `int` today, any unsized int | `[i64::MIN, i64::MAX]` | unchanged |

## Entry points that must honour the table

These were verified at 16794cef. Each one gets a test.

1. **Generation:** `input_gen.rs:128` `generate_random_value` calls `generate_int` (`:460`) and
   `generate_int_in_range` (`:478`).
2. **Shape check and regeneration:** `input_gen.rs:225` `value_matches_type_shape`, used by
   `coerce_value_to_type` (`:199`).
3. **Mutation:** `input_gen.rs:1955` `mutate_value` calls `mutate_int` (`:2107`) and
   `clamp_to_range` (`:2138`).
4. **Shrinking:** `input_gen.rs:3576` `shrink_candidates` calls `shrink_int` (`:3596`).
5. **Literal seeding:** `input_gen.rs:4020` in `literal_matches_type` (`:4014`).
6. **Boundary seeding:** `boundary_dict.rs:54` `get_boundary_values` and `int_boundaries` (`:109`)
   must filter by `int_range`. Its consumers are:
   - `generate_boundary_inputs` (`boundary_dict.rs:378`), called from `strategy.rs:507`,
     `scan_orchestrator.rs:3058` and `pipeline_orchestrator.rs:590`;
   - `default_candidate_values` (`input_gen.rs:3793-3798`).

   `interesting_pool.rs:748` only classifies values and needs no change.
7. **Solver range assertion:** `solver.rs:172` `assert_int_param_ranges`, called from
   `solve_for_new_path` (`:1224`), `solve_constraints` (`:1264`) and `solve_for_mcdc_independence`
   (`:1354`).

## Fixture (commit with this issue's branch)

Commit the fixture before changing code. `examples/rust` is excluded from the cargo workspace, and
the manifest only bounds the analyzer's crate-root walk, like `examples/rust/enum-color`. The
`String` guard stops the solver from pinning the integer param early, so random generation,
mutation and boundary seeding all reach it.

`examples/rust/int-width/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
# Known-answer fixture for integer width/signedness (int-width-signedness epic).
# The manifest only bounds the analyzer's crate-root walk; the crate is never built.
[package]
name = "int-width-fixture"
version = "0.0.0"
edition = "2021"
publish = false

[lib]
path = "src/lib.rs"
```

`examples/rust/int-width/src/lib.rs`:

```rust
// Known-answer fixture for integer width and signedness.
// The String guard keeps the solver from pinning the integer param early,
// so random generation, mutation and boundary seeding all reach it.

pub fn rank_usize(label: String, order: usize) -> u8 {
    if label.starts_with("en") { if order > 3 { 1 } else { 2 } } else { 0 }
}

pub fn rank_u64(label: String, n: u64) -> u8 {
    if label.starts_with("en") { if n > 3 { 1 } else { 2 } } else { 0 }
}

pub fn rank_u128(label: String, n: u128) -> u8 {
    if label.starts_with("en") { if n > 3 { 1 } else { 2 } } else { 0 }
}

pub fn rank_u8(label: String, n: u8) -> u8 {
    if label.starts_with("en") { if n > 3 { 1 } else { 2 } } else { 0 }
}

pub fn rank_i8(label: String, n: i8) -> u8 {
    if label.starts_with("en") { if n > 3 { 1 } else { 2 } } else { 0 }
}

pub fn rank_i64(label: String, n: i64) -> u8 {
    if label.starts_with("en") { if n > 3 { 1 } else { 2 } } else { 0 }
}
```

`scripts/check_int_width_bounds.py` is the bounds checker. It reads explore artifacts only, never
the rendered report:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assert every executed integer input in int-width fixture artifacts is within its type's bounds.

Usage: check_int_width_bounds.py <shatter-artifacts dir> [--full-u64]
Bounds follow int-unsigned64-clamp; --full-u64 switches to core-int-range-i128's exact u64 range.
"""
import glob, json, sys

I64_MAX = 2**63 - 1
full_u64 = "--full-u64" in sys.argv
U64_HI = 2**64 - 1 if full_u64 else I64_MAX
BOUNDS = {  # function -> (param index, min, max)
    "rank_usize": (1, 0, U64_HI), "rank_u64": (1, 0, U64_HI), "rank_u128": (1, 0, U64_HI),
    "rank_u8": (1, 0, 255), "rank_i8": (1, -128, 127), "rank_i64": (1, -2**63, I64_MAX),
    "at_u64_max": (0, 0, U64_HI), "above_i64_max": (0, 0, U64_HI), "at_i64_min": (0, -2**63, I64_MAX),
}
bad = seen = 0
for f in sorted(glob.glob(sys.argv[1] + "/explore-results/*/*.json")):
    d = json.load(open(f))
    fn = d.get("function_name")
    if fn not in BOUNDS or "observation" not in d:
        continue
    i, lo, hi = BOUNDS[fn]
    for inputs, _mocks, _result in d["observation"]["raw_results"]:
        seen += 1
        n = inputs[i]
        if not (isinstance(n, int) and not isinstance(n, bool) and lo <= n <= hi):
            bad += 1
            print(f"OUT OF BOUNDS {fn}: {n!r}")
print(f"checked {seen} executed inputs; out of bounds: {bad}")
sys.exit(1 if bad or not seen else 0)
```

## Baseline (run on main before changing code)

title: Core: exact integer ranges for every width up to 64 bits (u64 = [0, u64::MAX]) via an i128 IntRange carrier on the parameter-value paths
description:
Step 2 of epic `int-width-signedness-epic`. All paths are relative to the shatter repo root
(github.com/shatterproof-ai/shatter). Line numbers were verified at 16794cef, before
`int-unsigned64-clamp`, which does not move these sites.

## Problem

After `int-unsigned64-clamp`, `u64`/`usize` params are clamped to `[0, i64::MAX]`. The upper half of
`u64`, including `u64::MAX`, is never generated or solved for, because parameter ranges and values
are `i64`:

- `types.rs:315`, `:332`: `int_range(...) -> Option<(i64, i64)>`.
- `input_gen.rs:460`, `:478`, `:2107`, `:3596`: `generate_int`, `generate_int_in_range`,
  `mutate_int` and `shrink_int` read the value with `as_i64()` and compute in `i64`.
- `boundary_dict.rs:109`: the int boundary list is `i64` only.
- `solver.rs:176-177`: `assert_int_param_ranges` builds bounds with `Int::from_i64`.
- `solver.rs:1023-1030`: `extract_concrete_values` reads the model with `val.as_i64()` and silently
  drops any value that does not fit. `ConcreteValue::Int(i64)` (`solver.rs:37`) and
  `concrete_to_json` (`orchestrator.rs:1146`) carry it onward.

On main, Z3 asked for `n > 9_223_372_036_854_775_807` on a `u64` produced a model the extraction
dropped. The run fell back to `0` and a `-1` boundary seed, and the `upper-half` branch was never
reached.

Go avoids this today only through the separate `go_uint` complex kind, whose generator emits raw
`u64` JSON (`input_gen.rs:997-1010`). `core-go-alias-int-range` routes that kind onto the plain
int path, which is safe only once this issue lands.

## Contract

- **Range carrier:** `pub struct IntRange { pub min: i128, pub max: i128 }`.
  `TypeInfo::int_range()` and `types::int_range()` return `Option<IntRange>`.
- **Promised ranges:** exact for every width of 64 bits or less.

  | (width, signed) | range |
  |---|---|
  | 8/16/32 | exact, as today |
  | `(64, false)` (`u64`, `usize`) | `[0, u64::MAX]` |
  | `(64, true)` (`i64`, `isize`) | `[i64::MIN, i64::MAX]` |
  | `(128, false)` (`u128`) | clamped to `[0, u64::MAX]` |
  | `(128, true)` (`i128`) | clamped to `[i64::MIN, i64::MAX]` |
  | width or signedness absent | `[i64::MIN, i64::MAX]`, unchanged |

  The 128-bit clamp is documented in the `int_range` doc comment and in SPEC. The clamp exists
  because no value outside the 64-bit ranges is ever generated or put on the wire. JSON numbers stay
  `serde_json` `u64` or `i64`, and there is no wire-format change.
- **Paths that widen to i128.** These are all parameter-value paths:
  - generation: `generate_int`, `generate_int_in_range`;
  - mutation: `mutate_int`, `clamp_to_range`;
  - shrinking: `shrink_int`;
  - the shape check: `value_matches_type_shape` must accept `as_u64()` values within range;
  - boundary seeding: `int_boundaries` gains `u64::MAX` and `u64::MAX - 1`, filtered by range;
  - the Z3 parameter range assertion: bounds built from the i128 decimal string, e.g.
    `Int::from_str`, or `Int::from_u64` for the upper bound;
  - Z3 model extraction for integer variables: `extract_concrete_values` parses the model value as
    i128, via `as_u64()` fallback or the decimal string;
  - `ConcreteValue::Int` becomes `i128`;
  - `concrete_to_json` emits `u64` JSON when the value is above `i64::MAX` and `i64` JSON otherwise,
    and never emits a value outside the param's `IntRange`.
- **Paths that stay i64:**
  - `ConstValue::Int(i64)` (`sym_expr.rs:68`): integer literals mined from source and used as
    constants in path constraints, including `SymExpr` → Z3 at `solver.rs:513`;
  - `LiteralValue::Int` (literal seeding). It is compared against the i128 range but stays i64.

  A source literal above `i64::MAX`, such as `u64::MAX` written in code, is therefore not a
  symbolic constant. Its branch is reached through the boundary seeds and the generator endpoints,
  not through Z3. Widening `ConstValue` is out of scope.

## Fixture (append to `examples/rust/int-width/src/lib.rs`, committed by `int-unsigned64-clamp`)

These functions use `if`, because a function that only computes a boolean expression has no branch
and is skipped by explore:

```rust
pub fn at_u64_max(n: u64) -> &'static str {
    if n == u64::MAX { "max" } else { "other" }
}

pub fn above_i64_max(n: u64) -> &'static str {
    if n > 9_223_372_036_854_775_807 { "upper-half" } else { "lower-half" }
}

pub fn at_i64_min(n: i64) -> &'static str {
    if n == i64::MIN { "min" } else { "other" }
}
```

## Baseline (run before changing code, on the tip of `int-unsigned64-clamp` or main)

```bash
git rev-parse HEAD
cargo build -p shatter-cli && cargo build --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml
tmp=$(mktemp -d) && cp -r examples/rust/int-width "$tmp"/
for mode in "" --concolic; do
  for f in at_u64_max above_i64_max at_i64_min; do
    rm -rf "$tmp/int-width/shatter-artifacts" "$tmp/int-width/.shatter"
    target/debug/shatter explore "$tmp/int-width/src/lib.rs:$f" $mode --allow-host-writes \
      --max-iterations 60 --request-timeout 240
  done
done
```

Expected at 16794cef (recorded 2026-09-24):

| function | default explorer | `--concolic` |
|---|---|---|
| `at_u64_max` | only `"other"` (from `i64::MAX`), plus negative-input throws | not recorded; expected only `"other"` |
| `above_i64_max` | only `"lower-half"` (input `i64::MAX`) | only `"lower-half"` (input `0`), plus a `-1` boundary-seed throw |
| `at_i64_min` | reaches `"min"` | not recorded |

`at_i64_min` already reaches `"min"`, so it is a regression guard, not a failing case. After
`int-unsigned64-clamp`, the negative throws are gone but `"max"` and `"upper-half"` are still
unreached.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The fixture functions above are committed. The baseline output is pasted with
  `git rev-parse HEAD`.
- [ ] `IntRange` and the i128 value paths are implemented exactly as in **Contract**. The
  `int_range` doc comment and SPEC (plus `protocol/schemas/type-info.schema.json`'s `int_width`
  description) state the ranges and the 128-bit clamp.
- [ ] **Property tests over every (width, signed) row**, extending the table tests from
  `int-unsigned64-clamp` with the new bounds. For the generator, mutator, shrinker, boundary
  seeding and `concrete_to_json`:
  - every output is within `IntRange`;
  - both endpoints are reachable: `u64::MAX` and `0` for `(64,false)`, `i64::MIN` and `i64::MAX`
    for `(64,true)`;
  - `(128,false)` never yields a value above `u64::MAX`;
  - every value serializes as a JSON integer.
- [ ] **Solver tests.** Under the range assertion, `solve_constraints` with `x > 9223372036854775807`
  on a `(64,false)` param returns a model value above `i64::MAX` that survives
  `extract_concrete_values` and `concrete_to_json`. The same constraint on `(64,true)` is Unsat.
  Both fail or misbehave on main.
- [ ] **E2E** `e2e_rust_int_full_range` in `shatter-core/tests/e2e_concolic_rust.rs`, using
  `repo_examples_rust_dir().join("int-width/src/lib.rs")`, so no external checkout is needed. It
  asserts:
  - `at_u64_max` reaches `"max"`;
  - `above_i64_max` reaches `"upper-half"`;
  - `at_i64_min` reaches `"min"`;
  - every executed input is within the new bounds.

  Run it with
  `cargo build --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml && cargo test --test e2e_concolic_rust e2e_rust_int_full_range -- --include-ignored`.
  Paste the failing line from the pre-change tip and the passing line.
- [ ] Re-run the baseline loop on the branch. Inside the loop, after each `explore`, add
  `python3 scripts/check_int_width_bounds.py "$tmp/int-width/shatter-artifacts" --full-u64`. Paste output showing `"max"` and `"upper-half"` reached and
  `out of bounds: 0`.
- [ ] `task e2e` (all three suites) and `task affected` pass, with `Gates selected` recorded.

## Out of scope

- Bit-vector (wrapping and overflow) semantics.
- TS `bigint`.
- Widening `ConstValue::Int` or `LiteralValue::Int`.
- Values outside the 64-bit ranges and any string wire encoding for them. File a follow-up only if a
  target needs full `u128`/`i128`.
- Nested-field Z3 range assertions.

## Size

M–L
