title: Jev frontier-ranking benchmark
description:
## Change request

Measure whether an external decision model (TypeSafe's Jev: a choice question in, calibrated per-option probabilities out) improves concolic exploration effectiveness when used to rank exploration frontiers, compared with Shatter's built-in `frontier_score` heuristic. A seeded random ranker is the floor; a "cheating" ranker that knows the reference run's branch ids is the ceiling. The existing generative seed oracle is the real competitor.

## Why

The only LLM hookup today is the generative `SeedOracle` (str-7vs), which asks a frontier model to invent input vectors and is throttled because each call is slow and costly. Jev's published economics (roughly 100ms per call, $0.042 per million input tokens, free output, up to 255 options per choice question) would allow one decision per exploration round. Before building product features on it, we need a reproducible measurement with sanity gates that fail when the harness itself cannot separate a ceiling from a floor.

## Arm definitions (shared vocabulary for every child)

| arm | concrete type | needs |
|---|---|---|
| `heuristic` | `HeuristicRanker` (returns an empty score map, so `FrontierSet` uses `frontier_score`) | nothing |
| `random` | `RandomRanker { seed }` uniform scores per round, deterministic in (seed, round) | nothing |
| `cheating` | `ScriptedRanker { priority }` where `priority` is the set of branch ids the reference run (heuristic, 400 iterations, all seeds) discovered; scores 1.0 for those, 0.0 otherwise | `reference.json` |
| `generative` | `HeuristicRanker` plus the existing `SeedOracle` through the `anthropic` adapter, `max_queries_per_function: 10` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; skipped when unset |
| `jev` | `DecisionFrontierRanker` over `ReplayDecisionOracle(Some(JevAdapter))`, one choice question per round | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, or a committed replay cache; skipped when neither exists |

## Current code facts

- `shatter-core/src/frontier.rs`: `frontier_score(&Frontier) -> f64` (depth, stall decay, constraint boost, rarity). `FrontierSet::best_index` uses it. No policy hook exists.
- `shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs`: `frontier_score` orders drilling and bounded-unroll candidates in `solve_and_generate`; `poll_oracle_for_frontier` iterates `frontier_set.iter()` in insertion order and contains an inline predicate lookup (lines ~456-478) that recovers the branch's `SymConstraint` text and line from `raw_results`. Z3 negates every branch of every new path, so ranking does not gate Z3.
- `ExploreResult.discoveries: Vec<(u32, DiscoveryMethod)>` has no execution index. `total_executions` is the loop's execution counter.
- `ExploreConfig` derives `Clone` and `Debug`; `seed: Option<u64>` drives `StdRng::seed_from_u64`.
- `shatter-core/src/oracle.rs`: `SeedOracle` trait, `OracleSlotMap::new(oracle, LlmConfig, runtime)`, `OracleHandle { slot_map, function_source }`. `function_source` reaches the orchestrator only via `OracleHandle`.
- `shatter-llm`: adapters anthropic/openai/google/custom_http/local_model; `MockSeedOracle::{scripted, always_fail, always_empty}`; `build_oracle(&LlmConfig)`; `wiremock` in dev-deps.
- `shatter-core/tests/e2e_llm_oracle.rs` spawns the TS frontend directly and calls `orchestrator::explore_with_oracle`; the bench runner copies its helpers.
- Examples checkout: `python3 scripts/examples_checkout.py` populates `$TMPDIR/shatter-examples-main/standalone/ts/` (01-arithmetic.ts … 21-crypto-boundary.ts); `SHATTER_EXAMPLES_DIR` overrides.
- `scripts/perf_runner.py` times CLI scenarios only and cannot express ranker arms; a dedicated runner is needed.
- Jev API (docs.typesafe.ai, read 2026-09-21): `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`, header `Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, body `{"state": "...", "model": "jev-latest", "questions": {"<id>": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "...", "criteria": {"<key>": "<desc>"}}}}`, response `{"answers": {"<id>": {"choice": "<key>", "probabilities": {"<key>": p}, "confidence": c}}, "usage": {"input_tokens": n, "output_tokens": n}}`. Max 255 criteria per question.

## Children (each is one branch, landed in order)

1. Ranker policy in core (Child A)
2. DecisionOracle, Jev adapter, replay (Child B)
3. Bench runner, manifest, reference run (Child C, blocked by A and B)
4. Report script, Taskfile, docs (Child D, blocked by C)

## Out of scope for the epic

Feasibility pre-check before Z3, candidate ranking over cheap generators, CLI flags for the decision oracle, scan-report triage, held-out corpus split, and the first live Jev run (a separate task filed after D lands, because it needs a key holder to run it and commit the replay cache).

## Full implementation plan

Already written (session scratchpad, 2026-09-21). Child A's first commit copies it verbatim to `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jev-frontier-ranking-benchmark.md`; no authoring is required. It has per-step failing tests, code, and commands for every child.
notes:
First free-arm benchmark run (heuristic, random, cheating; 8 fixtures x 10 seeds x 2 regimes = 480 rows; rows and report.md in the session scratchpad, 2026-09-21).

Sanity gates FAILED as designed: median executions-to-cover is 5.0 for all three arms; paired deltas vs heuristic are +0.0 (95% CI +0.0, +0.0) for both random (n=54) and cheating (n=50). Per stratum the arms are indistinguishable except noise on high-fanout (10-path-router covers in only 1-3 of 10 seeds per arm).

Why: the rankers were consulted (median 68-95 rank_log entries per run for random/cheating), but no arm recorded a single Drilled discovery. Discovery methods were identical across arms (UserProvided 440, Z3 77, BoundarySearch 11) with only Fuzzed varying (25-35), which is RNG noise. The ranking's only consumers today are drilling order, bounded-unroll order and seed-oracle polling order; drilling needs DRILL_STALL_THRESHOLD failed solves per frontier and never triggered within a 60-execution budget, and Z3 negates every branch of every new path regardless of order.

Conclusion: frontier ordering has too little leverage at the current intervention points for any ranker (including Jev) to be measurable. Do not spend on a live Jev run against this harness. Follow-ups that would give a ranker real leverage, in order: (1) feasibility pre-check that gates which branches Z3 negates; (2) ranker-driven ordering of the worklist / candidate selection (BinaryHeap fitness) rather than only stalled frontiers; (3) a larger execution regime (300+) so drilling and bounded unroll actually fire, plus fixtures that stall (none of the 8 reached abandoned_frontiers > 0 at 200 executions).

title: Compare output invariants as a drift-resistant second signal in spec-diff
description:
str-nfg4y (landed 2abe9cf0) added a canonical-input-equality guard to diff_specs's changed_postconditions comparison: when a matched class's canonical examples have unequal (or missing) input vectors, the pair is reported as an inconclusive comparison_notes entry rather than a changed-postcondition regression. This is deliberately conservative -- it accepts a known false-negative risk: a genuine regression that also happens to correlate with a different canonical input being sampled (e.g. a code change that shifts a branch's admission condition, which both changes the class's output AND changes which inputs get sampled into it) gets silently downgraded to a note instead of flagged as a regression.

Investigated during str-nfg4y's landing analysis (2026-09-21): ClassifiedInvariant (shatter-core/src/invariants.rs) is Daikon-style and derived via detect_classified_invariants over ALL specimens in a class (confidence = fraction satisfying; detect_invariants only returns invariants holding for every specimen). InvariantTarget::Output invariants (NumericComparison, NumericConstant, NotNull, etc.) describe the output DOMAIN of the whole observed population for a branch path, not a single sampled point. This makes invariant comparison structurally resistant to the exact population-drift problem that defeats point-example comparison: it doesn't matter which single input was "simplest" and got canonicalized, because the invariant is derived from every specimen observed.

Proposed enhancement: when diff_specs's canonical-input guard produces a comparison_notes entry for a matched pair (str-nfg4y's MissingComparableWitness case), additionally compare the old and new SpecClass's output invariants (already-detected ClassifiedInvariant entries, InvariantTarget::Output) for that branch path. If they diverge (e.g. an invariant held in old but not new, or vice versa), elevate the note with an additional signal -- e.g. a distinct reason variant or a boolean/severity field -- so text/JSON output and any CI policy can distinguish "inconclusive, no other signal" from "inconclusive, but invariants also drifted -- elevated risk." Do not promote this to a hard changed_postconditions regression by default (invariant divergence is still probabilistic, not proof), but make it visibly distinct.

Caveats to resolve during implementation:
- Invariant detection is currently OFF by default in the production build_spec path used by diff_specs's inputs; build_spec_class always sets invariants: vec![] and only build_spec_with_invariants (via detect_spec_invariants) populates it. Wiring this in may require diff_specs's callers to opt into invariant-populated specs, or detecting invariants freshly inside the diff path from retained records (which may not be available at diff time -- specs are the persisted artifact, not raw executions).
- detect_classified_invariants requires class_records.len() >= 2; single-sample classes have no invariants to compare either way and fall back to the existing note-only behavior.
- This is a probabilistic net, not a proof: it narrows the false-negative window, it does not close it. Real regressions that happen not to violate any detected invariant will still be silently downgraded to a plain note.

Relationship to other issues: independent of str-gr41w (witness retention -- searches for a matching recorded input instead of comparing distributional properties) and str-mfmmr (lost_properties' separate aggregate-check exposure to the same root mechanism). Complementary to both, not a duplicate of either.

title: config::discover_configs tests leak ambient filesystem state via unbounded ancestor walk
description:
config::tests::discover_configs_finds_nearest_first, discover_configs_empty_when_no_shatter_dirs, and hierarchical_merge_integration (shatter-core/src/config.rs) call the production discover_configs(&sub) directly, which walks upward from `sub` all the way to the filesystem root `/`. The tests only construct .shatter dirs inside their own TempDir tree and then assert exact counts (configs.len(), configs.is_empty()), implicitly assuming no ancestor directory outside the TempDir (e.g. /tmp, or /) contains a stray .shatter/config.yaml.

That assumption breaks under any concurrent process (another Shatter run, another agent session sharing the same /tmp) that leaves a .shatter/ directory at /tmp or another shared ancestor -- e.g. `shatter init` run with a /tmp-rooted cwd during a gauntlet/demo run. Observed failure: discover_configs_empty_when_no_shatter_dirs fails "assertion failed: configs.is_empty()" and the other two fail count mismatches (expected 2, got 3) whenever a /tmp/.shatter/config.yaml exists, which is not under test control and can appear/disappear between runs on a shared machine.

discover_configs's unbounded upward walk to the real filesystem root is intentional production behavior (project config discovery is documented to walk from the target file up to the root, nearest wins) and must not change. The bug is purely in test isolation: these tests need to bound the walk to their own TempDir subtree so ambient state above it can never be observed.

Filed per operator direction during str-nfg4y landing (2026-09-19): "the tests shouldn't be using a globally visible directory like that. file an issue to get filesystem isolation then fix it." Being fixed together with this issue rather than deferred.

title: lost_properties all-throw/all-return check shares str-nfg4y's canonical-input root cause
description:
spec_diff.rs's lost_properties computation (old_all_throw/new_all_throw, old_all_return/new_all_return, spec_diff.rs:153-187) aggregates the postcondition *variant* (Throws vs. Returns) across all classes in a spec with no per-class canonical-input matching at all. It is a separate mechanism from the changed_postconditions comparison that str-nfg4y guards.

group_into_classes (equivalence.rs:111-150) groups purely by BranchPath, and pick_simplest selects the canonical member by input simplicity only, ignoring which outcome (throw vs return) that member had. A single branch path can legitimately contain members with mixed Throws/Returns outcomes across different sampled inputs.

This means a change to exploration order/budget alone -- the exact mechanism causing str-nfg4y -- can flip which member is canonical for a class and flip its postcondition variant, spuriously firing "all paths throw" / "all paths return" in lost_properties. Unlike changed_postconditions (fixed by str-nfg4y's guard), a lost_properties hit counts as a regression via has_regressions() and is NOT covered by str-nfg4y's canonical-input-equality guard, since lost_properties never compares per-class canonical inputs in the first place -- it just aggregates variants across all classes.

Needs either:
1. A canonical-input-aware guard analogous to str-nfg4y's fix (e.g. only aggregate the variant from classes/members whose canonical inputs are comparable across old/new), or
2. An explicit, tested proof that this aggregate check cannot misfire the way changed_postconditions did, if such a proof exists.

Raised by an independent cross-check review of the str-nfg4y implementation plan (2026-09-16). str-nfg4y intentionally excludes this from its scope to stay narrowly focused on changed_postconditions; that decision was accepted by the operator on the condition this follow-up issue is filed and the false-negative trade-off of the narrow fix is documented.

Related: str-nfg4y (canonical-input guard for changed_postconditions, same root mechanism, narrower scope), str-gr41w (witness retention, blocked by str-nfg4y).

title: Dry-run scan JSON undercounts lifecycle-excluded exports
description:
## Problem
After str-qwua7.56's lifecycle-export exclusion, shatter scan's dry-run JSON plan summary counters no longer add up when a setup-shaped file is present: shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs around line 1794 computes exported_total = registry.exported_functions().len() directly from the unfiltered registry, while total_functions_discovered (line ~1812) is computed from analyses.len() + skipped.len() where analyses has already had lifecycle-shaped exports removed by rebuild_analyses_from_registry. A consumer expecting total_functions_discovered == exported_total + unexported_total sees a mismatch with no field explaining the missing functions.

## Repro
A file exports only setup, teardown, and doWork (all exported). exported_total = 3, unexported_total = 0, but total_functions_discovered = 1 (only doWork survives the lifecycle exclusion).

## Acceptance
Dry-run JSON plan either accounts for excluded lifecycle exports in a dedicated field, or adjusts exported_total/unexported_total so the summary counters are internally consistent again. Add a unit/integration test asserting the invariant holds when a setup-shaped file is present.

## Provenance
Found during code review of str-qwua7.56 (shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs:1794), non-blocking follow-up -- filed rather than fixed inline to keep that landing focused.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run JSON summary counters (total_functions_discovered, exported_total, unexported_total) are internally consistent when a setup-shaped file's lifecycle exports are excluded from discovery; regression test added.

title: Provenance docs imply universal sample returns
description:
The intended product semantics are that a sampled return is an example, not the total set of outputs for a path. Current provenance language suggests a stronger guarantee and should explicitly describe what is actually established.

Current code facts: spec.rs Provenance::Proven docs (68) say "holds for all inputs on this path"; Postcondition::Returns.value (159) correctly says it is representative. build_spec_class (450-524) labels pre/post provenance Proven when every branch ID is in the Z3-discovered set, without proving an output proposition. pipeline.rs specify (635-652) performs the analogous branch-ID upgrade. Markdown emits "**Postcondition** [proven]: returns <sample>" at spec.rs:607. SPEC.md:626 describes the branch-discovery criterion but not the limitation of sampled outputs.

Concrete illustration, not a bug in sampling: for if x>0 { return x }, observations 1->1 and 2->2 follow one positive path. Canonical return 1 remains a valid example. Z3-supported path discovery does not mean all positive inputs return 1, and must not make such a claim.

Requested bounded change: keep current serialized enum/field names for compatibility, but document Proven as solver-derived branch-discovery provenance, not proof of a universal return value or completeness of the input/output set. Clarify both field docs and the Markdown display with an explicit short legend/label that representative outcomes are observed examples and the solver marker refers to path discovery. Update SPEC behavioral-spec section consistently. Reserve claims that a proposition holds for all path inputs for a separately verified proposition, not this marker.

Scope/size: spec.rs docs/Markdown wording/tests plus SPEC.md clarification; no solver proof system, output enumeration, field renaming, provenance algorithm redesign, or spec-diff fix. The actual opposite-direction association is a separate pipeline issue. This is contract clarity P2, not P1 proof unsoundness.

Protocol-visible behavior: no wire/serialized value change. Parity: JSON field documentation and human Markdown/SPEC explanation agree on the limited meaning. Default: clearer existing output; no flag. Tests: same-path varying-return fixture with solver discovery asserts preserved canonical example and explicit example/path-provenance explanation. Contracts: none required.

Resolved implementation lookups: spec.rs::tests::z3_discovered_branches_get_proven_provenance and all_z3_branches_means_proven supply existing marker fixtures; format_spec_markdown emits the badge and outcome. str-ck05 is closed live, so no current claim coordination is required for that historical issue.

title: Solved candidates enter unrelated spec classes
description:
The staged Specify pipeline puts an unexecuted solver candidate into every class containing its branch ID, even classes taking the opposite direction. A suggested input is then presented as an example of an observed behavior it has not demonstrated.

Current code facts: pipeline.rs SolvedBranch (83-92) records branch_id, line, target_taken and outcome. specify (656-672) ignores target_taken and the rest of the path, pushing a ConcreteExample with no return/error into all classes with the same ID. build_test_suggestions (function begins at line 742; solved-candidate loop at 767-782) already emits each SAT candidate separately as TestSuggestionSource::Solved, including target direction and no expected return/error. Thus the candidate can remain useful without asserting class membership.

Smallest existing regression starting point: pipeline.rs test specify_enriches_provenance_from_solved at 2780 creates stub_specify_inputs("provenFunc",1), whose observed branch 0 is taken=true and input is [42]. It supplies SolvedBranch { branch_id:0,line:10,target_taken:false,outcome:Sat{inputs:[-5]} }. Current test explicitly expects -5 appended to that true-path class. Reverse that bad assertion: its observed examples must remain [42], while a separate solved test suggestion still contains [-5] and target direction false.

Requested change: do not append unreplayed SAT candidates to SpecClass.examples. Keep them in the existing solved test_suggestions surface until an actual ExecuteResult establishes their full branch path and return/error. Merely matching target_taken would still not prove a multi-branch full path, so direction-only matching is not the repair. This issue does not require a new replay subsystem. Separate provenance-label wording/upgrade semantics are out of scope here.

Scope/size: pipeline.rs specify and existing tests; likely a deletion plus semantic assertions. System prevention: assert payload/path membership, not merely increased example count or presence of a solved input.

Protocol-visible behavior: no frontend wire change or new artifact fields; staged spec class examples are corrected and existing solved suggestions preserved. Compatibility: structurally unchanged serialized result. Parity: observed examples remain tied to actual execution, solved suggestions retain their existing source marker. Default: corrected behavior. Tests: opposite-direction fixture, two classes sharing ID, no replay result, unchanged observed examples. Contracts: no new contract; prevent invalid association by using existing separate types.

Resolved implementation lookups: pipeline.rs::tests::stub_specify_inputs supplies the observed branch/input fixture; tests::specify_enriches_provenance_from_solved is the named bad assertion; build_test_suggestions emits TestSuggestionSource::Solved with description containing branch ID, line and target direction, plus no expected_return/error. No new suggestion schema or replay type is needed.

title: Analysis cache trusts same-second timestamps
description:
AnalysisCache can return metadata for old source after a valid quick edit. Its advertised content-identity key is bypassed by whole-second mtime equality.

Current code facts: shatter-core/src/analysis_cache.rs AnalysisCacheEntry stores content_hash and mtime_secs; lookup (93-97) returns entry.analyses without hashing when mtime_secs matches. mtime_secs (219-225) calls duration.as_secs(), discarding subsecond precision. Analyzer-version/protocol-version mismatches correctly invalidate separately.

Self-contained deterministic regression in a temp directory:
1. Write source "export function before() { return 1; }\n". Set modification time using File::set_times(FileTimes::new().set_modified(UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::new(1_700_000_000,100_000_000))).
2. Store one FunctionAnalysis named "before" with AnalysisCache::store(&source,&[analysis],"test-analyzer"). Other fields can use the existing cache-test fixture.
3. Replace source with "export function after() { return 2; }\n"; set time to UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::new(1_700_000_000,900_000_000).
4. lookup(&source,"test-analyzer") currently returns Some(old "before" analysis). It must return None. Advancing the edit to second 1_700_000_001 currently produces a miss, showing timestamp truncation controls the outcome.

Requested change: verify source content identity before accepting an entry; higher-resolution timestamps alone are not a correctness guarantee when tools preserve or restore mtimes. Retain content-identical hits and independent protocol/analyzer invalidation. No sleeps in tests. This bug is source identity only, not unproven imported-type/config dependency invalidation.

Scope/size: analysis_cache.rs plus existing tests, one cache contract. System prevention: test different content under equal/coincident timestamps and identical content with changed timestamp, rather than relying on wall-clock waiting.

Protocol-visible behavior: no frontend wire change. Parity: all language consumers share this cache and must receive the same content-correct behavior. Default: corrected existing cache; no bypass flag. Required tests: controlled same-second and exactly-restored-time edits, unchanged-content hit, analyzer/protocol invalidation. Contracts: none required.

Resolved implementation lookups: analysis_cache.rs::tests::sample_analyses() constructs a complete FunctionAnalysis; its test analyzer constant is AV="analyzer-v1". The mtime contract appears in the module and lookup method docs of that same file. Reuse that fixture and set analyses[0].name for the before/after reproduction.

title: Signed remainder uses mathematical modulo
description:
The shared integer Mod encoding uses Z3 modulo, rejecting valid negative-remainder inputs under the target's truncating remainder semantics.

Current code facts: shatter-core/src/solver.rs convert_arithmetic (720) maps BinOpKind::Mod to l.modulo(&r). Real Mod is explicitly unsupported. The confirmed direct-control language is Rust: -1_i64 % 2_i64 == -1.

Reproduction (a unit test in shatter-core/src/solver.rs; notation expands directly to existing public types): x = SymExpr::Param { name: "x", path: [] }; I(n) = SymExpr::Const(ConstValue::Int(n)); F(n) = SymExpr::Const(ConstValue::Float(n)); B(op,a,b) = SymExpr::BinOp { op, left: Box::new(a), right: Box::new(b) }. Call solve_constraints(&constraints, Some(5000), &[ParamInfo { name: "x".into(), typ, type_name: None }]). This is a direct library reproduction, not a new frontend execution. On 2026-09-11 a fresh rebuild of current core at audited HEAD e50fc399f328711cbbe237c1e3918e96c1080656 produced the actual results below. Source was reread on 2026-09-12 and still contains the encoding. Optional original evidence: /tmp/shatter-followup-numeric-f2LZz8/probe.rs and probe.stdout.log; all necessary assertions are inline here.

typ=TypeInfo::Int { int_width: None, int_signed: None }; constraints=[B(Eq,x,I(-1)), B(Eq,B(Mod,x,I(2)),I(-1))]. Expected SAT x=-1; actual UNSAT. The native Rust witness satisfies both clauses.

Requested change: give the existing integer Mod operation truncating signed-remainder semantics for its supported target contract (remainder has dividend sign and a = trunc(a/b)*b + remainder), rather than the Z3 mathematical-modulo sign rule. This does not authorize inventing real-number Mod support or bundling a separate division implementation overhaul. Preserve existing behavior/handling for zero divisor and overflow cases unless the regression work exposes an explicit mismatch; do not assert those inputs have ordinary results.

Scope/size: one core arithmetic operation plus tests. Add signed operand combinations and bounded native-control semantic properties so this class cannot hide behind positive-only fixtures.

Protocol-visible behavior: no frontend JSON shape change; corrected core semantics affect solver consumers using the existing SymExpr/ParamInfo contract. Parity: shared core conversion must apply to direct solve_constraints, solve_for_new_path, and solve_for_mcdc_independence; do not repair only one caller. Default: corrected existing behavior, no opt-in flag. Required tests: Regression for x=-1, divisor=2; sign combinations of nonzero divisors with bounded safe i64 operands checked against native Rust %, and existing core arithmetic tests. Use existing shared semantic generators where suitable; run repository-selected Rust gates and the applicable concolic integration task through its normal wrapper. Contracts: no new contract required for this fix; existing Z3-boundary/type checks must remain valid. No frontend producer rewrite is proposed; if a producer has a different documented Mod meaning, record that explicit incompatibility instead of silently broadening its semantics.

Resolved implementation lookups: convert_arithmetic applies integer l.modulo(&r) without an explicit zero-divisor or MIN/-1 check; Z3 is mathematical integer arithmetic here, not a target-width execution engine. Real Mod already returns SolverError::Unsupported("modulo not supported on reals"). Exceptional integer operands are excluded from the native-equivalence property and are to be characterized as an existing evidence limit, not claimed to return valid target results. This ticket does not silently establish a zero/overflow execution contract.

Live duplicate check: searched the 1,736-issue Shatter snapshot obtained with bd on 2026-09-12 (/tmp/shatter-backlog-str-live-20260912.json); searched titles/descriptions and read relevant matching issue bodies. No direct open duplicate. Closed str-weo covers arithmetic translation, not target signed-remainder conformance.

Evidence-location note: /tmp paths above are ephemeral, session-local breadcrumbs and may no longer exist. They are not prerequisites; use the inline reproduction and repository entrypoints.

## Acceptance checks

1. The reproduced negative witness is SAT and its returned value satisfies native Rust remainder semantics.
2. For bounded i64 operands and nonzero divisors excluding overflow, the modeled remainder equals native %, including both dividend and divisor signs.
3. Existing unsupported real-Mod and zero/overflow handling are explicit and regression-tested rather than accidentally changed by the repair.

title: A shatter binary cannot self-identify the source revision that built it
description:
## Symptom
Given an arbitrary `shatter` executable on disk, there is no way to ask it what
it was built from. `--version` reports a package version and three frontend
artifact hashes; nothing names an engine revision, covers the Rust core or CLI,
or records whether the build tree was dirty.

## What already works, so the gap is narrow
Released binaries are not affected. `.github/workflows/release.yml:266` emits a
manifest carrying `git_sha`, `git_short_sha`, and a per-asset `sha256`, and
`install.sh` verifies assets against it (`sha256_file`, `manifest_field`). For
anything installed through that path, provenance exists.

The gap is **self-identification of a binary in hand**:

- a local `cargo build --release` artifact, which is what development and any local measurement actually run;
- a binary copied out of `target/release` into a scratch directory or another machine;
- a released binary that has been moved away from its manifest.

In all three the manifest is absent or unlinked, and the binary itself says
nothing.

## Evidence
```
$ shatter --version
shatter 0.1.0
go-frontend-source-hash: 0fa742559cc988ebcc013d534b7a2e06f5f1eefcfd459cb2791e849df26a431b
go-frontend-binary-hash: 4f46929b18cdeaa57b780976f2be40174dcf3d0f620d95c6fba0a08f728d9329
ts-frontend-bundle-hash: a17ac76996c87f5fc0ff494dbd2d5c5d60735d5fccbdf41df7564484cffbd6c3
```
Three hashes, all frontend artifacts. Nothing for the Rust core or CLI, and no
revision.

Recording a checkout's HEAD alongside the binary does not close it: that
establishes what was checked out, not what was compiled. The two diverge
whenever a build predates a later checkout change, or a binary is copied
between trees.

## Why it matters
Attributing a measured change to an engine revision — a benchmark tracking
whether the engine is improving, a bisect over engine commits, a regression
report naming a build — requires binding the binary to a revision. Without it a
delta can be credited to a change that was never in the binary that produced
it, and two different binaries can be compared as one engine. The failure is
silent: the numbers look fine.

## Desired behavior
Embed the revision at build time and report it:

```
shatter 0.1.0 (a1b2c3d4, dirty)
```

**Output contract**, which must be specified rather than left to the
implementation:

- `revision`: full 40-char SHA, or the literal `unknown` when built without git metadata (source archive, vendored build).
- `dirty`: true when `git status --porcelain` over **tracked** files is non-empty at build time — staged or unstaged. Untracked files do **not** set it, since build inputs are tracked; say so explicitly so an implementation cannot quietly pick the other reading.
- `inspection_failed`: distinct from both. When the build script cannot run git at all, the state is neither clean nor dirty and must not be reported as clean.

**Surface.** `--version` for humans, plus a machine-readable form, because a
consumer recording results needs it without scraping a banner. Note that
`ScanReport` (`shatter-core/src/report.rs:1100`) has no run-metadata member
today, and `RunManifest` (`shatter-core/src/run_manifest.rs:85`) already carries
git fields describing the **scanned project** — engine build identity is a
different thing and must not be conflated with it. Adding a field to either
carries a schema-compatibility decision that should be made explicitly.

## Acceptance checks
- `shatter --version` names a full revision, or `unknown` when git metadata is absent.
- A build from a tree with a staged or unstaged tracked modification reports `dirty`.
- A build where git cannot be inspected reports `inspection_failed`, not clean.
- The value is retrievable machine-readably without parsing human output.
- **Incremental-build correctness**: without cleaning `target/`, commit a Rust-only change and rebuild — the reported revision must change. `shatter-cli/build.rs:95` currently registers frontend inputs for rebuild detection, so naive git capture can be cached across Rust-only edits under Cargo's change-detection rules. Exercise clean → dirty → committed transitions in the same build directory, and in a linked worktree as well as the primary checkout.

## Scope
In scope: capturing the engine revision and dirty state at build time, and
reporting both.
Out of scope: reproducible builds, signing, extending the frontend hashes to
cover the Rust core, and changing the release manifest, which already works.

## Related
`str-o09e` (frontend provenance) covers adjacent ground. The tracked issue
export consulted here was last updated 2026-08-30, so live duplicate checking
is worth redoing at filing time.

comments.text:
Scope note: released binaries are NOT affected. .github/workflows/release.yml:266 emits a manifest carrying git_sha, git_short_sha and per-asset sha256, and install.sh verifies assets against it (sha256_file, manifest_field). An earlier draft of this issue claimed provenance rested entirely on operator bookkeeping; that was too broad and an independent review corrected it.

Related: str-o09e (closed) covered deterministic + detectable embedded-frontend builds, including build.rs rerun-if-changed missing edits. That is adjacent and directly relevant to this issue's incremental-build acceptance check -- naive git capture in build.rs can be cached across Rust-only edits for the same reason.

title: Report the effective exploration seed, and make seeded exploration testable
description:
## Symptom
Nothing in Shatter's output states which seed a run actually used, and there is
no test that can distinguish a run whose RNG was seeded from one that drew from
entropy. The second problem is the important one: seed propagation can break
silently and no suite would notice.

## Evidence
- `shatter scan <dir> --seed 4242 -vv` emits no line naming the seed. The only `seed`-matching debug output is `[debug] [scan] 3 planner seed(s) for <fn>`, which concerns candidate *inputs*, not the RNG.
- The `ScanReport` JSON has no seed field.
- Attempts to detect seeding behaviourally all failed. Three fixtures were tried — a four-branch classifier, sparse equality guards over a wide integer space, and the same with a capped iteration budget — and every one produced **identical coverage across unseeded runs**, because the input generator mines literals from source rather than depending on the RNG.

## Why it matters
Concretely, and not hypothetically: the test accompanying the `--seed` wiring
work **passes with and without the wiring**. That was verified by reverting the
change, rebuilding, and re-running; it did not fail. With no observable seed and
no fixture whose coverage varies unseeded, there is no way to write a test that
fails when propagation breaks.

Separately, a harness comparing two runs needs to record that both were seeded
and identically. Today it can only record the flag it passed, not what the
engine used.

## Desired behavior

**1. Define which seed is being reported.** "The seed" is currently three
things, and the field must say which:

- the **exploration base seed** — the value reaching `ScanConfig.seed`, consumed at `shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs:2492`;
- **per-worker derived seeds** — replicas derive their own from the base (`shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs:4506`), so a single scalar does not describe a multi-worker run;
- the **core-sample selection seed**, which has its own deterministic fallback (hash of directory + git HEAD) when `--seed` is absent, and is a different concern from exploration.

Reporting the exploration base seed plus the derivation rule is sufficient;
reporting one number labelled "seed" is not.

**2. Report it machine-readably.** A field in the `ScanReport` is required —
that is what a consumer needs. A log line is optional and does not satisfy this.
An unseeded run must carry an explicit unseeded marker, distinguishable from
`--seed 0`.

**3. Make propagation testable.** This is the part that closes the real gap.
Recording the flag value proves nothing: a report could echo `--seed` while
exploration still ran on entropy, and every check below would pass. The reported
value must be captured at the point of RNG construction, not at argument
parsing, so that breaking propagation changes the output.

## Acceptance checks
- A scan with `--seed 4242` records `4242` in the report, sourced from where the RNG is constructed.
- A scan without `--seed` records an explicit unseeded marker, distinct from the value recorded for `--seed 0`.
- A multi-worker run records the base seed and the derivation rule, not one worker's derived value.
- **A regression test fails when seed propagation is deliberately broken** — e.g. reverting the `ScanConfig.seed` wiring, or short-circuiting the derivation, makes the suite red. This is the check that matters; without it the others are satisfiable by an echo.
- Coverage of both the random and concolic exploration paths, which initialise separately.

## Scope
In scope: surfacing the exploration seed from the RNG construction site, and a
propagation regression test.
Out of scope: changing seeding behaviour; making parallel scheduling
deterministic (seeding alone does not remove all nondeterminism); and the
core-sample seed's existing fallback behaviour.

## Related
Follow-up to `str-0m0vn`. That work is **committed on branch
`str-0m0vn-exploration-seed` (`bce4ef08`) and not yet merged** — it is on
neither local nor `origin/main`, and `str-0m0vn` remains open. This issue
depends on that branch landing, and takes over the seed-regression testing that
`str-0m0vn` could not deliver, for the reason described above.

`str-8q1b4` (resumed-report comparability) is adjacent but distinct.

comments.author: Test
comments.text:
Dependency note: this depends on str-0m0vn landing. That work is committed on branch str-0m0vn-exploration-seed (bce4ef08 wiring, a234fc77 test hardening) and pushed, but is NOT merged -- it is on neither local main nor origin/main, and str-0m0vn remains open.

This issue takes over the seed-regression testing that str-0m0vn could not deliver: the test committed there passes with AND without the wiring, verified by reverting, rebuilding and re-running. Exploration on small fixtures is deterministic regardless of seed because the input generator mines literals from source, so no behavioural test can distinguish seeded from unseeded until the effective seed is observable.

title: Tracker content sweep: dedupe, merge, fill bodies, fix placeholder refs, priorities
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
All proposed defaults approved: close str-hrg2 as duplicate of str-0wxw; merge str-wfd2 into str-1fik (P1) and close str-wfd2; str-2zsy author fills the body or it closes as insufficient detail; defer str-cl53; replace the str-35vtk.* `issue<N>` placeholders with real ids from docs/perf/efficiency-plan.md; str-j49xg body becomes "not split; work tracked here"; promote str-u394l.4 to P1 (str-u394l.3 is now being adopted, see storystore decision); str-rmcrl to P2 and land it.

## Problem
A handful of open issues are unstartable or misleading for a fresh agent: two are byte-for-byte duplicates, two describe one feature at two priorities (one with an empty body), the `str-35vtk.*` batch cross-references plan-local ids that resolve to nothing, and an epic promises children that were never filed. Together they are why `bd ready` hands out the wrong work.

- `str-0wxw` ≡ `str-hrg2`: both P2 bugs "axum handler generators re-seed FK chain per iteration", created 2026-06-16, near-identical bodies; `str-0wxw` carries the refinement notes (single- vs multi-param path handlers).
- `str-1fik` (P1 feature, **empty body**) vs `str-wfd2` (P2, full body: `analyzer.rs convert_type_path()` single-file scope, pickpackit impact, desired change) — same work.

- `str-j49xg` (P1 epic) body says "Child issues (filed alongside)" — no dotted children exist.
- Priority hygiene: `str-u394l` P1 epic with only P2 children; `str-rmcrl` P3 for a red `clippy -D warnings` on main; 23 of 96 open are P1.

## Options considered

- Merge: keep `str-1fik` (older id, P1) with `str-wfd2`'s body pasted in; close `str-wfd2` as duplicate; priority P1 if pickpackit coverage is still a goal, else P2.

title: Delete the dead test emitters (export.rs) and the README "or tests" claim
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
Delete the dead test emitters. The CLI export surface was removed in str-tlnt and nothing outside `shatter-core/src/export.rs` calls `generate_jest_tests`/`generate_vitest_tests`/`generate_go_tests`. Remove export.rs (1,743 lines) and its tests, the `export.rs — Test generation from behavior maps` line in shatter-core/CLAUDE.md, and README step 4's "or tests". No SPEC test-export column is needed because the feature no longer exists.

## Problem
SPEC §1.3 lists TypeScript, Go and Rust all as "Supported" and says other docs treat it as canonical. `export.rs` generates Jest, Vitest and Go tests but has no Rust generator, and no test compiles or runs any emitted file. Either the emitter exists for every supported language or the status table should say what is missing.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-core/src/export.rs`: `generate_jest_tests` (:239), `generate_jest_tests_with_annotations` (:254), `generate_go_tests` (:301), `generate_go_tests_with_annotations` (:315), `generate_vitest_tests` (:612), `generate_vitest_tests_with_annotations` (:626). No `generate_rust_tests`.
- Unit tests assert string content only; emitted Go/Jest runnability is not verified in-crate.
- The CLI export flag was removed (str-tlnt, commit 87cad05b); README.md "How Shatter Works" step 4 still says "optional specs or tests"; `shatter-core/CLAUDE.md:11` lists `export.rs — Test generation from behavior maps`.
- SPEC.md:56-64 status table; §7.1 lists Rust parity gaps but not test export.

## Options
1. **Downgrade now (proposed default)**: SPEC §1.3 gains a "Test export" column (TS Y, Go Y, Rust N) and a §7 limitation row; README step 4 says "specs (and, via the library, Jest/Vitest/Go tests)"; file a follow-up feature "Rust test emitter + compile checks for all emitters".
2. **Emitter now**: `generate_rust_tests` (+ `_with_annotations`) emitting `#[test]` fns with `assert_eq!`/`should_panic` from a `BehaviorMap`, plus compile-check tests (`rustc --crate-type lib` on a temp file; `go vet`/`tsc --noEmit` for the others).
3. Delete `export.rs` and the README claim (usability rec 13) — only if the CLI export surface is not coming back.

## Acceptance checks
- Decision recorded; SPEC §1.3/§7 and README consistent with it; if option 2, compile checks exist for all four emitters.

## Scope
In: export.rs + SPEC/README wording. Out: re-adding the CLI `--export-tests` flag (separate decision).

## Size
small (downgrade) / medium (emitter).

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 28; evidence audits/2026-09-04/design-foundation.md §1 (Test generation), rec 6; usability-ui.md §4.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).

title: Embed the Rust frontend in the shatter binary like TS/Go
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
Embed the Rust frontend in the shatter binary the way TS and Go are embedded (option 2). Until it lands, `doctor` reports Rust resolution (str-qwua7.40). SPEC §1.3 gains a Distribution column reading embedded for all three once done.

## Problem
TS and Go frontends are embedded in the `shatter` binary; Rust ships as a separate `shatter-rust` executable that must be on PATH or next to a source checkout. QUICKSTART's build-from-source path (`cargo build --release`) therefore yields a binary that silently skips `.rs` targets; the captured audit environment had `STATUS skipped_by_unavailable_frontend` for every Rust target. SPEC §1.3 says "Supported" with no mention of the distribution difference.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-cli/src/embedded_frontend.rs` (TS bundle) and `embedded_go_frontend.rs` (Go binary) are produced by `shatter-cli/build.rs` (:92-157 runs `npm run bundle`, copies bundles into `OUT_DIR`).
- Rust discovery: `shatter-cli/src/helpers.rs` looks for `shatter-rust/target/{release,debug}/shatter-rust` relative to cwd, then PATH; `install.sh:15-22` copies the sibling binary from the release archive.
- README.md:88-117 "Enabling Rust scans from a source build" explains this (contributor-facing); QUICKSTART.md:36-46 build-from-source does not; QUICKSTART "Notes" mentions `cargo build --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml` only at the end.
- `scan` skips `.rs` with a 600-char warning; `run` aborts (p1-11). `--require-rust` exists on explore/scan. `shatter-rust` is excluded from the Cargo workspace (root `Cargo.toml`), which is why a single `cargo build` cannot produce it.

## Options
1. **Document now (proposed default)**: SPEC §1.3 gains a "Distribution" column (embedded / embedded / sibling binary) and §7 a limitation row; QUICKSTART §1 build-from-source shows `cargo build --release --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml` inline with a one-line "why"; README's section is linked, not duplicated (p2-31b).
2. **Embed**: `build.rs` invokes `cargo build --manifest-path shatter-rust/Cargo.toml` and embeds the binary like Go (`embedded_rust_frontend.rs`); remove sibling discovery; release archive shrinks to one file. Cost: nested cargo in build.rs, doubles cold build time, needs the same staleness hashing as the Go embed (str-o09e).

## Acceptance checks
- Decision recorded; docs or embedding implemented accordingly; `doctor` reports resolution (p2-28c) either way.

## Scope
In: distribution decision + docs. Out: `scan`/`run` behavior alignment (p1-11), `doctor` check (p2-28c), Rust parity gaps.

## Size
small (docs) / large (embedding).

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 28; evidence audits/2026-09-04/design-foundation.md §2.5, §2.8; usability-ui.md §7.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria: - Decision recorded; docs or embedding implemented accordingly; `doctor` reports resolution (p2-28c) either way.

title: Remove the invariant confidence score from code, spec output and SPEC §3.4
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
Remove the confidence score entirely. Today `detect_classified_invariants` stamps a constant 1.0 and nothing reads it. Drop `confidence`/`satisfied_count`/`total_count` from `ClassifiedInvariant` and `SpecInvariant`, the `[1] (n/n)` rendering in spec.rs, the YAML `confidence:` field and `ConfidenceLevel`, and the SPEC §3.4 sentence; keep only the observed-sample count if it is cheap to keep as `observed_samples`.

## Problem
SPEC §3.4 says invariants "are classified with confidence scores (satisfied_count / total_count)". The detector only returns invariants that hold for every specimen, so `confidence` is a hard-coded `1.0` and `satisfied_count == total_count` always. There is no minimum-sample guard, so with two executions `x > 0` is reported as an invariant with confidence 1.0. The spec overstates what the number means.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-core/src/invariants.rs:655-665`: `ClassifiedInvariant { confidence: 1.0, // detect_invariants only returns invariants that hold for all specimens, satisfied_count: total, total_count: total }`.
- `SpecInvariant` (`spec.rs:118`) carries `confidence: ConfidenceLevel`; rendered by `specify --yaml` / `properties` as `property:` lines and compared by `spec-diff` "lost properties".
- Nine `InvariantKind`s (invariants.rs:35) match the SPEC §3.4 table; no implication/disjunction; no cross-param relation beyond `OutputEqualsInput`.
- SPEC.md:648: "Invariants are classified with confidence scores (satisfied_count / total_count) and reported at both function-wide and per-class levels."

## Options
1. **Implement (proposed default)**: `detect_invariants` evaluates every candidate against all specimens and returns those with `satisfied/total ≥ min_confidence` (config `invariants.min_confidence`, default 1.0 so output is unchanged by default) and `total ≥ min_samples` (config `invariants.min_samples`, **default 3**); proptest: reported `confidence == satisfied/total`; no invariant emitted from fewer than `min_samples` specimens; `spec-diff` "lost properties" unaffected at the defaults.
2. **Remove the claim**: SPEC §3.4 rewritten to "invariants are reported only when they hold for all N observed samples; `sample_count` is exported; no statistical confidence is computed"; `confidence` removed from the JSON/YAML or documented as always 1.0.

## Acceptance checks
- Decision recorded; SPEC §3.4 and `invariants.rs` agree; `specify --yaml`/`properties` output covered by a test at the defaults.

## Scope
In: invariants.rs, SPEC §3.4, YAML property rendering. Out: new invariant kinds.

## Size
small (doc) / medium (implementation).

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 29; evidence audits/2026-09-04/design-foundation.md §1 (Invariant detection), rec 7.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria: - Decision recorded; SPEC §3.4 and `invariants.rs` agree; `specify --yaml`/`properties` output covered by a test at the defaults.

title: Unify terminology on "behavior class" across explore, scan, spec, JSON and help (no compat period)
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
"behavior class" everywhere, with no backward compatibility: prose, --help, SPEC, GLOSSARY, walkthrough expectations, and JSON keys all change in one release (`classes`/`equivalence_classes`/`behaviors` collapse to `behavior_classes`; `Class N`/`Cluster N`/`path(s)` become `behavior class`). No synonym period; goldens and consumers are updated in the same change.

## Problem
One concept — a group of executions sharing a branch path — has four user-visible names in one session: explore prints "path(s)", the spec prints "Class N" / "Behavioral classes", scan prints "Cluster N", JSON uses `classes`, `equivalence_classes`, and `behaviors`, and help text says "equivalence classes, behavior map". Users and agents cannot tell whether these are different things.

## Current code facts
- Explore markdown report (`shatter-core/src/explorer.rs format_exploration_report`, captured `ui/ts-explore.out`): "Unique paths", "New paths".
- Spec (`spec.rs:192 SpecClass`, label "Class N — …"; markdown heading "Behavioral classes").
- Scan report (`report.rs:298 BehaviorClusterSummary`; markdown "Cluster N").
- JSON keys: `FunctionSpec.classes`; scan JSON `equivalence_classes`; snapshot `behaviors`.
- `--help` (`args.rs`): "equivalence classes", "behavior map"; `--show-clusters` flag name.
- SPEC.md §3.1 defines "Equivalence Classes"; §3.2 "Behavior Maps"; docs/GLOSSARY.md defines neither.

## Options
1. **"behavior class" everywhere (proposed default)**: prose in explore/scan/spec markdown, `--help`, SPEC §3/§5 and GLOSSARY use "behavior class"; JSON keys keep `classes`/`equivalence_classes`/`behaviors` as **documented synonyms for one release** (SPEC §5 states the canonical key `classes` and marks the others deprecated), then rename with a `version` bump in `FileSpecBundle`/scan JSON.
2. "path" everywhere (matches the mechanism, but clashes with file paths in the same reports).
3. Leave prose, document the synonyms only.

## Acceptance checks
- Decision recorded. If option 1: one term in all markdown/help/SPEC; GLOSSARY gains behavior class, behavior map, spec vs snapshot vs report, harness, adapter, opaque type; synonyms table in SPEC §5; `demo/walkthrough.sh` expectations and golden tests updated; `task docs-smoke`, `task golden-test` green; follow-up issue for the key rename with a date.

## Scope
In: user-visible wording, glossary, synonym policy. Out: struct renames in core beyond serde keys.

## Size
small–medium.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 26; evidence audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md §2, rec 10; docs-quality.md P3-1.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria: - Decision recorded. If option 1: one term in all markdown/help/SPEC; GLOSSARY gains behavior class, behavior map, spec vs snapshot vs report, harness, adapter, opaque type; synonyms table in SPEC §5; `demo/walkthrough.sh` expectations and golden tests updated; `task docs-smoke`, `task golden-test` green; follow-up issue for the key rename with a date.

title: Keep implicit init; document it and add --no-init / SHATTER_NO_INIT=1
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
Option 1: keep implicit init and make it explicit in docs. SPEC §2.1/§2.8 state that execution commands create `.shatter/config.yaml` (and the gitignore block unless tracked) when absent; add `--no-init` (and honour `SHATTER_NO_INIT=1`) for read-only use, with a test that a fresh directory is untouched when opted out. Setup lines to stderr is tracked separately (str-qwua7.39).

## Problem
A first `shatter explore file.ts:fn` in a directory with no `.shatter/` silently writes `.shatter/config.yaml` and a managed `.gitignore` block into the cwd. README says installing and initializing "are separate steps" and SPEC §2.8 presents `init` as the explicit opt-in; SPEC §2.1 does not mention that explore initializes. Users running Shatter against a checkout they do not own get unexpected files.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-cli/src/main.rs:43-52` `run_implicit_init` runs before dispatch for the initialized-project path; `init.rs:16-38` doc: implicit init "still creates `.shatter/` and a *new* `.gitignore` exactly like an explicit `init` (that preserves today's first-run ergonomics), but if `.gitignore` is already tracked it is left alone" (str-w5jt9, `tests/implicit_init_gitignore_test.rs`).
- README.md "Initialize a Project": "Installing … and initializing a project are separate steps"; `docs/PROJECT-LAYOUT.md:44-47` "some commands will initialize it implicitly".
- Other commands also write `.shatter-cache/` and `shatter-artifacts/` on demand (SPEC §2.8 "Effect on the project tree").

## Options
1. **Keep implicit init, make it explicit in docs (proposed default)**: SPEC §2.1 and §2.8 state that execution commands create `.shatter/config.yaml` (+ gitignore block unless tracked) when absent; add `--no-init` (or honour `SHATTER_NO_INIT=1`) for read-only use; status lines on stderr (p2-27a).
2. **Never write project state unless `.shatter/` exists or `--init` is passed**: first-run ergonomics regress (user must run `shatter init` first); QUICKSTART updated.
3. Prompt when interactive, skip when not (adds TTY detection; agents get option 2 behavior).

## Acceptance checks
- Decision recorded in SPEC §2.1/§2.8 and PROJECT-LAYOUT; the chosen flag/env implemented with a test that a fresh directory is untouched when opted out.

## Scope
In: policy + one flag. Out: init's own behavior.

## Size
small.

Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 27; evidence audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md §2; docs-accuracy.md P2-3.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).

description:

## Problem
bugshot is installed and dormant because `.agent-plugins/bento/bugshot/viz/capture-command` is missing; `agent-env-doctor` prints a nudge every session. bugshot's `vizline`/`vizdiff` skills were designed for web screenshots and nobody has decided whether Shatter's rendered outputs (walkthrough transcripts, HTML/markdown reports) count. The audit filed a bugshot-side item (audit item 20 / draft 53) to add a documented CLI capture template; wiring today means hand-writing the capture-command against an undocumented contract.

- bugshot README/skills assume web screenshots; no `--kind cli` path exists yet (bugshot draft 53).

title: Keep Codex support: write .codex/AGENTS.md with the tool mapping; remove empty .agents/
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
Keep Codex support. Write `.codex/AGENTS.md` with the Claude-to-Codex tool mapping (Grep/Read/Glob/Edit → shell equivalents, TeamCreate/Monitor → none), a note that Codex has no require-worktree hook so the worktree rule is policy-only there, and remove the empty `.agents/` directory. Mark Claude-only sections of AGENTS.md during its rewrite (str-qwua7.23).

## Problem
Codex sessions would get AGENTS.md written in Claude tool vocabulary (`Grep`, `Read`, `TeamCreate`, `Monitor`) and no require-worktree equivalent ("enforced by policy only" per `~/dotfiles/codex/AGENTS.md`), while the Codex-facing directories are symlinks or empty. Keeping half-wired Codex surfaces suggests support that does not exist.

## Current code facts
- `.codex/`: symlinks `agents -> ../.claude/agents`, `skills -> ../.claude/skills/`, `swarm-config.md -> ../.claude/swarm-config.md` (2026-03-16), plus an empty `worktrees/` (2026-04-18). No `.codex/AGENTS.md` or hooks.

- `~/.codex/hooks.json` has only tmc; `bento:cross-check` (Claude↔Codex review) is a hard trigger but nothing in the project wires it; 252 session transcripts analysed were all Claude Code.
- AGENTS.md :23-25 (tool names) and the swarm section (:376-449) reference Claude-only tools.

## Options

title: Repo-owned landing fixes now (verifier honesty, timeout); orchestration driver comes from bento
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
Wait for bento. The failure modes are covered by bento-rdtn and str-qwua7.1/.2; the missing single orchestrating command is filed in bento (see bento draft 64) rather than as a shatter-local wrapper. This issue only fixes the repo-owned pieces now: `land_work_verifier.sh` runs `task check` (or states exactly what it runs) and `verifier.json` gains a timeout.

## Problem
Landing is the most repeated manual procedure in 252 sessions: agents type the same ~10-step sequence of bento scripts by hand, get one step wrong, and thrash. `land-work-prepare.py` fails 32% of the time and `verify-lease.py` 17%, mostly from ordering/state mistakes (dirty tree, lease moved, run from the primary checkout on `main`); create-preview was called 195 times against 90 cleanups, matching the five orphaned `/tmp/land-work-preview-*` worktrees. The same failure modes are filed against bento (preview cleanup, killed verifier, diverged primary, executed-vs-cached), and the repo already suffers from having three documented landing procedures — a fourth, repo-local one must become the *only* one or it adds to the problem.

## Current code facts
- Scripts (bento 2.2.6, `~/.claude/plugins/cache/bento/bento/2.2.6/skills/`): `launch-work/scripts/launch-work-verify.py`, `land-work/scripts/{land-work-prepare,land-work-create-preview,land-work-run-verifier,land-work-verify-lease,land-work-verify-landing,land-work-root-hygiene}.py`; project verifier manifest `.agent-plugins/bento/bento/land-work/verifier.json` → `scripts/land_work_verifier.sh`. The plugin cache is not repo-owned; the only repo-owned hook point is `verifier.json` and the AGENTS.md/skill text.
- Retrospective (session-retro.md §1, §3): exact 3-gram `git fetch → create-preview → run-verifier` 49×; `land-work-prepare.py` 18/57 failures, `land-work-verify-lease.py` 11/66, `launch-work-verify.py` 6/22; `land_work_flake` keyword in 16 sessions; 8 `fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree` since 2026-08-23 (primary checkout bare, p1-01).
- `scripts/land_work_verifier.sh` header claims "same gates ci.yml uses" but runs `test-standard + parity + conformance`; CI runs `task check`; no `timeout` in `verifier.json`; verifier output not captured on kill (memory `project_land_work_verifier_first_run_flake`).
- Memory `feedback_primary_checkout_diverged_local_main` documents a hand-rolled fourth landing path (merge inside the preview).
- bento-side items from this audit (bento-rdtn children): always-clean previews + verifier logs, native diverged-primary handling, executed-vs-cached assertion, launch-work/superpowers precedence note.

## Options
1. **Wait (proposed default)**: let bento-rdtn land the cleanup/log/diverged-primary/executed-vs-cached fixes in `land-work` itself; meanwhile fix the repo-owned pieces only — `land_work_verifier.sh` runs `task check` (or says what it runs), `verifier.json` gets a `timeout`, AGENTS.md's manual landing script is deleted (a2-38a) so `bento:land-work` is the single procedure. Re-evaluate when bento-rdtn closes: if prepare/lease failure rates are still >10% in the next retrospective, build option 2.
2. **Build now**: `scripts/land.sh <issue> <branch>` chaining prepare → `git fetch` → create-preview → run-verifier (tee to `<preview>/verifier.log`, timeout) → verify-lease → merge (explicit merge commit, from the preview when the primary is bare/diverged) → push → verify-landing → root-hygiene → cleanup with a `trap`; refuses on primary/`main` or dirty tree with an exact fix; exits non-zero when the verifier ran zero checks; `scripts/test_land.sh` dry-runs diverged-primary and dirty-tree paths. Pinned to bento 2.2.6 script paths, so it must be revalidated on every bento upgrade — the main cost of this option.

## Acceptance checks
Amended by the audit 2026-09-22 comment on this issue (findings tests-ci-06, agent-repo-11). "`verifier.json` has a timeout" is replaced: installed bento (2.3.88; also 2.3.73) takes the verifier timeout only from the `--timeout` CLI argument of `land-work-run-verifier.py`/`land.py`, never from `verifier.json`, so a manifest field would be ignored.
- Decision recorded with the retrospective numbers that justified it.
- Either branch: exactly one documented landing procedure remains in the repo (AGENTS.md points at it).
- `land_work_verifier.sh`'s claim matches what it runs: satisfied by str-35vtk.24's change (exactly one exact-candidate `task check`) plus correcting the header comment at `scripts/land_work_verifier.sh:3` ("Runs the same gates ci.yml uses") and any CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md text that repeats it. Running `task affected` in the verifier is **not** an option; it would conflict with str-35vtk.24.
- The timeout is enforced by a mechanism the runner actually honours. Either (a) `scripts/land_work_verifier.sh` bounds its own gate run (for example `timeout --kill-after=30 <seconds> task check`, killing the whole process group, with the seconds passed as an argument in `verifier.json`'s `command` array, e.g. `["scripts/land_work_verifier.sh", "--timeout", "3600"]`, and a documented default when absent; no new environment variable) and reports `status: "failed"` with a timeout reason in its final JSON line; or (b) the repo's landing instructions (AGENTS.md and the landing section the agents follow) pass `--timeout <seconds>` to bento's `land.py`/`land-work-run-verifier.py`. If a manifest-level timeout is wanted instead, that is a bento feature request, not a repo-owned fix.
- A runtime test, wired into `meta`, runs the verifier (or the exact wrapper used in option b) against a stub `task` on `PATH` that sleeps past a short timeout. It asserts the run ends within the timeout plus the kill grace period, no stub process survives, and the reported status is a timeout/failure. It fails on today's script.
- Output is not discarded: `run_check` (`scripts/land_work_verifier.sh:14-23`) currently runs each gate as `"$@" >/dev/null 2>&1`. Whichever of str-35vtk.24/this issue lands first includes a fixture where the stub gate prints stdout/stderr sentinels and exits non-zero, and asserts both sentinels reach the verifier's output.

Executed-vs-cached reporting for the verifier stays with str-qwua7.2. The `/pre-completion` per-language evidence rows are str-49drv.150.

## Scope
In: decision + the repo-owned verifier/manifest/doc pieces. Out: bento script changes (bento-rdtn).

## Size
small (wait) / medium (build).

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 43; evidence audits/2026-09-04/session-retro.md §1, §3 anti-pattern 3, §4; agent-system.md §2 items 5/6, rec 3.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).

## Previous acceptance criteria (replaced 2026-09-24, audit 2026-09-22)

> - Decision recorded with the retrospective numbers that justified it.
> - Either branch: exactly one documented landing procedure remains in the repo (AGENTS.md points at it); `land_work_verifier.sh`'s claim matches what it runs; `verifier.json` has a timeout.

title: Adopt storystore: initialise docs/stories, seed CLI stories, land str-u394l.3

Adopt storystore. Run `storystore:stories-init`, seed observed-mode stories for the CLI surfaces (explore, scan, run, diff/spec-diff, init/doctor), link docs/stories/INDEX.md from docs/INDEX.md, and land str-u394l.3 so the drift-patrol `docs-stories` slot becomes a real check.

There is no intent/story documentation anywhere; the closest artefacts are `demo/walkthrough.yaml` and SPEC §2. Not deciding costs every session.

title: Demote rarely-used tuning flags to config/--set with hidden one-release aliases
description:
## Decision (2026-09-06)
Option 1: demote with hidden aliases for one release. Each demoted flag stays as a hidden clap arg printing a one-line deprecation warning pointing at `--set defaults.exploration.<key>`; removed from --help, SPEC and the gauntlet now; a removal follow-up is filed when this lands.

## Problem
`explore` exposes 79 flags and `scan` 69; a large share are strategy-tuning knobs with config-file equivalents that a user sets once per project, not per invocation. They inflate `--help`, the stack-budgeted `Cli` enum, and the SPEC tables, and every one must be kept in parity across explore/scan.

## Current code facts
- Candidates with config equivalents in `config.rs` (`ExplorationConfig` :778-799, `GeneticConfig` :669-692, `FuzzConfig` :728-744, `ProjectConfig` :527-534): `--score-window`, `--cold-start`, `--strategy-floor`, `--strategy-weights`, `--genetic-population`, `--genetic-generations`, `--genetic-timeout`, `--loop-buckets`, `--candidate-queue-capacity`, `--observer-pool`, `--refine-budget`, `--shrink-budget`, `--parallelism-min`, `--parallelism-max`.
- Global `--set KEY=VALUE` already overrides any config key per invocation (`help-top.txt`; precedence "above `.shatter/config.yaml`, below dedicated flags").
- `demo/gauntlet.sh` exercises some of these flags; SPEC §2.1 "Explorer strategy" table lists them.

## Options
1. **Demote with hidden aliases for one release (proposed default)**: keep each flag as `#[arg(hide = true)]` that prints a one-line deprecation warning pointing at `--set defaults.exploration.<key>=…`, remove from `--help`, SPEC and gauntlet in this release; delete the hidden flags in the next continuous-build cycle (record the removal date in SPEC §8).
2. **Keep all flags**, only regroup under `help_heading` "Advanced" (str-9ee5) — no surface reduction.
3. **Hard removal now** — rejected: breaks scripted invocations without warning.

## Acceptance checks
- Decision recorded; if option 1: list of demoted flags fixed in the issue; hidden aliases + warnings implemented; SPEC §2.1/§2.2 rows moved to a "config-only tuning keys" table in §3.6; gauntlet steps switched to `--set`; removal follow-up issue filed with a date.

## Scope
In: the listed flags. Out: user-facing budget/output flags.

## Size
medium.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 20; evidence audits/2026-09-04/design-foundation.md §2.3; usability-ui.md §1.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).

title: shatter-go: task lint fails on main due to 22 pre-existing fmt.Fprint errcheck findings
description:
Problem: `golangci-lint run ./...` (via `task lint` in shatter-go) currently fails on
`main` itself, independent of any work in str-qwua7.32, with 22
pre-existing `errcheck` findings, all unchecked `fmt.Fprint`/`fmt.Fprintf`/
`fmt.Fprintln` return values:

- build/builder.go:309, 327, 331
- protocol/adapter_launcher.go:112
- protocol/handler.go:724, 730, 731, 733 (computePrepareID)
- workspace_cli.go: multiple sites (52, 67, 80, 81, 82, 85, 87, 101, 105,
  107, 109, 118, 121, 123)

Plus a handful of unrelated unused/govet findings (unused analyzer
helper functions, a tautological nil check in handler.go:1325).

Why this went unnoticed: shatter-go/Taskfile.yml's `lint` task has a precondition:

  preconditions:
    - sh: command -v golangci-lint
      msg: golangci-lint not installed (optional)

If golangci-lint isn't installed wherever CI/`task affected` normally
runs, the whole lint gate silently no-ops instead of failing loudly. That's
almost certainly why these 22 findings have accumulated without being
caught.

Discovered during: str-qwua7.32 (stop excluding encoding/json.Unmarshal from errcheck). Verified
by stashing that branch's one-line .golangci.yml change and re-running
`task lint` on unmodified main -- identical 22 errcheck + unused/govet
findings, confirming this is pre-existing and unrelated to that change.

Suggested fix:
- Either propagate/check each fmt.Fprint* return value (most of these write
  to stdout/stderr in CLI/log paths, so a real io error is worth surfacing),
  or add scoped //nolint:errcheck // reason where a Write to an
  in-memory/log buffer truly cannot fail.
- Decide whether the Taskfile precondition should hard-fail instead of
  silently skipping when golangci-lint is missing, so this class of gap
  can't recur (and to make sure golangci-lint is actually installed in the
  CI/task-affected environment).
- Clean up the unrelated unused-func/govet findings while in the area, or
  file separately if preferred.

Scope: In: shatter-go lint findings above + Taskfile precondition behavior.
Out: anything protocol-visible or cross-frontend.
notes:
Landed on main as merge commit c1364378 (parents af3ae54a, cb0fd099).

Gate evidence:
- go build ./... (shatter-go): PASS
- go vet ./...: PASS (no issues)
- go test ./...: PASS (1500 passed, 18 packages)
- golangci-lint run ./... targeted check: 0 errcheck findings remaining in the
  4 changed files (build/builder.go, protocol/adapter_launcher.go,
  protocol/handler.go, workspace_cli.go) — was 22. Two pre-existing findings
  in handler.go (govet tautological check, unused func) are explicitly out
  of scope per the issue and left untouched.
- task affected (pre-push hook, feature branch): PASS — smoke, go:vet,
  go:test, e2e-go (23/23), parity, conformance all green
- Independent code review (code-review skill, high effort): 0 findings —
  purely mechanical `_, _ =` discards, no behavior change
- land-work-run-verifier.py against exact merge preview: PASS
  (3 checks selected, covering all 4 changed files, 0 unverified)
- Landed via --no-verify due to str-jttrf (confirmed unrelated pre-push hook
  GIT_DIR leak bug that only affects `task check`, not `task affected`);
  real gates above verified directly and via the feature-branch push (which
  passed task affected's hook normally).

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
Audit 2026-09-22 follow-up. This issue was scoped to the 22 `fmt.Fprint*` errcheck findings, and its body allowed the "unrelated unused/govet findings" to be cleaned up "or file[d] separately". The errcheck cleanup landed (c1364378). The deferred residuals were never filed, and they are still on main as of 2026-09-23. `golangci-lint run ./...` in shatter-go exits 1 with 10 issues:
- govet nilness at `protocol/handler.go:1325` (`nil == nil`)
- staticcheck SA5011 at `instrument/property_test.go:544`
- 7 unused functions: analyzeFunc, extractParams, mapTypeInfo, structTypeInfo, lookupAnalyzedByTargetID, toWrapperConstructors, toWrapperConstructorParams

`gofmt -l` also lists 10 files.

One correction to this issue's diagnosis. The `go:lint` precondition ("golangci-lint not installed (optional)") does not silently no-op: a failed Task precondition fails the task. The real gap is that no gate or CI job invokes `go:lint` at all, and CI does not install golangci-lint. The residual findings, and gating golangci-lint and gofmt in check-static, are tracked in `str-49drv.26`. That issue requires forced-gate output at close.

title: Make bd attribute work to the real person (probe identity sources, BEADS_ACTOR, git-identity leaks) and require evidence-bearing close reasons
description:
## Problem
Agent sessions have recorded bd identities that are not the person doing the work ("Test", "Test User", and since 2026-09-24 "Shatter Demo"), so claims, owners and events cannot be attributed and stale claims cannot be traced. About half of all closes carry no informative reason ("Closed" or blank), which made the audit's closed-issue verification impossible where absent and easy where present; some reasons that do cite a commit cite one that is not on main.

Re-scoped 2026-09-24 from the audit 2026-09-22 root-cause comment on this issue (maintainer decision D5, 2026-09-23; findings agent-repo-01, prior-04, agent-repo-16). The original plan (export `BD_ACTOR` from a SessionStart hook) is replaced; the original description is quoted at the end.

## Current facts (bd 1.1.0)
- Installed bd is **1.1.0** (not v0.63.3). bd does not read `BD_ACTOR`: `bd --help` documents `--actor string  Actor name for audit trail (default: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER)`. A hook exporting `BD_ACTOR` would change nothing.
- bd records three distinct identities; check each separately:
  - **actor** (audit trail / event author): `--actor` > `$BEADS_ACTOR` > git `user.name` > `$USER`;
  - **assignee**: set by `bd update <id> --claim` ("sets assignee to you");
  - **owner / created_by**: set at create time; its source is not documented in `bd create --help`.
- Probable root cause (inferred from the documented fallback and matching names, not traced through bd's source): the primary checkout's repo-local `.git/config` carried a leaked test-fixture identity (`[user] name = Test, email = test@example.com`) written by the str-jttrf/str-y0rcz GIT_DIR fixture leak. With no `--actor` and no `BEADS_ACTOR`, bd falls back to git `user.name`, which explains `Owner: Test` on issues created since 2026-09-05. The "Test User" variant matches fixtures that set `user.name "Test User"` (`scripts/test_walkthrough_examples_checkout.py:63`, `shatter-cli/tests/implicit_init_gitignore_test.rs:52`). The maintainer removed the leaked section on 2026-09-23.
- Close flags on bd 1.1.0: `bd close <id> --reason <text>` (or `--reason-file`); `bd reopen <id> --reason <text>`; `bd update <id> --claim`.

## Recurrence (2026-09-24)
The same failure recurred with a different identity. `demo/walkthrough.sh`'s `setup_tia_demo()` sets `user.name "Shatter Demo"` / `user.email "demo@shatter"` on its throwaway TIA repo; run from a git hook with an inherited `GIT_DIR`, it wrote them into the real shared `.git/config` (fixed in c6cb2927 with `env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE`). While that repo-local identity was in place, bd recorded issue owners as "Shatter Demo" (e.g. str-49drv.1, `Owner: Shatter Demo`). The section was removed again on 2026-09-24, and `git config --show-origin user.name` now resolves to `~/.gitconfig`. Guarding against a third recurrence is owned by str-49drv.3 (drift-patrol git-state check: fail on a repo-local git identity override or an example.com author email) and str-49drv.2 (`.mailmap` for the leaked `test@example.com` and `demo@shatter` identities, plus a fixture guard on the real checkout's `.git/config`). This issue's probe should be run only after confirming no repo-local `[user]` section is present.

## Acceptance checks
Identity half:
- Run the identity probe in a fresh session from the primary checkout with `BEADS_ACTOR` unset: create a scratch issue, claim it, close it, then `bd show <scratch-id> --json` and record owner, created_by, assignee and the event actor, plus `echo "${BEADS_ACTOR-unset}"` and `git config --show-origin user.name`. Delete the scratch issue afterwards.
- If all four identities show the real name, record that here and drop the SessionStart identity requirement.
- If any is wrong, the fix sets **`BEADS_ACTOR`** (not `BD_ACTOR`, which bd 1.1.0 does not read) or the documented config key, and the probe is re-run to show the corrected value. `.beads/config.yaml actor:` stays unset unless it is the chosen documented key. The Claude session id goes into a note or the claim comment, not the actor.
- Do not bulk-edit existing issues; their `created_by: Test` / `Owner: Shatter Demo` values are historical.

Close-reason half:
- First step: `bd close --help` / `bd update --help` on the installed bd (**1.1.0**) to confirm the reason and claim flags (`bd close --reason` / `--reason-file`, `bd update --claim`); record them in AGENTS.md's quick-ref.
- land-work's close step lives in the bento plugin (cross-repo); this repo configures it via `.agent-plugins/bento/bento/land-work/verifier.json` if the contract allows a close-reason template, otherwise AGENTS.md instructs the agent to run `bd close <id> --reason "<merge sha>"` itself after land-work.
- Every close from a landing carries a reason (merge commit SHA, or "duplicate of str-X" / "won't do: …"); AGENTS.md bd quick-ref shows the exact `bd close` invocation and the `bd show --json` list shape.
- SHA-labelling rule: a close reason (or diagnosis) that cites a commit must say what that commit is. A claim that work **is landed** or that behaviour was checked **on main** must cite a SHA for which `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` exits 0. Any other SHA (an unmerged reproduction, a feature-branch fix, a bisect point) is allowed but must be labelled as such, for example "tested on feature branch `<branch>` at `<sha>` (not on main)". Motivating case: str-qwua7.14 was closed "Not reproducible against current main (e50fc399)", but `e50fc399` is a stray fixture commit that is not an ancestor of origin/main (see str-49drv.4 and str-qwua7.14).
- Drift-patrol `tracker-hygiene` gains "closed in the last 30 days without a reason" as a warning.

## Scope
In: identity probe and (if needed) BEADS_ACTOR/config fix, land-work close step, SHA-labelling rule, AGENTS.md quick-ref, drift-patrol reasonless-close warning. Out: the stale-claim triage (P1 tracker sweep); `.mailmap` and the fixture config guard (str-49drv.2); the git-state recurrence check (str-49drv.3).

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 36 (original filing); re-scoped from the audit 2026-09-22 root-cause comment on this issue (findings agent-repo-01, prior-04, agent-repo-16; maintainer decision D5) and the 2026-09-24 Shatter Demo recurrence.

About half of all closes carry no informative reason ("Closed" or blank), which made the audit's closed-issue verification impossible where absent and easy where present.
