SessionStart hooks (`~/.claude/settings.json`): tmux-state, `ensure-dolt.sh`, tmc agent-track, bento `seed-agent-plugins`, `ensure-worktree-permissions`, `register-require-worktree-hook`, `agent-env-doctor`, superpowers, session-id — none sets identity.
> - Close reasons over 1538 closed issues: "Closed" 670, blank 90, "all steps complete" 29, "Duplicate created by racing audit filing" 23, "Completed under str-hy9b expedition" 22.
> - `bento:land-work` closes the issue; `.agent-plugins/bento/bento/land-work/verifier.json` exists; no `--reason` is passed.
> - Retrospective: 8 `bd` unknown-flag errors (`--search`, `--reason`, `--issue-type`, `--note`, `--comment`, `--deps`) — the reason flag agents reach for may not be the real one; verify with `bd close --help` for v0.63.3.
>
> ## Acceptance checks
> - First step: `bd close --help` / `bd update --help` on v0.63.3 to confirm the reason and claim flags; record them in AGENTS.md's quick-ref.
> - Identity source: **`BD_ACTOR` exported by a project SessionStart hook** in `.claude/settings.json`, set to `git config user.name` (person semantics preserved for "assignee"); the Claude session id goes into a `bd update --note` (or the claim comment), not the actor. `.beads/config.yaml actor:` stays unset so the hook is the single source. A new `bd update --claim` in a fresh session shows that assignee, not "Test User".
> - land-work's close step lives in the bento plugin (cross-repo); this repo configures it via `.agent-plugins/bento/bento/land-work/verifier.json` if the contract allows a close-reason template, otherwise AGENTS.md instructs the agent to run `bd close <id> --reason "<merge sha>"` itself after land-work.
> - Every close from a landing carries a reason (merge commit SHA, or "duplicate of str-X" / "won't do: …"); AGENTS.md bd quick-ref shows the exact `bd close` invocation and the `bd show --json` list shape.
> - Drift-patrol `tracker-hygiene` gains "closed in the last 30 days without a reason" as a warning.
>
> ## Scope
> In: hook config, land-work close step, AGENTS.md quick-ref. Out: the stale-claim triage (P1 tracker sweep).
>
> ## Size
> small.
>
> ## Provenance

`<branch>` at `<sha>` (not on main)". Motivating case: str-qwua7.14 was

title: scan_orchestrator: replace rx.recv().expect and try_send().expect with errors on reachable paths
description:
## Problem
The worker-pool intake in `scan_orchestrator.rs` panics when the frontend-worker channel is closed or full. `mpsc::Receiver::recv()` returns `None` when every sender has dropped — which happens when all workers fail to spawn — so a spawn failure panics the whole scan instead of producing a `ScanError`, losing partial results and the checkpoint.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs:2270` `rx.recv().await.expect("pool should not be empty")`.
- `:2244`, `:2254` `.try_send(...).expect("channel has capacity for …")` — capacity assumption tied to pool sizing; panics if `--observer-pool`/`--candidate-queue-capacity` drift.
- `ScanError` enum exists at `scan_orchestrator.rs:388` (`thiserror`).
- Sites verified safe and out of scope: `scan_orchestrator.rs:3646,3653` (after `len()==1`/non-empty), `batch_scheduler.rs:333` (state-machine invariant).

## Acceptance checks
- `:2270` returns `Err(ScanError::WorkerPoolClosed)` (or similar) when `recv()` yields `None`.
- `:2244/:2254`: keep `try_send` (the intake loop must not block the scheduler) and map `TrySendError::Full` to `Err(ScanError::WorkerQueueFull { capacity })` — an error, not a wait — because capacity is derived from `--observer-pool`/`--candidate-queue-capacity` and a full queue indicates a sizing bug, not back-pressure; `TrySendError::Closed` → `WorkerPoolClosed`.
- Regression test: pool where every worker spawn fails → scan returns `Err`, checkpoint and partial report still written, exit 2 at the CLI.

## Scope
In: the three scan_orchestrator sites. Out: `timing.rs` locks (owned by p2-21a), general `unwrap_used` lint rollout (p2-21a), Rust FE locks (p2-35b).

## Size
small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 35; evidence audits/2026-09-04/rust-quality.md §3, rec 7.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- `:2270` returns `Err(ScanError::WorkerPoolClosed)` (or similar) when `recv()` yields `None`.
- `:2244/:2254`: keep `try_send` (the intake loop must not block the scheduler) and map `TrySendError::Full` to `Err(ScanError::WorkerQueueFull { capacity })` — an error, not a wait — because capacity is derived from `--observer-pool`/`--candidate-queue-capacity` and a full queue indicates a sizing bug, not back-pressure; `TrySendError::Closed` → `WorkerPoolClosed`.
- Regression test: pool where every worker spawn fails → scan returns `Err`, checkpoint and partial report still written, exit 2 at the CLI.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
**Audit 2026-09-22 (finding core-10): the premise is refuted, so rescope.**

**The original premise does not hold.** `scan_orchestrator.rs` contains no `try_send`. The pool-construction sites use `sender.send(fe).await.expect(...)` on a channel with capacity `max_workers` (`shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs:2237-2254`), so they cannot fail. `checkout()` (`:2268-2271`, `rx.recv().await.expect("pool should not be empty")`) cannot receive `None`, because `WorkerPool` owns its own sender, and shutdown drops it explicitly.

**The real hazard.** `replace_dead_worker_if_needed` (`:2317-2327`) calls `reap_dead_slot()` when `Frontend::spawn` fails. After each task, the task loop calls `pool.maybe_grow(remaining)` (`:4743`). `maybe_grow` (`:2336-2363`) increments `live_count` before it starts a detached spawn, and decrements it again if that spawn fails. If spawns keep failing (for example a broken frontend install), `live_count` can reach 0 while queued tasks block in `pool.checkout().await` (`:4608`). Once no task is running, nothing calls `maybe_grow` again, and the blocked checkouts wait until `join_with_dynamic_watchdog` (`:5536`) fires. A spawn failure is then reported as a timeout rather than a spawn error. The verifier confirmed the mechanism. It did not confirm that each task is then reported as `phase_timeout('task')`; the first step of this work is to reproduce that and record the actual reported outcome.

**Proposed rescope:**
- Retitle: "Fail fast when the scan worker pool is exhausted".
- Define exhaustion so a successful retry is never rejected: the pool is exhausted only when there are no live workers, **no spawn attempts in flight** (from `maybe_grow` or `replace_dead_worker_if_needed`), and tasks are still waiting. A plain `live_count == 0 && pending > 0` check is not enough: `maybe_grow` counts an in-flight spawn in `live_count` before it succeeds or fails, and a failed replacement can make `live_count` 0 for a moment while another spawn is still about to succeed. Track in-flight spawns explicitly, and keep the last spawn error.
- When exhaustion is detected (at the point where the last in-flight spawn fails), wake every blocked `checkout()` (for example by closing the channel or signalling a `Notify`), and have `checkout()` return `Err(ScanError::WorkerPoolExhausted { last_spawn_error })` instead of panicking or waiting.
- Regression tests, each failing on current `main` and passing after the fix, with output quoted in the close note:
  1. Every spawn after the initial pool fails: the scan returns `WorkerPoolExhausted` containing the spawn error text, within a bound far below the watchdog timeout, and no task timeout is reported.
  2. Transient failure: the first replacement spawn fails and the next succeeds. All tasks complete, and no `WorkerPoolExhausted` is returned.
  3. Checkouts blocked at the moment of exhaustion are woken and receive the error (no task is left waiting).
- Drop the `expect` → `?` conversion of the construction and checkout sites from scope, or keep it only as hygiene. Those sites are not reachable failure points.
- The existing acceptance item "checkpoint and partial report still written, exit 2 at the CLI" still applies to the new error path.

Line numbers verified on the audit branch (code identical to `56c86168`).

title: shatter-rust: poison-tolerant cache locks and module docs
description:
## Problem
The Rust frontend is a long-lived stdio process. Its harness/analysis caches are behind `Mutex`es locked with `.lock().unwrap()`; a single panic while a lock is held (e.g. in one execute request) poisons it and every later request panics, killing the session for the whole scan. Six modules also lack `//!` docs, which the rust-conventions skill requires.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-rust/src/handler.rs:197,215,233,258,274,290,310,317,326` — nine `self.*cache.lock().unwrap()`.
- `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs:5702,5899,5954,6077,6350,6478,7417,7481,7538,7599` — ten more of the same pattern.
- Other non-test unwraps worth a glance: `executor.rs:4480 dir.parent().unwrap()`, `:7017 kept.into_iter().next().unwrap()`, `:7198 public_module_path.unwrap()`, `:5760`, `:5877`; `expect(...)` in `generators.rs` ×5, `instrument.rs` ×3, `file_handle_generator.rs` ×2, `timing.rs`, `wasm_generator.rs`, `executor.rs:326/612/613/6750/6852/6868`.
- Missing `//!` module docs: `generators.rs`, `handler.rs`, `lib.rs`, `main.rs`, `timing.rs`, `wasm_generator.rs`. Clippy `-D warnings` enforced via `shatter-rust/Taskfile.yml:36`; no `missing_docs`.
- PARITY.md rows note Rust default exec timeout 5 s (`handler.rs:40`).

## Acceptance checks
- **Required**: all 19 cache lock sites go through one helper `fn lock_cache<T>(m: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<T>`. On poison the helper recovers the guard (`PoisonError::into_inner`) **and clears the cache map** (`guard.clear()`) before returning it, logging a warning — a poisoned cache may hold a half-inserted entry, so recover-and-invalidate is the safe policy; the next request rebuilds the harness. Test: a request that panics while holding the lock, followed by a normal request on the same handler, succeeds and observes an empty cache.
- **Required**: the five `executor.rs` `Option::unwrap`s (:4480, :7017, :7198, :5760, :5877) converted to `?`/`ok_or` or given a one-line invariant comment.
- **Optional ride-along** (split out if the PR grows): the `expect(...)` sweep in `generators.rs`, `instrument.rs`, `file_handle_generator.rs`, `timing.rs`, `wasm_generator.rs`.
- Docs hygiene (may be a separate small PR): `//!` docs added to the six modules; `#![warn(missing_docs)]` enabled in `shatter-rust/src/lib.rs` if the remaining count is small.

## Scope
In: shatter-rust. Out: harness template strings (emitted code, not executed in-process).

## Size
small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 35; evidence audits/2026-09-04/frontends-protocol.md A4, rec 11.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- **Required**: all 19 cache lock sites go through one helper `fn lock_cache<T>(m: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<T>`. On poison the helper recovers the guard (`PoisonError::into_inner`) **and clears the cache map** (`guard.clear()`) before returning it, logging a warning — a poisoned cache may hold a half-inserted entry, so recover-and-invalidate is the safe policy; the next request rebuilds the harness. Test: a request that panics while holding the lock, followed by a normal request on the same handler, succeeds and observes an empty cache.
- **Required**: the five `executor.rs` `Option::unwrap`s (:4480, :7017, :7198, :5760, :5877) converted to `?`/`ok_or` or given a one-line invariant comment.
- **Optional ride-along** (split out if the PR grows): the `expect(...)` sweep in `generators.rs`, `instrument.rs`, `file_handle_generator.rs`, `timing.rs`, `wasm_generator.rs`.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
**Audit 2026-09-22 note** (finding frontend-rust-05). This re-scopes the lock half of this issue.

**Current code (re-verified at main 16794cef):**
- `shatter-rust/src/handler.rs:480` (`Handler::run`) and `:529` (`dispatch`) have no `catch_unwind`, and neither does `shatter-rust/src/main.rs`. The only `catch_unwind` calls are in generated harness code and the generators' native invoke path. A panic while handling a request therefore ends the frontend process (main exits non-zero). No later request in production ever sees a poisoned lock.
- The cache Mutexes (`executor.rs:406` `CrateHarnessCache`, `:526` `CrateBridgeHarnessCache`, `:733` `HarnessCache`) are only accessed from the dispatch thread. The threads spawned at `executor.rs` ~3055, ~3206, ~5475 only forward child stdout and never touch the caches.

**Correction to the acceptance test as written.** A unit test *can* exercise poison recovery by wrapping a handler call in `catch_unwind` itself and then reusing the handler, so the test is not impossible. But it would pass without fixing anything real, because production cannot survive a panic without a handler-level boundary.

**Proposed re-scope (replaces the poison-tolerant-lock acceptance item):**
- **Required:** a panic boundary. Wrap `dispatch` in `std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))`, turn a caught panic into an `internal_error` response naming the panic message, and invalidate (clear) every harness cache the panicking request could have touched. Without this boundary the process dies on the first panic and nothing else in this issue matters.
- **Then, either** keep the Mutexes and route all 19 lock sites through the `lock_cache` recover-and-clear helper this issue already specifies, **or** replace the Mutexes with owned `HashMap`s on the handler (access is single-threaded). The owned-map option removes poisoning but does not by itself keep the process alive, so it is only acceptable together with the panic boundary above; its cache invalidation happens in the boundary's catch arm.
- Acceptance: an integration test that spawns **one** frontend process and, over the stdio protocol, sends a request that forces a panic inside dispatch (e.g. a test-only hook or a malformed input known to hit an `expect`), then a normal execute request. The first gets `internal_error` with the panic message, the second succeeds, and the process is still alive afterwards. Show it failing on main (process exits, second request gets no response) and passing on the branch; paste both into the close note.
- Keep the module-docs half of this issue and the Option::unwrap cleanup unchanged.

title: Install markdownlint-cli2 and lychee in CI (fail on missing under CI=1); decide on vale
description:
## Problem
`task docs` runs markdownlint-cli2, vale and lychee only if installed and prints `[skip]` otherwise. CI never installs them, so the doc lint gate has passed vacuously since it was written. Vale is configured with spelling only, so even locally it adds little.

title: Property tests for untested core modules: frontend.rs, mutation modules, invariants.rs, behavior.rs, call_graph.rs, parsers
description:
## Problem
`shatter-core/CLAUDE.md` says every non-trivial public function should have proptest coverage, prioritising trust boundaries and mutation contracts. 43 of 97 core modules have no `proptest!` block, including the subprocess protocol boundary (`frontend.rs`), both mutation modules, and the invariant inferencer — the exact modules the policy singles out.

## Current code facts

title: Move e2e_llm_oracle.rs out of shatter-core and drop the core→shatter-llm dev-dependency cycle
description:
## Problem
`shatter-core` dev-depends on `shatter-llm`, which depends on `shatter-core`, solely to host one E2E test. Cargo permits the dev-cycle, but it forces `shatter-llm` (and `reqwest`) to build before core's tests run and couples the oracle plugin to the engine's test graph.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-core/Cargo.toml:44` `shatter-llm` under `[dev-dependencies]`, used only by `shatter-core/tests/e2e_llm_oracle.rs`; `shatter-llm/Cargo.toml:9` depends on `shatter-core`.
- `anyhow = "1"` in core is used only by `oracle.rs` (7 uses); every other core error type is `thiserror`.
- CI covers `shatter-llm` with standalone clippy/test steps (`ci.yml`, str-35vtk.21); str-35vtk.36 (open) plans to fold them into `task check`.

- `oracle.rs` migrated to a `thiserror` `OracleError`; `anyhow` removed from `shatter-core/Cargo.toml`.
- `task check` green; coordinate with str-35vtk.36 so the moved test runs in the tier that now covers shatter-llm.

## Scope
In: one test move, two dependency removals. Out: shatter-llm functionality.

## Size
small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 30; evidence audits/2026-09-04/rust-quality.md §5, §7, rec 9; design-foundation.md §2.1.

title: `shatter doctor`: report whether shatter-rust is resolvable, from where, and its version/protocol match
description:
## Problem
A source build or a partial install leaves the Rust frontend unresolvable; today the user learns this only when a scan skips `.rs` files (600-char warning printed twice) or `run` aborts. `doctor` already reports embedded-frontend staleness and config presence but says nothing about the one frontend that is not embedded.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/doctor.rs`: reports embedded TS/Go hashes and staleness (str-o09e), un-ignored generated paths (str-1fwt), and the two config files' presence/precedence (:254-287, str-mktn). No Rust-frontend section.
- Resolution logic lives in `shatter-cli/src/helpers.rs` (`shatter-rust/target/{release,debug}/shatter-rust` relative to cwd, then PATH; `check_frontend_availability` @~497-584).

Audit 2026-09-22 (cli-ux-10) adds one check to this issue's Rust section. A resolvable `shatter-rust` is not enough: an installed or copied binary fails every Rust execution with `cannot locate shatter-rust-runtime crate; set SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH`, because `find_runtime_crate_path()` (`shatter-rust/src/executor.rs:1198-1223`) only honours `SHATTER_RUNTIME_PATH` or a `shatter-rust-runtime/` sibling within five ancestors of the `shatter-rust` executable. title: shatter-go: unify analyzer and instrument SymExpr builders over one shared type
description:
## Problem
The Go frontend builds symbolic expressions in two packages over two struct types: `protocol/analyzer.go` (static `branches[].condition`) and `instrument/symextract.go` (runtime `path_constraints`), the latter over a private `symExpr` "defined locally to avoid import cycles". They disagree on literals, identifiers, selector chains, call names, and wire shape, so the constraint the solver sees at runtime is not the one analyze reported for the same source.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go:2171 buildSymExpr`, `:2201 buildSymExprWithFlow`; `shatter-go/instrument/symextract.go:40 exprToSymExpr`, `:48 exprToSymExprWithFlow` over `symExpr` (:13).
- `true`/`false`/`nil` → consts in instrument (symextract.go:294-302), `unknown` in analyzer `identSymExpr` (analyzer.go:2297-2310).
- String literals: analyzer `strings.Trim(lit.Value, "`\"'")` (analyzer.go:2336-2347; wrong for escapes) vs `strconv.Unquote` (symextract.go:372).
- Selector chains: analyzer flattens nested `a.b.c` (`flattenSelector`, analyzer.go:2310); instrument handles one level (symextract.go:338-346).
- Call names: analyzer emits `exprString(call.Fun)` for any selector (analyzer.go:2359-2388); instrument returns `unknown` unless base is an ident (symextract.go:393-400).
- `buildBinOp` (analyzer.go:2263) does not guard `tokenToOp == ""`; instrument does (symextract.go:310). `buildSymExprWithFlow`'s `default:` (analyzer.go:2258-2262) sends `SelectorExpr` to the flow-less builder.
- Wire: `protocol.SymExpr.Path` no `omitempty` (types.go:510) → `"path":null` everywhere; `Args` required (types.go:518) vs `omitempty` in instrument (symextract.go:24). The `"args":null` regression test (analyzer_test.go:1983-2000, property_test.go:1309) covers only the analyzer.

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by p2-25d** (SymExpr construction spec): literal normalization, `unknown` collapse, and call form are decided there; this issue implements them for Go.
- Output changes require regenerating `protocol/conformance` golden fixtures for Go and re-running `task parity`/`task conformance`; list the regenerated files in the PR.

## Acceptance checks
- `SymExpr`/`SymConstraint` live in a leaf package imported by both `protocol` and `instrument`; `instrument.symExpr` deleted.
- One builder (flow-aware, with a resolver hook) used by both; a rapid property test asserts analyzer condition == instrument constraint for generated `if` expressions.
- Literal/identifier/selector/call behavior reconciled per the SymExpr construction spec (p2-25d); `omitempty` consistent; `task go:test` and `e2e_concolic_go` green; `task parity`/`conformance` green.

## Scope
In: shatter-go builders and types. Out: TS (str-rf2v), Rust (p2-25c), cross-frontend spec (p2-25d).

## Size
medium.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 25; evidence audits/2026-09-04/frontends-protocol.md A5 (Go), rec 6.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).

- One builder (flow-aware, with a resolver hook) used by both; a rapid property test asserts analyzer condition == instrument constraint for generated `if` expressions.
- Literal/identifier/selector/call behavior reconciled per the SymExpr construction spec (p2-25d); `omitempty` consistent; `task go:test` and `e2e_concolic_go` green; `task parity`/`conformance` green.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
**Audit 2026-09-22 note (finding frontend-go-04).** Re-verified at commit 56c86168. The scope of this issue is larger than two builders:

**There are four Go SymExpr builders**
1. `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go:2171` `buildSymExpr` (static).
2. `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go:2201` `buildSymExprWithFlow` (static, flow-aware), with its own `analyzerFlowMap` (`analyzer.go:1963`) and walker; re-implemented in `protocol/` by commit 34eb92c8.
3. `shatter-go/instrument/symextract.go` `exprToSymExpr(WithFlow)` over a private `symExpr` (runtime).
4. `shatter-go/protocol/loop_body_states.go:294` `buildGoLoopSnapshotSymExpr`. It resolves params before flow (the analyzer does the reverse), handles only Ident/BasicLit/Binary/unary `-`/Paren, and keeps stale flow values after unsupported compound assignments such as `%=` or `<<=` (`visitGoLoopSnapshotAssign`, loop_body_states.go:227). Whether the ordering difference changes results is unverified.

**The runtime builder never uses flow.** Instrument always calls `extractConstraint` with no flow map: `instrument/visitor.go:334, 350, 440` and `instrument/mcdc.go:81, 93`. `deadcode ./...` in shatter-go reports every function in `instrument/flow.go` (`snapshot`, `mergeFlowMaps`, `symExprsEqual`) and `instrument/flowwalk.go` (`walkStmtsForFlow`, `applyStmtToFlow`, `applyAssignToFlow`, `applyDeclToFlow`, `applyIfToFlow`, `flowLHSName`) as unreachable. Consequence: analyze reports `ite` conditions for flow-tracked locals while the runtime `branch_path` constraint for the same branch is `unknown`, so the solver cannot negate it.

**Docs are wrong.** `shatter-go/CLAUDE.md:57-58` ("Ite SymExpr Parity Contract") lists `instrument/flow.go` and `instrument/flowwalk.go` as steps 1-2 of the ite mechanism.

**Proposed additions to this issue's acceptance criteria**
- Delete `instrument/flow.go` and `instrument/flowwalk.go`; keep one flow-aware builder with a param-resolver hook in a leaf package (e.g. `shatter-go/symexpr`) used by the analyzer, instrument and loop snapshots.
- Thread the flow map into instrument's `transformIfStmt` so runtime constraints for flow-tracked locals match the static ones.
- rapid property: for generated if-chains over params and flow-tracked locals, the static branch condition equals the runtime constraint.
- Fix the CLAUDE.md ite section.

The rune/escape literal bug (CHAR typed as `str`, analyzer `strings.Trim`) is filed separately as a small fix ahead of this refactor: **str-49drv.102**. The dead-code sweep (**str-49drv.104**) leaves `instrument/flow*.go` to this issue.

title: shatter-rust: build runtime constraints as typed protocol::SymExpr instead of hand-formatted JSON
description:
## Problem
The Rust analyzer produces a full typed `SymExpr` for static branch conditions, but the instrumentor hand-formats JSON strings for runtime `path_constraints` and supports only comparison/logical operators. Arithmetic, bitwise, method/function calls and `let` patterns become `unknown` at runtime even though analyze promised a solvable expression (e.g. `x + 1 > 5`), so the concolic loop cannot negate them. The hand-rolled encoder is also a second place to get escaping/shape wrong.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-rust/src/analyzer.rs:1954 build_sym_expr` → `protocol::SymExpr` (serde); handles Path, Field (root-first chains; bug history at :1968-1974), Binary via `convert_bin_op` (:2261+, incl. arithmetic/bitwise/compound-assign), Unary, Lit, MethodCall with receiver, Call, Paren, Reference, `Let`.
- `shatter-rust/src/instrument.rs:519 constraint_for_expr` hand-formats JSON with `escape_json_string` (:704); handles only `Eq/Ne/Lt/Le/Gt/Ge/And/Or` (:523-530) and `Not/Neg`; calls (:576, :583), arithmetic, bitwise, `Let` → `{"kind":"unknown","hint":...}`.
- Consequence observed: runtime constraints strictly narrower than the static `branches[].condition` from the same frontend.

## Acceptance checks
- Resolution: `instrument.rs` calls the analyzer's `build_sym_expr` (moved to a shared `sym_expr_builder.rs` module used by both `analyzer.rs` and `instrument.rs`) with the same param-name environment the analyzer uses; the resulting `protocol::SymExpr` is serialized with `serde_json::to_string` so escaping is owned by serde; `escape_json_string` (:704) and the hand-written kind strings (:519-600) are deleted.
- Blocked by p2-25d only for the call-form decision; the mechanical change can proceed with today's analyzer semantics.
- Proptest: for generated `syn::Expr` conditions, the instrumented runtime constraint deserializes to the same `SymExpr` as the analyzer's branch condition.
- `e2e_concolic_rust` gains a case where an arithmetic branch (`x + 1 > 5`) is solved by Z3 via a runtime constraint; `task rust-fe:test` green.

## Scope
In: shatter-rust instrument.rs + shared builder. Out: ITE data-flow production (tracked `ite-symexpr-production-partial`).

## Size
medium.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 25; evidence audits/2026-09-04/frontends-protocol.md A5 (Rust), rec 6.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).

- Blocked by p2-25d only for the call-form decision; the mechanical change can proceed with today's analyzer semantics.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
**Audit 2026-09-22 note** (finding frontend-rust-02). Two concrete repros for this issue's "second place to get escaping/shape wrong" point, plus one gap the current acceptance does not cover.

**Repros (code re-verified at main 16794cef):**
- `shatter-rust/src/instrument.rs:671-702` `constraint_for_lit`: float literals are emitted with `f.base10_digits()` raw (`:682`), so `if x > 1. {}` produces `"value":1.`, which is not valid JSON.
- `instrument.rs:704` `escape_json_string` escapes only `\\`, `"`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, so `if s == "a\u{1}b" {}` embeds a raw U+0001 in the JSON string, which is invalid JSON.
- Audit probe (not re-run): an explore artifact listed the `x > 1.` and `s == "a\u{1}b"` constraints as kind `unknown`, and concolic explore never reached `if s == "a\u{1}b"` in 60 iterations. The analyzer's typed builder emits `1.0` and `"a\u0001b"` correctly for the same source.

**Please add to acceptance:**
- The proptest over generated conditions includes float literals written `1.`, `1e10`, `1.5e-3`, and string literals with arbitrary chars including U+0000-U+001F. It deserializes the emitted string as `protocol::SymExpr` (the instrumentor emits bare `SymExpr`; `shatter-rust-runtime/src/lib.rs:178-186` `branch_hit` wraps it into `SymConstraint::Expr`), not as `SymConstraint`.
- Silent `Unknown`: `branch_hit` (`shatter-rust-runtime/src/lib.rs:178-186`) turns any unparseable constraint into `SymConstraint::Unknown { hint }` with no warning or counter. Make that observable (a counter in the execute result / telemetry, or a warning on stderr that the frontend surfaces), with a unit test that feeds `{"value":1.}` and asserts the counter/warning. If you prefer to keep this issue narrow, say so here and the audit will file it separately.
- E2E: an `e2e_concolic_rust` case that reaches `if s == "a\u{1}b"` via a runtime constraint. Note that plain `cargo test --test e2e_concolic_rust` runs nothing (all cases are `#[ignore]`d); use the `task e2e-rust-governed` command with `-- --include-ignored` and paste the `test result:` line.

title: Write a one-page SymExpr construction spec and record or fix the Go call-shape divergence
description:
## Problem
Seven hand-written builders and six operator tables across three languages implement one vocabulary (`shatter-core/src/sym_expr.rs` `BinOpKind`/`UnOpKind`/`ConstValue`) with no spec for construction semantics. `protocol/schemas/sym-expr.schema.json` covers shape only. One cross-frontend divergence (call name/receiver form) is live and untracked.

## Current code facts
- Undefined by any doc: call `name`/`receiver` form; literal normalization (Go `strings.Trim` vs `strconv.Unquote`); when to collapse to `unknown` (TS `WithFlow` collapses all-unknown children, the other two do not); path direction (root-first — Rust had a bug, `analyzer.rs:1968-1974`); which node kinds are mandatory.
- Go emits method calls as `{kind:"call", name:"recv.Method", receiver:null}` (`analyzer.go:2359-2388`); TS (`instrumentor.ts:1941-1943`) and Rust (`analyzer.rs:2015-2028`) emit `{name:"Method", receiver:<expr>}`. Not in `parity-matrix.yaml` `allowed_divergences` nor conformance `known_drifts`.
- Core `BinOpKind` (`sym_expr.rs:107-110`) has `shl`, `shr`, `bit_clear`; TS `BinOpKind` (`protocol.ts:514-532`) and Rust FE omit them.
- `data/string-ops.yaml` names the 8 solver-supported string ops; nothing lists which call names frontends must emit for them.

## Step 0 (before writing the spec)
- Confirm what core consumes: `shatter-core/src/sym_expr.rs:47` declares `SymExpr::Call { receiver: Option<Box<SymExpr>>, args, name }` and `:138-139` walks `receiver` for param extraction; `shatter-core/src/solver.rs:436 infer_call_sort(name)`, `:534`, `:789` map calls to Z3 string ops by `name` — **confirmed during drafting**: `solver.rs:534-538` matches `SymExpr::Call { name, receiver, args } => convert_string_call(vars, name, receiver.as_deref(), args)`, i.e. the receiver expression is the string subject for the 8 `string-ops.yaml` operations. Go's `name:"recv.Method", receiver:null` form therefore yields no subject and cannot be solved — it is broken for the solver, not merely non-canonical. The spec must fix the canonical form as `name` = bare method name, `receiver` = expression, and p2-25b must change Go's `callSymExpr`/`callExprToSymExpr` (the `allowed_divergences` route is not acceptable for this one).
- **This issue lands before p2-25b and p2-25c**; both cite it.

## Acceptance checks
- `protocol/SYMEXPR.md` (or a section in PROTOCOL.md) defining: node kinds and mandatory set; call form (canonical: `name` = bare method/function name, `receiver` = expr or null); literal normalization rules; `unknown` collapse rule; path direction; op-kind vocabulary per language with the string-op mapping.
- Go changed to the canonical call form **or** an `allowed_divergences` entry + `known_drifts` pattern added — decided in the spec.
- Conformance golden case exercising a method-call condition passes in all three frontends.

## Scope
In: spec doc, one divergence decision, one conformance case. Out: the per-frontend builder refactors (str-rf2v, p2-25b, p2-25c) which should cite this spec.

## Size
small–medium.

Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 25; evidence audits/2026-09-04/frontends-protocol.md A5, A6, rec 6, 7.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
Audit 2026-09-22 correction (finding protocol-parity-14; evidence in `audits/2026-09-22/areas/protocol-parity.md`; re-checked 2026-09-23 at 56c86168):

- Step 0 says Go's `name="recv.Method", receiver=null` call form "cannot be solved" and must become bare name plus receiver. That is wrong for package-qualified free functions:
  - `shatter-core/data/string-ops.yaml:34` declares `{ language: go, method: "strings.HasPrefix", style: free }`.
  - `shatter-core/src/solver.rs:919` has a "Go-style: no receiver, two positional args (e.g. strings.Contains(s, substr))" branch, with tests around :2420.
  - Live Go analyze output for `strings.HasPrefix(s, "go_")` is `{name: "strings.HasPrefix", args: [param s, const]}`, which is solvable today.
- The real divergence is method calls on values. `u.IsAdmin()` emits `{name: "u.IsAdmin", args: []}`, because `callSymExpr` (`shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go:2359`) uses the whole selector as the name and drops the receiver. `collect_param_names` (`shatter-core/src/sym_expr.rs:125`) walks only receiver and args, so it loses param `u`.
- Proposed amended canonical form: package-qualified free functions keep `name="pkg.Fn", receiver=null` (matching string-ops.yaml `style: free`). Method calls on values emit `name=<bare method>, receiver=<expr>`. To tell them apart, the Go side must resolve whether the selector's X is a package identifier (`types.PkgName`) or a value.
- Add a regression test that Go `strings.*` constraints stay solvable after the change, and a test that a value-method call keeps its receiver param in `collect_param_names`.
- Path fix: the file is `shatter-core/data/string-ops.yaml`, not `data/string-ops.yaml`.
- The verifier rated this P3. The issue's acceptance text ("receiver = expr or null") already leaves room for the right answer, but the Step 0 wording would steer an implementer toward breaking free functions, so amend the body.

title: spec-diff: pair classes by behavior when branch paths are renumbered, not by exact BranchPath
description:
## Problem
`spec-diff` matches old and new classes by exact `BranchPath` (`Vec<(branch_id, taken)>`). Adding one branch to a function renumbers every subsequent branch ID, so unchanged behaviors get new paths and are reported as one ADDED plus one REMOVED. One real change reports 3 added / 2 removed and the CI signal is noise. Labels also embed a 1-based index ("Class 3 — …"), so even the human-readable output cannot be correlated across runs.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-core/src/spec_diff.rs:~93-97`: `old_by_path`/`new_by_path` are `HashMap<&BranchPath, &SpecClass>`; matching is `old_by_path.get(&new_class.branch_path)`.
- Captured evidence (`audits/2026-09-04/ui/specdiff.txt`, `v1.spec.json`, `v2.spec.json`): v1 "positive-even" path `[(0,F),(1,F),(2,T)]`; v2 same behavior path `[(0,F),(1,F),(2,F),(4,T)]` after a new branch was inserted → `[ADDED] Class 3 — returns "positive-even"` and `[REMOVED] Class 3 — returns "positive-even"`.
- `SpecClass.label` (`spec.rs:194`) is `"Class {i} — {postcondition}"`; `spec_diff.rs:250-273` prints labels.
- `compare` (cross-language) already ignores branch paths and pairs by input/output — the pairing logic exists.
- Preconditions are stored as externally tagged enums (`{"AllEqual": {"param_index":0,"value":2}}`) and are single-sample tautologies at low iteration counts; symbolic constraints exist in core but are not exported to the spec.

## Acceptance checks
- Matching algorithm: exact path match first; then pair unmatched classes that **agree on behavior**, defined as: same `postcondition.kind` and value (compared with `spec_diff.rs:301`'s nondeterminism-aware postcondition comparison, i.e. fields listed in `nondeterministic_fields` of either spec are ignored) **and** identical canonical example inputs (`examples[0].inputs`); examples whose outputs touch a nondeterministic field are excluded from the agreement test. Only what remains is ADDED/REMOVED. A path change on a paired class is reported as `[PATH]` (informational), not add/remove.
- Class `label` no longer embeds an index (or includes a stable path hash); JSON gains `class_id` = hash of postcondition+canonical example. **Consumers affected**: `spec_diff.rs:250-273` text renderer, `spec.rs` markdown renderer ("## Class N — …" headings), `specify --yaml` output, `stale`/`revalidate` readers of `FileSpecBundle`, `demo/walkthrough.sh` expectations, `shatter-cli/tests` snapshots and any `golden-test` fixtures containing `"label"` — grep and regenerate; bump `FileSpecBundle.version`.
- Test: the v1/v2 fixture pair above yields 1 added, 0 removed.
- Follow-up noted (not required here): export symbolic preconditions (`n > 0 && n % 2 == 0`) alongside the enum form.

## Scope
In: spec_diff matching, label/id stability, tests. Out: precondition symbolic export (note only), terminology (p2-26b).

## Size
medium.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 26; evidence audits/2026-09-04/usability-ui.md §3, rec 11; spec_diff.rs matching verified during drafting.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- Matching algorithm: exact path match first; then pair unmatched classes that **agree on behavior**, defined as: same `postcondition.kind` and value (compared with `spec_diff.rs:301`'s nondeterminism-aware postcondition comparison, i.e. fields listed in `nondeterministic_fields` of either spec are ignored) **and** identical canonical example inputs (`examples[0].inputs`); examples whose outputs touch a nondeterministic field are excluded from the agreement test. Only what remains is ADDED/REMOVED. A path change on a paired class is reported as `[PATH]` (informational), not add/remove.
- Class `label` no longer embeds an index (or includes a stable path hash); JSON gains `class_id` = hash of postcondition+canonical example. **Consumers affected**: `spec_diff.rs:250-273` text renderer, `spec.rs` markdown renderer ("## Class N — …" headings), `specify --yaml` output, `stale`/`revalidate` readers of `FileSpecBundle`, `demo/walkthrough.sh` expectations, `shatter-cli/tests` snapshots and any `golden-test` fixtures containing `"label"` — grep and regenerate; bump `FileSpecBundle.version`.
- Test: the v1/v2 fixture pair above yields 1 added, 0 removed.
- Follow-up noted (not required here): export symbolic preconditions (`n > 0 && n % 2 == 0`) alongside the enum form.
notes: Coordination note (2026-09-21, from str-nfg4y landing): the acceptance criteria's fallback pairing already requires "identical canonical example inputs (examples[0].inputs)" for unmatched-class agreement -- good, this independently matches str-nfg4y's canonical-input-equality principle. When implementing, reuse spec_diff.rs's canonical_examples_comparable() (or its str-gr41w-improved successor once that lands) for this input-equality check rather than a fresh ad hoc comparison, so this fallback path doesn't reintroduce str-nfg4y's original bug (comparing postconditions across unmatched canonical inputs) through a different matching route. Also apply the same nondeterminism-mask-aware equality already used for postcondition comparison consistently to this path's input comparison if inputs themselves can carry nondeterministic fields.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
**Audit 2026-09-22 note (finding artifacts-06): pairing by exact BranchPath also hides real changes.**

This issue describes renumbered branch IDs as noise (unchanged behavior shows up as ADDED + REMOVED). The 2026-09-22 audit found that the same pairing can also pair two different behaviors and hide the real regression.

Weight: under maintainer decision D2 (2026-09-23), the snapshot `shatter diff` command is being retired and `spec-diff` is the only regression tool. A false negative in spec-diff is therefore a false negative in Shatter's whole regression story, which makes this issue more important than when it was filed.

Evidence (files under `audits/2026-09-22/artifact-samples/` on branch `audit-2026-09-22` until the audit reports land):

- v1 `grade`: `n < 0` -> invalid, `n < 50` -> fail, else pass. v2 inserts `n > 100` -> overflow.
- v1 `fail` and v2 `overflow` share `BranchPath [(0,F),(1,T)]`, so they are paired (`sd-v1.json`, `sd-v2.json`).
- `spec-diff` output (`sd-diff.txt`): `Summary: 2 added, 1 removed, 1 precondition(s) changed, 1 class(es) with insufficient comparison evidence`, then `[ADDED] Class 2 — returns "fail"`, `[ADDED] Class 4 — returns "pass"`, `[REMOVED] Class 3 — returns "pass"`, a `[PRECOND]` change and `[INCONCLUSIVE] Class 2`. The word `overflow` never appears, so the real regression (inputs > 100 now return `overflow` instead of `pass`) is not reported. The command still exits non-zero here only because of the unrelated REMOVED class.
- Pairing code today (re-checked 2026-09-23, audit worktree HEAD 793f2b0b, code identical to 56c86168): `shatter-core/src/spec_diff.rs:134-141` builds `old_by_path`/`new_by_path` keyed on `&c.branch_path` and matches with `old_by_path.get(&new_class.branch_path)`; removed classes at `:201`. The `~93-97` line reference in this issue's description is stale.

What spec-diff can and cannot establish from these two files: v1 recorded "pass" only at input 50 and v2 recorded "overflow" only at input 101, and spec-diff does not execute targets. The files alone therefore cannot prove that a specific input moved from "pass" to "overflow". They do prove that v2 has a behavior ("overflow") that no v1 class has, and that the v1 "fail" and v2 "overflow" classes have different postconditions even though their branch paths match.

Proposed additions to this issue's acceptance criteria (pairing only):

- An exact `BranchPath` match must not by itself pair two classes whose postconditions differ (under the existing nondeterminism-aware comparison). Such classes are left unpaired, so the v2 class is reported ADDED and the v1 class REMOVED.
- Known-answer test using `sd-v1.json` / `sd-v2.json` (copy them into the test fixtures): the output contains an `[ADDED]` row for `returns "overflow"`, contains no `[PRECOND]` or `[INCONCLUSIVE]` row that pairs "fail" with "overflow", and the command exits non-zero. It fails on current code (the word `overflow` does not appear); record the failing run.

Not part of this issue: the concrete verdict "inputs > 100 changed from pass to overflow". That needs each class's symbolic input region and a solver check, and is owned by the new audit issue spec-diff-symbolic-region-verdicts (blocked by spec-preconditions-from-path-constraints), which uses the same grade pair as its known-answer test. That issue does not change pairing; whichever of the two lands second rebases and re-runs both sets of tests.

title: Adopt anyhow/CliError in shatter-cli and classify exit codes by downcast, not substring
description:
## Problem
rust-conventions says CLI entrypoints use `anyhow`; shatter-cli uses none. Errors travel as `Result<_, String>` and `main.rs` decides the exit code and the telemetry category by substring-matching the `Display` text. This is why SPEC §2.11's 0/1/2 convention is not implemented for tool errors (missing file, unsupported extension, unknown function, malformed spec, sandbox refusal all exit 1 — see the P1 exit-code item) and why any message wording change can silently change an exit code.

## Current code facts
- `grep -rl anyhow shatter-cli/src` → 0 files; 56 `Result<_, String>` signatures (`commands/explore.rs` 19, `build_frontend.rs` 7, `args.rs` 7, `embedded_*_frontend.rs` 12).
- `shatter-cli/src/main.rs:1335 fn error_exit_code(err: &(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)) -> i32` and `:1381 fn categorize_error(err: &dyn Display)` — `:1383-1395` match on `"no such file"`, `"not found"`, `"permission denied"`, `"timed out"`, `"spawn"`, `"frontend"`, `"config"`+`"parse"`.
- Core already has 30 `thiserror` enums to downcast to (`solver.rs:19 SolverError`, `frontend.rs:38 FrontendError`, `config.rs:60`, `explorer.rs:541`, `orchestrator.rs:730`, `scan_orchestrator.rs:388`).
- Core public API still returns stringly errors in `stratum.rs:63`, `core_sample.rs:182,:211`, `mock_value_space.rs:130`, `fingerprint.rs`, `config.rs` (10 sites) — these would need typed variants to be classifiable.
- Live behavior (usability review): `explore nope.ts:foo` → exit 1; `spec-diff bad.json v1.spec.json` → "failed to parse spec" exit 1; only clap usage errors exit 2.

## Prerequisite
- **p1-10 (implement SPEC §2.11 exit codes) first**: it defines which error classes map to 1 vs 2 and adds the integration tests; this issue replaces its interim substring mapping with typed classification. Do not start this before p1-10 has a merged mapping table.

## Signatures that change
- `shatter_core::stratum::parse_stratum_spec` (caller `shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs:804`), `core_sample::parse_sample_budget` (`scan.rs:847`), `core_sample::parse_batch_spec` (`scan.rs:865`), `mock_value_space.rs:130`, `fingerprint.rs` and the 10 `config.rs` sites — `Result<_, String>` → `Result<_, <Module>Error>` (`thiserror`), each with an `impl From<…> for CliError`.

## Acceptance checks
- A `CliError` enum (or `anyhow::Error` with `.context()` at the boundary) replaces `Result<_, String>` in `shatter-cli/src`; `error_exit_code` maps by `downcast_ref` to typed variants (`Usage`, `InputFile`, `Frontend`, `Timeout`, `Config`, `GateFired`) with no `msg.contains`.
- Exit-code integration tests per class (missing file, bad extension, unknown function, malformed spec JSON, host-write refusal → 2; `diff`/`spec-diff` divergence, `stale` drift, `--fail-on-failures` → 1).
- Stringly core parsers listed above return `thiserror` types; the 41 `writeln!().unwrap()` in `scan.rs`/`run.rs` are replaced by a `push_line` helper while those files are touched.

## Scope
In: shatter-cli error plumbing, exit-code tests, the listed core parser signatures. Out: message wording changes for users.

## Size
medium. Do together with (or immediately after) the P1 "implement SPEC §2.11 exit codes" item — this is its structural prerequisite.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 22; evidence audits/2026-09-04/rust-quality.md §5, rec 6; usability-ui.md §2, rec 2.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- A `CliError` enum (or `anyhow::Error` with `.context()` at the boundary) replaces `Result<_, String>` in `shatter-cli/src`; `error_exit_code` maps by `downcast_ref` to typed variants (`Usage`, `InputFile`, `Frontend`, `Timeout`, `Config`, `GateFired`) with no `msg.contains`.
- Exit-code integration tests per class (missing file, bad extension, unknown function, malformed spec JSON, host-write refusal → 2; `diff`/`spec-diff` divergence, `stale` drift, `--fail-on-failures` → 1).
- Stringly core parsers listed above return `thiserror` types; the 41 `writeln!().unwrap()` in `scan.rs`/`run.rs` are replaced by a `push_line` helper while those files are touched.

title: Purge dangling parity-divergence IDs and the false "does not emit preflight_failed" claims; add a patrol check
description:
## Problem
Source comments, crate CLAUDE.md files, and the conformance `known_drifts` cite divergence IDs that no longer exist in `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml`. The most-cited one carries a factual claim that is now false. The frontend-parity skill tells agents to treat CLAUDE.md prose as the contract, so agents will "preserve" a divergence that has already been resolved.

- `error-code-preflight-failed-typescript-only` — not in the matrix — cited at `shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md:208`, `shatter-go/CLAUDE.md:206`, `shatter-rust/CLAUDE.md:171`, `shatter-go/protocol/constants.go:19`, `shatter-go/protocol/types.go:590`, `shatter-rust/src/protocol.rs:531` and `:563`. Surrounding claim "Go/Rust declare but do not emit `preflight_failed`" is false: Go emits it at `shatter-go/protocol/handler.go:394`, Rust at `shatter-rust/src/handler.rs:650` (`run_preflight`).
- `loop-body-states-typescript-only` — `shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md:52`; not in matrix.
- `rust-side-effects-not-captured` — `shatter-rust/CLAUDE.md:25` ("status: resolved"); entry deleted.
- `protocol/conformance/conformance_cases.yaml:13-25` `known_drifts` first pattern cites `side-effect-thrown-error-placement`; not a matrix ID.
- `scripts/validate-parity.py` validates the matrix internally and vs registry; nothing scans other files for IDs. `scripts/drift-patrol.py` has `check_parity_expiry` (:405) but no reference-resolution check.
- Stale line refs: `shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md:17-18` cites "~278-352" / "~860-951"; builders are at `instrumentor.ts:874` and `:1862`.

## Acceptance checks
- All seven citations above removed or rewritten to the true state; the `preflight_failed` sentences corrected in the three CLAUDE.md files and two Go/Rust source comments.
- New `validate-parity.py` (or drift-patrol) step. **Divergence-ID definition**: a kebab-case token (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,}`) that either (a) appears as an `allowed_divergences[].id` anywhere in `git log -p -- protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` history, or (b) is cited on the same line as the words `divergence`/`allowed_divergences`/`known_drifts` in `*.md`, `*.go`, `*.rs`, `*.ts`, `*.yaml` under the repo (excluding `target/`, `node_modules/`, `.claude/worktrees/`). ## Provenance

title: Document every SHATTER_* environment variable in one table with its precedence, and test for undocumented ones
description:

About 25 `SHATTER_*` variables influence behavior. title: Enable clippy::unwrap_used and missing_docs in shatter-core as the conventions claim
description:
## Problem
The `rust-conventions` skill says `clippy::unwrap_used` is "the default policy for shatter-core: no `unwrap()` in library code" and names `missing_docs`/rustdoc lints as "the enforcement path". Nothing enables either lint, so the policy is enforced by discipline only. Doc coverage happens to be high; the 10 core unwraps are silent violations.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-core/Cargo.toml:46` has only `[lints.rust] unexpected_cfgs = { check-cfg = ['cfg(kani)'] }`; no `[lints.clippy]`; no `clippy.toml`; `#![warn(missing_docs)]` appears only inside a string literal at `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs:10231`.
- Gate is `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` (`Taskfile.yml:178`).
- Non-test `unwrap()` in core: 10 — `timing.rs:203,207,223` (`self.inner.lock().unwrap()`), `config.rs:1155` (`path.last().unwrap()`), `strategy.rs:959` (`candidates.last().unwrap()`), `nondeterminism.rs:351-375` (static `LazyLock<Regex>`, safe), `frontend.rs:203-205` (after `Stdio::piped()`, safe).
- `expect()` in core: 35; `html_templates.rs:213,273,487` `tmpl.render().expect(...)` abort from library code.
- Undocumented pub items: `scan_orchestrator.rs:3805 parallel_scan_with_progress` (1,346-line entry point), `:447 as_str`, `:468 ProgressHandler`, `config.rs:25-27` consts, `solver.rs:1161 solve_for_new_path`.

description:
## Problem

title: Stop excluding encoding/json.Unmarshal from errcheck in shatter-go
description:
## Problem
`shatter-go/.golangci.yml` excludes `encoding/json.Unmarshal` from `errcheck`. Ignoring an Unmarshal error is exactly how a malformed protocol request, config file, or recorder payload decodes to a zero-value struct that then "succeeds". The frontend is a long-lived stdio process consuming untrusted JSON from core, so this is a correctness hole, not style.

## Current code facts
- `shatter-go/.golangci.yml:18-27` `errcheck.exclude-functions` lists `(*os.File).Close`, `os.RemoveAll`, `os.Setenv`, `os.Unsetenv`, `(io.Closer).Close`, **`encoding/json.Unmarshal`**, `go/printer.Fprint`, `(*github.com/extism/go-sdk.Plugin).Close`.
- The other exclusions are best-effort cleanup or documented-infallible; `json.Unmarshal` is the only one that swallows data-validity errors.
- Candidate call sites hidden by the exclusion: protocol request decoding (`shatter-go/protocol/handler.go`), config loading (`shatter-go/config/loader.go`), recorder drain / fixture loader (`shatter-go/internal/fixture/loader.go`). Exact list = `golangci-lint run` output after removing the line.
- `shatter-go-tool` has no lint config (394 lines, low risk).

## Acceptance checks
- The `encoding/json.Unmarshal` line is removed; `task go:lint` passes.
- Every formerly-hidden site either propagates the error — protocol decoding returns an `error` response with `error_category: validation` (`protocol/registry.yaml:69-71` enum `[validation, runtime, infrastructure]`; use the existing `invalid_request`-class error code) and config/fixture loading returns a load error — or has an inline `//nolint:errcheck // reason` where ignoring is provably safe.
- At least one regression test: a malformed `execute` request body (e.g. `inputs` as a string) yields an error response, not a zero-value execution.

## Scope
In: shatter-go lint config and call sites. Out: TS/Rust decoding paths.

## Size
small–medium (depends on site count).

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 21; evidence audits/2026-09-04/frontends-protocol.md A3, rec 9.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- The `encoding/json.Unmarshal` line is removed; `task go:lint` passes.
- Every formerly-hidden site either propagates the error — protocol decoding returns an `error` response with `error_category: validation` (`protocol/registry.yaml:69-71` enum `[validation, runtime, infrastructure]`; use the existing `invalid_request`-class error code) and config/fixture loading returns a load error — or has an inline `//nolint:errcheck // reason` where ignoring is provably safe.
- At least one regression test: a malformed `execute` request body (e.g. `inputs` as a string) yields an error response, not a zero-value execution.
notes: Landed on main via merge abc72256 (leased origin/main 9fc7dadc + feature tip dae25798; branch required a rebase due to 4 landed commits ahead of its base, no manual conflict). Gate evidence: land-work-run-verifier.py against exact merge preview -> verifier_status passed, selected_check_count 3, unverified_paths [] (exit 0). Independent code review verdict: Ready to merge, no issues. Follow-up filed separately by branch author: str-2tyfk (pre-existing task lint gap, 22 unrelated fmt.Fprint errcheck findings on main hidden by golangci-lint's optional Taskfile precondition).

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
Audit 2026-09-22 follow-up. One of this issue's acceptance checks was "The encoding/json.Unmarshal line is removed; task go:lint passes." It was closed with the reason "Closed" and no lint output cited. At that point `task go:lint` could not pass: str-2tyfk, filed from this issue's own work, recorded pre-existing unused and govet findings that were deferred and never fixed. On main as of 2026-09-23, `golangci-lint run ./...` in shatter-go still exits 1 with 10 issues:
- govet nilness at `protocol/handler.go:1325` (`nil == nil`)
- staticcheck SA5011 at `instrument/property_test.go:544`
- 7 unused functions

Whether the json.Unmarshal exclusion removal and its call-site fixes are complete was not re-audited. This note concerns only the lint acceptance.

The gap that let this through is that no gate or CI job invokes `go:lint`, so "lint passes" was never checked mechanically. The fix, gating golangci-lint and gofmt in check-static with forced-gate proof at close, is tracked in `str-49drv.26`.

description:

title: Install the BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT env section setup-hooks.sh already defines (raise to 60 s), smoke-test bd post-checkout <10 s, retire hook-bypass guidance
description:
## Problem
Agents routinely bypass git hooks (`--no-verify`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`) because memory files tell them to, for a bug recorded as fixed. The root cause both memories trace to is the beads hooks' 300-second timeout on every checkout/commit/push in every worktree, which pushes `git commit`/`git push` past the 2-minute foreground tool limit. `scripts/setup-hooks.sh` already contains the fix (a Shatter-managed env section that exports `BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT=30` ahead of the bd-managed block) — but it is not installed in the live hooks, and nothing verifies it is.

## Current code facts
- Where the value is read: the **bd-managed** section (`# --- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION v0.63.3 ---`) in `.git/hooks/{pre-commit,pre-push,post-checkout,post-merge,prepare-commit-msg}:6` — `_bd_timeout=${BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT:-300}` then `timeout "$_bd_timeout" bd hooks run <hook>`; on exit 124 it prints "timed out after ${_bd_timeout}s — continuing without beads". bd rewrites this block on upgrade, so the value must be set *outside* it.
- Where it should be set: `scripts/setup-hooks.sh:41` `BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT_LINE='export BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT="${BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT:-30}"'`; `install_hook_env()` (:60-100) prepends a `# --- BEGIN SHATTER HOOK ENV ---` section right after the shebang, before the bd block, for `BEADS_HOOKS=(pre-commit post-merge pre-push post-checkout prepare-commit-msg)` (:42).
- Live state: `bash scripts/setup-hooks.sh --check` → `[miss] pre-push/post-checkout/prepare-commit-msg: Shatter hook environment missing or stale` ("5 hook(s) missing"); `grep BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT .git/hooks/*` finds only the bd default. `.beads/config.yaml` has no hook settings (`dolt.auto-start: true`, `idle-timeout: 0`); `.beads/hooks/*` are bd's thin shims (`exec bd hooks run …`) with no timeout.
- The 300 s case is a dead/locked dolt server: during the audit an orphaned `dolt sql-server` held the lock while `.beads/dolt-server.{pid,port}` were missing, so every `bd` call waited 10 s for auto-start and failed (p1-16).
- Memories `project_beads_git_hook_timeout` and `project_shatter_git_hook_test_corrupts_worktree` (under `~/.claude/projects/-home-ketan-project-shatter/memory/`, outside the repo) recommend `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` / `--no-verify`; the corrupting test was fixed 2026-07-05; `feedback_verify_hooks_before_bypass` says don't bypass.
- Retrospective: 100 `--no-verify` (46 commit, 54 push) and 23 hooksPath bypasses across 14 sessions; 9 commit/push timeouts at the 2-minute foreground limit. AGENTS.md says "Leave the managed git hooks alone".

## Acceptance checks
- `scripts/setup-hooks.sh:41` default raised to **60 s**: dolt cold start is ~10 s (`bd`'s own auto-start timeout) and a first `bd sync` after a long idle can take 20–40 s; 30 s risks aborting legitimate syncs, 60 s still fits inside the 120 s foreground tool limit with the Shatter quality section's own work. On exit 124 the Shatter env section (or a wrapper line in it) prints `bd dolt status` so the timeout is diagnosable.
- `scripts/setup-dev.sh` and the SessionStart hook chain run `scripts/setup-hooks.sh` (idempotent) so `--check` reports `[ok]` for all five hooks in every worktree; `grep BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT .git/hooks/pre-push` shows the Shatter line above the bd block.
- `scripts/test_setup_hooks.sh` gains: in a fresh linked worktree with the dolt server up, `time bd hooks run post-checkout` < 10 s; with the server unreachable (test sets `BD_DOLT_PORT`/points `BEADS_DB` at a temp dir rather than stopping the shared server), the hook returns within `BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT`+2 s and prints the status line.
- `docs/hooks.md` documents the variable and the override (`BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT=120 git push`).
- **Request to the user (not a deliverable of this issue)**: replace the two memory files above with one pointer line ("hooks may take >2 min under `task affected`; push in background; never `--no-verify` — see CLAUDE.md Tool rules"); the repo side keeps AGENTS.md's "leave hooks alone" rule and the a2-39 tool-rules line.

## Scope
In: setup-hooks.sh default + diagnostics, setup-dev/SessionStart wiring, test, docs/hooks.md. Out: memory files (user request), moving pre-push gates to CI, bento Stop-hook behavior, the dolt orphan fix (p1-16).

## Size
small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 42; evidence audits/2026-09-04/agent-system.md §1 (git hooks), §2 item 8, §3, rec 10; session-retro.md §3 anti-pattern 2, §4; `scripts/setup-hooks.sh --check` run during drafting.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- `scripts/setup-hooks.sh:41` default raised to **60 s**: dolt cold start is ~10 s (`bd`'s own auto-start timeout) and a first `bd sync` after a long idle can take 20–40 s; 30 s risks aborting legitimate syncs, 60 s still fits inside the 120 s foreground tool limit with the Shatter quality section's own work. On exit 124 the Shatter env section (or a wrapper line in it) prints `bd dolt status` so the timeout is diagnosable.
- `scripts/setup-dev.sh` and the SessionStart hook chain run `scripts/setup-hooks.sh` (idempotent) so `--check` reports `[ok]` for all five hooks in every worktree; `grep BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT .git/hooks/pre-push` shows the Shatter line above the bd block.
- `scripts/test_setup_hooks.sh` gains: in a fresh linked worktree with the dolt server up, `time bd hooks run post-checkout` < 10 s; with the server unreachable (test sets `BD_DOLT_PORT`/points `BEADS_DB` at a temp dir rather than stopping the shared server), the hook returns within `BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT`+2 s and prints the status line.
- `docs/hooks.md` documents the variable and the override (`BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT=120 git push`).
- **Request to the user (not a deliverable of this issue)**: replace the two memory files above with one pointer line ("hooks may take >2 min under `task affected`; push in background; never `--no-verify` — see CLAUDE.md Tool rules"); the repo side keeps AGENTS.md's "leave hooks alone" rule and the a2-39 tool-rules line.
close_reason: Superseded by str-49drv.199 (maintainer decision D4, 2026-09-23: retire the beads JSONL import on checkout and move to a Dolt remote; no hook timeout env var, no hook bypass). Measured: post-checkout spends ~6 min importing .beads/issues.jsonl.

comments.author: Ketan Gangatirkar
comments.text:
**Audit 2026-09-22 note: superseded (maintainer decision D4, 2026-09-23)**

This issue will not be implemented. The maintainer has decided not to change
`BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT` and not to add any hook env block.

Measured 2026-09-23: a direct, unwrapped `bd -v hooks run post-checkout`

export, last committed at 134dd616 on 2026-09-07, and bd 1.1.0 itself calls
it "an export, not cross-machine sync or source of truth". Tuning the timeout
only changes how much of that wait is cut off. It does not stop a stale
snapshot from being imported into a newer database.

Replacement work:
- str-49drv.198: checks whether the import has

- str-49drv.204: finds what the hook waits on, lists every
  import entry point, and records one latency baseline.
- str-49drv.199: stops the import on every entry
  point through bd configuration, makes the Dolt remote the sync channel, and

title: Break the four shatter-core module cycles and add a module-graph check to CI
description:
## Problem
Four pairs of core modules import each other. A leaf config type (`explorer::ExploreConfig`) depends on the top-level scan scheduler, and leaf utilities (`hash_branch_path`, `FrontendCapabilities`, `TerminationReason`) live inside a 7.5k-line orchestrator. Rust tolerates intra-crate cycles, so nothing stops the layering from collapsing further; the cycles are also why the random/concolic parallel-path drift is hard to refactor away.

## Current code facts
- Cycles (both directions of `use crate::`): `explorer ↔ orchestrator`, `explorer ↔ scan_orchestrator`, `orchestrator ↔ strategy`, `input_gen ↔ orchestrator`.
- `shatter-core/src/explorer.rs:175-178` — `ExploreConfig.budget_surplus: Option<Arc<crate::scan_orchestrator::BudgetSurplus>>` and `claim_policy: crate::scan_orchestrator::ClaimPolicy`.
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs:62 pub struct BudgetSurplus`; `ClaimPolicy` in the same file.
- `shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs:59 pub struct FrontendCapabilities`, `:304 pub enum TerminationReason`, `:784 pub fn hash_branch_path` — imported by `explorer.rs`.

title: Generate frontend capability tables from parity-matrix.yaml into crate CLAUDE.md and the frontend-parity skill; check in `task parity`
description:
## Problem
Capability/side-effect/timeout prose in the three frontend CLAUDE.md files and in `.claude/skills/frontend-parity/SKILL.md` is hand-copied from `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` and is now wrong in several places. The skill tells agents to treat that prose as the contract, so agents preserve divergences that were resolved months ago. `task parity` checks matrix ↔ registry ↔ handshake only.

## Current code facts
- Stale vs matrix: `shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md:147-150` and `shatter-rust/CLAUDE.md:117-120` "declares support for `outcome` only" (matrix `feature_capabilities`: TS has `execute_capture`, `host_write_isolation`, `instrumentable_line_count`; Rust `execute_capture`, `host_write_isolation`); `shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md:43-45` "TS is the only frontend that produces `ite`" (Go does: `analyzer.go:2201`, `shatter-go/CLAUDE.md:52-70`); `shatter-rust/CLAUDE.md:15` command list omits `prepare` (advertised at `handler.rs:567-575`).
- `.claude/skills/frontend-parity/SKILL.md:107-115` side-effect table shows Go `thrown_error`/file/network/env ✗ (matrix: captured); `:133` "Rust's analyze handler is a stub" (analyzer.rs is 4,475 lines), "Go lacks data flow tracking"; `:143` Rust timeout "stored, not yet applied".
- `scripts/validate-parity.py` (`task parity`, `Taskfile.yml:245-265`) and `scripts/protocol-codegen.py --check` (`protocol-codegen-check`, :296-310) are the existing generate-then-check patterns.
- Matrix sections available to render: `commands` (10), `complex_types` (32), `feature_capabilities`, side-effect capture rows, `allowed_divergences` (id/status/affected_frontends), exec/build timeout defaults live in code (`executor.ts:76`, `executor.go:18`, `handler.rs:40`) — not in the matrix.

## Design
- `scripts/gen-parity-tables.py [--check] [--write]` renders, per frontend, four markdown tables from `parity-matrix.yaml`: Commands (supported/unsupported), Complex types, Feature capabilities, Open divergences affecting this frontend. Output is written between `<!-- parity:begin frontend=<lang> -->` and `<!-- parity:end -->` markers in `shatter-{ts,go,rust}/CLAUDE.md`; a `<!-- parity:begin frontend=all -->` block in `frontend-parity/SKILL.md` holds the three-column comparison. Hand-written text inside the markers is overwritten; text outside is untouched.
- `--check` exits non-zero when any rendered block differs from the file (same contract as `protocol-codegen-check`); wired as a step of `task parity` and into `drift-patrol.py check_parity_expiry`'s neighbour slot.
- Timeout defaults are out of the matrix; the generator leaves a one-line pointer to `protocol/PARITY.md` for them.

## Acceptance checks
- Editing `parity-matrix.yaml` (e.g. flipping a Go side-effect row) makes `task parity` fail until `gen-parity-tables.py --write` is rerun.
- The five stale claims above no longer appear (grep for the quoted phrases returns nothing); the hand-written sentences are replaced by the generated block or deleted.
- `frontend-parity/SKILL.md` capability tables are inside markers; its prose says "the block below is generated — do not edit".

## Scope
In: generator, check wiring, marker blocks in three CLAUDE.md files and one skill. Out: slimming the rest of the CLAUDE.md prose (a2-38c); matrix content fixes (p2-24).

## Size
small–medium.

## Provenance

title: Add one "Tool rules" block to CLAUDE.md (file tools vs Bash, /usr/bin/grep, no foreground sleep, hooks-aware push, task facade, gate cache)
description:
## Problem
The retrospective over 252 sessions shows the same six tool mistakes recurring because no single rule states them: shell text tools where Read/Grep fit, `--no-verify` to dodge slow hooks, foreground `sleep` blocked by the harness, bare `cargo test` bypassing the task graph, and gate runs reported as passes when Task's checksum cache executed nothing. Three existing instructions about file access contradict each other.

## Current code facts
- Retrospective (session-retro.md §1, §3): 886 `grep/cat/sed/find` Bash calls in 104 sessions where Read/Grep/Glob fit; 100 `--no-verify` + 23 `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` in 14 sessions; 40 of 91 `sleep` calls blocked; bare `cargo test` 446 vs `task test*` 137; 9 commit/push timeouts at the 2-minute foreground limit (pre-push runs `task affected`).
- Contradiction: AGENTS.md:23-25 "Use Grep/Glob/Read, not shell grep/cat/sed" vs AGENTS.md RTK block :529-531 "always prefix with rtk … `rtk grep`" vs auto-mode harness "do your work through Bash". The Bash tool's `grep` is shadowed (memory `project_claude_code_grep_shadow`; this audit used `/usr/bin/grep`); the rtk PreToolUse hook rewrote `find -exec` during the audit.
- Task cache: 19 leaf tasks have `sources:` and 39 checksum files sit in `.task/checksum`; `Taskfile.yml:483-490` comment says `--force` does not propagate through `check-governed` ("force a stage directly (e.g. `task --force check-unit`)"). Not mentioned in CLAUDE.md, any skill, or the verifier.
- CLAUDE.md has no tool-usage section; its only `cargo test` mentions are the E2E commands (:50, :64).

## Acceptance checks
- CLAUDE.md gains a ≤ 15-line "Tool rules" block:
  1. Read/Grep/Glob/Edit for files; Bash for commands.
  2. Inside scripts and Bash pipelines use `/usr/bin/grep` and `/usr/bin/git` (the tool shell shadows `grep`; the rtk hook rewrites some commands). *Revisit trigger*: drop this line when the dotfiles rtk hook is narrowed and the grep shadow removed (dotfiles items 24/25 in the audit).
  3. Never foreground `sleep`; use Monitor/TaskOutput.
  4. `git commit`/`git push` with `run_in_background` — hooks run `task affected`/`task check` and exceed the 2-minute foreground limit; never `--no-verify` or `core.hooksPath` overrides.
  5. Never bare `cargo test`/`npm test`/`go test` when a `task` target exists.
  6. Gates are checksum-cached: a run that prints "task is up to date" executed nothing. **Today**: force the leaf you need (`task --force check-unit`, `task --force e2e-ts`) or delete `.task/checksum` before claiming a gate passed; `task check-fresh` (p1-02) will replace this once it lands.
- AGENTS.md :23-25 replaced by a pointer to the block and the RTK block removed (coordinated with a2-38a); CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md budget still met.
- Non-blocking follow-up: the str-u394l.4 lint (p2-33b) asserts the block exists and skills do not contradict it.

## Scope
In: CLAUDE.md block, AGENTS.md cross-reference. Out: dotfiles/rtk hook changes; the gate-cache fix itself (p1-02).

## Size
small.

## Provenance
Audit 2026-09-04, section 11, action item 39; evidence audits/2026-09-04/session-retro.md §3, §4; agent-system.md §2 item 1, §3.

Filed from the shatter audit 2026-09-04 (shatter repo, branch audit-2026-09-04, audits/2026-09-04.md).

The bento require-worktree hook blocks writes on `main`, and global rules forbid working on `main`, so the step cannot succeed in the primary checkout. Result: the 2026-07-10 audit issue (`str-sff87`) is still in_progress with no committed report — only a memory file claims one exists. Findings are filed as loose issues with no back-link to the audit, so follow-through cannot be verified without grepping the tracker. The skill also says "observation-only" earlier and then instructs writing, committing and filing.

## Current code facts
- `.claude/skills/audit/SKILL.md:379-385`: Phase 10 step 6 "Commit report: Stage and commit the audit report file (`audits/YYYY-MM-DD.md`) with message `audit: YYYY-MM-DD`"; no `launch-work`/`land-work` mention; step 3 creates issues without a parent.
- `require-worktree.sh` (bento PreToolUse Edit/Write) blocks edits on `main`; `~/dotfiles/codex/AGENTS.md` "Branches And Worktrees" forbids offering `main`.
- `str-sff87` "Project health audit 2026-07-10" in_progress 55 d; `audits/` contains `2026-02-28.md`, `2026-05-21.md`, and `2026-09-04.md` (this audit, produced in a worktree by hand).
- May audit filed no issues at the time ("Issues Created: None"); Feb audit's five issues all closed — the difference is whether filing happened inside the skill run.
- `scripts/drift-patrol.py check_tracker_hygiene` (:522) checks stale in_progress >14 d and orphaned children; nothing checks audit issues specifically.

## Decisions taken in this draft
- **Report path: keep `audits/<date>.md`** (the existing location; all three reports live there). p2-31a may later move the directory under `docs/audits/`; if it does, the skill and the patrol check are updated in that issue, not here.
- **Close-reason format** so the patrol can parse it: `report: audits/<date>.md` as the first line of the reason.
- The "observation-only" sentence is rewritten to "read-only with respect to product code; the audit's own outputs are the report and tracker issues, produced on a feature branch".

## Acceptance checks
- SKILL.md Phase 10 lists, in order: `bd create` an `audit`-labelled issue → `bento:launch-work` on it → write `audits/<date>.md` in that worktree → file findings with `--parent <audit-id>` and list them in the report's final table → `bento:land-work`, which closes the audit issue with reason `report: audits/<date>.md`. - `str-sff87` closed with an explicit reason (report reconstructed from the memory notes, or "report not produced").

## Scope
In: `.claude/skills/audit/SKILL.md`, drift-patrol check, `str-sff87`. Out: bento's own skills; moving the audits directory (p2-31a).

small.

AGENTS.md (30.5 KB) plus CLAUDE.md (8.5 KB) load every session (~10k tokens at 4 B/token) and a third of AGENTS.md is procedure that bento skills now own or that contradicts them. Retrospective data shows the rules that remain are not retained (886 shell-text-tool calls, 100 `--no-verify`, landing thrash), which is the expected outcome of burying five rules in 600 lines.

## Current code facts
- Section sizes (bytes): Git Workflow 14,997; Creating Issues 6,204; Landing the Plane 1,836; Host Build Cache Setup 1,722; Shared-Machine Resource Etiquette 1,505; Key Commands 992; bd Quick Reference 913; Issue Title Guidelines 715; Kapow Refute Workflow 523; Searching and Reading Files 421; Rules 250.
