title: TS no-capture timing test flakes under load
description:
# TS no-capture timing test flakes under load

Type: bug
Priority: P2
Labels: test,typescript,performance

## Symptom

`shatter-ts/src/executor.test.ts` contains two tests that compare sequential
wall-clock loops and require no-capture execution to finish in less than 1.5x
the capture loop. During a controlled two-worktree `check-fast` stress run at
commit `a440adf3c18785fbefd7192552abc8900c9a1d9b`, the
`executeFunction no-capture fast path` case failed with `noCaptureMs=2431`
against a `captureMs * 1.5` limit of `1846.5`. The concurrent companion's same
TS suite passed 976/976, and five subsequent candidate stress runs passed, so
the assertion is sensitive to phase-specific host contention rather than a
stable functional regression.

## Current code facts

- `shatter-ts/src/executor.test.ts:2796-2825` runs 200 capture executions,
  records `Date.now()`, then runs 200 no-capture executions and compares the
  two totals. The phases are not interleaved, randomized, or repeated.
- A second assertion at `shatter-ts/src/executor.test.ts:2906-2934` uses the
  same sequential wall-clock ratio for `executeInstrumented`.
- Shared-machine gates intentionally run under concurrent load, so either
  phase can receive materially different CPU scheduling and I/O contention.

## Smallest known reproduction

Run `task --force check-fast` concurrently in two clean, prebuilt worktrees at
the same commit. In the observed failure the candidate TS suite reported the
numbers above while the companion TS suite passed. The full candidate command
later passed five times under the same general setup, demonstrating a
stochastic load-sensitive failure rather than a consistently slower
implementation.

## Desired behavior

The tests should continue detecting a real no-capture performance regression
without failing because the two measurement phases receive different host
scheduling. Preserve the functional no-capture assertions; replace or harden
only the load-sensitive performance comparison.

## Acceptance checks

1. Add a regression test or deterministic measurement seam that reproduces the
   phase-skew problem before the fix and passes afterward.
2. Retain a meaningful assertion that no-capture avoids capture overhead; do
   not merely remove the performance guard or widen it without evidence.
3. In two clean, prebuilt same-commit worktrees, keep a companion loop of
   `task --force ts:test-fast` active while the candidate runs the same command
   five times sequentially; all five candidate runs and the focused executor
   tests pass with no wall-clock ratio flake. Record each run's interval and
   return code so overlap is explicit.

## Scope

In scope: TS executor test/benchmark mechanics and a small measurement helper
if needed. Out of scope: production executor behavior changes, unrelated Jest
tests, and weakening functional side-effect-capture coverage.

The choice of statistical method, clock, interleaving strategy, or deterministic
measurement seam is deliberately left to the implementing agent; it must meet
acceptance check 2 rather than being prescribed here.

Expected size: one focused TypeScript test file, under roughly 100 lines.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A deterministic phase-skew regression or measurement seam fails before the fix and passes afterward. 2. A meaningful guard still proves no-capture avoids capture overhead; functional capture assertions remain intact and focused executor tests pass. 3. With a companion loop of task --force ts:test-fast active in a clean prebuilt same-commit worktree, five sequential candidate runs of that command pass; record intervals and return codes to prove overlap.
notes: Landed on main via merge eeac3622 (leased origin/main abc72256 + feature tip e61138d1; rebase required 6 commits forward, no manual conflict). Gate evidence: land-work-run-verifier.py against exact merge preview -> verifier_status passed, selected_check_count 3, unverified_paths [] (exit 0). Independent code review verdict: Merge with fixes (2 Minor, non-blocking) -> filed as follow-ups str-l261l and str-25kcm; no Critical/Important findings, no changes required before merge.

title: Widen --seed to also seed exploration RNG (scans are currently unreproducible)
description:
## Symptom
There is no way to make `shatter scan` or `shatter explore` reproducible. Two runs
over identical source with identical flags produce different coverage and different
discovered inputs, so run-to-run variance cannot be separated from real change.

## Evidence
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs:167-168` defines `pub seed: Option<u64>` — "Random seed for reproducibility. If None, uses entropy."
- The core honors it: `shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs:2492` builds its RNG via `match config.seed`, and the value is threaded into explore configs (`scan_orchestrator.rs:1722`, `:3087`, `:4359`).
- The CLI never sets it. `--seed` is plumbed as `core_sample_seed` (`shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs:207`) and its help text reads "Seed for deterministic core sample selection"; every CLI construction of the scan/explore config passes `seed: None`.
- No environment variable sets it either (no `SHATTER_SEED`; only `SHATTER_SEEDS_DIR`, which is the input pool directory, unrelated).

## Desired behavior
**Widen the existing `--seed` so it also sets `ScanConfig.seed`**, rather than adding
a second seed flag.

Rationale for the choice: widening is backward compatible in the direction that
matters. Someone passing `--seed 42` today gets deterministic core-sample selection;
afterwards they get that *plus* seeded exploration — strictly more determinism, never
less, and no existing invocation changes meaning in a way that could break. Two seed
flags on one command is also a usability trap, since the obvious flag would be the
wrong one for the common case. Update the flag's help text, which currently reads
"Seed for deterministic core sample selection".

A CLI flag is the requirement; an env var is optional and not requested here.

## Acceptance checks
- Two scans of the same fixture at the same seed produce identical `functions[]` coverage numbers.
- Omitting the flag preserves today's entropy behavior.
- A test asserts run-to-run identity at a fixed seed and difference at differing seeds.

## Scope
In scope: CLI/env wiring to `ScanConfig.seed` and a determinism test.
Out of scope: making parallel scheduling deterministic; seeding alone will not remove all variance.

## Why it matters beyond reproducibility
Any longitudinal measurement of Shatter has to absorb this variance with repeats and
noise bands instead. Exposing the seed shrinks that overhead directly.
close_reason: aafc8ba7 landed on main (gate: land.py verify step passed on full task test-standard; regression test scan_seed_reproducibility passes; code review found two real known-gap follow-ups (str-pbqyr: seed correlation across functions in default single-worker path, str-9m9o3: cache freshness ignores seed) filed rather than blocking, since this change is strictly additive over the prior never-wired state and the author's own commit already documented a related known verification gap)

title: FailedFunctionReport discards structure the orchestrator already has (no category, timeout phase flattened)
description:
## Symptom
Failure analysis across a scan must cluster on free-text `reason` strings, while the
parallel `SkippedFunctionReport` carries a structured `category`. Worse, the
orchestrator *already* distinguishes failure kinds internally — including a build vs
execution timeout phase discriminator — and that structure is flattened into prose at
the report boundary. Consumers regex it back out, inconsistently.

## Current code facts (verified before filing)
- `FailedFunctionReport` is defined at `shatter-core/src/report.rs:1036` and constructed in exactly **one** place: `report.rs:219`, which routes `skipped_functions` entries carrying `SkipCategory::Error` into the `failed` array. Its fields are `function_name`, `display_name`, `qualified_id`, `file_path`, `reason`, `language` — no category.
- Failures originate upstream as `SkippedFunction { category: SkipCategory::Error, reason }`. Only three production paths produce that category:
  1. **Missing analysis** — `scan_orchestrator.rs:4013-4017`, literal reason `"no analysis found"`.
  2. **Timeout** — `FunctionOutcome::Timeout { function_name, limit, phase }` (`scan_orchestrator.rs:410-419`) is converted at `:4980-4983` via `let reason = phase_timeout_reason(phase, limit)` and pushed with `category: SkipCategory::Error` at `:4991`.
  3. **Exploration error** — `FunctionOutcome::Error { function_name, error }` (`scan_orchestrator.rs:423-426`), pushed with `SkipCategory::Error` near `:5046`; `error` is already free text at the source.
- `FunctionOutcome::Timeout.phase` is documented at `scan_orchestrator.rs:414-418` as `"build"` for Prepare vs `"execution"` for the concolic loop, added specifically "so the user can distinguish `--build-timeout` from `--timeout-per-fn`" (str-7v73). A third value `"task"` is used at `:4888`. **This structure exists and is discarded.**
- Adjacent outcomes deliberately do *not* become failures: `TotalTimeout` maps to `SkipCategory::Interrupted`, and `Unsupported` maps to `SkipCategory::Unsupported` "rather than `SkipCategory::Error`" (`scan_orchestrator.rs:430-434`, str-31j.4). Those are out of scope here.

## Desired behavior
Add a structured `category` to `FailedFunctionReport`, set where the
`SkipCategory::Error` row is created — never inferred later by pattern-matching
`reason` text — with `reason` retained for detail.

Closed taxonomy, one row per verified production source:

| Variant | Source |
|---|---|
| `no_analysis` | `scan_orchestrator.rs:4013-4017` |
| `build_timeout` | `FunctionOutcome::Timeout` with `phase == "build"` |
| `execution_timeout` | `FunctionOutcome::Timeout` with `phase == "execution"` |
| `task_timeout` | `FunctionOutcome::Timeout` with `phase == "task"` (`:4888`) |
| `exploration_error` | `FunctionOutcome::Error` — free-text `error` preserved in `reason` |

If a future failure site cannot be mapped confidently, add `other` rather than guessing:
a wrong category is worse than an honest unclassified one.

## Acceptance checks
- Every emitted `FailedFunctionReport` carries a non-empty category.
- A fixture that times out during harness build yields `build_timeout`, and one that times out during exploration yields `execution_timeout` — the distinction currently recoverable only by parsing `phase_timeout_reason` output.
- Failures whose reason strings differ only in interpolated paths, durations, or identifiers share a category.
- Field is `#[serde(default)]` so pre-existing reports still decode; `SCAN_REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` (currently 9) bumps.

## Scope
In scope: the `FailedFunctionReport` type, category population at the three sites above, schema version bump.
Out of scope: changing which outcomes count as failures (`TotalTimeout` and `Unsupported` mappings stay as they are), and changing failure reason text.

## Size
Small — one struct field, three population sites, one schema bump.

title: shatter scan cannot honor shatter.scope.yaml: --scope exists only on explore
description:
## Symptom
`shatter scan` silently ignores a project's `shatter.scope.yaml`. A project whose
eligible source set is defined by that file gets a different corpus depending on
which subcommand is used, with no warning.

## Evidence
- `shatter explore --help` exposes `--scope <SCOPE>` ("Path to a scope configuration YAML file (shatter.scope.yaml)").
- `shatter scan --help` contains zero occurrences of "scope".
- Scope handling lives in `shatter-core/src/scope.rs` and is reachable only through the explore path.
- Downstream consequence: kapow maintains `shatter.scope.yaml` (excludes 318 `*_test.go`, `*.stories.tsx`, a mock provider package, and generated `field_name_gen.go`) and reimplements the parsing in shell (`scripts/shatter-source-set.sh:224-256`) because it cannot pass the file to the engine for a whole-directory run.

## Desired behavior
`shatter scan` accepts `--scope <path>` with the same semantics as `explore`, and
discovers `shatter.scope.yaml` by the same upward-walk rule used for `.shatter/config.yaml`.

## Acceptance checks
- `shatter scan <dir> --scope <file>` excludes scope-excluded paths from the scanned set.
- `shatter list-targets` reflects the same exclusions, so the selection is inspectable without a full scan.
- A scan with and without `--scope` on a fixture with excluded files produces different `total_discovered_functions`, asserted in a test.

## Scope
In scope: wiring `--scope` into scan's file selection and `list-targets`.
Out of scope: changing scope file semantics, or auto-applying scope without the flag.
notes: Landed on main at 9912463548e8ce04b555b86987e665b845e6c303. Gate evidence: task affected → exit 0 (smoke, core:clippy, core:test, cli:clippy, cli:test, e2e-ts, e2e-go, e2e-rust, gauntlet); task check → exit 0; exact-preview verifier → exit 0 (task test-standard, task parity, task conformance); guarded lease verification and landing verification → exit 0.

title: Core Git callers inherit hook env
description:
# Core Git callers inherit hook env

Type: bug
Priority: P2
Labels: core,git
Provenance: follow-up discovered while fixing `str-eq9t8`, whose merge `aa2cf69b` added the scrubbed `scm::git_command` boundary.

## Symptom

Four Git subprocess callers outside `shatter-core/src/scm.rs` still inherit repository-selection variables such as `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`. When Shatter runs from a managed Git hook, these callers can read the outer hook repository, return the wrong commit or file age, or silently take a fallback even though their intended repository is valid.

The affected functions are:

- `core_sample::default_seed(scan_dir)`, which should incorporate `scan_dir`'s full HEAD when available and otherwise hash only `scan_dir`.
- `test_runner::git_head_commit(root)`, which should return `root`'s short HEAD while preserving its existing error contract.
- `test_prioritization::git_file_age_days(project_root, file, now_epoch)`, which should read history from `project_root` and preserve the existing `365.0` fallback for missing or unusable history.
- `bench::detect_git_commit()`, which should continue reporting the full HEAD of the process current working directory and return `None` when it cannot do so.

## Current code facts

- Landed merge `aa2cf69b` introduced `scm::git_command(root)`, which sets `current_dir(root)` and removes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, and `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`. It is currently private to `scm.rs`.
- `shatter-core/src/core_sample.rs::default_seed` launches raw `git rev-parse HEAD` with `current_dir(scan_dir)`.
- `shatter-core/src/test_runner.rs::git_head_commit` launches raw `git rev-parse --short HEAD` with `current_dir(root)`.
- `shatter-core/src/test_prioritization.rs::git_file_age_days` launches raw `git log -1 --format=%ct -- <file>` with `current_dir(project_root)`.
- `shatter-core/src/bench.rs::detect_git_commit` launches raw `git rev-parse HEAD` without `current_dir`; its only caller is `shatter-cli/src/commands/bench.rs`, so the existing repository selection is the CLI process current working directory. Preserve that behavior without changing the public function signature or CLI caller.

## Smallest deterministic reproduction

Use a child test process so tests never mutate process-global environment in the parallel parent. The parent creates separate `foreign` and `target` temporary repositories with distinct commits and commit timestamps. It resolves the foreign repository's index and object directory to absolute paths, then launches the child with those paths in `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` (and may set the other repository-selection variables covered by `scm::git_command`).

In the child, invoke each affected caller against `target`; for `bench::detect_git_commit`, set the child process current directory to `target`. Before the fix, at least the commit-producing calls consult foreign repository state or fail. After the fix, every result must match the target repository exactly.

## Acceptance checks

1. Make the landed scrubbed command constructor reusable within `shatter-core` and route all four affected Git launches through it. Do not duplicate a partial environment-removal list.
2. Add child-process regression coverage using absolute foreign index/object paths and exact target expectations: `default_seed` equals the clean target-repository seed; `git_head_commit` equals target's short HEAD; prioritization uses the target file timestamp to produce the expected age; and `detect_git_commit` equals target's full HEAD when the child current directory is target.
3. Preserve current public signatures, repository-root semantics, Git arguments, and fallbacks, including `default_seed`'s scan-dir-only fallback, `git_file_age_days`'s `365.0`, and `detect_git_commit`'s `None`. Existing and new focused tests plus the normal Rust quality gate pass.

## Scope

In scope: `shatter-core/src/scm.rs`, `core_sample.rs`, `test_runner.rs`, `test_prioritization.rs`, and `bench.rs`, plus tests colocated in those modules. Expected change is a mechanical five-file hardening under roughly 160 lines.

Out of scope: changes to managed hooks; scrubbing Git configuration/identity variables beyond the six already governed by `scm::git_command`; changing CLI benchmark invocation or public APIs; changing fallback values or unrelated Git behavior.
acceptance_criteria: All four callers use the shared scrubbed Git command boundary; deterministic child-process regressions prove target-repository results under absolute foreign Git index/object paths; existing signatures, root semantics, arguments, fallbacks, and Rust gates remain unchanged and passing.
notes:
Cross-check of str-k7cla found shatter-core/src/scm.rs test helper git_ok() clears five repository-local Git variables but omits GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES; include this consistency fix when addressing remaining core Git callers.
Landed on main via merge 6836489a (leased origin/main eeac3622 + feature tip 845c9d8f; rebase required 8 commits forward, no manual conflict). Gate evidence: land-work-run-verifier.py against exact merge preview -> verifier_status passed, selected_check_count 3, unverified_paths [] (exit 0). Independent code review verdict: Ready to merge; reviewer empirically confirmed the regression test fails without the fix. One Minor non-blocking dedup nit filed as follow-up str-noghq.

title: Build accelerator doctor
description:
Task, P2, `build,developer-experience,sccache`; no prerequisite.

`python3 scripts/build-cache-doctor.py [--json] [--require-acceleration]`; Task calls human form. JSON v1: `{schema:int=1,status:string,wrapper:{configured:string|null,resolved_path:string|null,source:string},linker:{name:string,configured:string|null,resolved_path:string|null,source:string},sccache:{state:string,binary_path:string|null,cache_dir:string|null,cache_size_bytes:int|null,stats:object|null},budgets:{cargo_build_jobs:string|null,cargo_source:string,shatter_cpu_budget:string|null,shatter_source:string},diagnostics:[strings]}`. Per-component source enum `environment|user_config|gate_environment|repo_config|default|none`; sccache state `active|installed_inactive|missing|wedged|error`; linker name `mold|lld|other|none`; diagnostics fixed `wrapper_missing,wrapper_not_sccache,wrapper_unexecutable,linker_missing,linker_unexecutable,sccache_missing,sccache_wedged,sccache_stats_error,invalid_config`.

Precedence/exact inputs: `RUSTC_WRAPPER` environment; then `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml` or `$HOME/.cargo/config.toml` `[build].rustc-wrapper`; then repo `.cargo/config.toml`. Gate environment applies only to budget fields: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` then repo Cargo jobs; `SHATTER_CPU_BUDGET` then none. Target rustflags/linker: `CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_RUSTFLAGS`, then user `[target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu].rustflags`, then repo same; parse `-fuse-ld=mold|lld`. Effective wrapper requires configured executable resolving absolute/PATH and basename sccache. Sccache cache-dir precedence is `SCCACHE_DIR`, then a cache location reported by `sccache --show-stats`, then `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/sccache`; cache size is logical apparent regular-file bytes without following symlinks, null when path absent/unreadable. Configured linker wins; otherwise discover executables with PATH, preferring mold over lld when both exist, recording configured=null/source=none but name/resolved_path for the discovered option. Discovery alone is partial, never accelerated; strict requires the linker be configured and executable. Top status: `accelerated` only when wrapper resolves to active sccache and configured linker resolves to executable mold/lld; `partial` when any sccache/linker component is installed/configured but full condition is false, including installed-inactive, wedged, discovered linker only, good configured linker only, or active sccache only; `inactive` when neither component is installed/configured; `error` for malformed config or unexpected probe error. Strict success only for accelerated; default warnings exit0 except top error exits70; strict unmet exit2; args64. `sccache --show-stats` timeout2s => wedged/partial. Named keys only; unrelated env absent. No target totals.

Acceptance: conflicting precedence/PATH/config fixtures and all enums; snapshots/exits/timeout; mutation/service/secret guard. Out: install/edit/service/cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: conflicting precedence/PATH/config fixtures and all enums; snapshots/exits/timeout; mutation/service/secret guard.
close_reason: Landed on main at 31484c3c (merge of str-35vtk.32-build-accelerator-doctor, head 919bdc4f). Gate evidence: land-work verifier (scripts/land_work_verifier.sh) against exact merge candidate — task test-standard: exit 0, task parity: exit 0, task conformance: exit 0 (all 3 selected checks passed, 3/3 changed files covered). Additionally: 57/57 scripts/test_build_cache_doctor.py unit tests pass (conflicting precedence/PATH/config fixtures, all enum values, snapshot/exit-code tests, 2s sccache-stats timeout test, mutation/service/secret-guard tests), task smoke passed, task e2e passed (TS/Go/Rust), task check-fast passed. Independent code review found 2 Important bugs (unhandled AttributeError crash on structurally-malformed TOML instead of status=error/exit 70; compute_cache_size returned 0 instead of null for an unreadable-but-existing cache dir) plus 1 unused import — all fixed with 5 regression tests before landing, verified via re-run gates. One Minor finding deferred as follow-up (str-35vtk.34): relative-path rustc-wrapper values resolved via PATH lookup instead of repo-relative, unlike cargo's own semantics — moderate confidence, not required by this issue's spec.

title: Worktree target report JSON
description:

Add an orthogonal `--json` mode with v1 `{worktrees:[{path,branch,issue_id:string|null,issue_status:string|unknown,current:bool,primary:bool,targets:[{kind,path,exists,bytes}]}],total_bytes}`; existing callers without `--json` remain compatible. `current` means realpath equals invoking PWD; `primary` is primary Git worktree. title: [bug] cold-build retry watchdog claim keyed only by progress_index, shared across replica tasks
description:
## Problem

str-807vi's watchdog-extension fix for the cold-build retry (claim_build_timeout_retry /
build_timeout_retry_claimant) tracks which task should get an extended join-watchdog
window by progress_index alone. Under --workers-per-fn > 1, progress_index is shared
across replica tasks for the same function (per ExploreTask's own doc comment) — it does
not uniquely identify one in-flight task.

Consequence: a replica task that never claimed the retry can inherit the extended
watchdog meant for its sibling replica that did claim it. A genuinely hung task on that
shared progress_index can then go undetected for up to 2x build_timeout instead of the
intended single build_timeout window, defeating part of the point of the watchdog.

## Fix direction

ExploreTask needs a unique per-replica identifier (not just progress_index) that
propagates through the claim/claimant/spawn/join call sites in
shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs, so the watchdog extension applies only to the
specific task instance that made the claim.

## Context

Found during independent code review while landing str-807vi (crashed-session leftover
worktree, str-807vi-cold-build-retry-watchdog). str-807vi's fix passes tests and E2E and
is otherwise sound, but this bug means it's a partial/unsafe fix under
--workers-per-fn > 1. str-807vi is being held unmerged pending a decision on whether to
fix this now or land str-807vi as a documented partial fix.

title: Rust execution-harness profile
description:
Generated Rust execution-harness manifests should use the same compact development profile as the repository workspaces:

[profile.dev]
debug = "line-tables-only"
split-debuginfo = "unpacked"

[profile.dev.package."*"]
debug = false

Current code facts:
- shatter-rust/src/executor.rs::generate_cargo_toml_with_user_deps builds the generated Cargo.toml string. It currently emits package, workspace, and dependency sections but no profile section.
- The repository workspace roots gained this profile under str-35vtk.2; generated harness crates are independent workspaces and therefore do not inherit it, increasing debug-artifact size and cache pressure.

Scope:
Update only generate_cargo_toml_with_user_deps and its focused unit coverage. Other manifest generators and their existing profile policies are out of scope. Do not merge the standalone Rust frontend into the root workspace, change dependency forwarding, or alter runtime behavior.

Acceptance:
- A focused unit test proves generated execution-harness manifests contain the exact profile settings above.
- task e2e-rust passes.
- task conformance passes.

Tracker relationship: standalone task discovered from str-35vtk.2; it is not another child of str-35vtk.
notes:
Landed on main at 162e9d2e (merge of str-cdgxr-harness-profile, feature commit 6b2943da).

Gate evidence (exact merge candidate):
- cargo test --lib generate_cargo_toml (shatter-rust): all 8 generate_cargo_toml_* tests pass, incl. new generate_cargo_toml_includes_compact_dev_profile
- task e2e-rust: 12/12 passed (392.97s)
- task conformance: 42/42 checks passed (4 frontends x 18 cases)
- land-work-run-verifier.py: passed, 3 selected checks, all changed paths (shatter-rust/src/executor.rs) covered

Independent code review (medium effort) found 2 Minor, non-blocking issues:
1. Commit message framed str-35vtk.2's root-workspace profile as already landed; it is not yet merged (separate unmerged branch) — this harness change is self-contained and correct regardless, but the parity claim is aspirational, not current fact. Worth revisiting when str-35vtk.2 actually lands to confirm the profile shapes still match.
2. The compact-profile TOML block is a separate hardcoded string literal in executor.rs rather than sourced from a shared definition with the checked-in Cargo.toml profile sections — acknowledged duplication risk if the policy is tuned later. Out of scope for this issue per its own stated scope.

title: [BUG] generateLoopMockFile skips shatterMockN_callIdx decl for passthrough mocks but shatterResetMockCounters references it unconditionally
description:
shatter-go/instrument/executor.go's generateLoopMockFile skips the entire
per-mock declaration block (including `var shatterMockN_callIdx int64`) for
mocks with DefaultBehavior == BehaviorPassthrough (the `continue` at the top
of the mock-emission loop). But shatterResetMockCounters, emitted separately,
loops over ALL mocks unconditionally and emits
`atomic.StoreInt64(&shatterMockN_callIdx, 0)` for every index N regardless of
behavior.

Failure scenario: call generateLoopMockFile with a single passthrough wire
mock, e.g. []MockConfig{{Symbol: "a.util.Do", ReturnValues: []any{1},
DefaultBehavior: BehaviorPassthrough}}. The emitted source references
shatterMock0_callIdx in shatterResetMockCounters but never declares it.
Verified by writing the generated source to a temp file and running `go
build`: fails with "undefined: shatterMock0_callIdx". Any harness with a
passthrough wire mock fails to compile.

Pre-existing bug, confirmed present before str-heegk's commit (f5c38109) --
not introduced by that fix, so not fixed as part of it. Found by independent
code review during the str-heegk landing.

Fix: either skip passthrough indices in shatterResetMockCounters's loop too,
or always declare shatterMockN_callIdx regardless of behavior.
notes:
Landed on main at eb4bc1c8 (merge of str-zn94g-passthrough-mock-counter, feature commit 2d89aec3).

Gate evidence (exact merge candidate, rebased twice onto a moving main due to concurrent landings from other sessions):
- go build ./... (shatter-go): passes
- go test ./instrument/... -run TestGenerateLoopMockFile: all 4 tests pass, incl. new TestGenerateLoopMockFile_PassthroughOnly_Compiles and TestGenerateLoopMockFile_MixedPassthroughAndNonPassthrough_Compiles (type-check generated source, not just parse)

title: axum/crate-bridge harnesses: thread-local coverage lost for handlers with real cross-thread awaits
description:
Follow-up from str-oc67 code review. str-oc67 fixed the axum crate harness (generate_axum_harness, shatter-rust/src/executor.rs) so it uses a current-thread tokio runtime instead of a multi-thread one — this fixed thread-local line/branch coverage being silently dropped (lines_executed=[]/branch_path=[]) for DB-backed handlers whose execution hops onto a different tokio worker thread via a real .await point, because shatter-rust-runtime's line/branch tracking is thread_local! and flush_results() only reads the block_on thread's copy.

The identical bug still exists, unfixed, in three sibling harness generators in the same file:

- generate_crate_bridge_wrapper (executor.rs:4737) — builds a multi-thread tokio::runtime::Runtime::new() and flushes on the calling thread afterward (~line 4874). This is the harness with built-in sqlx::PgPool support, i.e. the canonical DB-backed-handler path outside axum routing (e.g. invoked via shatter_crate_bridge_entry).
- generate_harness (executor.rs:2507) — single-file async function harness, same multi-thread runtime + calling-thread flush pattern.
- generate_dispatch_harness (executor.rs:2805) — batch dispatch harness (special-cases axum-shaped return types), same pattern.

Any async function reached through these paths that awaits work scheduled onto a different tokio worker thread (its own internal tokio::spawn, or a driver's internal thread-hop) will report full execution + correct return value but empty lines_executed/branch_path — same silent 0-coverage symptom as str-oc67, different entry point.

Fix: apply the same current-thread-runtime fix (or a more general fix that aggregates thread-local counters across threads, which would cover all four generators at once and avoid the block_in_place caveat noted in str-oc67's review) to these three generators.

Acceptance: each of the three generators gets a test with a handler/function that forces a genuine cross-thread await (mirroring str-oc67's crate_backed_axum_handler_with_spawned_await_reports_executed_branch_lines), confirming non-empty lines_executed/branch_path.

title: Investigate empty lines_executed / lost return value for kapow's env-guarded run() entrypoints
description:
## Problem

kapow's `api/cmd/fixtureutil/main.go::run(databaseURL, fixtureDir string, skipMigrate bool) error`
and `api/cmd/testlanes/main.go::run() error` both explore with `iterations > 0` but
`lines_executed: []`, `return_value: null`, `thrown_error: null` — the exploration
runs but observes nothing. These were the only 2 of 764 `api/` observation records with
`iterations > 0` and `lines_covered == 0`.

This is the (A) half of str-wvfke, which fixed the downstream misclassification
(`Postcondition::ReturnsVoid` asserted for a non-void, unobserved return — see
`Postcondition::Unobserved` in `shatter-core/src/spec.rs`) but did **not** find the root
cause of the empty observation itself.

## What str-wvfke ruled out

str-wvfke added an in-repo reduction —
`examples/go/main-run-error-return/main.go`: a `package main` function named `run`,
called by `main` -> `os.Exit`, with an unavoidable-error empty-input guard, same shape as
both kapow reproductions. Exercised via
`cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go -- e2e_go_main_run_error_return_is_observed_and_never_void`.

Result: **does not reproduce.** Both the erroring and nil-returning arms are fully
observed — non-empty `lines_executed`, and both the error message and the nil return are
captured. So "package main, function named run, called by main -> os.Exit" is not
sufficient on its own to trigger the bug.

## Leads not yet tried

- kapow's real `run()` reads `os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")` — an environment-variable read on
  the failing guard path. The in-repo reduction avoids env vars entirely; try adding one.
- kapow's real project has a full `project_root` / module layout, multiple files, and
  likely more complex mocking/frontend setup than the single-file reduction. Try
  reproducing directly against a trimmed copy of kapow's own `api/cmd/fixtureutil` package
  rather than a fresh single-file fixture.
- Confirm whether this reproduces on current kapow HEAD at all — the artifacts referenced
  in str-wvfke were from 2026-08-14 at engine commit `ce1d0199`; unrelated fixes since then
  may have already resolved it.

## Acceptance

- Either reproduce the empty-`lines_executed` bug against a kapow-shaped fixture (env-var
  guard and/or real project_root) and fix it, or confirm affirmatively (e.g. against
  current kapow HEAD) that it no longer occurs and close as not-reproducible.

title: Budget-exhausted scans emit one timed-out row per unattempted function
description:
## Problem

When a scan exhausts its total budget, every function it never reached is emitted as its own report
row reading `timed out (total scan budget exceeded)`. On a large module that is thousands of rows
carrying no information beyond "not attempted", and the report never states what the budget was or
how much of it was consumed — so the reader cannot tell that raising `--timeout-total` is the fix.

The wording is also misleading: "timed out" reads as "this function was attempted and did not
finish", which for most of these rows is false.

## Current code facts (verified 2026-08-14, engine @ ce1d0199)

- `shatter-core/src/report.rs:3716` emits the per-function row reason:
  `reason: "timed out (total scan budget exceeded)".to_string()`.
- `shatter-core/src/report.rs:129` documents that string as a reason value.
- `shatter-core/src/report.rs:1957` already emits a distinct SUMMARY line using different wording —
  `"  - **interrupted (total scan budget exceeded):** {interrupted}"` — so an aggregate count is
  partly modelled; the per-function rows are the redundant part.
- The budget knob is `shatter scan --timeout-total <secs>`, "Total scan timeout in seconds.
  Default: 300s. Overridden by shatter.config.json when not explicitly set."

## Resolved: the state already exists, so this is a rendering change

`shatter-core/src/report.rs:61` documents it: *"str-smcx adds `\"interrupted\"` skipped entries for
functions not attempted because the run-level scan budget expired. Schema bumps to v7."* The
never-attempted set is therefore already modelled and counted (`report.rs:243` emits the
`"interrupted"` skip reason; `:95` counts it; `:1957` renders the summary line). The defect is that
these functions ALSO get a per-function row whose reason string says "timed out", duplicating the
summary and mislabelling functions that were never attempted.

This keeps the work in the reporting layer — no orchestrator state threading.

## Evidence (target repo kapow, default 300s budget)

| Target | Functions with results | Rows reading "total scan budget exceeded" | Report size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api` | 138 | 2,002 | 7,809 lines |
| `tools/kapow` | 387 | 1,380 | — |

93.5% of `api` rows carry no information beyond "not attempted". (Note: the 138 vs 2,002 figures are
functions-with-results vs unattempted-function rows, not two counts of the same set.)

**In-repo repro**: run `shatter scan` on any multi-file example directory with
`--timeout-total 5` to force budget exhaustion.

## Desired behavior

- Distinguish "attempted and interrupted" from "never attempted" in both wording and structure.
- Summarize never-attempted functions as a count rather than one row each. The full list is already
  available in the JSON report's skipped entries, so no new flag is needed for the human-readable
  report.
- State the effective budget, how much was consumed, and the next step (raise `--timeout-total` or
  narrow the target).

Target output shape, roughly:

```
Scan complete: 138 functions analyzed, 2,002 not attempted (total budget 300s exhausted)
  Raise --timeout-total or narrow the target to reach the remaining functions.
```

## Acceptance

- With a forced-exhaustion scan (`--timeout-total 5`) on an example directory, the report contains
  at most one summary line for never-attempted functions, not one row each.
- The report states the effective budget value and that it was exhausted.
- "timed out" is no longer used for functions that were never attempted.
- Functions that WERE attempted and interrupted mid-flight still report distinctly from those never
  attempted — a change that collapses both into "not attempted" does not pass.
- A `shatter-core` test covers the budget-exhausted rendering.

## In scope / out of scope

In scope: reporting of budget-exhausted scans.
Out of scope: changing the default budget, scan scheduling/prioritization, and scan performance —
all of which "how to get further" invites but none of which belong here.

## Size

Small — reporting-layer only, since the never-attempted state is already tracked.

## Artifacts

`kapow/shatter-review/2026-08-14/targets-sandboxed/api/stdout.txt`
close_reason:

Independent code review confirmed all acceptance criteria: single
summary line for never-attempted functions across all three rendering
surfaces (scan_orchestrator text, CLI Markdown, HTML), effective budget
value stated without misrepresenting an unconfigured budget as
exhausted, "timed out" wording fully removed from the never-attempted

Review found 2 Minor gaps: format_parallel_scan_report's Some(budget)

budget-caption formatting is near-duplicated across 4 call sites
(report.rs/html_templates.rs/render.rs/scan_orchestrator.rs) -- left
as-is per the review's own assessment that the sites format slightly
differently (Markdown/HTML-escaped/termimad) so triplication is

title: scan/explore/analyze implicitly run init and append to tracked .gitignore files
description:
## Problem

`scan`, `explore`, and `analyze` implicitly run `init` when `.shatter/` is absent, writing into the
user's repository without being asked — including appending to `.gitignore` files that are TRACKED
in git. Running a scan should not dirty someone's working tree.

The codebase already recognizes this concern: both call sites guard the implicit init with an
"external audit mode" escape. But that escape requires a three-flag combination, so a plain
`shatter scan . --all` still writes.

## Current code facts (verified 2026-08-14, engine @ ce1d0199)

- `shatter-cli/src/main.rs:38-48` — `maybe_implicit_init()`; prints
  `"No .shatter/ found — initializing project"` (`:43`) and calls `commands::init::run_init` (`:44`).
- Three call sites: `main.rs:242` (explore), `main.rs:402` (analyze), `main.rs:531` (scan).
- Existing guards: `explore_external_audit_mode` (`main.rs:240`) and `scan_external_audit_mode`
  (`main.rs:529`), both defined as `!outputs.is_empty() && no_cache && no_seeds`, with a comment
  saying such runs "must not write `.shatter/` into the audited project". `analyze` (`:402`) has no
  guard at all.
- The `.gitignore` block markers are `shatter-cli/src/generated_paths.rs:41` (`GITIGNORE_BEGIN`) and
  `:44` (`GITIGNORE_END`); `commands/init.rs:151` imports them.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd <repo-with-a-go-module-and-no-.shatter>
shatter scan . --all
```

```
No .shatter/ found — initializing project
  Created  .shatter/
  Created  .shatter/config.yaml  (detected language: go)
  Created  .gitignore  (4 generated path(s) ignored)
```

## Actual behavior

Across 12 module directories of target repo kapow in one run:

- 2 TRACKED `.gitignore` files modified (`tools/dbverify/.gitignore`, `tools/samplesql/.gitignore`)
- 10 new `.gitignore` files created
- 12 `.shatter/` directories created

The appended block is well-marked and benign in content:

```
# >>> shatter generated paths (managed by `shatter init`)
.shatter-cache/
.shatter/seeds/
shatter-artifacts/
.shatter/cache/
# <<< shatter generated paths
```

The content is not the objection. The objection is that a scan modified tracked files unbidden.

## Decision required before implementation

Pick ONE and state it in the issue before starting:

- **(a) Never write implicitly.** Use in-memory defaults; `.shatter/` is created only by an explicit
  `shatter init`. Cleanest contract, but changes first-run behavior for every existing caller.
- **(b) Keep implicit init, never touch tracked files.** Create `.shatter/` and new `.gitignore`
  files, but skip any `.gitignore` already tracked in git.
- **(c) Generalize the existing audit-mode guard** so it does not require the three-flag
  combination.

Recommendation: (b) as the minimum correctness fix, since it preserves first-run ergonomics while
making the tracked-file write impossible. (a) is the cleaner contract if a behavior change is
acceptable.

## Acceptance

- `shatter scan` (and `explore`, `analyze`) on a repo with no `.shatter/` never modifies a file that
  is tracked in git. Under (a), `git status` is entirely unchanged.
- The chosen behavior is consistent across all three call sites, including `analyze`, which is
  currently unguarded.
- A gauntlet or conformance case asserts the tree state after running on an uninitialized fixture.

## In scope / out of scope

In scope: the three `maybe_implicit_init` call sites and whether/what they write.
Out of scope: the content or format of `shatter init`'s `.gitignore` block; the behavior of an
explicit `shatter init`, which should keep writing exactly as it does today.

## Known dependents to check

Walkthrough and gauntlet scripts, and any README/SPEC text that assumes a bare `shatter scan` works
in an uninitialized directory.

## Size

Small under (b); medium under (a) because of doc and demo fallout.

## Artifacts

`kapow/shatter-review/2026-08-14/targets-sandboxed/*/stdout.txt`
close_reason:
Landed on main at 1f3cd59e3c55cde749f59635379b289819d53ce7 (merge commit; feature tip f141ff4074bedd2a8d397d5935329754e1df7711).

Gate evidence:
- cargo test -p shatter-core --lib scm:: -> 35/35 pass
- cargo test -p shatter-cli -> 558+ pass across all suites, including the
  new implicit_init_gitignore_test.rs end-to-end regression
- task walkthrough -> all steps passed

Chose option (b) from the issue: kept implicit init (first-run

git. Independent code review confirmed: is_path_tracked resolves
paths correctly relative to the target project dir (matches what a
human running git status there would see), no TOCTOU concern (single-

tracked-gitignore skip, all three call sites (explore/analyze/scan)

just string content. Review found 2 Minor items -- both closed before

instead of hand-rolling its own Command invocation, and the doc

spurious/transient git failure on a genuinely-tracked path (a narrow,
documented residual gap, not a correctness contract this function can
fully uphold).

title: One file's frontend error aborts the whole batch analyze, discarding all other files
description:
## Problem

`batch_analyze` returns `Err` on the first per-file frontend error, so one slow or broken file
discards analysis for every other file in the batch. A 500-file scan can return nothing because of
a single re-export barrel.

## Current code facts (verified 2026-08-14, engine @ ce1d0199)

- `shatter-core/src/batch_analyze.rs:159` —
  `pub async fn batch_analyze(...) -> Result<FunctionRegistry, BatchAnalyzeError>`.
  A single error short-circuits the whole call; there is no per-file error channel in the return
  type.
- `shatter-core/src/batch_analyze.rs:137-146` — the error enum:
  ```rust
  pub enum BatchAnalyzeError {
      #[error("frontend error for {file}: {source}")]
      Frontend { file: String, source: FrontendError },
      #[error("no frontend configured for language: {0:?}")]
      NoFrontend(Language),
  }
  ```
  `Frontend` already carries the offending `file`, so the information needed to record-and-continue
  is present; it is simply used to abort.

So the fix is localized to the core batch-analyze driver: accumulate per-file failures into the
returned registry (or a sibling failures list) instead of returning `Err` on the first one.

## Reproduction

Target repo kapow:

```bash
cd kapow/web && shatter scan . --all
```

```
[info] Discovered 500 source file(s) in /home/ketan/project/kapow/web
Error: batch analyze failed: frontend error for
  /home/ketan/project/kapow/web/src/components/search/index.ts: request timed out after 30s
```

Exit 1, zero results for the other 499 files. The offending file is a re-export barrel that exceeds
the 30s default request timeout.

**In-repo repro for the regression test**: prefer a `shatter-core` unit test with a stubbed frontend
that returns an error for one file in the batch — smaller and deterministic, unlike a
timing-dependent stall. The existing tests in `batch_analyze.rs` (around `:756`-`:925`) already
construct stub frontends and are the pattern to follow.

## Expected behavior

A per-file frontend error is recorded against that file, analysis continues for the rest, and the
summary reports how many files failed and why.

## Surface-level answers (recommendations, not blockers)

- **`FileFailure` fields**: `{ file: String, source: FrontendError }`, mirroring the existing
  `BatchAnalyzeError::Frontend` variant.
- **Exit code with `--fail-on-failures` unset**: exit 0. Per-file analyze failures are reported but
  do not fail the run unless the operator asks for a threshold — that matches the flag's existing
  opt-in shape.
- **`run.rs:349`**: print the failures and continue, same as scan. Silently dropping them would
  reintroduce the invisibility this issue is about.
- **`BatchAnalyzeError::Frontend`**: keep the variant if anything still returns it; delete it if
  nothing does. Do not keep a dead variant for compatibility — this is an internal core API.

## Acceptance

- A batch analyze of N files in which one errors returns analyses for the other N-1 — asserted on
  the count, not merely on non-emptiness.
- The failure is attributable to the specific file in the output.
- Exit-code behavior follows the existing `--fail-on-failures` flag
  (`shatter-cli/src/args.rs:994`, `fail_on_failures: Option<u32>` — a threshold count, so the
  natural mapping is that per-file analyze failures count toward it) rather than aborting
  unconditionally.
- A `shatter-core` test covers the mixed success/failure batch.
- The scan summary visibly reports the failure count — a change that fixes the core but silently
  drops failures at the CLI does not pass.

## Resolved: no protocol change is required

`batch_analyze` is core-internal. `BatchAnalyzeError` is a Rust-side enum in
`shatter-core/src/batch_analyze.rs`, and the per-file error it already carries comes from a normal
frontend response — the frontends report errors per request today, and the aggregation decision is
entirely core-side. Nothing new crosses the frontend boundary, so `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml`
needs no update and no cross-frontend work is implied.

Non-test call sites to update for a signature change (both in the CLI, both immediately adjacent to
their own reporting):

- `shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs:680`
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/run.rs:349`

## Recommended return shape

Return the failures alongside the registry rather than inside it — e.g.
`Result<BatchAnalyzeOutcome, BatchAnalyzeError>` where `BatchAnalyzeOutcome { registry, failures:
Vec<FileFailure> }`, keeping `BatchAnalyzeError` for whole-run failures such as
`NoFrontend(Language)`. This preserves the existing `FunctionRegistry` shape for all downstream
consumers and confines the change to the two call sites above.

## In scope / out of scope

In scope: `batch_analyze` continuing past per-file errors, and reporting them.
Out of scope: why the barrel file is slow, and whether the 30s request-timeout default should
change — file separately.

## Size

Small — one core function, a new outcome struct, two CLI call sites, and a unit test. No protocol or
cross-frontend work.

## Artifacts

`kapow/shatter-review/2026-08-14/targets-sandboxed/web/stderr.txt`
close_reason:
Landed on main at 9d1130ce (merge of str-z160s-batch-analyze-continue).

batch_analyze() now records per-file frontend failures (FileFailure) into
BatchAnalyzeOutcome{registry, failures} instead of aborting the whole batch
on the first error. scan.rs and run.rs surface the failures; scan's opt-in
--fail-on-failures/--failure-threshold policy (evaluate_failure_policy) was
extended with an extra_failures parameter so a file that never produced a
function-level attempt still counts toward the gate.

Gate evidence:
- cargo test -p shatter-core --lib: 3352/3352 pass (1 ignored)
- cargo test -p shatter-cli: all pass (scan_failure_policy.rs 4/4)
- cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go -p shatter-core -- --include-ignored: 23/23 pass
- task walkthrough: all steps passed
- Independent code review (general-purpose subagent): verdict "Merge with
  fixes"; both Important findings fixed (duplicated percentage/threshold
  math consolidated into evaluate_failure_policy; eprintln! -> log::warn!/
  log::error! to match file convention) and re-verified
- land-work-run-verifier.py: verifier_status=passed, 3 selected checks,
  0 unverified paths (re-run after a second rebase when main moved)
- land-work-verify-landing.py: sha_matches=true, tree_matches=true

title: Receiver is reused across iterations, so single-use methods report phantom panics
description:
## Problem

A method whose receiver is constructed once and then invoked repeatedly reports crashes that cannot
occur in production. A single-use object (one that closes a channel it owns, marks itself done, or
otherwise mutates terminal state) panics on every call after the first, and those panics are
reported as ordinary behavior classes with high sample counts — exactly the shape a reviewer would
file as a target-repo bug.

## Current code facts (verified 2026-08-14, engine @ ce1d0199)

- `shatter-go/protocol/receiver_construction.go` already contains the machinery to notice receivers
  that need real construction: `ReceiverRequiresConstruction` (`:11-30`) returns true when the
  receiver struct carries unexported reference-typed fields — explicitly "a map, channel, function,
  interface, or pointer type" (`:17`). Its result is wired through
  `PlanOptions.ReceiverRequiresConstruction` and the `synthesizeExecuteReceiverKind` path in
  `handler.go`, producing `UnsatisfiedRequirementKindRequiresConstruction` (`:28-30`).
- The reproducing type below has exactly that shape — an unexported `results` channel — so detection
  is expected to fire. What is NOT established is whether the constructed (or zero) receiver is
  rebuilt per iteration or reused across all iterations of a function. The evidence says reused.

## Smallest reproduction (evidence is external; an in-repo fixture is part of the work)

Observed in target repo kapow:

```go
// api/internal/searchindex/lifecycle.go:132-143
func (l *Lifecycle) run(ctx context.Context, command string, cfg Config) {
	defer close(l.results)

	if err := l.runBuild(ctx, command, cfg); err != nil {
		l.fail(err)
		l.results <- Result{Err: err}
		return
	}

	l.ready()
	l.results <- Result{}
}
```

`run` is called once per `Lifecycle` in production. Shatter called it 83 times, producing FOUR
reported classes, all identical:

```
Class 1 — throws panic: close of closed channel   (64 samples)
Class 2 — throws panic: close of closed channel   (8 samples)
Class 3 — throws panic: close of closed channel   (8 samples)
Class 4 — throws panic: close of closed channel   (3 samples)
```

Reported coverage 6/12 — i.e. the panic path is what got measured.

**First work item**: add an `examples/go/` fixture — roughly ten lines, a struct with an unexported
channel and a method doing `defer close(c)` — and confirm it reproduces. Required by acceptance
regardless of the fix chosen.

## Decision required before implementation (do not leave to the implementer)

- **(a) Reconstruct the receiver per iteration.** Correct-by-construction, but needs an answer for
  how a receiver with unexported reference fields is rebuilt — zero value does not match production,
  and constructor discovery is exactly what epic `str-mhinv` is about.
- **(b) Keep reuse, mark affected classes as order-dependent.** Cheaper, but needs a new spec field
  that does not exist today, and leaves the misleading coverage number in place.

Recommendation: (a), scoped to receivers that `ReceiverRequiresConstruction` already flags, so it
composes with `str-mhinv` rather than duplicating it. Confirm before starting.

## Acceptance

- The in-repo fixture does not produce a panic class attributable solely to receiver reuse.
- A Go frontend test covers per-iteration receiver state.
- `cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go` passes.
- If (b) is chosen instead, the spec field is added and `task parity` + `task conformance` pass.

## In scope / out of scope

In scope: Go receiver lifecycle across iterations of one function.
Out of scope: TypeScript and Rust equivalents (file siblings if the same reuse exists); constructor
discovery for arbitrary receiver types, which is epic `str-mhinv`; and the class-clustering defect
below.

## Split out, not part of this issue

Four separate classes were emitted for one identical panic message and one identical failure mode —
class clustering did not collapse them. Worth its own issue.

## Size

Medium under option (a) — bounded by reusing the existing `ReceiverRequiresConstruction` signal.

## Artifacts

`kapow/shatter-artifacts/files/api__internal__searchindex__lifecycle.go.json`

title: File-content seeding for structured-decode functions that read from a path, not a param
description:
## Background

str-b27zm added a `.shatter/config.yaml` `seeds` pool
(`functions.<glob>.seeds: map[string][]<document>`) that lets an operator
supply example YAML/JSON documents for a function **parameter** that gets
`json.Unmarshal`/`yaml.Unmarshal`'d into a struct. The Go planner
(`shatter-go/planner/param.go`) emits one Literal `ValuePlan` per seed
document for that parameter, so the explorer's candidate/mutation source has
several valid document shapes to execute instead of pure-random bytes.

That mechanism only helps when the structured document arrives **as the
function's own argument value**. str-b27zm's original acceptance criteria
named Zolem's `internal/fixture/loader.go` (`Load`, `loadOne`,
`loadFixturesYAML`) as the verification target, but those functions do not
fit the shape:

- `Load()` (no params — reads from receiver fields)
- `loadOne(dir string) (Fixture, *CompiledCELMatcher, bool, error)` — takes a
  **directory path**, then does
  `os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "meta.yaml"))` followed by
  `yaml.Unmarshal(metaData, &m)` internally
  (`~/project/zolem/internal/fixture/loader.go`, `loadOne`, around the
  `meta.yaml` read)
- `loadFixturesYAML(path string, fixtures []Fixture)` — same shape, takes a
  **file path**, reads and unmarshals internally

Seeding the `dir`/`path` string parameter with a YAML document is useless —
the parameter only names a filesystem location; the actual bytes decoded via
`yaml.Unmarshal` come from whatever is on disk at that path, which the
parameter-value seed pool has no way to influence. Reaching these functions'
decode-success branches requires a materially different mechanism: seeding
*file content* on the sandboxed filesystem at (or reachable from) the path
the function will read, not seeding a parameter value.

str-b27zm's team lead explicitly scoped this out of that issue's mechanism
(param-value seed pool) and asked for it to be filed separately rather than
implemented inline.

Zolem currently works around this specific case by hardcoding a fixed
existing directory as a `defaults` value for `loadOne`'s `dir` param
(pointing `dir` at a real pre-existing fixture directory on disk,
`testdata/fixtures/sample-anthropic`, in Zolem's `.shatter/config.yaml`)
rather than synthesizing content — which only ever exercises the one
fixture already on disk, not a pool of variants.

## Desired behavior

Some way to seed the *content* of one or more files a target function reads
during execution, so functions that read-then-decode from a path (rather
than decoding a direct parameter) can reach their decode-success/parse
branches with varied structured input, analogous to what str-b27zm's `seeds`
pool does for direct parameters.

## Scope

In scope:
- Design and implement a file-content seeding mechanism for at least the Go
  frontend (the frontend where this gap was found), covering the case where
  a function reads one or more files from a caller-controlled or
  caller-inferable path and decodes their contents.
- Verify end-to-end against a real low-coverage function that reads
  structured content from disk — `internal/fixture/loader.go`'s `loadOne`
  and/or `loadFixturesYAML` in the Zolem checkout (`~/project/zolem`) are
  reasonable real targets, replacing str-b27zm's now-moot use of these same
  functions as its own verification target.

Out of scope (explicitly, per str-b27zm's scoping decision):
- The parameter-value seed pool mechanism itself (already landed in
  str-b27zm — `shatter-go/config/loader.go` `FunctionConfig.Seeds`,
  `shatter-go/planner/param.go`).
- Schema-aware structured-input synthesis (tracked separately as str-4q7bd).

## Acceptance checks

- A function that reads one or more files from disk and decodes their
  content (e.g. via `os.ReadFile` + `yaml.Unmarshal`/`json.Unmarshal`) can be
  given one or more example file contents via `.shatter` config, keyed by
  some caller-resolvable notion of "which file" (e.g. a path pattern, or the
  parameter that names the path).
- The explorer's execution reaches decode-success branches gated on that
  file content that are otherwise unreachable (random bytes on disk, or a
  fixed single-fixture default, do not reach them).
- Verified end-to-end on `internal/fixture/loader.go` (`loadOne` and/or
  `loadFixturesYAML`) in the Zolem checkout, showing a measurable
  line/branch coverage lift versus the current single-fixture-default
  baseline.
- New/modified public functions have unit + property coverage per
  formal-methods-policy.

## Notes for the implementing agent

- This is a materially different mechanism from str-b27zm's parameter-value
  seed pool — it needs to intercept or pre-stage filesystem reads inside the
  target's execution sandbox, not just supply a `ValuePlan` for an argument.
  Expect this to touch the sandbox/execution-adapter layer
  (`shatter-go/sandbox/`, `shatter-go/launcher/`), not just the planner.
- Check for an existing sandbox file-staging mechanism before building a new
  one — grep `shatter-go/sandbox` and `shatter-go/launcher` for any existing
  "stage a file into the sandbox" primitive first.
- Open design questions to resolve during implementation (not pre-decided by
  this issue): (a) how a config entry names "which file" this seeds — a path
  pattern, the parameter that carries the path, or something else; (b)
  whether staged content is a single global stage or isolated per candidate
  execution when the explorer tries multiple seed variants across runs.
  Propose a design and confirm it before broad implementation, the same way
  str-b27zm's design was proposed and confirmed before code was written.
- Frontend parity: a Go-only landing is acceptable, matching str-b27zm's
  precedent. `.shatter/config.yaml`'s `seeds`/`defaults` sections are
  declared Go-only in `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml` (`hint_config_v1`) with
  no wire probe, since they are consumed entirely within the Go frontend
  before any protocol-visible `ValuePlan` is emitted; a file-content seeding
  mechanism can follow the same precedent unless it turns out to need a
  protocol-visible change, in which case update `protocol/parity-matrix.yaml`
  and run `task parity` + `task conformance` per this repo's frontend-parity
  contract.
- Coverage-lift acceptance check: no specific percentage threshold is
  prescribed. Capture the current baseline coverage for `loadOne`/
  `loadFixturesYAML` (e.g. via a focused Zolem scan) before implementing, the
  same way str-b27zm's own E2E test established a no-seed baseline
  (single-outcome branch only) to compare the seeded result against.

title: Schema-aware structured-input synthesis
description: Follow-up from str-ior1/str-2fui investigation (2026-06-15, Zolem 90% coverage goal), the longer-term complement to the seed-pool follow-up filed alongside this issue. When a function decodes a param/body into a known struct type (YAML/JSON unmarshal), synthesize a structured instance from the target struct's own schema (field types, tags) rather than relying solely on user-provided seed examples — generalizes str-e41w's HTTP request body synthesis approach to YAML/JSON struct decoders more broadly (loaders, selectors, config parsers). This is the dominant remaining lever for Zolem's LINE coverage gap (branch coverage was already lifted to 62% via budget fixes; line stayed at ~26% because function bodies sit behind these structured decodes).
acceptance_criteria: Given a function whose param type is decoded via YAML/JSON unmarshal into a struct with resolvable field types, the input generator synthesizes a structurally valid document (not just type-valid top-level bytes) that a decoder accepts, without requiring a user-provided seed. Verified end-to-end on at least one real low-coverage Zolem fixture loader/selector showing a measurable line coverage lift versus the seed-pool-only approach. New/modified public functions have appropriate unit + property coverage per formal-methods-policy.
notes:
Landed on main as merge commit 9fd5f38e (merging str-4q7bd-schema-struct-synth, feature head 410e0944).

Gate evidence (exact merge candidate, tree 3d93d09e):
  go build ./...                                           -> exit 0
  go vet ./...                                              -> exit 0
  go test ./... (shatter-go, 18 packages incl. protocol 476-332s under contention) -> exit 0
  cargo test --test e2e_concolic_go --include-ignored (21) -> exit 0
  task parity                                               -> exit 0 (16 golden checks)
  task conformance                                          -> exit 0 (42 checks)
  task test-standard                                        -> exit 0
  task smoke                                                -> exit 0
  land-work-run-verifier.py against merge preview           -> exit 0 (3 selected checks, 0 unverified paths)

Design (approved before implementation): detection (structdecode.go) mines json.Unmarshal/yaml.Unmarshal call sites where the byte-source resolves to a param (direct or one local alias) and the target resolves to a named struct; synthesis (structsynth.go) recursively walks the struct's TypeInfo (go/types) to build a structurally valid representative document, bounded depth + cycle guard; feeds into the existing str-b27zm SeedsByName -> Literal ValuePlan pipeline (new mergeStructDecodeSeeds), ranked after any operator-configured seed. Zero Rust-core/protocol.rs changes.

Acceptance criteria: new deterministic E2E fixture (examples/go/struct-schema-synth, no .shatter/config.yaml) + Rust E2E test prove structured-decode branches are reached with zero operator seeds. Real Zolem validation on NormalizeGeminiDiscovery (operator seed removed from a scratch config) showed 2 paths/47% line coverage on main (str-b27zm only) vs 4 paths/50% on this branch (adding schema synthesis) -- a measurable lift attributable specifically to synthesis, isolating pre-existing literal-mining.

Independent code review (forked before merge) found two real silent-failure bugs, both fixed with regression tests before landing: (1) unwrapToIdent accepted any single-arg function call as a type conversion, so a transform like decrypt(data) would wrongly attribute the decode site to the untransformed param and seed unusable plaintext -- fixed via info.Types[e.Fun].IsType() gating. (2) normalizeHintLiteral returned synthesized JSON object/array literals unquoted for plain string-family decode-source params, a wire-type mismatch against the 'string' TypeHint contract -- fixed by folding the plain-string family into the existing re-encoding branch. Filed str-fyouj (P3, non-blocking) for the review's third finding: structsynth.go's schema walker duplicates the analyzer's existing TypeInfo traversal.

Scope: narrower first slice as approved (excludes generics/interface{}/file-path-indirected decodes/*http.Request bodies). str-yd31w linked as the *http.Request fast-follow, not folded in.

Rebased twice during landing (real conflict resolved in shatter-go/planner/param.go against concurrently-landed str-ijtww's isHTTPRequestBodyParam->isSymbolicBodyParam rename; second rebase was a clean no-op replay against str-oqynx with no file overlap). Machine hit two full reboots during this landing (once mid-verification killing the original teammate process, once mid-wait on a later gate run) -- work survived both via already-pushed branch state; re-verified from scratch after each.

title: pickpackit: register WorkspaceWriter generator for Shatter axum adapter
description:
pickpackit's api/.shatter/config.yaml has no generators entry for the WorkspaceWriter custom Axum extractor (api/src/handlers/access.rs:181, impl FromRequestParts<AppState> for WorkspaceWriter), introduced by pickpackit commit ok4a0b843 (pp-lckn: replace per-handler workspace authz calls with structural extractors). shatter-rust/src/adapters.rs classify_axum_extractors only recognizes a fixed built-in extractor list; any other type name is classified Unsupported unless the seed input carries a __shatter_native replay marker produced by a config-registered generator (the same mechanism api/.shatter/config.yaml already uses for State and CurrentAccount, generators/pickpackit.rs). Without a WorkspaceWriter entry, all tags.rs handlers (and any other handler taking WorkspaceWriter) fail at explore time with 'unsupported: axum handler has unsupported extractor types: WorkspaceWriter'.

This is a pickpackit-repo config-only change (add a generators: WorkspaceWriter: generators/pickpackit.rs entry plus a native generator function returning a replayable WorkspaceWriter value), NOT a shatter-core/shatter-rust engine change. Mirror the existing CurrentAccount generator (generators/pickpackit.rs::CurrentAccount) as the pattern to follow.

Discovered while investigating str-6fjl, which turned out to be stale: the dispatch_failed/harness-compile scenario it described no longer reproduces because this extractor-classification failure now happens earlier in the pipeline. See str-6fjl's notes for the full repro trace.
notes: Swarm triage 2026-09-07 (str-qwua7.17): assignee cleared — issue is OPEN with no notes/started date and no evidence of active work (no branch found, not started). This is a pickpackit-repo config-only change, not shatter-core work.

title: shatter-core: diff_files/diff_files_range lack existence filter + subdir scoping (parallel path to changed_files fix)
description:
Follow-up from str-a2wkn (landed). GitProvider::changed_files was fixed to (a) scope tracked-diff output to the scan root via a '-- .' pathspec, matching ls-files's existing cwd-scoping, and (b) filter out paths that no longer exist on disk (covers rename-out-of-root, rename-into-root, and plain deletion with one rule).

diff_files and diff_files_range (shatter-core/src/scm.rs, used by 'scan --since'/'--until' in shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs) are structurally the same git-diff-based path and have the identical unfixed problem: git diff --name-only <range> can name a deleted or renamed-away file, and neither method applies an existence filter or a scoping pathspec. This is the parallel-code-path pattern CLAUDE.md calls out explicitly (random vs concolic, buildSymExpr vs buildSymExprWithFlow) -- the fix landed in changed_files but not its sibling feeding the same CLI surface.

Known concrete impact (from str-a2wkn's own testing): 'scan --since ... --until ...' run from a repo subdirectory with changes elsewhere currently hard-errors via strip_prefix(&root).map_err(...) treating an out-of-root path as fatal, rather than degrading gracefully like the --changed path now does.

Apply the same two contracts (subdir-scoped pathspec + existence filter) to diff_files/diff_files_range, or explicitly document why they differ if a caller genuinely needs repo-wide/nonexistent-inclusive semantics (e.g. str-81xiw diff-scoped exploration, which is in flight and should adopt the same contract when it lands).

title: shatter-rust: TypeInfo has no tuple variant, tuple param generation seeds objects the harness rejects
description:
Discovered during str-wg4jo (tuple-index overlay fix). shatter-rust's analyzer.rs convert_tuple maps a Rust tuple to TypeInfo::Object with field names "0"/"1" (no positional/tuple TypeInfo variant exists). input_gen::generate_object seeds tuple params as JSON objects ({"0":..,"1":..}), but the generated harness's serde_json::from_value::<(T,U)> deserialization requires a JSON array and rejects the object outright, so the function never executes and no constraints are ever recorded for Z3 to solve -- a tuple param yields 0 coverage today regardless of downstream overlay logic.

Reproduced empirically with fixture 'pub fn classify_pair(p: (i64,i64))':
  classify_pair({"0":0,"1":0}) -> throws runtime_error: input 0 deserialization failed: invalid type: map, expected a tuple of size 2
  0 paths, 0/2 branches

Fix needs a positional/tuple signal in TypeInfo plus array-shaped handling across generate_object / mutate_object / crossover_object / shrink_object / default_for_type / value_matches_type_shape -- materially broader than a single-function fix.

str-wg4jo (landed, commit b9813a24) fixed the overlay side (overlay_json_path now correctly places tuple-index constraint values into a JSON array when the declared type is positional) -- that fix is a PREREQUISITE for this one: without it, a solved constraint would clobber a correct array back into an object. No E2E tuple case exists yet for the same reason -- it would necessarily fail until the generation side lands here.

title: Cold-build-retry watchdog extension reads claim state at wrong time
description:
## Problem

str-slnr attempted to fix a pre-existing defect: the scan orchestrator's
cold-build retry (claims a doubled build budget via `claim_build_timeout_retry`
to warm the launcher cache for a layer, per str-cir6/str-kuc0) was
"structurally unreachable" because the outer join watchdog
(`shared_pool_task_watchdog`, sized for a single build attempt) always aborted
the retrying task mid-rebuild before the retry could complete.

The attempted fix (task_join_limit / build_timeout_retry_claimant, tracking
the claimant's progress_index so the joiner could extend the watchdog for
exactly that one task) was reverted after independent code review found it
doesn't reliably work: see shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs's join loop
in `parallel_scan_with_progress`.

## Root cause of the attempted fix's unreliability

The join loop drains `pending_handles` (a plain Vec) via `remove(0)` — strict
FIFO by submission order — awaiting each handle one at a time with
`tokio::time::timeout(join_limit, &mut handle)`. All tasks are spawned
concurrently up front (`tokio::spawn`), so by the time the joiner reaches
handle i in FIFO order, that task's own internal retry-claim event (which
happens inside its own async flow, roughly `build_timeout` after it started)
may or may not have occurred yet — this is a race entirely dependent on how
long the OTHER handles earlier in the FIFO queue took to join, not related to
task i's own timing at all.

`task_join_limit` was computed synchronously, once, at that arbitrary moment,
and the resulting timeout duration was then fixed for the entire await — never
re-checked. So:
- If the joiner reaches task i's handle BEFORE its claim event: the extension
  never applies, and the retrying task is aborted mid-rebuild exactly as
  before the fix (the defect this was meant to solve persists).
- If the joiner reaches it AFTER (by luck, because earlier handles were slow):
  the extension does apply, but doesn't account for time already elapsed
  while the joiner was busy elsewhere, so the effective budget is inconsistent
  run to run.

This was caught by independent code review (a fresh subagent given only the
diff and stated purpose) and independently verified by direct code reading of
the join loop before landing.

## Desired behavior

A correct fix needs the join loop restructured away from sequential FIFO
draining, e.g.:
- Join handles in completion order using `futures::stream::FuturesUnordered`
  instead of a Vec + `remove(0)`, so slow/hung tasks don't block visibility
  into other tasks' claim state.
- Or: compute each task's deadline from ITS OWN spawn time (pass a
  `tokio::time::Instant` deadline into the spawned task and have the task
  itself enforce it / signal back), rather than the external joiner guessing
  a timeout value once before it starts watching.
- Or: use `tokio::select!` with a periodic re-check of the claimant atomic
  while awaiting the handle, extending the effective deadline dynamically
  instead of computing it once up front.

Any of these must preserve the str-cir6/str-kuc0 invariant that the extension
applies to ONLY the single retry claimant, never to other tasks in the layer
(this part of the current unreliable implementation IS correct and tested —
see the `progress_index`-keyed claim design, which is fine to keep).

## Acceptance

- A test that reproduces the timing dependency (e.g. simulate a slow prior
  handle in the FIFO queue delaying when the joiner reaches the claimant's
  handle, and assert the claimant still gets its full extended budget
  regardless of that delay) — the current unit tests only exercise the pure
  `task_join_limit` function with the claim already recorded, which doesn't
  catch this class of bug.
- The cold-build retry can actually complete under realistic concurrent load
  (validate against the examples/go/local-admin-server fixture added by
  str-slnr, or a scenario specifically engineered to trigger BuildTimedOut on
  a task that isn't first in the FIFO queue).

## Related

str-slnr (parent investigation), str-cir6, str-kuc0 (established the
single-retry-per-layer invariant this must not violate).
notes: Held unmerged: independent code review during landing found the watchdog-extension claim is keyed only by progress_index, which is shared across replica tasks under --workers-per-fn > 1 (see str-3wv4h). Branch str-807vi-cold-build-retry-watchdog rebases cleanly, unit tests + full E2E pass, but this is an unsafe partial fix as-is. Holding until str-3wv4h decision (fix now vs. land as documented partial fix).
