title: Generator prefetch has no retry or concurrency limiting; fails under DB pool pressure
description:
Follow-up to str-mt78j (which fixed *attribution* only: a starved extractor now names the generator prefetch failure instead of reporting a bare "unsupported extractor types" error).

The underlying fragility remains: `crate::input_gen::prefetch_custom_values` issues `count` sequential `generate` requests per configured generator with no retry and no cross-function concurrency limit. Under a parallel scan (`--parallelism 6` x default generator pool max 8), a target whose generator opens a database connection exhausts the pool and every prefetch fails; the scan then degrades to built-in values for the whole run. Evidence: pickpackit full `shatter scan api/src --require-rust` produced 85 starved functions, while the same binary/config/database passed 11/11 focused, and low-pressure settings (SHATTER_PICKPACKIT_POOL_MAX=2 --parallelism 3) largely passed.

Scope:
- Retry a failed `generate` a bounded number of times with backoff before recording a prefetch failure.
- Bound concurrent generator prefetch across the scan (a semaphore sized from parallelism / generator pool config) so prefetch does not self-contend.
- Consider surfacing a run-level warnings section aggregating prefetch failures across functions (str-mt78j surfaces them per-function only).

Acceptance:
- A generator that fails transiently and succeeds on retry produces values (unit test with a scripted frontend that errors once then succeeds).
- Concurrency limiting is observable in a test (max in-flight generate requests <= configured bound).
- No regression in `cargo test -p shatter-core` or `cargo test --test e2e_concolic_rust`.

title: Element/field-level opaque-param stubs for handles nested in array/object params
description:
Follow-up to str-syj9b (typed opaque-param stub registry).

str-syj9b binds a stub for a parameter when a single stub can substitute the whole argument value: the handle directly, or wrapped in nullable/union (`Page | undefined`, `Page | Widget`), which `bindableStubKey` in `shatter-ts/src/analyzer.ts` unwraps. The execute-time overlay (`overlayStubInputs` in `handlers.ts`) replaces the entire positional argument with one recording proxy.

A registry-covered handle nested inside an `array`, `object` field, or `complex` inner — e.g. `locators: Locator[]`, `ctx: { page: Page }` — is currently SCRUBBED to a plain empty object (safe fallback: no crash, no stub) but NOT bound, because the whole-argument overlay cannot stand in for an array element or object field. This is documented in `shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md` (Opaque-Param Stub Registry Contract) and covered by a fallback test in `src/opaque-stub-analyzer.test.ts` ("scrubs but does NOT bind a handle nested in an array").

Scope: extend the binding + overlay to element/field-level. Likely needs a structured binding path (param index + nested path, mirroring Go's ReceiverFieldPlan `path`) and an overlay that walks the reconstructed argument to inject stubs at the bound sub-paths (arrays: fill N elements; object fields: set the field). Add analyzer detection for nested sentinels with their path, thread the path through the internal worker channel, and apply in `reconstruct`/overlay. Add unit + E2E coverage for `Locator[]` and `{ page: Page }`.

Value: optional/array Playwright params are plausible in real handler code (kapow); this closes the remaining coverage gap left by str-syj9b.

comments.author: Test User
comments.text: Open sub-case (from str-syj9b landing review): bindableStubKey binds a union to the FIRST opaque variant it finds, so a union of two distinct opaque handle types (e.g. Page | Locator) silently loses coverage of the second variant. Multi-opaque-variant unions need per-variant stub selection (or a way to explore each handle variant). Include in the element/field-level rework.

title: Random explorer path + protocol metadata for errors.Is/As sentinel coverage
description:
Follow-up to str-kvzh7 (which delivered the Go-only concolic/planner slice for errors.Is/As sentinel mining).

## Context

str-kvzh7 made synthetic error params satisfy `errors.Is(err, pkg.ErrX)` sentinel-comparison branches via the CONCOLIC/planner path only: the Go analyzer mines sentinel targets, the wrapper bakes a sentinel table and decodes a new `{"__complex_type":"error","sentinel":N}` input shape, and the planner emits those as Literal ValuePlans. That slice is Go-only and parity-neutral.

The issue's original acceptance said 'both explorer paths verified'. The RANDOM explorer path is NOT yet covered: shatter-core's `generate_error` (input_gen.rs) emits `{__complex_type:error, class, message}` and never a sentinel selector, because the Rust core does not know the per-param sentinel count.

## Change

1. Carry the sentinel count Go->core on the error param's `TypeInfo::Complex.metadata` map (already an existing #[serde(default)] map — additive key e.g. `sentinel_count`; NOT a new typed field, but generate_error's error-input shape gaining a `sentinel` field IS protocol-visible).
2. shatter-core input_gen.rs `generate_error`: when metadata carries sentinel_count > 0, sometimes emit `{__complex_type:error, sentinel:N}` for N in [0,count).
3. Verify the random explorer reaches all sentinel arms on the str-kvzh7 fixture.

## Protocol / parity

Protocol-visible: the error `__complex_type` wire shape gains an optional `sentinel` field, and Complex metadata gains `sentinel_count`. When picked up this needs the parity contract updated (shatter-go CLAUDE.md + protocol/parity-matrix.yaml) and `task parity` + `task conformance`. The index space MUST match the wrapper's baked table order from str-kvzh7 (both derive from the same deterministic MineErrorSentinels traversal).

## Depends on

str-kvzh7 (concolic slice + wrapper table + miner). No hard blockers otherwise.

title: Rust frontend: emit execute-response capability fields (scope_events, capture_truncation, discovered_dependencies, connection_failures, runtime_crypto_boundaries)
description: shatter-rust/src/protocol.rs::Response lacks five ExecuteResult fields the core defines (shatter-core/src/protocol.rs ExecuteResult): scope_events (scope-annotated trace for scope-aware path collapsing), capture_truncation (TruncationInfo for captured side effects), discovered_dependencies (deps found at execution time that static analysis missed), connection_failures (drives LiveFirst fallback), and runtime_crypto_boundaries (runtime-intercepted encrypt/decrypt APIs for boundary splitting). Core deserializes all via #[serde(default)] so absence is currently safe, but the Rust frontend can never contribute these capabilities. Tracked as parity divergence rust-execute-response-fields-partial in protocol/parity-matrix.yaml. Implementing requires the Rust execute/instrument path to produce each signal; see the TS/Go executors for the reference behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Rust Response carries and emits the five fields when the Rust execute path can produce them; parity-matrix rust-execute-response-fields-partial updated or resolved; e2e_concolic_rust covers at least scope_events emission.

title: Project health audit 2026-07-10
description:
# Project health audit 2026-07-10

## Problem

Shatter needs a current, evidence-backed assessment of code quality, documentation fidelity and organization, architecture, goal fulfillment, UI/CLI usability, test coverage, operational table stakes, build/test throughput, issue hygiene, and the agent/plugin workflows that allowed deficiencies to persist.

## Fixed Audit Target

Audit commit `e3614d3f51eddaa7c94d9b9bba96b0c23cc08eb4` from local `main` as observed on 2026-07-10. Create the audit branch directly from that commit so concurrent changes to `main` cannot alter the evidence base.

## Authoritative Scope

Run all ten phases defined in `.claude/skills/audit/SKILL.md`: build health; code-quality sampling; four-frontend protocol consistency; documentation accuracy with `SPEC.md` as the primary behavioral contract; Beads issue hygiene; core foundation review; agent effectiveness; contributor and end-user usability; closed-issue regression sampling; and programmatic session-transcript retrospective.

Answer these eight review questions explicitly: code well-formedness and quality; code/documentation agreement; documentation quality and organization; design quality; goal fulfillment; UI/CLI attractiveness, consistency, and ergonomics; unit/integration/E2E test depth; and end-user plus owner/operator table-stakes capability. Also assess `docs/stories`, build/test infrastructure thoroughness, and feedback-loop efficiency under multiple concurrent agents.

Do not fix product deficiencies during the audit.

## Required Checks and Sampling

Run and record command, exit status, wall time, material skips, and first useful failure evidence for: workspace `cargo test`; `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`; `(cd shatter-ts && npm test)` and `(cd shatter-ts && npx tsc --noEmit)`; `(cd shatter-go && go test ./...)` and `(cd shatter-go && go vet ./...)`; `task smoke`; `task e2e`; `task conformance`; documented docs/link/smoke gates discovered from `Taskfile.yml`, package manifests, and `.github/workflows`; and `bash demo/gauntlet.sh --auto --delay 0`. Check the gauntlet's documented binaries and sample inputs first; if unavailable, record the exact missing prerequisite rather than silently skipping it.

Resolve the installed storystore skill directory at `/home/ketan/.codex/plugins/cache/storystore/storystore/0.1.1/.codex-plugin/skills/`. Run its `stories-audit/scripts/audit.py --repo-root <audit-worktree> --strict --report-path /tmp/shatter-stories-audit-2026-07-10.md` and `stories-coverage/scripts/coverage.py --repo-root <audit-worktree> --strict --report-path /tmp/shatter-stories-coverage-2026-07-10.md`; if those script directories are absent, stop that check and report plugin layout failure as directed by the skills.

Allow up to 60 minutes per required full gate. Run each required gate once against the fixed worktree; rerun only when necessary to distinguish a shared-machine/resource transient from a deterministic result, and report both outcomes. A skip is allowed only for a named unavailable external dependency or environment capability and must remain an explicit audit gap.

For closed-issue regression sampling, check every closed P0/P1 issue and every closed bug returned by `bd`, plus a deterministic sample of up to 10 P2 features/tasks sorted by issue ID. Record the selection and evidence for each checked issue.

For performance, time the full gates and discover the smallest documented or runnable per-language, per-package, per-test, smoke, and E2E loops. Report duplicated compilation/bootstrap, shared-resource contention risks, cache isolation, and whether CI/local task graphs permit independent agents to avoid unrelated work. Causal claims must be labeled as inference unless directly demonstrated.

## External Agent-System Scope

Inspect only the installed artifacts active for this project: bento 1.2.1 launch/land/swarm/cross-check/issue-readiness/closure flows; bugshot plugin build `34b04dd10028c4e8e7f2525a228e20e2e3f1c9e7` and any project capture/baseline configuration; storystore 0.1.1 plus `docs/stories`; root/project `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`; and shared guidance under `/home/ketan/dotfiles/docs/`. Support findings with an exact artifact path and observable conflict, omission, repeated transcript pattern, or failed deterministic check. Project-local findings may become Shatter issues. Cross-repository findings may be filed only in an identified owning tracker; otherwise retain an issue-ready draft in the report.

For session evidence, select the Claude project directory whose encoded path resolves to `/home/ketan/project/shatter`, then programmatically parse every top-level `*.jsonl` transcript over 5 KiB, exactly as the audit skill requires. Report aggregate counts, distributions, anonymized session identifiers, and short paraphrased examples only. Do not reproduce secrets, environment values, full prompts, or verbatim transcript passages. The corpus has no date cutoff; record file count, byte count, earliest timestamp, and latest timestamp so the sample is reproducible.

## Severity and Filing Rules

P1 means broken required gates, incorrect/security-sensitive behavior, or verified regression. P2 means a material quality, design, documentation, testing, usability, operational, or throughput gap. P3 means polish. Before filing any P1/P2 item: search Beads by at least two distinctive keyword sets; record an existing issue when matched; otherwise pass the bento issue-readiness fresh-reviewer workflow. Tracker writes for confirmed findings are an explicit administrative exception to observation-only product work; uncertain findings remain report-only.

The completed report must pass `bento:cross-check` as a report artifact. Record reviewer mode, challenges, and disposition; the gate passes when every substantive challenge is either incorporated or explicitly rebutted with evidence.

Run Beads reads and writes from the primary checkout as required by the tracker skill. Audit-created finding issues must be visible in `bd show` before report cross-check so their IDs and disposition can be recorded. They remain open for future work. The audit issue itself remains in progress until the report branch is landed and pushed, then closes with the verified merge SHA under the Beads closure rule. Do not stage or commit `.beads` files on the audit branch; use the installed `bd` backend's normal persistence and verify final state with `bd show`/`bd stats`.

## Coordinated Work Packages

This task is an explicit single-run exception defined by `.claude/skills/audit/SKILL.md`: all ten phases produce one dated report and must not be fragmented into separate product-fix issues. Parallel agents perform bounded, read-only evidence packages and return findings to the lead: (1) code/design/protocol/foundation/testing depth; (2) documentation/SPEC/stories/UI/usability/table stakes; and (3) build/CI efficiency plus bento/bugshot/storystore/global-instruction/session evidence. The lead alone runs tracker mutations, full gates, issue-regression sampling, synthesis, report edits, cross-check, and landing. No subagent edits repository files or files issues.

## Deliverable

Commit only `audits/2026-07-10.md` on the audit branch, with prioritized evidence-linked findings, an executive and goal-fulfillment summary, build/test results and timings, a testing-depth assessment, table-stakes gaps, issue-ready external-system recommendations, and a deduplicated list of tracker issues created for confirmed P1/P2 work. Beads mutations are handled through `bd` and are not part of the report commit.

## Acceptance

- The report maps all ten named phases and eight named review questions to evidence, a finding, or a justified no-finding result, including `docs/stories` and the bounded external agent/plugin systems.
- Required quality gates and end-to-end checks are run with results, skipped coverage, and useful timing/throughput evidence recorded.
- The specified closed-issue sample is evidenced; every filed P1/P2 issue records deduplication and readiness review; the audit report records an independent cross-check and disposition before landing.

## Boundaries

In scope: observation, report authoring, tracker issue filing, and report landing. Out of scope: implementing any identified product, documentation, test, infrastructure, or agent-system fix.
acceptance_criteria: The dated audit report covers the fixed target and required matrix; all gates and sampling are evidenced; confirmed P1/P2 issues are deduplicated and readiness-reviewed; the report is cross-checked and landed.

title: TS execution isolation: require('fs') path-redirection shim for host-write default-deny opt-in
description:
Discovered from str-gg9v. Go and Rust frontends now isolate unsandboxed target
execution to a throwaway working directory (SHATTER_HOST_WRITE_DIR) when the
operator opts into --allow-host-writes / SHATTER_ALLOW_HOST_WRITES=1. The
TypeScript frontend is covered by the default-deny refusal gate (it still
refuses to run without a sandbox or opt-in) but has NO throwaway-directory
isolation once a user opts in: TS runs targets via vm.runInContext in the same
long-lived process, and main.ts dispatches requests CONCURRENTLY (fires
handleRequest without awaiting). A global process.chdir() around execution
would race across concurrent invocations and is unsafe -- confirmed by the
prior session's attempt, which broke relative source-path resolution when it
chdir'd the whole frontend process.

The correct fix is a new require('fs') path-redirection shim installed in the
sandbox: rewrite relative write paths (fs.writeFileSync, fs.open, etc.) to
resolve under SHATTER_HOST_WRITE_DIR instead of the process cwd, scoped
per-invocation (not a global chdir), so concurrent dispatches do not
interfere with each other.

Acceptance: a TS target using fs.writeFileSync with a relative path, executed
with --allow-host-writes and no OS sandbox, writes into the throwaway
directory (confirmed via SHATTER_HOST_WRITE_DIR), not the invoking repo, even
when other concurrent invocations are in flight against the same frontend
process.

Out of scope: OS-level sandboxing (existing backends cover that); the
default-deny refusal gate itself (already covers TS, unaffected by this).

title: TS host-write isolation: redirect relative fs writes to throwaway dir
description:
Follow-up from str-gg9v (default-deny host writes). str-gg9v added throwaway-temp-dir execution isolation for the Go and Rust frontends (the CLI exports SHATTER_HOST_WRITE_DIR and each subprocess frontend points target-execution cwd there). The TypeScript frontend is NOT covered and is protected only by the default-deny gate.

TS runs targets in-process via vm.runInContext (shatter-ts/src/executor.ts). Once a user opts into unsandboxed execution (--allow-host-writes), a target's relative-path fs writes still land in the caller cwd. Confirmed: explore on a TS fn calling fs.writeFileSync leaks input-named files into the invoking dir.

CONCURRENCY HAZARD (do not repeat): a global process.chdir(isolationDir) around execution is UNSAFE. shatter-ts/src/main.ts dispatches requests concurrently (rl.on('line') fires handleRequest without awaiting), so invocations overlap and race on the process-global cwd.

Correct approach: per-invocation path rewriting. Wrap the sandbox require('fs')/require('node:fs')/require('fs/promises') in createAdapterAwareRequire (executor.ts) so relative write paths are rewritten under SHATTER_HOST_WRITE_DIR (from env). No global chdir. Cover write/append/open/mkdir/rename/rm/createWriteStream + promises.* variants. Optionally record created files as file_write side effects.

Acceptance: with --allow-host-writes a TS target writing ./foo leaves no file in the invoking repo; analysis unaffected; safe under concurrent dispatch. Discovered-from: str-gg9v.

title: bin_only dispatch harness never imports user_code — local struct/enum params fail to compile
description:
The bin_only dispatch harness generator (`generate_dispatch_harness` in `shatter-rust/src/executor.rs`) emits parameter deserialization bindings with **bare** type names taken verbatim from the source signature (e.g. `let c: Color = serde_json::from_value(...)`), while qualifying function calls and globals as `user_code::...`. The user source is wrapped in `mod user_code { ... }`, so a bare local type name does not resolve, and the harness fails to compile with `error[E0425]: cannot find type <T> in this scope`.

This affects **any** function whose parameter is a locally-defined struct OR enum — not just enums. It surfaced during str-2nfoe (fieldless-enum `enum_values` extraction), where the analyzer output was correct but the acceptance E2E reached zero match arms because the harness never compiled. A plain struct param (`fn f(w: Widget)`) reproduces the identical failure.

str-2nfoe already shipped the minimal fix as a disclosed prerequisite: added `use crate::user_code::*;` to `generate_dispatch_harness`, mirroring the single-function `generate_harness` (which has always had it), plus a regression test `generate_dispatch_harness_imports_user_code_glob`. So the immediate compile break is resolved on `str-2nfoe-rust-enum-values`.

This follow-up exists for two reasons:
1. Track the general bug and its broader impact (local struct params, not only enums) for the record, since the fix landed under an enum-scoped issue.
2. Investigate the parallel-parity angle: `generate_harness` (single-function) vs `generate_dispatch_harness` (production bin_only path) diverged on this import for an unknown period. This is exactly the kind of parallel-code-path drift the project warns about (CLAUDE.md: random explorer vs concolic orchestrator, buildSymExpr vs buildSymExprWithFlow). Someone should grep both generators (and the axum variants at `generate_axum_harness` / `generate_axum_crate_harness`, plus `generate_crate_bridge_wrapper`) for other invariants present in one but missing in the other — e.g. derive injection, tokio wrapping, side-effect capture, stdout/stderr redirect, static-mut snapshotting.

Acceptance:
- Confirm the str-2nfoe fix covers the general struct-param case (add an executor-level E2E or unit exercise with a locally-defined struct param through bin_only if not already covered by the enum E2E).
- Audit `generate_harness` vs `generate_dispatch_harness` (and the axum/crate-bridge generators) for other one-sided invariants; file or fix any additional divergences found.
- Document the "both harness generators must import user_code and stay in parity" rule in shatter-rust/CLAUDE.md if the audit confirms it is load-bearing.

title: React native-alias seeding misses nested/duplicate react copies (pnpm version conflicts)
description: Follow-up from str-rzsej. The native React-alias seeding (installNativeReactAliasesForFile in shatter-ts/src/executor.ts) keys off the *target file's* own react resolution and seeds Module._cache at that resolved filename. A dependency that has its OWN nested/duplicate react copy (pnpm version-conflict layout, e.g. web/node_modules/.pnpm/react@18 vs .../react@19) resolves its transitive require('react') to a DIFFERENT filename that was never seeded, so the null-dispatcher crash can still occur for that dependency.
acceptance_criteria: A dependency with a nested duplicate react copy executes under the react-hook adapter without null-dispatcher crashes. Likely requires patching Module._load globally rather than seeding per resolved filename (out of scope for str-rzsej).

title: analysis cache not invalidated by frontend changes; --no-cache does not clear it
description:
## Symptom

.shatter-cache/analysis/ entries persist across frontend (analyzer) changes: after fixing TS array-ness recovery (str-ya5dx), focused pickpackit scans kept generating the OLD degraded inputs (entries: {}) until .shatter-cache/analysis was manually deleted — even with --no-cache, which evidently only bypasses the behavior-map cache. Cost: engine/frontend analyzer fixes silently don't take effect for previously-scanned files; measurement reruns attribute stale results to the new binary.

## Expected

The analysis cache key must include the analyzing frontend's identity (bundle hash / build id / version), so a frontend change invalidates prior analyses. --no-cache should bypass (or an explicit flag should clear) the analysis cache too.

## Evidence

2026-07-07 str-ya5dx validation: identical focused scan of web/src/domain/bundles.ts with a fixed frontend produced entries: {} until rm -rf .shatter-cache/analysis; afterwards all 9 fns behavioral (validateDraft error_only→10/16L 4/7B). Unit probe proved the new analyzer emits correct TypeInfo, isolating the cache as the only stale layer.

title: solved_object_path camelCases struct field segments — snake_case Rust fields get wrong overlay keys
description: shatter-core/src/orchestrator.rs (~:1162,1171-1187): solved_object_path runs every path segment through json_field_name, which camelCases snake_case (unit_price -> unitPrice). Rust serde-derive structs expect the raw snake_case key, so a Z3-solved field value lands under a key serde rejects (missing field unit_price) and the execution fails. Masked until now because Rust field constraints never reached the overlay (kind:unknown before the str-do53 field-chain lowering); the e2e fixture's single-word fields dodge it. Fix: skip conversion when the raw segment matches a declared TypeInfo::Object field name from ParamInfo, or make the conversion frontend-aware. Add a snake_case field to the cross-file e2e fixture as the regression. Found in str-do53 review (Important 2).

title: crate-backed dispatch harness lacks materialize_complex + emits unqualified struct-param types (E0425), no crate_bridge fallback
description:
Discovered during str-8euf. There are three Rust execute harness modes:
 1. pure bin-only (isolated: serde + serde_json only)
 2. crate-backed DISPATCH (generate_dispatch_harness, forwards user deps) —
    the mode a SAME-FILE struct-param fn routes to (execute_function_crate_backed)
 3. crate_bridge (generate_crate_bridge_wrapper) — has the materialize_complex
    call at executor.rs ~4209.

Two problems make mode 2 fail for a single-file struct/chrono param:

(a) mode 2 does NOT call shatter_rust_runtime::materialize_complex, so a
    struct with a chrono/uuid field can't deserialize (the {"__complex_type":...}
    envelope reaches chrono's serde unchanged).

(b) mode 2's generate_dispatch_harness references struct param types by BARE
    name, e.g. `let t: Trip = serde_json::from_value(...)`, but the user source
    is wrapped in `mod user_code`, so `Trip` is undefined:
      error[E0425]: cannot find type `Trip` in this scope
      2 + use crate::user_code::Trip;
    -> CompilationFailed. Routing only falls back to crate_bridge on
    ExecuteError::NonExecutable (executor.rs ~5316-5331), NOT on
    CompilationFailed, so it never reaches mode 3 where both problems are solved.

Reproduction: a single-file crate with `struct Trip { ..., starts_on: NaiveDate }`
and `fn classify_trip(t: Trip)` fails at execute; the SAME struct split into a
sibling domain.rs (so it routes to crate_bridge) executes fine (returns real
branch values). That is why the str-8euf e2e fixture is deliberately multi-file
(e2e_rust_chrono_naive_date_field_materializes_and_executes).

Fix direction: make materialize_complex + qualified (user_code::) struct/enum
type references consistent across all three harness modes; alternatively/also,
add CompilationFailed of the "cannot find type / DeserializeOwned" class to the
crate_bridge fallback trigger so single-file struct params degrade gracefully.

Evidence: executor.rs generate_dispatch_harness (~2596-3010, unqualified `{ty}`
param deser + no materialize_complex), routing at execute_function (~5288-5332),
materialize_complex wiring in the crate_bridge dispatch loop (~4209).
acceptance_criteria: A SINGLE-FILE crate whose target fn takes a same-file struct param (incl. one with chrono/uuid fields) executes with real coverage: (1) the crate-backed dispatch harness runs materialize_complex on inputs like crate_bridge does, and (2) references struct/enum param types via the user_code module (no E0425), OR the CompilationFailed of this class falls back to crate_bridge. Add a single-file struct-param e2e case reaching real coverage; the str-8euf chrono fixture no longer needs to be multi-file to route around this.

title: input generator emits invalid values for synthesized enum fields (unknown-variant deserialize failures)
description:
Discovered during str-8euf pickpackit validation. The by-reference domain
functions in pickpackit api/src/suggestions.rs now EXECUTE via crate_bridge
(post str-osr7 by-ref + str-8euf chrono/uuid materialization), but coverage is
capped because the input generator emits INVALID values for the synthesized
`Option<TripPurpose>` enum field of `Trip`.

Observed (real scan output, GLOB='**/suggestions.rs'):
  input 1 deserialization failed: unknown variant `zmmpjmttyedydn`, expected
    one of `personal`, `business`, `medical`, `family`, `other`
  input 1 deserialization failed: invalid type: integer `0`, expected string or map
  input 1 deserialization failed: invalid type: boolean `false`, expected string or map
  input 1 deserialization failed: unknown variant ` `, expected one of `personal`,...

Many generated inputs are wasted this way, so line coverage stalls:
  supply_applies_to_trip 46.2%, supplied_item_ids 14.3%, score_item 39.1%,
  suggested_packing_items 34.0% (5/5 completed, 14/14 branches, but low line%).

Root cause: the analyzer already synthesizes cross-file enums with their variant
list (str-do53 registry carries enum variants), but the input generator does not
draw the field value from those variants — it produces arbitrary strings /
ints / bools that the target enum's serde derive rejects at from_value time.

Fix direction: when generating a value for a field whose TypeInfo is a
synthesized enum, pick from the enum's known variants (unit variants -> the
variant name string; struct/tuple variants -> a map with recursively-generated
fields). The analyzer already carries the variants, so this is a generator-side
change.

Cross-language angle: the same contract applies to TS discriminated
unions / string-literal unions and Go const-enum (iota / string const) groups —
the generator should draw from the declared members in all three frontends.
Note in protocol/parity-matrix.yaml if the value-generation contract is made
explicit.

Evidence: shatter-core input_gen.rs (generate_value for enum/union TypeInfo);
analyzer enum synthesis (str-do53). Validation frontend = str-do53 worktree
(by-ref + chrono + field-path).
acceptance_criteria: For a fn consuming a struct with an enum field synthesized from a same-crate cross-file enum (e.g. pickpackit Trip.purpose: Option<TripPurpose>), generated inputs draw the enum field ONLY from the enum's real variants; a focused scan of api/src/suggestions.rs shows no 'unknown variant' / 'expected string or map' deserialize errors on the enum field and materially higher line coverage on the by-ref domain fns. Add generator unit coverage that a synthesized enum TypeInfo yields only valid variant values.
close_reason:
Landed on main (merge commit 9c2db7e0, merging str-mambd-enum-variant-gen).

Resolution summary: str-mambd's originally-scoped generator-side fix
(StringLiteral TypeInfo variant) was superseded by str-2nfoe's more general
enum_values field on TypeInfo::Union, which landed on main independently
after this issue was filed. This branch's remaining work re-targeted the
gaps str-2nfoe didn't close: the concolic solver (solver.rs) and the fuzzer
mutation strategy (mutate_union in input_gen.rs) both ignored enum_values,
so Z3-solved and mutation-sourced candidates for a closed-domain enum field
could still be invalid or fail to diversify across variants.

Gate evidence (task check run against the exact verified merge candidate,
a clean merge preview at base a6f81e96a83c6d08764bf6504917214fff7db38a):
  task check -> exit 0, zero FAIL/error lines in the full log

Additional evidence from this session:
  cargo build -p shatter-core --tests -> exit 0
  cargo test -p shatter-core --lib -> 3279 passed, 1 ignored
  cargo clippy -p shatter-core --lib --tests -- -D warnings -> no issues in changed files
  task e2e (full TS+Rust+Go E2E suite) -> 54/54 passed, including new
    regression test e2e_rust_nested_enum_field_domain_reaches_several_arms

Two transient environmental flakes were observed on an earlier, superseded
merge candidate under heavy concurrent system load (a Go test timeout in
shatter-go/protocol and a JS relative-timing perf assertion in
shatter-ts/src/executor.test.ts) -- both in files this change never
touches, and both confirmed passing in isolation. They did not recur on the
final task check run against the landed candidate.

title: [bug] flaky test: t07_multiple_conditions_independent_slots assumes scripted-oracle FIFO matches poll order
description:
### Problem

`t07_multiple_conditions_independent_slots` (shatter-core/tests/oracle_unit.rs, assertion at ~line 338) is flaky under load: observed 1 failure in 8 runs on a contended host (and a failure inside a `task core:test-ignored --force` gate run), passing standalone and on quiet re-runs.

### Mechanism (verified by reading the test, 2026-07-06)

The test fires two oracle queries for two different condition slots (`map.poll(100, ...)`, `map.poll(200, ...)`) against a `ScriptedOracle::new(vec![resp_a, resp_b])` that hands out scripted responses in FIFO order to whichever async query task reaches it first. The assertions then require slot 100 to have received `"a"` and slot 200 `"b"` — i.e. they assume the two spawned query tasks reach the oracle in poll order. Tokio provides no such ordering guarantee for two independent tasks; under scheduler pressure the second task can dequeue the first scripted response, and the assertion `v1 == Some(vec![json!("a")])` fails.

Failure evidence: `thread 't07_multiple_conditions_independent_slots' panicked at shatter-core/tests/oracle_unit.rs:338: assertion left == right failed`.

### Requested Behavior

Make the test order-independent while keeping its real assertions (two independent slots each eventually resolve; tokens accumulate):
- Either key the ScriptedOracle's responses by condition/prompt content (so each slot deterministically gets its own response), or
- assert on the SET of results across the two slots (`{v1, v2} == {["a"], ["b"]}`) plus `tokens_used == 30`, or
- serialize: fire and await slot 100's completion before polling slot 200 (mirroring how t06 sequences).

Whichever is chosen, the test name/comment should keep documenting that slots are independent.

### Acceptance

- `for i in $(seq 20); do cargo test -p shatter-core --test oracle_unit; done` green under parallel load (e.g. while another cargo build runs).
- No change to OracleSlotMap production code (test-only fix), unless reading it reveals the ordering is supposed to be guaranteed — in that case the bug is in the slot map and the fix belongs there instead (state which in the closing note).
notes: Landed on main at 5df14961 (merge commit) via bento:land-work. Gates: cargo test -p shatter-core --test oracle_unit 10/10 passed on rebased candidate; task test-standard exit 0; 100 consecutive runs under CPU contention 0 failures (per teammate). Independent review verdict: Ready to merge (Minor-only findings, no blocking issues).

title: shatter-core: honor enum_values in mutation, shrinking, repair/pool, and auto-mock paths
description:
### Problem

str-pjlc1 gave `TypeInfo::Union` an optional `enum_values` value domain, and (post cross-review) the random generator (`generate_random_value`/`generate_union`), `default_for_type`, `get_boundary_values`, the LLM prompt schema (`type_to_schema` emits JSON Schema `enum`), and the LLM response matcher (`type_matches`) all honor it. Remaining input-construction paths in shatter-core still treat domain-carrying unions as plain type unions, so they can produce off-domain values that validating decoders reject:

- `mutate_value`/`mutate_union` (shatter-core/src/input_gen.rs): mutation of a valid enum value wanders off-domain at the plain-union rate rather than mostly swapping between members.
- `shrink_candidates`/`shrink_union` (input_gen.rs): shrinking an enum value proposes base-variant shrinks ("" etc.) that can't reproduce the failure if the decode gate rejects them.
- Object repair / pool-literal row filling / boundary-search seeding (`boundary_search.rs`, `recursive.rs` object-field paths — grep `Union { variants, .. }` for arms that discard `enum_values`).
- `auto_mock.rs`: auto-mock return-value synthesis for enum-typed returns.

### Requested Behavior

Each path prefers `enum_values` when non-empty:
1. `mutate_union`: with a domain, mutate by swapping to a different domain member most of the time; keep a small off-domain probe rate consistent with `ENUM_INVALID_PROBE_PERCENT` (defined at the top of input_gen.rs, str-pjlc1).
2. `shrink_union`: shrink toward the FIRST domain member (canonical minimal), never to off-domain base-variant values, when a domain exists.
3. Sweep every `Union { variants, .. }` match arm in shatter-core (the `..` silently discards `enum_values`) and decide per site: honor the domain or document why not. Add `enum_values` to the destructuring at sites that honor it so future field additions surface as compile decisions, not silent drops.
4. `auto_mock` enum returns draw from the domain.

### Acceptance

- Unit tests per changed path (mutation stays mostly in-domain; shrink lands on a domain member; repaired/filled object fields with enum-typed fields carry valid members).
- `cargo test -p shatter-core` green; e2e_concolic_go enum tests still pass.
- A grep inventory in the commit message listing every `Union {` arm and its decision.

### Out of Scope

- Frontend emission work (str-knf0v TS, str-2nfoe Rust).
- Z3/concolic symbolic treatment of enum domains (domains as symbolic constraints — separate design).

title: config include/exclude globs silently no-op when scan root is a subdirectory of the project root
description:
## Symptom

pickpackit's shatter.config.json excludes web/src/**/*.test.tsx etc. A scan invoked as 'shatter scan web/src' matches exclude patterns against paths relative to the SCAN ROOT (features/x.test.tsx), so project-root-anchored patterns never match and are silently ignored. Visible symptom: 'shatter scan web/src --all' explored 154 test-file functions (fixtures/helpers are unexported, so default exported-only scans masked this). Same family as str-g9i4v (ls-files cwd-relative): path-anchoring inconsistencies between components.

## Expected

Config-file patterns should be anchored at the config file's directory (project root) regardless of scan root — or at minimum the mismatch should warn. CLI --include/--exclude are reasonably scan-root-relative, but config patterns written against the documented include set (web/src/**) must keep working for subdir scans.

## Workaround

Pass scan-root-relative CLI excludes: --exclude '**/*.test.*' --exclude '**/*.spec.*'.

## Notes

Consider a regression test: config with root-anchored exclude + scan of subdir → excluded file not discovered. Also audit include_patterns and .shatterignore/.gitignore matching for the same relativity bug (discovery.rs filter_file_list strips the scan root prefix before matching).
notes:
Landed on main at 19109785 (merge commit) via bento:land-work.

Root fix: find_project_config (shatter-core/config.rs) walks up from the scan directory to locate shatter.config.json; DiscoveryOptions gained per-set include_anchor/exclude_anchor (shatter-core/discovery.rs) so config-origin patterns match relative to the config dir rather than the scan root, while CLI --include/--exclude stay scan-root-relative.

Code review caught two parity/edge-case gaps in the original commit, both fixed before landing:
1. run_scope_from_project_config (shatter-cli/commands/run.rs) still used single-directory load_project_config instead of the new walk-up, so 'shatter run <subdir>' silently dropped a project-root config entirely (not just mis-anchored). Now uses find_project_config like scan.
2. 'scan --since X --until Y' moves discovery into a temp directory holding historical file contents, but the anchors still pointed at the original working tree's config dir, so strip_prefix always failed and anchoring silently no-op'd for that flag combination. The temp directory now mirrors the anchor->root nesting so anchors keep resolving; extracted into two pure, unit-tested helpers (until_anchor_mirror_prefix, until_temp_anchor).

Gate evidence (project verifier scripts/land_work_verifier.sh, run against the exact merge candidate):
  task test-standard -> passed
  task parity        -> passed
  task conformance    -> passed

Also ran directly: cargo test -p shatter-cli --bin shatter -> 544 passed; cargo test -p shatter-core --lib -> 3306 passed, 1 ignored; cargo clippy -p shatter-core -D warnings -> clean; cargo clippy -p shatter-cli --bin shatter -D warnings -> clean.

Filed non-blocking cleanup follow-up from code review: str-qxmlz (redundant double canonicalize of project_config_dir in main.rs).

title: shatter-go: prepare_id fast path must revalidate config-mock fingerprint
description:
### Problem

The Go frontend's explicit prepare_id fast path never revalidates config mocks against the current `.shatter/config.yaml`. `handleExecute` (shatter-go/protocol/handler.go) resolves the current mock set via `resolveExecMocks`, but when `req.PrepareID` names a still-valid cached harness, that harness — keyed by the mock fingerprint AT PREPARE TIME — is used without comparing fingerprints. Editing config mocks mid-session (between prepare and later executes) silently keeps the old substitutions active; only a new session or a stale/missing prepare_id picks up the change. Related: `resolveConfigPath` (same file, str-c8djq fix round) memoizes the "no config file exists" result per directory, so a config CREATED mid-session is also invisible until a new session.

### Current Code Facts (str-c8djq branch, verified 2026-07-05)

- `computePrepareID` includes `instrument.MockFingerprint(mocks)`, so a driver that re-prepares gets a fresh harness; the issue is only the execute-with-cached-id path.
- `preparedExecution` implementations store no record of the fingerprint they were built with (see `preparedHarnesses map[string]preparedExecution`).
- Practical exposure today is low: shatter CLI runs spawn a fresh frontend per explore, so config edits between runs are picked up. Mid-session edits matter for long-lived sessions (future watch mode, LSP-style integration).

### Requested Behavior

1. `preparedExecution` records the mock fingerprint (and config path + mtime/size) it was built under.
2. The explicit prepare_id path compares the current `MockFingerprint(resolveExecMocks(...))` to the stored one; on mismatch, log at INFO, invalidate the harness, and rebuild via the normal path (same flow as the existing `IsValid()` artifact check).
3. `resolveConfigPath` negative memo gains the same session-freshness note in shatter-go/CLAUDE.md, or (preferred) the path memo is revalidated with a single stat when a fingerprint mismatch is suspected.

### Acceptance

- Test: prepare → mutate injected config loader output → execute with the same prepare_id → new expression takes effect (harness rebuilt), old harness cleaned up.
- Hot path unaffected: fingerprint comparison uses the already-memoized config load (two stats per execute, no YAML re-parse) — assert no regression in the existing config-cache tests.

### Out of Scope

- TS/Rust frontends (no prepare-side config mocks yet).
- File-watcher based invalidation.
close_reason: Landed on main via merge f4536381 (str-hr40t-prepare-id-fingerprint, --no-ff). Gate evidence on exact merge candidate: task test-standard -> exit 0, zero failures. Round 1 independent review found one Important issue: rebuilt harness after fingerprint mismatch was never re-cached, causing rebuild-per-execute instead of rebuild-per-prepare_id. Fixed in commit 092a4dbf via recacheAfterMockChange flag re-registering the harness under the new fingerprint; also consolidated 3 of 4 eviction sites onto forgetPreparedHarness and added preparedTargetKey helper to prevent key-shape desync. Round 2 independent review verdict: Ready to merge, no remaining issues -- traced full control flow confirming correct re-registration, teardown skip, and no leak. Teammate's own gates: go test ./... 1432 pass, go vet clean, e2e_concolic_go 19/19, task smoke. Deliberately out of scope (documented in shatter-go/CLAUDE.md): resolveConfigPath negative-memo revalidation for configs created mid-session -- issue's own 'preferred' approach has no sound single-stat trigger, would restore the per-execute directory walk the memo exists to eliminate. Files: shatter-go/protocol/handler.go, prepared_launcher.go, 2 test files, shatter-go/CLAUDE.md.

title: shatter-go: single shared qualified-call walker for mock resolve + rewrite; cover generic instantiations
description:
### Problem

The Go mock-substitution feature (str-c8djq) has two structurally identical AST walkers that must agree exactly but share no code:

- `resolveMockSubstitutionScopes` (shatter-go/protocol/mock_resolve.go): funcStack push/pop over FuncDecl/FuncLit, CallExpr→SelectorExpr→Ident match on `ident.Name+"."+sel.Sel.Name`, records per-function allow-lists using `instrument.FuncKeyForDecl`.
- `RewriteMockCallSites` (shatter-go/instrument/mocksubst.go): the same traversal shape, performing the rewrite, gated by the recorded allow-lists.

Only `FuncKeyForDecl` is shared. If one walker's call-site recognition is extended (parenthesized selectors, chained selectors, a new AST shape) and the other isn't, `TypeResolved=true` with a stale allow-list means mocks silently stop applying (empty allow-list = rewrite nowhere) with no error and no test pinning the traversals together.

Known shared gap (consistent today only by parallel construction): generic instantiations `pkg.Func[T](...)` have `*ast.IndexExpr`/`*ast.IndexListExpr` as `CallExpr.Fun`, not `*ast.SelectorExpr` — neither side matches, so mocks never apply to generic package functions.

### Requested Behavior

1. Extract one shared traversal — e.g. `instrument.WalkQualifiedCalls(file *ast.File, visit func(enclosingFuncKey, qualifier, funcName string, call *ast.CallExpr, selIdent *ast.Ident))` — used by both the resolver and the rewriter, so the two passes cannot desync.
2. Handle generic instantiations in the shared walker (unwrap IndexExpr/IndexListExpr Fun to reach the SelectorExpr) — both sides gain it simultaneously.
3. A test that pins agreement: for a corpus of tricky sources (shadowing, package-scope literals, generics, nested literals), assert the resolver's recorded (funcKey, qualifier, funcName) set equals the set of sites the rewriter would consider.

### Current Code Facts (str-c8djq branch)

- Both walkers and `mockCallSiteAllowed` live as described above; `boundByFunc` shadow sets are computed only in the rewriter.
- `packageScopeFuncLitBoundNames` (added in the str-c8djq fix round) is rewriter-side only; the resolver doesn't need it (it has TypesInfo) but the shared walker must preserve both sides' guards.

### Out of Scope

- Package-identity mock keying (separate issue).
- Position-based rewriting across original/instrumented ASTs (would obsolete the allow-list model; note as a possible design direction in the issue discussion, not required).
close_reason: Landed on main via merge edf92876 (str-n0rtz-shared-call-walker, --no-ff). Gate evidence on exact merge candidate: task test-standard -> exit 101 with 1 flaky failure (scan_with_no_cache_no_seeds_does_not_dirty_target_project, 60s build-timeout under swarm CPU contention); confirmed environmental by isolated rerun -> passed in 45.21s (cargo test -p shatter-cli --test clean_scan_no_project_writes ... --test-threads=1). Diff is Go-only (shatter-go/instrument, shatter-go/protocol), unrelated to the flaky Go-build scan harness. Teammate's own pre-rebase gates: go test ./... 1422 pass, go vet clean, e2e_concolic_go 19/19, e2e_concolic_ts 24/24, e2e_concolic_rust 11/11. Independent code review verdict: Ready to merge, no Critical/Important findings. New shared instrument.WalkQualifiedCalls used by both resolver and rewriter; generics (IndexExpr/IndexListExpr) fully implemented; pinning test asserts bidirectional set-equality between resolver and rewriter candidate sets.

title: JSON-aware body generation for symbolic request bodies (struct-tag mining, structure-aware mutation)
description:
str-e41w review: the symbolic *http.Request body is a plain string slot — random/boundary mutation floods handlers with non-JSON that dies at the parse guard, and conditions on decoded struct fields resolve to symExpr unknown so Z3 cannot refine bodies. Coverage plateaus at parse-error/empty-object paths plus seeds/hints.

Directions (compose): (a) structure-aware mutation — when a param's plans include JSON-object seeds, mutate at the JSON level (add/remove/perturb fields); (b) known-answer harvesting — mine field names from the handler's decode-target struct tags (the analyzer already type-checks it) and synthesize candidate bodies; (c) longer term, flow from json.Unmarshal targets into branch conditions for real symbolic treatment. (b) is the cheapest high-leverage step and language-generic (struct tags / interface shapes exist in Go/TS/Rust/Java).

Acceptance (first slice, b): for a handler decoding into a struct with N tagged fields, the planner emits a generated body containing all tagged fields with type-appropriate values; zolem provider handlers gain body-field branches beyond the static seeds without config hints; extend examples/go/http-request-body with a field-gated branch not covered by static seeds.

comments.author: Test User
comments.text: Related: str-4q7bd (Schema-aware structured-input synthesis) is implementing a TypeInfo-walking synthesizer for the param-decode case (json/yaml.Unmarshal(paramBytes, &target) -> resolvable struct). Scoped to exclude *http.Request bodies to keep blast radius small (see str-4q7bd design). str-yd31w's HTTP-body struct-tag-mining case could reuse the same synthesizer as a fast-follow once str-4q7bd lands.

title: Symbolic method + config-overridable auth headers for synthesized *http.Request
description:
str-e41w fixed method=POST, path=/, and three stub auth headers (x-api-key, Authorization Bearer, x-goog-api-key) on synthesized requests. Consequences (str-e41w review):

1. Handlers gated on r.Method == GET (early 405 on non-GET) previously ran their body under the old GET fixed request; they now always take the 405 arm. Method should become a planned/symbolic dimension guarded to valid verbs (httptest.NewRequest panics on invalid ones).
2. The stub header set is baked into codegen: a handler rejecting ambiguous auth (both x-api-key and Authorization present) or validating token values 401s on every request with no config knob; a fourth convention (X-Auth-Token) needs a generator release. Make headers overridable via .shatter/config.yaml (hint_config_v1), keeping the current trio as defaults.

Design must stay language-generic (TS/Rust equivalents per parity-matrix go-symbolic-http-request-body resolution note).

Acceptance: method plannable/explored (at minimum GET/POST); header set overridable per project config; a GET-gated zolem admin handler reaches its GET arm again in a focused scan; parity divergence text updated.

title: Typed opaque-param stub registry: structurally-valid stubs for framework handles (Playwright Page/Locator)
description:
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo kapow.

#### Symptom

~20 kapow functions taking Playwright `Page`/`Locator` params fail every iteration with `page.locator is not a function` / `page.goto is not a function` etc. — the param gets a random object/primitive, and there is no mechanism to supply a structurally-valid stub.

#### Current Code Facts (verified 2026-07-01)

- shatter-ts opaque handling: `OPAQUE_NODE_TYPES` (analyzer.ts:1391) covers Node stdlib only; `INFRA_NPM_PACKAGES` (analyzer.ts:1459) covers DB/cloud SDKs; neither includes @playwright/test. Types marked `kind:"opaque"` (analyzer.ts:738/756/764) cause the core to skip, not stub.
- Go precedent to generalize: the runtimeval registry (shatter-go/runtimeval/registry.go) + `go_runtime_values` config supply runtime expressions per type at wrapper-build time; TS has no analogous per-type stub provider (browser-dom adapter stubs globals, not typed params).
- Config precedent: hint_config_v1 `generators` names registry entries per param (Go-only today).

#### Change

1. TS: add a per-type stub registry keyed by declared type name/module (e.g. `@playwright/test:Page`) that produces a structurally-valid stub object (methods returning stubs/resolved promises, recording calls); wire it where param values are materialized in the executor, before generic generation. Ship built-in entries for Playwright Page/Locator; make the registry user-extensible via `.shatter/config.yaml` (mirror go_runtime_values shape — kapow already uses that pattern for Go).
2. Analyzer: mark such params with their resolved module+type so the executor can look them up (extend the opaque marking with the source module instead of bare opaque).
3. Cross-language design note: this is the TS analogue of Go go_runtime_values / Rust native-replay generators; keep config schema language-neutral (type key + language-specific factory payload) so Java/C++ could adopt the same shape.

#### Design decisions (resolving reviewer questions)

- Core-skip boundary: IN scope to resolve. Preferred shape: the analyzer stops emitting bare `opaque` for registry-covered types (emits e.g. `{kind:"stubbed", module, type}` or keeps the param but flags it runtime-supplied, mirroring Go's `runtime_value` argument-plan kind which the wire already carries) so shatter-core needs no new generation arm; if a minimal core change proves unavoidable, keep it to "treat stub-flagged params as satisfiable" and no more.
- Stub semantics: lazily-generated recording Proxy — any method returns another stub/resolved-promise-of-stub, any property access returns a stub, with a small enumerated override map per registered type for calls whose RETURN VALUE feeds branches (e.g. locator().count() → rotate {0, 1, 3}; isVisible() → rotate {true,false}). Depth-bounded.
- Config sketch (frontend-local, no wire change):
  ```yaml
  ts_runtime_values:
    "@playwright/test:Page":
      stub: proxy            # built-in recording proxy
      overrides: { "locator.count": [0, 1, 3], "locator.isVisible": [true, false] }
  ```
  Name/shape may be adjusted to match hint_config_v1 conventions; parity matrix: declare as TS capability analogous to Go-only hint entries (config is frontend-local; no protocol change expected).

#### Out of scope

- Driving a real browser.
- Go/Rust changes (their registries exist; parity text update only if config schema is shared).
- Generic mock substitution (str-c8djq).

#### Acceptance

- Unit test: fixture function `async function go(page: Page)` with a branch on a page.locator result explores both branches with the stub (stub methods recorded).
- kapow validation: the `page.* is not a function` cluster (~20 fns) executes past the first page call in a re-run.
- Config-extensibility test: a user-defined stub entry in .shatter/config.yaml is honored for a custom type.
- TS suite + `task conformance` green; document in shatter-ts CLAUDE.md.
notes: Landed on main via merge commit 4dd96453 (branch str-syj9b-opaque-stub-registry, merged --no-ff, rebased onto str-nryo before landing). Gate evidence: task check (full quality suite) -> exit 0, run against the exact merge-preview candidate (tree fa435633 matched landed tree). Two independent code reviews: initial verdict 'Merge with fixes' (Important: nested opaque types in nullable/union/array silently lost stub binding) -> fixed via bindableStubKey unwrapping nullable/union, re-reviewed 'Ready to merge'. Follow-ups filed: str-zctg2 (element/field-level nested handle stubs, now also covers multi-opaque-variant unions per addendum comment). Minor non-blocking note: opaque-stub-registry.ts contains an intentional literal NUL byte in STUB_SENTINEL_LABEL_PREFIX (collision-proofing), which makes git treat the file as binary in diffs -- functionally fine (verified by passing gates) but hurts diff/review readability going forward; worth a lightweight follow-up to switch to a Symbol or out-of-band map if this file sees frequent changes.

title: Mine errors.Is/As sentinel targets so error-typed params can satisfy sentinel-comparison branches
description:
Repo: shatter (~/project/shatter). Found while raising coverage on target repo kapow.

### Symptom

Even once `error` params decode (see the `__complex_type:error` decode issue), `errors.New(message)` can never satisfy branches like `errors.Is(err, nl.ErrQuestionRequired)` — kapow `runErrorMessage` (api/internal/chat/service.go:536-543) switches on two sentinel comparisons plus default; only the default arm is reachable with synthetic errors.

### Current Code Facts (verified 2026-07-01)

- Sentinel candidates are Go *expression references* (`nl.ErrQuestionRequired`), not JSON literals — they must ride the runtime-value/`RuntimeValueExpr` wrapper path (shatter-go/wrapper/wrapper.go:549-557), with imports threaded per the str-gxjs.1 mechanism, not the JSON-literal path.
- The analyzer already walks the target body with full `TypesInfo` (shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go) — the arguments of `errors.Is`/`errors.As` calls are resolvable to package-level exported `Err*` var references.
- Planner param candidates come from `classifyParamFamily` (shatter-go/planner/param.go:250); there is no mechanism for expression-valued candidates today except the registry-backed `generators` config (config/loader.go) and `runtime_value` argument plans (see shatter-go CLAUDE.md, Feature Capability Parity: `argument_plans[].kind == runtime_value` with `literal` carrying the Go source expression).

### Change

1. Analyzer: for a function with an `error`-typed param, collect sentinel expressions used as the second argument of `errors.Is`/`errors.As` within the target body (exported references only; cap count). Attach to the param's value domain metadata.
2. Planner: for such params, emit candidates {nil, errors.New("shatter"), each mined sentinel} — sentinels as `runtime_value`-kind argument plans carrying the source expression + import.
3. Wrapper: materialize sentinel candidates via direct assignment (`var err error = nl.ErrQuestionRequired`) with imports threaded (str-gxjs.1 pattern).

Language portability: the same mining generalizes to TS (`instanceof`/error-class comparisons), Rust (matching on error enum variants), Java (exception classes in catch/instanceof), C++ (exception types) — mechanism = "mine comparison targets from the body, propose them as candidates".

### Scope statement

Go frontend only in this issue; the portability notes below are design constraints, not deliverables. Cap mined sentinels at 16 per param (log truncation at warn level).

### Depends on

- str-jn9r0 — the `__complex_type:error` decode fix (nil/errors.New arms).
- str-pjlc1 (enum value-domain TypeInfo plumbing) if it lands first — share its metadata field; otherwise carry the domain on the Go-side planner only (no protocol change needed since `runtime_value` argument plans already exist on the wire; see shatter-go CLAUDE.md Feature Capability Parity).

### Out of scope

- Unexported sentinels (cannot be referenced from generated wrapper package).
- errors.As target-type construction beyond sentinel vars.

### Acceptance

- Fixture: function switching on `errors.Is(err, pkgA.ErrOne)` / `errors.Is(err, pkgA.ErrTwo)` / default explores all three arms.
- kapow validation: `runErrorMessage` covers all switch arms. How to run: from ~/project/kapow, `SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=bwrap <binary> explore api/internal/chat/service.go --spec` (or the full set via `SHATTER=<binary> bash scripts/shatter-source-set.sh explore`).
- Unit + rapid property tests for the miner (no false positives on non-sentinel second args); Go E2E case per shatter-go CLAUDE.md rule; both explorer paths verified.
notes: Landed on main via merge commit b8d02ebe. Gate evidence (rerun against exact merge preview after rebase onto origin/main 432b4329): task test-standard (3273 unit + 24 e2e_concolic, 0 failed), task e2e-go (19/19 incl. e2e_go_error_sentinel_discovers_all_arms), task parity (16/16 golden checks), task conformance (42 checks, only known/allowlisted drift). Independent code review verdict 'merge with fixes' -- addressed both: documented %w wrapped-error scope limit in MineErrorSentinels doc comment + shatter-go/CLAUDE.md, added positive test for errors.As mining an exported package-level var target.

comments.author: Test User
comments.text: Scope narrowed (team-lead approved option B): this issue now delivers the GO-ONLY CONCOLIC/PLANNER slice — analyzer sentinel miner, wrapper baked sentinel table + {"__complex_type":"error","sentinel":N} decode, planner emitting sentinel candidates as Literal ValuePlans. Parity-neutral, no wire change. The 'both explorer paths verified' criterion is split: the RANDOM explorer path + protocol metadata (generate_error sentinel field, Complex.metadata sentinel_count) is tracked in follow-up str-3lsgf. Rationale: str-gxjs.1/str-r2q7 moved runtime_value resolution to build-time (baked once, materializes to null per-execution), invalidating the issue's original runtime_value mechanism; sentinels need pointer identity so errors.New can't satisfy errors.Is — hence the wrapper-baked-table + input-selector design.

title: shatter-advise: detect inline-SQL handlers as shatter-friendliness opportunity
description:
When scanning a codebase, `shatter-advise` should detect handlers (or other
entry-point functions) that embed SQL queries inline rather than delegating to a
repository / DAO layer, and surface this as a shatter-friendliness opportunity.
Inline-SQL handlers present two problems for concolic coverage:
- **Fat entry points.** The handler mixes auth/validation logic with DB access.
  Shatter must exercise the full HTTP stack to reach any branch that is purely
  about DB result shapes (empty row, FK violation, stale data). A DAO function
  testing the query in isolation would expose those branches directly.
- **Generator complexity.** Generators must reconstruct the entire FK chain
  (account → workspace → entity → child) just to exercise one branch in one
  handler. A repository function would need only the minimal fixture for its query.
For each handler that embeds a SQL literal directly — detected via `sqlx::query`,
`sqlx::query_scalar`, `sqlx::query_as` in the handler body itself (not in a named
helper) — shatter-advise should flag it as `shatter_friendliness: low` with reason
`inline_sql` and suggest extracting DB access into a repository function.
Rust-specific detector initially; the same pattern applies in Go (`db.Query` in
handlers) and TypeScript (`prisma.*` calls in route handlers).
notes: Landed on shatter-agents main at 6ed8ffd via bento:land-work (git merge --no-ff, no PR, per that repo's convention). Gates: 15/15 unit tests, build-plugins + check-plugins-clean clean, py_compile clean, pre-commit/pre-push hooks verified passing (bd hooks run, exit 0). Independent review found a Critical bug (bodyless fn signature misattribution) which was fixed with regression tests before landing; verified independently before merge.

title: diff-explore CLI shell
description:
# diff-explore CLI shell

## Problem

Users need a stable command surface for diff-scoped exploration that does not collide with existing snapshot comparison.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-cli/src/args.rs` already defines `CliCommand::Diff { snapshot, current, json }` for `shatter diff <snapshot> <current>`.
- `scan --changed` / `scan --since` already narrow at file granularity, but not function granularity.

## Required Behavior

Add a new v1 command surface:

```text
shatter diff-explore [<base-ref>] [--staged] [--include-tests] [--format json|text] [--output-dir <path>]
```

Rules:

- Existing `shatter diff <snapshot> <current>` remains unchanged.
- `<base-ref>` and `--staged` conflict.
- If `<base-ref>` is omitted and `--staged` is not set, resolve in order: upstream merge-base, local `main`, local `master`, then `HEAD~1`.
- `--format` defaults to `text`.
- `--output-dir` defaults under `.shatter/diff-run/<timestamp>/`.

Do not add `--jobs` in this issue; concurrency can be a follow-up after sequential behavior is correct.

## Acceptance Checks

- CLI parses `shatter diff-explore main`.
- CLI parses `shatter diff-explore --staged`.
- CLI rejects `shatter diff-explore main --staged` with a configuration error.
- Existing `shatter diff old.json new.json` tests still pass unchanged.
- Help text makes clear this is git diff-scoped exploration, not snapshot comparison.

title: diff-explore runs selected targets
description:
# diff-explore runs selected targets

## Problem

After diff hunks are mapped to functions, Shatter needs to explore exactly those selected function targets through existing execution machinery.

## Required Behavior

Wire `shatter diff-explore` target selection into existing function-level exploration:

- discover/analyze supported changed files with existing frontend paths,
- respect default test-function exclusion unless `--include-tests` is set,
- explore only functions selected by the diff mapper,
- produce one per-function spec artifact for each attempted target,
- classify attempted target outcomes as `explored`, `partial`, `unsupported`, or `error_only` using existing exploration results where possible.

Keep this CLI/core orchestration only. Do not add frontend protocol fields.

## Acceptance Checks

- Fixture with five Go functions and edits inside two function bodies attempts exactly those two functions.
- Fixture with one changed test function excludes it by default and includes it with `--include-tests`.
- A new supported source file attempts all default-included functions in that file.
- An unsupported selected function records an attempted target outcome rather than a file-level skip.

title: diff-explore summary and exit codes
description:
# diff-explore summary and exit codes

## Problem

Diff-scoped exploration needs machine-readable output for hooks and CI, plus exit codes that distinguish unsupported functions from empty diffs and configuration errors.

## Required Behavior

Write `<output-dir>/summary.json` for every `shatter diff-explore` run and emit the same JSON to stdout when `--format json` is set.

Minimum summary fields:

- `base_ref`
- `head_ref`
- `staged`
- `files_skipped`
- `functions_found`
- `functions_attempted`
- `outcomes`
- `targets[] { file, function, outcome, cases_found, spec_path, reason? }`
- `skipped[] { file, reason }`

`spec_path` must be relative to the git root.

Exit codes:

- `0`: all attempted targets are `explored` or `partial`.
- `1`: any attempted target is `unsupported` or `error_only`.
- `2`: no function targets were found after diff parsing and skips.
- `3`: CLI/config/environment error.

## Acceptance Checks

- `--format json --output-dir <dir>` writes parseable `<dir>/summary.json` and emits structurally equivalent JSON on stdout.
- A diff touching only unsupported files exits 2 and records skip reasons.
- A run with one unsupported attempted function exits 1.
- Repeated runs against the same diff are deterministic after ignoring timestamped paths.

title: Diff hunk function mapper
description:
# Diff hunk function mapper

## Problem

Shatter has file-level changed filtering, but no reusable way to map a git diff hunk to the functions that changed. This is the foundation for diff-scoped exploration.

## Current Code Facts

- `shatter-core/src/scm.rs` already shells out to git for changed-file queries and uses three-dot semantics for `diff_files` / `diff_files_range`.
- `shatter-core/src/batch_analyze.rs::FunctionRegistry` stores `FunctionEntry { file_path, name, start_line, end_line, exported, ... }` and preserves full `FunctionAnalysis` by qualified name.

## Required Behavior

Add a small internal diff-hunk model and mapper that:

- obtains unified-zero git diff hunks for `<base-ref>...HEAD` and `--cached` staged mode,
- records changed new-file ranges for additions/modifications,
- records enough old/new range information to handle deletion-only hunks inside existing functions,
- reports file-level skips for deleted, binary, submodule, and unsupported-language files,
- selects functions by intersecting hunk ranges with existing frontend-reported function line ranges.

Deletion-only hunks must not be dropped. For v1, map a deletion-only hunk to the enclosing function by using the hunk header's new-file anchor line and neighboring new-file range after deletion.

## Acceptance Checks

- A hunk with added lines inside a function maps to that function.
- A deletion-only hunk inside a function maps to that function.
- A deleted file produces a `file_deleted` skip and no function target.
- Binary/submodule diffs produce file-level skips.
- Tests cover the mapper without running full exploration.
notes: Landed on main (0a3c162b). Gate evidence: cargo test -p shatter-core --lib scm:: (24 passed) run against the exact merge candidate. Independent code review found and this branch fixed a deletion-only-hunk-at-file-top edge case (new_start=0).

title: materialize_seed_for_plan drops hint seeds for functions with context.Context params
description:
## Symptom

`.shatter/config.yaml` `defaults:` hints for string/byte parameters are silently ignored for functions that also take a `context.Context` (or any other parameter resolved as `RuntimeValue` by the planner).

`HTTPChatCompletion(ctx context.Context, upstream string, ...)` with `upstream: "http://localhost:11434"` hint → all explored paths use `upstream=""`.

## Root cause

`materialize_value()` in `shatter-core/src/planner_consumer.rs` returns `None` for `ValuePlanKind::RuntimeValue`. `materialize_seed_for_plan` uses `?` on the result, so when the planner emits a `runtime_value` plan for `ctx` (Go wrapper bakes `context.Background()` at compile time), the whole seed is dropped — taking the valid `Literal` plans for `upstream` and `model` with it.

The actual input array already has `null` at the ctx slot confirming that passing `null` for RuntimeValue params is correct.

## Fix

Emit `Value::Null` for `RuntimeValue` in `materialize_value` so Literal/Zero plans for sibling params survive.

## Files

- `shatter-core/src/planner_consumer.rs` — `materialize_value`, line ~334
close_reason: Already fixed on main via str-r2q7 — materialize_value emits Value::Null for RuntimeValue so sibling Literal/Zero plans survive materialization. Verified in shatter-core/src/planner_consumer.rs.

title: Epic: Diff-scoped exploration
description:
# Epic: Diff-scoped exploration

Migrated from mistakenly filed shatter-agents issue `sa-tyb`.

Add first-class git diff-scoped exploration to Shatter so pre-commit and PR-CI workflows can explore only functions affected by a diff instead of re-running a full project or file-level scan.

Current constraints:

- `shatter-cli/src/args.rs` already defines `shatter diff <snapshot> <current>` for snapshot comparison. Do not repurpose that command incompatibly.
- Use `shatter diff-explore` as the v1 command name unless maintainers choose an unambiguous `explore` submode before implementation starts.
- Reuse existing SCM, discovery, frontend analysis, `FunctionRegistry`, and function-level exploration machinery. Do not add a separate regex-only language parser for diff mode.
- Keep frontend protocol/wire output unchanged for v1.

Intended v1 flow:

1. Resolve a git diff source (`<base-ref>` or `--staged`).
2. Parse changed hunks, including deletion-only hunks.
3. Analyze supported changed files with existing frontends.
4. Map hunk line ranges to frontend-reported function ranges.
5. Explore the selected functions.
6. Write a stable machine-readable summary plus per-function artifacts.

Out of scope for this epic: transitive caller impact, non-git VCS, new frontend protocol fields, and replacing the existing snapshot-comparison `shatter diff` command.

Do not repurpose that command incompatibly", and they use `shatter diff-explore` as the v1 name. That constraint is going away. Under D2 the snapshot `shatter diff` command and its Snapshot module are being removed, and `shatter spec-diff` becomes the regression tool, in **<retire-snapshot-diff id>**. That issue adds no alias or shim, so once it lands the `diff` subcommand name is unused.

Whether diff-scoped exploration takes the `diff` name or keeps `diff-explore` is for this epic to decide. D2 and the retirement issue deliberately do not decide it. Nothing in this epic's scope changes. If the epic does choose `diff`, note that the shatter-agents plugin's `shatter-diff` skill currently documents a nonexistent `shatter diff --staged` (being withdrawn in shatter-agents withdraw-shatter-diff-skill). Any future plugin guidance should follow whatever name this epic picks.

title: Rust prepare conformance timeout
description:
## Symptom

`task conformance` exits 201. Root cause: `rust/prepare_supported_rust` returns no response (timeout or crash). This single missing response desyncs req/resp IDs, cascading into ~15 additional "expected N got N-1" failures — masking the real root from the summary.

Observed during swarm on 2026-06-18 when tm-2ud1 verified str-2ud1 gates. The failure reproduces on a clean main tree (pre-existing).

## Suspected cause

Plain `prepare` command (no plan field) to the Rust frontend times out or crashes during conformance harness execution — likely a compile-time or startup timeout when the Rust frontend is invoked cold.

## Acceptance

`task conformance` exits 0, or the Rust prepare case at minimum returns a valid response without timing out.

## Related

- str-2ud1 (closed): conformance failure was pre-existing when verifying prepare.plan metadata — not introduced by that change
- str-qe9pp: separate Rust parity/conformance drift (handshake golden mismatch)
notes:
Landed on main at ac80c831 (merge of str-uoclg-rust-prepare-conformance-timeout). Fix: added timeout_s: 240 override + comment to prepare_supported_rust in protocol/conformance/conformance_cases.yaml, mirroring the existing execute_outcome_shape_rust pattern for cold-cargo-build cost.

Gate evidence:
- task conformance -> PASS (4 frontends x 18 cases = 42 checks, all passed)
- task smoke -> PASS (one retry past an unrelated Go-frontend explore timeout flake, unrelated to this change)
- land-work-run-verifier.py against merge preview -> exit 0, verifier_status=passed, selected_check_count=3, unverified_paths=[]
- Independent code review -> Ready to merge, no issues (Critical/Important/Minor)
- land-work-verify-landing.py -> sha_matches=true, tree_matches=true (landed tree 06016e6 matches verified preview)

Test-config-only change (protocol/conformance/conformance_cases.yaml, +4 lines); no protocol-visible frontend behavior changed, no parity-matrix update required.

title: Agent rules drift lint
description:
## Problem

The audit found drift in the agent system itself. Project instructions duplicate the RTK block, the local audit skill contains an invalid `bd epic list` command, and audit/issue-readiness/launch-work instructions are not fully aligned about when an audit may write reports or file issues. These failures affect agent behavior even when project code is correct.

Because agent rules, local skills, first-party plugins, and global dotfiles all influence Shatter work, they need a lightweight lint/check path instead of relying on occasional manual review.

## Current Code Facts

- AGENTS.md contains the RTK instruction block twice.
- `.claude/skills/audit/SKILL.md` instructs `bd epic list`, but the installed Beads command exposes `bd epic status` and rejects `bd epic list`.
- The audit skill says observation-only, then also instructs writing an audit report, creating issues, committing, and pushing.
- The issue-readiness skill requires a fresh issue reviewer before filing tracker issues.
- The launch-work policy requires a linked worktree before repo file edits, including docs and config edits.

## Desired Behavior

Add an agent-rule drift lint that validates project-local agent instructions and selected first-party/global instruction references for known failure classes:

- duplicated generated instruction blocks;
- invalid command examples for tools such as `bd` and `task`;
- missing launch-work mention before report-writing workflows;
- issue-filing workflows that omit issue-readiness review;
- stale references to deprecated documentation paths or plugin names.

## First Scan Set

Start with this bounded scan set:

- `AGENTS.md`;
- `.claude/skills/audit/SKILL.md`;
- the project-local `.claude/skills/pre-completion/SKILL.md`;
- installed bento skill instructions for launch-work and issue-readiness;
- shared dotfiles agent-guidance files that are directly loaded by Shatter workflows.

If a referenced upstream instruction lives outside the Shatter repo, the check
may report it as an external finding instead of editing it locally.

## Required Trigger

The lint must be runnable by a command, such as `task agent-rules-check` or `scripts/validate-agent-rules`, and wired into the scheduled drift patrol. It should also be named in the audit skill or agent completion guidance so agent-system drift is checked during governance audits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The lint detects the current duplicated RTK block in AGENTS.md.
- The lint detects at least one invalid documented command example, using `bd epic list` as the regression case.
- The lint or accompanying policy flags audit workflows that both claim read-only mode and require repo writes without naming launch-work/worktree requirements.
- The check is included in the scheduled drift patrol or equivalent recurring trigger.
- Follow-up notes identify which fixes belong in Shatter-local files versus upstream first-party plugin/global instruction repos.

## Out of Scope

- Rewriting every global agent instruction.
- Building a complete natural-language verifier for all policies.
- Changing plugin release processes except where needed to make this lint actionable.
notes:
## Problem
str-u394l.4 (open since 2026-06-17) describes the lint in terms of the June failure classes. The 2026-09-04 audit found new, mechanically checkable drift that the lint should cover, and confirms none of it is caught by any existing gate.

## Current code facts
