title: Go wrapper imports for Zolem
description: Zolem full Shatter scans fail during Go wrapper compilation because generated wrappers reference qualified parameter types such as context.Context, io.Writer, and package-local imported types without importing their packages. The same scan also shows stale zero-argument constructor calls for constructors whose signatures now require parameters, causing every attempted Zolem function to fail before execution.
acceptance_criteria: Zolem's make shatter no longer fails from generated Go wrapper compile errors for missing imports or wrong constructor arity.
notes: Implemented on branch str-iylc-go-wrapper-imports-zolem: wrapper discovery hashes now include per-target import metadata so stale generated wrappers are invalidated, and wrapper target import collection no longer records result-only selector packages that the generated source never names. Verified go test ./wrapper ./planner ./protocol, cargo build --release, and Zolem make shatter with the rebuilt binary.

title: Scan ID qualified-key review
description: Review compute_scan_id after qualified_id is exposed on the wire. Decide whether scan_id derivation should include the same stable qualified key so checkpoint and resume behavior remains robust when duplicate names or receiver-qualified methods are present.
acceptance_criteria: The scan_id derivation decision is documented in code or tests. If behavior changes, checkpoint/resume regression tests cover duplicate named functions. If behavior stays path-based, tests or notes explain why the existing key remains stable enough.

title: Explore CLI report conflates branch_count with unique_paths
description:
shatter-core/src/report.rs:404-405 sets branch_count and branches_covered both from exploration.unique_paths, conflating path enumeration with branch coverage. Affects the standalone explore CLI's final report (frontend-agnostic). The scan path is unaffected — it goes through scan_orchestrator which populates branch_count from analysis.branches.len(). Discovered while fixing str-qo1.11.

Acceptance: explore CLI final report uses analyzer-derived branch counts, not unique_paths. branch_count and branches_covered are distinct, accurate values for all frontends.

title: Overlay smoke test fails with buildvcs probe
description: shatter-go/overlay/TestBuilder_GoBuildOverlaySmokeTest invokes `go build -overlay` directly (not via BuildLauncher) and fails with `error obtaining VCS status: exit status 128` when an ancestor of the test tempdir contains a broken .git. Same root cause as str-qo1.15 but on a separate code path the str-qo1.15 fix did not cover (test uses raw exec, not BuildLauncher). Fix: pass -buildvcs=false in the test's build args. Trivial.

title: Scan qualified function IDs follow-up: receiver-disambiguated IDs and wire exposure
description:
Follow-up to str-fuhw (Scan qualified function IDs). The initial fix in str-fuhw-qualified-ids switches scan-internal maps (file_map, analysis_map, scan_set, selected_set, by_name) to qualified IDs of form "<file>::<name>" and adds a regression fixture for two files each defining Write. Deferred items captured here:

1. **Same-file different-receiver Go methods.** "<file>::<name>" does not disambiguate two methods named Write on different receivers in the same file. Needs either receiver-decorated names emitted by shatter-go, or a richer qualified-ID format like "<file>::<receiver>::<name>" (or "<file>::<name>@<start_line>"). Crosses into shatter-go frontend scope, which str-fuhw was constrained not to touch.

2. **Wire-format qualified_id exposure.** Add a qualified_id field to ScanReport / FunctionReport JSON so downstream consumers (CI rerun wrappers, dashboards) can reliably distinguish duplicate-named functions across files. Overlaps with str-tzbr (CLI JSON stdout contract) and should land after that contract is finalized.

3. **compute_scan_id robustness review.** Currently path-based (safe for the str-fuhw bug). Re-evaluate whether qualified IDs should also feed into scan_id derivation once the wire change in (2) lands, to keep checkpoint resume keys stable across refactors.

4. **Rename FunctionResult.function_name semantics.** Today it stores a bare name for backward-compatible display. Once (2) is on the wire, consider promoting function_name to qualified_id and adding a separate display_name. This is a wire schema change and must be coordinated with report.rs, batch_state.rs, html_templates.rs, progress events, and any external consumers.

Acceptance for this follow-up: items 1 and 2 land at minimum; 3 and 4 may be split out further.
close_reason: All child follow-ups str-fuhw.1.1 through str-fuhw.1.4 are closed and landed on main; latest landing 66b495090f7244d4bac793231d19020e5abc05b3

title: Go harness disables buildvcs
description:
With a fresh Go workspace, focused Zolem exploration failed before meaningful harness compilation with:

```
error obtaining VCS status: exit status 128
    Use -buildvcs=false to disable VCS stamping.
```

Repro shape:

```
SHATTER_GO_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/tmp/shatter-zolem-fresh-workspace \
  shatter explore --project-dir /home/ketan/project/zolem --no-cache \
  internal/response/faker.go:tokenizeWords
```

Go's default `-buildvcs=auto` tries to stamp binaries with repository metadata when the main package/module/current directory appear to be in a VCS checkout. Shatter's generated overlay/launcher builds are disposable test harnesses, often built from generated workspace paths against real module paths, so VCS stamping adds no value and can fail before exploration.
acceptance_criteria: Go frontend harness and launcher builds disable VCS stamping or otherwise avoid VCS probes for disposable generated binaries. A regression builds an overlay-based generated launcher from a real module checkout without requiring git status to succeed. Zolem focused explore in a fresh SHATTER_GO_WORKSPACE_ROOT no longer fails with `error obtaining VCS status`.
close_reason: Fixed in 9255a983; merged to main. Added -buildvcs=false to BuildLauncher and setup loader go build invocations. Two regression tests in shatter-go/launcher/launcher_buildvcs_test.go cover both white-box (fake-go shim) and black-box (broken ancestor .git) reproduction.

title: Stale flags untracked funcs
description: A spec generated for only Refute `detectServerKey` was checked with `shatter stale selector.go spec.json`. The command returned exit 1 and marked the other functions in the file (`ForFile`, `prefersTSMorph`, `prefersOpenRewrite`, `detectLanguageID`) as stale even though they were never present in the targeted spec. Missing/untracked functions should not be conflated with stale changed functions.
acceptance_criteria: `shatter stale` distinguishes fresh, stale, removed, and untracked/not-in-spec functions. When a spec contains one targeted function from a multi-function file, unchanged sibling functions are reported as untracked or omitted, not stale, and exit-code policy reflects only actual stale/removed tracked functions unless a strict full-file mode is requested.
close_reason: Fixed in 492f9a36 / merge 76669d27..main. Added IncrementalPlan.untracked bucket; shatter stale exits 0 unless tracked drift. --strict opts in to legacy full-file behavior. Regression tests in spec.rs cover the bead repro.

title: Concurrent frontend spawn busy
description: Launching multiple Go-frontend Shatter commands against Refute concurrently caused `failed to spawn Go frontend: failed to spawn frontend: Text file busy (os error 26)`. Agent workflows often run independent probes in parallel, so the frontend build/spawn path needs locking, immutable binaries, or clear serialization.
acceptance_criteria: Two independent Shatter Go commands can start concurrently without `Text file busy`, or the CLI serializes/locks the shared frontend build artifact and reports a clear wait. Regression test or integration script launches two small Go probes concurrently and asserts both complete or one waits cleanly without spawn failure.
close_reason: Fixed in 5b79bb3a: serialize Go frontend extraction with unique tmp paths

title: Quiet mode hides reports
description: Focused Refute exploration with `--stdout --format text --quiet` exited 0 but printed no final exploration report, while artifacts on disk contained completed results. `--quiet` is documented as reducing log verbosity, not suppressing the command result. This makes quiet mode unusable for scripts that want clean final output.
acceptance_criteria: Quiet mode suppresses info/progress logging but still emits the requested command result to stdout or the requested output path. Regression tests cover focused explore and scan with `--quiet --stdout --format text/json` and assert the final report is present.
close_reason: Fixed in a7f7d10a; merged. Removed log_enabled!(Info) gates from 5 report-emission sites in explore.rs; added matching gate to emit_explore_progress' eprintln. 4 regression tests in shatter-cli/tests/quiet_report_emission.rs cover explore+scan × text+json under --quiet --stdout (json explore remains rejected per str-tzbr contract).

title: Scan artifact side effects
description: A bounded Refute scan was invoked with explicit `/tmp` report outputs plus `--no-cache --no-seeds`, but Shatter still wrote scan artifacts under `/home/ketan/project/refute/shatter-artifacts/...` and used the Go analysis cache, logging cache misses on the dry run and cache hits on the following real run. This makes it hard to run Shatter as a clean external audit tool and makes `--dry-run`/`--no-cache` semantics surprising.
acceptance_criteria: Document and enforce side-effect policy for scan/explore. With explicit external output paths plus cache/seeds disabled, scan does not write project-local artifacts unless an artifact directory is explicitly requested. `--no-cache` suppresses Go analysis cache reads/writes or the help text clearly distinguishes behavior-map cache from frontend analysis cache. Regression test runs scan against a fixture and asserts no project-local artifact/cache directories are created.
close_reason: Fixed in 57ad1acb: clean external-audit mode for scan suppresses project-local artifacts when -o + --no-cache + --no-seeds

title: Authoritative status export
description:
Some earlier confusion came from wrapper scripts aggregating Shatter outputs differently from the core tool, and from report consumers scraping markdown/TSV paths. Shatter should provide one authoritative status export for broad-run analysis.

The export should include:
- run manifest identity and source snapshot
- per-file status and per-target statuses
- artifact paths with existence contract
- denominator metrics and source-set classification
- failure taxonomy and line-weighted impact
- report validity/reliability
- threshold gate decisions
- frontend availability/preflight results

Markdown can be derived from this structure, but automation should not need to parse human report prose to understand run health.

Downstream scripts no longer need to infer success/partial/failed by scraping markdown.

title: Source-set line classifier
description:
The Kapow analysis had to use ad hoc path regexes to estimate obvious non-test/demo/story lines (~100k) versus total physical selected lines (~197k). Shatter should own this classification instead of making users compute it after the fact.

Add a source-set classifier that operates before target discovery and records why each file/line bucket is in scope. The classifier does not decide coverage by itself; it gives context for denominators and no-target reasons.

Suggested buckets:
- production-ish executable source
- test/spec/story/demo/e2e source
- generated/schema/scalar source
- declaration/type-only/config constants source
- fixture/sample/docs source
- policy-excluded or scope-excluded source

Reports should make it easy to say: "Shatter selected N files / X physical lines; Y lines are production-ish; completed exploration represents Z lines."
acceptance_criteria: Reports classify selected source lines/files into production-ish, test/spec/story/demo, generated/schema, declaration/type-only/config, fixture/sample, and excluded-policy buckets. The classifier is exposed in JSON and summarized in markdown. Tests cover representative Go, TS/TSX, Rust, config, generated, and test paths.
notes: Decomposed into str-jeen.37 (classifier core), .38 (cross-language fixtures), .39 (markdown summary).

title: Broad-run validation corpus
description:
Kapow is a valuable real-world stress test, but it is large, mutable, and subject to concurrent source churn. Shatter needs a stable broad-run validation corpus that captures the failure classes discovered in Kapow while remaining suitable for regression testing.

Fixture/corpus should include representative modules for:
- large source set where completed denominator is tiny unless failed spans count
- source files added/removed during a simulated run
- dangling artifact path prevention
- Go internal packages, generated harness import references, mixed package _test.go siblings, and rewrite syntax edge cases
- TS private helpers not exported, TSX/type-only syntax, project aliases, missing dependency preflight, browser globals
- unavailable Rust frontend in a mixed-language run
- no-target files by reason category

This can be a synthetic repo under tests/fixtures or a scripted mini-repo generated during tests. The goal is to make broad-run reliability testable without depending on a moving external Kapow checkout.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable broad-run validation corpus or fixture suite exists that exercises Kapow-discovered failure classes without requiring a live mutable Kapow checkout. CI or a documented local gate compares denominator, artifact integrity, stale-source detection, and failure-class counts against expected thresholds.
notes: Implemented under branch str-jeen.14 (3 commits: 17445c98 fixtures+manifest, a14370ef gate+tests, 03e66c7b Taskfile+docs). 13/13 fixtures pass under cargo-debug shatter; gate verified to exit 1 on threshold regression; 27 unit/property tests pass; test-standard clean. Awaiting team-lead landing.
close_reason: Landed in merge 0c929389. New corpus at tests/broad-run-corpus/ + scripts/broad_run_validation_gate.py + Taskfile entries broad-run-validation / broad-run-validation-tests. Documented local gate, not wired into mandatory CI per task scope. Threshold ratchet table in docs/validation/broad-run-corpus.md surfaces which open str-jeen P1 beads should tighten which thresholds when they land.

title: Coverage budget gates
description:
Broad-run users need a way to fail CI or local validation when Shatter produces a technically completed but low-validity report.

Add optional gates such as:
- --min-source-representation-percent
- --max-failed-span-percent
- --max-unsupported-span-percent
- --fail-on-stale-source-set
- --fail-on-missing-artifacts
- --fail-on-low-report-validity

Defaults should preserve current behavior unless the project config opts in. The report should show which gates were evaluated and why they passed/failed. This builds on the denominator, span accounting, artifact-contract, and validity-status issues.
acceptance_criteria: CLI/config supports thresholds for minimum source representation, maximum failed/unsupported span rate, stale source-set failure, and missing artifact failure. Tests cover pass/fail behavior and JSON output includes threshold decisions.

title: Concurrency semantics spec
description:
Define the concrete semantics for concurrent single-function exploration before implementation.

Decide and document:
- Whether `--seed` under parallelism requires exact candidate/output order or bounded reproducibility only.
- Function-level setup, execution-level setup, and teardown behavior across observer subprocesses.
- Candidate queue capacity, duplicate suppression, drain/shutdown behavior, and timeout behavior.
- Result ordering in `ObservationOutput` and progress counters under out-of-order completion.
- Whether the first implementation covers random exploration only, concolic exploration, or both.

This is a decision/spec issue, not implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Determinism, setup/teardown, queue shutdown, timeout, result ordering, and initial mode scope are documented. The spec identifies required regression fixtures for later child issues. str-frc child issues are adjusted if the chosen semantics change their scope.
close_reason: Concurrency semantics spec landed on main as 15507a55. See docs/specs/concurrent-single-function-exploration.md.

title: Bound GOMAXPROCS in go-frontend
description: Each spawned go-frontend invokes 'go build' on wrapper compilation; that toolchain run uses GOMAXPROCS=nproc by default, so N frontends * nproc threads exhausts CPU/memory on large hosts. Set GOMAXPROCS=2 (or min(2, nproc/parallelism)) in the env passed to embedded_go_frontend.rs spawn. Caps the inner toolchain without changing Shatter-level concurrency. Cleanest tactical fix for the kapow scan blowup.

title: batch_analyze ParseError on build-tag-excluded files aborts scan
description:
Discovered during str-hy9b.J3 kapow re-run validation (post str-s3s4/gq7c/dcqc fixes).

Go frontend returns ParseError for files whose //go:build tag excludes them from the default build configuration. Example from kapow:

  Error: batch analyze failed: frontend error for /home/ketan/project/kapow/api/ui/embed.go:
    frontend error (ParseError): target file "/home/ketan/project/kapow/api/ui/embed.go" not found in loaded package syntax

api/ui/embed.go has `//go:build ui` so under default tags it is not part of the loaded package syntax. The analyzer hits the file via discovery, fails to find it in the loaded syntax, and emits ParseError.

shatter-core/src/batch_analyze.rs only soft-skips ErrorCode::NotSupported (added by str-s3s4). All other error codes — including ParseError — still abort the entire scan.

Options:
1. Go frontend: return NotSupported (not ParseError) when a file is excluded by build tags. Semantically accurate: this configuration does not support this file. Pairs with eventual str-jl9r (build-tag-aware analysis) which would still benefit from the soft-skip behavior for tags shatter doesn't enable.
2. Rust core: extend the soft-skip in batch_analyze to also tolerate ParseError (or better, a new BuildTagExcluded code). Riskier — ParseError covers real syntax errors that we DO want surfaced.

Recommend option 1 plus a focused test: scan a Go directory containing a //go:build tag excluded file and assert the scan completes with the file logged as skipped.

Triggered by 3 files in kapow (api/tools.go, api/ui/embed.go, api/ui/stub.go).
Workaround for J3: --exclude the offending files.
close_reason: Duplicate of str-8amu (same bug: Go ParseError on //go:build-excluded files aborts batch_analyze). str-8amu is higher priority (P1 vs P2) and the canonical issue going forward.

title: Go frontend reports function line numbers past end of file
description:
Discovered during str-hy9b.J3 kapow re-run.

A function in a kapow source file was reported by the Go analyzer with start_line=148, end_line=>=148, in a file that only had 43 lines. This caused a panic in shatter-core/src/fingerprint.rs::extract_function_source: 'range start index 148 out of range for slice of length 43'.

Defensive fix landed in shatter-core (clamp both indices to lines.len()), but the Go frontend should not be reporting line numbers past EOF in the first place. Likely root cause: the package-aware analyzer reporting positions from a sibling file in the package while the protocol layer attributes them to the requested target file.

Reproduce: run a kapow scan; the panic surfaces somewhere in the analyze stage. With the defensive fix the scan continues, but downstream consumers (fingerprint registry, source code excerpt UI) will silently get empty function bodies for those targets.

Fix: in shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go, ensure StartLine/EndLine on FunctionAnalysis only reflect positions within the function's *own* file. Cross-check fset position file against the requested target file before recording line numbers.
close_reason: Skip declarations whose fset position file != requested target file in analyzer's file.Decls loop. Defensive cross-check via declarationBelongsToTargetFile (abs-path equality + single-file synthetic-module base-name fallback). Tests cover multi-file fixtures + direct helper assertion. Landed: 0727affa.

title: Wire generic instantiation planner into classify/receiver
description:
Follow-up to str-hy9b.F5. The planner module shatter-go/planner/generics.go was landed standalone. Wiring requires:

1. protocol/types.go — add TypeParams []TypeParamInfo{Name, Constraint} to DiscoveredTarget
2. protocol/discovered_target.go — populate TypeParams in BuildDiscoveredTarget by walking fn.Type.TypeParams.List; render constraint exprs (handle qualified idents like cmp.Ordered, interface literals, type-set unions)
3. planner/classify.go — replace blanket HasTypeParams → UnsupportedReasonGenericUnconstrained with per-typeparam dispatch via PlanGenericInstantiations
4. planner/receiver.go — same
5. planner/plan.go — emit one InvocationPlan per (instantiation × value-plan) cross product
6. Wrapper generator: emit Identity[string](v) instead of Identity(v) for generic calls. Needs new field on InvocationPlan (e.g. GenericTypeArgs []string) and threading through the launcher.

Item 6 is the real risk and likely wants its own design pass. Suggest decomposing further if it grows.

AC: real generic functions in the test corpus get plans (not just unsatisfied) and the resulting wrappers compile and run.

Live str-szcn3, str-aatcq and str-7zhdh are closed; str-j49xg/str-mhinv remain open owners of other adapter/receiver work. Do not reopen historical fixes without fresh reproduction.

Resolved rerun entrypoints: Kapow Makefile's make shatter runs shatter-preflight then shatter-explore; shatter-explore calls scripts/shatter-source-set.sh explore with SHATTER and SHATTER_TIMEOUT. That script's explore mode accepts positional eligible files/directories, --filter glob, and --jobs N (default1); defaults are SHATTER_TIMEOUT=30, request/build timeout240, and SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=bwrap. It writes shatter-artifacts/source-code-status.tsv and files/* artifacts. A targeted Go rerun can use the script's positional api/... file selection; preserve the actual selected argv rather than describe it as an all-project rerun.

Resolved report categories: shatter-core/src/report.rs exports completion_outcome values behavioral/error_only/dispatch_failed/skipped_by_policy, codebase completed_with_behavior/completed_error_only/completed_dispatch_failed/completed_skipped_by_policy, failed_functions with structured failed rows, unsupported_functions, and skipped entries whose interrupted category means never attempted due to budget. These are report classifications, not proof that every behavioral sample was an admissible application invocation.

Within the existing rerun comparison, record current revisions, exact backend/argv/scope/budget/cache state; separate these outcomes instead of equating completion with useful behavior. Explain old raw-span versus new instrumentable Go denominator explicitly: a denominator correction alone is not newly reached behavior. Include one human-readable example actually observed by the rerun, with its input/state limitations; no new configured-receiver fixture or guaranteed successful result is required. Keep TS reruns with their existing owners.

Actual run revision/backend/cache identity is determined at rerun time; historical absent metadata is marked unknown. This filing task performs no adopter run. Live tracker refresh: 2026-09-13.

## Acceptance checks

1. Comparison names actual revisions/command/backend/budget/scope and separates the available report outcome categories, including skipped-by-policy and budget-never-attempted where present.
2. Go denominator changes are separated from newly reached lines; one actual observed example is explained with invocation limits, without prescribing success.

title: Explore report omits failed functions
description:
Observed while running `make shatter-explore` in the Kapow repo on 2026-04-16.

Kapow invokes `shatter explore <file> --spec -o <file>.md --spec-out <file>.json` once per eligible source file. In that run, 108 attempted files produced zero-byte markdown reports even though Shatter analyzed functions, wrote per-function explore artifacts, and recorded failures in `shatter-artifacts/explore-results/.../summary.json`.

Examples:
- `api/internal/auth/context.go`: empty markdown, but `summary.json` reports `total_functions: 5`, `completed: 0`, `failed: 1`, and the log shows `use of internal package ... not allowed`.
- `web/src/lib/auth/index.ts`: empty markdown, but `summary.json` reports two failed functions and the log shows `Function "..." not found in instrumented module exports`.
- `api/internal/annotation/service.go`: markdown is non-empty only because two functions completed; five failed functions are still omitted from the markdown even though they appear in the per-file summary.

The current implementation writes markdown from `acc.md_fragments.join(...)` in `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs`. Fragments are only appended for functions that make it through result assembly, so discovered functions that fail before assembly disappear from the human-readable report entirely.

This violates the documented contract in `SPEC.md` that the markdown report is a human-readable summary of all explored functions, and it makes downstream wrappers like Kapow overcount empty artifacts as useful output.
acceptance_criteria:
- Per-file markdown report enumerates every analyzed function for the target file.
- Functions that fail, time out, or are skipped before result assembly still appear in markdown with status and a concise human-readable error message.
- Failure messages preserve the useful diagnostic cause without dumping full raw logs into the report.
- Successful functions continue to render their normal behavior/coverage sections.
- A zero-byte markdown file is only possible when analyze finds zero functions.
- Regression tests cover at least one file with all functions failing and one mixed-success file.

title: Scan staged-output seam

title: Explore CLI staged runner

title: Pre-execution constraint evaluator to skip predictable paths
description:
The orchestrator currently executes every candidate input in the worklist and only discovers after execution whether the path was already known. A ConstraintEvaluator can predict this before paying the IPC round-trip cost by substituting concrete values into known SymExpr constraint trees.

Architecture:
- ConstraintEvaluator takes a SymExpr and HashMap<String, ConcreteValue>, returns Option<bool> — Some(true/false) if fully evaluable, None if it hits an Unknown subexpression.
- Lives in the orchestrator's execution dispatch, not inside any specific strategy. Before any execute call, regardless of InputSource (Z3-solved, random, drilled, boundary, fuzzed), run the candidate through the evaluator.
- If evaluation matches a known path with full confidence (all constraints are Expr and evaluate to match a path in covered_paths), skip the execution.
- Conservative default: if any constraint is Unknown or non-deterministic, always execute.

Applies to all input sources: Z3-solved inputs (solution may satisfy a different known path), random/boundary inputs (many retrace known paths), drilled inputs, and future fuzz inputs.

Cost model: one shallow SymExpr tree walk per constraint per candidate. Even evaluating every candidate against every known path is far cheaper than one IPC round-trip.

Edge cases:
- Non-deterministic frontends (time-dependent branches, random state): prediction could be wrong. Execute if any constraint is flagged non-deterministic or Unknown.
- Skipped inputs count toward worklist drain but not toward execution counts or plateau counters.
- Evaluator bugs that incorrectly skip inputs are worse than wasted executions — conservative (execute on uncertainty) is correct.

Implementation: new module constraint_eval.rs in shatter-core. Integration point: orchestrator.rs execution dispatch, before the execute protocol call.
acceptance_criteria:
1. ConstraintEvaluator correctly evaluates SymExpr trees with concrete value substitution
2. Orchestrator skips execution for candidates that match known paths with full constraint confidence
3. Candidates with Unknown or partial constraints are always executed (no false negatives)
4. Skipped inputs do not count toward plateau counters or execution metrics
5. All existing InputSource types are filtered (Z3, Random, Drilled, Boundary)
6. Proptest coverage for evaluator correctness (arbitrary SymExpr + concrete values)

title: Orchestrator resume-from-state for explore batches
description: Currently orchestrator::explore() starts fresh each batch, rediscovering previously-covered paths until reaching novel territory. This produces O(batches) rediscovery per function in the str-b2my.6 round-robin batching loop. A resume-from-state API — persisting the worklist, covered_paths set, and input seeds across batches — would eliminate the tax and let EXPLORE_BATCH_ITERATIONS drop below 500 without hurting effective throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Batches 2..N of the same function in a broad-scope explore run make new progress from the start without rediscovering paths already covered in earlier batches.

title: str-bo4z.1 follow-up: migrate explore.rs cache.store calls to store_with_fingerprint
description:
Follow-up from str-bo4z.1 (cache invalidation on body change).

shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs has two call sites that persist behavior maps without setting a fingerprint:
- explore.rs:1966 — cache.store(&bmap)
- explore.rs:2040 — cache.store(&bmap)

After str-bo4z.1, BehaviorMapCache::is_fresh drops any on-disk entry whose stored fingerprint is None or mismatches. Until these call sites migrate to the new cache.store_with_fingerprint(&bmap, fingerprint), explore-written entries will be dropped on every subsequent run (safe — just forces re-explore, no stale data served).

Fix: plumb the current deep fingerprint (already in AssemblyOpts at explore.rs:2010) through to both cache.store call sites and switch to store_with_fingerprint.

Coordinate with str-b2my.6 which also touches explore.rs.

Scope: shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs only.

Acceptance:
- Both call sites use cache.store_with_fingerprint
- E2E concolic tests still pass
- Manual verification: running explore twice in a row on an unchanged function serves from cache on the second run (is_fresh returns true)
close_reason: Duplicate of str-bo4z.11 (P1, parented under epic str-bo4z). Both cover the same explore.rs migration; keeping the better-linked one.

title: shatter-go: stack overflow in type analyzer — infinite recursion on struct types
description:
The Go analyzer crashes with a goroutine stack overflow (1 GB limit) when analyzing files with cyclical struct type references. Triggers on `api/internal/nl/prompt.go`.

```
runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit
fatal error: stack overflow
```

The infinite loop occurs between `structTypeInfo` and `goTypeToTypeInfoWithContext` in `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go`. The cycle repeats:
- `goTypeToTypeInfoWithContext` → `structTypeInfo` (line 681)
- `structTypeInfo` → `goTypeToTypeInfoWithContext` (line 584/586)

**Root cause:** Type resolution doesn't guard against cycles in struct types, likely via `interface{}` fields, self-referencing `*go/types.Named`, or embedded types that refer back to themselves.

**Fix:** Add a visited-set (e.g., `map[types.Type]bool`) parameter to both functions to detect cycles. When a type is seen a second time, return a reference/stub instead of recursing. See stdlib's `go/types.NewMethodSet` for the pattern.

**Impact:** Only 1 of 137 targets hit this, but it's a hard crash. Any codebase with struct types that form reference cycles through interfaces or pointer indirection will trigger it.

See: /home/ketan/project/kapow/shatter-artifacts/bug-3-stack-overflow-type-recursion.md

title: shatter-go: deserialization error — missing field 'fields' (5 targets)
description:
The Go analyzer omits the `fields` key when a struct has no exported fields, or when the type is an alias/wrapper. The Rust deserializer expects `fields` unconditionally.

Affects 5 targets, including `api/internal/config/config.go` and `api/internal/fixture/fixture.go`. Error:
```
Error: analyze failed: failed to deserialize response: missing field `fields` at line 1 column XXXXX
```

**Root cause:** Same as bug 1 — Go analyzer omits optional fields that should default to empty collections.

**Fix:** Add `#[serde(default)]` to the `fields` field in the Rust analyzer response struct. A single pass through all collection-typed fields would likely fix both this bug and bug 1.

**Related:** Bug 1 (missing field 'args') has the same root cause.

See: /home/ketan/project/kapow/shatter-artifacts/bug-2-deserialization-missing-fields.md

title: shatter-go: deserialization error — missing field 'args' (19 targets)
description:
The Go analyzer emits function descriptors where some functions have zero parameters, and the `args` field is either omitted or set to null instead of `[]`. The Rust frontend cannot deserialize these responses.

Affects 19 targets across api/ (14) and tools/ (5) modules. All fail with:
```
Error: analyze failed: failed to deserialize response: missing field `args` at line 1 column XXXXX
```

**Root cause:** Go analyzer omits `args` field for zero-parameter functions.

**Fix:** Add `#[serde(default)]` to the `args` field in the Rust analyzer response struct, or ensure the Go analyzer always emits `"args": []`.

**Related:** Bug 2 (missing field 'fields') has the same root cause — both are optional fields that the Go analyzer sometimes omits.

See: /home/ketan/project/kapow/shatter-artifacts/bug-1-deserialization-missing-args.md

title: Embedded frontend cache writes
description:
Embedded frontend extraction currently fails when the default cache location is unwritable, which causes helper tests and npx task smoke to fail with read-only filesystem errors.

Repro in a constrained environment:
- cargo test fails in shatter-cli helper tests with failed to write frontend bundle / failed to write go frontend binary
- npx task smoke fails before exploration for the same reason

Expected behavior:
Frontend extraction uses a writable cache directory or returns a deterministic, testable fallback when the default location is not writable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a regression test that exercises unwritable default cache behavior.
- Helper tests pass under the constrained setup.
- npx task smoke no longer fails for this cache-write reason.

title: Project root Go fixture stale
description: The full cargo test sweep on 2026-04-05 exposed shatter-core/src/project.rs::detects_go_project_via_go_mod using examples/go/01-simple-branch.go, but examples/go no longer exists in this repo. The test now walks up to the repo root and incorrectly detects TypeScript via ./package.json. Update the fixture path or test setup to reflect the current Go project layout without depending on removed examples.

title: Examples external checkout
description: Remove the examples git submodule and make Shatter rely on the separate https://github.com/shatterproof-ai/examples repository via external checkouts under /tmp. Update scripts, tasks, tests, Docker demo flows, and documentation so they no longer assume examples/ exists inside this repo. Use latest main/HEAD from the external repo rather than a pinned submodule SHA, with SHATTER_EXAMPLES_DIR as an override for advanced/local use.
acceptance_criteria: The repo no longer tracks examples as a submodule; walkthrough/gauntlet/task/test flows resolve examples from an external checkout under /tmp by default; Docker/demo/perf paths no longer mount or read repo-local examples/; contributor and CI docs no longer instruct submodule init or recurse-submodules; SHATTER_EXAMPLES_DIR override is documented and supported where needed.

title: fix(rust-frontend): harness generation partial move error for Result-returning functions

  68 |     if let Err(ref msg) = result {

title: TS frontend: structural deep-equal, worker_threads, and efficient snapshotting
description:
Two performance improvements for the TypeScript frontend executor:

1. **Structural deep-equal instead of JSON.stringify comparison**: executor.ts lines ~1082-1093 use JSON.stringify(before) !== JSON.stringify(after) to detect global state changes. This is O(n) serialization on both sides just to check equality, and it's lossy (undefined, functions, circular refs are silently dropped or mangled by JSON.stringify). Replace with a structural deep-equal (Node's util.isDeepStrictEqual or a lightweight equivalent). This is both faster and more correct. (See also str-mro9 for the full structuredClone + snapshotting overhaul.)

2. **worker_threads for CPU-bound instrumentation**: Node is single-threaded, so instrumentation (AST parsing, transformation, SymExpr building) blocks the event loop. For scan mode with many functions, this serializes work that could be parallelized. Move instrumentation to a worker_threads pool. The main thread handles protocol I/O; workers handle CPU-bound AST transforms. This matters most when the TS frontend is processing many files during scan.
acceptance_criteria:
Instrumentation can run on worker_threads (at least for scan mode with multiple files).
All existing property tests and E2E tests pass.

title: Persistent harness subprocess for warm iteration speed
description:
Instead of spawning a new process per execute call, keep the compiled harness running as a long-lived subprocess that accepts input/output pairs over stdin/stdout in a loop. This eliminates subprocess spawn overhead (~10ms per call) and enables sub-5ms warm iterations.

The harness main() becomes a read-execute-write loop:
- Read JSON request from stdin (one line)
- Reset runtime state
- Execute function with deserialized inputs
- Write JSON result to stdout (one line)
- Loop until EOF (signals shutdown)

The frontend handler maintains a map of function → running subprocess. On execute:
- If subprocess exists and is alive → send inputs, read result
- If subprocess exists but died → restart it
- If no subprocess → compile (if needed) and start

Depends on stdin-based input passing (str-9u7n) being done first, since the loop protocol is an extension of stdin-based inputs.
acceptance_criteria:
Harness binaries run as persistent subprocesses, reused across execute calls for the same function.
Warm iteration (same function, different inputs) completes in <5ms.
Subprocess is cleaned up on teardown/shutdown.
Crash recovery: dead subprocess is detected and restarted transparently.

title: Multi-format output with extension-inferred format and additive -o flags
description:
Add support for multiple simultaneous output destinations on shatter commands (scan, explore, export, etc.), with format inferred from file extension.

## Output model

### Format inference from extension
| Extension | Format |
|---|---|
| .html | HTML report |
| .md | Markdown |
| .json | JSON |
| .txt | Plain text (markdown with formatting stripped) |
| other | Error: "unknown output format for extension '.foo' — supported: .html, .md, .json, .txt" |

Unknown/unhandled extensions are rejected with a clear error message.

### Flags
- `-o <path>` — write output to file, format inferred from extension. Multiple allowed; additive.
- `--stdout` — force console output in addition to file output. Format controlled by `--format` (defaults to markdown).
- `--format <fmt>` — controls stdout format only. One of: markdown, json, html, text.

### Behavior matrix
| Flags | Result |
|---|---|
| (none) | Stdout in markdown (current behavior, unchanged) |
| `-o report.html` | HTML file, no stdout |
| `-o report.html -o report.md` | Both files, no stdout |
| `-o report.html --stdout` | HTML file + markdown on stdout |
| `-o report.html --stdout --format json` | HTML file + JSON on stdout |
| `--stdout --format json` | JSON on stdout (no file) |

### Key principles
- No `-o` flags → stdout by default (backwards compatible)
- `-o` present → files only, stdout suppressed unless `--stdout` explicitly given
- Formats are additive: each `-o` is independent
- Same format to multiple files is allowed (no reason to prevent it)

## Affected files
- `shatter-cli/src/main.rs` — shared output flags on relevant subcommands
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs` — current output logic → refactor to multi-destination
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs` — same

title: Learning mode: suggest opaque types from execution failures
description:
After a scan or explore run, suggest types that should be added to the opaque types config based on execution evidence, optionally confirmed by static analysis heuristics.

## Two tiers of suggestions

### Tier 1: High confidence (execution + static confirmation)
Types where:
- Every generated input for the type caused consistent failures (constructor throws, undefined method, type assertion failure — not branch-dependent errors)
- Static analysis heuristics (str-io5d) also flag the type (no public constructor, transitive opacity, no implementors)

Both signals agree → high confidence the type is genuinely opaque.

### Tier 2: Execution-only (no static confirmation)
Types that consistently failed execution across multiple functions/inputs, but static analysis did not flag them. These may be opaque for reasons static analysis can't detect (requires async init, needs env vars, returns useless stub without real connection, etc.) or may be false positives (missing test setup, env issue).

Reported separately with lower confidence.

## Detection logic

1. During execution, track parameters whose generated values consistently fail. Tag failures by parameter type and failure pattern (exception type, message pattern).
2. After the run, aggregate: types that failed across multiple functions or ≥N inputs for the same function are candidates.
3. Filter candidates through static heuristics (str-io5d): match → tier 1, no match → tier 2.
4. Report both tiers with the failure pattern and (for tier 1) the static reason.

## User-facing output

### CLI text
```
Suggested opaque types (high confidence — static + execution):
  pg.Client        no public constructor; 4/4 executions failed
  redis.RedisClient  constructor requires net.Socket (opaque); 3/3 failed

Suggested opaque types (execution failures only):
  MyOrmModel       4/4 executions threw TypeError; no static signal

To add all high-confidence suggestions:
  shatter config add-opaque pg.Client redis.RedisClient

To add all suggestions:
  shatter config add-opaque pg.Client redis.RedisClient MyOrmModel
```

The `shatter config add-opaque` command accepts multiple type names and writes them to `.shatter/config.yaml`. The printed command is explicit and editable — the user can remove types before pasting.

### HTML report
- Two sections: high confidence and execution-only
- Each type has a checkbox: high-confidence checked by default, execution-only unchecked by default
- All/none bulk selectors per section
- Dynamically-updated `shatter config add-opaque ...` command string at the bottom reflecting current checkbox selections — user copies and pastes

## Dependencies
- str-asnl (diagnostics format — categories and nesting paths used in suggestion output)
- str-io5d (static analysis heuristics — used for tier 1 confirmation)

## Affected files
- `shatter-core/src/executability.rs` — candidate tracking during execution
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` — aggregation and reporting
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs` — CLI output formatting
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs` — CLI output formatting
- Report templates (HTML) — checkbox UI, dynamic command generation
- Config CLI — `shatter config add-opaque` subcommand

title: Static analysis heuristics for opaque type detection (high confidence)
description:
Detect opaque types through static analysis without execution. These are high-confidence heuristics where the type system provides strong evidence that a type cannot be synthesized.

## Heuristics

### 1. No exported constructor or factory
If a type has no public constructor and no exported `create*`/`new*`/`open*` factory function in its module, it cannot be instantiated. Both TypeScript's type checker and Go's AST expose this information.

### 2. Constructor requires opaque arguments (transitive opacity)
If the only constructor takes another opaque type (e.g., `new TLSSocket(socket: net.Socket)`), the type is transitively opaque. This is recursion on the same analysis — walk constructor parameter types and check each.

### 3. Interface with no concrete implementors in scope
A Go interface like `io.Reader` with no visible struct implementing it in the analyzed package. For TypeScript, an interface or abstract class with no concrete class implementing/extending it in the analyzed files.

### 4. Abstract class / private constructor
TypeScript `abstract class` or classes with `private`/`protected` constructor — no direct instantiation possible.

## Integration points

- Frontends (TS analyzer, Go analyzer) perform the static analysis during the `analyze` command
- Results feed into `TypeInfo` — a new field or variant indicating the static detection reason
- `check_executability()` in `shatter-core` consumes these signals alongside the existing hardcoded opaque lists
- Works in `analyze` and `--dry-run` modes (no execution needed)
- Detected types should carry the reason for detection (feeds into str-asnl diagnostics)

## Value
Today, opaque type detection relies entirely on hardcoded lists of known types per language. This means any third-party or application-specific type that wraps external resources goes undetected until execution fails. Static analysis catches these at analysis time, before any execution budget is wasted.

## Affected files
- `shatter-ts/src/analyzer.ts` — add constructor/factory analysis
- `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go` — add constructor/implementor analysis
- `shatter-core/src/types.rs` — extend `TypeInfo` to carry static detection metadata
- `shatter-core/src/executability.rs` — consume static signals

title: Improved opaque type diagnostics: explain WHY types are opaque
description:
When Shatter skips a function due to opaque parameter types, the current diagnostic is minimal:

```
Skipped 3 function(s) (unexecutable parameter types):
  processWithSocket: param "sock" has opaque type net.Socket
```

This tells the user *what* was skipped but not *why* the type is opaque or where in a complex type the opacity lives.

## Requirements

### Opacity categories
Each opaque type should be tagged with a category explaining why it can't be synthesized:

| Category | Examples | Explanation shown |
|---|---|---|
| Network handle | `net.Socket`, `net.Conn` | "requires live network binding" |
| I/O stream | `stream.Readable`, `io.Reader`, `os.File` | "wraps OS file descriptor or pipe" |
| Database connection | `database/sql.DB`, `pg.Client` | "requires live database connection" |
| Concurrency primitive | `chan T`, `Worker` | "runtime scheduling state" |
| Process handle | `child_process.ChildProcess` | "wraps OS process" |
| User-configured | (from config) | user-supplied reason, or "user-configured opaque type" |

Built-in opaques get categories at definition time in `OPAQUE_NODE_TYPES` (TS) and `opaqueGoTypes` (Go). User-configured opaques in `.shatter/config.yaml` should accept an optional reason:

```yaml
opaque_types:
  - DatabaseConnection                        # falls back to "user-configured opaque type"
  - name: HttpClient
    reason: "requires live HTTP connection"   # shown in diagnostics
```

### Structural nesting path
Show where in the type tree the opacity lives:
- Full path for nesting depth ≤ 3: `param "config" → field "db" → pg.Client (database connection handle)`
- Collapsed beyond 3 levels: `param "config" → ... → field "connection" → pg.Client (database connection handle)`
- HTML reports should allow expansion of collapsed paths via interaction (click-to-expand or hover)

### SkipReason changes
Extend `SkipReason` in `executability.rs` to carry:
- `category: OpaqueCategory` (enum for the categories above)
- `nesting_path: Vec<PathSegment>` (e.g., `[Param("config"), Field("services"), MapValue, Field("connection")]`)
- `user_reason: Option<String>` (for user-configured types)

### Output changes
- CLI text: `processWithSocket: param "sock" → net.Socket (network handle — requires live network binding)`
- CLI text (nested): `initApp: param "config" → field "db" → pg.Client (database connection — requires live database connection)`
- HTML report: full path expandable, category shown as badge/tag
- JSON report: structured `skip_reasons` with all fields

### Tips (secondary)
Where actionable, append a brief tip: "consider adding a generator or mocking this dependency". Low priority — diagnostics come first.

## Affected files
- `shatter-core/src/executability.rs` — `SkipReason` struct, `check_executability()`
- `shatter-core/src/types.rs` — `find_opaque_label()` → needs to return path + category
- `shatter-ts/src/analyzer.ts` — `OPAQUE_NODE_TYPES` → add category tags
- `shatter-go/protocol/analyzer.go` — `opaqueGoTypes` → add category tags
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/explore.rs` — skip reporting format
- `shatter-cli/src/commands/scan.rs` — skip reporting format
- `shatter-core/src/scan_orchestrator.rs` — report formatting (text, HTML, JSON)
- Config parsing — support new `opaque_types` object format

title: Per-input path highlighting in HTML reports
description:
Highlight execution paths for specific sample inputs through the displayed source code in HTML reports.

## Use case

Users want to select a specific input from the paths table and see exactly which source lines that input executed, highlighted in the source code view. This enables tracing execution for individual test cases.

## Scope

1. Add interactive path selection (clicking a row in the paths table highlights its executed lines in the source code view)
2. Use lines_executed data already present in ExecutionSummary
3. CSS classes for per-input highlighting (distinct from overall coverage)
4. JavaScript for toggling highlights when a path row is selected
5. Multiple highlight colors or a clear active-path indicator to distinguish from general coverage

## Design notes

- The source code display (str-y8gq) already shows line-level coverage. This adds a second layer: which specific lines a particular input traversed.
- Keep the report self-contained (inline JS, no external deps)

## Acceptance criteria

- Clicking a path row highlights its executed lines in the source view
- Highlight is visually distinct from general coverage annotation
- Clicking another row switches the highlight
- Works without external JS dependencies (inline script)
acceptance_criteria: Interactive per-input path highlighting in source code view; self-contained inline JS; visually distinct from coverage annotation

title: Source code in HTML reports
description:
Include the tested source code in HTML exploration and scan reports, displayed alongside coverage data.

## Use case

Users need to understand coverage overall and on a per-input basis, and trace execution through the source. The report should be a standalone artifact readable without checking out the code.

## Scope

1. Read source files during report generation using the file path + line range already available in ObservationOutput/FunctionReport
2. Display source code in a <pre><code> block within each function's <details> section
3. Annotate lines with coverage status (covered/uncovered) using CSS classes
4. Show line numbers alongside source
5. Pass project_root through the report generation pipeline so source files can be resolved
6. Handle missing/unreadable source files gracefully (show location string only, as today)

## Non-goals (follow-up issues)

- Syntax highlighting (can use a JS library later)
- Per-input path highlighting (separate issue)
- Interactive source navigation

## Acceptance criteria

- Source code appears in HTML reports for each function
- Lines are annotated with covered/uncovered CSS styling
- Line numbers displayed
- Missing source files degrade gracefully
- Askama templates used (depends on str-heiu)
acceptance_criteria: Source code displayed in HTML reports with line-level coverage annotation; graceful fallback for missing files

title: feat: HTML report output format
description:
## Summary

Add `--format html` output option to CLI commands (explore, scan, export, spec). Generate self-contained HTML reports from exploration and scan results.

## Architecture

**Shared data model**: Same format-agnostic Rust structs used by the Markdown output (str-nyle) feed into HTML-specific MiniJinja templates. No conversion between formats — each has its own templates optimized for its strengths.

```
Rust structs ──→ MiniJinja ──→ scan.md.j2  ──→ termimad ──→ terminal  (str-nyle)
                           └──→ scan.html.j2 ──→ file
```

## Scope

1. Add HTML templates for each command (`scan.html.j2`, `explore.html.j2`, etc.)
2. Generate self-contained HTML (inline CSS, no external dependencies)
3. Use full HTML/CSS capabilities: collapsible `<details>` sections, syntax-highlighted code, styled tables, summary stats
4. `--format html` writes to stdout or `--output report.html`

## Libraries

| Crate | Role | License |
|---|---|---|
| MiniJinja | Templating engine (shared with str-nyle) | Apache-2.0 |

## Dependencies

- Depends on str-nyle for the shared data model and MiniJinja infrastructure
- Templates are independent — HTML templates use full HTML/CSS, not derived from Markdown

## Notes

- Self-contained output: single HTML file with embedded CSS, no CDN links
- Suitable for CI artifacts, sharing with non-CLI users, embedding in dashboards

title: feat: Markdown output format with terminal rendering
description:
## Summary

Replace the current ad-hoc terminal formatting with Markdown as the primary output format, rendered to the terminal via termimad. This becomes the **default** output format — the current plain ANSI output is deprecated.

## Architecture

**Shared data model**: All CLI commands (explore, scan, export, spec) produce format-agnostic Rust structs (e.g., `ScanReport`, `ExploreResult`). These structs feed into format-specific MiniJinja templates. This issue covers the Markdown templates and terminal rendering; HTML templates are tracked in str-gkqy.

```
Rust structs ──→ MiniJinja ──→ scan.md.j2  ──→ termimad ──→ styled terminal
                           └──→ scan.html.j2 ──→ file     (str-gkqy)
```

## Scope

1. Define format-agnostic report structs (shared with str-gkqy)
2. Add MiniJinja dependency and Markdown templates for each command
3. Add termimad dependency for terminal rendering of the generated Markdown
4. Make `--format md` the default output format
5. Deprecate the current plain ANSI output (keep behind `--format plain` temporarily)
6. `--format md --no-color` outputs raw Markdown (suitable for piping to files)

## Libraries

| Crate | Role | License |
|---|---|---|
| MiniJinja | Templating engine | Apache-2.0 |
| termimad | Terminal Markdown rendering | MIT |

## Notes

- Markdown is the single source for terminal output — no more hand-coded ANSI formatting
- termimad handles tables, code blocks, headings, and colors
- Raw Markdown output is useful for piping (`shatter scan . --format md --no-color > report.md`)
- Shares the data model and templating infrastructure with str-gkqy (HTML output)

title: fix: TS frontend crashes with EPIPE during scan timeouts
description:
## Problem

The walkthrough script produces numerous EPIPE stack traces during step 5 (Scan Standalone TypeScript). When the scan orchestrator times out a function exploration, it `drop(frontend)` which kills the child process and closes the pipe. If the TS frontend is mid-write of its response, Node.js emits an unhandled `EPIPE` error on stdout and crashes with a full stack trace.

## Root Cause

`shatter-ts/src/main.ts` has no error handler on `process.stdout`. When the Rust core drops a timed-out frontend (`scan_orchestrator.rs:901`), the pipe reader is closed. The TS frontend's next `process.stdout.write()` emits an `'error'` event with code `EPIPE`, which Node treats as an unhandled error.

## Fix

Add a `process.stdout.on('error')` handler in `main.ts` that catches `EPIPE` and exits silently (code 0). Re-throw non-EPIPE errors to preserve crash visibility for real bugs.

## Files

- `shatter-ts/src/main.ts`

description:
Boost priority of negation candidates targeting loop boundary positions (iteration 0, 1, first exit) since off-by-one and empty-input bugs cluster at boundaries.

Key components:
- IterationPosition enum: First, Second, FirstExit, Interior, NonLoop
- classify_iteration_positions(): walks scope_events, maintains per-loop-id iteration counter
- Fitness boost in solve_and_generate(): First/FirstExit → fitness 1.0, Second → 0.9, Interior/NonLoop → None
- Uses existing fitness-based priority in WorklistEntry::cmp()
- Graceful fallback: empty scope_events → all NonLoop, no boosting

title: Loop analysis: loop-invariant branch detection
description:
Detect branches inside loops whose taken value is constant across all observed iterations; skip redundant negation for later occurrences. Uses dynamic approach (observe executions in orchestrator) — language-agnostic, no frontend/protocol changes.

Key components:
- LoopInvariantDetector: tracks per (loop_id, branch_id) whether taken is constant across multi-iteration executions
- Revocation: if a previously-invariant branch is observed to vary, remove classification
- first_occurrence_indices(): for invariant branches, return only the first occurrence index in branch_path
- Combine skip_indices with converged-loop set from diminishing returns technique
- Config: min_observations (default 2)

Testing: unit tests with synthetic traces, proptest (never marks varied branch as invariant), integration test verifying solver negates invariant branch once not N times.
notes: See docs/plans/loop-analysis-compiler-techniques.md — Technique 2

title: Loop analysis: coverage-guided diminishing returns
description:
Track per-loop branch coverage and suppress negation candidates for loops whose coverage has converged. When no new (branch_id, taken) pairs appear for a configurable window of consecutive observations, mark the loop as converged and skip its branches in solve_and_generate().

Key components:
- extract_loop_context(): map branch_ids to enclosing loop_ids via scope_events
- LoopCoverageTracker: per-loop coverage accumulation, stale counting, convergence detection
- Wire into explore() and solve_and_generate() in orchestrator.rs
- Config: loop_convergence_window (default 3, 0 disables)
- Graceful fallback: no-op when scope_events is empty (Go frontend safe)

Testing: unit tests for convergence logic, proptest for extract_loop_context, integration test verifying reduced executions without coverage loss.

title: Test case prioritization: order tests by marginal coverage per unit time
description:
Order tests by bug-catching ROI to maximize coverage reached per second of execution. Composes with TIA (str-zwgc) as a downstream stage: TIA selects affected tests, prioritization orders them, optional budget cutoff stops early.

## Algorithm

Greedy submodular maximization ("additional greedy"):
1. Score each test: (lines not yet covered by selected tests) / execution_time
2. Pick highest-scoring test, add to ordered list, mark its lines as covered
3. Recalculate scores for remaining tests (marginal coverage decreased)
4. Repeat until all tests ordered

O(n^2) with n=1,487 tests is about 2M comparisons, well under a second. Provably within (1 - 1/e) of optimal; in practice near-optimal at this scale.

## Data requirements

Extends the TIA coverage map (str-zwgc) with:
- Per-test execution time (every runner already reports this)
- Line-level coverage per test (not just file-level)
- Unique line count per test (lines no other test covers)
- Precomputed priority score: unique_lines / duration_s

Priority scores recomputed whenever the map refreshes (after any coverage-instrumented test run). Single pass over the map.

## Change recency weighting

Bias scores toward recently-changed code where bugs concentrate. Weight covered lines by days_since_last_change of their file (git log -1 --format=%ct -- file). Lines in recently-changed files get a multiplier. This makes the ordering adapt to what the developer is actively working on.

## Pipeline composition with TIA

All tests (1,487) -> TIA (str-zwgc): filter to change-affected -> Affected tests (~50-200) -> Prioritize: order by marginal coverage/time -> Ordered sequence -> Budget cutoff (optional): stop after N seconds -> First k tests that fit budget

The coverage map serves both stages. TIA uses file-to-test for selection, prioritization uses line-level coverage plus timing for ordering. One data structure, two optimizations.

## Flags

- shatter test --budget=10s: run prioritized tests until time budget exhausted
- shatter test --prioritize: run all affected tests but in priority order (fail-fast: most likely to catch bugs runs first)

## Prerequisites

- TIA coverage map infrastructure (str-zwgc)
- Baseline coverage measurement (never been run on this codebase)
- cargo-nextest for per-test filtering and timing
close_reason: Test case prioritization. 26 tests pass. Branch str-j0hu commit 2b9e984

title: Test impact analysis: coverage-based selective test execution
description:
Implement test impact analysis (TIA) to accelerate local development by running only the tests affected by changed files. The system maintains a coverage map recording which tests touch which source files, then uses that map to select the minimal test set for a given set of changes.

## Design

**Coverage map** stored at `.shatter/test-markers/coverage-map.yaml`:
- Forward map: test → {file: blob_hash} (update direction)
- Reverse map: file → [tests] (query direction, derived from forward)
- Blob hashes via `git hash-object` for content-addressable comparison

**Query flow**: `git diff --name-only` → changed files → reverse lookup → union of affected tests → format runner-specific filter

**Update flow**: after test run with coverage instrumentation, parse coverage output → update forward map entries for tests that ran → rebuild reverse map. Atomic write via temp file + rename.

**Staleness tracking**: each file entry records the blob hash at recording time. Changed hash = stale = must re-run associated tests. Import-change detection: if a file's imports changed (not just function bodies), broadly invalidate its dependents.

**Cold start**: empty map treats all files as unmapped → falls back to crate/package-scoped testing. Map populates incrementally as tests run with coverage.

**Tiered test markers**: tree hash (from `git write-tree`) stored at `.shatter/test-markers/<tier>` after a tier's tests pass. Pre-commit hook compares current tree hash against the required tier's marker.

## Flags

- `shatter test` (or wrapper script) — run only affected tests based on coverage map
- `shatter test --all` — run all tests regardless, bypassing TIA selection (always available as escape hatch)
- `shatter test --record` — force coverage recording to refresh the map
- `shatter test --tier=<quick|standard|full|e2e>` — run the specified tier and write its marker on success

## Runner integration

- Rust: `cargo-nextest` with `-E 'test(=name)'` filter expressions (requires installing cargo-nextest). Falls back to `cargo test -- name1 name2` for module-level filtering.
- TypeScript: Vitest with explicit file paths or `--testNamePattern`
- Go: `go test ./package/ -run 'TestA|TestB'`

## Coverage collection

LLVM source-based coverage via `cargo-llvm-cov --json` for Rust (~10-20% overhead). Vitest `--coverage` for TS. `go test -coverprofile` for Go. For local dev loops where tests take 5-15s, always-on coverage is acceptable (~1-3s overhead). Alternatively, periodic recording with `--record` flag.

## Current test landscape (for reference)

- 1,487 Rust tests across ~60 modules + 3 integration test files
- 195 Go tests across protocol/instrument/generators packages
- 6 TS test files
- No cargo-nextest installed yet
- No cross-cutting test groups; filtering is by module/crate/package name
- Existing tiers: Quick (cargo test), Standard (+clippy), Full (+TS+Go), E2E (+e2e_concolic), Walkthrough (+demo script)
notes: Plan saved to docs/plans/str-zwgc-test-impact-analysis.md. Exploration confirmed reuse of scm.rs (GitProvider, run_git), file_lock.rs (FileLock), existing serde_yaml dep. Three phases: P1 core data model + CLI, P2 coverage recording, P3 pre-commit integration.

title: Add remaining high-value contracts to solver bridge and protocol boundary
description:
The contracts crate was added in str-xlo9 with 3 annotations. The contracts policy (shatter-core/CLAUDE.md) identifies 5 qualifying sites. Two are annotated; three remain:

1. solve_for_new_path() postcondition: solved value JSON types match ParamInfo::type_info. The invariant str-6ayh violated. Proptest only catches this if someone writes a type-checking property; the contract catches it on every call path including E2E.

2. to_z3_expr() precondition: all SymExpr::Param nodes reference valid indices in the param list. Invalid index causes Z3 to use the wrong variable, producing silently wrong solutions.

3. Protocol validation wrappers: create validate_execute_result() and validate_analyze_result() with postconditions — branch_path non-empty, param_values length matches arity, function signatures have valid param counts. These functions don't exist today (serde types are used directly); creating them is the deliverable.

NOT in scope: expanding beyond the 5 qualifying sites, orchestrator state, pure functions, or anything proptest covers.

title: Fuzz targets for shatter-core Rust deserialization boundaries
description:
Go has 10 fuzz targets finding real bugs. Rust shatter-core has zero fuzz targets — only proptest (which uses structured generation, not byte-level mutation). Add cargo-fuzz or proptest bytes-based fuzzing for:

1. Protocol JSON parsing: arbitrary bytes → serde_json::from_slice::<Request>() never panics.
2. SymExpr deserialization: arbitrary bytes → serde_json::from_slice::<SymExpr>() never panics.
3. TypeInfo deserialization: same for TypeInfo (recursive type, high surface area).
4. YAML spec parsing: arbitrary bytes → serde_yaml::from_slice never panics on spec types.
5. String ops YAML loading: malformed string-ops.yaml content → build.rs/solver gracefully errors.

The Go fuzz tests found a real timeout overflow bug. Rust deserialization has similar untested boundaries.

title: Go semantic property tests beyond roundtrips
description:
All Go PBT is roundtrip serialization. No behavioral properties on:

1. Analysis: arbitrary Go source snippets (valid function signatures) → analyzer extracts correct parameter count and types. Use rapid to generate simple Go function signatures.
2. Instrumentation: instrumented code preserves original function behavior — for simple functions, executing instrumented vs original with same inputs produces same output.
3. Mock generation: sanitizeMockName is idempotent (sanitize(sanitize(x)) == sanitize(x)) and always produces valid Go identifiers (starts with letter/underscore, contains only alphanumeric/underscore).
4. Executor: for any valid function + valid inputs, executor either returns a result or a structured error (never panics, never hangs past timeout).
5. Protocol handler: for any sequence of valid protocol messages, handler produces valid responses in the same order (no reordering, no drops).

title: Proptest coverage for input_gen mutation and shrink at vector level
description:
Current PBT on input_gen has only 4 trivial type-preservation checks (mutate int→number, str→string, bool→bool, vec length). No properties on:

1. mutate_inputs (vector-level): arbitrary (Vec<Value>, Vec<ParamInfo>) → output vec same length, each element matches its ParamInfo type, at least one element differs from input (mutation actually mutates).
2. crossover_inputs: arbitrary parent pairs → child has same length as parents, each element type-compatible with ParamInfo.
3. shrink_candidates: arbitrary (Value, TypeInfo) → all candidates are valid for the TypeInfo, none equal the original, candidates are strictly simpler (for numeric: abs(candidate) <= abs(original), for strings: len(candidate) <= len(original), for arrays: len(candidate) <= len(original)).
4. Generator-aware mutation: when generators provide value_sources, mutated values should still satisfy generator constraints.
5. Idempotent shrinking: shrinking an already-minimal value (0, empty string, false, null) produces empty candidates vec.

title: Proptest coverage for orchestrator state machine and worklist ordering
description:
The orchestrator has only 3 properties on overlay_solved_values. No PBT coverage on:

1. Worklist ordering: arbitrary WorklistEntry insertions → entries dequeue in priority order (UserProvided > Z3Solved > Fuzzed > Seed).
2. Path deduplication: executing the same branch path twice → covered_paths set prevents re-exploration (second execution doesn't add to worklist).
3. Constraint accumulation: after N executions with symbolic constraints, the constraint set grows monotonically (constraints are never lost).
4. Budget exhaustion: with budget=N, explore loop terminates after at most N executions.
5. Convergence: with a finite set of reachable paths, explore eventually stops finding new paths (no infinite loops).

These properties test the core exploration loop invariants that unit tests can't easily cover.

title: Proptest coverage for spec and export roundtrips
description:
Spec/export was listed in str-ho1d but not delivered. Zero PBT on:

1. format_spec_yaml roundtrip: arbitrary FunctionSpec → YAML serialize → deserialize → assert structural equality.
2. format_spec_json roundtrip: same for JSON output.
3. format_spec_markdown: arbitrary FunctionSpec → markdown output is non-empty, contains function name, contains all class labels.
4. Export test generation: arbitrary BehaviorMap → generated test cases reference valid function names and use valid input values.
5. Invariant conversion: arbitrary ClassifiedInvariant → SpecInvariant conversion preserves label text, maps confidence correctly (≥0.95→High, ≥0.75→Medium, else Low), maps kind to valid InvariantCategory.

title: Fallback boundary search for unknown/opaque constraints
description:
When Z3 returns unknown or timeout for a constraint, and Shatter has inputs on both sides of a branch, use coverage-guided binary-search-style shrinking to find the boundary concretely. Currently falls back to naive fuzz_inputs() which is blind.

Prerequisites:
- Need one input on each side (true-path witness, false-path witness)
- Need shrink_candidates infrastructure

Algorithm:
1. Start with input A (true branch) and input B (false branch)
2. Interpolate/mutate A toward B using type-aware candidates
3. Re-execute each candidate
4. Track which side of the branch each result takes
5. Converge on transition point

More effective than random fuzzing because it has directional signal. This is essentially delta debugging applied to input space.

No code reuse from proptest — shared algorithmic pattern but entirely different execution model (subprocess protocol vs in-process function calls).

Related: str-e0a4 (type-aware mutation), str-e0uy (hybrid concolic + fuzzing)
notes: Epic: str-08r7 (Formal methods and property-based verification)

title: Boundary refinement phase with separate execution budget
description:
After the discovery phase (find distinct behaviors), run a separate refinement phase that binary-searches between known inputs on opposite sides of each branch to find precise transition points.

Key design:
- SEPARATE budget from discovery (e.g. --refine-budget N per boundary, distinct from --max-executions)
- Discovery benefits from breadth (spread inputs across the domain)
- Refinement benefits from focus (narrow in on a known boundary)
- Mixing them in the same loop with the same budget means one steals from the other

Algorithm per boundary:
1. Take two inputs: one triggering behavior A, one triggering behavior B
2. Interpolate/mutate between them using shrink_candidates
3. Re-execute, track which behavior each result triggers
4. Converge on the precise transition point

Output:
- Precise boundary descriptions in behavioral spec
- Minimal inputs at each transition point
- Higher-quality seeds for the interesting pool

Shatter should prioritize finding precise boundaries — this is a distinct phase, not mixed into discovery.
notes: Epic: str-08r7 (Formal methods and property-based verification)

title: Minimal witness shrinking: simplify discovered inputs
description:
After discovering an input that triggers a behavior, shrink it to the simplest input that still triggers the same behavior.

Algorithm:
1. Take an input that triggers behavior B
2. For each parameter, try shrink candidates (simpler values)
3. Re-execute via frontend; if still triggers B, keep the simpler version
4. Stop when no further simplification preserves B

Benefits:
- Cleaner, more readable test cases in export output
- Better seeds for the interesting pool (simpler seeds mutate more productively)
- More readable behavioral specs
- Minimal witnesses are the most informative examples of each behavior

Uses shrink_candidates function. No code reuse from proptest — shared algorithmic pattern (directed search via execution feedback) but execution goes through Shatter's frontend subprocess protocol, not in-process.
notes: Epic: str-08r7 (Formal methods and property-based verification)

title: Shrink candidates function: type-aware input simplification
description:
Implement shrink_candidates(value: &Value, type_info: &TypeInfo) -> Vec<Value> — given a value and its type, produce progressively simpler variants. This is the inverse of mutation (toward simpler, not toward novel).

Shrink strategies by type:
- Numbers: halve toward zero, try 0, try 1, try -1
- Strings: remove last char, remove first char, try empty, try single char
- Booleans: try false
- Arrays: remove last element, remove first element, try empty
- Objects: remove optional fields one at a time
- Nullable: try null

Shared infrastructure for minimal witness shrinking and boundary refinement. Related to but distinct from str-e0a4's type-aware mutation.

title: Add contracts crate to shatter-core solver bridge and trust boundaries
description:
Add the contracts crate (design-by-contract) to shatter-core with a HIGH bar for usage — only where Rust's type system genuinely cannot express the invariant.

## Where contracts are warranted

### Solver bridge (primary target)
Crosses Rust/Z3 FFI boundary where Rust types can't help — Z3 sorts are runtime values.

- solve_for_new_path(): Pre: all Param nodes reference valid param indices. Post: solved values have types matching ParamInfo.
- infer_sort(): Post: returned Sort matches the TypeInfo of the referenced parameter.
- overlay_solved_values(): Pre: solved_values keys are valid param indices. Post: output length equals input length. Post: each output value's JSON type matches ParamInfo's TypeInfo.
- to_z3_expr(): Pre: SymExpr tree is well-formed (no dangling Param references).

### Protocol deserialization boundary
JSON from frontend subprocesses — types can't guarantee structural validity:

- parse_execute_result(): Post: branch_ids are non-empty, param_values length matches arity.
- parse_analyze_result(): Post: function signatures have valid parameter counts.

### Orchestrator state transitions

- add_to_worklist(): Post: worklist is non-empty after add.
- mark_path_covered(): Post: covered_paths contains the new hash.

### Where contracts are NOT warranted

- Functions where the type signature already encodes the contract
- Simple transformations where proptest is more valuable
- Internal helpers with a single call site
- Any function where the pre/postcondition restates the type signature

## Relationship with Kani

Complementary: contracts document intent inline and catch violations at runtime (debug builds). Kani proves contracts hold for ALL inputs statically. Write the contract first, optionally add Kani harness later for the most critical ones.

## Documentation

Add section to shatter-core/CLAUDE.md explaining the contracts usage policy with the high bar. Include examples of good contracts (solver bridge) vs bad contracts (restating types).
notes: Epic: str-08r7 (Formal methods and property-based verification)

title: Add proptest to shatter-core, fast-check to shatter-ts, rapid to shatter-go
description:
Add property-based testing across all Shatter components. Liberal usage policy — use proptest/fast-check/rapid for any non-trivial function where interesting invariants exist.

## Rust (proptest in shatter-core)

Add proptest as a dev-dependency. Priority targets:

1. Protocol roundtrips: arbitrary Request/Response → serialize → deserialize → assert equality.
2. SymExpr sort inference: arbitrary SymExpr trees with known param types → assert infer_sort() returns correct Z3 sort. Prevents str-6ayh class of bug.
3. Input mutation type preservation: arbitrary (TypeInfo, Value) pairs → mutate → assert output matches type contract.
4. Path hash determinism: arbitrary BranchOutcome sequences → assert path_hash is deterministic.
5. Overlay solved values: arbitrary param lists and solved value maps → assert overlay preserves vector length and type compatibility.
6. Spec/export roundtrips.

### When to use proptest (guidance for contributors)

Use proptest when a function has:
- Roundtrip property (serialize/deserialize, encode/decode, parse/format)
- Invariant that should hold for ALL inputs (length preservation, type preservation, monotonicity)
- Multiple code paths that should produce equivalent results (parallel path parity)
- Boundary behavior hard to enumerate by hand
- Any function touching the solver bridge

Don't bother for: simple getters/setters, thin wrappers, tests easier as specific examples.

## TypeScript (fast-check in shatter-ts)

Add fast-check as a devDependency. Priority targets:
1. Protocol message roundtrips.
2. SymExpr builder consistency (buildSymExpr and buildSymExprWithFlow parity).
3. Instrumentor output validity.

fast-check properties are executable TypeScript using fc.property() with vitest. No DSL.

## Go (rapid in shatter-go)

Add rapid as a test dependency. Priority targets:
1. Protocol message roundtrips.
2. Executor timeout parsing (arbitrary env var strings → valid duration or default).
3. Analysis result consistency.

Also use native Go fuzzing (testing.F) for parsing/deserialization code.

## Documentation

Add sections to each component's CLAUDE.md explaining the PBT usage policy with examples of good properties and anti-patterns.
